dx: **ACUTE PYELONEPHRITIS IN PREGNANCY — ascending bacterial infection of the renal pelvis and parenchyma, most often ESCHERICHIA COLI, in a woman whose URETERS ARE DILATED BY PROGESTERONE AND COMPRESSED BY THE GRAVID UTERUS.** That urinary stasis is why ascending infection is **both MORE COMMON and MORE SEVERE in pregnancy.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: REACHING THE MANAGEMENT TASK, AND OPENING IT WITH ADMISSION FOR INTRAVENOUS ANTIBIOTICS.** **The station is scored TASK BY TASK. A beautiful history, a complete examination and a polished differential list followed by the bell scores highly on three domains and ZERO on the fourth — and fails.**

**THE COROLLARY: DO NOT REASON YOUR DIFFERENTIALS ALOUD. LISTING THEM IS THE TASK. EXPLAINING EACH ONE IS A CHOICE TO SPEND YOUR MANAGEMENT TIME ON SOMETHING YOU WERE NOT ASKED TO DO.** **Cap the list at TWENTY-FIVE SECONDS — time it — and DO NOT ADD A REASON TO ANY ITEM.**

**SAY THESE FOUR FIRST AND YOU HAVE PASSED THE MANAGEMENT TASK: 1 REFER TO THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT AND ADMIT · 2 INTRAVENOUS ANTIBIOTICS · 3 INTRAVENOUS FLUIDS · 4 SEND A URINE MICROSCOPY AND CULTURE BEFORE THE FIRST DOSE. Everything else is bonus, said only if the clock allows.**

**The history must be driven by A PREGNANCY-SPECIFIC DIFFERENTIAL LIST, not a generic tiredness mnemonic — that is where candidates who know the answer still lose the diagnostic domain.** **MUST-NOT-MISS, SAID OUT LOUD: PRE-ECLAMPSIA · CHORIOAMNIONITIS · ACUTE FATTY LIVER OF PREGNANCY · APPENDICITIS · SEPSIS. Naming these is worth marks even though none is the answer.**
**CORRECTION — the lecture calls pre-eclampsia 'a little too early' at 20 weeks. TWENTY WEEKS IS THE DEFINITIONAL THRESHOLD, so it is LEGITIMATELY ON THE LIST FROM TODAY ONWARDS, not prematurely.**

**CORRECTION — the lecture attributes more renal stones in pregnancy to progesterone. PROGESTERONE-RELATED BILIARY STASIS DOES INCREASE GALLSTONES; the incidence of RENAL CALCULI IS NOT MEANINGFULLY RAISED — although urinary stasis makes AN EXISTING STONE MORE LIKELY TO OBSTRUCT AND BECOME INFECTED. Asking about haematuria remains correct.**

**ANTIBIOTICS: empirical IV CEFTRIAXONE 1 g DAILY, or CEFAZOLIN 2 g 8-HOURLY. Oral switch once AFEBRILE AND STABLE FOR 24–48 HOURS — CEFALEXIN 500 mg 6-HOURLY or AMOXICILLIN-CLAVULANATE 875/125 12-HOURLY, directed by sensitivities. TOTAL 10–14 DAYS, counting IV and oral together.** VERIFY.

**NOT IN PREGNANCY: TRIMETHOPRIM, a FOLATE ANTAGONIST, avoid in the first trimester · NITROFURANTOIN, which DOES NOT REACH RENAL TISSUE SO IT DOES NOT TREAT PYELONEPHRITIS AT ALL, and is avoided at term · QUINOLONES and TETRACYCLINES, contraindicated · NSAIDs FROM 20 WEEKS ONWARDS · gentamicin only on specialist advice.**

**TEST-OF-CURE URINE MCS ONE TO TWO WEEKS AFTER FINISHING — PREGNANCY IS ONE OF THE FEW SITUATIONS WHERE IT IS REQUIRED — then MONTHLY CULTURE for the remainder of the pregnancy.** **STARTING ANTIBIOTICS WITHOUT A CULTURE: pregnancy is an ABSOLUTE INDICATION to send one first.** **MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 · PATS · Wallaroo Hospital with obstetric escalation to the WCH or Lyell McEwin.**
plan: **AT THE DOOR: 'before I start, could you give me her observations, please? BLOOD PRESSURE, PULSE, RESPIRATORY RATE AND TEMPERATURE.'**
**Introduce and SIGNPOST ONCE — then do not re-signpost between blocks, you do not have the seconds.**

**BLOCK 1 — CONVERT VAGUE INTO SPECIFIC, and the fourth question of the consultation is the one that matters: 'are you feeling TIRED AND LOW IN ENERGY, are you feeling SLEEPY, OR ARE YOU FEELING FEVERISH?'** Then **when did it start · constant or coming and going · getting worse · anything better or worse.**
**BLOCK 2 — THE FEVER QUESTIONS: HAVE YOU MEASURED YOUR TEMPERATURE · ANY CHILLS OR SHIVERS · have you taken anything for it, AND DID IT HELP?**
**'I'm going to ask a series of quick questions now, and MOST OF THEM WILL BE A SIMPLE YES OR NO.' CYSTITIS: any burning or pain passing urine · passing urine MORE OFTEN · ANY BLOOD IN YOUR URINE?**

**PYELONEPHRITIS: any NAUSEA OR VOMITING · any tummy pain · ANY PAIN IN YOUR SIDE OR BACK, AROUND WHERE YOUR KIDNEYS ARE?** Then **WHERE EXACTLY, AND DOES IT GO ANYWHERE — site and radiation only, you do not have time for a full pain history.**

**STI, with permission: are you sexually active at the moment · do you use condoms · ANY RASH OR ULCERS in the genital area · ANY VAGINAL DISCHARGE? HIV AND SYSTEMIC: any LUMPS OR BUMPS anywhere · any NIGHT SWEATS?**
**OTHER INFECTION: any sore throat, runny nose or cough · any HEADACHE OR STIFF NECK · any travel recently?**
**PRE-ECLAMPSIA: any BLURRING OF VISION OR SEEING SPOTS · any SWELLING of legs, hands or face · any BAD HEADACHE · ANY RIGHT UPPER ABDOMINAL PAIN?**
**GESTATIONAL DIABETES, as TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS: have you been MORE THIRSTY than usual · are you PASSING LARGE AMOUNTS of urine?** **Polyuria and frequency are different questions.**

**LIVER: any YELLOWING of skin or eyes · is your urine DARKER · are your stools PALE · ANY ITCHING, ESPECIALLY OF YOUR HANDS AND FEET? ANAEMIA: any racing of your heart or breathlessness on exertion?**
**OBSTETRIC BACKGROUND: how many weeks are you · any problems in the pregnancy so far · ANY TIGHTENINGS, ANY FLUID OR BLEEDING FROM BELOW · IS THE BABY MOVING NORMALLY?**
**MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES — ASKED NOW, BEFORE YOU PROPOSE AN ANTIBIOTIC, NOT AFTER: any regular medicines · ANY ALLERGIES TO ANTIBIOTICS, AND WHAT HAPPENED?**

**EXAMINATION — NAME THE FINDING, NEVER THE REGION. General appearance: alert or drowsy, jaundice, rash, dehydration. ALL FOUR VITAL SIGNS AGAIN — she may be septic. Throat: swelling or redness. Chest: air entry equal, added sounds. Heart sounds and murmurs.**

**ABDOMEN: any bruising, swelling or distension · ANY SUPRAPUBIC TENDERNESS · ANY RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT TENDERNESS · any hepatosplenomegaly?** Then **THE UTERUS: FUNDAL HEIGHT · IS THE UTERUS TENDER · FETAL HEART RATE?**

**THE SPECIAL TEST: 'IS THERE ANY RENAL ANGLE TENDERNESS?' Then THE DIPSTICK BY NAME.** **Pelvic ONLY if time — INSPECTION ONLY, six words, or skip it. A full speculum and bimanual at 5:30 is the commonest way to lose management.**

**READ THE FINDINGS BACK OUT LOUD, then NAME PYELONEPHRITIS with the reasons — burning, frequency, fever, vomiting, TENDERNESS OVER YOUR KIDNEY, and the urine test.** In Version B add: **'your pain has been LOW DOWN, which often points to a bladder infection. But on examination YOU'RE TENDER OVER YOUR KIDNEY, with a fever and vomiting — that combination tells me THE INFECTION HAS GONE UP FROM THE BLADDER TO THE KIDNEY.'**

**THE DIFFERENTIAL LIST, NAMED NOT EXPLAINED, 25 SECONDS.** Then **MANAGEMENT: emergency department today, admission, ANTIBIOTICS THROUGH A DRIP AND FLUIDS THROUGH A DRIP, culture before the antibiotics start, oral switch once stable, 10–14 days total, THE REPEAT URINE TEST A WEEK OR TWO AFTER FINISHING, and OBSTETRIC REVIEW OF THE BABY.**
pefe: **NEVER NAME A REGION — NAME THE FINDING. 'I'd like to examine the abdomen' earns you 'what are you looking for?' and costs FIFTEEN SECONDS. 'On palpation of the abdomen, is there any SUPRAPUBIC TENDERNESS?' earns you an answer.**
**Do not sacrifice management for a pelvic examination. You have ALREADY EXCLUDED discharge and rash on history. IF YOU MENTION THE PELVIC EXAMINATION AND NEVER MENTION MANAGEMENT, YOU FAIL.**

**Investigations: URINE MCS BEFORE THE FIRST DOSE · FBE, UEC, CRP · BLOOD CULTURES IF FEBRILE OR RIGORS · paracetamol for fever and pain · an antiemetic for vomiting · OBSTETRIC REVIEW for fetal wellbeing and assessment for preterm labour.**

**What results change management: RESISTANT ORGANISM → change the antibiotic, DO NOT WAIT FOR CLINICAL FAILURE · NOT IMPROVING AT 48–72 HOURS → RENAL TRACT ULTRASOUND looking for OBSTRUCTION, PYONEPHROSIS OR A RENAL ABSCESS · POSITIVE BLOOD CULTURES → longer IV course and infectious diseases · UTERINE TENDERNESS OR FETAL TACHYCARDIA → CHORIOAMNIONITIS UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE · PROTEINURIA WITH RAISED BLOOD PRESSURE → a SECOND diagnosis, investigate for pre-eclampsia in parallel.**

**Escalate for: SYSTOLIC BELOW 90 · PULSE ABOVE 120 · RIGORS · CONFUSION · OLIGURIA · UTERINE TENDERNESS · FETAL HEART RATE OUTSIDE 110–160 · REGULAR CONTRACTIONS · severe headache with visual disturbance · jaundice.**

**If she resists admission, DO NOT SOFTEN IT: 'the reason I won't treat this with tablets at home is that a kidney infection in pregnancy CAN SPREAD INTO THE BLOODSTREAM AND CAN BRING ON EARLY LABOUR. Both are far less likely if we treat it properly from today. IS THERE SOMETHING AT HOME I CAN HELP YOU ORGANISE so that going in is possible?'**
**After the episode: consider SUPPRESSIVE PROPHYLAXIS — for example CEFALEXIN 250 mg AT NIGHT — after a SECOND episode.** VERIFY.

stem: Jane Miller, 17, Year 12 student, presenting with tiredness over two to three months. Your completed assessment: recent examinations with considerable stress; bed after 1 am, up at 6:30; easy-going personality; mood normal, no anxiety disorder; three to four cups of coffee every night while studying. No weight loss, fever, night sweats, lumps or travel; no snoring or witnessed apnoeas; no medications, alcohol or drugs; periods regular and not heavy. Examination and vital signs normal.
tasks: Explain your assessment to the patient — diagnosis and cause of the tiredness (about 3 minutes)
Counsel her regarding your management plan
Answer the patient's questions
findings: THE STEM IS DELIBERATELY ENORMOUS — DO NOT RE-TAKE THE HISTORY
ALMOST ALL OF IT IS NEGATIVE FINDINGS, placed there SO THAT YOU CAN CONFIDENTLY CLOSE DOWN the other causes of tiredness. EVERYTHING ON THE CARD IS YOURS TO QUOTE BACK AS EVIDENCE
The arithmetic that IS the diagnosis
BED AFTER 1 am, UP AT 6:30 = ABOUT FIVE HOURS. AN ADOLESCENT NEEDS EIGHT TO TEN. Say the subtraction out loud — it is the whole explanation
The caffeine, as chemistry not as a lifestyle failing

THREE TO FOUR CUPS EVERY NIGHT while studying. CAFFEINE HALF-LIFE IS ABOUT 5 HOURS (range 3–7), so ABOUT HALF IS STILL CIRCULATING AT BEDTIME. Four evening cups is roughly 380 mg. Instant coffee 60–100 mg a cup · espresso shot 60–120 mg · 250 mL energy drink about 80 mg
Negatives handed to you in the stem

NO weight loss · NO fever or night sweats · NO lumps · NO travel · NO SNORING OR WITNESSED PAUSES · NO medications · NO alcohol or other drugs · PERIODS REGULAR AND NOT HEAVY · MOOD NORMAL, NO ANXIETY DISORDER · EXAMINATION AND VITAL SIGNS NORMAL
THE QUESTION THE STATION IS BUILT AROUND
'CAN I HAVE TEMAZEPAM? MY FRIEND TAKES IT AND IT HELPS HER.' And the follow-ups: 'JUST A FEW, FOR EXAMS' · 'MY FRIEND'S DOCTOR GAVE IT TO HER' · 'SO THERE'S NOTHING WRONG WITH ME?'
THE ONE QUESTION THAT SEPARATES THE MIMIC

'ON SCHOOL HOLIDAYS, WHEN YOU CAN SLEEP WHENEVER YOU LIKE, DO YOU SLEEP WELL AND WAKE UP FEELING FINE?' YES, ONCE I CATCH UP → INSUFFICIENT SLEEP. 'I sleep well BUT ONLY IF I GO TO BED AT 3 AND GET UP AT 11' → DELAYED SLEEP-WAKE PHASE DISORDER, managed with TIMED MORNING BRIGHT LIGHT and a gradual schedule shift, NOT hygiene alone
VERSION B — she is already taking them

TAKING HER MOTHER'S TEMAZEPAM NIGHTLY FOR THREE WEEKS, or buying it online, and wants a script of her own. Becomes a RISK AND DEPENDENCE consultation: HOW MUCH, HOW LONG, SOURCE, other sedatives, DRIVING, mood and self-harm. DO NOT STOP ABRUPTLY — supervised taper with her regular GP
VERSION C — the escalation
BMI 34 · LOUD SNORING · MOTHER REPORTS SHE STOPS BREATHING · falls asleep in class. NOW there is a positive feature of a specific sleep disorder, and POLYSOMNOGRAPHY IS GENUINELY INDICATED
VERSION — the third party
MOTHER ATTENDS AND DOES THE TALKING: 'just give her something so she can sleep before her exams.' ADDRESS JANE DIRECTLY, OFFER PART OF THE CONSULTATION ALONE, decline warmly, explain to both
CONSENT AND CONFIDENTIALITY AT 17

In South Australia a 16- or 17-YEAR-OLD CONSENTS TO THEIR OWN TREATMENT AS AN ADULT WOULD. Say it once, with its limit: 'what we talk about STAYS BETWEEN US, UNLESS I'M WORRIED YOU OR SOMEONE ELSE IS AT RISK OF SERIOUS HARM — and if that happened I'D TELL YOU FIRST'

dx: **CHRONIC INSUFFICIENT SLEEP — formally BEHAVIOURALLY INDUCED INSUFFICIENT SLEEP SYNDROME. THE SLEEP IS NORMAL IN QUALITY; THERE IS NOT ENOUGH OF IT.** **Use 'SLEEP RESTRICTION' or 'SLEEP DEPRIVATION' with the patient and KEEP THE FORMAL NAME FOR THE EXAMINER.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: DECLINING THE BENZODIAZEPINE IN A WAY THAT LEAVES HER HOLDING A BETTER PLAN.** **TWO FAILURE MODES SIT EITHER SIDE OF THE PASS. The first is the doctor who PRESCRIBES. The second, and MUCH COMMONER, is the doctor who REFUSES CORRECTLY AND STOPS THERE — 'no, we don't use those, they're addictive.' CLINICALLY RIGHT AND COMMUNICATIVELY FATAL: the patient leaves with nothing, and the examiner marks A FAILURE OF SHARED DECISION-MAKING.**

**THE PASS IS A TRADE, NOT A REFUSAL. FOUR MOVES: VALIDATE the request · DECLINE WITH REASONS · SUBSTITUTE immediately with the thing that works better · CONTRACT with a date.** **NEVER END ON THE REFUSAL — the sentence after 'no' must be 'WHAT I'M OFFERING INSTEAD WORKS BETTER.'**

**The reasons, in her language: DEPENDENCE — your body gets used to it, it stops working at the same dose, we increase it, and stopping gives WITHDRAWAL, WORSE SLEEP THAN BEFORE, anxiety, shakiness · NEXT-DAY DROWSINESS, which matters for your DRIVING and your STUDY · NOT RECOMMENDED IN SOMEONE YOUR AGE · and MOST IMPORTANTLY, IT DOESN'T FIX THE CAUSE. You'd still be going to bed at one with four coffees in you.**

**COVERAGE IS THE CURRENCY. A counselling station is scored on HOW MANY MANAGEMENT COMPONENTS YOU WERE SEEN TO COVER, not on how beautifully you covered one. Missing ONE heading is not a fail; MISSING FOUR IS. Say each one, briefly, and move on.**

**DO NOT RUSH THE EXPLANATION. The stem gives it THREE MINUTES — that is a FLOOR, NOT A CEILING. A candidate who says 'you've got a sleep problem, now let's talk management' in twenty seconds HAS SKIPPED THE REASONING, THE DEFINITION AND THE EXCLUSIONS — THREE SEPARATELY MARKED THINGS.**

**SAY WHAT YOU EXCLUDED, AND ON WHAT EVIDENCE: 'you haven't lost weight, you have NO FEVERS OR NIGHT SWEATS, NO LUMPS, NO TRAVEL, your PERIODS ARE NORMAL, you DON'T SNORE OR STOP BREATHING at night, your MOOD IS FINE, and your examination and observations today are ALL NORMAL. THAT IS WHAT LETS ME BE CONFIDENT.'**

**CBT-I IS FIRST LINE IN AUSTRALIA — MORE EFFECTIVE THAN SLEEPING TABLETS, AND THE BENEFIT LASTS AFTER YOU STOP. Refer to a psychologist under a GP MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT PLAN; supervised Australian ONLINE programmes if appointments are hard to reach.**

**CORRECTION — 'we don't have melatonin in Australia' is NOT CORRECT. PROLONGED-RELEASE MELATONIN 2 mg IS REGISTERED HERE for primary insomnia, but ONLY IN PEOPLE AGED 55 AND OVER. In adolescents it is OFF-LABEL, mainly for CIRCADIAN RHYTHM DISORDERS, under specialist advice.** If challenged: **'it would be off-label at 17, and IT IS NOT THE TREATMENT FOR BEHAVIOURALLY INDUCED INSUFFICIENT SLEEP.'** VERIFY.

**Hypnotic benzodiazepines: EXCEPTIONAL CIRCUMSTANCES ONLY, LOWEST EFFECTIVE DOSE, NO MORE THAN ABOUT 2–4 WEEKS INCLUDING THE TAPER, and NOT RECOMMENDED UNDER 18. South Australia has REAL-TIME PRESCRIPTION MONITORING.** VERIFY. **Kids Helpline 1800 55 1800 · headspace 12–25 · Sleep Health Foundation · healthdirect 1800 022 222.**
plan: **Open with a QUESTION, even though the task says 'counsel': 'how have things been since we last spoke — tell me how you've been feeling?'** It buys rapport, gives you a sentence to build on, and **is where the hidden agenda surfaces.**

**THE HIGHEST-VALUE SENTENCE IN THE STATION, in the first ninety seconds: 'BEFORE I START EXPLAINING ANYTHING, IS THERE ANYTHING IN PARTICULAR YOU WERE HOPING WE'D SORT OUT TODAY — OR ANYTHING YOU WERE WORRIED ABOUT?'**
**Empathy, then INVITATION: 'that's miserable when you're trying to get through Year 12. IS IT ALL RIGHT IF WE TALK ABOUT WHAT I THINK IS GOING ON, AND THEN MAKE A PLAN TOGETHER?'**

**NAME IT: 'the most likely cause is a SLEEP PROBLEM. Sleep problems come in several types — BREATHING ones like sleep apnoea, BODY-CLOCK ones, and NIGHTMARE disorders. In your case I think it's SLEEP RESTRICTION: YOUR SLEEP ITSELF IS FINE, THERE JUST ISN'T ENOUGH OF IT.'**

**DEFINE IT: 'enough good-quality sleep is a BASIC REQUIREMENT for your body and mind to work properly — CONCENTRATION, MEMORY, MOOD, APPETITE, IMMUNE SYSTEM. Someone your age needs EIGHT TO TEN HOURS. Going to bed after one and getting up at half past six GIVES YOU ABOUT FIVE.'**

**REASON IT — THE MARKS LIVE HERE: 'it started WHEN YOUR EXAMS STARTED. Sleep problems are VERY OFTEN TRIGGERED BY A STRESSFUL PERIOD AND THEN KEEP GOING AFTER THE STRESS HAS PASSED, because THE PATTERN IS SET. The coffee is part of it too — three or four cups in the evening IS STILL WORKING IN YOUR BODY AT BEDTIME.'**

**SAY WHAT YOU EXCLUDED, item by item, from the stem's negatives.** Then **TEACH-BACK: 'just so I know I've explained it clearly — IF A FRIEND ASKED YOU TONIGHT WHAT THE DOCTOR SAID, WHAT WOULD YOU TELL THEM?'**
**Open the plan with its aim: 'our main aim is to improve the QUALITY AND THE AMOUNT of your sleep. THERE ARE SEVERAL PARTS AND I'LL GO THROUGH THEM ONE AT A TIME.'**

**1 SLEEP HYGIENE — NAME SPECIFICS, NOT THE PHRASE: SAME BEDTIME AND SAME WAKE TIME SEVEN DAYS A WEEK · BED ONLY FOR SLEEP, no phone, laptop, television or study in bed · dark, quiet, cool room, pets out · IF YOU'RE NOT ASLEEP IN TWENTY TO THIRTY MINUTES, GET UP, DO SOMETHING BORING IN DIM LIGHT, come back when sleepy.**
**2 SLEEP DIARY for two weeks: each night the time you went to bed; each morning roughly when you fell asleep, HOW MANY HOURS, and QUALITY OUT OF TEN.**

**3 CBT-I, SAID TO BE FIRST LINE and better than tablets, with a psychologist or a supervised online programme. 4 CAFFEINE — THE BIG ONE FOR HER: none after EARLY AFTERNOON, total cut right down, and WARN OF A HEADACHE FOR A FEW DAYS if she drops it quickly.**

**5 RELAXATION: mindfulness, slow breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, yoga — free apps for all of them. 6 LIFESTYLE: exercise in the DAYTIME OR AFTERNOON not late evening · regular meals · NO alcohol, smoking or vaping · SCREENS OFF well before bed.**
**7 NAMED SUPPORT — 'support groups' scores nothing: THE SLEEP HEALTH FOUNDATION fact sheets, and HEADSPACE, the free service for people her age.**

**THE MOOD AND SAFETY SCREEN, one sentence, kindly, EVEN THOUGH THE STEM SAYS MOOD IS NORMAL: 'and how has your mood been in yourself? Any thoughts of harming yourself?'** Then **DRIVING: 'don't drive when you feel sleepy — pull over.'**

**THE TABLET, IN FOUR MOVES: VALIDATE, DECLINE WITH REASONS, SUBSTITUTE, CONTRACT.** **'Give me FOUR WEEKS with the diary and the plan. Come back and we'll look at it together, and if it hasn't worked WE THINK AGAIN — BUT WE THINK AGAIN PROPERLY, NOT BY REACHING FOR A TABLET.'**

**Handle the pushbacks: 'just a few for exams' → 'a tablet during exams is EXACTLY WHEN THE NEXT-DAY GROGGINESS WOULD COST YOU MOST.' 'My friend's doctor gave it to her' → 'DIFFERENT PEOPLE, DIFFERENT SITUATIONS — and I can only prescribe what I think is right FOR YOU.' 'So there's nothing wrong with me?' → 'THERE IS SOMETHING WRONG — IT JUST ISN'T A DISEASE.'**

**PROTECT THE LAST MINUTE: red flags, the conditional escalation — bloods then a sleep study IF she doesn't improve — and THE REVIEW DATE AT FOUR WEEKS WITH THE DIARY, 'and if you're struggling before then, COME EARLIER.'**
pefe: **No examination and no investigations at the desk — the stem gives you a normal examination and normal observations.**

**Bloods ONLY IF SHE DOES NOT IMPROVE: TSH · FBE AND FERRITIN · EUC and LFT · COELIAC SEROLOGY · blood glucose.** **FERRITIN MATTERS MOST IN A MENSTRUATING ADOLESCENT and is the one the source teaching omits.**

**CORRECTION — the source promises a sleep study up front. MAKE IT CONDITIONAL. POLYSOMNOGRAPHY IS NOT A SCREENING TEST FOR TIREDNESS: reserve it for a FEATURE OF A SPECIFIC SLEEP DISORDER, or FAILURE TO RESPOND to a properly delivered behavioural programme.**

**Do not miss: DEPRESSION WITH SUICIDAL IDEATION — tiredness in a 17-year-old is a presentation of depression UNTIL YOU HAVE ASKED · NARCOLEPSY, sleep attacks and CATAPLEXY — 'do your knees ever give way when you laugh?' · OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNOEA, and ASK THE PARENT AS WELL AS THE PATIENT · ANAEMIA with heavy periods and pallor · DROWSY DRIVING in a learner or provisional driver · bullying, abuse or an unsafe home.**

stem: Bill Hartley, 62, has come in because he had a fall yesterday afternoon.
tasks: Take a focused history from the patient
Ask the examiner for relevant physical examination findings
Explain your provisional diagnosis and differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: THE STEM DOES NOT SAY SYNCOPE

It does not say how many falls, and it does not say why. ALMOST EVERY AMC SYNCOPE CASE ARRIVES DISGUISED AS A FALL. Ask the examiner for BP, PULSE, RESPIRATORY RATE AND TEMPERATURE before you start — get this EVEN IN A RECURRENT-FALLS CASE, because he may have struck his head
THE DEFINING QUESTION — ask it in the first ninety seconds

'DID YOU LOSE CONSCIOUSNESS COMPLETELY, OR WERE YOU AWARE OF YOUR SURROUNDINGS?' BLACKED OUT, REMEMBERS NOTHING → syncope structure. AWARE, COULD HEAR PEOPLE → RECURRENT FALLS structure — STOP AND CHANGE. Candidates fail by PICKING A STRUCTURE FROM THE WORD 'FALL' AND COMMITTING TO IT
VERSION A — the cardiac ending

BLACKED OUT WHILE WALKING UP THE DRIVEWAY. NO WARNING AT ALL. Brief. Some EXERTIONAL CHEST TIGHTNESS AND BREATHLESSNESS recently. Examination: EJECTION SYSTOLIC MURMUR RADIATING TO THE CAROTIDS, SLOW-RISING PULSE → AORTIC STENOSIS. Same package with PALPITATIONS instead of a murmur = ARRHYTHMIA; with FAMILY SUDDEN DEATH IN THE 20s–30s = HOCM or LONG QT
VERSION B — reflex

STANDING FOR TWO HOURS AT A PARADE ON A HOT DAY. DIZZY, SWEATY, NAUSEATED FIRST. Witnesses say HE WENT PALE. TIRED BUT NOT CONFUSED afterwards → VASOVAGAL. Situational variants: WHILE COUGHING, STRAINING AT STOOL, OR PASSING URINE
VERSION C — not syncope at all
JERKY MOVEMENTS OF ARMS AND LEGS · BIT THE TONGUE · WET HIMSELF · CONFUSED FOR 20 MINUTES afterwards → SEIZURE. Switch structures and HUNT THE CAUSE OF THE SEIZURE
VERSION D — the one that caught candidates out
LONG-HAUL FLIGHT LAST WEEK · CALF SWELLING · PLEURITIC CHEST PAIN AND BREATHLESSNESS → PULMONARY EMBOLISM. It caught people because THEY ONLY HAD NEURO AND CARDIAC DIFFERENTIALS
VERSION E and F

E: RECENTLY STOPPED A REGULAR MEDICATION, or INCREASED a sedative or antihypertensive → drug-induced or WITHDRAWAL syncope. F: 'I WAS AWARE THE WHOLE TIME' — tripped on a rug, THIRD FALL THIS YEAR → RECURRENT FALLS, a completely different station
THE SIGNPOST THAT SAVES TWO MINUTES — verbatim

CHEST PAIN MATTERS BOTH BEFORE AND AFTER. So does headache. SAY THIS ONCE, OUT LOUD, BEFORE THE DIFFERENTIALS: 'I'm going to run through some symptoms now. FOR EACH ONE, COULD YOU TELL ME WHETHER YOU HAD IT BEFORE THIS HAPPENED, AFTER IT, OR NOT AT ALL? That way I won't have to ask you everything twice'
THE FINDING THAT IS AN ABSENCE

MOST SYNCOPE COMES WITH WARNING. CARDIAC SYNCOPE CHARACTERISTICALLY DOES NOT. Ask 'DID YOU HAVE ANY WARNING AT ALL — did you know you were about to go down, any dizziness, sweating, nausea, or a racing heart?' AND LISTEN FOR 'NOTHING'. ABSENCES ARE EASY TO MISS BECAUSE NOTHING IS VOLUNTEERED
RED FLAGS — THIS PATIENT DOES NOT GO HOME

SYNCOPE ON EXERTION · SYNCOPE WHILE LYING FLAT OR SEATED · NO PRODROME AT ALL · PALPITATIONS IMMEDIATELY BEFORE · FAMILY SUDDEN CARDIAC DEATH UNDER 40 · known structural heart disease or heart failure · ABNORMAL ECG · new chest pain, breathlessness, headache or focal neurology · SIGNIFICANT INJURY · AGE OVER 60 · RECURRENT EPISODES OVER A SHORT PERIOD
findingsLabel: Six endings from one stem — the defining question, and the finding that is an absence
must: FAIL — Running the wrong structure: a syncope work-up on someone who never lost consciousness.
FAIL — Discharging exertional or unheralded syncope as 'probably just a faint'.
FAIL — Never asking about warning symptoms. The single highest-yield question in the cluster.
FAIL — Missing the seizure screen, or confusing tiredness with postictal confusion.
ASK — Did you lose consciousness completely, or were you aware of your surroundings?
ASK — Has anyone in your family died suddenly and unexpectedly, especially young?

dx: **SYNCOPE is TRANSIENT COMPLETE LOSS OF CONSCIOUSNESS from GLOBAL CEREBRAL HYPOPERFUSION, with RAPID ONSET, SHORT DURATION and SPONTANEOUS COMPLETE RECOVERY.** **A SEIZURE is abnormal cortical electrical activity — jerking, tongue bite, incontinence, and a CONFUSED POSTICTAL PHASE. RECURRENT FALLS means consciousness was PRESERVED — an entirely different structure.**

**TWO DISCRIMINATORS, ARRIVING WITHIN NINETY SECONDS OF EACH OTHER. ONE: SYNCOPE OR FALL — the stem will not tell you, so ASK THEN CHOOSE. TWO: THE MISSING PRODROME — no prodrome, on exertion, supine onset, or palpitations first, EQUALS CARDIAC.**

**WHY THE MNEMONICS FAIL HERE: the published lists are built for COMPLETENESS, NOT FOR AN EIGHT-MINUTE STATION. BUILD IT FROM MECHANISM. Consciousness fails for TWO reasons: THE BRAIN ISN'T WORKING, or THE HEART ISN'T DELIVERING BLOOD TO IT. Then bolt on REFLEX, METABOLIC, DRUGS, INFECTION and, LAST OF ALL, PSYCHOGENIC.**

**CONFUSION VERSUS TIREDNESS DECIDES CASES. 'When you came round, WERE YOU CONFUSED, OR JUST TIRED?' CONFUSION IS POSTICTAL AND MEANS SEIZURE. TIREDNESS ALONE IS COMPATIBLE WITH VASOVAGAL AND IS NOT A POSTICTAL PHASE.**

**SAY THE NEGATIVES — THEY ARE HALF THE REASONING. 'No jerking, no tongue bite, no incontinence, no postictal confusion' is WHAT EXCLUDES SEIZURE; 'NO PRODROME' is WHAT MAKES IT CARDIAC. Say them explicitly rather than assuming the examiner infers them.**

**ASK ABOUT INJURIES EVEN WHEN THE ANSWER IS NO. If he STRUCK HIS HEAD and later has an intracranial bleed, NOBODY CAN TELL WHETHER THE BLEED CAUSED THE COLLAPSE OR THE COLLAPSE CAUSED THE BLEED.** Also ask **whether he had hit his head BEFORE the event.**

**THE AORTIC STENOSIS TRIAD: SYNCOPE, ANGINA AND DYSPNOEA ON EXERTION. Once ANY of these appears, PROGNOSIS WITHOUT INTERVENTION IS POOR and the patient needs URGENT ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY and cardiology referral for valve replacement.**

**IF PRESSED ON THE NEUROLOGICAL DIFFERENTIALS: keep them on the list for completeness, but have the nuance ready — TIA AND STROKE ARE UNCOMMON CAUSES OF ISOLATED TRANSIENT LOSS OF CONSCIOUSNESS, BECAUSE A FOCAL DEFICIT DOES NOT USUALLY IMPAIR CONSCIOUSNESS. The exceptions worth naming are VERTEBROBASILAR EVENTS and SUBARACHNOID HAEMORRHAGE.**

**DRIVING IS THE MARK MOST CANDIDATES LEAVE ON THE TABLE. Advise NO DRIVING until assessed, and name that fitness to drive after a blackout is governed by the AUSTROADS standard, with non-driving periods depending on the cause, whether it was treated, and whether the licence is PRIVATE OR COMMERCIAL — COMMERCIAL STANDARDS ARE CONSIDERABLY STRICTER.** **In SA the licensing authority is the REGISTRAR OF MOTOR VEHICLES, and doctors here carry A LEGAL DUTY TO NOTIFY where a patient is unfit and continues to drive — a duty that DOES NOT EXIST IN THE SAME FORM IN EVERY OTHER STATE.** VERIFY.

**Scripting each ending. CARDIAC: 'I'm concerned this came from YOUR HEART rather than a simple faint, because YOU HAD NO WARNING AT ALL and it happened WHILE YOU WERE EXERTING YOURSELF.' VASOVAGAL: 'this looks like a simple faint — but I'LL STILL DO A HEART TRACING TO BE SAFE.' UNCERTAIN: 'I CAN'T TELL YOU THE CAUSE YET, AND I'M NOT GOING TO GUESS. What I CAN tell you is WHICH SERIOUS CAUSES I NEED TO RULE OUT FIRST, AND HOW.'**
plan: **Ask the examiner for the vital signs FIRST.** Then **WIPE, open question, and EMPATHY EXACTLY ONCE: 'I'm so sorry to hear that, and that's a very reasonable thing to be worried about. Let's work out together what's going on.'**

**THE DEFINING QUESTION.** Then **'DID ANYONE SEE IT HAPPEN?' — in the OSCE the answer is ALWAYS YES, and THAT WITNESS IS YOUR SOURCE for the jerking, the pallor and the duration, NONE OF WHICH THE PATIENT CAN REPORT THEMSELVES.**

**THE SEIZURE SCREEN, THREE QUESTIONS, IMMEDIATELY: any JERKY MOVEMENTS of your arms or legs · DID YOU BITE YOUR TONGUE · DID YOU WET OR SOIL YOURSELF?** **Three noes → continue down syncope. Three yeses → this is a seizure and you are now looking for its cause.**

**TIMING: HOW LONG WERE YOU UNCONSCIOUS — seconds to a minute is typical, BEYOND A FEW MINUTES IS ALARMING · IS THIS THE FIRST TIME · CAN YOU DESCRIBE EACH EPISODE?** **Role-players are briefed with detail on EVERY episode — ask, and they hand you the pattern.**

**CONTEXT, five questions: WHAT WERE YOU DOING when it happened · were you in a HOT OR HUMID place · did it happen AFTER CHANGING POSITION · had you been STANDING FOR A LONG TIME · did it follow any STRONG EMOTION, FEAR OR PAIN?** **Exercise → cardiac. Coughing, straining, passing urine → situational. SUPINE → CARDIAC, because gravity isn't the problem when supine, so THE PUMP IS.**
**BEFORE — FOUR QUESTIONS, KEY POINTS ONLY: WARNING SYMPTOMS · had you MISSED MEALS, were you DRINKING NORMALLY · had you HIT YOUR HEAD AT ALL BEFORE this happened · any FEVER OR RASH beforehand?**
**AFTER — THREE QUESTIONS: were you CONFUSED, OR JUST TIRED · DID ANYONE SAY YOU LOOKED PALE · DID YOU INJURE YOUR HEAD, OR ANY OTHER PART OF YOUR BODY, WHEN YOU FELL?**

**THE DISCIPLINE RULE: NO SYMPTOMS IN THE BEFORE/AFTER BLOCK. Headache, chest pain, palpitations and nausea belong in the DIFFERENTIALS step, asked ONCE, with the signpost. Asking them here means asking them AGAIN later — and that duplication is exactly what runs candidates out of time.**
**GIVE THE BEFORE-OR-AFTER SIGNPOST, then CNS: headache · blurred vision · SLURRED SPEECH · weakness in any part of your body · numbness?**
**CVS AND RESPIRATORY: CHEST PAIN · RACING OF THE HEART · shortness of breath · cough · SWELLING IN THE LEGS?** **Leg swelling covers BOTH heart failure AND the DVT behind a PE.**

**GI: nausea or vomiting, abdominal pain if time. THE ADDED THREE: ANY LONG TRAVEL RECENTLY — PE · any YELLOWING of skin or eyes — hepatic encephalopathy · DO YOU FEEL THE COLD OR THE HEAT MORE THAN OTHERS — thyroid.**
**DRUGS, with the two-in-one: alcohol, how much · recreational drugs · 'DO YOU TAKE ANY MEDICATIONS REGULARLY, OR HAVE YOU RECENTLY STOPPED ANY?' — catches BOTH overdose AND withdrawal.**

**PAST HISTORY: DIABETES — autonomic neuropathy and hypoglycaemia · known heart disease or previous heart attack · epilepsy · psychiatric history. FAMILY: anyone with similar episodes, and HAS ANYONE DIED SUDDENLY AND UNEXPECTEDLY, ESPECIALLY YOUNG?**
**PSYCHOGENIC LAST, ALWAYS, AND ONLY TWO QUESTIONS: 'were you BREATHING FAST before it happened?' and 'was there anything STRESSFUL going on?' HYPERVENTILATION AND TRIGGER — NOT A MOOD ASSESSMENT.**
**EXAMINATION from the examiner — the generic syncope sequence, ending with THE THREE OFFICE TESTS.**

**NAME THE DIAGNOSIS with the ending's script, and SAY THE NEGATIVES that carry the reasoning.** Then **the differentials across MORE THAN ONE SYSTEM — CNS, CVS, RS, reflex, endocrine, drugs, infection.**

**DISPOSITION AND THE SAFETY-NET: 'if you BLACK OUT AGAIN, or get CHEST PAIN, A RACING HEART, SEVERE BREATHLESSNESS, A SUDDEN SEVERE HEADACHE, or ANY WEAKNESS OR NUMBNESS — CALL AN AMBULANCE ON TRIPLE ZERO.'** Then **DON'T DRIVE, DON'T WORK AT HEIGHTS OR WITH MACHINERY, DON'T SWIM ALONE.**
pefe: **The generic syncope sequence: general appearance — alert or drowsy, PALLOR, dehydration, RASH · vital signs REVISITED WITH TWO ADDITIONS ONLY, since you already have BP and pulse rate: 'IS THERE A POSTURAL DROP IN BLOOD PRESSURE?' and 'WHAT IS THE PULSE RHYTHM?'**

**Then NEUROLOGICAL — cranial nerves, FUNDOSCOPY for papilloedema, tone, power, reflexes, sensation, coordination · CARDIOVASCULAR — S1 and S2, murmurs or added sounds, and IF A MURMUR IS REPORTED, CHARACTERISE IT AND CHECK FOR RADIATION TO THE CAROTIDS · RESPIRATORY · ABDOMINAL.** **If a cause declares itself, DEEPEN THAT SYSTEM rather than continuing at survey level.**
**OFFICE TESTS: BLOOD GLUCOSE, URINE DIPSTICK, and A 12-LEAD ECG IN EVERY SINGLE PATIENT. Plus POSTURAL BP, and BETA-hCG IN ANY WOMAN OF CHILDBEARING AGE.**
**POSTURAL DROP IS 20 mmHg SYSTOLIC OR MORE, or 10 mmHg DIASTOLIC OR MORE, WITHIN 3 MINUTES OF STANDING.**

**WHAT TO LOOK FOR ON THAT ECG: rate and rhythm · HEART BLOCK OR PAUSES · PROLONGED QTc — above about 450 ms in men, 470 ms in women, and ABOVE 500 ms IS HIGH RISK · SHORT PR WITH A DELTA WAVE for pre-excitation · LVH for aortic stenosis and HOCM · ischaemic changes · RIGHT HEART STRAIN for PE · BRUGADA PATTERN IN V1–V2.**

**Bloods: FBC, EUC with CALCIUM AND MAGNESIUM, LFT, TSH, TROPONIN if ischaemic features, D-DIMER ONLY IF PE IS GENUINELY BEING CONSIDERED. Targeted: ECHOCARDIOGRAM if a murmur, cardiac history or exertional syncope · HOLTER or extended monitoring if arrhythmia is suspected · CT HEAD ONLY for focal neurology, significant head injury, anticoagulation or thunderclap headache — NOT ROUTINELY.**

**Avoid: labelling it vasovagal BECAUSE THE PATIENT LOOKS WELL · discharging exertional or unheralded syncope · GIVING NITRATES OR OTHER VASODILATORS IN SUSPECTED SEVERE AORTIC STENOSIS · reaching for psychogenic before organic causes are excluded · a reflex CT head.** **PATS and cardiology telehealth in MM5; MedSTAR coordinates retrieval if unstable.**

stem: Jane, 17, presented after she fainted for 30 seconds while attending a parade. Witnessed by friends, who called an ambulance. BSL and ECG normal.
tasks: Take a history (4 minutes)
Ask the examiner for the physical examination findings — given only if you ask specifically
Explain your diagnosis and your differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: THE TRAP SET IN THE FIRST LINE OF THE STEM

'BSL AND ECG ARE ALREADY NORMAL' IS BAIT. Candidates read it as 'cardiac and metabolic causes are excluded' AND DELETE THOSE BLOCKS FROM THE HISTORY. A NORMAL ECG DOES NOT EXCLUDE HOCM, CPVT OR AN INTERMITTENT ARRHYTHMIA. A normal glucose two hours later, after a sweet drink, DOES NOT EXCLUDE HYPOGLYCAEMIA AT THE TIME. NEVER SUBTRACT FROM YOUR STRUCTURE — ONLY EVER ADD
THE FINDING RELEASED ONLY IF YOU ASK BY NAME

BP 120/80 SITTING → 94/62 STANDING. That is a fall of 26 SYSTOLIC AND 18 DIASTOLIC — a drop of 20 OR MORE SYSTOLIC or 10 OR MORE DIASTOLIC WITHIN 3 MINUTES meets the definition of POSTURAL HYPOTENSION. IF YOU NEVER ASK FOR IT BY NAME, YOU NEVER GET IT
THREE EPISODES — and the diagnosis lives in the first two

1 JUMPED OUT OF BED AND RUSHED TO ANSWER THE PHONE · 2 SAW BLOOD, FELT DIZZY, FAINTED · 3 TODAY AT THE PARADE. TWO UNMISTAKABLE REFLEX TRIGGERS. 'Is this the first time?' → 'NO, IT'S THE THIRD TIME' → 'CAN YOU DESCRIBE ALL THREE FOR ME?'
Today's context
STANDING 1–2 HOURS · VERY HOT DAY · CROWDED PARADE · EMOTIONAL ATMOSPHERE. Out for 30 SECONDS. She says 'nothing special, just standing' — the detail comes only from the four context questions
THE PRODROME — the finding that makes it reassuring
'MY VISION WENT BLURRY AND I FELT LIGHT-HEADED.' Say it back out loud: 'THAT WARNING IS VERY TYPICAL OF A SIMPLE FAINT, AND IT'S REASSURING'
After: TIRED, NOT CONFUSED

'Tired, but I KNEW WHERE I WAS.' POST-EVENT FATIGUE IS NORMAL IN VASOVAGAL SYNCOPE. ONLY CONFUSION POINTS TO A SEIZURE. Do not change tack. Pallor is common in reflex syncope and DOES NOT ARGUE AGAINST IT
THE INCIDENTAL CLUE she volunteers

'I GET HEADACHES ALL THE TIME AND TAKE NUROFEN.' ADD THREE QUESTIONS — EARLY-MORNING VOMITING, WEIGHT LOSS, FOCAL DEFICIT — AND REQUEST FUNDOSCOPY. THEN RETURN TO YOUR STRUCTURE. Ninety seconds on a headache history and you never finish the syncope structure. Regular analgesia most days raises MEDICATION-OVERUSE HEADACHE — flag it for the GP
Everything else NEGATIVE

NO jerking, tongue bite or incontinence · NO chest pain, palpitations or exertional symptoms · NO missed meals, alcohol or drugs · NO medications · CVS, respiratory, abdominal and neurological examination NORMAL · AND NO FAMILY HISTORY OF SUDDEN CARDIAC DEATH — that negative is WHAT LETS YOU BE REASSURING
VERSION B — the online adaptation, FOUR findings

15-YEAR-OLD, collapse AT THE END OF A 100 m RUN. Hot day, SKIPPED BREAKFAST, prodrome of dizziness, GIVEN ORAL REHYDRATION SOLUTION, PALE, postural drop. MOTHER PRESENT. Task 2 becomes: TELL THE MOTHER IN LAY LANGUAGE WHAT EXAMINATIONS YOU WOULD PERFORM — findings then appear on a card
RED FLAGS that force a cardiac pathway

SYNCOPE DURING EXERTION, not immediately after · SYNCOPE WHILE SUPINE · NO PRODROME · PALPITATIONS IMMEDIATELY BEFORE · FAMILY HISTORY OF SUDDEN CARDIAC DEATH UNDER 40–50 · known structural heart disease · ABNORMAL ECG · SIGNIFICANT INJURY

must: FAIL — Shrinking the structure because the stem says the ECG and BSL are normal.
FAIL — Naming postural hypotension as the primary diagnosis for a true syncope.
FAIL — Only exploring today's episode; the two earlier faints never surface.
FAIL — Panicking at multiple findings: three co-equal diagnoses and no commitment.
ASK — Blood pressure sitting and standing — is there a postural drop?

dx: **VASOVAGAL (REFLEX) SYNCOPE — the commonest cause of transient loss of consciousness in adolescents. Benign, but RECURRENT AND INJURY-PRONE.** **Mechanism in one line: a trigger provokes an ABNORMAL AUTONOMIC REFLEX → VASODILATATION AND VENOUS POOLING IN THE LEGS, with or without BRADYCARDIA → transient GLOBAL CEREBRAL HYPOPERFUSION → LOC → FALLING FLAT RESTORES PERFUSION → rapid complete recovery.**

**THE DIAGNOSTIC TRIAD: TYPICAL TRIGGER — prolonged standing, heat, crowds, pain, fear, THE SIGHT OF BLOOD, sudden rising, micturition, cough. PRODROME — light-headedness, BLURRED OR GREYING VISION, warmth, nausea, sweating, TINNITUS. RAPID COMPLETE RECOVERY — brief fatigue is normal, CONFUSION IS NOT.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE — THE MULTIPLE-FINDINGS DRAMA. The examination hands you a SECOND positive, and in Version B a THIRD and FOURTH. THIS IS DELIBERATE: extra findings were added SPECIFICALLY TO FAIL CANDIDATES WHO MEMORISED A RECALL AND STOP WORKING ONCE THE FIRST POSITIVE APPEARS.**

**Candidates then panic and either SWITCH TO THE NEWEST FINDING as the headline, or PRESENT THREE CO-EQUAL DIAGNOSES AND COMMIT TO NONE. BOTH FAIL.** **The correct move: EXTRA FINDINGS MEAN YOUR HISTORY AND EXAMINATION WERE THOROUGH — THAT IS A REWARD. NAME ONE MOST LIKELY PROVISIONAL DIAGNOSIS, THEN LIST THE OTHERS IN ORDER.**

**WHY VASOVAGAL OUTRANKS THE POSTURAL DROP. POSTURAL HYPOTENSION TYPICALLY CAUSES DIZZINESS OR PRESYNCOPE, NOT TRUE LOSS OF CONSCIOUSNESS — if a postural drop alone caused syncope, EVERY PATIENT ON ANTIHYPERTENSIVES WOULD BE FAINTING REPEATEDLY; they get dizzy, sit down, and recover.**

**And REFLEX SYNCOPE ITSELF PRODUCES A TRANSIENT AUTONOMIC DISTURBANCE, so a postural drop measured SOON AFTER an episode is often A CONSEQUENCE OF THE REFLEX EVENT RATHER THAN AN INDEPENDENT CAUSE.** **The two earlier episodes have NOTHING TO DO WITH POSTURE.** **Postural hypotension is A DIAGNOSIS OF LAST RESORT, NOT FIRST.**

**THE SCRIPT — THREE REASONS, THEN THE DROP AS EVIDENCE: 'the most likely cause is VASOVAGAL SYNCOPE — a simple faint. FIRST, where it happened today: a hot day, standing still for a couple of hours, a crowded parade — THAT'S THE CLASSIC SETTING. SECOND, your TWO EARLIER EPISODES FIT THE SAME PATTERN. THIRD, YOU HAD A CLEAR WARNING FIRST. One thing I found is that your blood pressure DROPS A LITTLE WHEN YOU STAND — that FITS WITH, AND SUPPORTS, the same diagnosis.'**

**BRIEF MYOCLONIC JERKS ARE COMMON IN REFLEX SYNCOPE AND DO NOT MAKE IT A SEIZURE — a few seconds of jerking as she goes down, with immediate recovery, no confusion and no tongue bite, is CONVULSIVE SYNCOPE.**

**Management to tell her: RECOGNISE THE WARNING AND ACT IMMEDIATELY — lie down and RAISE THE LEGS, or sit with the head between the knees · COUNTER-PRESSURE MANOEUVRES at the first symptom — CROSS THE LEGS AND TENSE THE THIGHS AND BUTTOCKS, GRIP ONE HAND HARD IN THE OTHER AND PULL OUTWARDS, tense the arms · FLUIDS across the day, more in heat · AVOID prolonged motionless standing, hot crowded places, dehydration, alcohol, skipping meals · KEEP THE CALF MUSCLES MOVING if you must stand still.**

**Drug therapy — midodrine or fludrocortisone — is SPECIALIST-INITIATED and ONLY for FREQUENT, DISABLING, REFRACTORY episodes.** **Liberalise salt ONLY if there is no hypertension or renal or cardiac disease.** **In SA the driver must notify AND THE TREATING DOCTOR HAS A STATUTORY DUTY TO REPORT someone believed unfit — unlike most other states, where reporting is discretionary.** VERIFY.
plan: **To the examiner: 'may I have her vital signs — BLOOD PRESSURE SITTING AND STANDING, pulse rate and rhythm, respiratory rate, saturation and temperature? IS SHE HAEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE?'** If told to proceed, **'thank you, I'll take it that she is stable' — and move on without losing rhythm.**

**Introduce, ask how she likes to be addressed, and frame it: 'I can see how worrying this must have been. Let's work through it together — I'll ask you some questions, then check your examination findings, and WE'LL TRY TO FIND OUT WHY THIS KEEPS HAPPENING.'**

**CONFIRM TRUE SYNCOPE, THEN EXCLUDE SEIZURE — ask even though the stem says 'fainted': DID YOU LOSE CONSCIOUSNESS COMPLETELY, or were you aware of what was going on · YOUR FRIENDS WERE WITH YOU — did they say you had any JERKY MOVEMENTS, did you BITE YOUR TONGUE, did you WET OR SOIL YOURSELF · HOW LONG WERE YOU OUT FOR?**
**'IS THIS THE FIRST TIME THIS HAS HAPPENED?' Then 'CAN YOU DESCRIBE ALL THREE EPISODES FOR ME?'** **This is where the diagnosis is actually made — NOT in today's story.**

**TODAY'S CONTEXT: what exactly were you doing at the moment it happened · HOW LONG HAD YOU BEEN STANDING · WAS IT A HOT OR HUMID DAY · WAS IT CROWDED · any STRONG EMOTIONS, FEAR OR PAIN · had you just CHANGED POSITION?**

**THE PRODROME QUESTION: 'DID YOU GET ANY WARNING BEFORE YOU FAINTED — LIGHT-HEADEDNESS, YOUR VISION GOING BLURRY OR GREY, FEELING HOT, SWEATY, SICK, OR RINGING IN YOUR EARS?'** Then **missed meals · fluids · head injury beforehand · fever or rash.**
**AFTER: 'when you came round, WERE YOU CONFUSED, OR JUST TIRED?' · did anyone say you LOOKED PALE · DID YOU INJURE YOURSELF IN THE FALL?**

**Signpost the review: 'I'll run through a list of symptoms — for each, tell me if you had it BEFORE OR AFTER the faint.' CNS: any headaches · blurred or double vision · slurred speech · weakness or numbness?**

**The headache positive gets THREE QUESTIONS AND NO MORE: EARLY-MORNING VOMITING · WEIGHT LOSS · any waking at night with headache, or headache WORSE LYING DOWN, COUGHING OR STRAINING.** Then **RETURN TO THE STRUCTURE.**

**CVS — ask it, ECG or no ECG: any CHEST PAIN · ANY RACING OR POUNDING OF THE HEART, ESPECIALLY JUST BEFORE YOU FAINTED · short of breath at rest, on exertion, LYING FLAT or AT NIGHT · ankle swelling?**
**RESPIRATORY: cough · haemoptysis · pain on breathing in · WHEEZE WITH EXERCISE. GI: nausea or vomiting · tummy pain · BLACK OR BLOODY BOWEL MOTIONS?**
**HAEM AND GYNAE, asked privately and matter-of-factly: ARE YOUR PERIODS REGULAR, AND ARE THEY HEAVY · have you been more tired than usual · IS THERE ANY CHANCE YOU COULD BE PREGNANT?**

**DRUGS, plainly — common and expected in this age group and setting: any ALCOHOL at the parade · any RECREATIONAL DRUGS · any regular medications, or anything STARTED OR STOPPED RECENTLY? PSYCH: were you BREATHING VERY FAST before it happened · any TINGLING in your hands or around your mouth · anything stressful at school or home?**

**PAST HISTORY AND FAMILY: any medical conditions or operations · does anyone in your family have HEART PROBLEMS, EPILEPSY, OR FAINTING LIKE THIS · HAS ANYONE IN YOUR FAMILY DIED SUDDENLY AT A YOUNG AGE?**
**Ask the examiner for the examination, NAMING WHAT YOU WANT — and ask for the POSTURAL BLOOD PRESSURE BY NAME.**

**COMMIT TO ONE DIAGNOSIS with the three-reason script, THEN present the postural drop as SUPPORTING EVIDENCE.** Then **the ranked differentials — and say explicitly that A NORMAL ECG DOES NOT EXCLUDE HOCM OR AN INHERITED ARRHYTHMIA.**

**Management and the SAFETY-NET, said out loud: 'come straight back if you faint WITHOUT ANY WARNING, if it happens WHILE YOU'RE EXERCISING OR LYING DOWN, if you get CHEST PAIN OR A RACING HEART beforehand, if you INJURE YOURSELF, or if the faints BECOME MORE FREQUENT.'** Then **GP follow-up including the headaches and the ibuprofen.**
pefe: **Name what you want. GENERAL: alert or drowsy · PALLOR · dehydration · rash · INJURY FROM THE FALL · BMI.** **VITALS: BP LYING OR SITTING AND AGAIN AFTER 3 MINUTES STANDING — IS THERE A POSTURAL DROP · pulse rate AND RHYTHM · respiratory rate, temperature, saturation.**

**NEURO: cranial nerves · FUNDOSCOPY FOR PAPILLOEDEMA — the examination that follows logically from the chronic headache, and asking for it SHOWS THE EXAMINER YOUR REASONING · tone, power, reflexes, sensation, coordination · gait · neck stiffness.**

**CVS: JVP · apex beat, DISPLACED OR HEAVING · any MURMURS — and if so SITE, TIMING AND RADIATION · carotid bruits · peripheral pulses.** **RESPIRATORY and ABDOMEN. OFFICE TESTS: BSL, ECG, urine dipstick, and WITH HER CONSENT A URINE PREGNANCY TEST.**

**Do now: LYING AND STANDING BLOOD PRESSURE — the single highest-yield bedside test here · bedside glucose · 12-LEAD ECG READ YOURSELF for QTc, DELTA WAVE, BRUGADA PATTERN, LVH WITH DEEP T INVERSION, AV BLOCK · assess for injury · FBE and UEC · urine pregnancy test · dipstick.**

**Do next: USUALLY NOTHING FURTHER. Typical vasovagal syncope is a CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS and does NOT need an echocardiogram, brain imaging, tilt-table testing or a Holter monitor.** **Add tests ONLY FOR A REASON: echo if a MURMUR, EXERTIONAL syncope or FAMILY SUDDEN DEATH · Holter for PALPITATIONS or recurrent unexplained syncope · CT brain ONLY for head injury, focal deficit or headache red flags · iron studies if anaemic.**

**Do not miss: HOCM and INHERITED ARRHYTHMIA — a normal ECG excludes NEITHER · aortic stenosis · seizure · INTRACRANIAL PATHOLOGY BEHIND THE CHRONIC HEADACHE · HYPOGLYCAEMIA AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT · anaemia · pregnancy · injury sustained in the fall.**

**Avoid: ordering an undifferentiated panel — NAME SPECIFIC TESTS AND SAY WHY · 'it's just a faint, nothing to worry about' with no safety advice · REASSURING BEFORE YOU HAVE ASKED ABOUT FAMILY SUDDEN DEATH.** **In Version B, PLAIN WORDS TO THE MOTHER: 'I'll look at her neck and chest, feel the chest, and listen to her heart' — not 'a praecordial examination and auscultation for murmurs'.**

Ask the examiner for the relevant physical examination findings

findings: Observations given on arrival

ALERT AND ORIENTATED NOW · BP 118/74 · PR 78 regular · RR 16 · SpO2 99% RA · T 36.8 · BGL 5.4 · GCS 15. Ask the examiner up front for VITALS INCLUDING A POSTURAL DROP, PULSE RHYTHM, BEDSIDE GLUCOSE AND GCS
WITNESSED BY HER PARENTS — take their account

SAY IT OUT LOUD: 'YOUR PARENTS SAW IT AND YOU DIDN'T — THEIR DESCRIPTION IS THE MOST VALUABLE INFORMATION I HAVE. May I go through exactly what they told you?' Taking the history entirely from a patient WHO WAS UNCONSCIOUS FOR THE EVENT is a fail
What the witnesses describe

GENERALISED JERKING OF ARMS AND LEGS · UPWARD EYE DEVIATION · URINARY INCONTINENCE · POST-ICTAL CONFUSION AND DROWSINESS. Post-ictal confusion is typically 5–30 MINUTES; in SYNCOPE they are ORIENTATED WITHIN ABOUT A MINUTE
VERSION A — the classic recall
AT A PARTY. Remembers drinking CHAMPAGNE, CANNOT SAY HOW MUCH. 'I BLACKED OUT — I DON'T REMEMBER THE NIGHT.' Nil regular medications; denies recreational drugs BUT CANNOT VOUCH FOR LAST NIGHT
VERSION B — the online recall, and the only positive in the history
NO party. 'I'M NOT ALLOWED TO DRINK ALCOHOL.' No recreational drugs. TEMAZEPAM 10 mg NIGHTLY FOR ABOUT A YEAR for insomnia — RAN OUT AND HAS NOT TAKEN IT FOR TWO DAYS
THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES VERSION B

'DO YOU TAKE ANY REGULAR MEDICATIONS — AND HAVE YOU STOPPED, RUN OUT OF, OR MISSED ANY OF THEM RECENTLY?' ASK IT EVERY TIME. ABRUPT CESSATION OF A BENZODIAZEPINE, AN ANTIEPILEPTIC, BACLOFEN OR ALCOHOL ARE ALL SEIZURE TRIGGERS
THE DELIBERATE DISTRACTOR

TWO FEBRILE CONVULSIONS AS A YOUNG CHILD. Acknowledge it, record it, and EXPLICITLY SAY LATER that SIMPLE FEBRILE CONVULSIONS IN CHILDHOOD ONLY MODESTLY RAISE LATER RISK AND DO NOT EXPLAIN TODAY. Building an epilepsy diagnosis on two childhood febrile fits is a fail

WOKE LATE, MISSED BREAKFAST · NO head injury · NO fever · NO focal deficit · no early-morning headache or vomiting · no family history of epilepsy or sudden cardiac death
OFFER PRIVACY EARLY — one line, repeatedly rewarded

'Some of what I need to ask is QUITE PRIVATE. WOULD YOU PREFER TO TALK WITH ME ON YOUR OWN FOR A FEW MINUTES, and then we can bring your parents back in?' This unlocks an honest alcohol, drug and SAFETY history in Version A
THE HIDDEN SAFETY AGENDA in Version A

dx: **A GENERALISED TONIC-CLONIC SEIZURE — ALMOST CERTAINLY PROVOKED (ACUTE SYMPTOMATIC), NOT EPILEPSY. A SINGLE PROVOKED SEIZURE IS NOT A DIAGNOSIS OF EPILEPSY.** **EPILEPSY is TWO OR MORE UNPROVOKED seizures MORE THAN 24 HOURS APART, or ONE unprovoked seizure with a HIGH RECURRENCE RISK.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: COMMIT TO THE EVENT AND STAY HONEST ABOUT THE CAUSE. Candidates fail in TWO OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS — they either REFUSE TO SAY THE WORD 'SEIZURE' AND HEDGE EVERYTHING, or they SEIZE ON ONE TRIGGER AND PRESENT IT AS PROVEN.**

**The examiner wants A THIRD THING: A CONFIDENT DIAGNOSIS OF THE EVENT, A MOST-LIKELY TRIGGER OFFERED AS A PROBABILITY, AND A STRUCTURED DIFFERENTIAL THAT SHOWS YOU HAVE ACTIVELY EXCLUDED THE DANGEROUS CAUSES.**

**WHY THE STRUCTURE DOES NOT CHANGE: every question in the loss-of-consciousness structure EARNS ITS PLACE WHETHER THE EVENT TURNS OUT TO BE A SEIZURE OR A FAINT. 'Was it hot? Did you miss meals? Any warning? Any head injury? Any fever or rash?' are SIMULTANEOUSLY SYNCOPE QUESTIONS AND SEIZURE-CAUSE QUESTIONS.** **Candidates who switch to a memorised seizure list LOSE THE METABOLIC, CARDIAC AND ORTHOSTATIC SCREEN AND FAIL ON COMPLETENESS.**

**Explain the event in plain English: 'a seizure happens when there's A SHORT BURST OF ABNORMAL ELECTRICAL ACTIVITY IN THE BRAIN, A BIT LIKE A TEMPORARY ELECTRICAL STORM. IT STOPS ON ITS OWN, and you've recovered fully, WHICH IS REASSURING.'**

**VERSION A: 'I CAN'T PROVE WHICH SINGLE THING TRIGGERED IT, AND I WANT TO BE STRAIGHT WITH YOU ABOUT THAT. The most likely trigger is THE ALCOHOL — ANY AMOUNT OF ALCOHOL CAN LOWER THE BRAIN'S SEIZURE THRESHOLD, SO THIS ISN'T ABOUT HOW MUCH YOU DRANK. Two other things may have contributed: you can't remember part of the night, SO I CAN'T EXCLUDE SOMETHING YOU TOOK OR SOMETHING PUT IN YOUR DRINK; and you MISSED BREAKFAST.'**

**VERSION B: 'the most likely reason is that you STOPPED YOUR TEMAZEPAM TWO DAYS AGO. Tablets in that family cause the body to become PHYSICALLY DEPENDENT when taken every night for a long time, and stopping suddenly makes the body react — poor sleep, anxiety, tremor, and AT THE MORE SEVERE END, A SEIZURE. THAT IS NOT YOUR FAULT, AND IT'S VERY TREATABLE.'**

**THEN NAME WHAT YOU EXCLUDED: 'what I've looked for and NOT found today are the serious causes — A BRAIN INFECTION, BLEEDING IN THE BRAIN, A GROWTH, A SALT OR SUGAR PROBLEM, AND A HEART RHYTHM PROBLEM. Your examination, sugar and heart tracing are all normal.'**

**DRIVING, SOUTH AUSTRALIA: advise her NOT TO DRIVE AND DOCUMENT THAT YOU DID. Under Austroads a private driver is generally NOT FIT TO DRIVE FOR 6 MONTHS after a first seizure; where a CLEAR PROVOKING FACTOR has been identified and corrected, the period may be shortened ON SPECIALIST ADVICE. COMMERCIAL DRIVERS FAR LONGER.** **SA AND THE NT ARE THE ONLY TWO JURISDICTIONS WHERE THE TREATING DOCTOR ALSO HAS A LEGAL DUTY TO NOTIFY the Registrar; elsewhere it is DISCRETIONARY.** VERIFY.

**'How much alcohol does it take?' — ANY AMOUNT CAN, because alcohol LOWERS THE SEIZURE THRESHOLD; risk rises with quantity, and WITHDRAWAL AFTER HEAVY REGULAR USE IS A SEPARATE AND MORE DANGEROUS MECHANISM. DO NOT TELL A PATIENT THAT A SMALL AMOUNT IS SAFE.** **NHMRC: no more than 10 standard drinks a week and 4 on any day; one standard drink is 10 g.**
plan: **To the examiner before you sit: vitals INCLUDING A POSTURAL DROP, pulse rate AND RHYTHM, respiratory rate, saturation, temperature, BEDSIDE GLUCOSE AND GCS.**

**WIPE, confirm name and date of birth, CHECK SHE IS COMFORTABLE AND NOT IN PAIN.** Then **acknowledge and signpost: 'that must have been very frightening, for you AND FOR YOUR PARENTS. Let me ask you about the whole morning in detail, then about your general health.'**
**OFFER PRIVACY — one line, and it unlocks the rest of the history.**

**BLOCK 1, BEFORE: take me through the whole morning · WERE YOU STANDING, SITTING OR LYING DOWN · was the room hot, had you been standing a long time · DID YOU GET ANY WARNING — light-headed, sweaty, ringing in the ears, vision going grey · ANY ODD SMELL OR TASTE, A RISING FEELING IN YOUR TUMMY, OR DÉJÀ VU · any CHEST PAIN OR PALPITATIONS beforehand · WHEN DID YOU LAST EAT AND DRINK · any KNOCK TO THE HEAD · any FEVER, HEADACHE, NECK STIFFNESS OR RASH?**

**BLOCK 4, PREVIOUS EPISODES AND NEURO SCREEN: has anything like this happened before, EVEN A BRIEF BLANK SPELL OR JERK ON WAKING · ANY FITS AS A CHILD, WITH OR WITHOUT A FEVER · any headaches, ESPECIALLY EARLY MORNING OR ON COUGHING · VOMITING FIRST THING · blurred or double vision, slurred speech, weakness, numbness, unsteadiness · weight loss or night sweats?**
**BLOCK 5, SADMA BROUGHT FORWARD DELIBERATELY. THE MEDICATION QUESTION FIRST, IN BOTH HALVES.** Then **clarify dose, duration, WHY IT WAS STARTED, WHO PRESCRIBES IT, and any other sedatives.**

**Then, normalising it: 'a few questions now about alcohol, any drugs and your medications — I ASK EVERYONE THESE.' Do you drink · were you out last night, ROUGHLY HOW MUCH · IS THERE ANY CHANCE SOMETHING WAS PUT IN YOUR DRINK, OR THAT YOU TOOK SOMETHING YOU WEREN'T CERTAIN ABOUT · any recreational drugs, EVEN OCCASIONALLY · smoking · allergies?**

**BLOCK 6, PAST AND FAMILY HISTORY: diabetes, heart problems, epilepsy, mental health · previous head injury or brain surgery · IN THE FAMILY, EPILEPSY, OR ANYONE WHO DIED SUDDENLY AND UNEXPECTEDLY BEFORE 40?**

**SOCIAL IMPACT, and it is scored: DO YOU DRIVE · what do you do for work or study · DO YOU SWIM, OR WORK AT HEIGHTS · do you live alone · ANY CHILDREN IN YOUR CARE · IS THERE ANY CHANCE YOU COULD BE PREGNANT, WHEN WAS YOUR LAST PERIOD · is there anything you were particularly worried this might be?**
**Ask the examiner for the examination findings.**
**NAME THE EVENT CONFIDENTLY — 'what you had was A SEIZURE, a fit' — with the plain-English explanation.**
**GIVE THE TRIGGER AS A PROBABILITY, using the Version A or Version B script, and NAME THE CONTRIBUTORS rather than collapsing to one cause.**
**NAME WHAT YOU EXCLUDED and why that is reassuring.** Then **the structured differential: metabolic, drug-related, CNS infection, bleed or lesion, cardiac, psychogenic.**
**DRIVING, plainly and kindly, INCLUDING THE NOTIFICATION DUTY — and tell her YOU WILL HELP HER WITH THE PAPERWORK.**

**SAFETY-NETTING: no driving · NO SWIMMING, BATHING ALONE OR WORKING AT HEIGHTS until reviewed · SHOWER RATHER THAN BATHE · no machinery · SOMEONE SHOULD STAY WITH HER TONIGHT.** Then **FIRST-AID ADVICE FOR THE WITNESS: PROTECT THE HEAD, NOTHING IN THE MOUTH, RECOVERY POSITION, TIME IT, CALL 000 IF OVER 5 MINUTES.**
pefe: **Do now: ABC, recovery position, oxygen if hypoxic, IV access · BEDSIDE GLUCOSE, THE SINGLE MOST TIME-CRITICAL TEST · 12-LEAD ECG for QTc, DELTA WAVE, BLOCK · GCS, pupils, FOCAL DEFICIT, temperature · INJURY SURVEY: HEAD, TONGUE, SHOULDER, TEETH.**

**Do next: FBE, UEC, CMP with CALCIUM, MAGNESIUM AND PHOSPHATE, LFT, CRP, ETHANOL LEVEL, URINE DRUG SCREEN, BETA-hCG · CT BRAIN IF ANY RED FLAG · observe until back to baseline · REFER TO FIRST-SEIZURE CLINIC for outpatient EEG and MRI · DOCUMENT THE WITNESS ACCOUNT VERBATIM.**

**Red flags: seizure OVER 5 MINUTES or recurrent without recovery — STATUS · FAILURE TO RETURN TO BASELINE · FOCAL ONSET OR PERSISTENT FOCAL DEFICIT, since TODD'S PARESIS NEEDS IMAGING · fever, headache, neck stiffness, rash · head injury or anticoagulation · PREGNANCY OVER 20 WEEKS · FIRST SEIZURE OVER AGE 40 · onset while SUPINE or ON EXERTION with palpitations.**

**STATUS EPILEPTICUS — 5 MINUTES OR MORE continuous, or repeated seizures without recovery: airway, oxygen, IV access, glucose, TIME THE SEIZURE · MIDAZOLAM 10 mg IM, INTRANASAL OR BUCCAL, or 0.1 mg/kg IV, REPEAT ONCE AFTER 5 MINUTES · second line LEVETIRACETAM 40–60 mg/kg IV, MAX 3 g, or valproate, or PHENYTOIN 20 mg/kg IV WITH CARDIAC MONITORING · still seizing at 30 minutes → ANAESTHETICS AND ICU.** VERIFY.

**HYPOGLYCAEMIA: BGL below 4.0, severe below 2.8 — 50 mL of 50% GLUCOSE IV, or 15 g oral if conscious. IN SUSPECTED ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE OR MALNUTRITION, THIAMINE 100–300 mg IV BEFORE GLUCOSE.** **Hyponatraemia seizure risk rises BELOW ABOUT 125.**

**BENZODIAZEPINE WITHDRAWAL: RECOMMENCE TEMAZEPAM AT THE USUAL DOSE to stop the withdrawal, then a SLOW PLANNED TAPER with the regular GP — commonly 10–25% OF THE DOSE EVERY 1–2 WEEKS, adjusted to symptoms. NEVER STOP ABRUPTLY.** Address the underlying insomnia with **sleep hygiene and CBT-I.** VERIFY.

**Avoid: STARTING AN ANTIEPILEPTIC after a single provoked seizure · SODIUM VALPROATE IN A WOMAN OF CHILDBEARING POTENTIAL · LABELLING THIS 'EPILEPSY' · abruptly ceasing a benzodiazepine · GIVING GLUCOSE BEFORE THIAMINE in suspected alcohol dependence · DISCHARGING HER TO DRIVE HOME · a judgemental tone.** **If spiking is possible: offer YARROW PLACE, the SA statewide sexual assault service, and a social worker — NO EXAMINATION OR REPORTING WITHOUT HER CONSENT.**

stem: Jane, 25, brought in by ambulance after collapsing at work. The episode happened immediately after her manager accused her of shoplifting.
tasks: Take a history (6 minutes)
Explain your diagnosis and differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: NO PHYSICAL EXAMINATION IN THIS STATION

THAT ABSENCE IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT — IT SHAPES WHAT YOU ARE ENTITLED TO CONCLUDE. A generous SIX-MINUTE history window with the examination removed tells you the diagnosis LIVES ENTIRELY IN THE HISTORY and you are expected to EARN IT BY EXCLUDING EVERYTHING ELSE FIRST
TWO COMPLAINTS THE STRUCTURE HAS TO SURVIVE

'I DIDN'T LOSE CONSCIOUSNESS' normally sends you down the RECURRENT FALLS pathway. 'MY ARMS AND LEGS WERE SHAKING' normally sends you down the SEIZURE pathway. NEITHER PATHWAY FITS, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Stay in the syncope structure and LET THE CONTRADICTION ACCUMULATE
THE RECONFIRMING QUESTION — say it out loud

'Jane, CAN I JUST CHECK SOMETHING WITH YOU, BECAUSE IT'S IMPORTANT. You're telling me YOUR ARMS AND LEGS WERE SHAKING — BUT YOU WERE AWARE OF EVERYTHING THE WHOLE TIME, AND YOU CAN REMEMBER IT. IS THAT RIGHT?' → 'YES — I COULD HEAR THEM TALKING ABOUT ME AND CALLING THE AMBULANCE.' Recording the two answers separately, without reconfirming, IS A FAIL
THE FIVE FEATURES THAT MAKE THE DIAGNOSIS

1 CONSCIOUSNESS RETAINED THROUGHOUT · 2 BILATERAL JERKING OF ARMS AND LEGS AT THE SAME TIME · 3 NO TONGUE BITE, NO INCONTINENCE · 4 NO POSTICTAL CONFUSION, clear-headed immediately · 5 AN IMMEDIATE EMOTIONAL TRIGGER. POINTS 1 AND 2 TOGETHER ARE THE CRUX
The rest of the event

ABOUT 20–30 SECONDS · WITNESSED by her boss and colleagues · FIRST EPISODE EVER · arguing with her boss when it happened · NOT hot, NOT prolonged standing, NO change of position · NO pallor · NO injuries
THE HEAD INJURY QUESTION IS NOT A FORMALITY HERE

SHE COLLAPSED DURING A PHYSICAL CONFRONTATION WITH HER EMPLOYER. YOU DO NOT KNOW THAT NOBODY LAID HANDS ON HER. Asking about head injury and injuries sustained is A CLINICAL NECESSITY — and IT ALSO OPENS A DOOR IF THERE IS SOMETHING SHE HAS NOT FELT ABLE TO SAY
THE SPECIFIC PANIC QUESTION
'DURING THE EPISODE ITSELF — DID YOU FEEL FRIGHTENED THAT YOU WERE ABOUT TO DIE?' Her answer is NO, which ARGUES AGAINST A PANIC ATTACK. A YES WOULD HAVE REDIRECTED YOU
What she says that tests the station

'MY BOSS ACCUSED ME OF SHOPLIFTING. I DIDN'T DO IT.' And later, on hearing the diagnosis: 'ARE YOU SAYING I MADE IT UP? BECAUSE THAT'S WHAT MY BOSS THINKS TOO.' She may become TEARFUL — PAUSE, offer tissues, 'TAKE YOUR TIME'
Everything organic is NEGATIVE

No headache, visual change, slurred speech, weakness or numbness · no chest pain, palpitations, breathlessness or leg swelling · no nausea or vomiting · EATING AND DRINKING AS USUAL · no alcohol, drugs or medications taken or ceased · no fever or rash · no travel · NO personal or family history of seizures or sudden death
FURTHER SUPPORTING FEATURES, if you have time

LONGER DURATION than a typical convulsion · ASYNCHRONOUS OR OUT-OF-PHASE LIMB MOVEMENTS · SIDE-TO-SIDE HEAD SHAKING · WAXING-AND-WANING course · EYES HELD CLOSED WITH RESISTANCE TO OPENING, since epileptic seizures usually have the EYES OPEN · ICTAL CRYING · PRESERVED MEMORY. NONE IS INDIVIDUALLY DIAGNOSTIC
findingsLabel: No examination — the contradiction that is the diagnosis, and the accusation she fears
must: FAIL — An accusatory explanation: 'there's nothing physically wrong, it's not a real seizure.'
FAIL — Announcing psychogenic at two minutes with four minutes of history unused.
FAIL — Omitting the risk assessment for self-harm and harm to others.
FAIL — Taking a side on the shoplifting, or voicing malingering.
ASK — You were shaking, but aware the whole time — is that right?
ASK — Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself, or anyone else?

dx: **PSYCHOGENIC NON-EPILEPTIC SEIZURE — an episode that RESEMBLES an epileptic seizure but arises from PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS rather than ABNORMAL CORTICAL ELECTRICAL ACTIVITY.** **IT IS NOT DELIBERATE. This is NOT MALINGERING and NOT FACTITIOUS DISORDER. She is not producing it on purpose.**

**Terminology: also called a PSEUDOSEIZURE, and increasingly a FUNCTIONAL or DISSOCIATIVE seizure. USE 'PSYCHOGENIC' OR 'FUNCTIONAL' WITH THE PATIENT — 'PSEUDO' SOUNDS LIKE AN ACCUSATION OF PRETENDING.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE IS THE EXPLANATION, NOT THE DIAGNOSIS. Most candidates reach the right answer; FEWER DELIVER IT SAFELY.** **Consider where she is sitting: PUBLICLY ACCUSED OF STEALING, she denies it, and she is now in hospital. If your explanation lands as 'there's nothing physically wrong with you', SHE HEARS A SECOND ACCUSATION — that she FAKED A COLLAPSE TO ESCAPE THE FIRST ONE.** **That is why the AMC set this against a SHOPLIFTING allegation rather than any other stressor.**

**THE WORDS: 'what you had is a PSYCHOGENIC SEIZURE — sometimes called a FUNCTIONAL seizure. It looks very like an epileptic seizure, and YOUR ARMS AND LEGS REALLY WERE SHAKING — but it doesn't come from abnormal electrical activity in the brain, which is what epilepsy is. WHAT HAPPENED TO YOU WAS REAL. YOU WEREN'T PUTTING IT ON, AND YOU COULDN'T HAVE STOPPED IT.'**

**NEVER SAY: 'there's nothing wrong with you' · 'it's all in your head' · 'IT'S NOT A REAL SEIZURE' — clinically true but HEARD AS 'YOU FAKED IT' · 'you might have pretended' · 'pseudoseizure'. SAY 'NOT AN EPILEPTIC SEIZURE' RATHER THAN 'NOT A REAL SEIZURE' — ONE WORD, ENTIRELY DIFFERENT MEANING.**

**IF SHE CHALLENGES YOU: 'NO — I'M SAYING THE OPPOSITE. I BELIEVE WHAT HAPPENED TO YOU, and I don't think you had ANY CONTROL OVER IT. This is A RECOGNISED MEDICAL CONDITION WITH A NAME AND A TREATMENT. It's just that the treatment ISN'T EPILEPSY TABLETS — it's working with someone on the stress that set it off.'**

**PSYCHOGENIC IS A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION. Candidates who recognise the pattern at ninety seconds and jump straight to it SCORE BADLY — not because the answer is wrong, but because THEY HAVE EXCLUDED NOTHING.** **You still do not know whether her boss SHOVED HER before she went down, whether she is HYPOGLYCAEMIC, or whether she has an ARRHYTHMIA.**

**FRAME IT AS PROVISIONAL AND SAY WHY: a CONFIDENT SINGLE-VISIT DIAGNOSIS OF A FUNCTIONAL SEIZURE IS NOT SAFE PRACTICE. Name VIDEO-EEG as the definitive test, and acknowledge that EPILEPTIC AND PSYCHOGENIC SEIZURES COEXIST IN A MEANINGFUL MINORITY — ONE DIAGNOSIS DOES NOT EXCLUDE THE OTHER.**

**THE THREE FEATURES TO NAME EXPLICITLY: AWARENESS RETAINED DURING BILATERAL JERKING · NO POSTICTAL CONFUSION · AN IMMEDIATE EMOTIONAL TRIGGER. If you say nothing else about your reasoning, say these three — THEY ARE THE WHOLE ARGUMENT.**

**IF ASKED WHY NOT 'CONVERSION DISORDER': strictly, DSM-5 CLASSIFIES PSYCHOGENIC NON-EPILEPTIC SEIZURES WITHIN FUNCTIONAL NEUROLOGICAL SYMPTOM DISORDER (CONVERSION DISORDER), UNDER THE 'WITH ATTACKS OR SEIZURES' SPECIFIER — THESE ARE NOT COMPETING DIAGNOSES, ONE SITS INSIDE THE OTHER.** Safest answer: **'I'd call this a functional non-epileptic seizure. In DSM-5 terms that sits within functional neurological symptom disorder, but I'd want a neurological examination and ideally VIDEO-EEG before formalising the label — and FUNCTIONAL SEIZURE is the term I'd use with the patient.'**
plan: **To the examiner: 'could I please have the vital signs — blood pressure, pulse rate, respiratory rate and temperature?'**

**WIPE, then THE CONFIDENTIALITY STATEMENT BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it is what earns you the right to ask the risk question later: 'everything we discuss today STAYS BETWEEN YOU AND ME, UNLESS THERE'S A RISK OF HARM TO YOU OR SOMEONE ELSE. Is that alright?'**

**EMPATHY AND DELIBERATE NEUTRALITY ON THE ACCUSATION: 'that sounds like a horrible thing to have happen, and I'm sorry you've had such a distressing day. MY JOB HERE ISN'T TO SORT OUT WHAT HAPPENED AT WORK — IT'S TO WORK OUT WHY YOU COLLAPSED.'**

**BLOCK A, THE EVENT: did you lose consciousness COMPLETELY, or were you AWARE of your surroundings · DID ANYONE WITNESS IT · any JERKY MOVEMENTS of your arms or legs · did you BITE YOUR TONGUE, did you WET OR SOIL YOURSELF · HOW LONG DID IT LAST · IS THIS THE FIRST TIME · what were you doing IMMEDIATELY BEFORE · was it HOT, had you been STANDING a long time, any CHANGE OF POSITION?**
**THE RECONFIRMING QUESTION, said out loud, so the examiner sees you recognised the contradiction rather than simply recording two answers.**
**BLOCK B, BEFORE: any WARNING before it happened · MISSED MEALS, drinking normally · ANY HEAD INJURY BEFOREHAND · any FEVER OR RASH?**
**AFTER: when it stopped, WERE YOU CONFUSED OR CLEAR-HEADED · did anyone say you LOOKED PALE · DID YOU INJURE YOUR HEAD, OR ANYWHERE ELSE?**

**BLOCK C, ORGANIC EXCLUSION, SIGNPOSTED AND ASKED ONCE: 'for the next questions, tell me if you had it BEFORE this, AFTER it, or NOT AT ALL.' CNS: headache · blurred vision · slurred speech · weakness · numbness.**
**CVS AND RESPIRATORY: chest pain · racing heart · breathlessness · leg swelling · cough. GI: nausea · vomiting · abdominal pain.**

**DRUGS: alcohol · recreational drugs · ANY MEDICATIONS REGULARLY, OR RECENTLY STOPPED? THE ADDED THREE: long travel · weather preference · yellowing of the skin. PAST AND FAMILY HISTORY: any past medical history · FAMILY HISTORY OF SIMILAR EPISODES OR SUDDEN DEATH?**
**BLOCK D, THE PSYCHOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT — using the spare time the AMC gave you. HYPERVENTILATION: were you breathing fast just before it happened? Then THE SPECIFIC PANIC QUESTION.**

**MOOD AND FUNCTION, four questions and no more: how has your MOOD been lately · how's your SLEEP · and your APPETITE · ARE YOU STILL ENJOYING THE THINGS YOU NORMALLY ENJOY?** **Enough for a screen without turning this into a depression station.**

**PSYCHOSOCIAL: WHO DO YOU LIVE WITH · any stresses at home · TELL ME ABOUT WORK, HOW ARE THINGS THERE · any problems, any difficulties with anyone?** **Work is where the case lives.** For a 25-year-old, **frame it as a general screen — home, relationships, work, finances, substances, mood, safety — rather than HEADSS.**

**THE RISK QUESTION — DO NOT LEAVE THIS STATION WITHOUT IT: 'Jane, I ASK EVERYONE THIS and I'd like to check with you too — with everything that's happened today, HAVE YOU HAD ANY THOUGHTS OF HARMING YOURSELF, OR OF HARMING ANYONE ELSE?'** If positive, **explore IDEATION, PLAN, INTENT, MEANS, PREVIOUS ATTEMPTS AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS, and arrange SAME-DAY mental health assessment.** Also worth screening: **CURRENT OR PAST ABUSE OR TRAUMA, over-represented in functional seizures and which SHE MAY NEVER HAVE BEEN ASKED ABOUT.**
**DELIVER THE EXPLANATION using the scripted words — the condition, then 'WHAT HAPPENED TO YOU WAS REAL', then the mechanism in plain terms.**

**NAME THE THREE DECIDING FEATURES, then the differentials — EPILEPTIC SEIZURE INCLUDING FRONTAL LOBE FIRST, then other intracranial pathology, head injury during the altercation, arrhythmia and convulsive syncope, hypoglycaemia and electrolytes, drug or alcohol withdrawal, and panic attack.** **Say PROVISIONAL and name VIDEO-EEG.**

**If she challenges you, use the scripted reply.** Then **the plan: glucose and ECG, neurology referral, NO ANTIEPILEPTICS, psychological therapy, DRIVING ADVICE, and safety-netting with CRISIS CONTACT DETAILS BEFORE SHE LEAVES.**
pefe: **There is no examination in this station — but the bedside tests are still yours to name.**

**Do now: BEDSIDE GLUCOSE AND A 12-LEAD ECG WITH QTc — IN EVERY COLLAPSE, NO EXCEPTIONS · EUC with CALCIUM AND MAGNESIUM · FBC · BETA-hCG · assess for INJURY SUSTAINED during the episode · THE RISK ASSESSMENT.**

**Do next: NEUROLOGY REFERRAL AND EEG — VIDEO-EEG TELEMETRY IS THE DEFINITIVE TEST, capturing an event while recording brain activity · MRI BRAIN if any focal feature · REFERRAL FOR PSYCHOLOGICAL THERAPY, with CBT having the best evidence · screen for DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, TRAUMA AND ABUSE, all strongly associated · GP follow-up and a MENTAL HEALTH CARE PLAN.**
**THE EXPLANATION ITSELF IS THERAPEUTIC. A careful, believing explanation IMPROVES OUTCOMES; a dismissive one WORSENS THEM.**
**DO NOT START ANTIEPILEPTIC MEDICATION. People with functional seizures are FREQUENTLY TREATED WITH ANTICONVULSANTS FOR YEARS WITHOUT BENEFIT AND WITH REAL HARM.**

**Avoid: diagnosing MALINGERING — it requires CONSCIOUS INTENT, which you cannot establish and MUST NOT ASSUME, and it is NEVER a diagnosis to voice to the patient · TAKING A POSITION ON THE SHOPLIFTING · DISCHARGING WITHOUT EXCLUDING HYPOGLYCAEMIA AND AN ARRHYTHMIA.**

**DRIVING: she must not drive until assessed. ANY BLACKOUT, ANY CAUSE — including a functional seizure — falls under the AUSTROADS standard, with different periods for PRIVATE AND COMMERCIAL licences. In SA the authority is the REGISTRAR OF MOTOR VEHICLES and doctors carry a LEGAL DUTY TO NOTIFY where a patient is unfit and continues to drive.** Also: **no working at heights or with machinery, and no swimming alone, until reviewed.** **PATS for EEG and psychology travel; TELEHEALTH PSYCHOLOGY matters where local services are thin.**
