stem: A 70-year-old woman has come to see you about recurrent falls. Observations are normal.

Version B: on a 'fluid tablet' and a blood-pressure tablet 'ending in -sartan'; has depression and takes temazepam to sleep; 'numbness in my legs'. Version B2 (2024): on clonidine and a fluid tablet, recently changed by the GP, and amitriptyline instead of temazepam.
tasks: Take a relevant focused history
Ask the examiner for the relevant examination findings
Explain your diagnosis and differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: THE EXAMINATION IS NORMAL — AND THAT IS THE TEST

NORMAL POSTURAL BP · NORMAL SENSATION · NORMAL LOWER LIMBS. CANDIDATES GO QUIET BECAUSE THEY HAVE NOTHING LEFT TO SAY. A NORMAL EXAMINATION DOES NOT DELETE A SYMPTOM — the numbness she reports STILL COUNTS
VERSION B — what she gives you
'I HAVE NUMBNESS IN MY LEGS' · 'I'M ON A FLUID TABLET AND A BLOOD PRESSURE TABLET ENDING IN -SARTAN' · 'I HAVE DEPRESSION, AND I TAKE TEMAZEPAM TO SLEEP.' The risk-factor screen is otherwise negative
VERSION B2 — the 2024 swap

'I'M ON CLONIDINE AND A FLUID TABLET — THE GP CHANGED IT RECENTLY — AND AMITRIPTYLINE INSTEAD OF THE TEMAZEPAM.' IDENTICAL REASONING: BOTH NEW DRUGS CAUSE SEDATION AND POSTURAL HYPOTENSION. DO NOT BE THROWN
THE DRUG QUESTION MUST NAME THE CATEGORIES

'ANY MEDICATIONS?' → 'JUST MY BLOOD PRESSURE TABLETS.' ASK SPECIFICALLY ABOUT SLEEP, PAIN, AND ANYTHING FROM THE CHEMIST, or the temazepam never appears. Then NAME THE DRUG, THE DOSE, THE DURATION, AND WHO STARTED IT
POSTURAL HYPOTENSION STILL GETS NAMED — BUT SAY WHY

'Your blood pressure was steady WHEN WE MEASURED IT TODAY — but THAT DOESN'T RULE THE PROBLEM OUT, BECAUSE THE DROP IS INTERMITTENT, and you're on TWO TABLETS THAT LOWER BLOOD PRESSURE. At home, getting up quickly first thing, IT CAN FALL FURTHER THAN IT DID HERE.' ASSERTING IT WITHOUT THE REASON SCORES NOTHING
THE BENZODIAZEPINE IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE ITEM

'TEMAZEPAM WORKS, BUT IT STAYS IN THE SYSTEM OVERNIGHT AND LEAVES YOU DROWSY AND SLOWER TO REACT — IN SOMEONE YOUR AGE IT ROUGHLY DOUBLES THE CHANCE OF A FALL.' REDUCE SLOWLY RATHER THAN STOP SUDDENLY
NEVER STOP CLONIDINE ABRUPTLY
REBOUND HYPERTENSION. In Version B2 this is the single pharmacological trap
AMITRIPTYLINE IN AN OLDER FALLER
DROWSINESS, POSTURAL DROP AND ANTICHOLINERGIC EFFECTS — a poor choice. SAY YOU WOULD REVIEW THE INDICATION WITH HER DOCTOR RATHER THAN CEASE IT YOURSELF
THE FOURTH CAUSE IS THE MOOD ITSELF

'YOUR MOOD AND YOUR SLEEP ARE TIED TOGETHER — IF THE DEPRESSION ISN'T WELL CONTROLLED YOU'RE AWAKE AT NIGHT AND DROWSY BY DAY, AND THAT ADDS TO THE FALLS.' Screen mood, sleep, AND ask a safe suicide-risk question
THE THIAZIDE HAS A SECOND CONSEQUENCE
THIAZIDES CAUSE HYPONATRAEMIA. Check UEC — a low sodium is its own falls mechanism and is easy to miss when the story is about blood pressure
findingsLabel: Versions B and B2 — a normal card, and the drug list that explains everything
must: FAIL — Going quiet because the examination is normal.
FAIL — 'Any medications?' answered as blood pressure tablets only, and the sleeping tablet never found.
FAIL — Naming one cause. One tidy label is the commonest way to fail this station.
FAIL — Ceasing clonidine abruptly, or stopping the amitriptyline yourself.
ASK — Any medicines at all, including anything for sleep, for pain, or over the counter?
ASK — Did you hurt yourself? Could you get yourself up?

dx: **MULTIFACTORIAL RECURRENT FALLS, MEDICATION-DRIVEN. Name FOUR: POSTURAL HYPOTENSION from two blood-pressure-lowering agents · BENZODIAZEPINE (or TRICYCLIC) SEDATION · THE LEG SYMPTOMS SHE REPORTS · and POORLY CONTROLLED MOOD AND SLEEP.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE EXAMINATION IS NORMAL, AND YOU MUST STILL NAME POSTURAL HYPOTENSION AND THE SYMPTOM SHE REPORTED. Candidates GO QUIET WHEN THE EXAMINER SAYS 'EXAMINATION IS NORMAL' BECAUSE THEY HAVE NOTHING LEFT TO SAY.**

**A NORMAL EXAMINATION DOES NOT ERASE A SYMPTOM. Say it out loud: 'ALTHOUGH THE TESTING OF THE NERVES IN YOUR LEGS CAME BACK NORMAL, THE FACT THAT YOU FEEL NUMBNESS IN THEM IS ITSELF SOMETHING THAT MAKES FALLS MORE LIKELY, SO I'M NOT DISMISSING IT. I'll CHECK YOUR B12 AND YOUR SUGAR.'**

**POSTURAL HYPOTENSION WITH A NORMAL TEST IS DEFENSIBLE — BUT ONLY WITH ITS REASON. A SYSTOLIC DROP UNDER 20 mmHg MAKES IT LESS LIKELY BUT DOES NOT EXCLUDE IT, BECAUSE IT IS INTERMITTENT AND DRUG-RELATED. Say why; do not just assert it.**

**THE BENZODIAZEPINE LINE: 'temazepam works, BUT IT STAYS IN THE SYSTEM OVERNIGHT AND LEAVES YOU DROWSY AND SLOWER TO REACT — IN SOMEONE YOUR AGE IT ROUGHLY DOUBLES THE CHANCE OF A FALL. I'd like to REDUCE IT SLOWLY RATHER THAN STOP IT SUDDENLY, AND WORK ON YOUR SLEEP ANOTHER WAY.'**

**VERSION B2 PHARMACOLOGY, AND THE TRAP: NEVER STOP CLONIDINE ABRUPTLY — REBOUND HYPERTENSION.** **AMITRIPTYLINE IS ANTICHOLINERGIC AND ORTHOSTATIC and is relatively contraindicated in an elderly faller: 'I'd REVIEW THE INDICATION WITH HER GP OR PSYCHIATRIST RATHER THAN STOP IT ABRUPTLY.'**

**SOURCE CORRECTION — the source says tricyclics are no longer used in Australia and mirtazapine is used instead. THAT OVERSTATES IT. AUSTRALIAN FIRST-LINE PHARMACOTHERAPY IS AN SSRI; MIRTAZAPINE IS CHOSEN WHEN SEDATION OR APPETITE STIMULATION IS WANTED; TRICYCLICS ARE STILL USED, MOSTLY FOR NEUROPATHIC PAIN AND MIGRAINE PROPHYLAXIS.**
**THE THIAZIDE'S SECOND CONSEQUENCE IS HYPONATRAEMIA — check UEC. A LOW SODIUM IS ITS OWN FALLS MECHANISM and is easy to miss when the conversation is about blood pressure.**

**THE FRAME, AS ALWAYS: 'falls at your age ALMOST NEVER COME FROM ONE SINGLE THING — they're SEVERAL SMALL THINGS STACKING UP, and that's GOOD NEWS BECAUSE EACH ONE IS FIXABLE. I'VE FOUND FOUR.'** Then **each cause in plain English, the medical name once, and the link to the falls.**

**MANAGEMENT IS DEPRESCRIBING, NOT ADDING: HOME MEDICINES REVIEW · taper the benzodiazepine · REDUCE OR STAGGER THE ANTIHYPERTENSIVES · substitute the TCA · and NEVER ADD A SEDATIVE FOR 'BETTER SLEEP'.** **Then BALANCE-CHALLENGING EXERCISE, which is the SINGLE BEST-EVIDENCED INTERVENTION, plus OT home assessment, optometry, and bone health.**

**THE FOURTH CAUSE — MOOD AND SLEEP TIED TOGETHER — and an offer to review it properly.**

stem: A 77-year-old man has come to see you about recurrent falls; the most recent happened while he was working in the garden. Observations are normal.
tasks: Take a relevant focused history
Ask the examiner for the relevant examination findings
Explain your diagnosis and differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: THE EXAMINATION CARD IS ENTIRELY NORMAL

NO POSTURAL DROP · CARDIOVASCULAR NORMAL · NEUROLOGICAL NORMAL · MUSCULOSKELETAL NORMAL · GLUCOSE NORMAL. A COMPLETELY NORMAL EXAMINATION IS EXACTLY WHAT A RESOLVED TIA LOOKS LIKE. IT IS NOT REASSURANCE
THE SENTENCE THE WHOLE STATION TURNS ON

'THE LAST ONE HAPPENED IN THE GARDEN. MY VISION BLURRED JUST BEFORE I FELL, AND FOR A BIT AFTERWARDS.' Filing transient visual blurring under 'dizziness' AND REASSURING HIM BECAUSE EVERYTHING IS NORMAL IS THE AUTOMATIC FAIL
The three falls are three different mechanisms

ONE WAS A TRIP · ONE HAPPENED ON STANDING · ONE IN THE GARDEN WITH THE VISUAL BLURRING. ASK HIM TO TALK YOU THROUGH EACH ONE SEPARATELY — a generic 'what happened?' gets a generic answer and the garden fall never separates out
What he says that sounds reassuring and is not

'NO CHEST PAIN, NO SWEATING — I JUST FELT COLD' · 'NO, I NEVER BLACKED OUT.' Absent chest pain DOES NOT EXCLUDE A CARDIAC CAUSE FOR A FALL DURING EXERTION, and absent LOC does not make a transient neurological event benign
CHASE THE VISUAL SYMPTOM — five questions

HOW LONG DID IT LAST · ONE EYE OR BOTH · WAS IT BLURRING, OR LOSS OF PART OF THE FIELD, OR A CURTAIN COMING DOWN · ANY SLURRED SPEECH, FACIAL DROOP OR ARM WEAKNESS AT THE SAME TIME · HAS IT HAPPENED BEFORE, EVEN BRIEFLY?
A FALL DURING EXERTION IS A SECOND RED FLAG
He was ACTIVE IN THE GARDEN. EXERTIONAL COLLAPSE ALWAYS RAISES THE HEART — aortic stenosis, arrhythmia, ischaemia — SO ASK FOR THE MURMUR BY NAME AND ORDER THE ECG
The risk-factor screen is otherwise NEGATIVE
NO PAST HISTORY · NO MEDICATIONS · the six domains empty. THAT EMPTINESS IS NOT A REASON TO RELAX — it is what leaves the visual symptom standing alone as the finding
THIS IS A TODAY PROBLEM, NOT A NEXT-WEEK ONE
'IT HAS RECOVERED COMPLETELY, WHICH IS WHY EVERYTHING IS NORMAL NOW, BUT IT IS A WARNING SIGN, AND I WANT YOU ASSESSED TODAY, NOT NEXT WEEK'
DRIVING IS A SEPARATE MARK AND IT IS ROUTINELY DROPPED

AFTER A SUSPECTED TIA, NO PRIVATE DRIVING FOR AT LEAST TWO WEEKS, FOUR WEEKS COMMERCIAL, under Austroads. IN SA AND THE NT THE DOCTOR ALSO HAS A LEGAL DUTY TO REPORT AN UNFIT DRIVER — TELL HIM BEFORE YOU REPORT
STILL NAME THE THIRD CAUSE
ONE FALL HAPPENED AS HE STOOD UP, SO POSTURAL HYPOTENSION REMAINS PART OF THE PICTURE EVEN WITH A NORMAL POSTURAL BP TODAY — THE DROP IS INTERMITTENT. Three falls, three named mechanisms
findingsLabel: Version D — a normal card, and the one sentence that changes the hour
must: FAIL — Filing the transient visual blurring under 'dizziness' and reassuring him.
FAIL — Reassuring because the examination is normal. That is what a resolved TIA looks like.
FAIL — Not asking him to describe each fall separately, so the garden fall never separates out.
FAIL — No driving advice after a suspected TIA.
ASK — How long did the blurring last, one eye or both?
ASK — Any slurred speech, facial droop or arm weakness at the same time?

dx: **TRANSIENT ISCHAEMIC ATTACK — LEAD WITH THIS. Then a CARDIAC CAUSE for the fall during exertion, and POSTURAL HYPOTENSION for the fall on standing. THREE FALLS, THREE NAMED MECHANISMS.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: ESCALATING RATHER THAN REASSURING. THE VISUAL BLURRING IS THE WHOLE STATION.** **A COMPLETELY NORMAL EXAMINATION IS EXACTLY WHAT A RESOLVED TIA LOOKS LIKE — the normality is the expected finding, not the answer.**

**THE SCRIPT: 'the MOST IMPORTANT THING YOU'VE TOLD ME is the BLURRING OF YOUR VISION AROUND THE TIME OF THAT FALL. That may have been A BRIEF INTERRUPTION TO THE BLOOD SUPPLY OF PART OF THE BRAIN — A MINI-STROKE, or a TRANSIENT ISCHAEMIC ATTACK. It has RECOVERED COMPLETELY, which is why everything is normal now, BUT IT IS A WARNING SIGN, AND I WANT YOU ASSESSED TODAY, NOT NEXT WEEK.'**

**THEN THE SECOND: 'the second thing is YOUR HEART. YOU FELL WHILE YOU WERE ACTIVE IN THE GARDEN — A FALL DURING EXERTION ALWAYS MAKES ME THINK ABOUT THE HEART, so I want that tracing and possibly AN ULTRASOUND OF THE HEART.'**

**AND THE THIRD: 'one of your falls happened AS YOU STOOD UP, so A DROP IN BLOOD PRESSURE ON STANDING is likely part of the picture too.'** **A normal postural BP today does not exclude it — THE DROP IS INTERMITTENT.**

**THEN THE DRIVING, AND SAY YOU ARE SORRY TO HAVE TO: 'PLEASE DON'T DRIVE FOR NOW. After a suspected mini-stroke THE NATIONAL RULES SAY AT LEAST TWO WEEKS OFF THE ROAD, and WE'LL REVIEW IT TOGETHER.'**

**CHASE THE VISUAL SYMPTOM RATHER THAN RECORDING IT: DURATION · ONE EYE OR BOTH · BLURRING VERSUS FIELD LOSS VERSUS A CURTAIN DESCENDING · ACCOMPANYING SPEECH, FACE OR ARM SYMPTOMS · PREVIOUS EPISODES.** **AMAUROSIS FUGAX — a curtain over one eye — points to the CAROTID CIRCULATION and makes carotid imaging urgent.**

**ABSENT CHEST PAIN DOES NOT EXCLUDE A CARDIAC CAUSE. 'No chest pain, no sweating, I just felt cold' IS NOT REASSURANCE IN A 77-YEAR-OLD WHO COLLAPSED DURING EXERTION — ASK FOR THE MURMUR OF AORTIC STENOSIS BY NAME AND GET AN ECG.**

**THE EMPTY RISK-FACTOR SCREEN IS NOT A REASON TO RELAX. No past history and no medications is precisely what LEAVES THE VISUAL SYMPTOM STANDING ALONE AS THE FINDING — and it means you have nothing else to blame the falls on.**
**FRAME IT AS ALWAYS: 'falls at your age ALMOST NEVER COME FROM ONE SINGLE THING.' But HERE THE ORDER MATTERS — THE TIA GOES FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES WHAT HAPPENS IN THE NEXT HOUR.**
plan: **Say the observations out loud, WIPE, open question, acknowledge.** Then **SIGNPOST THE LONG LIST and ask the agenda question.**
**FALL OR FAINT: did you BLACK OUT, EVEN FOR A SECOND · do you REMEMBER HITTING THE GROUND · any SHAKING OR JERKING, TONGUE BITING, WETTING YOURSELF?**

**CHARACTERISE, AND INSIST ON EACH ONE SEPARATELY: HOW MANY FALLS AND WHEN DID THEY START · TALK ME THROUGH EACH ONE — WHAT WERE YOU DOING AT THE TIME · DID YOU HURT YOURSELF · COULD YOU GET YOURSELF UP?**

**When the garden fall and the visual blurring appear, STOP AND CHASE IT: HOW LONG DID IT LAST · ONE EYE OR BOTH · WAS IT BLURRING, LOSS OF PART OF THE FIELD, OR A CURTAIN COMING DOWN · ANY SLURRED SPEECH, FACIAL DROOP OR ARM WEAKNESS AT THE SAME TIME · HAS ANYTHING LIKE IT HAPPENED BEFORE, EVEN BRIEFLY?**
**THE REST OF THE CNS SCREEN: any weakness or numbness anywhere · trouble swallowing · unsteadiness or veering to one side · headache · any SPINNING sensation?**

**CVS — AND THE EXERTIONAL FALL MAKES THIS MANDATORY: any CHEST PAIN OR TIGHTNESS · PALPITATIONS · more BREATHLESS THAN USUAL, OR WORSE ON EXERTION · ankle swelling · any FAMILY HISTORY OF SUDDEN DEATH?**

**GI and meals: vomiting, diarrhoea, BLACK OR BLOODY MOTIONS · are you EATING REGULARLY?** Then **VASCULAR RISK FACTORS: blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, SMOKING, previous stroke or heart trouble.**
**PAST HISTORY with the four questions, then MEDICATIONS INCLUDING ANYTHING FOR SLEEP, PAIN OR FROM THE CHEMIST — AND SPECIFICALLY ANY BLOOD THINNERS — and allergies.**

**THE SIX RISK DOMAINS IN ORDER, quickly since they are negative: HOME lighting and hazards · URINARY frequency, urgency, nocturia · MSK joints, balance, feet, FOOTWEAR · SENSES eyes and hearing last checked, BIFOCALS · DRUGS · ALCOHOL, QUANTIFIED.**
**GERIATRIC AND SOCIAL SCREEN: who's at home · who helps · meals · function · memory · mood · weight loss · STILL DRIVING · AFRAID TO MOVE ABOUT SINCE THE FALLS?**
**HARD STOP ON HISTORY. SADMA and family history of stroke and cardiac disease.**

**ASK THE EXAMINER IN ORDER: general appearance, hydration, bruising or injury · GAIT AND TIMED UP AND GO · vitals with LYING AND STANDING BP AT ONE AND THREE MINUTES and PULSE RHYTHM · BEDSIDE GLUCOSE.**

**Then THE NEUROLOGICAL EXAMINATION IN FULL — cranial nerves, VISUAL FIELDS AND VISUAL ACUITY, FUNDOSCOPY, limbs, sensation, coordination, Romberg · CAROTID BRUITS BY NAME · cardiovascular for A MURMUR OF AORTIC STENOSIS and the PULSE RHYTHM FOR AF · lower limb joints and footwear · abdomen and dipstick.**
**LEAD WITH THE TIA, in plain words, with the 'today not next week' line.**
**THEN THE HEART, because of the exertional fall — and THEN the postural drop for the fall on standing. THREE FALLS, THREE MECHANISMS.**
**THE PLAN: ASPIRIN NOW unless contraindicated · URGENT SCAN OF THE BRAIN AND THE VESSELS IN THE NECK · A TRACING OF THE HEART and possibly an echocardiogram · BLOOD TESTS.**
**DRIVING, with the apology and the reason.** Then **RED FLAGS — if any weakness, speech trouble or visual loss comes back and STAYS, CALL AN AMBULANCE — a REVIEW DATE, and TEACH-BACK.**
pefe: **Do now: ASPIRIN 300 mg STAT unless contraindicated · lying and standing BP at 1 and 3 minutes · BEDSIDE GLUCOSE · AN ECG IN EVERY FALLS PATIENT, AND HERE SPECIFICALLY FOR ATRIAL FIBRILLATION · blood pressure recorded properly · injury survey.**

**URGENT SAME-DAY TIA PATHWAY: CT OR CT ANGIOGRAPHY OF THE BRAIN AND NECK VESSELS · CAROTID IMAGING · ECG with HOLTER IF PAROXYSMAL AF IS SUSPECTED · ECHOCARDIOGRAM given the exertional fall · FBE, UEC, LIPIDS, HbA1c, COAGULATION.**
**MRI is more sensitive than CT for posterior circulation events — say so if the visual symptom suggests a vertebrobasilar territory.**

**Do not miss: TIA ITSELF, where the normal examination is the expected finding · ATRIAL FIBRILLATION behind an embolic event · CAROTID STENOSIS, where AMAUROSIS FUGAX makes imaging urgent · AORTIC STENOSIS OR ARRHYTHMIA behind the exertional fall · GIANT CELL ARTERITIS if there is headache, scalp tenderness or jaw claudication with the visual symptom · SUBDURAL after any head strike.**

**Avoid: REASSURING BECAUSE THE EXAMINATION IS NORMAL · calling the visual blurring 'dizziness' · SENDING HIM HOME TO SEE HOW HE GOES · omitting the driving advice · discharging without addressing BONE HEALTH.**

**DRIVING: after a suspected TIA, NO PRIVATE DRIVING FOR AT LEAST TWO WEEKS, FOUR WEEKS COMMERCIAL, under Austroads Assessing Fitness to Drive.** **SA AND THE NT ARE THE JURISDICTIONS WHERE THE DOCTOR HAS A LEGAL DUTY TO REPORT an unfit driver to the Registrar of Motor Vehicles; elsewhere it is discretionary. TELL THE PATIENT BEFORE YOU REPORT.** VERIFY.

**Then the rest of the falls plan, unchanged: BALANCE-CHALLENGING EXERCISE, OT HOME HAZARD ASSESSMENT, OPTOMETRY, BONE HEALTH AND DXA, MY AGED CARE 1800 200 422, and REVIEW.** **Secondary prevention once confirmed: antiplatelet or anticoagulation depending on AF, a STATIN, and BLOOD PRESSURE CONTROL.**

stem: A 72-year-old woman has come to see you about recurrent falls. She has hypertension on a 'fluid tablet' and was diagnosed with polymyalgia rheumatica six months ago, taking prednisolone as prescribed under specialist follow-up. She gets up at night to pass urine. Observations are normal.
tasks: Take a relevant focused history
Ask the examiner for the relevant examination findings
Explain your diagnosis and differential diagnoses to the patient
Name the one investigation you would order
findings: FOUR TASKS — the fourth is one named investigation
History · examination findings · diagnosis and differentials · AND ONE INVESTIGATION. Budget for it: running out of time before the fourth task loses a whole domain
The examination card
NO POSTURAL DROP · CARDIOVASCULAR NORMAL · MUSCULOSKELETAL NORMAL · NEUROLOGICAL NORMAL · URINE DIPSTICK POSITIVE FOR GLUCOSE. ONE POSITIVE ON THE WHOLE CARD, AND IT IS THE DIPSTICK
What she gives you

'I'VE GOT HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE, ON A FLUID TABLET' · 'I WAS DIAGNOSED WITH POLYMYALGIA RHEUMATICA SIX MONTHS AGO AND I TAKE STEROIDS — YES, I TAKE THEM PROPERLY, AND I SEE THE SPECIALIST' · 'NO SHOULDER OR HIP PAIN AT THE MOMENT' · 'I DO GET UP AT NIGHT TO PASS URINE'
THE GLYCOSURIA HAS TWO READINGS

IT CAN MEAN DIABETES, OR IT CAN BE A SIDE EFFECT OF THE STEROID — STEROIDS PUSH THE SUGAR UP. Either way, OVER TIME HIGH SUGARS AFFECT THE EYES AND THE NERVES IN THE LEGS, AND BOTH OF THOSE CAUSE FALLS. Her examination is clear TODAY, which is good, BUT YOU STILL TEST FOR IT
THE DISCRIMINATOR NOBODY VOLUNTEERS

POLYMYALGIA RHEUMATICA IS ASSOCIATED WITH GIANT CELL ARTERITIS. ASK BY NAME: ANY NEW HEADACHE · ANY SCALP TENDERNESS WHEN YOU BRUSH YOUR HAIR · ANY JAW ACHE WHEN CHEWING · ANY LOSS OR BLURRING OF VISION. Then SAFETY-NET THEM: 'RING ME THE SAME DAY IF ANY OF THOSE START'
PMR AFFECTS FALLS EVEN WITHOUT CURRENT PAIN
POLYMYALGIA CAUSES STIFFNESS AND PAIN IN THE HIPS AND SHOULDERS, WHICH MAKES WALKING LESS STEADY AND RISING FROM A CHAIR HARDER. 'No pain at the moment' on treatment DOES NOT DELETE THE MECHANISM
THE THIAZIDE STAYS ON THE LIST
'YOUR FLUID TABLET CAN DROP YOUR BLOOD PRESSURE WHEN YOU STAND. IT MEASURED NORMALLY TODAY, BUT THAT DROP COMES AND GOES, SO IT STAYS ON THE LIST.' Assert it WITH the reason, never without
THE FOURTH CAUSE IS THE SITUATION
SHE IS GETTING UP AT NIGHT TO PASS URINE, IN THE DARK, STILL HALF ASLEEP. THAT ALONE CAUSES FALLS — and it is the easiest of the four to fix. Nocturia on a diuretic is a mechanism, not a detail
THE STEROID HAS A SECOND FALLS CONSEQUENCE
LONG-TERM CORTICOSTEROIDS CAUSE PROXIMAL MYOPATHY AND ACCELERATE BONE LOSS. A FALLER ON SIX MONTHS OF PREDNISOLONE NEEDS BONE PROTECTION ASSESSED, NOT JUST A FALLS PLAN
The trap in the explanation
CALLING THE WHOLE CASE 'A SIDE EFFECT OF STEROIDS' AND STOPPING. BUILD THE LIST FROM THE HISTORY INSTEAD — four causes, each tied to something she told you
findingsLabel: Version E — one positive on the card, and the association nobody volunteers
must: FAIL — Calling the whole case a steroid side effect and stopping there.
FAIL — Missing that PMR is associated with giant cell arteritis.
FAIL — Going quiet because the examination is normal apart from the dipstick.
FAIL — Running out of time and never naming the one investigation.
ASK — Any new headache, scalp tenderness, or jaw ache when chewing?
ASK — Any loss or blurring of your vision?

dx: **MULTIFACTORIAL RECURRENT FALLS. FOUR CAUSES: THIAZIDE-RELATED POSTURAL HYPOTENSION · STEROID-INDUCED HYPERGLYCAEMIA OR NEW DIABETES · PMR HIP AND SHOULDER STIFFNESS, WITH THE GIANT CELL ARTERITIS VISUAL RISK ALONGSIDE IT · AND NOCTURIA IN THE DARK.**
**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: HAVING SOMETHING TO SAY WHEN THERE IS ALMOST NOTHING POSITIVE. BUILD THE LIST FROM THE HISTORY, NOT FROM THE CARD.**

**THE SECOND DISCRIMINATOR: POLYMYALGIA RHEUMATICA IS ASSOCIATED WITH GIANT CELL ARTERITIS. MENTIONING HEADACHE, JAW CLAUDICATION AND VISUAL LOSS — AND SAFETY-NETTING THEM — IS WHAT SEPARATES THIS ANSWER.**

**THE SCRIPT: 'there ISN'T ONE SINGLE ANSWER HERE, so let me tell you THE THINGS THAT ADD UP. ONE: your FLUID TABLET CAN DROP YOUR BLOOD PRESSURE WHEN YOU STAND. It measured normally today, BUT THAT DROP COMES AND GOES, SO IT STAYS ON THE LIST.'**

**'TWO: there's SUGAR IN YOUR URINE. That can mean DIABETES, or it can be A SIDE EFFECT OF THE STEROID — STEROIDS PUSH THE SUGAR UP. Over time HIGH SUGARS AFFECT THE EYES AND THE NERVES IN THE LEGS, and BOTH OF THOSE CAUSE FALLS. Your examination is clear today, which is good, BUT I WANT TO TEST FOR IT.'**

**'THREE: POLYMYALGIA RHEUMATICA CAUSES STIFFNESS AND PAIN IN THE HIPS AND SHOULDERS, WHICH MAKES WALKING LESS STEADY. **'FOUR: you're GETTING UP AT NIGHT TO PASS URINE, IN THE DARK, STILL HALF ASLEEP. THAT ALONE CAUSES FALLS' — and it is the easiest of the four to fix.**

**THE FOURTH TASK, ANSWERED PRECISELY: 'the one investigation I would do is an HbA1c, which tells us THE AVERAGE BLOOD SUGAR OVER THE LAST THREE MONTHS. If the task means AN OFFICE TEST rather than a formal investigation, then A RANDOM CAPILLARY BLOOD GLUCOSE HERE IN THE CLINIC, and I'd follow it with A FASTING GLUCOSE OR HbA1c.'**

**THE STEROID HAS A SECOND FALLS CONSEQUENCE NOBODY MENTIONS: LONG-TERM CORTICOSTEROIDS CAUSE PROXIMAL MYOPATHY AND ACCELERATE BONE LOSS. A faller on six months of prednisolone needs BONE PROTECTION ASSESSED — DXA, CALCIUM AND VITAMIN D, AND ANTIRESORPTIVE THERAPY WHERE INDICATED.**
**THIAZIDES ALSO CAUSE HYPONATRAEMIA — check UEC. A LOW SODIUM IS ITS OWN FALLS MECHANISM and is easy to miss when the conversation is about the sugar.**

**THE GCA SAFETY-NET, SPELLED OUT AND SAME-DAY.** Then **the other red flags, a REVIEW DATE, and TEACH-BACK: 'can you tell me back the two things you'll change tonight, and the symptoms you'd ring me about?'**

tasks: Take a history from the patient (4 minutes)
Ask the examiner for the physical examination findings — given only if you name them specifically
Explain your diagnosis and your differentials to the patient
findings: YOU ARE TOLD ONLY WHAT YOU NAME

THE KNEES AND THE FUNDI ARE THE TWO FINDINGS THAT SEPARATE A PASS FROM A FAIL — AND YOU ARE TOLD NEITHER UNLESS YOU ASK FOR THEM BY NAME. 'NEUROLOGICAL EXAMINATION' WILL NOT GET YOU THE FUNDI; 'LOWER LIMB EXAMINATION' WILL NOT GET YOU THE KNEE JOINTS
What the examiner gives on request

Alert, no pallor · VITALS NORMAL, NO POSTURAL DROP · pulse regular · FUNDOSCOPY: DIABETIC RETINOPATHY · VISUAL ACUITY REDUCED · power normal, BILATERAL GLOVE-AND-STOCKING SENSORY LOSS · CVS and respiratory normal · TENDERNESS IN BOTH KNEE JOINTS · REDUCED RANGE OF MOVEMENT BILATERALLY · TIMED UP AND GO PROLONGED · RANDOM GLUCOSE 15 · glycosuria · ECG sinus
HE NEVER VOLUNTEERS THE RETINOPATHY — YOU FIND IT
He mentions blurry vision if asked. THE RETINOPATHY ITSELF ONLY APPEARS IF YOU REQUEST FUNDOSCOPY AND VISUAL ACUITY EXPLICITLY
THE FORK, ASKED FIRST

'WHEN YOU FALL, DO YOU LOSE CONSCIOUSNESS, OR ARE YOU STILL AWARE OF YOUR SURROUNDINGS?' → 'I'M ALWAYS AWARE.' SAY THE ANSWER OUT LOUD SO THE EXAMINER HEARS YOU BRANCH: 'SO THESE ARE FALLS RATHER THAN BLACKOUTS'
THE PATTERN, NOT JUST THE ANSWERS

THREE FALLS IN THREE UNRELATED SETTINGS — walking in the living room, gardening, slipping getting out of bed — WITH NO POSITIONAL OR ACTIVITY TRIGGER. THAT IS THE SIGNATURE OF MULTIPLE ACCUMULATED RISK FACTORS RATHER THAN A SINGLE MECHANISM. Falls that ALL happen on standing point at postural hypotension instead
THE CONCERN HE OPENS WITH

'WHAT IF I FALL AND THERE'S NO ONE THERE TO HELP ME?' ACKNOWLEDGE IT ONCE, WARMLY, AND MOVE — then ANSWER IT CONCRETELY AT THE END with a PERSONAL ALARM, a CHECK-IN ARRANGEMENT, and A PLAN FOR WHAT TO DO IF HE CANNOT GET UP
THE FOUR DIABETES QUESTIONS deliver two diagnoses in thirty seconds

WHEN DIAGNOSED — eight or nine years ago · WHAT TREATMENT — metformin · ARE YOU TAKING IT REGULARLY — 'ONLY WHEN I REMEMBER' · REGULAR FOLLOW-UP AND BLOODS — NO · ANY COMPLICATIONS — THE NUMBNESS AND THE BLURRED VISION

'THERE WAS NO POSTURAL DROP, AND NO POSITIONAL TRIGGER IN THE HISTORY, SO ORTHOSTATIC HYPOTENSION IS UNLIKELY HERE.' It shows you ACTIVELY EXCLUDED THE COMMONEST REVERSIBLE CAUSE rather than never considering it

dx: **MULTIFACTORIAL RECURRENT FALLS WITH THREE CONTRIBUTORS: DIABETIC SENSORY (PERIPHERAL) NEUROPATHY · OSTEOARTHRITIS OF BOTH KNEES · DIABETIC RETINOPATHY — all on a background of UNCONTROLLED TYPE 2 DIABETES.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: WHETHER YOU COMBINE YOUR FINDINGS. THIS CASE IS DELIBERATELY CONSTRUCTED WITH THREE SEPARATE CONTRIBUTORS SO THAT A CANDIDATE WHO HAS MEMORISED 'THE DIABETIC NEUROPATHY CASE' WILL NAME ONE, SOUND CONFIDENT, AND FAIL.** **An examiner who knows the recall is SPECIFICALLY LISTENING for whether you combined them.**

**THE OPENING SENTENCE, LEARNED VERBATIM: 'the first thing I want to say is that FALLS USUALLY HAVE MORE THAN ONE CAUSE — AND THAT'S CERTAINLY TRUE IN YOUR CASE. I'VE FOUND THREE THINGS THAT ARE EACH ADDING TO YOUR RISK. Let me take you through them.'** **The examiner hears it IN THE FIRST FIVE SECONDS and knows you understand the concept rather than the recall.**

**THE PATTERN TO REUSE THREE TIMES: NAME IT → EXPLAIN IT IN ONE PLAIN SENTENCE → LINK IT EXPLICITLY TO FALLS.** **NERVES: 'the high sugar has DAMAGED THE NERVES IN YOUR LEGS. WHEN YOU CAN'T FEEL YOUR FEET PROPERLY, IT'S MUCH EASIER TO TRIP.' KNEES: 'OSTEOARTHRITIS causes PAIN AND STIFFNESS, AND THAT MAKES YOU LESS STEADY.' EYES: 'IF YOU CAN'T SEE CLEARLY, YOU DON'T SEE THE STEP OR THE OBSTACLE.'**

**THEN THE THREAD: 'TWO OF THOSE THREE COME BACK TO THE SAME THING: YOUR DIABETES HASN'T BEEN WELL CONTROLLED. Your sugar today was 15, which is high. GETTING THAT UNDER CONTROL IS THE SINGLE CHANGE THAT PROTECTS YOUR NERVES AND YOUR EYES FROM HERE.'**

**ORDER MATTERS IN THE DIFFERENTIALS: RISK FACTORS FOR FALLS COME BEFORE THE SYNCOPE DIFFERENTIALS. A candidate who launches into arrhythmias and brain tumours BEFORE MENTIONING LIGHTING AND JOINT PAIN HAS SHOWN THEY ARE STILL THINKING ABOUT BLACKOUTS, NOT FALLS.**

**BOX 1, SAID FIRST — other falls risk factors checked and absent: balance and inner-ear causes · URINARY, rushing to the toilet at night · HOME ENVIRONMENT, poor lighting, stairs, slippery surfaces, loose rugs, clutter · alcohol, drugs and MEDICATIONS THAT CAUSE DROWSINESS OR LOWER BLOOD PRESSURE · POSTURAL HYPOTENSION.**

**BOX 2, SAID SECOND — causes of collapse, WITH THE REASON EACH IS UNLIKELY: neurological, cardiac, metabolic, reflex. 'The reason I don't think any of these is the answer is that YOU'VE NEVER LOST CONSCIOUSNESS, your heart rhythm and heart sounds are normal, THERE'S NO POSITIONAL TRIGGER AND NO DROP IN YOUR BLOOD PRESSURE ON STANDING.'**

**GLOVE-AND-STOCKING LOSS IS CLASSIC FOR DIABETIC NEUROPATHY BUT NOT SPECIFIC. The differential worth naming if pressed: VITAMIN B12 DEFICIENCY — AND METFORMIN ITSELF LOWERS B12 OVER YEARS — ALCOHOL, HYPOTHYROIDISM, CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE AND MEDICATION. That is why you check those bloods rather than assuming the diabetes explains everything.**

**ANSWER HIS ACTUAL WORRY OUT LOUD: A PERSONAL ALARM OR MEDICAL ALERT PENDANT, A CHECK-IN ARRANGEMENT with family or neighbours, and A PLAN FOR WHAT TO DO IF HE CANNOT GET UP.** **If he asks 'am I going to end up in a home?', reframe: THE POINT OF FINDING CAUSES IS THAT MOST OF THEM ARE TREATABLE.**
plan: **Ask the examiner for vitals — blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, temperature.** Then **WIPE and an open question.**

**ADDRESS THE CONCERN ONCE, WARMLY, AND MOVE: 'that's a very understandable thing to be worried about. Is it alright if we go through some questions, then I'll examine you and we'll try to find the cause? WE'LL MAKE A PLAN ABOUT THAT WORRY BEFORE YOU LEAVE.'** **The empathy mark is a SINGLE SPECIFIC ACKNOWLEDGEMENT PLUS A PROMISE YOU KEEP — not repeated reassurance that eats the history.**

VESTIBULAR: any SPINNING sensation when it happens. METABOLIC: DO THE FALLS HAPPEN AFTER YOU'VE MISSED A MEAL?**

**STEP 3, PAST HISTORY AND THE FOUR DIABETES QUESTIONS: WHEN WERE YOU DIAGNOSED · WHAT TREATMENT, AND ARE YOU ABLE TO TAKE IT REGULARLY · ARE YOU HAVING REGULAR FOLLOW-UPS AND BLOOD TESTS · HAVE YOU HAD ANY COMPLICATIONS — ANY NUMBNESS IN YOUR LEGS, OR ANY BLURRING OF YOUR VISION?**

**STEP 4, THE FIVE RISK DOMAINS. HOME: describe your home — STAIRS, PETS, SLIPPERY SURFACES, LOOSE RUGS, POOR LIGHTING, AND WHAT FOOTWEAR DO YOU USE? URINARY: do you WAKE IN THE NIGHT to pass urine, any new urgency or frequency?**
**MSK: any JOINT PAIN · any BALANCE problems · any DEFORMITIES in your legs? SENSES: any problems with your VISION OR YOUR HEARING? DRUGS: any other MEDICATIONS, ALCOHOL, OR RECREATIONAL DRUGS?**

**STEP 5, THE GERIATRIC SCREEN ONLY IF TIME REMAINS — four questions, thirty seconds: MEMORY · MOOD · ENOUGH SUPPORT AT HOME · DESCRIBE YOUR DIET.** **Spare time goes here, NOT to SADMA or family history, neither of which earns anything in this case.**
**ASK THE EXAMINER, NAMING EVERY ITEM: general appearance — alert or drowsy, pallor · VITALS PLUS A POSTURAL BLOOD PRESSURE · PULSE RHYTHM.**
**FUNDOSCOPY · VISUAL ACUITY — the two nobody asks for.** Then **LOWER LIMB POWER AND SENSATION.**
**CARDIOVASCULAR — S1, S2, MURMURS, ADDED SOUNDS · RESPIRATORY — air entry and added sounds · LOWER LIMB INSPECTION for swelling and deformity.**
**PALPATE THE JOINTS, ESPECIALLY THE KNEES · RANGE OF MOVEMENT OF THE KNEES · TIMED UP AND GO · OFFICE BLOOD SUGAR · URINE DIPSTICK AND ECG.**
**THE OPENING SENTENCE — 'falls usually have more than one cause, and I've found three.'**
**THE THREE CAUSES, each NAMED, EXPLAINED IN ONE PLAIN SENTENCE, AND LINKED TO FALLS.** Then **THE THREAD: two of the three come back to the uncontrolled diabetes, and the glucose of 15.**
**BOX 1 — the other falls risk factors you checked and excluded. THEN BOX 2 — the causes of collapse, with the reason each is unlikely.**

**THE PLAN, TREATING EVERY CONTRIBUTOR: diabetes control and adherence, diabetes educator and dietitian, ANNUAL CYCLE OF CARE · PODIATRY AND FOOTWEAR AND DAILY FOOT INSPECTION · physiotherapy for the knees · OPHTHALMOLOGY for the retinopathy and current glasses · OT HOME ASSESSMENT.** Then **ANSWER HIS FEAR: A PERSONAL ALARM, A CHECK-IN ARRANGEMENT, AND WHAT TO DO IF HE CANNOT GET UP.**

**Investigations: HbA1c — THE CONTROL FIGURE THE OFFICE GLUCOSE ONLY HINTS AT · UEC AND eGFR for nephropathy AND METFORMIN SAFETY · URINE ALBUMIN:CREATININE RATIO, the third microvascular complication · FBC, VITAMIN B12 AND TFTs for other causes of a peripheral neuropathy · VITAMIN D AND CALCIUM · lipids and blood pressure · knee X-rays only if the osteoarthritis diagnosis is uncertain, THOUGH IT IS LARGELY CLINICAL · CONSIDER DEXA GIVEN FALLS PLUS AGE — FRACTURE RISK, NOT JUST FALL RISK.**

**THE DIABETES IS THE ENGINE: address adherence HONESTLY — WHY DOES HE FORGET? COST? SIDE EFFECTS? — restart regular review, set an INDIVIDUALISED HbA1c TARGET, refer to a DIABETES EDUCATOR AND DIETITIAN, and arrange the ANNUAL CYCLE OF CARE including RETINAL SCREENING AND FOOT CHECKS.**

**THE NEUROPATHY: optimise glycaemic control, CORRECT ANY B12 DEFICIENCY, PODIATRY, WELL-FITTING SUPPORTIVE FOOTWEAR, and DAILY FOOT INSPECTION.** **THE KNEES: PARACETAMOL FIRST LINE, TOPICAL NSAIDs, PHYSIOTHERAPY FOR QUADRICEPS STRENGTHENING, weight management, a walking aid if appropriate — and BE CAUTIOUS WITH ORAL NSAIDs IN AN OLDER DIABETIC because of RENAL AND GASTROINTESTINAL RISK.**
**THE EYES: OPHTHALMOLOGY REFERRAL for the retinopathy, ensure the GLASSES PRESCRIPTION IS CURRENT, and ADVISE AGAINST MULTIFOCAL LENSES WHEN WALKING OUTDOORS OR ON STAIRS.**

**THE FALLS THEMSELVES: OT HOME ASSESSMENT — lighting, rails, removal of loose rugs, bathroom modification · PHYSIOTHERAPY OR A GROUP STRENGTH AND BALANCE PROGRAMME, which is the single most useful referral combination · MEDICATION REVIEW · VITAMIN D IF DEFICIENT · consider a FALLS CLINIC.**

**EQUITY: multifactorial falls management ASSUMES ACCESS. Podiatry, physiotherapy, OT home visits and ophthalmology are ALL HARDER TO REACH RURALLY, AND SUPPORTIVE FOOTWEAR COSTS MONEY. NAME THE BARRIER AND PLAN AROUND IT — outreach services, telehealth review, ABORIGINAL HEALTH WORKER involvement, and a GP MANAGEMENT PLAN to subsidise the allied health visits.**

stem: John, 60, has come in complaining of recurrent falls. He has a history of stroke two years ago.
tasks: Take a history
Physical examination findings — on screen, or requested from the examiner
Explain your diagnosis and your differentials to the patient
(Online variant) Explain the consequences of recurrent falls
findings: WHY THE STEM MENTIONS THE STROKE

IT IS NOT BACKGROUND. IT IS A DIRECT INSTRUCTION TO ASK ONE QUESTION: IS THERE ANY RESIDUAL NEUROLOGICAL DEFICIT? Did he make a full recovery, or DOES HE STILL HAVE WEAKNESS OR NUMBNESS DOWN ONE SIDE? Everything else about the stroke is secondary to that question
The examination findings

Alert, no pallor · POSTURAL BP SITTING 120/80, STANDING 94/56 · pulse regular · LEFT ARM AND LEFT LEG POWER 3/5, RIGHT SIDE 5/5 · tone, reflexes, plantars and gait CONSISTENT WITH A PREVIOUS STROKE · lower limb sensation INTACT · fundoscopy NO hypertensive retinopathy · CVS and chest normal · MILD EPIGASTRIC TENDERNESS, no mass · TIMED UP AND GO PROLONGED · glucose normal · ECG sinus
DO THE ARITHMETIC OUT LOUD — under pressure it is easy to fumble
SYSTOLIC 120 − 94 = A FALL OF 26. DIASTOLIC 80 − 56 = A FALL OF 24. BOTH POSITIVE. Say the numbers AND the conclusion: 'THAT IS A DROP OF 26 SYSTOLIC AND 24 DIASTOLIC — A POSITIVE POSTURAL DROP'
THE CRITERION IS EITHER VALUE, NOT BOTH

A sustained fall of 20 mmHg SYSTOLIC OR 10 mmHg DIASTOLIC WITHIN 3 MINUTES OF STANDING. AT LEAST ONE PAST EXAM GAVE A DIASTOLIC-ONLY DROP — A CANDIDATE WHO CHECKS ONLY THE SYSTOLIC WILL CALL IT NEGATIVE. Some references use 15 for the systolic; quote 20 and add that if challenged
THE PATTERN IS HANDED TO YOU

FOUR FALLS, EVERY ONE ON CHANGING POSITION — standing up out of the couch, getting out of bed. ASK THE TRIGGER QUESTION DIRECTLY — 'DOES A CHANGE OF POSITION FROM SITTING OR LYING TO STANDING SET THEM OFF?' — WHICH CONVERTS AN INFERENCE INTO A DOCUMENTED POSITIVE
INTERPRETING 3/5 POWER

GRADE 3 IS MOVEMENT AGAINST GRAVITY BUT NOT AGAINST RESISTANCE — A SUBSTANTIAL DEFICIT. Say: 'reduced power, 3 out of 5, in the left arm and leg, CONSISTENT WITH RESIDUAL HEMIPARESIS — AND THAT IS ITSELF A MAJOR RISK FACTOR FOR FALLING'
'I GET SHORT OF BREATH WHEN I'M GARDENING'

DO NOT SKIP PAST IT. EXERTIONAL DYSPNOEA IN A HYPERTENSIVE WITH PREVIOUS CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE IS ISCHAEMIA OR HEART FAILURE UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE. One extra question — any cough? — then FLAG POSSIBLE ISCHAEMIC HEART DISEASE AND INVESTIGATE IT
THE EPIGASTRIC PAIN — three questions, no more

DO YOU GET REFLUX OR HEARTBURN · ARE YOU TAKING ANY ANTI-INFLAMMATORY PAINKILLERS, NUROFEN, VOLTAREN, ASPIRIN · HAVE YOU LOST ANY WEIGHT? In the recalls the answers are NO, NO AND NO. ASK THEM ANYWAY — it is how you would find an OCCULT GI BLEED CAUSING ANAEMIA AND FALLS. FLAG IT AS NEEDING ITS OWN REVIEW
THE DIFFERENTIAL EVERYBODY OMITS

CANDIDATES LEAVE STROKE AND TIA OFF THE LIST BECAUSE THE PATIENT HAS ALREADY HAD A STROKE — AS THOUGH A PAST EVENT EXCLUDED A FUTURE ONE. THE OPPOSITE IS TRUE. Say it: 'YOU'VE ALREADY HAD ONE STROKE, WHICH MEANS YOUR RISK OF ANOTHER IS HIGHER, AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY WE TREAT YOU TO PREVENT IT'
DO NOT TELL HIM TO STOP THE TABLET

EVERY CLASS OF ANTIHYPERTENSIVE CAN CONTRIBUTE — diuretics most notoriously, but ACE inhibitors, ARBs and calcium channel blockers as well — SO THE SPECIFIC DRUG MATTERS LESS THAN THE FACT THAT HE IS ON ONE. Say 'I WOULD REVIEW THE DOSE AND TIMING', not 'he is on the wrong tablet'. HE HAS HAD A STROKE AND NEEDS BLOOD PRESSURE CONTROL
findingsLabel: The stroke in the stem is a question — and the drop you must compute aloud
must: FAIL — Finding the postural drop, announcing it, and stopping there.
FAIL — Omitting stroke and TIA because he has already had one.
FAIL — Noting 'stroke two years ago' and never asking about residual deficit.
FAIL — Telling him to stop his blood pressure tablet.
ASK — Does changing position, from sitting or lying to standing, set them off?
ASK — Did you make a full recovery, or are you left with any weakness or numbness?

dx: **FOUR CAUSES. ONE: POSTURAL (ORTHOSTATIC) HYPOTENSION, almost certainly AGGRAVATED BY HIS ANTIHYPERTENSIVE. TWO: RESIDUAL LEFT HEMIPARESIS from the stroke. THREE: POSSIBLE ISCHAEMIC HEART DISEASE. FOUR: THE RISK OF A FURTHER STROKE OR TIA.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE IS NOT FINDING THE POSTURAL DROP — THAT IS HANDED TO YOU. It is whether you DELIVER FOUR CAUSES, REASON EACH FROM BOTH THE HISTORY AND THE EXAMINATION rather than reading findings off a list, and HAVE THE CONFIDENCE TO INCLUDE ANOTHER STROKE IN A MAN WHO HAS ALREADY HAD ONE.**

**THE REASONING SENTENCE, FOR CAUSE ONE, EVERY TIME: 'I'M CONFIDENT ABOUT IT FOR TWO REASONS. FIRST, I FOUND IT ON EXAMINATION — your blood pressure was 120 over 80 sitting and 94 over 56 standing. AND SECOND, when you described your falls, ALMOST ALL OF THEM HAPPENED AS YOU CHANGED POSITION. THE HISTORY AND THE EXAMINATION AGREE.'** **That is the difference between A CANDIDATE REPORTING A NUMBER AND A CANDIDATE DEMONSTRATING CLINICAL THINKING.**
**THE SHAPE, FOUR TIMES OVER: NAME IT → EXPLAIN IT IN ONE PLAIN SENTENCE → LINK IT EXPLICITLY TO FALLS — and for cause one, GIVE THE TWO REASONS YOU BELIEVE IT.**

**CAUSE TWO: 'I also found SOME REMAINING WEAKNESS IN YOUR LEFT ARM AND LEG from your stroke — on testing, the strength there is reduced. THAT WEAKNESS MAKES YOU LESS STEADY ON YOUR FEET AND INCREASES THE RISK OF FALLS.'**

**CAUSE THREE: 'I'm also concerned about THE SHORTNESS OF BREATH YOU GET WHEN YOU'RE GARDENING. Put together with YOUR BLOOD PRESSURE AND YOUR PREVIOUS STROKE, there's a chance you have SOME NARROWING OF THE ARTERIES SUPPLYING THE HEART, which could be contributing to the falls. I'd like to INVESTIGATE THAT PROPERLY.'**

**CAUSE FOUR, said honestly: 'HAVING HAD A STROKE MEANS YOU ARE AT HIGHER RISK OF HAVING ANOTHER ONE, OR A MINI-STROKE — AND THOSE CAN CAUSE FALLS TOO. THAT'S NOT TO FRIGHTEN YOU: IT'S EXACTLY WHY WE TREAT YOUR BLOOD PRESSURE AND KEEP YOU ON PREVENTIVE MEDICATION.'**

**AND THE LOOSE END: 'separately, I want to come back to THE PAIN IN YOUR UPPER TUMMY. It may well be unrelated to the falls, BUT I DON'T WANT TO LEAVE IT, so let's look into that at your next visit.'**

**THE MEDICATION LINE, STATED FAIRLY AND WITHOUT BLAME: 'your blood pressure tablet is LIKELY CONTRIBUTING, so we'll REVIEW THE DOSE AND THE TIMING — BUT PLEASE DON'T STOP IT YOURSELF, BECAUSE IT'S PROTECTING YOU FROM ANOTHER STROKE.'**

**THE FOURTH TASK, CONSEQUENCES: HEAD INJURY, INCLUDING BLEEDING AROUND THE BRAIN, PARTICULARLY ON BLOOD-THINNING MEDICATION · FRACTURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE HIP, BUT ALSO WRIST AND SPINE, USUALLY MEANING AN OPERATION AND LONG REHABILITATION · LOSS OF INDEPENDENCE, WITH MANY PEOPLE NEVER RETURNING TO THEIR PREVIOUS LEVEL · FEAR OF FALLING, WHICH MAKES PEOPLE MOVE LESS AND GET WEAKER · AND RECURRENCE, BECAUSE HAVING FALLEN IS THE STRONGEST PREDICTOR OF FALLING AGAIN.** Close with: **'WE AIM TO PREVENT FALLS BY REDUCING THE RISK FACTORS — ONE BY ONE, STARTING WITH THE ONES WE'VE FOUND TODAY.'**
plan: **Ask the examiner for vitals.** Then **WIPE and an open question.** Then **EMPATHY ONCE, SHORT AND SPECIFIC: 'falls are frightening, and it's absolutely right that you've come in.'** **Repeated reassurance in a four-minute history costs you the risk-factor block, WHICH IS WHERE THE MARKS ARE.**
**THE FORK: when you fall, DO YOU LOSE CONSCIOUSNESS, OR ARE YOU STILL AWARE · any JERKY MOVEMENTS?** Then **SAY THE BRANCH OUT LOUD.**

**HOW MANY FALLS · CAN YOU DESCRIBE EACH OF THEM · WHAT WERE YOU DOING JUST BEFORE · DOES CHANGING POSITION, FROM SITTING OR LYING TO STANDING, SET THEM OFF · AND DID YOU INJURE YOURSELF OR FRACTURE ANY BONES?**

**ORGANIC SCREEN. NEURO: slurred speech, WEAKNESS, numbness. CVS: chest pain, racing of the heart, ANY SHORTNESS OF BREATH. GI: nausea, vomiting, ABDOMINAL PAIN. VESTIBULAR: any spinning. METABOLIC: do the falls happen after a missed meal?**

**THE RISK DOMAINS. HOME: stairs, slippery surfaces, LIGHTING, loose rugs, clutter, FOOTWEAR, RAILS IN THE BATHROOM. URINARY: NOCTURIA, urgency, frequency. MSK: joint pain, BALANCE PROBLEMS WHICH MAY PERSIST AFTER A STROKE, deformities, numbness. SENSES: vision and hearing. DRUGS: other medications, alcohol, recreational drugs.**
**GERIATRIC SCREEN: MEMORY · MOOD · SUPPORT AT HOME · DIET.**

**ASK THE EXAMINER, NAMING EACH: general appearance — alert, pallor · POSTURAL BLOOD PRESSURE · PULSE RHYTHM · POWER IN THE UPPER AND LOWER LIMBS · TONE, REFLEXES, PLANTARS AND GAIT · SENSATION IN THE LOWER LIMBS.**

**DO THE ARITHMETIC OUT LOUD — 26 SYSTOLIC, 24 DIASTOLIC, BOTH POSITIVE.**
**THE OPENING SENTENCE: 'falls usually have more than one cause, and in your case I've found SEVERAL THINGS CONTRIBUTING.'**
**CAUSE ONE WITH ITS TWO REASONS, and the medication line WITHOUT blame and WITHOUT telling him to stop.**
**CAUSES TWO, THREE AND FOUR — the residual weakness, the possible ischaemic heart disease, and the risk of another stroke.** Then **the loose end: the epigastric pain needs its own review.**

**BOX 1 — other falls risk factors, checked. THEN BOX 2 — causes of collapse, with the reason each is unlikely: 'you've never lost consciousness, your rhythm and heart sounds are normal, AND THE PATTERN FITS THE BLOOD PRESSURE DROP.'**

**THE CONSEQUENCES — head injury, hip fracture, loss of independence, fear of falling, recurrence — then FAST ADVICE AND 000 for any sudden weakness, numbness, speech or visual disturbance.** Then **THE CLOSING LINE: 'we aim to prevent falls by reducing the risk factors.'**

stem: Jenny, 40, presents with widespread aches and pains all over her body. Her ESR and CRP are normal. Her mother has rheumatoid arthritis and she is worried she has it too. She has previously been diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome.
tasks: Take a focused, relevant history (5 minutes — you will be prompted)
Physical examination findings will be given to you on a card
Explain your most likely diagnosis and your differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: THE PEFE CARD

TENDERNESS OVER TRAPEZIUS AND MULTIPLE TENDER POINTS · JOINT EXAMINATION ENTIRELY NORMAL WITH FULL RANGE OF MOVEMENT · NO swelling, redness, deformity or rash. ESR AND CRP NORMAL, given in the stem. READ IT AS EVIDENCE: A NORMAL JOINT EXAMINATION IS WHAT LETS YOU SAY FIBROMYALGIA
THE ROLE-PLAYER IS BRIEFED TO BE FRUSTRATED
'EVERY DOCTOR TELLS ME NOTHING IS WRONG' · 'I'M SICK OF BEING TOLD IT'S IN MY HEAD.' SHE IS NOT DIFFICULT — SHE IS FRIGHTENED AND UNVALIDATED. THE FIRST THIRTY SECONDS OF YOUR CONSULTATION ARE MARKED
IF YOU REASSURE BEFORE ASSESSING, YOU LOSE THE STATION
'I'M SURE IT'S NOTHING SERIOUS' COSTS THE COMMUNICATION MARKS. VALIDATE THE EXPERIENCE, PROMISE THE PROCESS, COMMIT TO NOTHING ABOUT THE OUTCOME
THE TWO QUESTIONS THAT DECIDE THIS STATION
THE SITE QUESTION separates PMR (shoulders and hips) from FIBROMYALGIA (everywhere). THE IMPACT QUESTION opens the psychosocial door LEGITIMATELY, EARLY, WITHOUT LABELLING
'IT'S ALL OVER MY BODY' — do not accept it

'To help me narrow it down — IS IT THE JOINTS OR THE MUSCLES? AND CAN YOU NAME ME TWO OR THREE SPOTS?' If she is abrasive — 'I DON'T KNOW, DOCTOR' — re-frame, DO NOT ARGUE: 'that's completely fine. JUST POINT TO WHERE IT BOTHERS YOU MOST RIGHT NOW'
THE FLAT NON-PATTERN IS THE CLUE
'IT MAKES NO DIFFERENCE — MORNING, NIGHT, REST, ACTIVITY.' NO INFLAMMATORY AND NO MECHANICAL PATTERN. SAY IT BACK LATER AS EVIDENCE: 'YOUR PAIN HAS NO INFLAMMATORY PATTERN'
HER STATED FEAR IS HANDED TO YOU IN THE STEM
HER MOTHER HAS RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS AND SHE IS CONVINCED SHE HAS IT. ACKNOWLEDGE IT EARLY AND PROMISE TO RETURN TO IT — THEN REFUTE IT AT THE END WITH HER OWN FINDINGS, NOT WITH REASSURANCE
THE IBS IS SUPPORTING EVIDENCE, NOT A DISMISSAL
IBS IS A FIBROMYALGIA CO-TRAVELLER. NOTE IT, ASK ABOUT BLOOD AND WEIGHT LOSS, AND USE IT LATER AS PART OF THE POSITIVE CASE
WHAT A STATIN WOULD CHANGE

'I'VE BEEN ON A CHOLESTEROL TABLET' → 'WHICH ONE, AND WHEN DID IT START RELATIVE TO THE ACHES?' THEN CHECK CK. Asking about medications INCLUDING FROM THE CHEMIST OR HEALTH-FOOD SHOP is how statin myopathy is found
THE MOTOR VEHICLE ACCIDENT VARIANT

A PROPORTION OF THESE PATIENTS DATE THEIR WHOLE-BODY PAIN TO A CAR ACCIDENT. That reframes it towards CHRONIC POST-TRAUMATIC PAIN and WHIPLASH-ASSOCIATED DISORDER — and in SA opens a RETURNTOWORKSA OR CTP CLAIM. Ask about trauma INCLUDING A CAR ACCIDENT

FAIL — Labelling fibromyalgia in the first two minutes, before any organic exclusion.
FAIL — No psychosocial assessment at all in a chronic pain patient.

dx: **FIBROMYALGIA — CHRONIC WIDESPREAD MUSCULOSKELETAL PAIN OF AT LEAST THREE MONTHS, IN AT LEAST FOUR OF FIVE BODY REGIONS, with FATIGUE, UNREFRESHING SLEEP AND COGNITIVE CLOUDING, arising from ALTERED CENTRAL PAIN PROCESSING rather than structural joint or muscle disease, AND NOT BETTER EXPLAINED BY ANOTHER CONDITION.**
**THERE IS NO CONFIRMATORY TEST. It is confirmed by A NORMAL TARGETED WORK-UP PLUS POSITIVE CLINICAL FEATURES.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE PSYCHOSOCIAL BLOCK — TAKEN AFTER THE ORGANIC SWEEP, NEVER INSTEAD OF IT. Candidates who run a beautiful musculoskeletal history and stop there FAIL. Candidates who LEAD with psychology run out of time for groups 1–7 AND CANNOT LOGICALLY REACH THE DIAGNOSIS.**

**THE ORDER IS NOT COSMETIC: FIBROMYALGIA AND EVERY DSM-5 SOMATIC-SYMPTOM DIAGNOSIS REQUIRE THAT SYMPTOMS ARE NOT BETTER EXPLAINED BY ANOTHER MEDICAL CONDITION — SO THE ORGANIC SWEEP IS A FORMAL PRE-REQUISITE, NOT A COURTESY.**

**THE VALIDATION LINE, LEARNED VERBATIM: 'I can hear HOW OVERWHELMING THIS HAS BEEN, and I'm sorry you've had that experience with other doctors. YOUR PAIN IS REAL AND I TAKE IT SERIOUSLY. I'm here to help you today — WE WILL LOOK INTO THIS PROPERLY.'**

**EIGHT DIFFERENTIAL GROUPS, ANNOUNCED BY NAME AS YOU GO — AN UNSPOKEN STRUCTURE SCORES NOTHING: 1 RED FLAGS AND MALIGNANCY · 2 INFECTION · 3 THE ARTHRITIDES · 4 SOFT TISSUE AND MUSCLE · 5 NEUROLOGICAL · 6 ENDOCRINE AND METABOLIC · 7 MEDICATIONS · 8 PSYCHOSOCIAL, LAST.**

**THE EXPLANATION THAT PASSES: 'you most likely have FIBROMYALGIA. It causes WIDESPREAD PAIN ALL OVER THE BODY WITHOUT ANY STRUCTURAL DAMAGE in the muscles or joints — and I HAVE CHECKED FOR THAT. It is a REAL, RECOGNISED CONDITION in which THE PAIN-SIGNALLING SYSTEM BECOMES OVER-SENSITIVE, so ordinary signals are felt as pain. IT IS NOT IN YOUR HEAD AND IT IS NOT YOUR FAULT.'**

**THEN REFUTE THE RA FEAR WITH HER OWN FINDINGS: 'I've thought carefully about rheumatoid arthritis BECAUSE YOU WERE WORRIED ABOUT IT. You have NO JOINT SWELLING, NO DEFORMITY, NO PROLONGED MORNING STIFFNESS, your pain is NOT WORSE IN THE MORNING AND NOT BETTER WITH MOVEMENT, and your INFLAMMATORY MARKERS ARE NORMAL.'** Then add honestly: **'FIBROMYALGIA CAN OCCUR ALONGSIDE RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS, SO IF ANYTHING CHANGES WE WILL REASSESS.'**

**CORRECTION — WEIGHT LOSS AND FATIGUE ARE NOT SPECIFIC TO CANCER. RA, PMR AND CHRONIC INFECTION ALL CAUSE BOTH. A SINGLE POSITIVE RED FLAG DOES NOT LICENSE YOU TO ANNOUNCE MALIGNANCY — YOU WEIGH THE WHOLE PICTURE.**

**CORRECTION — the source says syphilis and HIV do not cause body aches. SECONDARY SYPHILIS CLASSICALLY CAUSES GENERALISED ARTHRALGIA AND MYALGIA with fever, a PALM-AND-SOLE RASH and lymphadenopathy; HIV SEROCONVERSION causes a MONONUCLEOSIS-LIKE ILLNESS WITH MYALGIA. KEEP THE SEXUAL HISTORY — IT IS A REAL YIELD.**

stem: A 72-year-old man presents with aches and pains all over his body for the past few weeks. He is otherwise well. Observations are normal.
tasks: Take a focused, relevant history
Physical examination findings will be given to you on a card
Explain your most likely diagnosis and your differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: What he gives on questioning

PAIN IS MAINLY SHOULDERS AND HIPS · WORSE IN THE MORNING · REST MAKES IT WORSE, ACTIVITY EASES IT · STIFFNESS YES · NO swelling, redness or rash · WEIGHT LOSS YES, appetite normal, no lumps, TIRED YES. Some recalls add HEADACHE
THE PEFE CARD

ESR AND CRP RAISED · girdle tenderness with PAIN ON MOVEMENT BUT PRESERVED PASSIVE RANGE · no synovitis, no small-joint swelling · TEMPORAL ARTERIES to be examined ON REQUEST · power formally normal despite the difficulty rising
THE SITE QUESTION IS WHAT SEPARATES THIS FROM FIBROMYALGIA
SHOULDERS AND HIPS → PMR. EVERYWHERE → FIBROMYALGIA. Do not accept 'all over my body' — ask 'IS IT THE JOINTS OR THE MUSCLES, AND CAN YOU NAME ME TWO OR THREE SPOTS?'
THE PATTERN PIVOT
'WORSE IN THE MORNING, BETTER ONCE I GET MOVING' → IMMEDIATELY ASK 'HOW LONG DOES THE STIFFNESS LAST?' 45 TO 60 MINUTES OR MORE, IN SHOULDERS AND HIPS, OVER 50, IS PMR. THEN SCREEN GCA
THE FOUR QUESTIONS THAT ARE A SINGLE-ITEM FAIL IF OMITTED

ANY NEW HEADACHE, ESPECIALLY AROUND THE TEMPLES · IS YOUR SCALP TENDER when you comb your hair or lie on the pillow · ANY PAIN IN THE JAW WHEN YOU CHEW that eases when you stop · ANY CHANGE IN YOUR VISION — BLURRING, DOUBLE VISION, OR A CURTAIN COMING ACROSS? UNTREATED GCA CAUSES IRREVERSIBLE BLINDNESS
A NORMAL TEMPORAL ARTERY DOES NOT EXCLUDE GCA

The superficial temporal artery may be PROMINENT, THICKENED, BEADED, TENDER OR PULSELESS. LOOK AT AND PALPATE BOTH TEMPLES IN EVERY PMR-PATTERN PATIENT — BUT A NORMAL-FEELING ARTERY DOES NOT EXCLUDE THE DIAGNOSIS
THE FUNCTIONAL QUESTIONS THAT CONFIRM GIRDLE INVOLVEMENT

DO YOU STRUGGLE TO GET OUT OF A CHAIR · CLIMB STAIRS · COMB YOUR HAIR? These separate TRUE GIRDLE PAIN AND STIFFNESS from a vague ache — and the power is FORMALLY NORMAL, which is what distinguishes PMR from POLYMYOSITIS
WEIGHT LOSS AND FATIGUE DO NOT DISCRIMINATE
THEY OCCUR IN PMR, RA, CHRONIC INFECTION AND MALIGNANCY ALIKE. DO NOT USE THEM TO CHOOSE — and DO NOT ANNOUNCE MALIGNANCY ON A SINGLE RED FLAG. The PATTERN is what discriminates
THE RESPONSE TO STEROID IS ITSELF DIAGNOSTIC SUPPORT
A DRAMATIC RESPONSE TO LOW-DOSE PREDNISOLONE WITHIN 3 TO 7 DAYS supports the diagnosis. ABSENCE OF RESPONSE SHOULD MAKE YOU DOUBT IT AND RE-OPEN THE MALIGNANCY QUESTION
Do not skip the medication question

STATIN MYOPATHY IS THE COMMONEST MIMIC OF PROXIMAL ACHING IN THIS AGE GROUP. 'ANY MEDICATIONS AT ALL, INCLUDING FROM THE CHEMIST OR HEALTH-FOOD SHOP' — and if a statin, WHEN DID IT START RELATIVE TO THE ACHES, THEN CHECK CK
findingsLabel: Girdle pain over 50 — and the four questions that are a single-item fail
must: FAIL — Missing the GCA screen. Four questions, every patient over 50 with girdle pain.
FAIL — Accepting 'all over my body' without establishing shoulders and hips.
FAIL — Announcing malignancy on weight loss and fatigue alone.
FAIL — Never asking about medications, so statin myopathy is never considered.
ASK — How long does the morning stiffness last before you loosen up?
ASK — Any change in your vision — blurring, double vision, or a curtain coming across?

dx: **POLYMYALGIA RHEUMATICA — an INFLAMMATORY condition of people OVER 50 causing BILATERAL SHOULDER AND OFTEN HIP-GIRDLE PAIN with PROLONGED MORNING STIFFNESS, RAISED INFLAMMATORY MARKERS and a RAPID RESPONSE TO LOW-DOSE CORTICOSTEROID.** **IT SHARES A DISEASE SPECTRUM WITH GIANT CELL ARTERITIS.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE EASY PART. THE MARKED STEP IS KNOWING THAT PMR AND GCA ARE ONE DISEASE SPECTRUM, AND SCREENING FOR THE ONE THAT BLINDS PEOPLE.** **NOT ASKING ABOUT VISION IN A PMR-PATTERN PATIENT IS A SINGLE-ITEM AUTOMATIC FAIL IN MOST EXAMINERS' HANDS.**

**THE SAFETY-NET, SAID EVEN IF ALL FOUR ANSWERS ARE NEGATIVE: 'this condition is CLOSELY RELATED TO ANOTHER ONE AFFECTING THE ARTERIES AT THE TEMPLES, WHICH CAN AFFECT EYESIGHT. You don't have those symptoms now. BUT IF YOU EVER GET A NEW HEADACHE, JAW PAIN ON CHEWING, OR ANY CHANGE IN VISION, YOU MUST BE SEEN THE SAME DAY — GO TO THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, DON'T WAIT FOR AN APPOINTMENT.'**

**THE PATTERN IS THE ARGUMENT, NOT THE SYMPTOMS. If challenged 'why not cancer?': 'BECAUSE THE PAIN HAS A CLEAR PATTERN — WORSE AFTER REST, BETTER WITH ACTIVITY, WITH PROLONGED MORNING STIFFNESS CONFINED TO THE SHOULDER AND HIP GIRDLES. WEIGHT LOSS AND FATIGUE OCCUR IN BOTH, SO I HAVE NOT USED THEM TO DISCRIMINATE. IF HE FAILS TO RESPOND TO LOW-DOSE PREDNISOLONE WITHIN A WEEK, I WOULD RE-OPEN THE MALIGNANCY QUESTION.'**

**EIGHT DIFFERENTIAL GROUPS, ANNOUNCED BY NAME — AN UNSPOKEN STRUCTURE SCORES NOTHING: RED FLAGS AND MALIGNANCY · INFECTION · THE ARTHRITIDES · SOFT TISSUE AND MUSCLE · NEUROLOGICAL · ENDOCRINE AND METABOLIC · MEDICATIONS · PSYCHOSOCIAL LAST.**

**TREATMENT: PREDNISOLONE 15 mg DAILY, guideline range roughly 12.5–25 mg. EXPECT A DRAMATIC RESPONSE WITHIN 3–7 DAYS. TAPER SLOWLY, USUALLY OVER 12–24 MONTHS. RELAPSE IS COMMON.** **FOR GCA THE DOSE IS 40–60 mg DAILY, with IV METHYLPREDNISOLONE IF THERE IS VISUAL LOSS.** VERIFY against current Therapeutic Guidelines.

**DO NOT DELAY TREATMENT FOR THE BIOPSY. Temporal artery biopsy STAYS INFORMATIVE FOR A WEEK OR TWO AFTER STARTING STEROID — so if any GCA feature is present, START HIGH-DOSE CORTICOSTEROID AND ARRANGE URGENT OPHTHALMOLOGY OR RHEUMATOLOGY REVIEW THE SAME DAY.**

**BONE PROTECTION IS PART OF THE PRESCRIPTION, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT: CALCIUM AND VITAMIN D, WEIGHT-BEARING EXERCISE, CONSIDER A BISPHOSPHONATE, AND BASELINE BONE DENSITY.** **Then MONITOR BP, GLUCOSE, WEIGHT, MOOD, CATARACT AND INFECTION RISK on long-term steroid.**

**THE RED FLAGS ARE UNCONDITIONAL AT EVERY AGE: WEIGHT LOSS · NIGHT SWEATS · BONE PAIN ESPECIALLY AT NIGHT · LUMPS OR BUMPS · FEVER OR RIGORS.** **Add in this age group: BONE PAIN WITH ANAEMIA, HYPERCALCAEMIA AND A VERY HIGH ESR IS MYELOMA — and a VERY HIGH ESR IS A MYELOMA CLUE, NOT A PMR CLUE.**

**RURAL ACCESS MATTERS: rheumatology from MM5 means an outpatient referral to the RAH or Flinders — ASK FOR A TELEHEALTH APPOINTMENT to avoid the drive, and use PATS for travel and accommodation subsidy when an in-person visit is required.** **For ACUTE VISUAL LOSS WITH SUSPECTED GCA: GIVE THE STEROID, THEN PHONE THE ON-CALL OPHTHALMOLOGY REGISTRAR; MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 if retrieval is needed.**

**GROUP 6, ENDOCRINE AND METABOLIC: DO YOU FEEL THE COLD MORE THAN OTHERS · constipation, dry skin, hair thinning, weight change · INCREASED THIRST OR PASSING MORE URINE · bone pain, tummy pain, nausea, low mood?**

**SADMA and close: smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs, allergies, other conditions or surgery, family history · 'is there anything I haven't asked about that you were hoping to discuss today?'**

stem: A 57-year-old woman presents with aches and pains all over her body for the past week. She returned two weeks ago from a holiday in the United States. Observations are normal.
tasks: Take a focused, relevant history
Physical examination findings will be given to you on a card
Explain your most likely diagnosis and your differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: THE CARD
PHOTOGRAPH OF THE FOREARM SHOWING A TARGET OR BULLSEYE RASH · AXILLARY LYMPHADENOPATHY. Variable across role-players: FEVER, SWEATS, TIREDNESS. Some recalls add HEADACHE
ERYTHEMA MIGRANS IS NOT ALWAYS A BULLSEYE

It may be UNIFORMLY RED, BLUE-RED, BLISTERED CENTRALLY, OR MULTIPLE if disseminated. It EXPANDS SLOWLY OVER DAYS, IS USUALLY NEITHER ITCHY NOR PAINFUL, and appears ROUGHLY 3 TO 30 DAYS AFTER THE BITE. ABSENCE OF A RASH DOES NOT EXCLUDE THE DIAGNOSIS — A SUBSTANTIAL MINORITY NEVER DEVELOP ONE
THE EXAMINER HAS A YES/NO BOX
DID THIS CANDIDATE TAKE A COMPLETE TRAVEL HISTORY? TWO QUESTIONS WILL NOT TICK IT, EVEN WITH AN OTHERWISE STRONG PERFORMANCE. 'DID YOU GO BUSHWALKING?' AND NOTHING ELSE IS THE AUTOMATIC FAIL
ALL EIGHT TRAVEL QUESTIONS, OUT LOUD, IN ORDER

A WHERE EXACTLY AND HOW LONG, AND WHAT ACTIVITIES · B ANY BUSHWALKING OR CAMPING, AND DID YOU NOTICE ANY TICK OR INSECT BITES · C ANY CONTACT WITH SICK PEOPLE OR ANIMALS · D ANY DRUGS, OR MUCH ALCOHOL
…and the second four

E ANY EXPOSURE TO BLOOD — TATTOOS, PIERCINGS, MEDICAL OR DENTAL PROCEDURES, TRANSFUSION · F ANY STREET FOOD OR UNTREATED WATER · G DID YOU SEE A GP BEFORE TRAVELLING, VACCINES OR MALARIA TABLETS · H DID YOU HAVE SEX WHILE OVERSEAS, AND DO YOU USE CONDOMS
ASK ABOUT THE TICK DIRECTLY

'DID YOU NOTICE A TICK, AND DID YOU PULL IT OFF?' Then advise FREEZE IT, DON'T SQUEEZE IT — an ether-containing spray, or FINE-TIPPED FORCEPS GRASPING CLOSE TO THE SKIN. DO NOT TWIST, BURN OR APPLY CHEMICALS, WHICH PROMOTE REGURGITATION OF GUT CONTENTS
THREE THINGS TOGETHER MAKE THE DIAGNOSIS
SHE WAS IN AN AREA WHERE IT OCCURS · SHE WAS BUSHWALKING · AND SHE HAS A CHARACTERISTIC RASH WITH A SWOLLEN GLAND IN THE ARMPIT. Say the three out loud as your reasoning
TREAT NOW, DO NOT WAIT FOR SEROLOGY
SEROLOGY IS FREQUENTLY NEGATIVE IN THE FIRST WEEKS. IF ERYTHEMA MIGRANS IS PRESENT WITH A COMPATIBLE EXPOSURE, TREAT IMMEDIATELY
THE AUSTRALIAN POSITION, HANDLED GENTLY

LOCALLY ACQUIRED CLASSICAL LYME BORRELIOSIS IS NOT RECOGNISED IN AUSTRALIA — there is no accepted evidence that Borrelia burgdorferi is endemic here, SO A DIAGNOSIS REQUIRES TRAVEL TO AN ENDEMIC REGION. A comparable illness without that exposure is described as DSCATT. ACKNOWLEDGE THE SYMPTOMS, DECLINE THE UNVALIDATED TEST, OFFER STRUCTURED FOLLOW-UP
THE AUSTRALIAN DIFFERENTIALS THAT OUTRANK IMPORTED ONES

In an Australian patient, ROSS RIVER VIRUS and BARMAH FOREST VIRUS — mosquito-borne alphaviruses causing POLYARTHRALGIA, MYALGIA AND PROFOUND FATIGUE LASTING MONTHS — are FAR MORE LIKELY THAN ANY IMPORTED INFECTION. Also Q FEVER from abattoir, farm and livestock exposure, and BRUCELLOSIS in feral-pig hunters

dx: **EARLY LYME DISEASE — infection with BORRELIA BURGDORFERI SENSU LATO, transmitted by IXODES TICKS in endemic regions of NORTH AMERICA, EUROPE AND PARTS OF ASIA, presenting early with ERYTHEMA MIGRANS AND A FLU-LIKE ILLNESS.**
**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE COMPLETE TRAVEL HISTORY. THE EXAMINER HAS A SINGLE YES/NO BOX FOR IT, AND TWO QUESTIONS WILL NOT TICK IT EVEN WITH AN OTHERWISE STRONG PERFORMANCE.**

**TIE IT TO THE FINDINGS, THREE THINGS TOGETHER: 'I think you most likely have LYME DISEASE. It is a BACTERIAL INFECTION CARRIED BY TICKS. I'm saying that because of THREE THINGS TOGETHER: you were IN AN AREA WHERE IT OCCURS, you were BUSHWALKING, and you have A VERY CHARACTERISTIC RASH ON YOUR FOREARM WITH A SWOLLEN GLAND IN THE ARMPIT. IT RESPONDS WELL TO A COURSE OF ANTIBIOTIC TABLETS.'**

**TREATMENT: DOXYCYCLINE 100 mg TWICE DAILY FOR ERYTHEMA MIGRANS, usual duration 10 TO 21 DAYS. AMOXICILLIN OR CEFUROXIME if doxycycline is contraindicated — PREGNANCY, OR CHILDREN UNDER 8.** VERIFY against current Therapeutic Guidelines.

**WARN ABOUT TWO THINGS: PHOTOSENSITIVITY WITH DOXYCYCLINE, and a POSSIBLE JARISCH-HERXHEIMER REACTION IN THE FIRST 24 HOURS.** **DISCUSS WITH INFECTIOUS DISEASES IF THERE IS CARDITIS, NEUROLOGICAL INVOLVEMENT OR ARTHRITIS.**

**TWO-TIER SEROLOGY — SCREENING EIA, THEN IMMUNOBLOT ON REACTIVE SAMPLES — AT AN AUSTRALIAN ACCREDITED LABORATORY. BUT DO NOT WAIT FOR IT: SEROLOGY IS FREQUENTLY NEGATIVE IN THE FIRST WEEKS, AND A COMPATIBLE EXPOSURE WITH ERYTHEMA MIGRANS IS TREATED CLINICALLY.**
**DO NOT SEND SPECIMENS TO OVERSEAS OR NON-ACCREDITED LABORATORIES OFFERING 'CHRONIC LYME' PANELS — RESULTS ARE UNVALIDATED AND DRIVE HARMFUL LONG-COURSE ANTIBIOTICS.**

**THE AUSTRALIAN POSITION: LOCALLY ACQUIRED CLASSICAL LYME BORRELIOSIS IS NOT RECOGNISED HERE, SO THE DIAGNOSIS REQUIRES TRAVEL TO AN ENDEMIC REGION. Patients with a comparable illness WITHOUT that exposure are described under DSCATT — DEBILITATING SYMPTOM COMPLEXES ATTRIBUTED TO TICKS. HANDLE IT GENTLY: ACKNOWLEDGE THE SYMPTOMS, DECLINE THE UNVALIDATED TEST, AND OFFER STRUCTURED FOLLOW-UP.** VERIFY current SA Health guidance and notifiable status.

**EIGHT DIFFERENTIAL GROUPS, ANNOUNCED BY NAME — AN UNSPOKEN STRUCTURE SCORES NOTHING: RED FLAGS AND MALIGNANCY · INFECTION · THE ARTHRITIDES · SOFT TISSUE AND MUSCLE · NEUROLOGICAL · ENDOCRINE AND METABOLIC · MEDICATIONS · PSYCHOSOCIAL LAST.** **RED FLAGS ARE UNCONDITIONAL — EVERY AGE, EVERY DURATION, however infective the story looks.**
**PREVENTION COUNSELLING FOR FUTURE TRAVEL: LONG SLEEVES · PERMETHRIN-TREATED CLOTHING · DEET · DAILY TICK CHECKS INCLUDING SCALP AND GROIN · AND CORRECT TICK REMOVAL — FREEZE IT, DON'T SQUEEZE IT.**
plan: **WIPE, confirm her name, then: 'ARE YOU IN ANY PAIN RIGHT NOW? Would you like something for it before we talk?'** Then **confidentiality and an open question.**
**Validate and frame: 'your pain is real and I take it seriously. Let me ask you some questions so I can work out what is going on, and then I'll explain what I think and what we do next.'**

**EXPLORE THE PAIN: WHERE EXACTLY — JOINTS OR MUSCLES, NAME ME TWO OR THREE SPOTS · how long, sudden or gradual, constant or intermittent, getting worse · dull or sharp · does it travel · out of ten at its worst · anything better or worse · HOW IS IT AFFECTING YOUR LIFE?**

**PATTERN: pain at night · worse in the morning or at the end of the day · worse with rest or activity · morning stiffness and HOW LONG.** Then **the MSK screen: SWELLING · REDNESS OR RASHES — and this is where the forearm gets mentioned · stiffness moving the joints · recent injury or trauma.**
**SIGNPOST: 'I'm now going to run through a checklist of possible causes; some questions will sound unrelated, but I ask them of everyone with this problem.'**

**GROUP 1, RED FLAGS — UNCONDITIONAL EVEN THOUGH THE STORY LOOKS INFECTIVE: WEIGHT LOSS without trying · appetite · LUMPS OR BUMPS · unusually tired · NIGHT SWEATS SOAKING THE SHEETS · BONE PAIN, PARTICULARLY AT NIGHT.**
**GROUP 2, INFECTION — and then STOP AND DO ALL EIGHT TRAVEL QUESTIONS: any FEVER OR CHILLS · any FLU-LIKE ILLNESS · contact with anyone unwell or with animals · sore throat with swollen glands.**
**TRAVEL A: WHERE EXACTLY DID YOU GO AND HOW LONG WERE YOU THERE? TELL ME ABOUT THE ACTIVITIES YOU DID. TRAVEL B: ANY BUSHWALKING OR CAMPING, AND DID YOU NOTICE ANY TICK OR INSECT BITES?**
**Then DIRECTLY: 'DID YOU NOTICE A TICK, AND DID YOU PULL IT OFF?' — and how did you remove it?**

**TRAVEL C: ANY CONTACT WITH SICK PEOPLE OR ANIMALS WHILE AWAY? TRAVEL D: ANY DRUGS, OR MUCH ALCOHOL? TRAVEL E: ANY EXPOSURE TO BLOOD — TATTOOS, PIERCINGS, MEDICAL OR DENTAL PROCEDURES, TRANSFUSION?**
**TRAVEL F: ANY STREET FOOD OR UNTREATED WATER? TRAVEL G: DID YOU SEE A GP BEFORE TRAVELLING — VACCINES OR MALARIA TABLETS? TRAVEL H: DID YOU HAVE SEX WHILE OVERSEAS, AND DO YOU USE CONDOMS?**

**GROUP 3, THE ARTHRITIDES, quickly: family history of arthritis · deformity · RASHES, SCALY PATCHES OR NAIL CHANGES · fingers changing colour in the cold · mouth ulcers, hair loss, sun sensitivity · recent diarrhoea or discharge · RED OR PAINFUL EYES?**

**GROUP 4, SOFT TISSUE AND MUSCLE: ANY MEDICATIONS AT ALL, INCLUDING FROM THE CHEMIST OR HEALTH-FOOD SHOP · pain and stiffness across both shoulders and hips · struggling to get out of a chair, climb stairs or comb your hair?** Then **the GCA SCREEN given her age: NEW HEADACHE · SCALP TENDERNESS · JAW PAIN ON CHEWING · ANY CHANGE IN VISION.**

**GROUP 5, NEUROLOGICAL — and it matters here because Lyme disseminates: HEADACHES · pins and needles or numbness · weakness · problems with walking or balance · ANY WEAKNESS OF THE FACE · change in speech or vision.** Then **GROUP 6, ENDOCRINE: cold intolerance, constipation, thirst, polyuria.**
**GROUP 8, ANNOUNCED AS LAST: mood · sleep · who is at home and anything stressful · managing daily activities · and the self-harm question in long-standing pain.** Then **SADMA and close.**
**Take the card. DESCRIBE THE RASH RATHER THAN NAMING IT FIRST — an expanding red lesion with central clearing on the forearm, WITH A TENDER AXILLARY NODE.**
**NAME LYME DISEASE WITH THE THREE REASONS TOGETHER.** Then **the differentials by group name, each with a one-clause reason — and in an Australian patient, ROSS RIVER AND BARMAH FOREST FIRST.**

**THE PLAN: TREAT NOW WITH DOXYCYCLINE, DO NOT WAIT FOR SEROLOGY · two-tier serology at an ACCREDITED AUSTRALIAN LABORATORY · WARN ABOUT PHOTOSENSITIVITY AND THE JARISCH-HERXHEIMER REACTION · PREVENTION COUNSELLING for future travel · SAFETY-NET for CARDITIS, NEUROLOGICAL INVOLVEMENT OR ARTHRITIS.**

stem: Mrs Ellen Hartnett, 70, lives alone in a single-storey house. Admitted six days ago after a fall at home; fractured neck of femur repaired the next day. Medically stable, afebrile, wound clean; discharge planned within 48 hours. OT assessment today: independent with basic personal care (showers, toilets alone); needs assistance with meal preparation and cooking; balance impaired — holds furniture and walls when walking; mobility poor. Conclusion: not safe for discharge home unless proper support is in place.
Her son, Mr Ross Hartnett, 46, is in from a country town an hour away. Works full time, school-aged children. He cannot take her home or stay with her, and wants her discharged to her own house.
tasks: Explain the occupational therapist's report and what it means to the son
Discuss the discharge planning for this patient with him
findings: THIS IS NOT A DIAGNOSTIC STATION
IT IS A NEGOTIATION DRESSED AS AN EXPLANATION. The clinical content is easy; THE MARKS SIT IN HOW YOU HANDLE A RELATIVE ASKING YOU TO DO SOMETHING UNSAFE, FOR REASONS THAT ARE ENTIRELY UNDERSTANDABLE
THE OT REPORT, IN ONE SENTENCE

INDEPENDENT FOR PERSONAL ADLs — dressing, eating, ambulating, toileting, hygiene — BUT DEPENDENT FOR INSTRUMENTAL ADLs — shopping, housework, finances, FOOD PREPARATION, transport, medications. SAY THAT SENTENCE: IT IS THE THERAPIST'S OWN PHRASE AND IT SHOWS YOU READ THE REPORT
THE SON'S POSITION, AND WHY IT IS NOT UNREASONABLE

HE WORKS FULL TIME · HAS SCHOOL-AGED CHILDREN · LIVES AN HOUR AWAY · CANNOT TAKE HER HOME OR STAY WITH HER — AND WANTS HER DISCHARGED TO HER OWN HOUSE. He is FRIGHTENED, GUILTY AND STRETCHED. IF YOU MEET THAT WITH A RULE, YOU LOSE HIM; IF YOU MEET IT WITH AGREEMENT, YOU FAIL THE STATION
THE CONSENT SENTENCE — the station is lost in the first thirty seconds more often than the last

'I HAVE SPOKEN WITH YOUR MOTHER AND SHE IS HAPPY FOR ME TO GO THROUGH ALL OF THIS WITH YOU.' WITHOUT IT THE WHOLE CONVERSATION IS A CONFIDENTIALITY BREACH. If the stem does not say she consented, DO NOT INVENT IT AND DO NOT SKIP IT — say it as an action, and if the examiner says she has not been asked, GO AND ASK HER
HIS MENTAL MODEL IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM
'THE HIP IS FIXED, SO SHE CAN GO HOME.' EVERY LATER DISAGREEMENT FLOWS FROM IT. Correcting it in twenty seconds — REPAIRED, NOT RECOVERED — DOES MORE WORK THAN ANY SERVICE YOU CAN NAME
VERSION B — the reversal

A WORSE REPORT: she also needs help to SHOWER AND TRANSFER. HE DEMANDS PERMANENT NURSING HOME PLACEMENT BEFORE HE LEAVES — but nursing staff report SHE IS FULLY ALERT, ORIENTATED, AND HAS REPEATEDLY SAID SHE WANTS TO GO HOME. Added task: respond to the request for permanent residential care
VERSION C — the complaint
He opens by asking WHY HER OSTEOPOROSIS WAS NEVER TREATED AND WHETHER THE FALL WAS PREVENTABLE. A COMPLAINT PLUS A PLAN — no defensiveness, no blaming a colleague
THE LINE THAT RESOLVES THE WHOLE STATION

'THE AIM OF EVERYTHING I HAVE JUST DESCRIBED IS TO GET YOUR MOTHER HOME. THE QUESTION ISN'T WHETHER SHE GOES HOME — IT IS WHETHER SHE GOES HOME TODAY WITH NOTHING, OR IN A FEW WEEKS WITH THE SUPPORT THAT KEEPS HER THERE'
THE DINNER QUESTION, AND WHY IT WORKS

'CAN I PUT IT ANOTHER WAY? IF SHE WENT HOME THIS AFTERNOON, WHO WOULD COOK HER DINNER TONIGHT?' — THEN WAIT FOR THE ANSWER. It moves the argument FROM ABSTRACT SAFETY TO A CONCRETE FACT HE ALREADY KNOWS. MOST ROLE-PLAYERS DEFLATE HERE, AND THE EMOTION UNDERNEATH IS WHERE THE EMPATHY MARKS ARE
THE ONE HISTORY QUESTION YOU MUST STILL ASK

You should not run a history. But you cannot plan a discharge without one fact: 'CAN YOU DESCRIBE HER LIVING ARRANGEMENTS — WHO IS AT HOME WITH HER, AND WHAT SUPPORT DOES SHE ALREADY HAVE?' Ask it once, early, and LABEL IT: 'I just need one piece of information before we plan'

FAIL — Agreeing to an unsafe discharge: 'if you're sure, we could try it and see.'
FAIL — Never mentioning osteoporosis. Rails, meals and physio, and not one word about the bone.
FAIL — Never mentioning clot prevention, or letting the injection stop at the ward door.

dx: **POST-OPERATIVE FUNCTIONAL DECLINE AFTER A MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURED NECK OF FEMUR, in a woman who LIVES ALONE, with AN UNSAFE DISCHARGE ENVIRONMENT AND NO AVAILABLE CARER.** **THREE PROBLEMS STACKED: A BONE THAT BROKE TOO EASILY, A BODY THAT CANNOT YET DO WHAT IT MUST, AND A FAMILY THAT CANNOT FILL THE GAP.**

**MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE means AFTER A FALL FROM STANDING HEIGHT OR LESS. OVER 50 THIS IS OSTEOPOROSIS UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE — AND A HIP OR SPINE FRACTURE IS TREATED WHATEVER THE BONE DENSITY SHOWS.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE, MOVE ONE: REFUSE THE BINARY. He offers two doors — HOME TODAY OR A NURSING HOME. BOTH ARE WRONG, AND ARGUING INSIDE HIS FRAME LOSES EITHER WAY. NAME A THIRD PATH OUT LOUD, TIME-LIMITED: REHABILITATION NOW, THEN A BLOCK OF TRANSITION OR RESTORATIVE CARE, THEN HOME WITH SUPPORT — RESPITE AS A FALLBACK, NOT A DESTINATION.**
**'She is not safe to go home' ALONE IS HEARD AS OBSTRUCTIVE. 'All right, we'll try home' FAILS ON SAFETY. YOU MUST SAY THE MIDDLE, NOT IMPLY IT.**

**MOVE TWO: PUT THE PATIENT BACK IN THE ROOM. HE IS NOT THE DECISION-MAKER. Two sentences carry it — one at the start, one at the end: 'I'VE SPOKEN WITH YOUR MOTHER AND SHE'S HAPPY FOR ME TO GO THROUGH THIS WITH YOU' and 'NOTHING GETS DECIDED IN THIS ROOM. What I'd like to do is BRING THE THREE OF US TOGETHER WITH THE THERAPIST SO YOUR MUM CAN TELL US WHAT SHE WANTS.'**

**THE ONE-SENTENCE TEST AT SEVEN MINUTES: DID I OFFER A THIRD OPTION, AND DID I SAY HER NAME AS THE PERSON WHO DECIDES? BOTH YES, YOU HAVE PASSED. EITHER NO, YOU HAVE NOT — WHATEVER ELSE YOU COVERED.**

**IF HE DEMANDS PERMANENT CARE (Version B): 'I have to be straight with you: YOUR MOTHER MAKES THIS DECISION, NOT ME AND NOT YOU. She is alert and she has told the nurses she wants to go home — WE CANNOT PLACE HER ANYWHERE SHE DOES NOT AGREE TO. What we CAN offer is RESPITE: a short stay while we set up support at home, AND SHE COMES HOME AT THE END OF IT.'**

**DE-BLAME EXPLICITLY WHEN HE SAYS HE CANNOT HELP: 'thank you for being straight with me — THAT ISN'T A FAILING, and it helps. MY JOB IS TO BUILD A PLAN AROUND WHAT IS ACTUALLY POSSIBLE.'** Then **offer him CARER GATEWAY 1800 422 737.**

**CORRECTION — THE PROGRAMME NAMES CHANGED. HOME CARE PACKAGES AND SHORT-TERM RESTORATIVE CARE CEASED ON 1 NOVEMBER 2025, replaced by SUPPORT AT HOME under the Aged Care Act 2024. CHSP CONTINUES, transitioning no earlier than July 2027. SAFE WORDING: 'AN AGED CARE ASSESSMENT THROUGH MY AGED CARE, LEADING TO AN ONGOING SUPPORT-AT-HOME BUDGET' — NEVER QUOTE A PACKAGE LEVEL.** VERIFY.

**HONEST ABOUT RECOVERY: SIX TO TWELVE MONTHS, MOST GAIN IN THE FIRST THREE, AND SOME PEOPLE SETTLE BELOW THEIR PREVIOUS LEVEL. Never 'she'll be back to normal in a few weeks' — honest, then immediately constructive.**
plan: **WASH OR GEL AND OFFER HIM A SEAT — STANDING OVER A RELATIVE READS AS A VERDICT.** Then **CONFIRM WHO HE IS: 'are you Mrs Hartnett's son?' — KNOW WHO YOU ARE SPEAKING TO BEFORE YOU DISCLOSE ANYTHING.** Then **a quiet room, not the corridor.**

**THE APOLOGY AND THE CONSENT SENTENCE: 'I'm sorry to hear your mum has been unwell — it must have been a worrying week. I'VE SPOKEN WITH HER AND SHE'S HAPPY FOR ME TO GO THROUGH EVERYTHING WITH YOU.'** Then **ASSESS UNDERSTANDING FIRST: 'before I start — CAN YOU TELL ME WHAT HAS HAPPENED SO FAR, AS YOU UNDERSTAND IT?'** **NEVER OPEN WITH THE REPORT.**

**SIGNPOST, THEN THE AGENDA QUESTION — a scoring item, not a courtesy: 'IS THERE ANYTHING IN PARTICULAR YOU'RE WORRIED ABOUT THAT YOU WANT TO MAKE SURE WE COVER?'** **The hidden agenda is almost never 'what services are available' — it is 'I FEEL LIKE A BAD SON', 'I CANNOT AFFORD THIS' OR 'IS SHE DYING?'**
**THE ONE FACT YOU NEED, LABELLED: 'I just need one piece of information before we plan — WHO IS AT HOME WITH HER, AND WHAT SUPPORT DOES SHE ALREADY HAVE?'**

**SUMMARISE HER CONDITION BEFORE EXPLAINING ANYTHING — and correct the mental model: 'a hip fracture has A LONG RECOVERY PHASE, usually AT LEAST SIX MONTHS, SOMETIMES A YEAR. THE OPERATION IS THE START OF THE RECOVERY, NOT THE END OF IT.'**

**THE REPORT, LEADING WITH WHAT SHE CAN DO: 'the GOOD NEWS is she can SHOWER AND USE THE TOILET ON HER OWN — that is genuinely important, and A LOT OF PEOPLE CAN'T AFTER THIS OPERATION. Where she needs help is PREPARING MEALS AND COOKING. And HER BALANCE IS NOT SAFE — she is HOLDING ONTO THE FURNITURE.'** Then **the technical phrase ONCE, immediately explained.**

**BOX 1, PAIN: 'if it is not controlled she won't move, and IF SHE DOESN'T MOVE SHE WON'T RECOVER. She goes home with A WRITTEN PAIN PLAN, NOT JUST A SCRIPT. Some painkillers MAKE PEOPLE DROWSY OR UNSTEADY, WHICH INCREASES THE RISK OF ANOTHER FALL. The aim is NOT to be completely pain-free — it is to control it to the level where SHE CAN DO HER DAILY ACTIVITIES.'**

**BOX 2, BALANCE AND MOBILITY: PHYSIOTHERAPY, THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THE RECOVERY — balance training and strengthening · AND A WALKING AID CHOSEN AND FITTED BY THE PHYSIOTHERAPIST, because AN AID AT THE WRONG HEIGHT CAUSES FALLS RATHER THAN PREVENTING THEM.**

**BOX 3, HOME SAFETY: AN OT HOME VISIT — a HAZARD ASSESSMENT AT THE HOUSE with specific recommendations: GRAB RAILS BY THE TOILET AND SHOWER, HANDRAILS ON THE STEPS, NON-SLIP MATS, BETTER LIGHTING, RUGS REMOVED OR SECURED · AND A PERSONAL ALARM SHE WEARS, SO IF SHE DOES FALL SHE ISN'T ON THE FLOOR FOR HOURS.**

**BOX 4, SUPPORT AT HOME — the piece that answers his question: 'I can arrange AN AGED CARE ASSESSMENT through MY AGED CARE, and I'LL START THAT TODAY RATHER THAN ON THE DAY SHE LEAVES, BECAUSE THAT IS WHAT SHORTENS THE WAIT.'** Then **what the assessor arranges: help with COOKING, CLEANING AND SHOPPING, personal care, community nursing, MEALS ON WHEELS — and SHORT-TERM CARE, OR A RESIDENTIAL PLACE WHICH CAN BE RESPITE RATHER THAN PERMANENT.**

**THE THIRD OPTION, NAMED AS THREE STAGES: REHABILITATION NOW, usually a couple of weeks and THE PART THAT ACTUALLY GETS HER WALKING · THEN TRANSITION CARE, UP TO ABOUT TWELVE WEEKS at home or in a bed · THEN HOME WITH ONGOING SERVICES. EVERY STAGE OF THAT IS AIMED AT HOME. WOULD YOU BE ABLE TO LIVE WITH THAT?'**

**BOX 5 — SAY BOTH BEFORE 7:00, WHATEVER ELSE IS UNFINISHED. BONE: 'she broke her hip FALLING AT STANDING HEIGHT — a MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE, and it tells us the bone is more fragile than it should be. THAT IS OSTEOPOROSIS. We will do a bone density scan, BUT BECAUSE IT WAS A HIP FRACTURE WE START TREATMENT REGARDLESS OF WHAT THE SCAN SHOWS — THE FRACTURE ITSELF IS THE DIAGNOSIS.'**

**CLOTS: 'after a hip operation, and because she is moving less, THERE IS A REAL RISK OF A CLOT IN THE LEG THAT CAN TRAVEL TO THE LUNGS. So she goes home ON A BLOOD-THINNING INJECTION FOR A SET PERIOD — UP TO ABOUT FIVE WEEKS FROM THE OPERATION — and then it stops. IT DOESN'T MEAN SHE STAYS IN BED; THE OPPOSITE — MOVING IS PART OF THE TREATMENT.'**

**BOX 6, REVIEW AND THE GERIATRIC SCREEN: FRACTURE CLINIC AT ABOUT SIX WEEKS · GP WITHIN A WEEK OF GETTING HOME · A FALLS ASSESSMENT, BECAUSE THE MOST IMPORTANT THING WE CAN DO IS WORK OUT WHY SHE FELL · lying and standing BP, a MEDICATION REVIEW, eyes, hearing and feet · AND HER MOOD AND MEMORY BEFORE SHE GOES.**
**If he pushes again, THE HOLD AND THEN THE DINNER QUESTION — and WAIT FOR THE ANSWER.**
**THE LINE THAT RESOLVES IT — home today with nothing, or in a few weeks with the support that keeps her there.**

**CLOSE BY PUTTING HER BACK IN THE ROOM: 'NOTHING GETS DECIDED HERE. I'd like to BRING THE THREE OF US TOGETHER WITH THE THERAPIST so your mum can tell us what she wants.'** Then **CARER GATEWAY for him, and 'what have I missed for you?'**
