**BONE: any MINIMAL-TRAUMA HIP OR VERTEBRAL FRACTURE OVER 50 IS TREATED REGARDLESS OF THE DXA T-SCORE — SCAN FOR A BASELINE TO MONITOR, NOT TO DECIDE. ZOLEDRONIC ACID 5 mg IV ONCE YEARLY over at least 15 minutes, given AT LEAST TWO WEEKS AFTER THE REPAIR, needing eGFR ABOVE ABOUT 35 and a VITAMIN D REPLETE, NORMOCALCAEMIC patient first; warn about a FLU-LIKE REACTION after the first dose. Alternatives: DENOSUMAB 60 mg SUBCUT SIX-MONTHLY, NEVER STOPPED WITHOUT A REPLACEMENT AGENT because of REBOUND VERTEBRAL FRACTURES; or ALENDRONATE 70 mg WEEKLY. COLECALCIFEROL 1000–2000 IU DAILY, CALCIUM 1300 mg/DAY.** VERIFY.

**CLOTS: ENOXAPARIN 40 mg SUBCUT DAILY FOR UP TO 35 DAYS FROM HIP FRACTURE SURGERY; 20 mg DAILY IF CREATININE CLEARANCE BELOW 30. Add MECHANICAL PROPHYLAXIS AND MOBILISATION FROM DAY ONE, and ARRANGE DISTRICT NURSING OR TEACH THE INJECTION BEFORE DISCHARGE.** **CORRECTION: RIVAROXABAN AND APIXABAN ARE APPROVED AFTER ELECTIVE HIP AND KNEE REPLACEMENT, NOT AFTER HIP FRACTURE SURGERY, where LOW MOLECULAR WEIGHT HEPARIN IS STANDARD.** VERIFY.

**PAIN: REGULAR PARACETAMOL 1 g FOUR TIMES DAILY, MAXIMUM 3 g DAILY IF FRAIL, UNDER ABOUT 50 kg, OR LIVER DISEASE. A short course of LOW-DOSE IMMEDIATE-RELEASE OXYCODONE for breakthrough, WITH A REGULAR APERIENT. AVOID NSAIDs, TRAMADOL AND LONG-ACTING OPIOIDS, AND NEVER A BENZODIAZEPINE 'FOR SLEEP'.** **CORRECTION: the post-fracture analgesic plan is WRITTEN BY THE TREATING TEAM AND CONTINUED BY THE GP — A PAIN CLINIC IS FOR PAIN PERSISTING BEYOND THE EXPECTED RECOVERY PERIOD.** VERIFY.

**CORRECTION — DO NOT SAY 'I'LL DO AN MMSE': it is COPYRIGHT RESTRICTED IN AUSTRALIA and less sensitive here. Use the 4AT FOR DELIRIUM and the MoCA FOR COGNITION ONCE SETTLED; RUDAS for culturally and linguistically diverse patients, KICA-COG for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients, GDS-15 FOR MOOD.**

**Do not miss: OSTEOPOROSIS TREATMENT, THE SINGLE MOST-DROPPED ITEM · EXTENDED VTE PROPHYLAXIS, AND THAT IT CONTINUES AFTER DISCHARGE · HER CONSENT, HER CAPACITY, HER WISHES · DELIRIUM, which is REVERSIBLE AND INVALIDATES ANY CAPACITY JUDGEMENT MADE TODAY · A CARDIAC OR SYNCOPAL CAUSE FOR THE FALL · WOUND OR JOINT INFECTION, ANAEMIA, CONSTIPATION, RETENTION · DEPRESSION AND FEAR OF FALLING · ELDER ABUSE — ASK YOURSELF WHOSE INTERESTS THE DISCHARGE PRESSURE SERVES · THE CAUSE OF THE FALL, because A FRACTURE TREATED WITHOUT A FALLS ASSESSMENT IS HALF A JOB.**

**SA: MY AGED CARE 1800 200 422, with the HOSPITAL SOCIAL WORKER STARTING THE ASSESSMENT WHILE SHE IS STILL AN INPATIENT. In MM5, COUNTRY HEALTH CONNECT runs community nursing and personal care, ALLIED HEALTH IS THIN, SO BOOK AT REFERRAL NOT DISCHARGE, and PATS covers travel to the metropolitan fracture clinic and DXA.** **A RELATIVE CANNOT CONSENT FOR A COMPETENT PATIENT, WHO MAY DECIDE UNWISELY. Elder abuse: SA 1800 372 310, national 1800 353 374. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are eligible for aged care assessment FROM 50. INTERPRETERS THROUGH TIS NATIONAL 131 450 — NEVER THE SON.**

stem: Mrs Denise Harper, 60, retired schoolteacher, tripped over a garden hose this afternoon and fell onto her outstretched right hand. No LOC, no head strike. BP 138/82 · HR 78 reg · RR 16 · T 36.7 · SpO2 98% RA · BGL 5.8. Isolated right wrist injury, skin intact, neurovascularly normal. X-ray: minimally displaced extra-articular Colles' fracture, acceptable alignment. Paracetamol and ibuprofen given. Below-elbow plaster of Paris applied; post-cast neurovascular check normal. Ready for discharge.
tasks: Explain to Mrs Harper how to care for the plaster at home
Explain your follow-up plan
Answer her questions
findings: THIS IS NOT A CAST-CARE STATION

IT IS A FRACTURE-AFTERCARE STATION WEARING A CAST-CARE COSTUME. Candidates fail HAVING GIVEN FAULTLESS PLASTER ADVICE, because plaster advice is THE PART EVERYBODY PREPARES AND IT IS WORTH THE LEAST. THE LAST THREE MINUTES CARRY MORE MARKS THAN THE FIRST FIVE
THE THREE TAILS THAT DECIDE IT

THE RED FLAGS · THE PHYSIOTHERAPY · AND THE REASON A 60-YEAR-OLD'S BONE BROKE IN A FALL FROM STANDING HEIGHT. SAY THE PHRASE 'MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE' OUT LOUD AND NAME THE DEXA — ARRANGING IT SILENTLY IN YOUR HEAD DOES NOT SCORE
SIGNPOST FIVE HEADINGS — the highest-yield line in the station

'I'd like to cover FIVE THINGS: what you've actually broken, how to look after the plaster, THE WARNING SIGNS THAT WOULD BRING YOU STRAIGHT BACK, the plan over the next six weeks, AND ONE IMPORTANT THING ABOUT YOUR BONES.' It BUYS THE EXAMINER'S PATIENCE — once you have named five headings, the examiner KNOWS THE BONE CONVERSATION IS COMING AND STOPS MARKING YOU DOWN FOR NOT HAVING REACHED IT
FOUR CAST-CARE GROUPS — say the four words before you start
SWELLING · DRY · CLEAN · MOVING. ALMOST EVERY ITEM OF CAST-CARE ADVICE THAT EXISTS SITS UNDER ONE OF THEM, and the grouping IS WHAT STOPS YOU RAMBLING. Keep the whole block to TWO AND A HALF MINUTES
THE TRAP INSIDE THE PLASTER ADVICE

'REST IT AND KEEP IT STILL' SOUNDS CARING AND IS WRONG. You are immobilising A WRIST, NOT AN ARM. The line the examiner wants: THE WRIST STAYS STILL, EVERYTHING ELSE KEEPS MOVING. Fingers, elbow and shoulder are free and must be used
GET THE RINGS OFF BEFORE SHE LEAVES
IF THE FINGERS SWELL TONIGHT A RING BECOMES A TOURNIQUET and they end up being cut off
CORRECTION — blue fingers are a LATE sign

COLOUR CHANGE AND PULSELESSNESS ARE LATE IN A TIGHT FOREARM. THE EARLIEST RELIABLE WARNINGS ARE PAIN OUT OF PROPORTION, PAIN THAT ESCALATES RATHER THAN SETTLES, PAIN NOT RELIEVED BY ADEQUATE ANALGESIA, AND PAIN ON PASSIVE EXTENSION OF THE FINGERS. Teach the early ones first, keep colour change because IT IS THE EASIEST SIGN FOR A PATIENT TO RECOGNISE
CORRECTION — a complete plaster on day one is itself the risk

Standard Australian practice for an ACUTE distal radius fracture is A BACKSLAB, OR A COMPLETED CAST SPLIT DOWN TO SKIN, precisely because SWELLING PEAKS AT 24–48 HOURS. The stem hands you a complete POP, so RUN THE STATION AS WRITTEN — but if challenged, say you would want it UNIVALVED BEFORE DISCHARGE, or at minimum EXPLICIT INSTRUCTIONS TO RETURN IMMEDIATELY FOR SPLITTING
THE FALLS QUESTION IS NOT OPTIONAL

'DID YOU TRIP, OR DID YOU FEEL DIZZY OR FAINT OR BLACK OUT AT ALL BEFOREHAND?' A fall in a 60-year-old is EITHER MECHANICAL OR A SYNCOPAL EVENT THAT HAPPENS TO HAVE PRODUCED A WRIST FRACTURE, AND THOSE ARE DIFFERENT DISEASES. IF SHE BLACKED OUT, THIS STATION STOPS BEING ABOUT PLASTER
THE HIDDEN AGENDA, AND WHERE IT HIDES

In several recalls she is THE SOLE CARER FOR A DEPENDENT HUSBAND, or LIVES ALONE OUT OF TOWN AND CANNOT DRIVE. If you never ask 'IS THERE ANYTHING WORRYING YOU ABOUT GOING HOME?', A WELL-BRIEFED ROLE-PLAYER RAISES IT IN THE LAST THIRTY SECONDS. Ask at the start, and again before you close

dx: **MINIMALLY DISPLACED COLLES' FRACTURE — an EXTRA-ARTICULAR fracture of the DISTAL RADIUS, within about 2 cm of the joint, with DORSAL DISPLACEMENT AND DORSAL ANGULATION of the distal fragment. VOLAR DISPLACEMENT INSTEAD WOULD MAKE IT A SMITH'S FRACTURE. Classically follows A FALL ONTO THE OUTSTRETCHED HAND.**
**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: GETTING PAST THE PLASTER TO THE THREE TAILS. The examiner is LISTENING FOR THE WORDS 'MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE' AND 'DEXA'.**

**THE BONE BLOCK, VERBATIM: 'you broke this bone FALLING FROM STANDING HEIGHT, ON THE FLAT. A HEALTHY BONE AT YOUR AGE SHOULDN'T BREAK FROM A FALL LIKE THAT. We call that a MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE, and it's a signal THE BONE MAY BE THINNER THAN IT SHOULD BE — that's OSTEOPOROSIS. So I'm going to arrange a BONE-DENSITY SCAN, called a DEXA, and some blood tests. TREATING IT NOW CUTS THE CHANCE OF THE NEXT FRACTURE — WHICH COULD BE A HIP — SUBSTANTIALLY.'**

**THE FOLLOW-UP PLAN IS A PICTURE, NOT A PHRASE: 'FRACTURE CLINIC IN ONE WEEK. They'll take ANOTHER X-RAY then, because OCCASIONALLY THESE SLIP IN THE FIRST WEEK OR TWO, and it's MUCH EASIER TO FIX EARLY. If the position is good, the plaster stays on until ABOUT SIX WEEKS, and then IT COMES OFF AT THE CLINIC — NOT AT HOME.'**

**THEN PHYSIOTHERAPY, SAID OUT LOUD: 'when it comes off, EXPECT A STIFF WRIST AND A WEAKER ARM. THAT IS NORMAL AFTER SIX WEEKS IN PLASTER, NOT A COMPLICATION. I'll arrange PHYSIOTHERAPY, or a HAND THERAPIST — it usually takes A COUPLE OF MONTHS OF EXERCISES to get most of your movement and grip back.'**

**TWO FAMILIES OF RED FLAGS, EACH WITH AN ACTION. TIGHT CAST: escalating pain, pain not eased by painkillers, PAIN ON STRAIGHTENING THE FINGERS, pins and needles, numbness, pale or blue or cold fingers, inability to move them → COME STRAIGHT BACK TO EMERGENCY, DON'T WAIT FOR THE CLINIC. SKIN AND INFECTION: fever, BAD SMELL, discharge or staining through the plaster, A FIXED BURNING SPOT, new blister or raw skin at the edge → SAME DAY, GP OR US.**

**CORRECTION — THE TREATMENT THRESHOLD. You will hear it given as a T-score of about −1 or −1.5. THAT IS NOT RIGHT. OSTEOPOROSIS IS A T-SCORE OF −2.5 OR LOWER; −1.0 TO −2.5 IS OSTEOPENIA.** **More importantly, IN A WOMAN OF 60 WHO HAS JUST FRACTURED FROM A STANDING FALL, THE FRACTURE ITSELF ESTABLISHES CLINICAL OSTEOPOROSIS — A DEXA IN THE OSTEOPENIC RANGE DOES NOT CANCEL THAT, IT GIVES A BASELINE TO MONITOR AGAINST.** VERIFY current PBS wording.

**IF ASKED 'WHAT IF THE DEXA IS NORMAL?': 'A NORMAL DEXA WOULD NOT REASSURE ME ON ITS OWN. She has had A FRAGILITY FRACTURE, WHICH ROUGHLY DOUBLES HER RISK OF THE NEXT ONE, so I would still address calcium, vitamin D, exercise, smoking and falls risk, LOOK FOR SECONDARY CAUSES, and discuss pharmacological therapy with her GP.'**

**VERSION B, THE RESISTANT PATIENT: NAME IT ONCE, OFFER, ACCEPT A 'NO' WITHOUT ABANDONING IT, AND DOCUMENT. 'That's completely your decision and I WON'T PUSH IT. I do want to be straight with you though: A BROKEN WRIST FROM A SIMPLE TRIP IS OFTEN THE FIRST SIGN OF THINNING BONES, AND THE NEXT ONE CAN BE A HIP. I'LL PUT IT IN THE LETTER TO YOUR GP SO YOU CAN PICK IT UP WHENEVER YOU'RE READY.'** **PUSHING HARDER FAILS; DROPPING IT ALSO FAILS.**

**VERSION C, THE CHILD: DO NOT TRANSPLANT THE ADULT ENDING — NO DEXA, NO FALLS CLINIC. A BUCKLE (TORUS) FRACTURE gets a REMOVABLE WRIST SPLINT OR CAST FOR 3–4 WEEKS, and a ROUTINE REPEAT X-RAY IS USUALLY NOT NEEDED. The parent needs RED FLAGS TRANSLATED FOR A CHILD: 'IF HE STOPS USING HIS FINGERS, OR HE'S CRYING WITH PAIN THAT THE PARACETAMOL WON'T TOUCH, BRING HIM STRAIGHT BACK.'** VERIFY.
plan: **WIPE and sit down. Then TWO QUESTIONS BEFORE ANY INSTRUCTIONS: 'HOW IS THE PAIN RIGHT NOW? And IS THERE ANYTHING IN PARTICULAR THAT'S WORRYING YOU ABOUT GOING HOME WITH THIS ON?'**
**SIGNPOST THE FIVE HEADINGS — and commit yourself to the bone conversation in front of the examiner.**

**BLOCK 1: 'you've broken THE END OF ONE OF THE TWO BONES IN YOUR FOREARM — the RADIUS, just above the wrist. THE BROKEN END HAS TIPPED SLIGHTLY BACKWARDS, and when it does that we call it A COLLES' FRACTURE. The pieces are STILL LINED UP WELL, so this can be treated IN A PLASTER RATHER THAN WITH AN OPERATION.'** **SHOW IT ON YOUR OWN FOREARM — examiners notice. And POINT OUT THE FREE THUMB: 'if you'd broken the little SCAPHOID bone instead, we'd have wrapped the thumb in too.'**

**NAME THE FOUR GROUPS, THEN RUN THEM. SWELLING — the whole point: KEEP THE ARM UP, a sling by day and ON A COUPLE OF PILLOWS AT NIGHT SO THE HAND SITS HIGHER THAN YOUR HEART · ICE wrapped in a thin towel ON TOP OF THE PLASTER, 15–20 MINUTES EVERY TWO OR THREE HOURS for the first few days · KEEP THE FINGERS MOVING, a full fist and straighten right out, EVERY HOUR WHILE AWAKE.**

**DRY: 'yours is PLASTER OF PARIS, and IF IT GETS WET IT GOES SOFT AND STOPS HOLDING THE BONE. For showering, TWO PLASTIC BAGS with the top one TAPED TO YOUR SKIN. If it does get damp, A HAIRDRYER ON THE COOL SETTING — NEVER WARM OR HOT, BECAUSE YOU CAN BURN SKIN YOU CAN'T SEE. No swimming and no baths for six weeks.'**

**CLEAN AND INTACT: 'NOTHING GOES DOWN INSIDE THE PLASTER — no knitting needles, pens or coat hangers, NO MATTER HOW MADDENING THE ITCH GETS. No powder, no lotion, no oil near the edges. If it itches, BLOW COOL AIR DOWN IT. DON'T TRIM OR PAD THE EDGES YOURSELF. And for the first day rest it on SOMETHING SOFT, because plaster of Paris TAKES A DAY OR TWO TO FULLY HARDEN.'**
**MOVING: 'your FINGERS, ELBOW AND SHOULDER ARE ALL FREE AND I WANT YOU USING THEM.'** Then **GET THE RINGS OFF NOW, in the room.**

**RED FLAGS, FAMILY ONE — AND LEAD WITH THE EARLY SIGNS: 'if the pain GETS WORSE RATHER THAN BETTER, or your painkillers STOP TOUCHING IT, or it HURTS TO STRAIGHTEN YOUR FINGERS, or they go NUMB OR TINGLY, LOOK PALE OR BLUE OR FEEL COLD, or you CAN'T MOVE THEM — COME STRAIGHT BACK TO EMERGENCY, DON'T WAIT FOR THE CLINIC. WE CAN SPLIT THE PLASTER IN A COUPLE OF MINUTES AND THAT FIXES IT.'**

**FAMILY TWO: 'a FEVER, a BAD SMELL coming from the plaster, ANY OOZE OR STAINING through it, or a BURNING, RUBBING PAIN IN ONE FIXED SPOT. That can mean A PRESSURE SORE OR AN INFECTION UNDER THERE, and BECAUSE WE CAN'T SEE IN, YOU HAVE TO TELL US. SAME DAY — your GP or us.'**
**THE FOLLOW-UP PLAN: CLINIC AT SEVEN DAYS WITH A REPEAT X-RAY · CAST OFF AT ABOUT SIX WEEKS, AT THE CLINIC NOT AT HOME · AND A LETTER TO YOUR GP TODAY.**
**PHYSIOTHERAPY, NAMED — and NORMALISE THE STIFFNESS FIRST so it is not heard as a complication.**
**THE BONE BLOCK, VERBATIM — minimal-trauma fracture, DEXA, bloods, and the offer: 'IS THAT SOMETHING YOU'D BE HAPPY FOR ME TO ORGANISE?'**
**AND IN THE SAME BREATH, THE FALLS QUESTION: 'can I just check — DID YOU TRIP, OR DID YOU FEEL DIZZY OR FAINT OR BLACK OUT AT ALL BEFOREHAND?'**
**DRIVING, which most candidates omit: NOT WHILE THE ARM IS IN PLASTER, AND NOT WHILE TAKING ANYTHING THAT MAKES HER DROWSY. Offer to WRITE IT DOWN AND HELP SORT TRANSPORT.**
**Return to the agenda you asked about at the start — the husband, the distance, whatever she raised — and BUILD THE PRACTICAL PLAN AROUND IT.**
**A WRITTEN CAST-CARE FACT SHEET PLUS THE DEPARTMENT'S PHONE NUMBER.** Then **TEACH-BACK BEFORE SHE STANDS UP: 'what are the two things that would bring you straight back?'**
pefe: **Do now: RE-CHECK AND DOCUMENT DISTAL NEUROVASCULAR STATUS — capillary refill, sensation in MEDIAN, ULNAR AND RADIAL territories, active finger flexion and extension, AND PAIN ON PASSIVE STRETCH · CHECK THE CAST — elbow free, thumb free, EDGE PROXIMAL TO THE KNUCKLE CREASES, no sharp edges, ONE FINGER SLIDES UNDER THE EDGE · RINGS AND TIGHT JEWELLERY OFF · SLING FITTED AND ELEVATION DEMONSTRATED RATHER THAN DESCRIBED.**

**Analgesia: PARACETAMOL 1 g FOUR TIMES DAILY, MAX 4 g/DAY · IBUPROFEN 200–400 mg THREE TIMES DAILY WITH FOOD if renal function and comorbidity allow · a short course of OXYCODONE 5 mg AS NEEDED ONLY IF SEVERE, WITH AN APERIENT.** **AVOID NSAIDs WITHOUT THOUGHT in an older patient, renal impairment, peptic ulcer disease, or on an ACE inhibitor and a diuretic.** VERIFY.

**Do next: DAY 7 fracture clinic with repeat X-ray and cast check · WEEK 2 a further film IF THE FRACTURE WAS REDUCED, because LATE DISPLACEMENT CLUSTERS IN THE FIRST FORTNIGHT · WEEK 6 cast off with clinical and radiographic union · then PHYSIOTHERAPY OR HAND THERAPY, 6–12 WEEKS of stretching and strengthening.**

**BONE-HEALTH WORKUP: DEXA OF LUMBAR SPINE AND HIP, MEDICARE-REBATED AFTER A MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE · bloods — CALCIUM, PHOSPHATE, ALP, 25-HYDROXY VITAMIN D, UEC WITH eGFR, LFT, FBE, ESR OR CRP, TFT; ADD PROTEIN ELECTROPHORESIS AND FREE LIGHT CHAINS, COELIAC SEROLOGY OR PTH where the picture suggests it · CALCIUM ABOUT 1300 mg/DAY FROM DIET FIRST · VITAMIN D TO KEEP 25-OH-D ABOVE 50 nmol/L · weight-bearing and resistance exercise, QUITLINE 13 7848 · ANTIRESORPTIVE THERAPY PER PBS CRITERIA, WITH A DENTAL CHECK FIRST.** VERIFY.
**THE DISCHARGE SUMMARY MUST CONTAIN THE WORDS 'MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE — PLEASE ARRANGE DEXA AND BONE-HEALTH BLOODS'. Book fracture clinic day 7 WITH THE X-RAY REQUEST ALREADY WRITTEN.**

**Do not miss: MEDIAN NERVE SYMPTOMS BEFORE SHE IS DISCHARGED · THE SECOND INJURY — head strike, hip, ribs, the other wrist · AN OPEN FRACTURE, where ANY SKIN BREACH CHANGES EVERYTHING · WHY SHE FELL, mechanical or syncopal.**

**COMPARTMENT SYNDROME IF IT DEVELOPS: SPLIT THE CAST TO SKIN AT ONCE, ALL LAYERS, LIMB AT HEART LEVEL — NOT ELEVATED — analgesia, URGENT ORTHOPAEDICS, fasciotomy if it does not settle. MUSCLE TOLERATES ABOUT 4–6 HOURS.** **MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 if retrieval is needed; PATS where the DEXA or clinic is more than 100 km away.**

findings: THE DEXA REPORT — interpret it, do not read it

L1–L4 BMD 0.882, T −2.1, Z −1.2 · FEMORAL NECK 0.811, T −1.4, Z −0.8 · TOTAL HIP 0.848, T −1.3, Z −0.7. IGNORE THE RAW BMD. IGNORE THE Z-SCORE. NAME THE T-SCORE, NAME THE RANGE, THEN NAME THE CONDITION
THE BLOODS ARE NORMAL FOR A REASON

FBE · FASTING GLUCOSE · UEC, CREATININE AND eGFR · LFT · TSH ALL NORMAL. CORRECTED CALCIUM 2.38. TOGETHER THEY EXCLUDE RENAL, HEPATIC, THYROID, DIABETIC, MYELOMA-TYPE AND CALCIUM CAUSES. SAY THAT OUT LOUD — IT IS WORTH MARKS AND TAKES FOUR SECONDS. The one abnormal: 25-OH VITAMIN D 30, when it should be above 50
THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES THE STATION

'HAVE YOU EVER BROKEN A BONE — EVEN YEARS AGO, AND EVEN IF IT SEEMED MINOR AT THE TIME?' MISS IT AND YOU CANNOT CHOOSE A MANAGEMENT PLAN. In the recalls THE ANSWER IS NO — WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY CANDIDATES STOP ASKING IT, AND EXACTLY WHY THE EXAMINER IS LISTENING FOR IT
THE TRAP BUILT INTO THE STEM

The stem gives a man on an INHALED corticosteroid and TEMPTS YOU TO DISMISS IT. INHALED CORTICOSTEROID STILL COUNTS AS GLUCOCORTICOID EXPOSURE FOR BONE, AND THE REPEATED ORAL COURSES COUNT FOR MUCH MORE. BOTH BELONG IN YOUR CONTRIBUTING-FACTORS ANSWER
THE EIGHT-DAY PREDNISOLONE IS AN ERROR TO CORRECT

ASK ABOUT DAIRY SPECIFICALLY, NOT 'HOW IS YOUR DIET?'

A general question gets 'PRETTY GOOD, DOCTOR' AND YOU SCORE NOTHING. Same rule as asking specifically about red meat in an iron-deficiency station. NAME THE FOOD GROUP: 'milk, cheese, yoghurt — roughly how much in a day?'
FIVE SECONDS TO SEPARATE A FALL FROM A FAINT

'WHEN YOU FALL, DO YOU BLACK OUT COMPLETELY, OR ARE YOU AWARE THE WHOLE TIME?' IF HE BLACKS OUT, THIS IS NO LONGER AN OSTEOPENIA STATION — IT IS A SYNCOPE STATION, and the priority becomes AN ECG AND A POSTURAL BLOOD PRESSURE. In the recalls HE IS AWARE THROUGHOUT AND TRIPS MECHANICALLY

dx: **OSTEOPENIA ON DEXA — a T-SCORE BETWEEN −1.0 AND −2.5 at the lumbar spine, femoral neck or total hip — WITH VITAMIN D DEFICIENCY, GLUCOCORTICOID EXPOSURE AND RECURRENT FALLS. THREE DIAGNOSES IN ONE PATIENT, AND THE EXAMINER MARKS ALL THREE.**

**OSTEOPOROSIS IS A T-SCORE AT OR BELOW −2.5, OR ANY MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE OF THE HIP OR SPINE REGARDLESS OF THE T-SCORE.** **NORMAL IS ANYTHING AT OR ABOVE −1.0 — the WHO recognises THREE CATEGORIES, NOT FOUR.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: ASKING WHETHER HE HAS EVER BROKEN A BONE — AND THEN BEING VISIBLY SEEN TO BRANCH YOUR MANAGEMENT ON HIS ANSWER.** **Candidates who fail ALMOST ALWAYS KNOW THE DRUGS. What they do is RECITE A MEMORISED OSTEOPENIA PLAN WITHOUT ESTABLISHING WHICH OF THE THREE PLANS APPLIES.**

**THREE BRANCHES: HIP OR VERTEBRAL MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE → TREAT, ANY T-SCORE. OTHER MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE → TREAT IF T IS −1.5 OR LOWER. NO FRACTURE → CALCULATE THE RISK FIRST.** **A wrist fracture moves the threshold from −2.5 to −1.5 — which in this man with a spine T of −2.1 IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A TABLET AND NO TABLET.**

**REPEAT HIS ANSWER BACK BEFORE YOU BRANCH — IT IS NOT ENOUGH TO ASK AND HEAR THE ANSWER, THE EXAMINER NEEDS TO HEAR YOU USE IT: 'you've told me you've NEVER BROKEN A BONE, and your scan shows OSTEOPENIA RATHER THAN OSTEOPOROSIS. That means I'M NOT GOING TO START A BONE TABLET TODAY. What I WILL do is put your details into A FRACTURE RISK CALCULATOR.'**

**CORRECTION — DO NOT SAY 'YOUR BONES ARE SOFT'. SOFT BONE IS OSTEOMALACIA, A MINERALISATION DEFECT AND A DIFFERENT DISEASE. In osteopenia the bone is NORMALLY MINERALISED BUT THERE IS LESS OF IT. Say: 'YOUR BONES HAVE THINNED — THERE'S LESS BONE THERE THAN THERE SHOULD BE.'**

**CORRECTION — IT IS HYPOCALCAEMIA, NOT HYPERCALCAEMIA, THAT YOU CHECK FOR BEFORE ZOLEDRONIC ACID OR DENOSUMAB. THESE ARE ANTIRESORPTIVE: THEY STOP BONE RELEASING CALCIUM INTO THE BLOOD, so the danger — PARTICULARLY WITH AN UNCORRECTED VITAMIN D DEFICIENCY, AS HERE — IS SYMPTOMATIC HYPOCALCAEMIA with TINGLING, CRAMPS, TETANY and rarely SEIZURES.**

**PREMATURE CLOSURE IS THE COMMONEST REASONING ERROR: 'he's on steroids, so it's steroid-induced bone loss' IS PROBABLY RIGHT — BUT SAYING IT WITHOUT FIRST CONFIRMING THE NORMAL BLOODS IS GUESSING THAT HAPPENS TO BE CORRECT. THE EXAMINER CANNOT TELL GOOD LUCK FROM GOOD REASONING UNLESS YOU NARRATE THE EXCLUSION.**

**THE SECOND DISCRIMINATOR IS THE CLOCK. The commonest failure mode is A CANDIDATE WHO EXPLAINS BISPHOSPHONATE PHARMACOLOGY BEAUTIFULLY FOR TWO MINUTES AND NEVER MENTIONS FALLS. HARD RULE: AT 6:30 YOU START THE FALLS PARAGRAPH, WHATEVER ELSE IS UNFINISHED.**

**WHY THIS STATION EXISTS: OSTEOPOROSIS MATTERS ONLY BECAUSE PEOPLE FALL. A MAN WITH THIN BONES WHO NEVER FALLS NEVER BREAKS ANYTHING. That is why the recalls always pair the two — AND WHY VERSION B, WITH NO FALLS AT ALL, STILL REQUIRES A FALLS-PREVENTION PLAN.**
plan: **Knock, wash hands, introduce, SIT DOWN AT HIS LEVEL with the results turned so he can see them: 'my colleague arranged some tests after your falls — I'd like to GO THROUGH THEM, ASK A FEW QUESTIONS, THEN MAKE A PLAN.'**

**AGENDA, five seconds: 'is there anything in particular you were hoping we'd cover today?'** Then **SIGNPOST THE THREE AREAS: 'your results, a few questions, and then A PLAN FOR YOUR BONES, YOUR CHEST AND YOUR FALLS.'** **Naming the three tells the examiner YOU HAVE SEEN ALL THREE PROBLEMS before you have said anything else.**
**THE SCAN, IN FOUR STEPS: what it measures and THREE SITES · TWO SCORES, and WHICH ONE YOU ARE USING AND WHY · THE T-SCORES AND THE RANGE · then NAME OSTEOPENIA.**

**PLAIN WORDS: 'osteopenia means YOUR BONES HAVE THINNED — there's less bone there than we'd expect. It's THE STAGE BEFORE OSTEOPOROSIS, which is when bones become fragile and break easily. So this is A WARNING, NOT A DISASTER — AND THERE'S A LOT WE CAN DO ABOUT IT.'**

**THE BLOODS IN ONE BREATH, THIRTY SECONDS: blood count, sugars, kidneys, liver, thyroid and calcium ALL NORMAL — 'the one thing that isn't: VITAMIN D, which you need for strong bones, IS LOW AT 30 WHEN IT SHOULD BE ABOVE 50.'** Then **CHECK UNDERSTANDING.**

**'Is it alright if I ask you some questions, so I can work out WHY YOUR BONES HAVE THINNED AND WHY YOU'VE BEEN FALLING?'** Then **Q1, THE FRACTURE QUESTION — and if yes, WHICH BONE AND HOW DID IT HAPPEN, A BIG INJURY OR A SIMPLE TRIP?**

**Q2 CALCIUM, NAMING THE FOOD GROUP: 'do you have DAIRY PRODUCTS regularly — MILK, CHEESE, YOGHURT? Roughly how much in a day?' Q3 VITAMIN D: 'how much time do you spend OUTDOORS IN THE SUN in a normal week?' Q4 EXERCISE: 'what sort of exercise do you manage — AND DOES YOUR BREATHING LIMIT WHAT YOU CAN DO?'**

**Q5 SMOKING, NEVER SKIPPED: 'are you still smoking, or have you stopped? If you've stopped, when?' Q6 CONTROL AND COMPLIANCE: 'ARE YOU USING YOUR PUFFER EVERY DAY AS PRESCRIBED? How many FLARE-UPS in the last twelve months? Were you ever ADMITTED with one? AND HOW MANY DAYS OF PREDNISOLONE DO YOU TAKE EACH TIME?'**

**THE FALL-OR-FAINT QUESTION FIRST.** Then **Q7, THE RISK-FACTOR LIST: 'any problems with your EYESIGHT OR HEARING? Any JOINT PAIN OR TROUBLE WITH YOUR BALANCE? Any DIZZINESS ON STANDING? Are you on any SLEEPING TABLETS OR BLOOD PRESSURE TABLETS? And at home — ANY STEPS, LOOSE RUGS OR POOR LIGHTING?'**
**THE FOUR-SECOND RED FLAGS: ANY NEW BACK PAIN, OR HAVE YOU LOST HEIGHT · any WEIGHT LOSS, NIGHT SWEATS OR BONE PAIN · any LOOSE STOOLS OR BLOATING · DO YOU LIVE ALONE, WHO IS AROUND IF YOU FALL?**

**CONTRIBUTING FACTORS IN PLAIN WORDS: THE STEROID TABLETS AND THE PUFFER — BOTH KINDS — plus THE COPD ITSELF, THE LOW VITAMIN D, LOW CALCIUM, INACTIVITY AND THE FALLS.** **Narrate the exclusion: the normal bloods rule out thyroid, kidney, liver and calcium causes.**

**BONE PLAN, BULLETS: no fracture → FRACTURE RISK CALCULATOR, TREAT IF HIGH · replace VITAMIN D · DIETARY CALCIUM, FOOD FIRST · WEIGHT-BEARING AND BALANCE EXERCISE · alcohol · AND A DENTAL REVIEW IF WE START A DRUG.**

**CHEST PLAN, BULLETS: SMOKING FIRST — Quitline 13 7848, and IF NICOTINE REPLACEMENT HAS FAILED, VARENICLINE OR BUPROPION PLUS BEHAVIOURAL SUPPORT · CHECK TECHNIQUE AND ADHERENCE BEFORE ESCALATING, then ADD THE NEXT INHALER · PULMONARY REHABILITATION · VACCINATIONS · AND FIVE DAYS OF PREDNISOLONE, NOT EIGHT.**
**HARD RULE — FALLS PLAN STARTS NOW WHATEVER IS UNFINISHED: FALLS CLINIC · VISION AND HEARING · PHYSIOTHERAPY BALANCE TRAINING · OT HOME REVIEW · MEDICATION REVIEW · PERSONAL ALARM.**
**ANSWER HIS FEAR DIRECTLY — the personal alarm, the falls service, and a plan he can describe to his family.**

**SAFETY NET AND FOLLOW-UP, ALL FOUR: REPEAT VITAMIN D IN THREE MONTHS · REPEAT DEXA IN TWO YEARS, SOONER IF THE STEROID BURDEN CONTINUES · COME BACK FOR ANY NEW FRACTURE, A FALL YOU CAN'T GET UP FROM, A HEAD STRIKE, OR SUDDEN SEVERE BACK PAIN · AND A WRITTEN COPD ACTION PLAN WITH THE CORRECTED FIVE-DAY COURSE.**
pefe: **No physical examination in this station. Do now: INTERPRET THE T-SCORE OUT LOUD AND NAME OSTEOPENIA · ASK THE FRACTURE QUESTION AND BRANCH ON THE ANSWER · CONFIRM THE BLOODS EXCLUDE SECONDARY CAUSES · START COLECALCIFEROL · PRESCRIBE DIETARY CALCIUM, NOT TABLETS · advise weight-bearing plus balance exercise · CORRECT THE PREDNISOLONE COURSE TO FIVE DAYS · refer to the falls service · ADDRESS SMOKING.**

**VITAMIN D: SUFFICIENT 50 OR ABOVE · MILD 30–49 · MODERATE 12.5–29 · SEVERE BELOW 12.5 nmol/L. MILD — as here at 30 — 1000–2000 IU DAILY. MODERATE TO SEVERE 3000–5000 IU DAILY FOR 6–12 WEEKS, then maintenance.** **CALCIUM 1000 mg DAILY FOR MEN TO 70; 1300 mg FOR WOMEN OVER 50 AND MEN OVER 70 — THREE TO FOUR SERVES OF DAIRY, DIET FIRST.** VERIFY.

**Do next: FRAX OR GARVAN FRACTURE RISK CALCULATION — THE FEMORAL NECK GOES INTO FRAX · if high risk, ALENDRONATE OR DENOSUMAB AFTER A DENTAL REVIEW AND AFTER CORRECTING VITAMIN D · REPEAT 25-OH VITAMIN D AT 3 MONTHS · REPEAT DEXA IN 2 YEARS, SOONER ON GLUCOCORTICOIDS · ESCALATE THE INHALER — A LABA IN VERSION A, A LAMA IN VERSION B · PULMONARY REHABILITATION · INFLUENZA, PNEUMOCOCCAL AND COVID-19 VACCINATION · HOME MEDICINES REVIEW if he is on sedatives or antihypertensives.**

**DRUGS — KNOW FOUR, MENTION TWO: ALENDRONATE 70 mg WEEKLY, or RISEDRONATE 35 mg WEEKLY — EMPTY STOMACH, FULL GLASS OF WATER, UPRIGHT FOR 30 MINUTES, TWO HOURS APART FROM CALCIUM · ZOLEDRONIC ACID 5 mg IV YEARLY, with a FLU-LIKE REACTION after the first infusion · DENOSUMAB 60 mg SUBCUT SIX-MONTHLY, where A DELAY BEYOND ABOUT FOUR WEEKS RISKS REBOUND VERTEBRAL FRACTURES AND IT MUST NEVER BE STOPPED WITHOUT STARTING A BISPHOSPHONATE.** VERIFY.

**PBS SUBSIDY REALITY: subsidy generally requires ESTABLISHED OSTEOPOROSIS — a T-score at or below −2.5, OR A PRIOR MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE — with additional criteria by age. A PATIENT WITH OSTEOPENIA AND NO FRACTURE MAY NOT MEET THEM EVEN WITH A HIGH CALCULATED RISK.** Safest wording: **'if the calculator shows a high risk I'd DISCUSS starting treatment, CHECK THE CURRENT PBS CRITERIA, and WE'D DECIDE TOGETHER.'** VERIFY.

**Do not miss: A PREVIOUS MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE · AN OCCULT VERTEBRAL FRACTURE — back pain, height loss · MYELOMA in anyone with anaemia, renal impairment or bone pain · SYNCOPE DRESSED UP AS A FALL · LOW CALCIUM OR VITAMIN D BEFORE AN ANTIRESORPTIVE.** **Specialist referral: T BELOW −3.0, A RECENT FRACTURE, TWO OR MORE FRAGILITY FRACTURES, OR FRACTURE ON TREATMENT.**

**Avoid: STARTING A BISPHOSPHONATE BEFORE CORRECTING VITAMIN D · REFLEX CALCIUM TABLETS · a pharmacology lecture · CALLING IT OSTEOPOROSIS · ESCALATING AN INHALER HE IS NOT TAKING · LEAVING FALLS OUT OF VERSION B · FALSE REASSURANCE THAT 'IT'S ONLY OSTEOPENIA'.** **Equity: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients develop chronic disease earlier — CONSIDER BONE ASSESSMENT AT A YOUNGER AGE, involve an Aboriginal Health Worker or ACCHS, and apply CLOSING THE GAP PBS CO-PAYMENT RELIEF. TIS National 131 450.**

stem: Jenny Halloran, 72, retired school administrator, lives with her husband. Low back pain for twelve days, sudden onset lifting a bag of shopping from the car boot. Your partner saw her eight days ago, started paracetamol and arranged a thoracolumbar X-ray; she is back for the result. Report: anterior wedge compression deformity L1, ~30% anterior height loss; alignment maintained; posterior cortex and pedicles intact; generalised reduced bone density; no lytic or sclerotic lesion — osteoporotic insufficiency fracture. BP 132/78 · HR 76 · afebrile · BMI 21. Localised thoracolumbar tenderness; legs neurologically normal, normal gait, no saddle numbness, no bladder/bowel disturbance.
tasks: Explain the X-ray findings to the patient
Explain the possible causes of her symptoms and of the fracture
Explain your immediate and long-term management to the patient
findings: THERE IS NO HISTORY TAKING IN THIS STATION

IF YOU OPEN WITH 'TELL ME ABOUT THE PAIN' THE EXAMINER WILL INTERRUPT YOU WITH 'STICK TO YOUR TASKS' — and you will have spent your opening minute EARNING NOTHING. ONE RAPPORT LINE, ONE AGENDA QUESTION, THEN STRAIGHT INTO THE FILM
The report, read for what it EXCLUDES

ANTERIOR WEDGE COMPRESSION DEFORMITY OF L1 with ~30% LOSS OF ANTERIOR HEIGHT · ALIGNMENT MAINTAINED · POSTERIOR CORTEX INTACT · PEDICLES INTACT AT ALL LEVELS · GENERALISED REDUCTION IN BONE DENSITY · NO LYTIC OR SCLEROTIC LESION. EVERY ONE OF THOSE NEGATIVES IS WHY YOU ARE ALLOWED TO SAY OSTEOPOROSIS
Already recorded by your partner

BP 132/78 · HR 76 · T 36.7 · WEIGHT 58 kg, BMI 21 · LOCALISED TENDERNESS OVER THE THORACOLUMBAR JUNCTION · NORMAL POWER, SENSATION, REFLEXES AND GAIT IN BOTH LEGS · NO SADDLE NUMBNESS, NO BLADDER OR BOWEL DISTURBANCE
BUILD THE FILM IN FIVE STEPS, WITH IT IN YOUR HANDS

1 THIS IS AN X-RAY OF YOUR SPINE · 2 ON ANY X-RAY THERE ARE REALLY ONLY THREE COLOURS — WHITE IS BONE, GREY IS SOFT TISSUE, BLACK IS AIR · 3 THIS WHITE COLUMN IS YOUR SPINE, BUILT OUT OF LITTLE BLOCKS CALLED VERTEBRAE · 4 IN ONE OF THOSE BLOCKS, HERE, I CAN SEE A BREAK · 5 IT IS A COMPRESSION OR WEDGE FRACTURE. Candidates who open with 'you have an osteoporotic L1 wedge fracture' HAVE SAID EVERYTHING AND EXPLAINED NOTHING
PICK THE FILM UP AND POINT — examiners score the gesture
Face-to-face, TURN IT TOWARDS HER. Online, say 'I'M GOING TO SHARE THE PICTURE WITH YOU — CAN YOU SEE IT?'
THE LINE THAT IS THE WHOLE CASE
'A HEALTHY BONE WOULD NOT BREAK FROM LIFTING A SHOPPING BAG. THE FACT THAT YOURS DID IS WHAT TELLS US THE BONE ITSELF IS THE PROBLEM'
What she asks, and what each question is testing

'IS IT CANCER?' — honest reassurance WITHOUT A LIE. 'BUT I ONLY PICKED UP A BAG' — the core concept. 'WILL I END UP BENT OVER LIKE MY MOTHER?' — kyphosis and her real fear. 'SHOULD I REST IN BED?' — A DELIBERATE TRAP. 'I DON'T LIKE TAKING TABLETS' — shared decision, so OFFER THE INFUSION OR INJECTION, DO NOT ARGUE
VERSION B — the second fracture

TWO PREVIOUS WEDGE FRACTURES, 6 cm HEIGHT LOSS, ON PREDNISOLONE 7.5 mg FOR POLYMYALGIA PLUS A PPI, and she 'DIDN'T GET ON WITH' ALENDRONATE TWO YEARS AGO. NAME THE DRUG CAUSES, EXPLORE WHY TREATMENT FAILED RATHER THAN RE-PRESCRIBING, and OFFER AN INJECTABLE SO ADHERENCE STOPS BEING THE PROBLEM
VERSION C — the look-alike, and the pivot

Same age and mechanism, but WEIGHT LOSS, NIGHT PAIN, and the report says PEDICLE DESTRUCTION WITH A LYTIC LESION. THIS IS A DIFFERENT STATION — PATHOLOGICAL FRACTURE FROM MALIGNANCY OR MYELOMA. DO NOT DELIVER THE OSTEOPOROSIS SPEECH
THE WINKING-OWL SIGN

A DESTROYED PEDICLE ON THE AP FILM IS THE FASTEST WAY TO SEPARATE MALIGNANCY FROM OSTEOPOROSIS, AND EXAMINERS REWARD IT. OSTEOPOROSIS: EVEN THINNING, PEDICLES INTACT, WEDGE SHAPE. MALIGNANCY: A HOLE IN THE BONE, A DESTROYED PEDICLE, RED-FLAG HISTORY

dx: **OSTEOPOROTIC (MINIMAL-TRAUMA) ANTERIOR WEDGE COMPRESSION FRACTURE OF L1, on a background of POSTMENOPAUSAL OSTEOPOROSIS.** **MINIMAL TRAUMA means a fall from STANDING HEIGHT OR LESS, or a force that WOULD NOT BREAK A HEALTHY BONE — LIFTING A SHOPPING BAG COUNTS.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THIS STATION GIVES YOU TWO PROBLEMS AND MOST CANDIDATES MANAGE ONLY ONE. The word 'osteoporosis' is SO LOUD that candidates spend six minutes on calcium, vitamin D and bisphosphonates AND NEVER ONCE SAY WHAT THEY WILL DO ABOUT THE BROKEN BONE IN FRONT OF THEM. THE TASK SAYS IMMEDIATE AND LONG-TERM FOR EXACTLY THAT REASON: IMMEDIATE IS THE FRACTURE, LONG-TERM IS THE BONE.**

**THE SENTENCE THAT FIXES IT: 'there are really TWO THINGS TO SORT OUT HERE, and I want to take them IN ORDER. The FIRST is THE BROKEN BONE ITSELF — getting on top of the pain and GETTING YOU MOVING AGAIN. The SECOND, and honestly THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE, is THE REASON IT BROKE. Let me start with the first.'**

**THE SENTENCE EXAMINERS LISTEN FOR: 'A MINIMAL-TRAUMA FRACTURE OF THE HIP OR THE SPINE IS ITSELF AN INDICATION TO TREAT, REGARDLESS OF THE BONE DENSITY RESULT. THE DEXA GIVES ME A BASELINE AND SOMETHING TO FOLLOW — IT DOES NOT GIVE ME PERMISSION.'**

**THE SIX CAUSES, IN THIS ORDER: AGE · THE CHANGE OF LIFE, where the DROP IN OESTROGEN SPEEDS BONE LOSS AND IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST REASON WOMEN GET THIS MORE THAN MEN · NOT ENOUGH CALCIUM · NOT ENOUGH VITAMIN D · NOT ENOUGH EXERCISE, because BONE RESPONDS TO BEING LOADED · MEDICAL CONDITIONS AND MEDICINES, PARTICULARLY STEROID TABLETS and to a lesser degree LONG-TERM STOMACH-ACID TABLETS.**

**USE THE HONEYCOMB: 'think of the inside of a bone as A HONEYCOMB — in osteoporosis THE WALLS GET THINNER AND THE SPACES GET BIGGER.'** **And 'WEDGE' IS NOT JARGON — it is A DOORSTOP SHAPE and she will picture it instantly. 'VERTEBRAL BODY', 'ANTERIOR HEIGHT LOSS', 'INSUFFICIENCY FRACTURE' AND 'OSTEOPENIC' ARE.**

**IF SHE ASKS 'IS MY BACK BROKEN?' DO NOT SOFTEN IT INTO NOTHING: 'YES — one of the blocks in your spine has a break in it. But I want to be clear about WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN: YOUR SPINAL CORD IS NOT INVOLVED, THE BACK WALL OF THE BONE IS INTACT, YOUR LEGS ARE WORKING NORMALLY, and this is NOT the kind of break that needs AN OPERATION OR A PLASTER.'**

**HEALING, HONESTLY: 'the bone usually KNITS OVER ABOUT SIX TO TWELVE WEEKS, and most of the sharp pain settles well before that. WHAT I CAN'T PROMISE IS THAT THE BLOCK GOES BACK TO BEING A PERFECT SQUARE — ONCE IT HAS SQUASHED DOWN, IT TENDS TO STAY THAT SHAPE. That is not a disaster, but IT IS EXACTLY WHY I WANT TO GET ON WITH STRENGTHENING THE REST OF THEM.'**

**CORRECTION — the source says delaying denosumab 'increases the risk of cancer'. IT DOES NOT. STOPPING OR DELAYING DENOSUMAB CAUSES REBOUND ACCELERATED BONE LOSS AND A CLUSTER OF NEW VERTEBRAL FRACTURES, SOMETIMES WITHIN MONTHS — so IT SHOULD NEVER BE STOPPED WITHOUT TRANSITIONING TO A BISPHOSPHONATE.**

**CORRECTION — the source says the injections cause HYPERcalcaemia. THEY CAUSE HYPOcalcaemia, WHICH IS WHY YOU CORRECT VITAMIN D AND CALCIUM FIRST.** **And the 'avoid 12 to 2' sun advice is TOO NARROW: in South Australia avoid roughly 10 am TO 3 pm IN SUMMER, when a few minutes on most days is plenty; LONGER, MID-MORNING OR MID-AFTERNOON EXPOSURE IS NEEDED IN WINTER.** VERIFY.
plan: **OPENING, 25 SECONDS AND NO MORE: 'I'm Dr —, one of the GPs here. Is it all right if I call you Jenny? How can I help you today?'**

**SIGNPOST AND BUY THE NEXT SEVEN MINUTES: 'I DO HAVE THE X-RAY HERE AND I HAVE THE ANSWER FOR YOU. What I'd like to do is THREE THINGS: first GO THROUGH THE PICTURE WITH YOU SO YOU CAN SEE WHAT I CAN SEE; then EXPLAIN WHY IT HAS HAPPENED; and then TALK ABOUT WHAT WE DO ABOUT IT, BOTH TODAY AND IN THE LONGER RUN.'**

**THE AGENDA QUESTION — six seconds, and THE ONLY PLACE A HIDDEN CONCERN CAN SURFACE when you are not allowed to take a history: 'before I start — IS THERE ANYTHING PARTICULAR YOU HAVE BEEN WORRYING ABOUT?'**
**STEPS 1–3, ORIENT HER BEFORE NAMING ANYTHING: the x-ray, the three colours, and THE BLOCKS CALLED VERTEBRAE.** **Pick the film up and point.**

**STEPS 4–5: 'IN ONE OF THOSE BLOCKS, HERE, I CAN SEE A BREAK. The type we're seeing is A COMPRESSION FRACTURE, OR A WEDGE FRACTURE. This happens when the bone has become WEAK AND FRAGILE — so weak that EVEN A SMALL STRAIN, LIKE LIFTING A BAG, is enough for THE BLOCK TO SQUASH DOWN AND COLLAPSE AT THE FRONT. When the front squashes and the back stays put, THE BLOCK STOPS BEING A SQUARE AND BECOMES A WEDGE — and you can see that here, COMPARED WITH THE NORMAL SQUARE ONES ABOVE AND BELOW.'**
**'So that is what the picture shows. CAN I EXPLAIN WHY IT HAS HAPPENED?'** Then **THE LEAD-IN: osteoporosis means the bones have become THIN, WEAK AND FRAGILE — and THE HONEYCOMB.**
**THE SIX CAUSES AS A LIST SHE CAN FOLLOW — age, the change of life, calcium, vitamin D, exercise, and conditions and medicines.** Then **THE LINE THAT IS THE WHOLE CASE about the shopping bag.**

**IF SHE VOLUNTEERS A RISK FACTOR — smoking, alcohol, being underweight, an early menopause, a mother or sister with a hip fracture, thyroid or breast-cancer tablets — REFLECT IT BACK: 'that is one of the things on my list, AND IT IS ONE WE CAN DO SOMETHING ABOUT.'** **You may respond to what she offers. YOU MAY NOT START ASKING.**

**'That is the why. Now let me tell you what we do about it — THERE ARE TWO HALVES TO THIS.' FIRST, THE FRACTURE: REGULAR PARACETAMOL 1 g FOUR TIMES DAILY, MAXIMUM 4 g IN 24 HOURS — REGULAR, NOT AS REQUIRED · a short course of a LOW-DOSE OPIOID with AN APERIENT STARTED AT THE SAME TIME if paracetamol is not enough.**

**'SHOULD I REST IN BED?' — 'NO. BED REST MAKES THE BONE THINNER AND MAKES YOU WEAKER. REST WHEN YOU NEED TO, BUT KEEP MOVING.'** Then **PHYSIOTHERAPY, and AN ORTHOPAEDIC OPINION ON BRACING — 'almost certainly not an operation; surgery is OCCASIONALLY used for pain that will not settle.'**
**'THAT IS THE FRACTURE ITSELF. THE BIGGER JOB IS THE BONE.' THE TESTS: a DEXA FOR A BASELINE · VITAMIN D · CALCIUM · and BLOODS TO LOOK FOR OTHER CAUSES.**

**THE DRUG CONVERSATION AS OPTIONS, NOT ONE ANSWER: ALENDRONATE 70 mg WEEKLY, upright 30 minutes; or ZOLEDRONIC ACID 5 mg IV ONCE A YEAR; or DENOSUMAB 60 mg SUBCUT EVERY SIX MONTHS HERE IN THE PRACTICE.** **If she dislikes tablets, OFFER THE INJECTABLE RATHER THAN ARGUING.**

**THE DENTIST, BEFORE THE FIRST DOSE: 'if you need any EXTRACTIONS OR IMPLANTS, have them done NOW, BEFORE WE START, because these medicines carry A SMALL RISK OF A JAW-HEALING PROBLEM.'** **And BALANCE IT so she does not decline: 'these are RARE AT THE DOSES WE USE, and THE RISK OF ANOTHER FRACTURE WITHOUT TREATMENT IS FAR HIGHER.'**

**THE NON-DRUG HALF: CALCIUM, THREE TO FOUR SERVES OF DAIRY DAILY, DIET FIRST · VITAMIN D with sensible sun exposure · SUPERVISED EXERCISE — 'I DON'T WANT YOU TURNING UP AT A GYM ON YOUR OWN WITH A FRACTURED SPINE' — so AN EXERCISE PHYSIOLOGIST AND A PHYSIOTHERAPIST · smoking, alcohol and caffeine.**

**FALLS PREVENTION — THE POINT MOST CANDIDATES FORGET, AND THE NEXT FRACTURE WILL BE HER HIP: FALLS CLINIC · OT HOME VISIT for rugs, lighting, cords and bathroom rails · BALANCE PHYSIOTHERAPY · REVIEW OF SEDATING MEDICINES · ANNUAL EYES · FEET AND FOOTWEAR.**

**THE FOUR Rs: REVIEW at one to two weeks then three months · REPEAT the DEXA in about two years · REFER · READING, the fact sheets.** Then **THE SAFETY-NET VERBATIM: 'come back sooner, or go to the hospital, if the pain BECOMES SEVERE AND DOES NOT SETTLE, or if you notice ANY WEAKNESS, NUMBNESS OR PINS AND NEEDLES IN YOUR LEGS, NUMBNESS AROUND THE BACK PASSAGE, OR TROUBLE PASSING URINE.'**
pefe: **Do now: TREAT THE FRACTURE — regular paracetamol, a short low-dose opioid WITH AN APERIENT if needed, KEEP MOVING WITH NO BED REST, PHYSIOTHERAPY, and an ORTHOPAEDIC OPINION ON BRACING · CHECK AND DOCUMENT THE LEGS BEFORE SHE LEAVES.**

**Do next this week: DEXA FOR A BASELINE · SERUM 25-OH VITAMIN D · SERUM CALCIUM WITH ALBUMIN, AND PHOSPHATE · then the SECONDARY-CAUSE SCREEN — FBE, ESR OR CRP, UEC AND eGFR, LFT INCLUDING ALP, TSH, COELIAC SEROLOGY, SERUM PROTEIN ELECTROPHORESIS AND FREE LIGHT CHAINS; TESTOSTERONE IF MALE.**

**START THE ANTIRESORPTIVE ONCE VITAMIN D AND CALCIUM ARE CORRECTED, AND AFTER A DENTAL REVIEW. Alendronate 70 mg WEEKLY on rising, PLAIN WATER, EMPTY STOMACH, UPRIGHT AND NOTHING ELSE BY MOUTH FOR 30 MINUTES — absorption is DESTROYED BY FOOD, CALCIUM, ANTACIDS AND IRON, and it is unsuitable if she CANNOT SIT OR STAND UPRIGHT or has an OESOPHAGEAL STRICTURE.** VERIFY.

**ZOLEDRONIC ACID 5 mg IV YEARLY OVER AT LEAST 15 MINUTES — a FLU-LIKE REACTION for a day or two after the first dose is common, and the dose is REDUCED OR AVOIDED IN RENAL IMPAIRMENT. DENOSUMAB 60 mg SUBCUT SIX-MONTHLY — convenient and effective, SUITABLE WHEN RENAL FUNCTION RULES OUT A BISPHOSPHONATE, BUT IT MUST NOT BE STOPPED OR DELAYED.** **Duration: FIVE YEARS ORAL, THREE YEARS IV, DENOSUMAB INDEFINITE.** VERIFY.

**MENOPAUSAL HORMONE THERAPY IS AN OPTION ONLY IF SHE ALSO HAS TROUBLESOME MENOPAUSAL SYMPTOMS — and it is NOT THE BEST CHOICE FOR BONE. In this station you do not know whether she has symptoms, SO DO NOT RAISE IT UNPROMPTED.**

**Do not miss: CORD COMPRESSION OR CAUDA EQUINA — new leg weakness, saddle numbness, retention — SAME-DAY EMERGENCY · MALIGNANCY OR MYELOMA BEHIND AN 'OSTEOPOROTIC' FRACTURE · A BURST FRACTURE with the posterior cortex involved · UNTREATED VITAMIN D DEFICIENCY OR HYPOCALCAEMIA BEFORE AN ANTIRESORPTIVE · UNDIAGNOSED HYPERPARATHYROIDISM.**

**Avoid: BED REST · 'I'LL REFER YOU TO A SPECIALIST' AS YOUR WHOLE MANAGEMENT ANSWER — the station explicitly wants the detail from you · REFLEXIVE NSAIDs AT 72 · CALCIUM SUPPLEMENTS FOR EVERYBODY, DIET FIRST · WAITING FOR THE DEXA BEFORE YOU COMMIT TO TREATMENT · FRIGHTENING HER OUT OF TREATMENT with a long account of jaw osteonecrosis.** **MRI is NOT needed to make this diagnosis — order it for NEUROLOGICAL SIGNS, UNCERTAINTY ABOUT WHETHER THE FRACTURE IS ACUTE OR OLD, where a STIR SEQUENCE SHOWS MARROW OEDEMA, or any suspicion of malignancy or infection.**

stem: Jenna, 27, presents with abdominal pain. BP 110/70 · HR 88 · RR 12 · T 36.5 · SpO2 98% RA.
Version B: day three, 96/58 · 118 · 22 · 38.7, lying very still — pain eased for a while this morning and is now everywhere.
tasks: Take a focused history (prompt bell at 4 minutes)
Ask the examiner for the physical examination findings — given only for examinations you request by name
Explain your diagnosis and your differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: THE BLANK STEM IS DELIBERATE
NO SITE, NO DURATION, NO ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS — just 'abdominal pain' and the vitals. IT IS TESTING WHETHER YOU HAVE ONE STRUCTURE YOU CAN RUN ON ANY ABDOMINAL PAIN
FINDINGS ARE GIVEN ONLY FOR EXAMINATIONS YOU REQUEST BY NAME
EVERY FINDING IS A QUESTION. IF YOU DID NOT ASK FOR IT, YOU DO NOT HAVE IT. Claiming 'there is rebound tenderness' without asking the examiner is a fail in its own right
THE THREE HISTORY KEY POINTS — every one is scored

MIGRATION OF THE PAIN · ANOREXIA · NAUSEA OR VOMITING. The examiner's stated position: A CANDIDATE WHO NEVER ASKED ABOUT THESE, BUT FOUND A POSITIVE ROVSING SIGN AND ANNOUNCED 'APPENDICITIS', DOES NOT PASS THE DIAGNOSTIC FORMULATION. THE EXAMINATION CANNOT RESCUE A HISTORY THAT NEVER HAPPENED
THE QUESTION SHE WILL NOT VOLUNTEER

'WHERE DID THE PAIN START? WAS IT ALWAYS THERE, OR DID IT BEGIN SOMEWHERE ELSE?' THE ROLE-PLAYER WILL NOT OFFER THE MIGRATION UNLESS ASKED DIRECTLY. ASK IT BEFORE 2:00. And ask 'IS IT WORSE ON MOVEMENT OR COUGHING?' — a yes is PERITONEAL IRRITATION DESCRIBED BY THE PATIENT RATHER THAN ELICITED BY YOUR HAND
THE APPETITE QUESTION IS WHERE ANOREXIA IS CAPTURED
It sits in the RED-FLAG AND CANCER SCREEN, and it is THE SINGLE MOST COMMONLY OMITTED KEY POINT IN THIS STATION. ASK IT REGARDLESS OF AGE OR DURATION
THE PAINKILLER — EXACTLY TWO QUESTIONS

'ARE YOU IN PAIN RIGHT NOW?' → 'WOULD YOU LIKE SOMETHING FOR THE PAIN?' THEN STOP. Do not ask about allergies, what she has taken, or which analgesic — THAT IS A FIVE-QUESTION DETOUR OUT OF A FOUR-MINUTE HISTORY AND IT COSTS YOU A DIFFERENTIAL GROUP. Role-players are briefed to DISPLAY pain, and offering analgesia SWITCHES OFF THE DISPLAY
ONE SENTENCE BUYS THE SEXUAL HISTORY

'I need to ask A FEW PERSONAL QUESTIONS ABOUT YOUR PERIODS AND YOUR SEXUAL HEALTH, BECAUSE SOME CAUSES OF THIS PAIN START IN THAT AREA. Is that all right?' IF YOU RUN OUT OF TIME ANYWHERE, DO NOT RUN OUT OF TIME HERE
VERSION B — the station changes character

DAY THREE. BP 96/58 · HR 118 · RR 22 · T 38.7 · LYING VERY STILL, GUARDING, RELUCTANT TO MOVE. PAIN EASED FOR A WHILE THIS MORNING AND IS NOW EVERYWHERE. A CANDIDATE WHO WORKS METHODICALLY THROUGH THE SEXUAL HISTORY AT A PULSE OF 118 HAS FAILED A SAFETY CRITERION, HOWEVER GOOD THE QUESTIONS WERE
TWO FURTHER VARIANTS

PREGNANT: appendicitis is THE COMMONEST NON-OBSTETRIC SURGICAL EMERGENCY IN PREGNANCY, and THE PAIN MAY SIT HIGHER as the uterus enlarges — ULTRASOUND FIRST, MRI IF NON-DIAGNOSTIC, DO NOT ORDER CT. CHILD OR ADOLESCENT: same structure, but DO NOT REQUEST A RECTAL EXAMINATION — it does not change management and READS AS UNSAFE PRACTICE
WHERE THE TIP SITS CHANGES THE EXAMINATION

RETROCAECAL IS COMMONEST — PSOAS SIGN, FEW ANTERIOR SIGNS. PELVIC IS SECOND — OBTURATOR SIGN, URINARY AND RECTAL SYMPTOMS. This is the answer to 'the abdomen felt almost normal — how could it be appendicitis?' — and it is why A PELVIC APPENDIX GIVES A FALSE POSITIVE ON THE URINARY QUESTIONS

dx: **ACUTE APPENDICITIS. OBSTRUCTION OF THE APPENDICEAL LUMEN — by a FAECOLITH, LYMPHOID HYPERPLASIA IN THE YOUNG, occasionally A TUMOUR IN THE OLDER PATIENT — causes DISTENSION, then VENOUS CONGESTION, MUCOSAL ISCHAEMIA AND BACTERIAL INVASION, and finally GANGRENE AND PERFORATION.** **THAT SEQUENCE IS WHY THE PAIN CHANGES CHARACTER, AND WHY DELAY MATTERS.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: YOU MUST DIAGNOSE FROM EVIDENCE YOU ACTUALLY COLLECTED, AND YOU MUST SAY THAT EVIDENCE OUT LOUD.** **A candidate who asks all three key points AND THEN SAYS 'IT'S APPENDICITIS' WITHOUT NAMING THEM ALSO LOSES MARKS. THE PASS IS THE REPLAY.**

**NAME IT, EXPLAIN IT IN TEN SECONDS, THEN GIVE FOUR REASONS: 'most likely you have ACUTE APPENDICITIS. The appendix is A SMALL FINGER-SHAPED POUCH ATTACHED TO THE LARGE BOWEL, on the right lower side. At the moment THAT POUCH IS INFLAMED.'**

**THEN THE REASONING BLOCK, WHICH IS WHERE THE MARKS ARE: 'FIRST, YOUR PAIN MOVED — it started around your belly button and settled in the right lower side, WHICH IS VERY TYPICAL. SECOND, YOUR APPETITE HAS GONE since yesterday. THIRD, YOU'VE BEEN FEELING SICK AND VOMITED. And FOURTH, when I examined you, THE SPECIFIC TESTS WE USE WERE POSITIVE.'** **It takes FORTY TO FIFTY SECONDS. LET IT — it is worth more than any two differentials you might squeeze in afterwards.**

**WHY THE PAIN MOVES: it is the VISCERAL-TO-PARIETAL TRANSITION. Early visceral pain is POORLY LOCALISED AND FELT AT THE UMBILICUS; once the inflamed appendix IRRITATES THE PARIETAL PERITONEUM, the pain BECOMES SHARP AND LOCALISED TO THE RIGHT ILIAC FOSSA.**

**DELIVER THE DIFFERENTIALS IN NAMED GROUPS, NOT AS A FLAT LIST — THE EXAMINER IS MARKING THE SHAPE OF YOUR REASONING AS MUCH AS ITS CONTENT: GI · RENAL AND URINARY · GYNAECOLOGICAL · OBSTETRIC · WALL AND HERNIA · OTHER.** **Four groups, ONE BEST DIFFERENTIAL IN EACH, ONE REASON EACH.**
**NEVER LEAVE 'AM I GOING TO NEED AN OPERATION?' UNANSWERED: 'VERY LIKELY YES, and the surgical team will see you. IT'S USUALLY KEYHOLE SURGERY AND MOST PEOPLE GO HOME WITHIN A DAY OR TWO.'**

**CORRECTION — 'WITH A THREE-WEEK LAST PERIOD I WOULDN'T DO A PREGNANCY TEST' IS WRONG. DO THE TEST. A MENSTRUAL HISTORY IS NOT A CONTRACEPTIVE METHOD AND IS NOT A DIAGNOSTIC TEST; WOMEN WITH ECTOPIC PREGNANCIES FREQUENTLY REPORT A RECENT, APPARENTLY NORMAL PERIOD.** If challenged: **'THE LAST MENSTRUAL PERIOD IS UNRELIABLE IN EARLY PREGNANCY, AND A MISSED ECTOPIC IS A PREVENTABLE DEATH.'**

**CORRECTION — THE ALVARADO SCORE IS NOT IN ROUTINE AUSTRALIAN USE AND IS NOT A DECISION RULE HERE. Its value is AS A CHECKLIST OF THE EIGHT THINGS WORTH ASKING AND FINDING: MIGRATION 1 · ANOREXIA 1 · NAUSEA OR VOMITING 1 · RIF TENDERNESS 2 · REBOUND 1 · TEMPERATURE 37.3 OR ABOVE 1 · LEUCOCYTOSIS 2 · LEFT SHIFT 1.** Say: **'I use the items as an aide-memoire, BUT THE DECISION TO OPERATE IN AUSTRALIA IS CLINICAL, WITH IMAGING AND A SURGICAL REVIEW.'**

**VERSION B, SAID OUT LOUD AT ABOUT 1:30: 'Examiner, before I continue — SHE IS TACHYCARDIC, HYPOTENSIVE AND FEBRILE WITH A RIGID ABDOMEN, so I'm concerned about A PERFORATED APPENDIX WITH PERITONITIS AND SEPSIS. I would like to START RESUSCITATION NOW: oxygen if needed, TWO LARGE-BORE CANNULAS, BLOOD CULTURES, A FLUID BOLUS, INTRAVENOUS ANTIBIOTICS, NIL BY MOUTH, and an URGENT SURGICAL REVIEW. MAY I CONTINUE WITH A FOCUSED HISTORY WHILE THAT IS HAPPENING?'**
plan: **TO THE EXAMINER BEFORE YOU SIT: 'is my patient HAEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE, and could I have the vital signs?'** Then **WIPE, compressed, and an open question.**

**RESPOND TO HER OPENING STATEMENT BEFORE ASKING ANYTHING ELSE — four parts, one breath: ACKNOWLEDGE, EMPATHISE, SIGNPOST, CONSENT. 'I'm really sorry to hear that. The pain you're describing IS CONCERNING TO ME TOO. I'll need to ask you a few questions, AND I PROMISE I'LL TAKE GOOD CARE OF YOU.'**
**THE PAINKILLER, TWO QUESTIONS ONLY, THEN MOVE.**

**THE PAIN BLOCK: CAN YOU SHOW ME WHERE · AND WHERE DID IT START, WAS IT ALWAYS THERE OR DID IT BEGIN SOMEWHERE ELSE · out of ten · sharp or a dull ache · when exactly · constant or coming and going · better, worse or the same · does it TRAVEL anywhere · ANYTHING THAT MAKES IT BETTER OR WORSE — FOOD, MOVEMENT, POSITION?**
**SAY THE MIGRATION BACK TO HER — 'so the pain MOVED from around your navel down to the right lower side' — then KEEP GOING. DO NOT DIAGNOSE OUT LOUD YET.**

**GI GROUP: any NAUSEA OR VOMITING — AND WHICH CAME FIRST, THE PAIN OR THE VOMITING · any BLOATING · ARE YOU PASSING WIND NORMALLY · any DIARRHOEA · CONSTIPATION · FEVERS OR CHILLS?** **Pain first supports appendicitis.**

**RED FLAGS AND CANCER SCREEN, WHERE ANOREXIA IS CAPTURED: any WEIGHT LOSS · HOW HAS YOUR APPETITE BEEN · any LUMPS OR BUMPS · any DIZZINESS OR LIGHT-HEADEDNESS · BLOOD IN THE BOWEL MOTIONS OR BLACK TARRY MOTIONS · change in bowel habit · ANYONE IN THE FAMILY WITH BOWEL CANCER?**

**KIDNEY AND BLADDER: any PAIN OR BURNING passing urine · going MORE OFTEN · any BLOOD in the urine?** **A pelvic appendix IRRITATES THE BLADDER AND CAN GIVE A FALSE POSITIVE — NOTE IT, DO NOT BE CAPTURED BY IT.** Then **GROIN, one question that rules out a whole group: ANY LUMP OR SWELLING IN YOUR GROIN?**

**THE PERMISSION SENTENCE, THEN THE PELVIC BLOCK: any VAGINAL BLEEDING · any DISCHARGE · WHEN WAS YOUR LAST PERIOD, AND ARE THEY REGULAR · ARE YOU SEXUALLY ACTIVE · DO YOU USE CONDOMS · EVER BEEN TOLD YOU HAD A SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTION?**

**IF THE BELL HAS NOT GONE: any OPERATIONS ON YOUR TUMMY BEFORE · regular medications and allergies. IF YOU ARE AT 3:40 AND HAVE NOT STARTED THE PELVIC BLOCK, SKIP PAST HISTORY, FAMILY HISTORY AND SOCIAL HISTORY ENTIRELY.**

**THE EXAMINATION REQUEST, BY NAME. GENERAL APPEARANCE — COMFORTABLE OR DISTRESSED, well or dehydrated, flushed or pale · IS THERE A POSTURAL DROP · INSPECTION: DOES THE ABDOMEN MOVE SYMMETRICALLY WITH RESPIRATION, any distension, scars, visible hernia, CULLEN OR GREY TURNER SIGN?**

**PALPATION: on SUPERFICIAL THEN DEEP palpation, IS THERE TENDERNESS AND WHERE IS IT MAXIMAL · IS THERE GUARDING · IS THERE RIGIDITY · IS THERE REBOUND TENDERNESS · any mass or organomegaly?** Then **PERCUSSION TENDERNESS and BOWEL SOUNDS — present, absent or high-pitched.**
**GROIN AND RECTUM, and TWO NAMED SPECIAL TESTS, NOT THREE: 'I'd like to check ROVSING SIGN. And I'd like to check the PSOAS SIGN.'**

**THE PELVIC EXAMINATION, WITH THE FIXED SENTENCE: 'WITH THE PATIENT'S CONSENT AND WITH A CHAPERONE PRESENT — on inspection any rash, lumps, bleeding or discharge; SPECULUM for discharge from the cervix; and on BIMANUAL, IS THERE CERVICAL MOTION TENDERNESS, what is the uterine size, IS THE UTERUS TENDER, is there ADNEXAL TENDERNESS OR A MASS?'** **You do this because you are performing A COMPLETE AND LOGICAL ASSESSMENT, NOT BECAUSE YOU ARE UNSURE.**
**OFFICE TESTS TO CLOSE: A URINE DIPSTICK, A URINARY βhCG, AND A CAPILLARY BLOOD GLUCOSE.**
**NAME IT, EXPLAIN IT IN TEN SECONDS, THEN THE FOUR REASONS.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS IN GROUPS, each with one reason it is less likely.** Then **the plan — NIL BY MOUTH, IV ACCESS AND FLUIDS, ANALGESIA AND ANTIEMETIC, BLOODS, ULTRASOUND FIRST, URGENT SURGICAL REFERRAL — and the SAFETY-NET: 'if the pain SUDDENLY GETS MUCH WORSE, SPREADS ACROSS YOUR WHOLE TUMMY, you can't keep fluids down, or you DEVELOP A FEVER OR FEEL FAINT — COME STRAIGHT BACK. DON'T WAIT UNTIL MORNING.'**
pefe: **Do now: NIL BY MOUTH · LARGE-BORE IV ACCESS · IV FLUIDS · ANALGESIA AND AN ANTIEMETIC · URINARY βhCG AND DIPSTICK · REFER TO THE SURGICAL TEAM.**

**Do next: FBE FOR LEUCOCYTOSIS WITH A LEFT SHIFT · CRP, UEC, LFT, LIPASE · GROUP AND HOLD · ULTRASOUND FIRST IN A YOUNG WOMAN, CT IF INCONCLUSIVE · SERIAL ABDOMINAL EXAMINATION IF EQUIVOCAL.** **Ultrasound is first-line in young women, children and pregnancy because it AVOIDS RADIATION — but A NON-VISUALISED APPENDIX DOES NOT EXCLUDE APPENDICITIS.**

**On CT look for A DILATED, THICK-WALLED APPENDIX WITH SURROUNDING FAT STRANDING — and, if present, FREE FLUID OR EXTRALUMINAL GAS SUGGESTING PERFORATION. On ultrasound, A BLIND-ENDING, NON-COMPRESSIBLE TUBULAR STRUCTURE with adjacent free fluid.**

**Definitive treatment: LAPAROSCOPIC APPENDICECTOMY AFTER RESUSCITATION — the standard operation in Australia, with SHORTER STAY AND LOWER WOUND INFECTION RATES than open. PERIOPERATIVE IV ANTIBIOTICS for uncomplicated disease; a THERAPEUTIC COURSE for PERFORATED OR GANGRENOUS appendicitis. The usual Australian shape is METRONIDAZOLE PLUS GENTAMICIN, with AMPICILLIN OR AMOXICILLIN added for complicated disease, or AMOXICILLIN–CLAVULANATE where gentamicin is contraindicated.** VERIFY.

**NON-OPERATIVE MANAGEMENT WITH ANTIBIOTICS ALONE EXISTS FOR SELECTED UNCOMPLICATED CASES, BUT RECURRENCE IS COMMON AND IT IS NOT WHAT YOU OFFER IN THIS STATION. Mention it only if asked, and then say SURGERY REMAINS STANDARD.**

**Do not miss: ECTOPIC PREGNANCY — THE βhCG · PERFORATION AND PERITONITIS · SEPSIS with tachycardia, fever and confusion · OVARIAN TORSION in sudden severe pain · CAECAL CANCER IN THE OLDER PATIENT.** **Escalation triggers: SYSTOLIC BELOW 100 OR A NARROW PULSE PRESSURE · PULSE ABOVE 100 · TEMPERATURE ABOVE 38 · A RIGID SILENT ABDOMEN · A POSITIVE βhCG WITH PAIN.**

**Avoid: WAITING FOR IMAGING BEFORE REFERRING · WITHHOLDING ANALGESIA TO 'PRESERVE THE SIGNS', which is outdated and does not mask the signs of an acute abdomen · CT AS THE FIRST SCAN IN A YOUNG WOMAN OR IN PREGNANCY · A RECTAL EXAMINATION IN A CHILD · PROMISING SHE WILL NOT NEED SURGERY.** **From a rural site: REFER EARLY TO THE ON-CALL SURGICAL REGISTRAR AND MAKE THE TRANSFER DECISION BEFORE IMAGING, NOT AFTER. MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33; PATS offered before they ask.**

stem: Doug Harmer, 50, presents to the emergency department with central abdominal pain for several hours.
tasks: Take a focused history (4–6 minutes)
Ask the examiner for the examination findings
Explain your diagnosis and differentials to the patient
findings: OPEN WITH STABILITY IN AN ED STEM

'Before I begin — MAY I CONFIRM THE PATIENT IS HAEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE? Blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature and oxygen saturation.' In a GP stem with a month of symptoms you can skip it. IN AN ED STEM WITH HOURS OF SEVERE PAIN, SKIPPING IT IS NOTICED
The history findings

SEVERAL HOURS OF COLICKY CENTRAL PAIN · FOUR EPISODES OF VOMITING, THE LAST TWO BILE-STAINED · ABDOMINAL DISTENSION · HAS NOT PASSED WIND FOR TWO DAYS AND HAS NOT OPENED HIS BOWELS FOR THREE · APPENDICECTOMY IN HIS TWENTIES
The examination findings, once requested

ABDOMEN DISTENDED AND GENERALLY TENDER WITH GUARDING · PERCUSSION HYPER-RESONANT · BOWEL SOUNDS ABSENT · RECTUM EMPTY. Negatives: NO GROIN LUMP · no weight loss or rectal bleeding · no urinary symptoms · PULSE REGULAR
THE FOUR CARDINAL FEATURES — ask each one

COLICKY CENTRAL PAIN · VOMITING · DISTENSION · ABSOLUTE CONSTIPATION. 'Any constipation?' → 'No' AND MOVING ON MISSES OBSTIPATION. ASK: 'WHEN DID YOU LAST PASS WIND? WHEN DID YOU LAST OPEN YOUR BOWELS?'
THE ONE VOMITING FOLLOW-UP THAT CHANGES THE DIAGNOSIS
'WHAT COLOUR IS IT? IS ANY OF IT GREEN? DOES IT SMELL UNPLEASANT, ALMOST LIKE BOWEL MOTION?' FOOD → BILIOUS (GREEN) → FAECULENT MAPS THE BLOCK FROM HIGH TO LOW
'THE PAIN COMES AND GOES IN WAVES'

COLIC MEANS A HOLLOW TUBE TRYING TO PUSH PAST A BLOCK — SAY SO OUT LOUD WHEN YOU GIVE REASONS. CONSTANT, SEVERE PAIN IN A SOFT ABDOMEN IS ISCHAEMIA, AND CONSTANT PAIN WITH FEVER AND LOCALISED PERITONISM IS STRANGULATION
SURGICAL HISTORY IS LIVE DATA

'ANY OPERATION ON THE ABDOMEN LEAVES SCAR TISSUE INSIDE. THAT SCAR TISSUE IS THE COMMONEST CAUSE OF A BLOCKAGE.' Say it WITHOUT SOUNDING ACCUSATORY — the communication challenge in this version is explaining adhesions from an old operation
ALWAYS ASK FOR THE GROIN

HERNIA IS THE SECOND COMMONEST CAUSE AND THE REASON YOU ALWAYS EXAMINE THE GROIN. The examiner WILL NOT VOLUNTEER A LUMP — you get it only when you ask for the inguinal region. Here it is NORMAL, and that negative is part of naming adhesions as the cause
The ischaemia screen, even here

'ANY FUNNY RACING OR IRREGULAR BEATING OF YOUR HEART? EVER BEEN TOLD YOU HAVE AN IRREGULAR HEARTBEAT?' · heart attacks, strokes, clots · and the question nobody asks: 'DO YOU GET CRAMPING PAIN AFTER MEALS, AND HAVE YOU BEEN AVOIDING FOOD BECAUSE OF IT?'
CLAIMING A FINDING YOU NEVER REQUESTED
DISTENSION, BOWEL SOUNDS, PERCUSSION NOTE AND THE RECTUM EACH HAVE TO BE ASKED FOR. If you did not request it, you do not have it
findingsLabel: Version A — four cardinal features, and obstruction is a mechanism not a diagnosis
must: FAIL — Naming 'bowel obstruction' and stopping, without a cause.
FAIL — Giving only the X-ray as management, with no resuscitation.
FAIL — Missing obstipation because he denies 'constipation'.
FAIL — Withholding analgesia to 'preserve the signs'.
ASK — When did you last pass wind? When did you last open your bowels?
ASK — Have you ever had an operation on your abdomen?

dx: **SMALL BOWEL OBSTRUCTION, MOST LIKELY ADHESIONAL — a MECHANICAL BLOCK to the passage of bowel contents, with PROXIMAL DILATATION, FLUID SEQUESTRATION AND VOMITING.**

**OBSTRUCTION IS NOT A DIAGNOSIS — IT IS A MECHANISM. The examiner WILL ask 'CAUSED BY WHAT?' Have the four ready in order of frequency in an adult: ADHESIONS — MOST COMMON BY A LONG WAY, AND THE ANSWER WHENEVER THERE IS A SCAR · HERNIA — SECOND, AND THE REASON YOU ALWAYS EXAMINE THE GROIN · TUMOUR · VOLVULUS. In children, add INTUSSUSCEPTION.**

**THE THREE CENTRAL-PAIN EMERGENCIES ARE DIAGNOSED ON QUESTIONS RATHER THAN ON IMAGING. The station tests whether you can distinguish A BLOCKED BOWEL from A STRANGLED BOWEL from A BOWEL LOSING ITS BLOOD SUPPLY — BECAUSE THE TREATMENT OF EACH IS DIFFERENT AND ONE OF THEM CANNOT WAIT FOR A SCAN.**

**GIVE THE REASONS IN HIS WORDS: the pain COMES IN WAVES, which is the bowel TRYING TO PUSH PAST A BLOCK · the vomiting has TURNED GREEN · his tummy has SWOLLEN · he HASN'T PASSED WIND FOR TWO DAYS · and he had AN APPENDIX OPERATION, which leaves SCAR TISSUE INSIDE — THE COMMONEST CAUSE OF A BLOCKAGE.**

**WHEN ASKED 'WHAT WOULD YOU DO NEXT?', THE IMAGING IS STEP SEVEN, NOT STEP ONE. THE EIGHT STEPS: NIL BY MOUTH · TWO LARGE-BORE CANNULAE AND BLOODS WITH A LACTATE · IV FLUIDS · NASOGASTRIC TUBE ON FREE DRAINAGE · ANALGESIA AND ANTIEMETIC · CATHETER WITH STRICT FLUID BALANCE · IMAGING · SURGICAL REFERRAL.**
**WITHHOLDING OPIOID ANALGESIA FOR FEAR OF MASKING SIGNS IS OBSOLETE AND IS NOW SCORED AGAINST YOU. Give analgesia and SAY YOU WILL RE-EXAMINE REGULARLY.**

**ADHESIONAL OBSTRUCTION WITHOUT STRANGULATION gets a CONSERVATIVE TRIAL — 'DRIP AND SUCK', SERIAL EXAMINATION, REPEAT IMAGING. MOST SETTLE IN 24–48 HOURS.** **A WATER-SOLUBLE CONTRAST STUDY such as Gastrografin down the NG tube both PREDICTS WHICH WILL SETTLE AND HELPS THEM SETTLE — contrast reaching the colon within 24 hours predicts resolution.** VERIFY local protocol.

**OPERATE FOR STRANGULATION, CLOSED LOOP, PERFORATION, OR FAILURE OF CONSERVATIVE MANAGEMENT.** **The signs of strangulation: CONSTANT PAIN, FEVER, TACHYCARDIA, LOCALISED PERITONISM, A RISING LACTATE → THEATRE.**

**READ THE FILMS: ERECT FOR AIR-FLUID LEVELS, SUPINE FOR DILATED LOOPS. SMALL BOWEL — VALVULAE CONNIVENTES CROSSING THE FULL WIDTH, a STACKED-COIN appearance, lying CENTRALLY. LARGE BOWEL — HAUSTRA CROSSING ONLY PART OF THE WIDTH, a POUCHED appearance, lying PERIPHERALLY.** **CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast is MORE SENSITIVE and gives THE LEVEL, THE CAUSE, AND WHETHER THERE IS ISCHAEMIA.**

**RURAL SA: Wallaroo and Kadina HAVE NO ON-SITE GENERAL SURGERY OVERNIGHT. Stabilise locally — drip, suck, analgesia, bloods — WHILE YOU RING THE RECEIVING GENERAL SURGICAL REGISTRAR AND MEDSTAR ON 1300 13 12 33. TQEH is the usual metropolitan receiving site for Yorke Peninsula; RFDS for fixed-wing retrieval. RING WHILE THE WORKUP RUNS, NOT AFTER IT.**
plan: **ASK FOR STABILITY — IN AN ED STEM IT IS A MARK.** Then **WIPE and an open question.**
**Acknowledge and signpost; offer analgesia in two questions and move on.**
**THE PAIN, FULL SICORA — but CHARACTER MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE: 'IS IT THERE ALL THE TIME, OR DOES IT COME IN WAVES AND THEN EASE OFF?'**
**THE OBSTRUCTION BLOCK — FOUR CARDINAL FEATURES. VOMITING: HOW MANY TIMES, WHAT COLOUR, IS ANY OF IT GREEN, DOES IT SMELL FAECULENT? DISTENSION: HAS YOUR TUMMY BECOME SWOLLEN OR BLOATED?**
**ABSOLUTE CONSTIPATION, ASKED THE RIGHT WAY: 'WHEN DID YOU LAST PASS WIND? WHEN DID YOU LAST OPEN YOUR BOWELS?'**

**THE CAUSE BLOCK: 'HAVE YOU EVER HAD AN OPERATION ON YOUR ABDOMEN?' — adhesions · 'ANY LUMP OR SWELLING IN YOUR GROIN, OR EVER BEEN TOLD YOU HAVE A HERNIA?' · 'any WEIGHT LOSS, BLOOD IN YOUR BOWEL MOTIONS OR CHANGE IN BOWEL HABIT?' — tumour · 'any LONG-STANDING CONSTIPATION?' — volvulus, impaction.**

**THE ISCHAEMIA BLOCK: 'any FUNNY RACING OR IRREGULAR BEATING OF YOUR HEART? Ever been told you have AN IRREGULAR HEARTBEAT, OR ATRIAL FIBRILLATION? Any HEART ATTACKS, STROKES, OR CLOTS IN THE LEGS? DO YOU GET CRAMPING PAIN AFTER MEALS, AND HAVE YOU BEEN AVOIDING FOOD BECAUSE OF IT?'**
**GI GENERAL AND RED FLAGS: fevers · appetite · blood or black stools · jaundice. In an older patient: 'ARE YOU ON BLOOD THINNERS? DO YOU TAKE ANTI-INFLAMMATORIES?'**

**KUB, THREE QUESTIONS: pain or burning passing urine · going more often · blood in the urine.** Then **the non-surgical mimics: THIRST AND POLYURIA for DKA · any RASH IN A BAND for shingles · any trouble passing urine at all for RETENTION.**
**SADMA — smoking, alcohol, drugs, medications, allergies — and a ONE-LINE SUMMARY BACK TO HIM.**
**THE EXAMINATION, REQUESTED BY NAME: general appearance — distressed, dehydrated, lying still or restless · VITALS AND A POSTURAL DROP · INSPECTION for DISTENSION, SCARS AND VISIBLE PERISTALSIS.**

**PALPATION — TENDERNESS AND WHERE, GUARDING, RIGIDITY, REBOUND, ANY MASS · PERCUSSION NOTE, HYPER-RESONANT OR DULL · BOWEL SOUNDS, ABSENT OR TINKLING · THE HERNIAL ORIFICES AND THE GROIN · and with consent and a chaperone, A RECTAL EXAMINATION for an empty rectum or a mass.**
**Bedside: capillary glucose and ketones, urine dipstick, ECG for rhythm.**
**NAME IT WITH ITS CAUSE — 'a BLOCKAGE IN YOUR SMALL BOWEL, MOST LIKELY FROM SCAR TISSUE LEFT BY YOUR APPENDIX OPERATION' — then the reasons in his words.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS: obstruction from a HERNIA — groin normal · a TUMOUR — no weight loss or bleeding · a VOLVULUS · then MESENTERIC ISCHAEMIA — pulse regular, pain not out of proportion · pseudo-obstruction · and a RUPTURED AAA in any older person with central pain.**

**THE EIGHT-STEP PLAN, WITH IMAGING AT STEP SEVEN — and tell him plainly: 'we'll put a tube down to rest your bowel and take the pressure off, give you fluids and pain relief, and THE SURGICAL TEAM WILL SEE YOU NOW. Many of these settle without an operation, but some need one.'**
pefe: **Do now: NIL BY MOUTH · TWO LARGE-BORE CANNULAE · FBC, UEC, LFT, LIPASE, CRP, VBG WITH LACTATE, GROUP AND HOLD · IV CRYSTALLOID AND POTASSIUM REPLACEMENT · NASOGASTRIC TUBE ON FREE DRAINAGE · ANALGESIA AND ANTIEMETIC · INDWELLING CATHETER WITH STRICT FLUID BALANCE · EARLY SURGICAL REFERRAL.**

**Do next: ERECT AND SUPINE ABDOMINAL X-RAY — MULTIPLE AIR-FLUID LEVELS ON THE ERECT FILM, DILATED LOOPS ON THE SUPINE · CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST, MORE SENSITIVE, GIVING LEVEL, CAUSE AND ISCHAEMIA · ERECT CHEST X-RAY if perforation is suspected, for GAS UNDER THE DIAPHRAGM.** **In suspected mesenteric ischaemia, GO STRAIGHT TO CT ANGIOGRAPHY.**

**Definitive: ADHESIONAL WITHOUT STRANGULATION → CONSERVATIVE TRIAL with drip and suck, serial examination and a WATER-SOLUBLE CONTRAST STUDY. OPERATE for STRANGULATION, CLOSED LOOP, PERFORATION, OR FAILURE OF CONSERVATIVE MANAGEMENT.**
**SIGMOID VOLVULUS: THE COFFEE-BEAN SIGN — a single grossly dilated loop arising from the pelvis with a dense line down the middle. Treated by FLEXIBLE SIGMOIDOSCOPIC DECOMPRESSION first.**

**CORRECTION — ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHAEMIA AND ISCHAEMIC COLITIS ARE COMMONLY TAUGHT AS ONE AND ARE NOT. THUMBPRINTING IS A COLONIC SIGN pointing to ISCHAEMIC COLITIS — watershed large bowel, low-flow, crampy left-sided pain with bloody diarrhoea, usually settling with supportive care. For SMALL BOWEL MESENTERIC ISCHAEMIA, DO NOT RELY ON A PLAIN FILM — REQUEST CT ANGIOGRAPHY.**

**Do not miss: STRANGULATION — fever, tachycardia, localised peritonism, rising lactate · CLOSED-LOOP OBSTRUCTION · A RUPTURED ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSM in any older person with central pain and shock · ISCHAEMIC BOWEL in a patient whose pain is FAR WORSE THAN THE ABDOMEN LOOKS.**

**Avoid: WITHHOLDING OPIOID ANALGESIA — OBSOLETE AND SCORED AGAINST YOU · NAMING 'OBSTRUCTION' WITHOUT A CAUSE · GIVING ONLY THE X-RAY AS MANAGEMENT.** **In a rural hospital, ring the receiving unit and MEDSTAR WHILE THE WORKUP RUNS. PATS for planned follow-up travel; Country Health Connect after discharge; TIS National 131 450.**

stem: Marion Deare, 55, presents with umbilical pain since last night and vomiting. BP 132/80 · HR 104 · RR 18 · T 37.6 · SpO2 98%.
tasks: Take a focused history (4–6 minutes)
Ask the examiner for the examination findings
Explain your diagnosis and differentials to the patient
findings: THE VITALS ARE ALREADY TELLING YOU SOMETHING
BP 132/80 · HR 104 · RR 18 · T 37.6 · SpO2 98%. TACHYCARDIC AND LOW-GRADE FEBRILE — THE EARLY SIGNATURE OF STRANGULATION RATHER THAN A SIMPLE BLOCK. Say it out loud before you start
THE LUMP IS REPORTED ONLY WHEN YOU ASK FOR THE INGUINAL REGION
The examiner WILL NOT VOLUNTEER IT. A candidate who examines the abdomen beautifully and never asks for the groin NEVER FINDS THE DIAGNOSIS
THE TWO QUESTIONS THE STATION RESTS ON
'EXAMINER, YOU MENTIONED A LUMP IN THE RIGHT GROIN. IS IT TENDER? AND IS IT REDUCIBLE — DOES IT PUSH BACK IN?' → TENDER, AND IT DOES NOT REDUCE. EVERYTHING ELSE IN THIS VERSION IS SCENERY
WHAT SHE SAYS ABOUT THE LUMP

'I'VE HAD A LUMP IN MY GROIN FOR YEARS, IT COMES AND GOES.' → 'IS IT TENDER NOW? CAN YOU PUSH IT BACK IN?' A LUMP THAT HAS STOPPED REDUCING AND BECOME TENDER IS A SURGICAL EMERGENCY. She describes it as having USED TO PUSH BACK IN — and now STUCK
THE OBSTRUCTION PICTURE IS THE CONSEQUENCE, NOT THE CAUSE

UMBILICAL COLICKY PAIN SINCE LAST NIGHT · VOMITING · check DISTENSION and ASK 'WHEN DID YOU LAST PASS WIND? WHEN DID YOU LAST OPEN YOUR BOWELS?' A LOOP OF BOWEL TRAPPED IN THE SAC OBSTRUCTS THE BOWEL AT THE SAME TIME AS IT LOSES ITS BLOOD SUPPLY
WHY THE PAIN IS AT THE UMBILICUS, NOT THE GROIN
SMALL BOWEL VISCERAL PAIN IS REFERRED TO THE PERIUMBILICAL REGION. The strangled loop IS IN THE GROIN; the pain she NOTICES FIRST is central. THAT MISMATCH IS WHY CANDIDATES NEVER THINK TO LOOK DOWN
ASK THE HERNIA QUESTION IN THE HISTORY AS WELL
'ANY LUMP OR SWELLING IN YOUR GROIN, OR HAVE YOU EVER BEEN TOLD YOU HAVE A HERNIA?' Asked in the CAUSE BLOCK, it lets you arrive at the examination ALREADY KNOWING WHERE TO LOOK
THE COMMUNICATION CHALLENGE

EXPLAINING THAT A LUMP SHE HAS HAD FOR YEARS IS NOW AN EMERGENCY. 'This lump has been there a long time, but SOMETHING HAS CHANGED TODAY — A LOOP OF BOWEL HAS BECOME TRAPPED IN IT AND ITS BLOOD SUPPLY IS BEING SQUEEZED'
DO NOT ATTEMPT REDUCTION
OF A TENDER HERNIA THAT HAS BEEN IRREDUCIBLE FOR HOURS — YOU CAN REDUCE DEAD BOWEL INTO THE ABDOMEN
THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A HERNIA AND A STRANGLED ONE
IS ANSWERED BY TWO BEDSIDE QUESTIONS — IS IT TENDER, AND DOES IT REDUCE? At operation a strangled loop is DUSKY AND CONGESTED; it is ASSESSED FOR VIABILITY, and IF IT DOES NOT PINK UP IT IS RESECTED
findingsLabel: Version B — a lump reported only if you ask, and two questions that decide everything
must: FAIL — Reporting a groin lump and not asking whether it is tender and reducible.
FAIL — Sending a tender irreducible hernia for a CT instead of to theatre.
FAIL — Never asking the examiner for the inguinal region.
FAIL — Attempting to reduce a tender hernia that has been irreducible for hours.
ASK — Examiner, is the lump tender? Is it reducible?
ASK — When did you last pass wind? When did you last open your bowels?

dx: **STRANGULATED INGUINAL HERNIA CAUSING OBSTRUCTION — A LOOP OF BOWEL TRAPPED IN A HERNIAL SAC TIGHTLY ENOUGH TO CUT OFF ITS BLOOD SUPPLY, OBSTRUCTING THE BOWEL AT THE SAME TIME.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: WHEN A LUMP IS REPORTED, ASK THE TWO QUESTIONS THAT DECIDE THE MANAGEMENT — IS IT TENDER, AND IS IT REDUCIBLE. BOTH ARE SINGLE SENTENCES. BOTH CHANGE THE ENTIRE PLAN. BOTH ARE WHAT CANDIDATES LEAVE OUT.**

**THEN SAY THE CONSEQUENCE OUT LOUD: 'Thank you. THAT CHANGES MY PLAN. This is a STRANGULATED HERNIA. I WOULD NOT SEND HER FOR IMAGING — I WOULD RESUSCITATE HER AND REFER HER FOR EMERGENCY SURGERY NOW.'**
**TENDER PLUS IRREDUCIBLE EQUALS THEATRE. NO IMAGING. NO DELAY. Sending her for a CT is a STARRED FAIL — the loop is DYING WHILE SHE WAITS FOR THE SCANNER.**

**THE THREE CENTRAL-PAIN EMERGENCIES ARE DIAGNOSED ON QUESTIONS, NOT IMAGING: A BLOCKED BOWEL — RESUSCITATE, DECOMPRESS, THEN IMAGE. A STRANGLED BOWEL — DO NOT IMAGE, REFER FOR THEATRE. A BOWEL LOSING ITS BLOOD SUPPLY — RESUSCITATE, LACTATE, AND CT ANGIOGRAPHY.** **This version is the middle one.**

**THE SIGNS OF STRANGULATION TO NAME: CONSTANT RATHER THAN COLICKY PAIN · FEVER · TACHYCARDIA · LOCALISED PERITONISM · A RISING LACTATE.** **She already has the tachycardia and the low-grade temperature on arrival — say that you have noticed them.**

**TO HER, PLAINLY: 'the lump in your groin is A HERNIA — a weak spot where bowel can push through. It's been coming and going for years, BUT TODAY A LOOP OF BOWEL HAS BECOME TRAPPED IN IT AND IS BEING SQUEEZED SO TIGHTLY THAT ITS BLOOD SUPPLY IS AT RISK. That's also WHY YOU'RE VOMITING — the bowel is blocked. THIS NEEDS AN OPERATION TODAY, AND THE SURGEONS ARE COMING NOW.'**
**THE OPERATION: REDUCE THE SAC, ASSESS THE BOWEL FOR VIABILITY, RESECT NON-VIABLE BOWEL, AND REPAIR THE DEFECT.**

**HERNIA IS THE SECOND COMMONEST CAUSE OF SMALL BOWEL OBSTRUCTION IN AN ADULT, AFTER ADHESIONS — which is the reason YOU EXAMINE THE GROIN IN EVERY ABDOMINAL PAIN STATION, including the ones where you think you already know the answer.**

**RURAL SA: stabilise locally WHILE YOU RING THE RECEIVING GENERAL SURGICAL REGISTRAR AND MEDSTAR ON 1300 13 12 33 — Wallaroo and Kadina have NO ON-SITE GENERAL SURGERY OVERNIGHT, TQEH is the usual receiving site, and RFDS provides fixed-wing retrieval. A strangulated hernia is a case where TRANSFER IS ARRANGED IN PARALLEL WITH RESUSCITATION, NEVER AFTER IT.**
plan: **ASK FOR STABILITY, THEN SAY WHAT THE VITALS MEAN: 'she is TACHYCARDIC AT 104 WITH A TEMPERATURE OF 37.6 — I'll keep that in mind.'** Then **WIPE and an open question.**
**Acknowledge, signpost, and the two-question analgesia offer.**

**THE PAIN, WITH CHARACTER FIRST: 'IS IT THERE ALL THE TIME, OR DOES IT COME IN WAVES AND THEN EASE OFF?' Then SITE, ONSET, RADIATION, SEVERITY — and HAS THE PAIN CHANGED IN CHARACTER SINCE LAST NIGHT?** **A change from colicky to constant is strangulation.**
**THE FOUR CARDINAL FEATURES: VOMITING — how many times, WHAT COLOUR, ANY GREEN, ANY FAECULENT SMELL · DISTENSION · and 'WHEN DID YOU LAST PASS WIND? WHEN DID YOU LAST OPEN YOUR BOWELS?'**
**THE CAUSE BLOCK, and ASK THE HERNIA QUESTION HERE: operations on the abdomen · 'ANY LUMP OR SWELLING IN YOUR GROIN, OR EVER BEEN TOLD YOU HAVE A HERNIA?'**

**When she mentions the lump, THE TWO QUESTIONS IN THE HISTORY: 'IS IT TENDER NOW? CAN YOU PUSH IT BACK IN?'** Then **HOW LONG HAS IT BEEN THERE · WHEN DID IT STOP GOING BACK IN · HAS IT CHANGED COLOUR?**

**The rest of the cause block briefly: WEIGHT LOSS, BLOOD IN THE BOWEL MOTIONS, CHANGE IN HABIT · long-standing constipation.** Then **the ischaemia screen: IRREGULAR HEARTBEAT, AF, clots, pain after meals.**
**GI GENERAL AND RED FLAGS; in an older patient, BLOOD THINNERS AND ANTI-INFLAMMATORIES.** Then **KUB, THREE QUESTIONS.**
**SADMA, and what makes the hernia worse: CHRONIC COUGH, heavy lifting, straining — relevant to the repair and to recurrence.**
**ONE-LINE SUMMARY BACK TO HER.**

**THE EXAMINATION, REQUESTED BY NAME: general appearance · vitals and a postural drop · INSPECTION for distension and scars · PALPATION for tenderness, guarding, rigidity, rebound · percussion · BOWEL SOUNDS.**

**AND THE INGUINAL REGION BY NAME: 'I'd like to examine BOTH GROINS AND THE HERNIAL ORIFICES.'** Then **THE TWO QUESTIONS TO THE EXAMINER: IS IT TENDER? IS IT REDUCIBLE?** Then **OVERLYING SKIN — RED OR DISCOLOURED — AND IS THERE A COUGH IMPULSE?**
**SAY THE CONSEQUENCE OUT LOUD: 'THAT CHANGES MY PLAN.'**
**EXPLAIN TO HER IN PLAIN WORDS — the lump she has had for years has TRAPPED A LOOP OF BOWEL TODAY, it is being SQUEEZED, and THAT IS WHY SHE IS VOMITING.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BRIEFLY: ADHESIONAL OBSTRUCTION — no previous surgery · a TUMOUR · a VOLVULUS · MESENTERIC ISCHAEMIA · and a groin lump that is NOT a hernia — lymph node, femoral aneurysm, abscess.**

**THE PLAN, NO IMAGING: NIL BY MOUTH · TWO LARGE-BORE CANNULAE and bloods with a LACTATE and GROUP AND CROSS-MATCH · IV FLUIDS · ANALGESIA · ANTIBIOTICS · NG TUBE if vomiting · CATHETER · and EMERGENCY SURGICAL REFERRAL NOW. 'YOU WILL NEED AN OPERATION TODAY.'**
pefe: **Do now: NIL BY MOUTH · TWO LARGE-BORE CANNULAE · FBC, UEC, LFT, CRP, VBG WITH LACTATE · GROUP AND CROSS-MATCH · IV FLUIDS AND ELECTROLYTE REPLACEMENT · ANALGESIA AND ANTIEMETIC · ANTIBIOTICS · NG TUBE ON FREE DRAINAGE IF VOMITING · CATHETER WITH FLUID BALANCE · EMERGENCY SURGICAL REFERRAL.**
**NO IMAGING. NO DELAY. A TENDER, IRREDUCIBLE HERNIA IS A CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS AND A THEATRE DECISION — A CT DELAYS SURGERY WHILE THE LOOP DIES.**
**DO NOT ATTEMPT REDUCTION OF A TENDER HERNIA THAT HAS BEEN IRREDUCIBLE FOR HOURS — YOU CAN REDUCE DEAD BOWEL INTO THE ABDOMEN.**
**Operation: REDUCE THE SAC, ASSESS VIABILITY — a DUSKY, CONGESTED LOOP that DOES NOT PINK UP IS RESECTED — RESECT NON-VIABLE BOWEL, REPAIR THE DEFECT.**

**Do not miss: STRANGULATION ITSELF — constant pain, fever, tachycardia, localised peritonism, RISING LACTATE · CLOSED-LOOP OBSTRUCTION · A RUPTURED AAA in any older person with central pain and shock · A FEMORAL HERNIA, which sits BELOW AND LATERAL TO THE PUBIC TUBERCLE, is MORE COMMON IN WOMEN, and STRANGULATES MORE READILY than an inguinal one.**

**A GROIN LUMP THAT IS NOT A HERNIA: an inguinal lymph node · a FEMORAL ARTERY ANEURYSM, which is PULSATILE and must NEVER BE INCISED · a saphena varix, which has a cough thrill and disappears lying down · an abscess · an undescended testis in a man.**

**Avoid: SENDING A TENDER IRREDUCIBLE HERNIA FOR IMAGING · WITHHOLDING ANALGESIA · naming 'obstruction' without its cause.** **Rural SA: MEDSTAR 1300 13 12 33 and the receiving surgical registrar WHILE YOU RESUSCITATE; RFDS for fixed-wing transfer; TQEH as the usual receiving site; TIS National 131 450.**
