stem: Reg Colman, 60, presents with generalised abdominal pain for a few days, much worse today. Pulse 90, irregular. He reports dark stools.
tasks: Take a focused history (4–6 minutes)
Ask the examiner for the examination findings
Explain your diagnosis and differentials to the patient
findings: THE STEM HANDS YOU TWO OF THE THREE CLUES
PULSE 90 AND IRREGULAR · DARK STOOLS. The third — PAIN OUT OF PROPORTION TO A SOFT ABDOMEN — only appears once you ask for the examination and SAY THE MISMATCH OUT LOUD
THE EXAMINATION

Pain rated 9–10/10, but the ABDOMEN IS SOFT WITH VERY LITTLE TENDERNESS · no peritonism early · IRREGULARLY IRREGULAR PULSE · bowel sounds may be present or reduced. Late: distension, peritonism, shock — BY WHICH POINT THE BOWEL IS DYING
THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT PATTERN IN THE WHOLE ABDOMINAL BLOCK
SEVERE, CONSTANT PAIN IN A SOFT ABDOMEN. Combine it with an IRREGULAR PULSE and you have MESENTERIC ISCHAEMIA. SAY THE WORDS 'OUT OF PROPORTION' ALOUD — IT IS WHAT CANDIDATES LEAVE OUT
DISTINGUISH MELAENA FROM ISCHAEMIC BLEEDING

'My stools have been dark.' → 'BLACK AND TARRY, OR DARK RED? ANY SMELL? ANY MEDICINES LIKE IRON TABLETS?' Melaena points upper GI; DARK RED OR BLOODY STOOL in this setting is a MUCOSA THAT IS LOSING ITS BLOOD SUPPLY
THE ISCHAEMIA BLOCK — ask all four

'ANY FUNNY RACING OR IRREGULAR BEATING OF YOUR HEART?' · 'HAVE YOU EVER BEEN TOLD YOU HAVE AN IRREGULAR HEARTBEAT, OR ATRIAL FIBRILLATION?' · 'ANY HEART ATTACKS, STROKES, OR CLOTS IN THE LEGS?' · 'DO YOU GET CRAMPING PAIN IN YOUR TUMMY AFTER MEALS, AND HAVE YOU BEEN AVOIDING FOOD BECAUSE OF IT?'
FOOD FEAR IS THE CLUE NOBODY ASKS ABOUT

CHRONIC MESENTERIC ISCHAEMIA produces POST-PRANDIAL PAIN, then FOOD AVOIDANCE AND WEIGHT LOSS — THE BOWEL'S VERSION OF INTERMITTENT CLAUDICATION. A 60-year-old with vascular risk factors, MONTHS of pain after eating and weight loss who now has severe constant pain HAS HAD A CHRONIC STENOSIS THROMBOSE ACUTELY. ASKING MARKS YOU OUT IMMEDIATELY
ASK ABOUT ANTICOAGULANTS BY NAME
'ARE YOU ON BLOOD THINNERS?' An irregular heartbeat NOT anticoagulated is the embolic story. Also 'DO YOU TAKE ANTI-INFLAMMATORIES?' in an older patient with dark stools
ASK FOR STABILITY FIRST IN AN ED STEM
'May I confirm the patient is HAEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE — blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature and saturation?' In an ED stem with hours of severe pain, SKIPPING IT IS NOTICED
IMAGING — NOT THE PLAIN FILM

A PLAIN ABDOMINAL X-RAY IS OFTEN NORMAL EARLY and cannot make this diagnosis. THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE IS CT ANGIOGRAPHY. Suspected mesenteric ischaemia needs A CENTRE WITH CT ANGIOGRAPHY AND VASCULAR SURGERY — RETRIEVE EARLY rather than scanning locally and transferring afterwards
THE LACTATE — useful, but not reassuring when normal
A RISING LACTATE supports established ischaemia. A NORMAL LACTATE EARLY DOES NOT EXCLUDE IT — the gut can be ischaemic before systemic lactate rises. Do not let a normal VBG delay the CT angiogram
findingsLabel: Version C — severe pain, a soft abdomen, and the words you must say aloud
must: FAIL — Never saying 'pain out of proportion' when the pain is worse than the abdomen looks.
FAIL — Relying on a plain film or thumbprinting to diagnose small bowel ischaemia.
FAIL — Never asking about the irregular heartbeat or anticoagulation.
FAIL — Withholding analgesia 'to preserve the signs'.
ASK — Any funny racing or irregular beating of your heart? Are you on blood thinners?
ASK — Do you get cramping pain after meals, and have you been avoiding food?

dx: **ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHAEMIA — SUDDEN LOSS OF ARTERIAL SUPPLY TO THE SMALL BOWEL, usually AN EMBOLUS FROM THE HEART IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION, or THROMBOSIS OF AN ALREADY NARROWED ARTERY.** The superior mesenteric artery is the usual culprit. **HIGH MORTALITY, AND TIME IS BOWEL.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: WHEN THE PAIN IS WORSE THAN THE ABDOMEN LOOKS, SAY 'OUT OF PROPORTION' OUT LOUD. It is a single sentence, it changes the entire plan, and it is what candidates leave out.**

**THE SENTENCE TO THE EXAMINER: 'what strikes me is THE MISMATCH: Reg is describing SEVERE, CONSTANT PAIN, but the abdomen is SOFT WITH VERY LITTLE TENDERNESS. That PAIN OUT OF PROPORTION TO THE EXAMINATION FINDINGS, in a man with AN IRREGULAR PULSE AND DARK STOOLS, makes me worried about THE BLOOD SUPPLY TO THE BOWEL.'**

**TO THE PATIENT, PLAINLY: 'Reg, your heart is BEATING IRREGULARLY. When it does that, BLOOD CAN POOL AND FORM A SMALL CLOT, and that clot CAN TRAVEL AND BLOCK ONE OF THE ARTERIES FEEDING THE BOWEL. When the bowel loses its blood supply IT HURTS A GREAT DEAL, BUT THERE IS VERY LITTLE TO FEEL FROM THE OUTSIDE — WHICH IS EXACTLY THE PATTERN YOU HAVE. This is serious and it needs A SPECIAL SCAN OF THE BLOOD VESSELS TODAY.'**

**WHY THE ABDOMEN IS SOFT: early ischaemia is a VISCERAL, MUCOSAL INJURY — the pain fibres fire, but THE PARIETAL PERITONEUM IS NOT YET INVOLVED, so there is NO GUARDING AND NO REBOUND. PERITONISM ARRIVES WITH TRANSMURAL INFARCTION — BY WHICH POINT THE BOWEL IS ALREADY DYING.**

**CORRECTION — TWO DIFFERENT DISEASES ARE COMMONLY TAUGHT AS ONE. ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHAEMIA is SMALL BOWEL, SMA EMBOLUS OR THROMBOSIS, PAIN OUT OF PROPORTION, diagnosed on CT ANGIOGRAPHY, treated by REVASCULARISATION AND RESECTION, with HIGH MORTALITY. ISCHAEMIC COLITIS is LARGE BOWEL at the WATERSHED AROUND THE SPLENIC FLEXURE, LOW-FLOW rather than embolic, CRAMPY LEFT-SIDED PAIN WITH BLOODY DIARRHOEA, THUMBPRINTING on film, and USUALLY SETTLES WITH SUPPORTIVE CARE.**

**If challenged: 'THUMBPRINTING IS A COLONIC SIGN AND POINTS TO ISCHAEMIC COLITIS. If I suspected acute mesenteric ischaemia of the small bowel I WOULD NOT RELY ON A PLAIN FILM — I WOULD REQUEST CT ANGIOGRAPHY.'**

**THE THREE CENTRAL-PAIN EMERGENCIES, DISTINGUISHED ON QUESTIONS NOT IMAGING: BLOCKED BOWEL — colicky pain, vomiting, distension, no flatus, a scar. STRANGLED BOWEL — a groin lump that is TENDER AND IRREDUCIBLE. BOWEL LOSING ITS BLOOD SUPPLY — PAIN OUT OF PROPORTION, AF, DARK STOOLS. THE TREATMENT OF EACH IS DIFFERENT AND ONE OF THEM CANNOT WAIT FOR A SCAN.**

**MANAGEMENT: RESUSCITATE · CORRECT FLUIDS AND ELECTROLYTES · BROAD-SPECTRUM ANTIBIOTICS · SYSTEMIC ANTICOAGULATION WITH HEPARIN · URGENT VASCULAR AND GENERAL SURGICAL REFERRAL · REVASCULARISATION — EMBOLECTOMY, THROMBOLYSIS OR BYPASS — WITH RESECTION OF NON-VIABLE BOWEL AND A PLANNED SECOND-LOOK LAPAROTOMY · then TREAT THE SOURCE: RATE OR RHYTHM CONTROL AND LONG-TERM ANTICOAGULATION FOR AF.** VERIFY.

**IN ANY OLDER PERSON WITH CENTRAL PAIN AND SHOCK, DO NOT MISS A RUPTURED ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSM — sudden central or back pain, collapse, a PULSATILE MASS, an older smoker. BEDSIDE ULTRASOUND AND THEATRE.** **SA: no on-site vascular surgery in Yorke Peninsula towns — ring the receiving registrar and MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 WHILE THE WORKUP RUNS, NOT AFTER IT.**
plan: **ED STEM — ASK FOR STABILITY FIRST: BP, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature and saturation.** Then **WIPE, open question, and acknowledge the severity: 'that sounds very painful, and I want to find out what's causing it quickly.'**

**THE PAIN — CHARACTER MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ANYWHERE: 'IS IT THERE ALL THE TIME, OR DOES IT COME IN WAVES AND THEN EASE OFF?' → constant.** Then **site, onset, how severe, radiation, anything better or worse, and HOW IT HAS CHANGED OVER THE FEW DAYS.** **Colicky central pain that comes in waves is obstruction; CONSTANT SEVERE PAIN IN A SOFT ABDOMEN IS ISCHAEMIA.**

**THE OBSTRUCTION BLOCK, ALL FOUR, BECAUSE IT IS YOUR MAIN DIFFERENTIAL: vomiting — how many times, WHAT COLOUR, IS ANY OF IT GREEN, DOES IT SMELL FAECULENT · has your tummy become SWOLLEN · WHEN DID YOU LAST PASS WIND · WHEN DID YOU LAST OPEN YOUR BOWELS?**

**THE DARK STOOLS: 'BLACK AND TARRY, OR DARK RED? ANY SMELL? ANY MEDICINES LIKE IRON TABLETS?'** Then **the cause block: ANY OPERATION ON YOUR ABDOMEN · ANY LUMP OR SWELLING IN YOUR GROIN · weight loss, blood, change in bowel habit.**
**THE ISCHAEMIA BLOCK: ANY FUNNY RACING OR IRREGULAR BEATING OF YOUR HEART · EVER TOLD YOU HAVE ATRIAL FIBRILLATION · ANY HEART ATTACKS, STROKES, OR CLOTS IN THE LEGS?**
**THE QUESTION NOBODY ASKS: 'DO YOU GET CRAMPING PAIN IN YOUR TUMMY AFTER MEALS, AND HAVE YOU BEEN AVOIDING FOOD BECAUSE OF IT? Has your WEIGHT DROPPED?'**

**MEDICATIONS, BY NAME: ARE YOU ON BLOOD THINNERS · DO YOU TAKE ANTI-INFLAMMATORIES · anything for your heart or blood pressure · digoxin?** **An irregular heartbeat NOT on anticoagulation is the embolic story.**

**GI GENERAL AND RED FLAGS: nausea, appetite, jaundice, heartburn. KUB THREE: burning, frequency, blood in the urine. OTHER: THIRST AND POLYURIA for DKA · BACK PAIN OR FAINTING for aneurysm · a band of pain for shingles.**
**SADMA — SMOKING, alcohol, drugs, allergies — vascular risk factors: BLOOD PRESSURE, CHOLESTEROL, DIABETES, PERIPHERAL VASCULAR DISEASE.** Then **a one-line summary back to him.**

**EXAMINATION, REQUESTED BY NAME: general appearance — comfortable or distressed, pale, sweaty · vitals and PULSE RHYTHM · inspection for distension and scars · PALPATION: WHERE IS THE TENDERNESS, IS THERE GUARDING, RIGIDITY, REBOUND · percussion · BOWEL SOUNDS · HERNIAL ORIFICES · a PULSATILE MASS · rectal examination with consent for blood.**
**OFFICE TESTS: ECG FOR AF · capillary glucose and ketones · urine dipstick.** Then **SAY THE MISMATCH OUT LOUD TO THE EXAMINER.**
**NAME IT TO THE PATIENT in plain words — the irregular heartbeat, the clot, the blocked artery, and why there is little to feel from the outside.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP, each with a reason: bowel obstruction — no colic, no distension, no scar · strangulated hernia — groin normal · RUPTURED AAA — no pulsatile mass, no shock · ischaemic colitis — this is small-bowel pattern · pancreatitis and peptic ulcer · DKA and other mimics.**

**THE PLAN: NIL BY MOUTH, TWO LARGE-BORE CANNULAE, BLOODS INCLUDING A VENOUS GAS AND LACTATE, IV FLUIDS, ANALGESIA AND ANTIEMETIC, HEPARIN, ANTIBIOTICS, URGENT CT ANGIOGRAPHY, VASCULAR AND SURGICAL REFERRAL — and from a rural site, MEDSTAR NOW, NOT AFTER THE SCAN.**
pefe: **Do now: NIL BY MOUTH · TWO LARGE-BORE CANNULAE · FBC, UEC, LFT, LIPASE, CRP, VENOUS GAS WITH LACTATE, COAGULATION, GROUP AND HOLD · IV CRYSTALLOID with potassium replacement · ANALGESIA AND ANTIEMETIC · INDWELLING CATHETER WITH STRICT FLUID BALANCE · 12-LEAD ECG FOR AF · EARLY SURGICAL AND VASCULAR REFERRAL.**

**Imaging: GO STRAIGHT TO CT ANGIOGRAPHY in suspected mesenteric ischaemia. A plain abdominal film is often normal early and cannot make the diagnosis. Erect chest X-ray only if perforation is suspected, looking for gas under the diaphragm.**

**What the results mean: A RAISED LACTATE AND METABOLIC ACIDOSIS support established ischaemia — BUT A NORMAL LACTATE EARLY DOES NOT EXCLUDE IT. A HIGH WHITE COUNT, RAISED AMYLASE AND RAISED PHOSPHATE may accompany infarction and are non-specific.**

**Definitive: RESUSCITATE · correct fluids and electrolytes · BROAD-SPECTRUM ANTIBIOTICS · SYSTEMIC HEPARIN · REVASCULARISATION BY EMBOLECTOMY, THROMBOLYSIS OR BYPASS · RESECTION OF NON-VIABLE BOWEL · A PLANNED SECOND-LOOK LAPAROTOMY · then RATE OR RHYTHM CONTROL AND LONG-TERM ANTICOAGULATION.** VERIFY.

**Do not miss: RUPTURED ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSM in any older person with central pain and shock · STRANGULATION — fever, tachycardia, localised peritonism, rising lactate · CLOSED-LOOP OBSTRUCTION · ISCHAEMIC BOWEL IN A PATIENT WHOSE PAIN IS FAR WORSE THAN THE ABDOMEN LOOKS.**

**Avoid: WITHHOLDING OPIOID ANALGESIA FOR FEAR OF MASKING SIGNS — THAT PRACTICE IS OBSOLETE AND IS NOW SCORED AGAINST YOU; give analgesia and say you will re-examine regularly · RELYING ON A PLAIN FILM OR ON THUMBPRINTING for small bowel ischaemia · SCANNING LOCALLY AND THEN TRANSFERRING, which costs the hours that decide whether bowel survives.**

**SA pathway: Wallaroo and Kadina have NO ON-SITE GENERAL OR VASCULAR SURGERY OVERNIGHT. Stabilise locally while you RING THE RECEIVING REGISTRAR AND MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33. Suspected mesenteric ischaemia needs A CENTRE WITH CT ANGIOGRAPHY AND VASCULAR SURGERY — RETRIEVE EARLY. RFDS for fixed-wing transfer; TIS National 131 450.**

stem: Kai Prosser, 16, attends with his mother. Vague abdominal pain 'all over' for months; stools a bit soft; he looks well.
tasks: Take a focused history
Ask the examiner for the examination findings
Explain your diagnosis and differentials
findings: THE EXAMINATION CARD HIDES THE WHOLE DIAGNOSIS

ABDOMEN NORMAL — AND TENDER RED RAISED LUMPS ON BOTH SHINS. IN VERSION A THIS IS THE ENTIRE DIAGNOSIS, sitting on an examination card that ALSO SAYS THE ABDOMEN IS NORMAL. Say 'ERYTHEMA NODOSUM' OUT LOUD
THE STEM PUNISHES FACE-VALUE READING
'VAGUE PAIN ALL OVER' · 'STOOLS A BIT SOFT' · 'HE LOOKS WELL.' VAGUE PAIN IN A TEENAGER IS NOT 'GROWING PAINS'. THE DIAGNOSIS IS FOUND BY ASKING ONE QUESTION THE PATIENT DID NOT EXPECT
DO NOT ACCEPT THE EUPHEMISM

'The stools are a bit soft' → 'TELL ME EXACTLY WHAT THEY LOOK LIKE. WHAT COLOUR? BULKY OR SMALL? DO THEY FLOAT? ARE THEY HARD TO FLUSH AWAY? DO THEY SMELL UNUSUALLY BAD? ANY BLOOD OR MUCUS? ANY URGENCY OR ACCIDENTS?'
THE TWO QUESTIONS THAT SEPARATE ORGANIC FROM FUNCTIONAL

'DOES THE PAIN OR THE DIARRHOEA WAKE YOU FROM SLEEP?' and 'HAVE YOU LOST WEIGHT WITHOUT TRYING?' FUNCTIONAL DISORDERS CHARACTERISTICALLY DO NOT WAKE PEOPLE AT NIGHT AND DO NOT CAUSE WEIGHT LOSS. SAY THIS REASONING ALOUD
THE EXTRAINTESTINAL SCREEN — twenty seconds, highest yield in the abdominal block

'ANY TENDER RED LUMPS ON YOUR SHINS? ANY ULCERS IN YOUR MOUTH? ANY RED, PAINFUL OR GRITTY EYES, OR BLURRED VISION? ANY JOINT PAINS, OR STIFFNESS IN YOUR BACK IN THE MORNING?' SKIN, MOUTH, EYES, JOINTS
ASK ABOUT THE MOUTH — ALMOST NOBODY DOES
RECURRENT APHTHOUS ULCERATION — shallow, painful ulcers with a pale base and a red rim — IS A RECOGNISED EXTRAINTESTINAL FEATURE OF IBD, PARTICULARLY CROHN DISEASE
GROWTH IS OFTEN THE FIRST SIGN IN A CHILD
'HAVE YOU GROWN AT THE SAME RATE AS YOUR FRIENDS? HAVE YOU STARTED PUBERTY?' GROWTH DELAY IS OFTEN THE FIRST SIGN OF PAEDIATRIC CROHN DISEASE. Missing it is a listed fail

THREE TO FOUR LOOSE MOTIONS A DAY · SOME MUCUS · URGENCY · WAKING AT NIGHT TO OPEN HIS BOWELS · tiredness · THREE KILOGRAMS OF UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS · RECURRENT MOUTH ULCERS · FALLEN BEHIND HIS FRIENDS IN HEIGHT. NO fever, travel, sick contacts or recent antibiotics

dx: **INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE — and given the MOUTH ULCERS AND GENERALISED PAIN, FAVOUR CROHN DISEASE.** **Months of vague pain in a teenager, soft stools with mucus, nocturnal diarrhoea, weight loss, GROWTH DELAY, and ERYTHEMA NODOSUM ON BOTH SHINS.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: CHARACTERISE THE STOOL IN THE PATIENT'S OWN DETAIL, ASK WHAT FOOD MAKES IT WORSE, AND LOOK OUTSIDE THE ABDOMEN — AND NEVER OFFER IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME AS A FIRST ANSWER.** **Every version of this station is failed the same way: ACCEPTING A VAGUE DESCRIPTION, RUNNING A PURELY ABDOMINAL HISTORY, AND REACHING FOR A FUNCTIONAL LABEL.**

**NAMING IT TO THE EXAMINER: 'you have described TENDER RED RAISED LUMPS ON BOTH SHINS — I would call that ERYTHEMA NODOSUM. In a 16-year-old with SEVERAL MONTHS OF ABDOMINAL PAIN AND LOOSE STOOLS, that combination POINTS STRONGLY TO INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. The other cause I would want to exclude is SARCOIDOSIS, and I would also consider STREPTOCOCCAL INFECTION, TUBERCULOSIS, DRUG CAUSES AND PREGNANCY.'**

**WHEN IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME IS THE ANSWER: it is a POSITIVE CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS, BUT ONLY IN THE ABSENCE OF ALARM FEATURES — recurrent pain related to defaecation with a change in stool frequency or form, WITHOUT WEIGHT LOSS, RECTAL BLEEDING, ANAEMIA, NOCTURNAL SYMPTOMS, A FAMILY HISTORY OF BOWEL CANCER OR IBD, AND GENERALLY UNDER 50. IF ANY ALARM FEATURE IS PRESENT, INVESTIGATE FIRST.** **Saying that sentence aloud is how you GET CREDIT FOR KNOWING THE DIAGNOSIS EXISTS WITHOUT FALLING INTO IT.**

**THE FOOD QUESTION IS ALSO THE COELIAC QUESTION: 'does any food make it worse — SPECIFICALLY BREAD, PASTA, CEREAL? WHAT ABOUT MILK AND DAIRY? ARE YOU EATING GLUTEN AT THE MOMENT?'** **The last question DETERMINES WHETHER THE COELIAC TEST WILL BE VALID.**

**CROHN VERSUS ULCERATIVE COLITIS: CROHN is PATCHY, TRANSMURAL, MOUTH TO ANUS, with MOUTH ULCERS, PERIANAL DISEASE, STRICTURES AND FISTULAE; ULCERATIVE COLITIS is CONTINUOUS FROM THE RECTUM, MUCOSAL, with BLOODY DIARRHOEA AND URGENCY, and an association with PRIMARY SCLEROSING CHOLANGITIS.** **Colonoscopy with biopsies decides it.**

**TO KAI, IN PLAIN WORDS: 'I think the most likely explanation is a condition called INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE — the lining of the bowel becomes inflamed, which is why you've had the pain, the loose motions, the ulcers in your mouth and the sore lumps on your shins. It is TREATABLE, and the aim is to get you BACK TO NORMAL, INCLUDING CATCHING UP ON YOUR GROWTH.'**

**EXCLUSIVE ENTERAL NUTRITION IS FIRST-LINE INDUCTION IN PAEDIATRIC CROHN DISEASE — a liquid formula as the sole diet for several weeks, which avoids steroids and SUPPORTS GROWTH. Corticosteroids are the alternative for induction; maintenance is THIOPURINES, METHOTREXATE OR BIOLOGICS.** VERIFY.

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP: ULCERATIVE COLITIS · INFECTIVE COLITIS — no travel, contacts or antibiotics, but STOOL CULTURE AND C. DIFFICILE STILL SENT · COELIAC DISEASE · FUNCTIONAL ABDOMINAL PAIN, EXCLUDED BECAUSE OF THE WEIGHT LOSS AND THE NOCTURNAL SYMPTOMS.**

**SA: suspected IBD is a PATS-supported referral to PAEDIATRIC GASTROENTEROLOGY at the WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL; Country Health Connect for ongoing care; TIS National 131 450. Offer a HEADSS-style psychosocial screen during the time alone — chronic illness in a teenager affects school, sport, mood and body image.**
plan: **WIPE, introduce yourself TO KAI, then to his mother. Open question to Kai.**

**OFFER TIME ALONE, THEN CONFIDENTIALITY WITH ITS LIMIT: 'what you tell me stays between us, UNLESS I'M WORRIED YOU OR SOMEONE ELSE IS AT RISK OF SERIOUS HARM.'** **Both sentences open the door to growth, mood and substance questions a teenager will not answer in front of a parent.**

**THE PAIN, BUT EXPECT VAGUENESS AND DO NOT FIGHT IT: where, how long, constant or intermittent, getting worse · 'DOES THE PAIN EVER WAKE YOU AT NIGHT?' · 'HOW IS IT AFFECTING SCHOOL? HAVE YOU MISSED DAYS?'** **Vague and chronic means you STOP CHASING THE PAIN AND START CHARACTERISING THE STOOL.**

**STOOL CHARACTERISATION — THE BLOCK THAT FINDS THE DIAGNOSIS: HOW MANY TIMES A DAY · WHAT DO THEY ACTUALLY LOOK LIKE — COLOUR, SIZE, CONSISTENCY · BULKY, PALE, GREASY OR FOUL-SMELLING, DO THEY FLOAT OR RESIST FLUSHING · ANY BLOOD OR MUCUS · ANY URGENCY OR ACCIDENTS · DOES IT WAKE YOU AT NIGHT TO OPEN YOUR BOWELS?**
**FOOD AND DIET: does any food make it worse — BREAD, PASTA, CEREAL, MILK AND DAIRY · have you tried cutting anything out, and did it help · ARE YOU EATING GLUTEN AT THE MOMENT?**

**THE EXTRAINTESTINAL SCREEN, FOUR QUESTIONS: TENDER RED LUMPS ON YOUR SHINS · ULCERS IN YOUR MOUTH · RED, PAINFUL OR GRITTY EYES, or blurred vision · JOINT PAINS, OR STIFFNESS IN YOUR BACK IN THE MORNING?**
**RED FLAGS AND GROWTH: WEIGHT LOSS — AND WAS IT INTENTIONAL · appetite · fever · TIREDNESS · 'HAVE YOU GROWN AT THE SAME RATE AS YOUR FRIENDS? HAVE YOU STARTED PUBERTY?'**
**INFECTION SCREEN: any TRAVEL · anyone else unwell · RECENT ANTIBIOTICS · any perianal pain, lumps or discharge?**

**FAMILY HISTORY: ANYONE IN THE FAMILY WITH CROHN, COLITIS, COELIAC DISEASE OR BOWEL CANCER?** Then **SADMA with EVERY PAINKILLER NAMED, including over-the-counter — and SMOKING, which matters especially in Crohn disease.**
**While his mother is out: a brief HEADSS screen — school, activities, mood, and how this is affecting him.** Then **bring her back in with his permission, and a one-line summary.**

**EXAMINATION BY NAME: general appearance — well or unwell, pale · HEIGHT AND WEIGHT ON A GROWTH CHART · vitals · MOUTH FOR ULCERS · EYES · HANDS for clubbing · abdomen for tenderness and masses · PERIANAL INSPECTION for tags and fistulae · JOINTS · AND THE SKIN OF THE SHINS.**
**When the shins are reported, NAME ERYTHEMA NODOSUM ALOUD and say what it means.**

**NAME IT TO KAI in plain words, and link every finding — the pain, the loose motions, the night waking, the ulcers, the shins, the height.** Then **say the IBS exclusion sentence so the examiner hears you considered and rejected it.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP, each with a reason.** Then **THE PLAN: FBC, CRP, ESR, IRON STUDIES, ALBUMIN, COELIAC SEROLOGY WHILE STILL EATING GLUTEN, STOOL CULTURE AND C. DIFFICILE, FAECAL CALPROTECTIN, and PAEDIATRIC GASTROENTEROLOGY FOR COLONOSCOPY WITH BIOPSIES.** Then **safety-net: BLOOD IN THE STOOL, HIGH FEVER, SEVERE PAIN OR A SWOLLEN TUMMY — come straight back.**
pefe: **Examination to request: HEIGHT AND WEIGHT PLOTTED ON A GROWTH CHART · general appearance and pallor · MOUTH for aphthous ulcers · EYES for episcleritis or uveitis · HANDS for clubbing · abdomen for tenderness and a right iliac fossa mass · PERIANAL INSPECTION for skin tags, fissures and fistulae · JOINTS · SKIN OF THE SHINS.**

**Investigations: FBC, CRP AND ESR, IRON STUDIES, ALBUMIN, LFTs · FAECAL CALPROTECTIN TO DISTINGUISH INFLAMMATORY FROM FUNCTIONAL · STOOL CULTURE INCLUDING CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE TO EXCLUDE INFECTION · COELIAC SEROLOGY — tTG IgA WITH TOTAL IgA, while still eating gluten · COLONOSCOPY WITH BIOPSIES FOR THE DIAGNOSIS · MR ENTEROGRAPHY FOR SMALL BOWEL CROHN DISEASE.**

**Management: GASTROENTEROLOGY REFERRAL — paediatric for a 16-year-old. INDUCE REMISSION WITH EXCLUSIVE ENTERAL NUTRITION, WHICH IS FIRST-LINE IN PAEDIATRIC CROHN DISEASE, or corticosteroids. MAINTAIN WITH THIOPURINES, METHOTREXATE OR BIOLOGICS.** VERIFY.

**Alongside: CHECK IRON, B12, FOLATE AND VITAMIN D · BONE HEALTH · SMOKING CESSATION, WHICH MATTERS ESPECIALLY IN CROHN DISEASE · VACCINATION REVIEW BEFORE IMMUNOSUPPRESSION · psychosocial support for school and mood.**

**Avoid: LABELLING IT IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME in a patient with weight loss, nocturnal symptoms or growth delay · STARTING A GLUTEN-FREE DIET BEFORE COELIAC SEROLOGY · attributing it to 'growing pains' or stress · taking the history from the parent · treating with antidiarrhoeals before infection and severe colitis are excluded.**

stem: Josh Meagher, 22, presents with bloating and abdominal discomfort for months, worse after bread and pasta. Stools are bulky, pale, foul-smelling and hard to flush. He has been on iron tablets for anaemia with no improvement.
tasks: Take a focused history
Ask the examiner for the examination findings
Explain your diagnosis and differentials
findings: THE STEM PUNISHES FACE-VALUE READING
FOOD-RELATED BLOATING IN A YOUNG MAN IS NOT 'IRRITABLE BOWEL'. The diagnosis is found by asking ONE QUESTION THE PATIENT DID NOT EXPECT — here, WHETHER THE IRON HAS WORKED
THE FAILURE YOU MUST NOTICE
'I'VE BEEN ON IRON TABLETS FOR MONTHS' → 'HAS YOUR BLOOD COUNT IMPROVED ON THEM?' IRON DEFICIENCY THAT DOES NOT RESPOND TO IRON IS MALABSORPTION UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE
CHARACTERISE THE STOOL — his exact words

'THEY'RE BIG AND PALE AND THEY STINK. THEY STICK TO THE BOWL AND I HAVE TO FLUSH TWICE.' BULKY, PALE, OFFENSIVE, HARD TO FLUSH = STEATORRHOEA — FAT IS NOT BEING ABSORBED. Say what it means when you give reasons
THE TRAP BRIEFED INTO THE ROLE-PLAYER
'I CUT BACK ON BREAD FOR A WEEK ONCE AND FELT BETTER, THEN WENT BACK TO IT.' HEARING THAT AND ADVISING HIM TO CUT GLUTEN OUT INVALIDATES BOTH THE SEROLOGY AND THE BIOPSY AND IS SCORED AS AN ERROR
THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE TEST IS VALID
'ARE YOU EATING GLUTEN AT THE MOMENT?' THE tTG AND THE BIOPSY ARE ONLY MEANINGFUL ON A GLUTEN-CONTAINING DIET
THE EXAMINATION

Thin, MILDLY PALE, possibly ANGULAR STOMATITIS OR GLOSSITIS · abdomen soft, mildly distended, non-tender · no masses · no organomegaly. ASK ABOUT AND LOOK FOR DERMATITIS HERPETIFORMIS — ITCHY BLISTERING RASH ON ELBOWS, KNEES AND BUTTOCKS, the skin form of coeliac disease
THE TWO QUESTIONS THAT SEPARATE ORGANIC FROM FUNCTIONAL

'DOES IT WAKE YOU AT NIGHT?' and 'HAVE YOU LOST WEIGHT WITHOUT TRYING?' Functional disorders characteristically DO NOT WAKE PEOPLE AND DO NOT CAUSE WEIGHT LOSS — and IRON-DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA IS ITSELF AN ALARM FEATURE THAT EXCLUDES IBS
STILL RUN THE EXTRAINTESTINAL SCREEN
SKIN, MOUTH, EYES, JOINTS — twenty seconds. MOUTH ULCERS AND DERMATITIS HERPETIFORMIS both occur in coeliac disease, and the screen is what keeps IBD on the table
FAMILY HISTORY AND ASSOCIATIONS
COELIAC DISEASE IN A FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVE · TYPE 1 DIABETES · AUTOIMMUNE THYROID DISEASE · DOWN SYNDROME. Ask — they raise the pre-test probability and change who else needs testing
THE HARDER VARIANT

ALREADY ON A GLUTEN-FREE DIET BEFORE TESTING. DO NOT PRETEND THE TESTS ARE VALID. Either arrange A SUPERVISED GLUTEN CHALLENGE BEFORE TESTING, or refer for specialist advice — SAYING THAT YOU RECOGNISE THE PROBLEM IS WHAT SCORES

dx: **COELIAC DISEASE — an IMMUNE-MEDIATED ENTEROPATHY in which GLUTEN — a protein in WHEAT, BARLEY AND RYE — triggers the immune system to attack the lining of the small bowel. The villi FLATTEN, so FAT AND IRON ARE NOT ABSORBED — which is why the stools are greasy and the iron tablets have not worked.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE GLUTEN WARNING, GIVEN BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE ABOUT DIET. Say it in the same breath as the diagnosis: 'Josh, I think this is coeliac disease. BEFORE I SAY ANOTHER WORD ABOUT DIET, ONE THING MATTERS MORE THAN EVERYTHING ELSE: KEEP EATING YOUR NORMAL DIET, INCLUDING BREAD AND PASTA, UNTIL THE TESTS ARE DONE.'**

**AND THE REASON: 'if you stop gluten now, THE BLOOD TEST AND THE BIOPSY CAN BOTH COME BACK FALSELY NORMAL, and we'd have to ask you to EAT IT AGAIN FOR SIX WEEKS AND START OVER. So the order is: BLOOD TEST, THEN A GASTROSCOPY WITH SMALL BIOPSIES, AND ONLY THEN THE DIET — which will be LIFELONG, and which A DIETITIAN WILL HELP YOU WITH.'**

**THE THREE REASONS, READ BACK: BLOATING WORSE WITH BREAD AND PASTA · BULKY, PALE, OFFENSIVE STOOLS THAT ARE HARD TO FLUSH, WHICH MEANS FAT IS NOT BEING ABSORBED · and IRON DEFICIENCY THAT HAS NOT RESPONDED TO IRON TABLETS.**

**TESTING: tTG IgA WITH A TOTAL IgA LEVEL — because IgA DEFICIENCY IS MORE COMMON IN COELIAC DISEASE AND GIVES A FALSELY NEGATIVE tTG IgA; if IgA-deficient, use IgG-based tests. CONFIRM WITH DUODENAL BIOPSY AT GASTROSCOPY: VILLOUS ATROPHY, CRYPT HYPERPLASIA AND INTRAEPITHELIAL LYMPHOCYTOSIS.**

**ANSWER HIS THREE QUESTIONS: IS IT SERIOUS — 'LIFELONG, BUT COMPLETELY MANAGEABLE, and people who stick to the diet feel entirely well.' FOREVER — 'YES — EVEN SMALL AMOUNTS OF GLUTEN KEEP THE DAMAGE GOING.' WILL MY KIDS GET IT — 'IT RUNS IN FAMILIES, SO YOUR FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVES SHOULD BE TESTED, INCLUDING ANY CHILDREN.'**

**WHEN IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME IS THE ANSWER: A POSITIVE DIAGNOSIS ONLY IN THE ABSENCE OF ALARM FEATURES — NO WEIGHT LOSS, BLEEDING, ANAEMIA, NOCTURNAL SYMPTOMS OR FAMILY HISTORY, generally under 50. HIS ANAEMIA ALONE EXCLUDES IT. SAY THE EXCLUSION CRITERIA ALOUD.**

**UNTREATED COELIAC DISEASE HAS CONSEQUENCES WORTH NAMING: OSTEOPOROSIS from calcium and vitamin D malabsorption · persistent IRON, FOLATE AND B12 DEFICIENCY · SUBFERTILITY · and a small increased risk of SMALL-BOWEL LYMPHOMA, which is reduced by adherence to the diet.** **Hence bone density assessment.**

**DO NOT CONFUSE IT WITH NON-COELIAC GLUTEN SENSITIVITY OR WHEAT ALLERGY: coeliac disease is AUTOIMMUNE WITH MUCOSAL DAMAGE and requires STRICT LIFELONG AVOIDANCE; sensitivity has NO SEROLOGICAL OR HISTOLOGICAL MARKER; wheat allergy is IgE-MEDIATED. The distinction is why TESTING BEFORE THE DIET matters.**

**SA: gastroscopy is a PATS-supported referral, usually through TQEH for Yorke Peninsula; dietitian access is often BY TELEHEALTH IN MM5 AREAS; COELIAC AUSTRALIA for practical support; TIS National 131 450.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP: IBD — Crohn in particular · lactose intolerance · non-coeliac gluten sensitivity · pancreatic insufficiency · giardiasis · IRRITABLE BOWEL, EXCLUDED BY THE ANAEMIA — SAY THE CRITERIA.**

**THE PLAN: tTG IgA WITH TOTAL IgA TODAY, FBC, IRON STUDIES, B12, FOLATE, VITAMIN D, CALCIUM · GASTROSCOPY WITH DUODENAL BIOPSIES · THEN A STRICT LIFELONG GLUTEN-FREE DIET WITH A DIETITIAN · bone density · TEST FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVES · COELIAC AUSTRALIA.** Then **answer his three questions.**

**Management: DO NOT START A GLUTEN-FREE DIET UNTIL THE TESTS ARE DONE. Then a STRICT LIFELONG GLUTEN-FREE DIET WITH AN EXPERIENCED DIETITIAN · REPLACE DEFICIENCIES · BONE DENSITY ASSESSMENT · OFFER TESTING TO FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVES · refer to COELIAC AUSTRALIA · repeat serology at 6–12 months to confirm response and adherence.**

**IF ALREADY GLUTEN-FREE: do not pretend the tests are valid — arrange a SUPERVISED GLUTEN CHALLENGE, commonly several weeks of daily gluten before testing, or refer for specialist advice. HLA-DQ2/DQ8 TYPING can help: A NEGATIVE RESULT ESSENTIALLY EXCLUDES COELIAC DISEASE, BUT A POSITIVE ONE DOES NOT CONFIRM IT.** VERIFY.

**What the iron failure teaches: in a young man, IRON DEFICIENCY IS NEVER A DIAGNOSIS IN ITSELF — it is a finding that demands a cause. In a young man with no blood loss, MALABSORPTION IS THE LEADING CAUSE; in an older patient, GI MALIGNANCY must be excluded endoscopically.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE SEQUENCE, AND THE RULE ABOUT THE SCANNER. The station is scored on whether you RUN A PRIMARY SURVEY FIRST, NAME ALL FOUR INVESTIGATIONS, and STATE THAT AN UNSTABLE PATIENT WITH FREE FLUID ON FAST GOES TO THEATRE, NOT TO CT.**

**THE SENTENCE TO THE EXAMINER: 'this is a trauma, so I would run a PRIMARY SURVEY FIRST. Then: a FAST SCAN looking for free fluid, a CHEST X-RAY AND PELVIC X-RAY, bloods including FULL BLOOD COUNT, COAGULATION, A VENOUS GAS AND GROUP AND CROSS-MATCH, and a URINE DIPSTICK FOR HAEMATURIA. IF HE IS HAEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE I would then get a CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST — BUT IF HE IS UNSTABLE WITH FREE FLUID ON FAST, HE GOES TO THEATRE RATHER THAN TO THE SCANNER.'**

**READ THE VITALS FOR WHAT THEY ARE: A HEART RATE OF 118 WITH A SYSTOLIC OF 104 IN A FIT 16-YEAR-OLD IS NOT REASSURANCE. CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS MAINTAIN THEIR BLOOD PRESSURE THROUGH VASOCONSTRICTION UNTIL THEY HAVE LOST A LARGE PROPORTION OF CIRCULATING VOLUME, THEN DECOMPENSATE ABRUPTLY. TACHYCARDIA IS THE EARLY SIGN — HYPOTENSION IS LATE.**

**TO TYLER, PLAINLY: 'the pain at the tip of your shoulder is IMPORTANT. There's a nerve that supplies the muscle under your lungs, and it SHARES A PATHWAY WITH THE NERVES FROM YOUR SHOULDER. If there is BLOOD OR IRRITATION UNDER THAT MUSCLE, your brain reads it as shoulder pain. With a handlebar injury to your left side, that makes me CONCERNED ABOUT YOUR SPLEEN, so I'm going to SCAN YOU AND CHECK YOUR BLOOD COUNT.'**

**THE THREE REASONS: A DIRECT BLOW TO THE LEFT FLANK · LEFT UPPER QUADRANT PAIN AND GUARDING · PAIN AT THE TIP OF THE LEFT SHOULDER, which is BLOOD IRRITATING THE DIAPHRAGM · and A RISING HEART RATE.**

**THE HANDLEBAR IS A SPECIAL MECHANISM: a focused, high-energy blow that also injures THE PANCREAS, THE DUODENUM AND BOWEL, AND THE LEFT KIDNEY — injuries that CAN BE MISSED ON EARLY IMAGING. Hence the URINE DIPSTICK FOR HAEMATURIA and the LIPASE, and a low threshold for repeat imaging if pain persists.**

**AFTER SPLENECTOMY OR SIGNIFICANT SPLENIC LOSS: VACCINATION against PNEUMOCOCCUS, MENINGOCOCCUS AND HAEMOPHILUS INFLUENZAE TYPE B, annual influenza, consideration of prophylactic antibiotics, and education about the RISK OF OVERWHELMING POST-SPLENECTOMY INFECTION.** **After non-operative management: NO CONTACT SPORT for a period set by the treating team — typically weeks to months.** VERIFY.

findings: THE DIAGNOSIS IS IN A BRAND NAME

'I'VE BEEN TAKING PANADEINE FORTE' — PARACETAMOL AND CODEINE. CODEINE IS AN OPIOID, AND OPIOIDS CAUSE CONSTIPATION. THAT IS THE DIAGNOSIS, and the treatment STARTS WITH STOPPING IT. The station tests WHETHER YOU KNOW WHAT IS IN IT
THE QUESTION THAT FINDS IT

'WHAT PAINKILLERS HAVE YOU BEEN TAKING — INCLUDING ANYTHING FROM THE CHEMIST?' → 'JUST PANADEINE FORTE FOR MY BACK. A FEW A DAY SINCE I HURT IT.' Name every painkiller, INCLUDING OVER-THE-COUNTER AND CODEINE-CONTAINING
THE TIMELINE IS THE REASONING
BACK INJURY TEN DAYS AGO → CODEINE STARTED → NO MOTION FOR SIX DAYS, BEGINNING DAYS AFTER THE CODEINE → BACK PAIN NOW SETTLED. SAY THE SEQUENCE ALOUD — IT IS THE CAUSAL ARGUMENT
CHARACTERISE THE STOOL
'NOTHING AT ALL FOR SIX DAYS. WHEN I DO GO IT'S LIKE LITTLE HARD PELLETS.' And the four obstruction questions: VOMITING · DISTENSION · WHEN DID YOU LAST PASS WIND · WHEN DID YOU LAST OPEN YOUR BOWELS
THE EXAMINATION CARD

SOFT, MILDLY DISTENDED · PALPABLE FAECAL LOADING IN THE LEFT ILIAC FOSSA · BOWEL SOUNDS PRESENT · RECTUM LOADED WITH HARD STOOL. ASK FOR THE DIGITAL RECTAL EXAMINATION BY NAME, WITH CONSENT AND A CHAPERONE — it is what confirms a loaded rectum
THE VARIANT THAT CHANGES THE ANSWER

ADD VOMITING AND NO FLATUS → OBSTRUCTION, NOT CONSTIPATION. 'That changes things. NOT PASSING WIND AND VOMITING SUGGESTS THE BOWEL IS BLOCKED RATHER THAN SIMPLY LOADED, and that needs HOSPITAL ASSESSMENT TODAY, NOT A LAXATIVE'
STILL EXCLUDE THE BACK

A BACK INJURY WITH NEW CONSTIPATION raises CAUDA EQUINA. Ask: ANY NUMBNESS BETWEEN THE LEGS OR AROUND THE BACK PASSAGE · ANY TROUBLE PASSING URINE · ANY LEG WEAKNESS. The answers are no — BUT ASKING IS THE MARK
IN A 20-YEAR-OLD WOMAN, PREGNANCY IS ON THE LIST
LAST MENSTRUAL PERIOD, AND A URINARY βhCG. Lower abdominal pain and bloating in a woman of reproductive age — the test takes two minutes
ASK HOW MUCH, AND HOW SHE GETS IT
HOW MANY A DAY, FOR HOW LONG, WHO PRESCRIBED IT. CODEINE HAS BEEN PRESCRIPTION-ONLY IN AUSTRALIA SINCE FEBRUARY 2018. Paracetamol dose matters too — confirm she has not exceeded 4 g in 24 hours
THE MISTAKE THAT IS A LISTED FAIL
TREATING THE CONSTIPATION WITHOUT STOPPING THE OPIOID — MACROGOL PRESCRIBED, CODEINE CONTINUED. STOP THE CAUSE FIRST. THEN THE LAXATIVE

dx: **OPIOID-INDUCED CONSTIPATION WITH FAECAL LOADING. The codeine in PANADEINE FORTE — PARACETAMOL WITH CODEINE — slows gut transit by acting on MU-OPIOID RECEPTORS IN THE BOWEL WALL, reducing peristalsis and secretion and increasing fluid absorption, so stools become HARD AND INFREQUENT.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: KNOWING WHAT IS IN THE BRAND NAME, AND STOPPING THE CAUSE BEFORE PRESCRIBING A LAXATIVE.** **Every version of the young-and-atypical abdomen is failed by taking the complaint at face value — here, prescribing macrogol and never asking what she takes.**

**THE SCRIPT: 'Elyse, your bowel is loaded with stool, and THE CAUSE IS THE CODEINE IN THE PANADEINE FORTE. Codeine SLOWS THE BOWEL RIGHT DOWN — that's what has caused this. YOUR BACK HAS SETTLED, SO WE STOP IT AND USE PLAIN PARACETAMOL INSTEAD. Then a laxative called MACROGOL to soften things through, and A SUPPOSITORY TODAY TO CLEAR WHAT IS ALREADY SITTING THERE.'**

**THE FOUR REASONS, READ BACK: NO MOTION FOR SIX DAYS, STARTING DAYS AFTER THE CODEINE BEGAN · HARD PELLET STOOLS · PALPABLE LOADING AND A LOADED RECTUM · and THE BACK PAIN THAT PROMPTED IT HAS ALREADY RESOLVED.**

**TREATMENT SEQUENCE: STOP OR REDUCE THE CODEINE → switch to SIMPLE ANALGESIA → an OSMOTIC LAXATIVE SUCH AS MACROGOL → add a STIMULANT such as senna or bisacodyl if needed → a SUPPOSITORY OR ENEMA FOR A LOADED RECTUM → fluids, mobility.** **Bulk-forming fibre alone is a POOR CHOICE in opioid constipation — it can worsen bloating in a slowed bowel.** VERIFY.

**EXPLAIN THE FUTURE: 'OPIOIDS WILL DO THIS AGAIN. If you ever need a codeine-containing medicine in future, START A LAXATIVE AT THE SAME TIME.'** **That sentence turns a one-off fix into prevention, and examiners score it.**

**THE OBSTRUCTION VARIANT: add VOMITING AND ABSOLUTE CONSTIPATION — NO FLATUS — and the answer changes. 'Not passing wind and vomiting suggests the bowel is BLOCKED RATHER THAN SIMPLY LOADED, and that needs HOSPITAL ASSESSMENT TODAY, NOT A LAXATIVE.'** **A stimulant laxative into an obstructed bowel risks PERFORATION.**

**CONSTIPATION ALSO CAUSES OVERFLOW: a heavily loaded rectum can present as LIQUID FAECAL LEAKAGE mistaken for diarrhoea. If she reports loose leakage alongside no proper motion, THINK OVERFLOW AND DO NOT GIVE AN ANTIDIARRHOEAL.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP: BOWEL OBSTRUCTION · CAUDA EQUINA FROM THE BACK INJURY · PREGNANCY · HYPOTHYROIDISM, HYPERCALCAEMIA AND HYPOKALAEMIA as metabolic causes · IRRITABLE BOWEL WITH CONSTIPATION · and in an older patient, COLORECTAL CANCER.**

**SAFETY-NET: 'if you start VOMITING, stop passing wind, your tummy becomes very swollen or much more painful, or you notice ANY NUMBNESS BETWEEN THE LEGS, TROUBLE PASSING URINE OR LEG WEAKNESS — come straight back.'**

**THE FOUR REASONS, then the plan in order: STOP THE CODEINE, PLAIN PARACETAMOL, MACROGOL, A SUPPOSITORY TODAY, fluids and mobility.**

stem: Ron Falzon, 60, presents with alternating constipation and diarrhoea, 5 kg of unintentional weight loss and some rectal bleeding. His aunt had bowel cancer. He says his screening test last year was normal.
tasks: Take a focused history
Ask the examiner for the examination findings
Explain your diagnosis and differentials
findings: THE SENTENCE THE STATION IS BUILT AROUND

'MY SCREENING TEST LAST YEAR WAS NORMAL.' The role-player is briefed to INSIST on it. A NORMAL SCREENING TEST LAST YEAR DOES NOT PROTECT A SYMPTOMATIC PATIENT. ACCEPTING IT AS REASSURANCE IS A STARRED FAIL
FOUR ALARM FEATURES, ALL IN THE STEM
AGE 60 · A PERSISTENT CHANGE IN BOWEL HABIT — alternating constipation and diarrhoea · 5 kg OF UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS · RECTAL BLEEDING. Plus A FAMILY HISTORY — an aunt with bowel cancer
QUALIFY THE WEIGHT LOSS
'WAS THE WEIGHT LOSS INTENTIONAL?' → 'NO, NOT ON PURPOSE.' UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS IS THE ALARM FEATURE; weight loss from dieting is not
CORRECT THE MISCONCEPTION KINDLY — the scripted line

'I'M GLAD YOU MENTIONED THE SCREENING TEST — IT'S GOOD THAT YOU DID IT. But I want to explain why it doesn't settle this. SCREENING TESTS ARE DESIGNED FOR PEOPLE WITH NO SYMPTOMS. YOU HAVE SYMPTOMS. In someone with symptoms, WE GO STRAIGHT TO LOOKING DIRECTLY, WITH A CAMERA TEST'
WHY THE KIT CAN BE NORMAL WITH A CANCER PRESENT

The immunochemical faecal occult blood test detects HUMAN HAEMOGLOBIN IN STOOL — tumours BLEED INTERMITTENTLY, so a single negative test does not exclude cancer; and a cancer can DEVELOP in the year since. The NBCSP test is every two years from 45 to 74 — AND ONLY FOR PEOPLE WITHOUT SYMPTOMS
CHARACTERISE THE BLEEDING

BRIGHT RED ON THE PAPER OR MIXED IN WITH THE STOOL · DARK OR CLOTS · ANY MUCUS · DOES IT DRIP INTO THE PAN. BLOOD MIXED WITH STOOL, WITH A CHANGE IN HABIT, is more concerning than streaks on the paper with a hard motion — BUT NEITHER IS ATTRIBUTED TO HAEMORRHOIDS IN A 60-YEAR-OLD WITHOUT A COLONOSCOPY
THE FAMILY HISTORY — get the detail

WHICH RELATIVE, WHAT AGE AT DIAGNOSIS, ANY OTHER CANCERS IN THE FAMILY — bowel, endometrial, ovarian, stomach. A FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVE UNDER 55, or multiple relatives, raises LYNCH SYNDROME. An aunt is second-degree — ask about the rest of the tree
THE SYMPTOMS OF ANAEMIA AND OBSTRUCTION

TIREDNESS, BREATHLESSNESS, DIZZINESS — iron deficiency from occult loss. And COLICKY PAIN, DISTENSION, VOMITING, NOT PASSING WIND — impending obstruction, which turns an urgent referral into an emergency
THE EXAMINATION

Pallor · weight · ABDOMINAL MASS · HEPATOMEGALY from metastases · lymphadenopathy including the LEFT SUPRACLAVICULAR NODE · DIGITAL RECTAL EXAMINATION WITH CONSENT AND A CHAPERONE — A LOW RECTAL CANCER CAN BE FELT
THE COMMUNICATION CHALLENGE

He came in believing he was cleared. YOU HAVE TO RAISE THE POSSIBILITY OF CANCER WITHOUT DISMISSING WHAT HE DID RIGHT, AND WITHOUT SOFTENING IT INTO SOMETHING HE CAN DEFER. Warning shot, the word, the reason, the plan

dx: **SUSPECTED COLORECTAL CANCER until proven otherwise — AGE 60, A PERSISTENT CHANGE IN BOWEL HABIT, 5 kg OF UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS, RECTAL BLEEDING, AND A FAMILY HISTORY.** **This warrants URGENT COLONOSCOPY, NOT REPEAT SCREENING.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: CORRECTING THE SCREENING MISCONCEPTION WITHOUT DISMISSING IT. SCREENING IS FOR THE ASYMPTOMATIC; SYMPTOMS GO STRAIGHT TO COLONOSCOPY. Say the sentence: 'SCREENING IS FOR PEOPLE WITHOUT SYMPTOMS. YOU HAVE SYMPTOMS.'**

**THE FULL SCRIPT: 'Ron, I'm glad you mentioned the screening test — IT IS GOOD THAT YOU DID IT. But I want to explain why it doesn't settle this. Screening tests are designed for people with NO SYMPTOMS; they look for problems BEFORE THEY CAUSE TROUBLE. You have symptoms — A CHANGE IN YOUR BOWEL HABIT, WEIGHT LOSS YOU DIDN'T INTEND, AND SOME BLEEDING. In someone with symptoms, WE GO STRAIGHT TO LOOKING DIRECTLY, WITH A CAMERA TEST. A normal kit last year DOESN'T CHANGE THAT.'**

**THEN NAME THE CONCERN, WITH A WARNING SHOT: 'Ron, I need to be honest with you about why I want this done quickly. I AM CONCERNED ABOUT THE POSSIBILITY OF A BOWEL CANCER. I'm not saying you have one — BUT THESE SYMPTOMS TOGETHER ARE EXACTLY THE ONES WE DON'T WAIT ON.'** **Then the five reasons: age · persistent change in habit · unintentional weight loss · bleeding · family history.**

**WHY A NORMAL FOBT DOES NOT EXCLUDE CANCER: tumours BLEED INTERMITTENTLY, so a single immunochemical test can be negative; A LESION CAN DEVELOP IN THE INTERVAL; and PROXIMAL CANCERS MAY BLEED LESS DETECTABLY. THE TEST IS VALIDATED AS A POPULATION SCREEN, NOT AS A DIAGNOSTIC TEST FOR SYMPTOMS.**

**ALTERNATING CONSTIPATION AND DIARRHOEA IS A CLASSIC LEFT-SIDED PATTERN — a narrowing lumen causes constipation, then liquid stool leaks past it. RIGHT-SIDED CANCERS more often present with IRON-DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA AND FATIGUE and few bowel symptoms. RECTAL CANCER gives BLEEDING, TENESMUS AND A SENSE OF INCOMPLETE EMPTYING.**

**IBS IS NOT THE ANSWER: a positive diagnosis ONLY in the absence of alarm features, AND GENERALLY UNDER 50. He has FOUR ALARM FEATURES AND IS 60. Say the exclusion criteria aloud.** **And NEVER ATTRIBUTE RECTAL BLEEDING TO HAEMORRHOIDS IN A 60-YEAR-OLD WITHOUT A COLONOSCOPY — haemorrhoids and cancer COEXIST.**

**THE FAMILY HISTORY MAY MATTER BEYOND HIM: a FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVE diagnosed UNDER 55, TWO OR MORE RELATIVES on the same side, or associated ENDOMETRIAL, OVARIAN OR GASTRIC CANCERS raise LYNCH SYNDROME — refer to FAMILIAL CANCER SERVICES, and his own children may need earlier colonoscopic surveillance.**

**MANAGEMENT: FBC AND IRON STUDIES · UEC, LFT · URGENT COLONOSCOPY WITH BIOPSY · STAGING CT CHEST, ABDOMEN AND PELVIS once confirmed · CEA AS A BASELINE for monitoring, NOT AS A DIAGNOSTIC TEST · MRI PELVIS for rectal cancer staging · MULTIDISCIPLINARY MANAGEMENT — surgery, with chemotherapy or radiotherapy according to stage.**

**SAFETY-NET: impending OBSTRUCTION — colicky pain, distension, vomiting, not passing wind — or HEAVY BLEEDING, DIZZINESS OR FAINTING means THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, NOT THE WAITING LIST.** **SA: urgent colonoscopy referral, usually through TQEH for Yorke Peninsula, with PATS for travel; Cancer Council 13 11 20 for support.**

stem: Jenny Walker, 25, administration officer, complains of bloating. T 36.7 · P 72 · BP 112/70 · RR 14 · BMI 21. Well and comfortable.
tasks: Take a focused history (6 minutes)
Tell the examiner your most likely diagnosis, with your reasons
Give the examiner your differential diagnoses
findings: ONE STEM, TWO ANSWERS

VERSION A: BLOATING SETTLES AFTER SHE OPENS HER BOWELS · STOOLS ALTERNATE HARD THEN LOOSE · STRESS AT WORK · ALL RED FLAGS NEGATIVE → IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME. VERSION B: WORSE AFTER PIZZA AND BREAD · GREASY, BULKY, HARD-TO-FLUSH STOOLS THAT FLOAT AND STICK TO THE PAN · IRON-DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA → COELIAC DISEASE
THE HANDED EXPLANATION IN VERSION B

'I'M A BIT LOW IN IRON BUT THAT'S MY PERIODS — THEY TOLD ME IT'S MY HEAVY PERIODS, AND I'M ON IRON TABLETS.' DO NOT ACCEPT IT. ANAEMIA IN THIS CONTEXT IS MALABSORPTION UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE. The candidate who accepts it LOSES COELIAC DISEASE
DEFINE THE WORD BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE

'WHEN YOU SAY BLOATED, CAN YOU DESCRIBE IT? IS IT THAT YOU'RE BURPING A LOT, OR PASSING MORE WIND, OR IS IT THAT YOUR TUMMY ACTUALLY LOOKS AND FEELS SWOLLEN?' BLOATING IS A SENSATION; DISTENSION IS A MEASURABLE INCREASE IN GIRTH — AND DISTENSION IS THE ONE THAT GETS A MASS OR ASCITES FOUND
THE FOUR STOOL DESCRIPTORS — learn them
GREASY · BULKY · FLOATS · HARD TO FLUSH, STICKS TO THE PAN. STEATORRHOEA IS THE SINGLE HIGHEST-YIELD QUESTION IN VERSION B, and without asking it Version B is diagnosed as IBS
THE NOCTURNAL QUESTION EARNS MARKS
'DOES IT EVER WAKE YOU AT NIGHT, OR IS IT ONLY WHEN YOU'RE AWAKE?' Symptoms that wake a patient point AWAY FROM FUNCTIONAL DISEASE. One question reframes the whole differential
THE OVARIAN CLUSTER — SAY THE WORDS

'DO YOU GET FULL VERY QUICKLY, AFTER ONLY A SMALL AMOUNT OF FOOD? ANY CHANGE IN HOW OFTEN YOU PASS URINE? ANY FAMILY HISTORY OF OVARIAN OR BREAST CANCER?' IN ANY WOMAN WITH PERSISTENT BLOATING, 'I WOULD WANT TO EXCLUDE OVARIAN CANCER' MUST BE SPOKEN — WHATEVER HER AGE
THE GYNAE BLOCK BY 5:00 AT THE LATEST
LAST PERIOD, REGULARITY, ANY CHANCE OF PREGNANCY, SEXUALLY ACTIVE, CONTRACEPTION. In a 25-year-old woman with bloating, 'I DIDN'T GET TO IT' READS THE SAME AS 'I DIDN'T THINK OF IT'
THE ORAL IRON IS A GENUINE SECOND DIFFERENTIAL IN VERSION B
ORAL IRON CAUSES BLOATING, CRAMPING AND CONSTIPATION IN ITS OWN RIGHT. Ask about EVERY MEDICATION, INCLUDING SUPPLEMENTS — and name it as a contributor
THE RASH THAT HANDS YOU THE DIAGNOSIS

AN ITCHY VESICULAR RASH ON ELBOWS, KNEES, BUTTOCKS OR SCALP IS DERMATITIS HERPETIFORMIS — COELIAC DISEASE OF THE SKIN. ERYTHEMA NODOSUM ON THE SHINS IS THE RASH OF IBD, NOT COELIAC. WHICH RASH BELONGS TO WHICH DIAGNOSIS IS A FAVOURITE EXAMINER PROBE
PILOTED VARIANT

One sitting ran FIVE MINUTES OF HISTORY, THEN AN EXAMINATION REQUEST, THEN DIAGNOSIS. TREAT FIVE MINUTES AS THE SAFE ASSUMPTION AND FINISH EARLY. If you are asked to examine, OFFER A PELVIC EXAMINATION CONDITIONALLY: 'given the possibility of an ovarian cause, I'd like to OFFER A PELVIC EXAMINATION WITH A CHAPERONE, if that's acceptable to you'

dx: **VERSION A — IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME, MEETING ROME IV, REACHED AS A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION. VERSION B — COELIAC DISEASE, with ORAL IRON AS A SECONDARY CONTRIBUTOR.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: WHETHER YOU INTERROGATE THE ANSWER THE PATIENT HANDS YOU, OR ACCEPT IT. In Version B she says her anaemia is 'just heavy periods' — ACCEPT THAT AND YOU LOSE COELIAC DISEASE. In Version A she says the bloating settles when she opens her bowels — TAKE THAT AS PERMISSION TO STOP ASKING AND YOU LOSE THE EXCLUSION MARKS THAT MAKE IBS DEFENSIBLE.**

**REFUSING THE HANDED EXPLANATION, VERBATIM: 'you mentioned you're low in iron and that it was PUT DOWN TO HEAVY PERIODS. THAT MAY WELL BE PART OF IT, BUT LOW IRON CAN ALSO MEAN THE BOWEL ISN'T ABSORBING PROPERLY, so I'd like to ask a few questions about your stools. Have you noticed them being GREASY OR BULKY, FLOATING, OR HARD TO FLUSH AWAY?'**

**EARNING IBS OUT LOUD: 'my provisional diagnosis is IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME. I SAY THAT POSITIVELY RATHER THAN BY DEFAULT: recurrent discomfort RELIEVED BY DEFECATION, an ALTERNATING STOOL FORM, and a clear stressor. IMPORTANTLY, I HAVE EXCLUDED THE ALTERNATIVES — no weight loss, no rectal bleeding, no anaemia, no nocturnal symptoms, no family history of bowel or ovarian cancer, no travel, no gluten or dairy relationship, and she is not pregnant.'**

**THE THIRD DISCRIMINATING BEHAVIOUR: IN ANY WOMAN WITH PERSISTENT BLOATING, THE PHRASE 'I WOULD WANT TO EXCLUDE OVARIAN CANCER' MUST BE SPOKEN. Ovarian cancer produces EXACTLY THESE NON-SPECIFIC SYMPTOMS and is THE CLASSIC MISSED DIAGNOSIS in this presentation. The cluster: BLOATING, EARLY SATIETY, PELVIC PAIN, URINARY FREQUENCY — PERSISTENT, and MORE THAN 12 TIMES A MONTH.**

**CORRECTION — ROME IV IS OFTEN TAUGHT AS 'SIX MONTHS OF PAIN', WHICH CONFLATES TWO WINDOWS. THE CRITERIA: ABDOMINAL PAIN AT LEAST ONE DAY PER WEEK OVER THE LAST THREE MONTHS, with ONSET AT LEAST SIX MONTHS BEFORE DIAGNOSIS, plus TWO OF THREE — RELATED TO DEFECATION, CHANGE IN STOOL FREQUENCY, CHANGE IN STOOL FORM.** If challenged: **'the symptom window is three months; the six months refers to the time since onset.'** **STRESS IS NOT A CRITERION.**

**DELIVER THE DIFFERENTIALS IN SIX NAMED GROUPS — SIX GROUPS BEAT A FLAT LIST OF TWELVE: MALIGNANCY — bowel and ovarian · OBSTRUCTION — adhesions or hernia · DIET — coeliac and lactose intolerance · INFECTION — giardia, post-infectious · MOTILITY — drugs including oral iron, diabetes, thyroid · FUNCTIONAL — IBS, LAST.** **Plus INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE and PREGNANCY.**

**VERSION B REASONING: 'my most likely diagnosis is COELIAC DISEASE — the GLUTEN RELATIONSHIP, the STEATORRHOEA indicating fat malabsorption, and the UNEXPLAINED IRON DEFICIENCY, WHICH I DO NOT ACCEPT AS MENSTRUAL UNTIL MALABSORPTION IS EXCLUDED. A second and genuine differential is her ORAL IRON, which causes bloating, cramping and constipation in its own right.' Add LACTOSE INTOLERANCE, WHICH CAN BE SECONDARY TO COELIAC DISEASE.**

**COELIAC TESTING: tTG-IgA WITH TOTAL SERUM IgA, TAKEN WHILE SHE IS STILL EATING GLUTEN, then DUODENAL BIOPSY. STARTING A GLUTEN-FREE DIET BEFORE SEROLOGY INVALIDATES BOTH. Coeliac disease affects roughly 1 IN 70 AUSTRALIANS and the MAJORITY REMAIN UNDIAGNOSED.** VERIFY. **Management: lifelong gluten-free diet with a DIETITIAN · replace iron, B12, folate, vitamin D, calcium, zinc · BONE DENSITOMETRY · SCREEN FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVES · PNEUMOCOCCAL VACCINATION, because FUNCTIONAL HYPOSPLENISM is recognised in coeliac disease.**

**IBS MANAGEMENT, EXPLAINED POSITIVELY — NOT AS 'NOTHING IS WRONG': regular meals, fluids, SOLUBLE FIBRE, reduce caffeine and alcohol · a LOW-FODMAP TRIAL WITH DIETITIAN-SUPERVISED REINTRODUCTION · symptom-targeted antispasmodic, laxative or loperamide by stool pattern · address the stressor, consider psychological therapy · REVIEW, AND RE-OPEN THE DIAGNOSIS IF ANY RED FLAG APPEARS.**
plan: **WIPE, open question.** Then **ACKNOWLEDGE AND SIGNPOST, INCLUDING THE AWKWARD PART: 'bloating can be really uncomfortable. I'll ask a series of questions — SOME ABOUT YOUR BOWELS AND YOUR PERIODS — then we'll make a plan together. Is that all right?'**
**AGENDA IN THE FIRST MINUTE, NOT THE LAST: 'before I start, was there anything in particular that worried you, or something you were hoping we'd do today?'**

**DEFINE THE BLOATING — burping, wind, or genuinely swollen · HOW LONG · CONSTANT OR COMES AND GOES · GETTING WORSE · WORSE AT ANY TIME OF DAY · DOES IT EVER WAKE YOU AT NIGHT · anything better or worse, AND IS IT WORSE AFTER EATING — ANY FOOD THAT SETS IT OFF?**
**GENERAL GI SCREEN: nausea · vomiting · pain · CONSTIPATION · DIARRHOEA · fever.** **Constipation and diarrhoea are the two you must have an answer to before moving on.**
**MALIGNANCY: WEIGHT LOSS without trying · appetite · lumps · tiredness. BOWEL CANCER: BLOOD OR VERY DARK STOOLS · lasting change in habit · FAMILY HISTORY OF BOWEL CANCER.**

**OVARIAN: DO YOU GET FULL VERY QUICKLY · ANY CHANGE IN HOW OFTEN YOU PASS URINE · FAMILY HISTORY OF OVARIAN OR BREAST CANCER. OBSTRUCTION: any SURGERY on your tummy · lump in the groin · PASSING WIND NORMALLY?**

**DIET — LACTOSE: worse after milk, cheese, yoghurt, ice-cream? DIET — COELIAC: ARE YOUR STOOLS GREASY OR BULKY, HARD TO FLUSH, STICKING TO THE PAN OR FLOATING · does BREAD OR PASTA make it worse · anyone with COELIAC DISEASE in the family?**
**If the anaemia is mentioned: DO NOT ACCEPT THE HANDED EXPLANATION — use the scripted line, then chase the stool.**
**INFECTION: travel, camping, tank water, fever, anyone else unwell. MOTILITY: ANY MEDICATIONS, INCLUDING OVER THE COUNTER OR SUPPLEMENTS — AND THE IRON · diabetes · weather preference.**
**IBD: joint pains, mouth ulcers, red or sore eyes, RASHES. IBS: DO YOUR STOOLS ALTERNATE · DOES OPENING YOUR BOWELS MAKE IT BETTER · HOW ARE THINGS AT HOME AND WORK?**
**GYNAE — BY 5:00 WHATEVER IS UNFINISHED: LAST PERIOD, ARE THEY REGULAR, ANY CHANCE OF PREGNANCY, SEXUALLY ACTIVE, CONTRACEPTION.**
**SADMA, past and family history, and a mini-HEADSS for stressors: who do you live with, how are things at work, anything stressful going on?**
**Close the history at 6:00. A one-line summary back.**

**TO THE EXAMINER — MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS WITH REASONS: Version A, IBS EARNED OUT LOUD with the exclusions listed; Version B, COELIAC with the three reasons and the refusal of the menstrual explanation.**
**THE DIFFERENTIALS IN SIX NAMED GROUPS, each with a reason it is less likely — AND SAY 'I WOULD WANT TO EXCLUDE OVARIAN CANCER'.**

**If asked for a plan: FBE, IRON STUDIES, CRP, UEC, LFT, TSH, tTG-IgA WITH TOTAL IgA WHILE ON GLUTEN, URINARY βhCG · PELVIC ULTRASOUND AND CA-125 if bloating persists · NO GLUTEN-FREE DIET BEFORE SEROLOGY.**

stem: Daniel Roberts, 20, apprentice diesel mechanic, complains of abdominal pain. T 36.6 · P 68 · BP 118/74 · RR 14 · BMI 23. Well.
tasks: Take a focused history (6 minutes)
Tell the examiner your most likely diagnosis, with your reasons
Give the examiner your differential diagnoses
findings: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS STEM

WHEN YOU ASK THE GENERAL AGGRAVATING-FACTOR QUESTION HE ANSWERS 'NO'. The dairy relationship ONLY APPEARS WHEN YOU NAME FOOD SPECIFICALLY, AND THEN NAME DAIRY. CANDIDATES WHO ACCEPT THE FIRST 'NO' DIAGNOSE IBS AND FAIL THE REASONING
THE ESCALATION — script it

'You mentioned nothing in particular makes it worse. CAN I ASK MORE SPECIFICALLY ABOUT FOOD — IS IT WORSE AFTER DAIRY, SO MILK, CHEESE, YOGHURT OR ICE-CREAM? WHAT ABOUT BREAD OR PASTA? WHAT ABOUT FATTY OR FRIED MEALS?' → 'ACTUALLY — YES. MILK AND ICE-CREAM. I GET CRAMPS AND BLOATING ABOUT AN HOUR AFTER, EVERY TIME. I'D NEVER PUT IT TOGETHER'
WHAT HE GIVES IF YOU ASK CORRECTLY

SIX MONTHS OF DULL, CENTRAL, PERIUMBILICAL PAIN, COMING AND GOING · 3–4/10 · episodes of an hour or two · BLOATING AND WIND · STOOLS ALTERNATE CONSTIPATED AND LOOSE · NO STRESS AT ALL · CRAMPS AND BLOATING EVERY TIME HE HAS DAIRY · FAMILY HISTORY OF MIGRAINE · ALL RED FLAGS NEGATIVE
HE VOLUNTEERS NOTHING
A young man with a six-month 'minor' symptom who has probably been told it is nothing. He answers briefly. IF YOUR QUESTIONS ARE BROAD YOU WILL GET SIX MINUTES OF 'NO'
QUANTIFY THE DAIRY

HOW MUCH, HOW SOON AFTER, DOES A SMALL AMOUNT DO IT OR ONLY A LARGE AMOUNT, IS HARD CHEESE OR YOGHURT ANY BETTER? Lactose intolerance is DOSE-DEPENDENT, with symptoms 30 MINUTES TO 2 HOURS after dairy — and hard cheese has little lactose
'THERE'S NO STRESS AT ALL'
STRESS IS NOT A ROME IV CRITERION. DO NOT USE ITS ABSENCE TO EXCLUDE IBS, AND DO NOT USE ITS PRESENCE TO PROVE IT
'MY STOOLS GO FROM HARD TO LOOSE'
PREMATURE CLOSURE ON IBS. Note it, then STILL EXCLUDE COELIAC DISEASE AND IBD BEFORE YOU COMMIT. IBS RANKS BELOW A REPRODUCIBLE FOOD TRIGGER
'MY MUM GETS MIGRAINES' — the red herring
ABDOMINAL MIGRAINE requires DISCRETE EPISODES WITH COMPLETE WELLNESS BETWEEN, anorexia, nausea or pallor, AND NO BETTER EXPLANATION. HERE THERE IS ONE. ACKNOWLEDGE IT, DO NOT LEAD WITH IT
RED FLAGS UNCONDITIONALLY — IBD PEAKS AT HIS AGE

WEIGHT LOSS · BLOOD OR MUCUS · NOCTURNAL PAIN OR DIARRHOEA · FEVER · ANAEMIA · MOUTH ULCERS, JOINT PAIN, EYE INFLAMMATION · PERIANAL PAIN OR DISCHARGE · family history of IBD or bowel cancer. ONE COMBINED SENTENCE COVERS THE EXTRA-INTESTINAL SCREEN
THE YORKE PENINSULA DETAIL
'ANY RECENT TRAVEL OR CAMPING? ANY TANK OR CREEK WATER? ANYONE ELSE AT HOME UNWELL? ANY RECENT GASTRO THAT THIS STARTED AFTER?' — GIARDIASIS and POST-INFECTIOUS LACTASE DEFICIENCY both hide here

dx: **LACTOSE INTOLERANCE — PRIMARY, ADULT-ONSET LACTASE NON-PERSISTENCE — with IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME as the principal alternative and COELIAC DISEASE as the alternative that MUST BE EXCLUDED, BECAUSE IT CAUSES SECONDARY LACTOSE INTOLERANCE.**

**DEFINITION WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD: LACTOSE INTOLERANCE IS A DEFICIENCY OF THE ENZYME LACTASE, NOT AN ALLERGY. Unabsorbed lactose reaches the colon, is FERMENTED BY BACTERIA into gas and short-chain fatty acids, and draws water in osmotically — WIND, BLOATING, CRAMPS AND LOOSE STOOL, 30 MINUTES TO 2 HOURS AFTER DAIRY.** **COW'S MILK PROTEIN ALLERGY is IMMUNE-MEDIATED, NOT DOSE-DEPENDENT, and typically presents in INFANCY.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: ESCALATING FROM THE GENERAL AGGRAVATING-FACTOR QUESTION TO A NAMED-FOOD QUESTION. He says 'no' to 'does anything make it worse?'. EVERYTHING IN THIS STATION — the diagnosis, the reasoning marks, the management — SITS BEHIND A SINGLE FOLLOW-UP: 'WHAT ABOUT FOOD? ANY PARTICULAR FOOD — DAIRY, BREAD, FATTY MEALS?'**

**THE SECOND DISCRIMINATING MOMENT — ABDOMINAL MIGRAINE: 'I considered abdominal migraine, BUT THE FINAL CRITERION IS THAT THE PAIN IS NOT ATTRIBUTABLE TO ANOTHER DISORDER, AND HERE IT IS — THERE IS A CLEAR AND REPRODUCIBLE DAIRY RELATIONSHIP.'** **The family history of migraine is BACKGROUND, NOT EVIDENCE.**

**THE THIRD — DO NOT LET A POSITIVE FOOD TRIGGER STOP YOU EXCLUDING COELIAC DISEASE. COELIAC DISEASE DAMAGES THE BRUSH BORDER AND CAUSES SECONDARY LACTOSE INTOLERANCE. FINDING A DAIRY TRIGGER DOES NOT EXCLUDE IT; IT MAKES CHECKING COELIAC SEROLOGY MORE IMPORTANT, NOT LESS.**

**THE 40-SECOND ANSWER: 'Daniel is a well 20-year-old with six months of intermittent, dull, periumbilical pain with bloating and wind and an alternating stool form. THE KEY POSITIVE is that his symptoms are REPRODUCIBLY TRIGGERED WITHIN AN HOUR OR TWO OF DAIRY. Important negatives: no weight loss, bleeding, nocturnal symptoms, fever, extra-intestinal features, perianal disease, gluten relationship, steatorrhoea, travel, surgery or stressor. MY MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS IS LACTOSE INTOLERANCE.'**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP: INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE — the must-not-miss at his age, unlikely with no blood, nocturnal symptoms or extra-intestinal features · COELIAC DISEASE, STILL TO BE EXCLUDED · GIARDIASIS · PEPTIC ULCER AND FUNCTIONAL DYSPEPSIA · CHRONIC PANCREATITIS · CONSTIPATION · IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME, LAST, AS A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION — his alternating stool form would fit, BUT A REPRODUCIBLE FOOD TRIGGER TAKES PRECEDENCE.**

**CONFIRM BY DIETARY TRIAL: STRICT LACTOSE EXCLUSION FOR TWO TO FOUR WEEKS, THEN A STRUCTURED RECHALLENGE — SYMPTOMS MUST RESOLVE AND RETURN. A HYDROGEN BREATH TEST if equivocal: a rise of at least 20 ppm over baseline after a 25–50 g lactose load.** VERIFY.

**MANAGEMENT IS REDUCTION, NOT ELIMINATION: most people TOLERATE ABOUT 12–15 g LACTOSE DAILY — ROUGHLY A CUP OF MILK — IN DIVIDED DOSES WITH OTHER FOOD · HARD CHEESES AND YOGHURT WITH LIVE CULTURES are usually better tolerated · LACTOSE-FREE MILK, or LACTASE ENZYME TABLETS with a dairy meal · PROTECT THE BONES with CALCIUM 1000 mg DAILY AND VITAMIN D · a DIETITIAN rather than unsupervised exclusion.** VERIFY.

**FRAME IT AS NORMAL PHYSIOLOGY: LACTASE NON-PERSISTENCE IS COMMON — the MAJORITY of the world's adults — and especially common in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, Asian, Mediterranean and Middle Eastern populations. It is NOT A DISEASE.** **SA: hydrogen breath testing is generally an ADELAIDE REFERRAL with PATS; dietitian through Country Health Connect.**
plan: **WIPE, open question.** Then **acknowledge, signpost, and the agenda: 'six months is a long time to put up with that. I'll ask about the pain, your bowels and your diet, then tell you what I think. WAS THERE ANYTHING IN PARTICULAR YOU WERE WORRIED IT MIGHT BE?'**

**SIQORAAA: WHERE EXACTLY — CAN YOU POINT WITH ONE FINGER · out of ten · DULL, SHARP, CRAMPY OR BURNING · WHEN DID IT START, HOW LONG DOES EACH EPISODE LAST · does it spread · ANYTHING THAT COMES WITH IT — BLOATING, WIND, NAUSEA · ANYTHING BETTER OR WORSE?**
**When he says 'no', ESCALATE IMMEDIATELY: 'WHAT ABOUT FOOD — DAIRY, BREAD, OR FATTY MEALS SPECIFICALLY?'**
**When dairy comes, QUANTIFY IT: WHICH FOODS · HOW MUCH · HOW SOON AFTER · DOES A SMALL AMOUNT DO IT · IS HARD CHEESE OR YOGHURT BETTER?**
**PATTERN: DOES IT EVER WAKE YOU AT NIGHT · worse at any time of day · how is it affecting work?** Then **GENERAL GI SCREEN: nausea, vomiting, bloating and wind, CONSTIPATION AND DIARRHOEA, fever.**
**RED FLAGS, UNCONDITIONALLY: WEIGHT LOSS · appetite · tiredness · BLOOD OR MUCUS · FEVERS OR NIGHT SWEATS · WAKING AT NIGHT.**

**IBD, ONE COMBINED SENTENCE: MOUTH ULCERS, JOINT PAINS, RED OR PAINFUL EYES, RASHES — ESPECIALLY TENDER RED LUMPS ON THE SHINS — ANY PAIN OR DISCHARGE AROUND THE BACK PASSAGE? Anyone in the family with Crohn disease or colitis?**
**COELIAC: worse after BREAD, PASTA OR BEER · stools GREASY, BULKY, PALE, FLOATING OR HARD TO FLUSH · COELIAC DISEASE IN THE FAMILY?**
**INFECTION: TRAVEL OR CAMPING · TANK OR CREEK WATER · ANYONE ELSE AT HOME UNWELL · A RECENT GASTRO THIS STARTED AFTER?**
**UPPER GI: heartburn, fatty meals, pain through to the back, ANTI-INFLAMMATORY TABLETS. SURGICAL: previous surgery, groin lump, passing wind.**
**IBS: DOES OPENING YOUR BOWELS MAKE IT BETTER · DO YOUR STOOLS ALTERNATE · HOW ARE THINGS AT HOME AND AT YOUR APPRENTICESHIP?** **Dairy must be named by 4:25 at the latest.**
**SADMA · past history · FAMILY HISTORY — COELIAC, IBD, BOWEL CANCER, AND THE MIGRAINE · diet and weight · a mini-HEADSS for a 20-year-old.**
**Close at 6:00 with a one-line summary and his ideas and concerns if not already covered.**
**TO THE EXAMINER: MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS WITH REASONS — LACTOSE INTOLERANCE, the reproducible dairy trigger, the timing, the dose relationship, and the negatives.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP — IBD first as the must-not-miss, COELIAC STILL TO EXCLUDE because it causes secondary lactose intolerance, then giardia, upper GI, constipation, and IBS LAST.** Then **dismiss abdominal migraine WITH ITS EXCLUSION CRITERION STATED.**
**If asked for a plan: SUPERVISED LACTOSE EXCLUSION AND RECHALLENGE · FBE, IRON STUDIES, CRP, tTG-IgA WITH TOTAL IgA, FAECAL CALPROTECTIN, STOOL PCR · DIETITIAN, CALCIUM AND VITAMIN D.**
pefe: **Do now — bedside: ABDOMINAL EXAMINATION INCLUDING HERNIAL ORIFICES AND PERIANAL INSPECTION · WEIGHT AND GROWTH · temperature · urinalysis · A FOOD AND SYMPTOM DIARY FOR TWO WEEKS.**

**Do next — first-line: FBE · IRON STUDIES AND FERRITIN · CRP AND ESR · LFT, UEC · tTG-IgA WITH TOTAL SERUM IgA · FAECAL CALPROTECTIN · STOOL PCR FOR OVA, CYSTS AND PARASITES · consider a HYDROGEN BREATH TEST if the dietary trial is equivocal.**

**Do not miss: FAECAL CALPROTECTIN OR COLONOSCOPY if there is ANY BLOOD, NOCTURNAL DIARRHOEA, WEIGHT LOSS OR RAISED INFLAMMATORY MARKERS · COELIAC SEROLOGY BEFORE YOU ATTRIBUTE EVERYTHING TO DAIRY · a PERIANAL EXAMINATION in a young person with chronic bowel symptoms.**

**Confirm: STRICT LACTOSE EXCLUSION FOR 2–4 WEEKS, then a STRUCTURED RECHALLENGE — SYMPTOMS MUST RESOLVE AND RETURN. Hydrogen breath test: a RISE OF AT LEAST 20 ppm OVER BASELINE after a 25–50 g lactose load indicates colonic fermentation of unabsorbed lactose.** VERIFY.

**Manage: a modest daily amount SPREAD ACROSS THE DAY AND TAKEN WITH OTHER FOOD · HARD CHEESES AND LIVE-CULTURE YOGHURT usually better tolerated · LACTOSE-FREE MILK OR LACTASE TABLETS · CALCIUM AND VITAMIN D · DIETITIAN REFERRAL · RE-OPEN THE DIAGNOSIS if red flags appear or the exclusion trial fails.**
**Secondary causes of lactose intolerance to keep in mind: COELIAC DISEASE · CROHN DISEASE · GIARDIASIS · RECENT GASTROENTERITIS, where post-infectious lactase deficiency is usually temporary.**

**Avoid: DIAGNOSING LACTOSE INTOLERANCE WITHOUT EXCLUDING COELIAC DISEASE · RECOMMENDING A GLUTEN-FREE DIET BEFORE SEROLOGY · COMPLETE DAIRY EXCLUSION WITHOUT CALCIUM REPLACEMENT · CALLING IT IBS BECAUSE THE STOOLS ALTERNATE · LEADING WITH ABDOMINAL MIGRAINE.**

stem: Steph Corrigan, 25, presents with severe epigastric pain since last night and repeated vomiting. Results: WCC raised · lipase markedly raised · AST and ALT 2–3× upper limit · bilirubin normal.
tasks: Take a focused history
Explain the results and your diagnosis
Give your differentials and management
findings: THE DIAGNOSIS IS ON THE DOOR SHEET — SO THE MARKS ARE NOT FOR SAYING IT

WCC RAISED · LIPASE MARKEDLY RAISED · AST AND ALT 2–3× UPPER LIMIT · BILIRUBIN NORMAL. THE MARKS ARE FOR FINDING THE CAUSE, INTERPRETING THE MILDLY ABNORMAL LIVER TESTS CORRECTLY, AND EXPLAINING RESULTS TO A FRIGHTENED 25-YEAR-OLD IN PLAIN ENGLISH
THE TRAP IN THE RESULTS

REPORTING THE MILDLY RAISED AST AND ALT AS A SECOND DISEASE. MILD TRANSAMINASE ELEVATION IS EXPECTED IN ACUTE PANCREATITIS. What it DOES do: AN ALT ABOVE ROUGHLY THREE TIMES THE UPPER LIMIT MAKES GALLSTONE PANCREATITIS CONSIDERABLY MORE LIKELY — use it as a POINTER TO THE CAUSE
THE THREE EPIGASTRIC ADD-ONS TO SICORA
'DOES IT GO THROUGH TO YOUR BACK?' · 'IS IT BETTER IF YOU SIT FORWARD OR CURL UP?' · 'WHAT DOES FOOD DO TO IT — BETTER, WORSE, OR NO DIFFERENCE?'
THE SIX CAUSE QUESTIONS — ask all six, every time

ALCOHOL — 'how much in a usual week, in standard drinks? A heavy session in the last few days?' · GALLSTONES — 'ever told you have gallstones? Gallbladder surgery?' · DRUGS — anti-inflammatories, steroids, AND 'ANY INJECTIONS FOR WEIGHT LOSS OR DIABETES — OZEMPIC, WEGOVY, TRULICITY?' · METABOLIC — HIGH TRIGLYCERIDES, family history, CALCIUM OR PARATHYROID · PROCEDURES AND TRAUMA — a recent ERCP, abdominal injury · INFECTION — recent viral illness, mumps
VERSION A — alcohol
'I HAD A BIG NIGHT ON SATURDAY.' → 'HOW MANY STANDARD DRINKS, OVER HOW LONG? HOW MUCH IN A USUAL WEEK? HAVE YOU EVER TRIED TO CUT DOWN?' QUANTIFY IT — 'a big night' is not a history
VERSION B1 — hypertriglyceridaemia

KNOWN HIGH CHOLESTEROL AND TRIGLYCERIDES, OR A FAMILY HISTORY, and a GROSSLY ABNORMAL LIPID PANEL. The serum may look LIPAEMIC. Triglycerides above about 11 mmol/L are the usual pancreatitis threshold. VERIFY
VERSION B2 — the GLP-1 agonist, and TWO DELIBERATE DECOYS

ON SEMAGLUTIDE FOR MONTHS. 'I'VE LOST 3 kg' — 'WAS THAT ON PURPOSE?' — INTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS ON A WEIGHT-LOSS INJECTION IS THE DRUG WORKING, NOT A RED FLAG. 'I ALREADY HAD MY GALLBLADDER OUT' — DO NOT ABANDON THE PANCREAS: STONES CAN SIT IN THE DUCT AFTER CHOLECYSTECTOMY, and THE DRUG ITSELF REMAINS IN PLAY
ONE CARDIAC QUESTION AND AN ECG — IN EVERY EPIGASTRIC STATION

'ANY CHEST PAIN OR TIGHTNESS? SHORTNESS OF BREATH? SWEATING? DOES IT GO INTO YOUR JAW OR DOWN YOUR ARM?' Then 'I WOULD LIKE AN ECG.' AN INFERIOR MI PRESENTS AS EPIGASTRIC PAIN AND NAUSEA. Omitting it is a starred fail
THE SINGLE TEST CANDIDATES FORGET
EVERY PATIENT WITH ACUTE PANCREATITIS GETS AN ABDOMINAL ULTRASOUND — TO LOOK FOR GALLSTONES AND DUCT DILATATION. Lipase quoted, imaging never mentioned, is a listed fail
THE SIGNS YOU NAME BUT DO NOT EXPECT

CULLEN'S SIGN — periumbilical bruising · GREY TURNER'S SIGN — flank bruising. Both reflect RETROPERITONEAL HAEMORRHAGE, are LATE AND UNCOMMON, and carry a POOR PROGNOSIS — name them in your inspection request
findingsLabel: The diagnosis is on the door sheet — the marks are for the cause and the liver tests
must: FAIL — Never asking a cardiac question or requesting an ECG.
FAIL — Calling the mildly raised AST and ALT a second, separate liver disease.
FAIL — Naming pancreatitis and never naming a cause.
FAIL — Recording 3 kg weight loss as a red flag without asking if it was intentional.
ASK — Any injections for weight loss or diabetes — Ozempic, Wegovy, Trulicity?
ASK — How many standard drinks, and any heavy session in the last few days?

dx: **ACUTE PANCREATITIS — acute inflammation of the pancreas from PREMATURE ACTIVATION OF ITS OWN DIGESTIVE ENZYMES, causing AUTODIGESTION of the gland and surrounding tissue. CAUSE BY VERSION: ALCOHOL (A) · HYPERTRIGLYCERIDAEMIA (B1) · GLP-1 AGONIST (B2).**

**THE DIAGNOSIS NEEDS TWO OF THREE: CHARACTERISTIC PAIN · LIPASE OR AMYLASE AT THREE OR MORE TIMES THE UPPER LIMIT · CHARACTERISTIC IMAGING. LIPASE IS PREFERRED — MORE SPECIFIC AND IT STAYS RAISED LONGER. THE HEIGHT OF THE LIPASE DOES NOT INDICATE SEVERITY.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: QUALIFY EVERY ABNORMAL NUMBER AND EVERY RED FLAG BEFORE YOU REACT TO IT. Mildly raised transaminases are EXPECTED, NOT A SECOND DISEASE. Three kilograms of weight loss on a weight-loss injection is A THERAPEUTIC EFFECT, NOT A RED FLAG. CANDIDATES FAIL BY TREATING DATA AS CONCLUSIONS.**

**EXPLAINING THE RESULTS, VERBATIM: 'Steph, the important blood test is an enzyme called LIPASE, which THE PANCREAS MAKES. Yours is VERY HIGH, and together with the type of pain you've described that tells me YOUR PANCREAS IS INFLAMED — acute pancreatitis. Your WHITE CELL COUNT IS UP, which is your body responding. Your LIVER TESTS ARE SLIGHTLY RAISED. THAT IS EXPECTED WITH PANCREATITIS AND DOES NOT MEAN YOU HAVE A SEPARATE LIVER PROBLEM — but it does make me want to CHECK YOUR GALLBLADDER WITH AN ULTRASOUND, because A SMALL STONE SLIPPING DOWN CAN SET THE PANCREAS OFF.'**

**THE CAUSES, GROUPED — GALLSTONES AND ALCOHOL ACCOUNT FOR ROUGHLY FOUR IN FIVE AUSTRALIAN CASES; THE REST ARE WORTH MARKS PRECISELY BECAUSE MOST CANDIDATES STOP AFTER TWO: TRIGLYCERIDES AND CALCIUM · DRUGS INCLUDING GLP-1 AGONISTS · obstruction, ERCP, trauma · infection · autoimmune · idiopathic.**

**VERSION B2, THE TWO DECOYS ANSWERED: 'you mentioned losing three kilos — WAS THAT ON PURPOSE? … Right, that's THE INJECTION DOING WHAT IT IS MEANT TO DO, so I'm not treating that as a warning sign. And you've had your gallbladder out, which makes gallstones LESS LIKELY — BUT NOT IMPOSSIBLE, BECAUSE A STONE CAN STILL SIT IN THE TUBE. I also have to be honest: THIS CLASS OF INJECTION CAN ITSELF, UNCOMMONLY, INFLAME THE PANCREAS. It's high on my list and WE WILL NEED TO STOP IT while we sort this out.'**

**THE GLP-1 AGONIST QUESTION NOW BELONGS IN EVERY ABDOMINAL HISTORY: PANCREATITIS IS A RECOGNISED ADVERSE EFFECT · RAPID WEIGHT LOSS OF ANY CAUSE PROMOTES GALLSTONE FORMATION · they DELAY GASTRIC EMPTYING, which matters peri-operatively. ASK BY BRAND AS WELL AS BY CLASS — patients say 'Ozempic', not 'a GLP-1 receptor agonist'.** VERIFY current PBS criteria.

**MANAGEMENT: ADMIT · IV ACCESS · AGGRESSIVE FLUID RESUSCITATION WITH A BALANCED CRYSTALLOID — HARTMANN'S — GUIDED BY URINE OUTPUT AND HAEMODYNAMICS · OPIOID ANALGESIA IS APPROPRIATE · antiemetics · oxygen if hypoxic · monitor electrolytes, calcium, glucose. THEN: EARLY ENTERAL NUTRITION RATHER THAN PROLONGED STARVATION · NO ROUTINE PROPHYLACTIC ANTIBIOTICS · score severity at 48 hours · ICU for organ failure.**

WHY THE STORY DOES NOT FIT

GALLSTONE PAIN comes on SUDDENLY AFTER FATTY FOOD, LASTS AN HOUR OR TWO, and often goes to the RIGHT SHOULDER. HIS is a GNAWING PAIN THAT HAS BEEN THERE FOR WEEKS, WORSE WHEN HE EATS, AND SETTLES WITH ANTACIDS

QUIET GALLSTONES ARE COMMON AND USUALLY LEFT ALONE

dx: **PEPTIC ULCER DISEASE — NSAID-RELATED, GASTRIC ULCER PATTERN — with INCIDENTAL, ASYMPTOMATIC GALLSTONES.** **A peptic ulcer is a break in the mucosal lining of the stomach or duodenum EXTENDING THROUGH THE MUSCULARIS MUCOSAE, most often caused by HELICOBACTER PYLORI or NSAIDs.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: QUALIFY THE REPORT BEFORE YOU REACT TO IT. STONES PLUS A FITTING STORY EQUALS BILIARY DISEASE. STONES PLUS A NON-FITTING STORY EQUALS AN INCIDENTAL FINDING. Candidates fail by TREATING DATA AS CONCLUSIONS.**

**REFUSING THE GALLSTONE TRAP, VERBATIM: 'Warren, the scan DOES SHOW SOME STONES in your gallbladder. BUT I DON'T THINK THEY ARE CAUSING THIS PAIN, and here is why: gallstone pain comes on SUDDENLY AFTER FATTY FOOD, LASTS AN HOUR OR TWO and often goes to the RIGHT SHOULDER. Yours is A GNAWING PAIN that has been there FOR WEEKS, it is WORSE WHEN YOU EAT, and it SETTLES WITH ANTACIDS. THERE IS NO INFLAMMATION OF THE GALLBLADDER ON THE SCAN. That pattern, PLUS THE IBUPROFEN YOU TAKE FOR YOUR BACK, points to AN ULCER IN THE STOMACH.'**

**THE MECHANISM IN ONE LINE FOR HIM: 'anti-inflammatories like ibuprofen BLOCK THE CHEMICALS THAT PROTECT THE LINING OF THE STOMACH, so the acid starts to wear a small raw patch in it — THAT'S THE ULCER.'** **Technically: NSAIDs INHIBIT COX-1 AND REDUCE PROSTAGLANDIN-MEDIATED MUCOSAL PROTECTION — mucus, bicarbonate, and blood flow.**

**GASTRIC VERSUS DUODENAL: GASTRIC — pain CLASSICALLY WORSE WITH EATING, and ALWAYS BIOPSIED TO EXCLUDE MALIGNANCY, then RE-SCOPED TO CONFIRM HEALING. DUODENAL — pain RELIEVED BY EATING AND WORST WHEN HUNGRY OR AT NIGHT; usually NOT re-scoped.** **The food pattern is suggestive, not diagnostic — endoscopy decides.**

**MANAGEMENT, IN ORDER: STOP THE OFFENDING NSAID AND DISCUSS ALTERNATIVES FOR THE BACK PAIN — paracetamol, physiotherapy, activity · START A PROTON PUMP INHIBITOR · TEST FOR H. PYLORI — urea breath test or stool antigen — AND STOP THE PPI BEFOREHAND OR THE TEST IS FALSELY NEGATIVE · advise on alcohol and smoking · SAFETY-NET FOR BLEEDING.**

**IF H. PYLORI IS POSITIVE: ERADICATION with A PPI PLUS AMOXICILLIN AND CLARITHROMYCIN FOR SEVEN DAYS, then CONFIRM ERADICATION with a repeat breath test at least four weeks after antibiotics.** VERIFY current Therapeutic Guidelines regimen and local resistance advice.

**ENDOSCOPY IF ANY ALARM FEATURE: AGE OVER 50 WITH NEW DYSPEPSIA · UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS · DYSPHAGIA · PERSISTENT VOMITING · ANAEMIA · EVIDENCE OF BLEEDING · A MASS.** **At 40 without alarm features, TEST-AND-TREAT with H. pylori testing plus stopping the NSAID is reasonable — BUT THE ULCER PATTERN WITH REGULAR NSAIDs MAKES A LOW THRESHOLD FOR GASTROSCOPY SENSIBLE.**

**THE GALLSTONES, HANDLED IN THREE SENTENCES: 'the stones are REAL · they're NOT CAUSING THIS · and if you ever get SUDDEN SEVERE PAIN UNDER THE RIGHT RIBS AFTER FOOD, A FEVER, OR YELLOWING OF YOUR SKIN OR EYES, THAT'S WHEN THEY'VE STARTED TO MATTER.' ASYMPTOMATIC GALLSTONES ARE NOT AN INDICATION FOR CHOLECYSTECTOMY.**

**IF HE MUST STAY ON AN NSAID: THE LOWEST DOSE FOR THE SHORTEST TIME, WITH PPI GASTROPROTECTION, and avoid combining with aspirin, steroids, SSRIs or anticoagulants.** **SAFETY-NET: VOMITING BLOOD, BLACK TARRY STOOLS, FAINTING, OR SUDDEN SEVERE PAIN WITH A RIGID TUMMY — CALL 000.** **SA: gastroscopy through Wallaroo or TQEH with PATS.**

findings: THE ONE CLUE THE CASE IS BUILT AROUND

'IT'S WORSE AFTER I EAT.' DO NOT STOP THERE. TWO FOLLOW-UP QUESTIONS: 'IS THERE A PARTICULAR FOOD THAT BRINGS IT ON?' and 'HOW SOON AFTER EATING DOES THE PAIN START?' CANDIDATES WHO ACCEPT THE ANSWER AND MOVE ON END UP UNABLE TO JUSTIFY THEIR DIAGNOSIS
THE TIMING ANSWER IS DIAGNOSTIC
PAIN WITHIN THE FIRST HOUR OF EATING, MADE WORSE BY THE MEAL → GASTRIC ULCER — THE ONE THAT CAN BE MALIGNANT. PAIN 2–5 HOURS AFTER A MEAL, AT NIGHT, RELIEVED BY FOOD OR ANTACID → DUODENAL ULCER
THE CAUSE HE MENTIONS IN PASSING

'I TAKE NUROFEN FOR MY BACK.' → DOSE, FREQUENCY, DURATION, AND WHETHER HE TAKES IT ON AN EMPTY STOMACH. And 'I TAKE QUICK-EZE FOR IT' → recognise it as an ANTACID; ask whether it helps and how often he needs it
THE UPPER-GI RED FLAGS — not the lower-GI ones

BLACK TARRY STOOLS · VOMITING BLOOD OR COFFEE GROUNDS · DIFFICULTY OR PAIN SWALLOWING · PERSISTENT VOMITING OR EARLY FULLNESS · WEIGHT LOSS · family history of stomach cancer · PAIN THAT WAKES HIM. BLEEDING FROM THE STOMACH GOES DOWN AS MELAENA OR UP AS HAEMATEMESIS — ASKING ABOUT FRESH RECTAL BLEEDING IS NOT THE QUESTION THAT FITS THE ANATOMY
ASK THE EXAMINER BEFORE YOU SIT DOWN
'BEFORE I BEGIN, COULD YOU TELL ME WHETHER THE PATIENT IS HAEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE, AND GIVE ME HIS VITAL SIGNS?' Ten seconds — it buys a mark and PROTECTS YOU IF THE STATION IS A DISGUISED BLEED
THREE ANATOMICAL GROUPS — announce them aloud
1 REFLUX AND PEPTIC ULCER · 2 PANCREAS · 3 LIVER AND GALLBLADDER — then CLOSE WITH THE CHEST. STRUCTURE THAT IS NOT AUDIBLE DOES NOT EXIST
VERSION A AND B

A: he points to the LEFT UPPER QUADRANT — open with reflux and peptic ulcer. B: he points to the EPIGASTRIUM — NOTHING IN YOUR STRUCTURE CHANGES; the three groups simply carry equal weight. DO NOT LET THE DIFFERENT POINTING FINGER DERAIL YOU
THE 15-SECOND CHEST SWEEP — never skip

'WITH ALL OF THIS, HAVE YOU HAD ANY CHEST PAIN OR TIGHTNESS, ESPECIALLY ON EXERTION? ANY SHORTNESS OF BREATH? ANY COUGH OR FEVER?' ACS AND LOWER LOBE PNEUMONIA BOTH PRESENT AS UPPER ABDOMINAL PAIN AND BOTH ARE FAIL-IF-MISSED
WHY THE OCCUPATION IS IN THE STEM

LONG-HAUL DRIVING = IRREGULAR MEALS, NIGHT SHIFTS, CAFFEINE, TAKEAWAY, AND REACHING FOR ANTI-INFLAMMATORIES TO GET THROUGH BACK PAIN. It also means LIMITED ACCESS TO A REGULAR GP — book review AROUND HIS ROSTER, and say so aloud
