dx: **PEPTIC ULCER DISEASE, MOST LIKELY NSAID-ASSOCIATED — regular Nurofen (ibuprofen) — with HELICOBACTER PYLORI as the other major cause to test for.** **Definition: a break in the mucosa of the stomach or duodenum EXTENDING THROUGH THE MUSCULARIS MUCOSAE, produced by acid and pepsin acting on a mucosa whose defences have been broken — by H. pylori, NSAIDs, or both.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: NAMING THE DIAGNOSIS IS EASY. THE MARK IS WON OR LOST ON THE SECOND DIFFERENTIAL. You must say, OUT LOUD AND UNPROMPTED, that you considered GASTRIC MALIGNANCY, name the features that made it less likely, and say what you would do to exclude it.** **'Peptic ulcer, reflux and gastritis' is THREE VERSIONS OF THE SAME BENIGN ANSWER and HAS EXCLUDED NOTHING.**

**THE ANSWER, VERBATIM: 'my most likely diagnosis is PEPTIC ULCER DISEASE, most probably caused by the ANTI-INFLAMMATORY TABLETS. My SECOND THOUGHT, and the one I have DELIBERATELY LOOKED FOR, is A CANCER OF THE STOMACH — ulcers in the stomach can be malignant. AGAINST THAT: he is 32, NO WEIGHT LOSS, NORMAL APPETITE, NO VOMITING OF BLOOD, NO BLACK STOOLS, NO DIFFICULTY SWALLOWING, NO FAMILY HISTORY. I would still confirm with GASTROSCOPY AND BIOPSY if he does not settle.'**

**CORRECTION — THE SOURCE RECORDING CONTRASTS 'PEPTIC ULCERS' WITH 'DUODENAL ULCERS' AND SAYS THE FIRST CAN BECOME MALIGNANT. PEPTIC ULCER DISEASE IS THE UMBRELLA TERM CONTAINING BOTH. The correct statement: GASTRIC ULCERS CAN BE MALIGNANT OR OVERLIE A MALIGNANCY AND MUST ALWAYS BE BIOPSIED; DUODENAL ULCERS ARE ESSENTIALLY NEVER MALIGNANT.** If challenged: **'peptic ulcer disease covers both sites; IT IS THE GASTRIC ULCER THAT CARRIES MALIGNANT POTENTIAL and needs biopsy and repeat endoscopy.'**

**EXPLAIN IT WITHOUT BLAME, IN WORDS A TRUCK DRIVER USES: 'the most likely cause is AN ULCER — A RAW PATCH IN THE LINING OF YOUR STOMACH. The Nurofen you've been taking for your back is a VERY COMMON CAUSE — IT STRIPS AWAY THE STOMACH'S PROTECTIVE LAYER. MOST PEOPLE HAVE NO IDEA IT CAN DO THAT.'**

**DECODE THE AUSTRALIAN BRANDS: QUICK-EZE, MYLANTA, GAVISCON — antacids or alginates · SOMAC — pantoprazole · NUROFEN — ibuprofen, THE CULPRIT · PANADOL — paracetamol, harmless here.** **If you truly do not recognise a brand, ASK THE PATIENT WHAT HE TAKES IT FOR — a legitimate clinical question. ASKING THE EXAMINER IS NOT.**

**THE FOUR MOVES, IN ORDER: STOP THE IBUPROFEN TODAY · TEST FOR H. PYLORI — urea breath test or faecal antigen · START A PPI · CHECK A FULL BLOOD COUNT FOR ANAEMIA — then review in 4–6 weeks.** **PPI: 4 WEEKS FOR A DUODENAL ULCER, 8 WEEKS FOR A GASTRIC OR NSAID-ASSOCIATED ULCER.**

**H. PYLORI ERADICATION, 7 DAYS: ESOMEPRAZOLE 20 mg TWICE DAILY + AMOXICILLIN 1 g TWICE DAILY + CLARITHROMYCIN 500 mg TWICE DAILY — dispensed as a combination pack. METRONIDAZOLE 400 mg TWICE DAILY REPLACES AMOXICILLIN IN PENICILLIN ALLERGY. CONFIRM CURE with a urea breath test ≥4 WEEKS AFTER THE ANTIBIOTICS AND ≥2 WEEKS OFF THE PPI. SEROLOGY STAYS POSITIVE AFTER TREATMENT AND CANNOT CONFIRM CURE.** VERIFY.

**ESCALATE IMMEDIATELY, FROM THE HISTORY ALONE: HAEMATEMESIS OR MELAENA WITH DIZZINESS OR COLLAPSE · SUDDEN SEVERE PAIN WITH A RIGID BOARD-LIKE ABDOMEN — perforation · JAUNDICE WITH FEVER AND RIGORS — cholangitis · CHEST TIGHTNESS WITH SWEATING — ACS. Any of these and THE STATION STOPS BEING A GENERAL PRACTICE HISTORY.**

**THE DRIVING POINT, IN PROPORTION: UNCOMPLICATED ULCER DISEASE DOES NOT AFFECT A COMMERCIAL LICENCE. It matters only with SYMPTOMATIC ANAEMIA, SYNCOPE OR OPIOID-LEVEL ANALGESIA, under Assessing Fitness to Drive — and SA AND THE NT ARE THE TWO JURISDICTIONS WHERE REPORTING AN UNFIT DRIVER IS A LEGAL DUTY.** **SAFETY-NET: vomiting blood, black stools, or pain that changes — come straight back or call 000.**
plan: **TO THE EXAMINER BEFORE SITTING: HAEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE, AND HIS VITAL SIGNS?**

**WIPE and the four-line opening, including the structure: 'I'd like to ask about this pain, then your digestive system in general, and a few to make sure we're not missing anything serious.'** Then **ONE OPEN QUESTION AND FIVE SECONDS OF SILENCE.**
**EMPATHY AND PARTNERSHIP BEFORE ANY CLOSED QUESTION, then THE AGENDA EARLY: 'was there something in particular you were worried this might be?'**

**PAIN: SHOW ME WITH ONE FINGER · out of ten · BURNING, GNAWING, DULL, SHARP, CRUSHING · when did it start, constant or coming and going, getting worse · THROUGH TO YOUR BACK OR UP TO YOUR SHOULDER · ANYTHING BETTER OR WORSE?**
**THE FOOD PROBE: 'IS THERE A PARTICULAR FOOD?' — spicy and alcohol, dairy, bread and pasta, fatty meals · 'HOW SOON AFTER EATING DOES IT START?' · 'DOES IT WAKE YOU AT NIGHT?'**
**GENERAL GI, RAPID-FIRE: nausea, vomiting, bloating, passing wind, diarrhoea, constipation, fever, change in habit.**

**'I'm going to ask a few questions I ask everybody with this kind of pain' — THE RED FLAGS: WEIGHT LOSS · APPETITE · LUMPS · TIREDNESS · NIGHT SWEATS · BLACK TARRY STOOLS · VOMITING BLOOD OR COFFEE GROUNDS · DIFFICULTY OR PAIN SWALLOWING · EARLY FULLNESS · STOMACH OR BOWEL CANCER IN THE FAMILY.**

**GROUP 1, REFLUX AND PEPTIC ULCER: heartburn · acid or metallic taste · WATER BRASH · worse lying flat · 'WHAT MEDICINES, TABLETS OR ANYTHING FROM THE CHEMIST — including things you buy yourself?' — then QUANTIFY THE NUROFEN · alcohol, smoking, coffee, spicy food, stress · previous ulcer · EVER TESTED FOR HELICOBACTER?**

**GROUP 2, PANCREAS: bores through to the back · better leaning forward · abdominal injury · viral illness · high triglycerides · gallstones.** **Alcohol and vomiting already asked — SAY SO rather than repeating.**
**GROUP 3, LIVER AND GALLBLADDER: yellowing · itching · dark urine or pale stools · attacks after fatty meals · fevers with shaking chills · tattoos, injecting, transfusions.**
**HARD CHECKPOINT — THE CHEST SWEEP: chest pain or tightness on exertion · breathlessness · cough or fever.**

**SADMA · past and family history · ONE QUESTION ON HIS WORK: 'how do the long shifts affect your meals — and how is this affecting your driving?'** Then **ideas, concerns, expectations, and a one-line summary.**
**TO JAMES, IN PLAIN ENGLISH: the ulcer, the Nurofen as a common cause most people don't know about, WITHOUT BLAME.** Then **the reasons — worse after food, regular ibuprofen, antacid response.**

**TO THE EXAMINER — PEPTIC ULCER FIRST, GASTRIC MALIGNANCY SECOND WITH THE FEATURES AGAINST IT, then oesophageal and pancreatic cancer, GORD, pancreatitis, biliary disease, hepatitis, ACS AND LOWER LOBE PNEUMONIA.**
**IF ASKED: stop the ibuprofen, test for H. pylori, PPI, FBC, review in 4–6 weeks booked around his roster — and the SAFETY-NET for vomiting blood, black stools or a change in the pain.**
pefe: **Do now: CONFIRM HAEMODYNAMIC STABILITY · EXAMINE THE ABDOMEN for guarding and rebound · DIGITAL RECTAL EXAMINATION FOR MELAENA with consent · ECG IF ANY CHEST SYMPTOM · STOP THE IBUPROFEN TODAY · START A PPI.**
**Do next: FBE, IRON STUDIES, UEC, LFT, LIPASE · H. PYLORI UREA BREATH TEST OR FAECAL ANTIGEN · REFER FOR GASTROSCOPY IF ALARM FEATURES, AGE OVER 50, OR FAILURE TO SETTLE · REVIEW IN 4–6 WEEKS.**

**What the results change: H. PYLORI POSITIVE → ERADICATE, then CONFIRM CURE · NEGATIVE WITH NSAID USE → drug-induced ulcer; stop the NSAID, PPI for 8 weeks, PARACETAMOL OR A TOPICAL NSAID instead · MICROCYTIC ANAEMIA → CHRONIC BLOOD LOSS UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE; GASTROSCOPY REGARDLESS OF AGE · GASTRIC ULCER AT ENDOSCOPY → MULTIPLE BIOPSIES AND REPEAT GASTROSCOPY AT 6–8 WEEKS · DUODENAL ULCER → no routine repeat.**

**Doses: ESOMEPRAZOLE 20 mg, OMEPRAZOLE 20 mg or PANTOPRAZOLE 40 mg ONCE DAILY — 4 weeks duodenal, 8 weeks gastric or NSAID-associated. Eradication: PPI BD + AMOXICILLIN 1 g BD + CLARITHROMYCIN 500 mg BD × 7 DAYS; METRONIDAZOLE 400 mg BD if penicillin-allergic.** VERIFY against Therapeutic Guidelines. If pressed on a number: **'I would prescribe according to the current Therapeutic Guidelines — a standard-dose PPI with amoxicillin and clarithromycin for seven days.'**

**Do not miss: GASTRIC CANCER BEHIND THE ULCER · A SILENT BLEED — check for anaemia · PERFORATION if the pain changes character — ERECT CHEST X-RAY, but A NORMAL FILM DOES NOT EXCLUDE IT; CT IS MORE SENSITIVE · CARDIAC PAIN MASQUERADING AS INDIGESTION.**
**Avoid: REASSURANCE WITHOUT RED-FLAG QUESTIONS · CONTINUING ANY NSAID · LONG-TERM PPI WITHOUT A DIAGNOSIS · SEROLOGY TO CONFIRM H. PYLORI CURE · ANTIBIOTICS WITHOUT TESTING FIRST.**

**SA: uncomplicated disease is managed in general practice. If he bleeds or perforates — resuscitate locally and MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33. Elective gastroscopy means Adelaide — PATS for travel and accommodation, Country Health Connect for coordination; Closing the Gap PBS co-payment for eligible patients; TIS National 131 450.**

SEPARATE DYSPHAGIA FROM ODYNOPHAGIA FIRST
'IS IT HARD TO SWALLOW, OR PAINFUL TO SWALLOW?' Patients use the same words for both. The whole history taken without asking whether it hurts is a listed fail
AXIS ONE — HIGH OR LOW

'IS IT HARD TO START THE SWALLOW — DO YOU COUGH OR CHOKE AS YOU BEGIN? OR DOES IT GO DOWN AND THEN GET STUCK? AND IF IT STICKS, IS THAT IN YOUR THROAT OR IN YOUR CHEST?' OROPHARYNGEAL = trouble initiating, choking; OESOPHAGEAL = sticks seconds later, points to chest
AXIS TWO — THE HIGHEST-YIELD QUESTION IN THE STATION
'DOES IT HAPPEN WITH SOLID FOOD ONLY, OR WITH LIQUIDS AS WELL?' SOLIDS ONLY = OBSTRUCTIVE; SOLIDS AND LIQUIDS FROM THE OUTSET = MOTILITY. ASK IT BY 1:30. Then PROGRESSION
ANTACID FAILURE IS A RED FLAG

'MYLANTA DOESN'T HELP ANY MORE.' ACKNOWLEDGE IT EXPLICITLY — A TREATMENT THAT STOPS WORKING IN A CHRONIC UPPER GI COMPLAINT IS A CHANGE THAT NEEDS EXPLAINING. And reflux is a ROUTE TO STRICTURE AND BARRETT'S ADENOCARCINOMA, NOT THE ENDPOINT
THE CANCER-SPECIFIC RED FLAGS — FOUR SITES, THE ONES CANDIDATES MISS

OROPHARYNGEAL — SORE THROAT THAT WON'T SETTLE, EAR PAIN, VOICE CHANGE · OESOPHAGEAL/GASTRIC — HAEMATEMESIS, MELAENA · THYROID — NECK LUMP, WEATHER PREFERENCE · LUNG/MEDIASTINAL — COUGH, HAEMOPTYSIS. The generic four alone do not tick the box
DO NOT DELIVER CANNED EMPATHY

The recalled openings differ — some role-players volunteer worry, some simply state the problem. DO NOT SAY 'I UNDERSTAND YOUR CONCERN' TO A PATIENT WHO HAS NOT EXPRESSED ONE — THE EXAMINERS HAVE SPECIFICALLY PENALISED THAT. Respond to what she said
GLOBUS IS NOT DYSPHAGIA
A SENSATION OF A LUMP IN THE THROAT BETWEEN MEALS, WITH ENTIRELY NORMAL SWALLOWING, is GLOBUS PHARYNGEUS — a different case, and a diagnosis of exclusion after a normal scope

dx: **VERSIONS A AND B — OESOPHAGEAL CARCINOMA: progressive solids-only dysphagia, weight loss, long reflux history with antacid failure, ex-smoker, alcohol. VERSION C — OESOPHAGEAL STRICTURE SECONDARY TO CHRONIC GASTRO-OESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE — note the wording carefully: NOT 'GORD'.**

**DEFINITIONS AND TWO AXES, NAMED ALOUD BEFORE LISTING ANYTHING: DYSPHAGIA = DIFFICULTY SWALLOWING; ODYNOPHAGIA = PAIN ON SWALLOWING. AXIS 1: OROPHARYNGEAL VS OESOPHAGEAL. AXIS 2: OBSTRUCTIVE VS MOTILITY.** **If you can say 'THIS IS A LOW, OBSTRUCTIVE DYSPHAGIA' before you name a disease, THE LIST WRITES ITSELF.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: LETTING A NORMAL EXAMINATION, OR A PLAUSIBLE BENIGN STORY, DISPLACE CANCER FROM THE TOP OF THE LIST WHILE RED FLAGS ARE STILL ON THE TABLE. VERSION B EXISTS PRECISELY TO TEST THIS. THE MIRROR ERROR IS VERSION C, where red flags are GENUINELY ABSENT and the answer is stricture.**

**VERSIONS A AND B, SCRIPTED: 'Susan, in your case I AM CONCERNED ABOUT THE POSSIBILITY OF A CANCER IN THE FOOD PIPE. I want to be clear IT IS NOT CONFIRMED — that is why I want to arrange a test. My reasons: YOU'VE HAD REFLUX FOR A LONG TIME AND THE MYLANTA HAS STOPPED WORKING, and it is getting worse. YOU HAVE LOST WEIGHT WITHOUT MEANING TO. And your swallowing problem happens ONLY WITH SOLID FOOD — that pattern suggests SOMETHING IS PHYSICALLY BLOCKING THE WAY.'**

**VERSION B, AFTER THE NORMAL CARD: 'I've examined you and I could not find anything abnormal today. I WANT TO BE HONEST WITH YOU: A NORMAL EXAMINATION DOES NOT RULE OUT A CANCER. EARLY TUMOURS VERY OFTEN CAUSE NO SIGNS AT ALL. My concern is based on your symptoms, AND IT HAS NOT CHANGED.'**

**VERSION C, SCRIPTED — AND DO NOT OMIT DIFFERENTIAL TWO: 'the most likely cause is NARROWING OF THE FOOD PIPE — A STRICTURE. These are SCARS, caused by LONG-TERM INFLAMMATION FROM ACID. The scarring narrows the pipe, and that is why solid food catches. I DO WANT TO SAY THAT A CANCER OF THE FOOD PIPE IS STILL ON MY LIST AND I HAVE NOT RULED IT OUT — you don't have the warning signs, which is reassuring, BUT THE CAMERA TEST IS WHAT TELLS US FOR CERTAIN.'**

**WHY 'GORD' IS THE WRONG ANSWER IN C: GORD DOES NOT ITSELF CAUSE DYSPHAGIA. IT CAUSES HEARTBURN, REGURGITATION AND OESOPHAGITIS. WHAT CAUSES THE SWALLOWING DIFFICULTY IS THE STRICTURE — FIBROUS NARROWING AFTER YEARS OF INFLAMMATION. SAY THE MECHANISM, NOT JUST THE PARENT CONDITION. And STILL BIOPSY IT — A MALIGNANT STRICTURE CAN LOOK BENIGN.**

**SIX NAMED GROUPS, NINE SECONDS EACH: CANCERS — oropharyngeal, oesophageal, thyroid, lung · STRICTURES AND REFLUX · INFECTIONS — pharyngitis, quinsy, candida · MOTILITY — NEUROLOGICAL (stroke, MS, myasthenia, diabetes), AUTOIMMUNE (scleroderma), ACHALASIA · MEDICATIONS · FUNCTIONAL, LAST.** **STROKE IS THE COMMONEST CAUSE OF OROPHARYNGEAL DYSPHAGIA — the neurological group is never 'not relevant'.**

**MEDICATIONS GET THEIR OWN GROUP: ACE INHIBITORS · SEDATIVES AND ANTIPSYCHOTICS · ANTICHOLINERGICS, SSRIs AND DECONGESTANTS — dry mouth · BISPHOSPHONATES AND DOXYCYCLINE — PILL-INDUCED OESOPHAGITIS, usually with odynophagia. ASK WHETHER THE SWALLOWING TROUBLE STARTED WHEN THE DRUG DID.**

**FIRST TEST: URGENT GASTROSCOPY WITH BIOPSY. 'BARIUM OBTAINS NO TISSUE. I would use barium first ONLY IF I SUSPECTED A PHARYNGEAL POUCH, where BLIND INTUBATION RISKS PERFORATION.'** **SA: Category 1 referral to an Adelaide upper GI unit — RAH, Flinders or TQEH — with PATS started at this visit; DIETITIAN AND SPEECH PATHOLOGY in the meantime; MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 if she obstructs completely or aspirates.**

findings: CONFIRM STABILITY BEFORE YOU SIT — THIS IS THE STATION WHERE IT IS COMPULSORY

'BEFORE I BEGIN, COULD I HAVE HER BLOOD PRESSURE, PULSE, RESPIRATORY RATE AND OXYGEN SATURATION — AND IS SHE ALERT AND ORIENTED?' → BP 118/72 · P 92 REG · RR 16 · SpO2 97% RA · ALERT. 'I VOMITED BLOOD' IS TWO SYMPTOMS FROM AN UNVERIFIED SOURCE

SPLIT THE BLOOD FROM THE VOMITING. COUNT THE VOMITS. CLARIFY NOSE, LUNG OR STOMACH BEFORE YOU BUILD A DIFFERENTIAL LIST. Candidates who take the label at face value spend six minutes on a differential for THE WRONG SYMPTOM
CLARIFY THE SOURCE — two questions, ten seconds

'HAVE YOU HAD ANY NOSEBLEEDS RECENTLY, OR THIS MORNING?' — A POSTERIOR NOSEBLEED DRAINS DOWN THE THROAT, IS SWALLOWED, AND COMES BACK UP AS 'VOMITED BLOOD'. 'DID YOU COUGH UP ANY BLOOD, AS OPPOSED TO VOMITING IT?' — haemoptysis is coughed, frothy, mixed with sputum
THE VOMIT COUNT RULES MALLORY-WEISS IN OR OUT

'HOW MANY TIMES DID YOU VOMIT? DID YOU FEEL SICK OR RETCH FIRST, AND THEN SEE BLOOD — OR WAS IT BLOOD FROM THE VERY FIRST VOMIT?' → 'JUST THE ONCE.' A SINGLE VOMIT ESSENTIALLY EXCLUDES IT. SAY SO WHEN YOU LIST DIFFERENTIALS — THAT IS A REASONING MARK
CHARACTER AND VOLUME — give her the scale

'WAS IT FRESH, BRIGHT RED, OR DARK? ANY CLOTS? AND ROUGHLY HOW MUCH — JUST STREAKS, A FEW DROPS, OR A LARGE AMOUNT?' Patients cannot estimate a volume; the scale gets a usable answer. → FRESH RED, NO CLOTS, MODERATE

FIRST EPISODE EVER · WEIGHT LOSS · APPETITE LOSS · TIRED · DARK STOOLS in most recalls · CHRONIC IBUPROFEN FOR ARTHRITIS · CURRENT SMOKER · DAILY ALCOHOL · NO DYSPHAGIA. THE 'NO' TO DYSPHAGIA IS WHAT LETS YOU ARGUE OESOPHAGEAL CANCER DOWN TO THIRD

FIRST — 'ARE YOU TAKING ANY MEDICATIONS AT ALL?' SECOND, SEPARATELY — 'I WANT TO ASK THIS ONE SEPARATELY: ARE YOU ON ANY BLOOD THINNERS — WARFARIN, APIXABAN, RIVAROXABAN, CLOPIDOGREL, OR ASPIRIN?' PATIENTS ROUTINELY DO NOT THINK OF THESE AS 'MEDICATIONS'. IN A BLEEDING 72-YEAR-OLD, MISSING ONE IS A SAFETY FAILURE

'HAVE YOU FELT DIZZY OR LIGHT-HEADED? FAINTED OR NEARLY FAINTED? MORE TIRED OR BREATHLESS THAN USUAL? HEART RACING?' If she says yes to fainting or looks unwell, STOP THE HISTORY, TELL THE EXAMINER, AND ESCALATE

ABDOMINAL PAIN → PEPTIC ULCER · INDIGESTION → GASTRIC CANCER ON AN ULCER · DYSPHAGIA → OESOPHAGEAL CANCER · HAEMATEMESIS → GASTRIC CANCER ON AN ULCER · IRON-DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA → GASTRIC CANCER ON AN ULCER. THE RECURRING CONCEPT IS AN ULCER THAT HAS BECOME MALIGNANT, UNMASKED BY RED FLAGS

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: TREATING 'I VOMITED BLOOD' AS A SINGLE SYMPTOM. IT IS TWO — THE BLOOD AND THE VOMITING — FROM A SOURCE YOU HAVE NOT YET ESTABLISHED. The candidates who pass ask: HOW MANY TIMES DID YOU VOMIT, DID YOU HAVE A NOSEBLEED, DID YOU COUGH IT UP.** **THE SECOND HALF IS THE SEPARATE ANTICOAGULANT QUESTION.**

**THE REASONS IN TWO HALVES: 'FIRST, you have RISK FACTORS FOR AN ULCER — the anti-inflammatory painkiller for a long time, smoking and daily alcohol. SECOND, you have RED FLAGS — you are losing weight, your appetite is not what it was, and you are tired. Together those make me concerned THERE MAY BE A CANCER ON THE BASE OF THAT ULCER.'**

Explain the investigations you would arrange, to Jimmy
findings: DO NOT OPEN WITH HAEMODYNAMIC STABILITY HERE

A CHRONIC SIX-MONTH COMPLAINT IN A GP ROOM, WITH A PATIENT SITTING COMFORTABLY. ASKING FOR VITAL SIGNS BEFORE YOU HAVE SAID HELLO BURNS TIME AND SIGNALS YOU HAVE NOT READ THE STEM. Take vitals within the examination request. CONTRAST HAEMATEMESIS, WHERE IT IS COMPULSORY
THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THE STATION
'MYLANTA USED TO HELP. NOT ANY MORE.' STOP. ACKNOWLEDGE IT: 'THAT CHANGE IS IMPORTANT — CAN I ASK A FEW QUESTIONS ABOUT THAT?' IT IS A RED FLAG IN ITS OWN RIGHT
CONVERT THE VAGUE WORD IN THE FIRST THIRTY SECONDS

'CAN YOU DESCRIBE WHAT YOU MEAN BY INDIGESTION — IS IT A HEARTBURN, A DISCOMFORT, OR FEELING BLOATED?' → 'A BURNING DISCOMFORT, UP HERE.' IT IS NOW A PAIN — site, severity, quality, radiation, timing, BUT FAST
THE CLOCK REALITY FROM THE RECALLS

CANDIDATES REACH THE END OF GENERAL GI QUESTIONS AT ABOUT 2:30. THAT LEAVES ROUGHLY 90 SECONDS FOR EVERY DIFFERENTIAL GROUP. RED FLAGS MUST START BY 2:30 — cancer first, then ulcer and reflux, then everything else, WITH CVS LAST
THE RED FLAGS — THE GENERIC FOUR WILL NOT PASS
WEIGHT LOSS (amount, period, intentional?) · APPETITE · LUMPS · TIREDNESS — PLUS THE SPECIFIC ONES CANDIDATES OMIT: DARK STOOLS · VOMITING BLOOD · DIFFICULTY SWALLOWING · PERSISTENT VOMITING

PALLOR · MELAENA ON PER RECTAL EXAMINATION · A PALPABLE LEFT SUPRACLAVICULAR (VIRCHOW'S) NODE. Vitals unremarkable — A NORMAL BLOOD PRESSURE DOES NOT EXCLUDE CHRONIC BLOOD LOSS. Abdomen otherwise soft and non-tender
NAME PER RECTUM AND THE NODES AS EXPLICIT STEPS

'AND I WOULD LIKE TO PERFORM A PER RECTAL EXAMINATION' and 'EXAMINE THE LYMPH NODES, INCLUDING THE LEFT SUPRACLAVICULAR FOSSA.' Omitting PR is a starred fail. DO NOT CLAIM FINDINGS THE CARD DID NOT GIVE — 'I TAKE IT THE REST IS UNREMARKABLE'
DO NOT SPEND FORTY SECONDS ON LIVER STIGMATA
THIS IS NOT A VARICES STATION. PALLOR, CACHEXIA AND NODES are the three general-appearance items that matter — 'THE TRIPLE LOSS: LOSS OF WEIGHT, LOSS OF APPETITE, LOSS OF COLOUR — THINK CANCER'
CVS GOES LAST — BUT IT GOES IN

'LAST ONE — DO YOU EVER GET ANY CHEST PAIN OR SHORTNESS OF BREATH WITH THIS, OR WHEN YOU EXERT YOURSELF?' ISCHAEMIC HEART DISEASE AS EPIGASTRIC DISCOMFORT IS THE MUST-NOT-MISS NON-GI DIAGNOSIS. PUT IT IN THE SAME BREATH AS SADMA SO IT CANNOT BE DROPPED

dx: **GASTRIC ADENOCARCINOMA ARISING ON THE BASE OF A PEPTIC ULCER — not simply 'gastric cancer'.** **The story is a LONG-STANDING ULCER — burning epigastric discomfort after food, initially Mylanta-responsive, classic risk factors — that has now developed MALIGNANT CHANGE: MYLANTA STOPPED WORKING, WEIGHT LOSS, MELAENA, PALLOR, VIRCHOW'S NODE.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: ENDOSCOPY MUST BE THE FIRST INVESTIGATION OUT OF YOUR MOUTH, AND CANCER MUST BE NAMED CLEARLY AT THE TOP WITHOUT ALARMING HIM.** **Candidates fail in TWO MIRROR-IMAGE WAYS: some SOFTEN THE DIAGNOSIS UNTIL HE NEVER HEARS THE WORD CANCER; others OPEN WITH 'YOU PROBABLY HAVE STOMACH CANCER' and destroy the consultation. THE PASS IS IN THE MIDDLE: NAME IT FIRST, SAY IT IS NOT CONFIRMED, THEN GIVE REASONS.**

**THE DELIVERY: 'Jimmy, I've been thinking about a number of different causes for your indigestion. In your case I AM CONCERNED ABOUT THE POSSIBILITY OF A GASTRIC CANCER — a cancer in the stomach. I want to be clear that THIS IS NOT CONFIRMED; that is exactly why I want to do a test.'**

**THE REASONS — DO NOT SKIP THESE: 'this has been going on FOR SIX MONTHS AND IT IS GETTING WORSE; THE MYLANTA THAT USED TO HELP HAS STOPPED WORKING; you have LOST WEIGHT WITHOUT MEANING TO; and your STOOLS HAVE TURNED DARK, which tells me THERE IS BLEEDING SOMEWHERE IN THE STOMACH.'** **On examination: PALLOR, MELAENA, AND A GLAND ABOVE THE LEFT COLLARBONE.**

**DIFFERENTIAL TWO, SAID OUT LOUD AND WHY IT IS SECOND: 'the second thing this could be is AN ULCER IN THE STOMACH THAT IS NOT CANCEROUS. An ulcer on its own can bleed and cause all of this. I think it's most likely you've had an ulcer for a while, and MY CONCERN IS THAT A CANCER MAY HAVE DEVELOPED ON TOP OF IT.'** **What pushes cancer above it: THE CONSTELLATION OF RED FLAGS PLUS THE SUPRACLAVICULAR NODE.**

**THEN LIST DIFFERENTIALS 3 TO 9 AS NAMED GROUPS WITHOUT REASONING THEM — REASON ONLY THE TOP TWO: GORD · PANCREATIC DISEASE · BILIARY · LACTOSE OR FOOD INTOLERANCE · DRUG-INDUCED GASTRITIS · ISCHAEMIC HEART DISEASE · IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME LAST — NEVER THE ANSWER WHEN RED FLAGS ARE PRESENT.**

**THE ENDOSCOPY EXPLAINED — THE FIRST SIX WORDS ARE 'THE MOST IMPORTANT TEST IS AN ENDOSCOPY': 'we pass a THIN, FLEXIBLE TUBE WITH A CAMERA down your food pipe into your stomach, so we can LOOK DIRECTLY AT THE LINING. If we see an ulcer or any abnormal area, we TAKE SMALL SAMPLES — BIOPSIES — and look at them under the microscope. That is what tells us exactly what we are dealing with. We'll also take blood to check whether the bleeding has made you ANAEMIC and whether YOUR IRON IS LOW.'**

**THE ORDER IS THE MARK: ENDOSCOPY WITH BIOPSY → FBE AND IRON STUDIES → STOP. H. pylori is biopsied at the scope; a urea breath test only if the scope is delayed — ONE LINE. NO FOBT — HE HAS VISIBLE MELAENA; THERE IS NOTHING OCCULT. BARIUM MEAL IS OBSOLETE. EMPIRICAL HIGH-DOSE PPI AS THE ANSWER MAY MASK AND DELAY THE DIAGNOSIS — TREATING IS NOT INVESTIGATING.**

**THE VARIANTS: 'JUST TELL ME STRAIGHT, DO I HAVE CANCER?' — 'I'll be straight with you. I DON'T KNOW YET, AND I WON'T PRETEND TO. The pattern is concerning enough that cancer is at the TOP OF THE LIST OF THINGS I NEED TO RULE OUT, and that's why I'm arranging an urgent camera test rather than waiting.'** **HE REFUSES THE SCOPE: 'that's your decision and I respect it. Can I ask what worries you about it? … What I'd ask is that YOU DON'T CLOSE THE DOOR ON IT.'**

**CORRECTION — 'PEPTIC ULCERS TURN MALIGNANT, DUODENAL ONES DON'T' IS IMPRECISE. GASTRIC ULCERS CARRY MALIGNANT POTENTIAL AND MUST BE BIOPSIED AND FOLLOWED TO HEALING; DUODENAL ULCERS ARE ESSENTIALLY NEVER MALIGNANT.** **SA: CATEGORY 1 URGENT GASTROSCOPY — RAH, Flinders or TQEH; the PRACTICE NURSE COMPLETES THE PATS FORM TODAY; Country Health Connect; a cancer care coordinator once diagnosed. SAY 'URGENT, CATEGORY 1' RATHER THAN INVENTING A NUMBER OF WEEKS.**

FOUR TASKS IN EIGHT MINUTES, with a MINI-BELL AT ABOUT FIVE. Candidates spend four or five minutes explaining what an endoscope is, get the prompt, then deliver a rushed management plan — OR NONE. RUNNING OUT OF TIME ON MANAGEMENT IS A FAIL. NINETY SECONDS ON THE REPORT, THREE MINUTES MAXIMUM OF HISTORY
THE REPORT — what it says and does not say

YES: OESOPHAGITIS · A SMALL SLIDING HIATUS HERNIA. NO: NO ULCER · NO BARRETT'S · NO DYSPLASIA · H. PYLORI NEGATIVE. TELLING HIM WHAT HE DOES NOT HAVE IS HALF THE COUNSELLING — he has waited weeks assuming the worst
SIGNPOST ALL FOUR TASKS UP FRONT

'FIRST I'LL GO THROUGH THE RESULTS. THEN A FEW QUESTIONS ABOUT THINGS THAT MAKE REFLUX WORSE, BECAUSE THEY CHANGE THE PLAN. THEN WHAT THE DIAGNOSIS MEANS AND WHAT WE'RE TRYING TO PREVENT, AND FINALLY A TREATMENT PLAN.' It buys permission to move briskly AND tells the examiner you budgeted for all four
THE ENDOSCOPE GETS ONE SENTENCE
'WE PASSED A THIN TUBE WITH A CAMERA DOWN YOUR FOOD PIPE INTO YOUR STOMACH, SO WE COULD LOOK DIRECTLY AT THE LINING.' HE HAS ALREADY HAD ONE — HE KNOWS WHAT IT FELT LIKE
DRAW THE HIATUS HERNIA — fifteen seconds
A TUBE, A HORIZONTAL LINE, A BAG AND A DOT. THE ONLY DIAGRAM IN THE AMC THAT RELIABLY EARNS ITS TIME, BECAUSE THE CONCEPT IS SPATIAL. Practise it — A DIAGRAM YOU FUMBLE COSTS MORE THAN IT EARNS
'RELEVANT HISTORY' MEANS RISK FACTORS, NOT A FRESH COMPLAINT

THERE IS NO COMPLAINT TO EXPLORE — THE DIAGNOSIS IS ON PAPER. A CANDIDATE WHO RUNS SOCRATES ON THE HEARTBURN HAS MISREAD THE TASK AND WILL NOT FINISH. Everything you ask must CHANGE THE MANAGEMENT PLAN
TREATMENT AND COMPLIANCE FIRST

'WHAT HAVE YOU TAKEN, WHAT DOSE, HOW OFTEN, EVERY DAY OR ON AND OFF, AND WHEN IN THE DAY — BEFORE FOOD OR AFTER?' Most 'failures' are TIMING OR ADHERENCE, NOT RESISTANCE. A PROPER PPI TRIAL IS 4–8 WEEKS, 30–60 MINUTES BEFORE A MEAL
'WOULD YOU SAY YOU'RE OVERWEIGHT?' — ASK IT PLAINLY

DO NOT ASK FOR A BMI — no patient knows it and no role-player is briefed with one. HE IS BRIEFED TO SAY HE IS OVERWEIGHT — BUT ONLY IF YOU ASK. WEIGHT LOSS IS THE LIFESTYLE MEASURE CANDIDATES FORGET, AND THE ONE WITH THE BEST EVIDENCE
SAY OUT LOUD WHY YOU ARE SKIPPING THE FULL RED-FLAG SCREEN

'BECAUSE THE ENDOSCOPY HAS ALREADY EXCLUDED ULCERATION, BARRETT'S AND MALIGNANCY, I'M NOT GOING TO REPEAT A FULL RED-FLAG SCREEN. I'LL ASK TWO — WEIGHT LOSS AND DARK STOOLS — AND SAFETY-NET THE REST AT THE END.' A DECISION, NOT AN OMISSION
'IS IT CANCER?'
'NO. WE SPECIFICALLY LOOKED FOR CANCEROUS AND PRE-CANCEROUS CHANGES AND TOOK SAMPLES, AND THERE WERE NONE. THAT IS GENUINELY GOOD NEWS'

dx: **GASTRO-OESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE CAUSING EROSIVE OESOPHAGITIS, with an INCIDENTAL SMALL SLIDING HIATUS HERNIA.** **SAY 'DISEASE' DELIBERATELY: REFLUX BECOMES REFLUX DISEASE ONCE IT CAUSES DEMONSTRABLE MUCOSAL INJURY — AND THE ENDOSCOPY HAS DEMONSTRATED EXACTLY THAT.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: FINISHING. The marks are weighted towards the last task, and almost every candidate knows reflux management — IT IS TIME DISCIPLINE. THE SECOND DISCRIMINATOR IS THE HIATUS HERNIA SENTENCE, WHERE CANDIDATES MAKE A LAST-SECOND UNFORCED ERROR UNDER TIME PRESSURE.**

**THE DIAGNOSIS IN ONE SENTENCE, THEN THE MECHANISM ON THE SAME DRAWING: 'you have a condition called GASTRO-OESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE, and it has caused the inflammation we saw. There's A GATEWAY between your food pipe and your stomach. In your case it's A BIT LOOSE, so some ACID MOVES UP INTO YOUR FOOD PIPE AND IRRITATES THE LINING.'** **Do not say 'you have GORD' — SAY THE WORDS.**

**THE HIATUS HERNIA, SAFELY: 'a small part of the top of your stomach has SLID UP THROUGH THAT MUSCLE INTO YOUR CHEST. It is NOT THE CAUSE OF THE INFLAMMATION, and we are not going to treat it as such. MOST SMALL HIATUS HERNIAS CAUSE NO SYMPTOMS AT ALL.'**

**CORRECTION — AS A PHYSIOLOGICAL CLAIM, 'THE HERNIA IS NOT CAUSATIVE' IS WRONG. A SLIDING HIATUS HERNIA DISPLACES THE GASTRO-OESOPHAGEAL JUNCTION FROM THE CRURAL DIAPHRAGM AND REMOVES PART OF THE ANTIREFLUX BARRIER — AN AGGRAVATING FACTOR, NOT THE CAUSE.** If pressed: **'I framed it that way because the hernia is not the explanation for his oesophagitis and I didn't want him to fixate on it. Physiologically it can make reflux worse, and a small sliding hernia is not itself an indication for treatment.'**

**COMPLICATIONS — FIVE, FAST, WITH THE FRAMING LINE: ULCERS · BLEEDING AND ANAEMIA · NARROWING FROM SCARRING · BARRETT'S — 'YOU DO NOT HAVE THIS' · CANCER OF THE FOOD PIPE. 'I'm telling you these NOT TO ALARM YOU — you have none of them today — but so you understand WHY WE TREAT THIS PROPERLY. The good news is that OESOPHAGITIS IS REVERSIBLE.'**

**MANAGEMENT ORDER: A PROTON PUMP INHIBITOR — NOT AN ANTACID — because EROSIVE DISEASE IS CONFIRMED · LIFESTYLE AND DIET WITH WEIGHT LOSS NAMED OUT LOUD · STOP THE OFFENDING DRUG — NSAID, aspirin, alendronate, doxycycline · GENERAL ADVICE — smaller meals, nothing 2–3 hours before bed, HEAD OF THE BED RAISED, stop smoking · REVIEW AT 4–8 WEEKS AND STEP DOWN · SAFETY-NET · SURGERY IN ONE LINE.**

**CORRECTION — 'HIGH-DOSE PPI IS 20 mg TWICE DAILY' should be confirmed. For erosive oesophagitis the more usual Australian regimen is ESOMEPRAZOLE 40 mg DAILY or equivalent FOR 4–8 WEEKS, with twice-daily dosing reserved for refractory or severe disease.** Safe answer: **'a high-dose PPI for erosive disease, for four to eight weeks, 30 to 60 minutes before a meal, and I would CHECK THE EXACT DOSE AGAINST THERAPEUTIC GUIDELINES.'** VERIFY.

**CORRECTION — ROUTINE TWO-YEARLY ENDOSCOPY FOR OESOPHAGITIS IS NOT STANDARD. SURVEILLANCE BELONGS TO BARRETT'S. Repeat endoscopy is indicated TO CONFIRM HEALING AND EXCLUDE UNDERLYING BARRETT'S AFTER SEVERE, LA GRADE C OR D, OESOPHAGITIS — because severe inflammation can conceal Barrett's — or if symptoms fail to settle.**

**SURGERY, ONE LINE: 'there is an operation — A FUNDOPLICATION, which wraps the top of the stomach around the food pipe to tighten that gateway. It ISN'T AN OPTION AT THIS STAGE and most people never need it.'** **SAFETY-NET, ALL SIX: DIFFICULTY SWALLOWING, PAIN ON SWALLOWING, VOMITING BLOOD, BLACK TARRY STOOLS, WEIGHT LOSS, PERSISTENT VOMITING.**

dx: **Biliary colic — transient obstruction of the cystic duct by a stone, causing pain without infection or inflammation. The stone falls back and the pain settles.**

**Explain the three as a PROGRESSION, not a list: a stone in the neck of the gallbladder that FALLS BACK gives biliary colic · a stone that STAYS gives cholecystitis · a stone that MOVES ON into the common bile duct and obstructs it gives cholangitis.** Said in that order the differences look inevitable rather than memorised.
**Biliary colic: episodes UNDER 6 HOURS · after fatty food · radiating to the RIGHT SHOULDER BLADE · no fever, no jaundice · normal bloods · normal examination between attacks.**

**The diagnosis is made on the history of the episodes, and a normal examination does not rule it out** — say that to the patient explicitly, because she will otherwise hear 'normal' as 'nothing wrong'.

**Ask the jaundice block in EVERY right upper quadrant station, whatever the vital signs say**: yellowing, dark urine, pale stools, itching. **Scleral icterus appears before skin jaundice, and in an examination-report format you never see the patient at all.**

**The layman explanation, one picture for three diseases**: **'your gallbladder is a small bag under the liver that stores bile, the fluid that helps digest fat. When you eat something fatty the bag squeezes. If there are stones in it, one can block the outlet — that gives pain for an hour or two until it falls back. If the stone stays stuck the bag becomes inflamed and infected. And if a stone escapes into the main drainage tube and blocks it, bile backs up into the blood, which turns you yellow, and the tube gets infected — that is the most dangerous of the three.'**

**Management: analgesia · reassurance · low-fat diet advice to reduce the frequency · ULTRASOUND to confirm the stones and LFTs to check the liver · then ELECTIVE LAPAROSCOPIC CHOLECYSTECTOMY, which is the only definitive treatment.**

**Her three questions, answered: dissolving tablets exist but work poorly, take a long time and the stones usually come back · she does not have to have surgery, it is her decision · but if she does nothing the attacks tend to continue and a stone may get properly stuck, which causes the more serious problems.** **You can live perfectly well without a gallbladder.**

**Courvoisier's law: in a jaundiced patient, a palpable but NON-TENDER gallbladder is unlikely to be gallstones** — chronic stone disease scars and shrinks the gallbladder. **Suspect malignant obstruction, typically carcinoma of the head of the pancreas or a periampullary tumour.** Say the law by name.

**A previous cholecystectomy does not close the biliary tree** — stones can remain in or form in the common bile duct, so **choledocholithiasis and cholangitis stay on the list.** **SA: elective cholecystectomy is a PATS-supported metropolitan referral; TIS National 131 450.**
plan: **'Examiner, may I confirm the patient is haemodynamically stable — blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature and saturations?'** Then introduce, **offer analgesia if she is in pain**, and open.

**The pain, full SICORA with the biliary specifics: show me where · out of ten · DOES IT COME ON AFTER FATTY OR RICH FOOD, AND HOW LONG AFTER · HOW LONG DOES AN EPISODE LAST · DOES IT TRAVEL TO YOUR RIGHT SHOULDER BLADE or the tip of the shoulder · have you had EXACTLY this before · is it constant now, or does it come and go?**

**The jaundice block — four questions, never skipped:** **have you or anyone else noticed any YELLOWING OF YOUR EYES OR SKIN · has your URINE GONE DARK · have your STOOLS GONE PALE or clay-coloured · ANY ITCHING?**

**The infection block: any fevers · ANY SHAKING CHILLS OR RIGORS, the sort where your teeth chatter and you cannot stop shivering · any confusion or drowsiness · any dizziness on standing?** The last two take you from Charcot's triad to Reynolds' pentad.

**The liver risk block: how much alcohol in a usual week, in standard drinks · any blood transfusions, tattoos, piercings, injecting drug use or travel overseas · how much paracetamol, and any herbal or over-the-counter medicines · any liver disease in the family?**

T 39.1 · HR 112 · BP 108/64 · RR 22 · SpO2 96%. IF YOU TAKE THESE AND DO NOT CHANGE GEAR — fluids, cultures, antibiotics — THE EXAMINER RECORDS THAT YOU DID NOT RECOGNISE SEPSIS

UNWELL AND JAUNDICED, with SCLERAL ICTERUS. Ask for scleral icterus by name in your general-appearance step — it is the single finding that converts cholecystitis into cholangitis

TENDER RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT WITH GUARDING. NO mass. LIVER NOT ENLARGED
MURPHY'S SIGN
POSITIVE — and this is the TRAP. It tells you the gallbladder is inflamed; it tells you NOTHING about whether the duct is blocked. MURPHY IS POSITIVE IN BOTH CHOLECYSTITIS AND CHOLANGITIS
The follow-up question that decides the station
'You have told me Murphy's sign is positive, which tells me the gallbladder is inflamed. BEFORE I COMMIT, IS THERE ANY SCLERAL ICTERUS, AND WHAT IS THE BILIRUBIN?'
Chest and dipstick
CHEST CLEAR. Urine dipstick shows BILIRUBIN
Bloods
WCC 18 · CRP 210 · BILIRUBIN 74 · ALP AND GGT CLEARLY RAISED · ALT mildly raised · LIPASE NORMAL. An OBSTRUCTIVE picture

dx: **Ascending cholangitis — infection of an obstructed biliary tree, usually by a stone in the common bile duct. A life-threatening emergency.**

**The discriminating behaviour: ask about jaundice, dark urine and pale stools in EVERY right upper quadrant station, and do not let a positive Murphy's sign stop you asking.** **Murphy is positive in cholecystitis AND in cholangitis. Jaundice is what separates them — and jaundice is what changes the treatment from an operating list to an emergency ERCP.**

**The sentence that rescues the station: 'Examiner, you have told me Murphy's sign is positive, which tells me the gallbladder is inflamed. Before I commit to cholecystitis, may I ask — is there any scleral icterus or jaundice, and what is the bilirubin?'** Then: **'that changes my diagnosis. With right upper quadrant pain, fever with rigors and jaundice, this is Charcot's triad and I am treating this as ascending cholangitis.'**
**CHARCOT'S TRIAD = pain + fever with rigors + jaundice. REYNOLDS' PENTAD adds hypotension and altered mental state** — suppurative cholangitis with septic shock.
**Treat it as sepsis: resuscitate · BLOOD CULTURES · IV ANTIBIOTICS WITHIN ONE HOUR · fluids · analgesia and an antiemetic · correct coagulopathy · VBG with lactate · HDU if unstable.**
**The definitive treatment is BILIARY DECOMPRESSION BY ERCP WITHIN 24 HOURS** — urgently if there is shock or failure to improve. **Cholecystectomy afterwards, on the same admission where possible.**
**The obstructive picture: bilirubin, ALP and GGT up, ALT mildly up.** **Lipase normal excludes pancreatitis.** **Ultrasound first, then MRCP if the duct is dilated but no stone is seen.**

**Say it to the patient straight without frightening him: 'you have an infection in the drainage tubes of your liver, which are blocked — almost certainly by a gallstone. It is serious, and you are already showing signs the infection is affecting your whole body. But it is very treatable and we are going to start straight away.'** To **'serious how?'**: **serious enough to be in hospital now and on antibiotics within the hour** — then name the three things that told you.

**SA: ERCP is not available on Yorke Peninsula. Suspected cholangitis is a TIME-CRITICAL RETRIEVAL — blood cultures and IV antibiotics within the hour at Wallaroo or Kadina, fluids, then MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 and the receiving unit at TQEH or the Royal Adelaide. DO NOT WAIT FOR LOCAL IMAGING BEFORE YOU MAKE THE CALL.** RFDS for fixed-wing transfer.

**Courvoisier's law: jaundice with a palpable NON-TENDER gallbladder is malignant obstruction until proven otherwise** — typically carcinoma of the head of the pancreas. **And a previous cholecystectomy does not close the biliary tree: stones remain in or form in the common bile duct.**
plan: **'Examiner, may I confirm he is haemodynamically stable — all four observations and saturations?'** → T 39.1, HR 112, BP 108/64. **Say it out loud: 'those observations concern me and I'll be moving quickly.'** Then **offer analgesia before you start.**

**The pain: show me where · out of ten · did it come on after a meal · DOES IT TRAVEL TO YOUR RIGHT SHOULDER BLADE or round to the back · is it constant now · HAVE YOU HAD EXACTLY THIS BEFORE?** → a couple of shorter episodes over the past year that settled — the colic that preceded it.

**The jaundice block, four questions, and he volunteers none of it:** **have you or anyone else noticed any YELLOWING OF YOUR EYES OR SKIN · has your URINE GONE DARK · have your STOOLS GONE PALE or clay-coloured · ANY ITCHING?**

**The infection block: any fevers · WAS THAT A PROPER RIGOR — teeth chattering, shaking the bed, couldn't stop · any confusion or drowsiness · any dizziness on standing?** The last two are what take you to Reynolds' pentad.

**The liver risk block: alcohol in standard drinks per week · blood transfusions, tattoos, piercings, injecting drug use, travel · paracetamol and any herbal or over-the-counter medicines · family history of liver disease.**

**GI red flags and the chest: nausea and vomiting, bowels, appetite · any weight loss, intentional or not · difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black motions, lumps · ANY COUGH, PHLEGM, BREATHLESSNESS OR PAIN ON DEEP BREATHING?** Then **SADMA**.

**Summarise back, then request the examination, naming every step:** **general appearance — alert, distressed, dehydrated, AND IS THERE SCLERAL ICTERUS OR JAUNDICE OF THE SKIN · all four vital signs including temperature · inspection for scars, distension, movement with respiration, scratch marks · palpation for tenderness, guarding, rigidity, rebound, a palpable gallbladder or LIVER EDGE, AND IF ENLARGED IS IT SMOOTH OR NODULAR, TENDER OR NON-TENDER · MURPHY'S SIGN, named · percussion for tenderness, liver span and shifting dullness · auscultation, bowel sounds AND THE CHEST BASES · groin and rectal examination with STOOL COLOUR ON THE GLOVE · office tests — urine dipstick, blood sugar, and a PREGNANCY TEST in a woman of reproductive age**

**Murphy's sign, named and described in full:** **'I would perform Murphy's sign.' With the patient lying flat and the abdomen exposed, place your hand at the RIGHT COSTAL MARGIN in the MID-CLAVICULAR LINE. Ask her to BREATHE ALL THE WAY OUT, press your fingers DEEPLY IN UNDER THE COSTAL MARGIN, then ask her to TAKE A DEEP BREATH IN. As the diaphragm descends it pushes the inflamed gallbladder onto your fingers. POSITIVE if she CATCHES HER BREATH AND STOPS INSPIRATION — and to be valid, THE SAME MANOEUVRE ON THE LEFT SHOULD NOT DO THAT.** **Then, on being told it is positive, ASK THE FOLLOW-UP about scleral icterus and bilirubin rather than committing.**

**Reason out loud: Murphy positive tells me the gallbladder is inflamed — but that is true in cholecystitis and in cholangitis, so it is THE JAUNDICE AND THE OBSTRUCTIVE LIVER TESTS that decide this. This is Charcot's triad: ascending cholangitis.**

**Tell the patient plainly**, answer 'serious how?' with the three findings that told you, then **the differentials: cholecystitis alone, a duct stone without infection, and hepatitis — and why each is less likely.**

**Immediate management, in order: a drip in each arm · BLOOD CULTURES · IV ANTIBIOTICS WITHIN THE HOUR · fluids · analgesia and an antiemetic · correct coagulopathy · ULTRASOUND to confirm · then ERCP WITHIN 24 HOURS for biliary decompression, and cholecystectomy afterwards on the same admission.** **In a rural setting, MedSTAR is being phoned while that is happening.** Offer to call someone for him.

stem: A 37-year-old woman (role-play: David Bennett, 41) presents complaining of diarrhoea. Duration not given.
tasks: Take a focused, relevant history (6 minutes)
Explain your most likely diagnosis and your differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: THE DURATION IS DELIBERATELY NOT ON THE DOOR

You will not know whether this is acute, semi-acute or chronic until you ask. DO NOT BUILD A DIFFERENT HISTORY FOR ACUTE AND CHRONIC. BUILD ONE LIST ORDERED ACUTE AT THE TOP AND CHRONIC AT THE BOTTOM, AND RUN THE WHOLE LIST WHETHER SHE SAYS THREE DAYS OR SIX MONTHS
THE VERSION ON THIS CARD — three findings at once

FIVE DAYS OF WATERY DIARRHOEA, 6–8 A DAY, NO BLOOD · AMOXICILLIN FOR A SORE THROAT, FINISHED 3 DAYS AGO · BALI SIX WEEKS AGO, STREET FOOD · FATHER HAD BOWEL CANCER. Variant C: FIVE TO SIX EPISODES, SLIMY, CRAMPS, ANTIBIOTICS 5 DAYS AGO, AND ON NEXIUM
MULTIPLE FINDINGS ARE THE EXAM DESIGN, NOT YOUR MISTAKE

SINCE 2024 THE AMC DELIBERATELY PLANTS SEVERAL POSITIVES — travel AND an antibiotic AND a family history. A CANDIDATE RUNNING THE FULL STRUCTURE COLLECTS ALL THREE. FINDING THREE THINGS IS EVIDENCE YOUR HISTORY WAS GOOD. CHOOSE ONE, SAY THE OTHERS ARE POSSIBLE, AND DO NOT ARGUE WITH YOURSELF IN FRONT OF THE PATIENT
EVERY POSITIVE GETS THREE FOLLOW-UPS

'I TOOK SOME ANTIBIOTICS' → 'WHICH ANTIBIOTIC? HOW LONG, AND WHAT FOR? AND DID THE DIARRHOEA START WHILE YOU WERE TAKING IT, OR AFTER YOU FINISHED?' Accepting 'antibiotics' and moving on is a listed fail
'I'VE JUST BEEN TO BALI' — ALL SEVEN LETTERS

WHERE, HOW LONG, WHAT ACTIVITIES · BUSHWALKING OR INSECT BITES · CONTACT WITH ANYONE UNWELL OR WITH ANIMALS · DRUGS WHILE AWAY · TATTOOS, PIERCINGS, MEDICAL OR DENTAL TREATMENT · FOOD AND WATER — STREET FOOD, ICE, UNBOTTLED WATER · SAW A GP BEFORE GOING. TWO QUESTIONS WILL NOT PASS
'MY FATHER HAD BOWEL CANCER' → 'HOW OLD WAS HE?'
THE AGE CHANGES THE SCREENING CATEGORY. A FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVE UNDER 60 moves surveillance from faecal occult blood testing to FIVE-YEARLY COLONOSCOPY
KNOW THE AUSTRALIAN BRANDS
NEXIUM, SOMAC, PARIET, LOSEC — PROTON PUMP INHIBITORS, and PPIs RAISE C. DIFFICILE RISK. GASTRO-STOP — LOPERAMIDE, AVOID WITH FEVER OR BLOOD. HYDRALYTE, GASTROLYTE — oral rehydration
C C C V O — THE CHARACTER BOX
COUNT · CONSISTENCY — watery, soft and loose, bulky · CONTENT — blood, mucus · VOLUME · ODOUR. And the NOCTURNAL question has THREE HOMES — timing, character, red flags — SO IT NEVER GETS LOST
THE TWO QUESTIONS EVERYONE SKIPS

'ANY CONSTIPATION BEFORE THIS STARTED?' — catches FAECAL IMPACTION WITH OVERFLOW. 'ANY ABDOMINAL PAIN?' — THE SINGLE MOST COMMONLY MISSED QUESTION, and the entry point to every acute abdomen presenting as diarrhoea
TWO RURAL SA ADDITIONS

'DO YOU DRINK RAINWATER FROM A TANK, OR BORE WATER?' — Giardia, Cryptosporidium, Campylobacter on the Yorke Peninsula. And RECENT HOSPITAL OR AGED-CARE CONTACT — the other major C. difficile risk factor besides antibiotics
findingsLabel: Duration not on the door — one structure, three planted findings, rank them and name one
must: FAIL — No travel history when travel is volunteered. 'Bali? OK — any medications?'
FAIL — No red flags because the patient is young or the history is short.
FAIL — Never asking about abdominal pain.
FAIL — Panicking at multiple findings: five diagnoses, no ranking, none named.
ASK — Which antibiotic, for how long, and did the diarrhoea start during or after?
ASK — How old was your father when he was diagnosed?

dx: **ANTIBIOTIC-ASSOCIATED DIARRHOEA, with PSEUDOMEMBRANOUS COLITIS FROM CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE as the version of it that must not be missed.** **Diarrhoea is an increase in stool FREQUENCY, FLUIDITY OR VOLUME relative to that person's normal. ACUTE UNDER 14 DAYS, PERSISTENT 14–30, CHRONIC BEYOND 4 WEEKS.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: RED FLAGS ARE ASKED UNCONDITIONALLY — AND POSITIVES ARE PROBED. Every recalled failure comes back to one of two behaviours: DECIDING THE CASE WAS 'TOO ACUTE' OR THE PATIENT 'TOO YOUNG' FOR CANCER QUESTIONS, or ACCEPTING A POSITIVE ANSWER WITHOUT PROBING IT.**

**RED FLAGS: WEIGHT LOSS · BLOOD · FEVER · NOCTURNAL DIARRHOEA · ABDOMINAL PAIN · RECENT TRAVEL · FAMILY HISTORY OF BOWEL CANCER, IBD AND COELIAC. ASKED IN A 22-YEAR-OLD WITH THREE DAYS OF SYMPTOMS EXACTLY AS IN A 67-YEAR-OLD WITH SIX MONTHS.**

**TEN DIFFERENTIAL GROUPS, ASKED ONE NAMED GROUP AT A TIME, ACUTE TO CHRONIC: GASTROENTERITIS · HEPATITIS A · IBD · COELIAC · LACTOSE · MEDICATIONS · HYPERTHYROIDISM · BOWEL CANCER RED FLAGS · HIV AND STI SCREEN · IRRITABLE BOWEL, LAST.** **Bowel cancer ranks eighth ONLY because the list runs acute to chronic — BEHAVIOURALLY, THE RED FLAGS COME EARLY AND ALWAYS.**

**RANK THE THREE FINDINGS, DO NOT PANIC: FIRST, ANTIBIOTIC-ASSOCIATED DIARRHOEA — the timing fits the course · SECOND, C. DIFFICILE COLITIS — must be excluded with a stool toxin PCR · THIRD, GASTROENTERITIS AND TRAVELLERS' INFECTIONS — Bali and street food, though six weeks is a long gap · COLORECTAL CANCER — UNLIKELY AT HIS AGE WITH NO RED FLAGS, BUT ON THE LIST BECAUSE OF THE FAMILY HISTORY.**

**C. DIFFICILE WINDOW: ONSET DURING THE COURSE OR UP TO 8 WEEKS AFTER, MOST OFTEN WITHIN 2 WEEKS. PPIs AND RECENT HOSPITAL OR AGED-CARE CONTACT ADD RISK. Pseudomembranous colitis gives PROFUSE WATERY DIARRHOEA, CRAMPS, TENESMUS, FEVER, sometimes blood.**

**SAY 'GASTROENTERITIS — AN INFECTION IN YOUR BOWEL'. 'BALI BELLY' AND 'TRAVELLER'S DIARRHOEA' ARE NOT DIAGNOSES. For travellers' infections, NAME THE GROUP — typhoid, malaria, E. coli, Giardia, amoebiasis, cholera — DO NOT GUESS THE ORGANISM.**

**TO THE PATIENT: 'the most likely cause is THE ANTIBIOTIC YOU FINISHED A FEW DAYS AGO. Antibiotics kill some of the GOOD BACTERIA in the bowel as well as the bad ones, and that upsets the balance. Usually it settles on its own, BUT OCCASIONALLY ONE PARTICULAR BUG CALLED C. DIFFICILE TAKES OVER, and I want to test for that.' Then the others as 'also possible' — travel infection, and the reason the family history matters.**

**IRRITABLE BOWEL, IF THAT IS THE VERSION, EARNED OUT LOUD: 'the reason I feel comfortable calling this IBS is that I've SPECIFICALLY CHECKED FOR THE THINGS THAT WOULD WORRY ME — NO BLOOD, NO WEIGHT LOSS, NO NIGHT-TIME SYMPTOMS, NO FEVER, AND NO FAMILY HISTORY OF BOWEL CANCER OR BOWEL DISEASE.'**

**PLAN: STOOL C. DIFFICILE TOXIN PCR · STOOL MCS AND PCR PANEL · ORAL REHYDRATION · AVOID LOPERAMIDE — IT PROLONGS TOXIN EXPOSURE AND RISKS TOXIC MEGACOLON · stop the PPI if safe · REVIEW IN 2–3 DAYS, sooner for fever, blood, severe pain or dizziness.** **SA: notifiable organisms to SA Health; a FOOD-HANDLER, CHILDCARE OR HEALTHCARE WORKER IS EXCLUDED UNTIL CLEARED; telephone follow-up for results.**
plan: **Hand hygiene, identity check, open question.** Then **RESPOND TO HIS CONCERN BEFORE ASKING ANYTHING: 'that sounds really unpleasant, and I can hear you're worried. Some questions will be QUITE PERSONAL, but they'll help me work out what's going on. Is that all right?'**
**TIMING: WHEN DID IT START · SUDDEN OR GRADUAL · CONSTANT OR COMING AND GOING · GETTING WORSE · DOES IT WAKE YOU AT NIGHT?**
**C C C V O: HOW MANY TIMES A DAY · WATERY, SOFT AND LOOSE, OR BULKY · ANY BLOOD OR MUCUS · HOW MUCH · ANY UNUSUAL SMELL?** Then **anything better or worse.**
**GENERAL GI: nausea or vomiting · bloating and wind · ANY CONSTIPATION BEFORE THIS STARTED · ANY ABDOMINAL PAIN · FEVER OR CHILLS.**
**GROUP 1, GASTROENTERITIS: 'HAVE YOU TRAVELLED ANYWHERE RECENTLY?' — and when Bali comes, ALL SEVEN LETTERS · ANYONE AT HOME OR WORK WITH THE SAME · TANK OR BORE WATER?**
**GROUP 2, HEPATITIS A: yellowing, itch, dark urine, pale stool. GROUP 3, IBD: joint pains, red or painful eyes, rashes, mouth ulcers.**
**GROUP 4, COELIAC: GREASY · FLOATS, STICKS TO THE PAN, HARD TO FLUSH · offensive. GROUP 5, LACTOSE: worse after dairy?**

**GROUP 6, MEDICATIONS — 'anything from the chemist or supermarket?' — and when he says antibiotics: WHICH, HOW LONG, WHAT FOR, AND DID IT START DURING OR AFTER? Recognise NEXIUM AS A PPI. Recent HOSPITAL OR AGED-CARE contact.**

**GROUP 7, THYROID: hot weather, racing heart. GROUP 8, RED FLAGS: WEIGHT LOSS — HOW MUCH, OVER WHAT PERIOD · appetite · lumps · tiredness · BLOOD · FAMILY HISTORY — AND AT WHAT AGE · over 45, the bowel screening kit.**
**GROUP 9, SEXUAL HEALTH SCREEN: sexually active, condoms. GROUP 10, IBS: pain settles on opening bowels, alternating habit, stress at home or work.**
**A one-line summary back.**
**NAME ONE DIAGNOSIS IN PLAIN WORDS — ANTIBIOTIC-ASSOCIATED DIARRHOEA — WITH REASONS DRAWN FROM WHAT HE TOLD YOU, then 'I also want to make sure it isn't C. DIFFICILE'.**

**THE GROUPED DIFFERENTIALS, each with why it is less likely — gastroenteritis and travellers' infections, IBD, coeliac, colorectal cancer because of his father, drugs including the PPI, thyroid — and IBS LAST.**

**Do next: STOOL MCS AND PCR PANEL — viral, bacterial and protozoal · STOOL C. DIFFICILE TOXIN PCR IF ANY ANTIBIOTIC EXPOSURE · COELIAC SEROLOGY ON GLUTEN · FAECAL CALPROTECTIN · FBC, CRP, UEC, IRON STUDIES, TFTs · HIV SEROLOGY where the sexual history warrants, with consent · COLONOSCOPY FOR ANY RED FLAG and anyone over 45 with a persistent change in habit.**

**Screening numbers: iFOBT EVERY 2 YEARS FROM 45 TO 74 AT AVERAGE RISK. Moderate risk — COLONOSCOPY EVERY 5 YEARS FROM 10 YEARS BEFORE THE EARLIEST FAMILY DIAGNOSIS OR AGE 50, WHICHEVER IS EARLIER.** VERIFY.

DIFFICILE in anyone recently given antibiotics · FAECAL IMPACTION WITH OVERFLOW in the older patient · ISCHAEMIC COLITIS — bloody diarrhoea with pain in an older vasculopath · ACUTE ABDOMEN — diverticulitis, appendicitis · HIV SEROCONVERSION where the sexual history is high risk.**

DIFFICILE · EMPIRICAL ANTIBIOTICS FOR UNDIFFERENTIATED TRAVELLERS' DIARRHOEA — current Australian guidance reserves antibiotics for severe or dysenteric illness · DIAGNOSING IBS WITH ANY RED FLAG · REASSURING BEFORE THE RED FLAGS HAVE BEEN ASKED.** VERIFY.

DIFFICILE · D — ALTERNATING HABIT, STRESS, NO RED FLAGS → IBS BY EXCLUSION · E — 3 MONTHS AFTER BALI → gastroenteritis, HEPATITIS A, travellers' infections · F — 6 MONTHS, STEATORRHOEA, WEIGHT LOSS, HOUSEBOUND → COELIAC.**

**SA: stool PCR through SA Pathology, reported within 24–48 hours — ARRANGE TELEPHONE FOLLOW-UP. SALMONELLA, CAMPYLOBACTER, SHIGELLA, CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS, GIARDIASIS, HEPATITIS A AND TYPHOID ARE NOTIFIABLE; exclude food-handlers, childcare and healthcare workers until cleared. PATS for colonoscopy travel; TIS National 131 450; MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 for shock or a surgical abdomen.**

stem: A 37-year-old woman presents with diarrhoea for six months.
tasks: Take a focused, relevant history (6 minutes)
Explain your most likely diagnosis and your differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: SAME STEM, DIFFERENT ANSWERS — THE STRUCTURE DOES NOT CHANGE
'A 37-YEAR-OLD WOMAN WITH DIARRHOEA FOR SIX MONTHS.' Run the SAME ten-group structure as every diarrhoea station. THE VERSION CHANGES WHAT SHE ANSWERS; IT DOES NOT CHANGE WHAT YOU ASK
WHAT SHE GIVES WHEN ASKED
SIX MONTHS OF DIARRHOEA · GREASY STOOLS THAT FLOAT AND STICK TO THE PAN, HARD TO FLUSH · 5 kg UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS · NOT LEAVING HOME FOR FEAR OF LEAKING · AVOIDING WORK AND SHOPPING
THE SCRIPTED LINE — ASK 'HOW IS THIS AFFECTING YOUR LIFE?'

'I DON'T LEAVE THE HOUSE ANY MORE.' THE ROLE-PLAYER WAS TOLD TO SAY IT. ACKNOWLEDGE IT EXPLICITLY: 'THAT SOUNDS REALLY ISOLATING — NOT BEING ABLE TO GO TO WORK OR DO THE SHOPPING. THANK YOU FOR TELLING ME. THAT'S EXACTLY THE KIND OF THING I NEED TO KNOW'
THE COELIAC TRIAD — all three together is close to diagnostic in the exam

'ARE YOUR STOOLS GREASY OR OILY? DO THEY FLOAT, STICK TO THE PAN, OR ARE THEY HARD TO FLUSH? ARE THEY PARTICULARLY OFFENSIVE?' STEATORRHOEA = FAT MALABSORPTION. When she says yes, go straight to FAMILY HISTORY AND WEIGHT LOSS
QUANTIFY THE WEIGHT LOSS
'HOW MUCH, OVER WHAT PERIOD — AND WERE YOU TRYING?' → 5 kg, NOT INTENTIONAL. That is a RED FLAG — and it is what keeps BOWEL CANCER ON THE LIST as differential two
ASK ABOUT GLUTEN AND WHETHER SHE IS STILL EATING IT
'DOES BREAD OR PASTA MAKE IT WORSE? ARE YOU EATING GLUTEN AT THE MOMENT?' THE SEROLOGY IS ONLY VALID ON A GLUTEN-CONTAINING DIET
THE ITCHY RASH IS THE ASSOCIATION TO NAME
'ANY ITCHY, BLISTERING RASH ON YOUR ELBOWS, KNEES, BUTTOCKS OR SCALP?' DERMATITIS HERPETIFORMIS IS COELIAC DISEASE OF THE SKIN. If she volunteers an itchy rash, name it
FAMILY HISTORY — COELIAC AND AUTOIMMUNE
COELIAC DISEASE IN A FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVE · TYPE 1 DIABETES · AUTOIMMUNE THYROID DISEASE — one practice card gives a SISTER WITH THYROID DISEASE. And bowel cancer or IBD in the family
STILL ASK EVERY RED FLAG

BLOOD · FEVER · NOCTURNAL DIARRHOEA · ABDOMINAL PAIN · TRAVEL. AND THE IBD EXTRA-INTESTINAL SCREEN — joints, eyes, rash, MOUTH ULCERS (which occur in coeliac disease too). The positive steatorrhoea answer DOES NOT LICENSE STOPPING
IRON DEFICIENCY IS PART OF THE PICTURE

'HAVE YOU BEEN TOLD YOU'RE LOW IN IRON? MORE TIRED THAN USUAL? ANY BREATHLESSNESS?' Unexplained iron deficiency in a young woman is MALABSORPTION UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE — do not accept a menstrual explanation without asking

must: FAIL — Never asking how the diarrhoea is affecting her life, so the housebound line never surfaces.
FAIL — Not characterising the stool, so steatorrhoea is missed.
FAIL — Advising a gluten-free diet before coeliac serology and biopsy.
FAIL — Labelling IBS despite 5 kg unintentional weight loss.
ASK — Are your stools greasy, floating, sticking to the pan, or hard to flush?
ASK — How is this affecting your day-to-day life?

dx: **COELIAC DISEASE — then BOWEL CANCER, then the rest.** **Six months of diarrhoea with STEATORRHOEA — greasy, floating, sticking, hard to flush — and 5 kg OF UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS, with a life now restricted by fear of leaking.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE SAME AS EVERY DIARRHOEA VERSION — RUN THE WHOLE STRUCTURE, ASK THE RED FLAGS UNCONDITIONALLY, AND PROBE EVERY POSITIVE. IN VERSION F THE ADDITIONAL MARK IS FOR ASKING 'HOW IS THIS AFFECTING YOUR LIFE?' AND ACKNOWLEDGING THE SCRIPTED ANSWER.**

**THE REASONS, IN HER WORDS: 'I think this is most likely COELIAC DISEASE. The stools you describe — GREASY, FLOATING, HARD TO FLUSH — tell me YOUR BOWEL ISN'T ABSORBING FAT PROPERLY. Together with LOSING WEIGHT WITHOUT TRYING over six months, that points to a problem with absorption in the small bowel, and coeliac disease is the commonest cause.'**

**EXPLAIN THE CONDITION PLAINLY: 'coeliac disease is a reaction to GLUTEN — a protein in WHEAT, BARLEY AND RYE — where your immune system attacks the lining of the small bowel. The tiny finger-like folds that absorb food get flattened, so you don't absorb FAT, IRON AND OTHER NUTRIENTS properly.'**

**THE GLUTEN WARNING IN THE SAME BREATH AS THE DIAGNOSIS: 'PLEASE KEEP EATING YOUR NORMAL DIET, INCLUDING BREAD AND PASTA, UNTIL THE TESTS ARE DONE — if you stop now, THE BLOOD TEST AND THE BIOPSY CAN COME BACK FALSELY NORMAL.'**

**DIFFERENTIAL TWO IS BOWEL CANCER, AND SAY WHY IT IS THERE: 'the WEIGHT LOSS IS A WARNING SIGN I DON'T IGNORE. At your age bowel cancer is uncommon, but it is on my list, which is why I'd want to look directly at the bowel if the coeliac tests don't explain everything.'**

**THE REST, BY GROUP: INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE — especially Crohn's, which can cause malabsorption · CHRONIC PANCREATITIS OR PANCREATIC INSUFFICIENCY — the other steatorrhoea cause · GIARDIASIS — tank water, travel · HYPERTHYROIDISM — weight loss with diarrhoea · LACTOSE INTOLERANCE, which can be SECONDARY TO COELIAC · medications · IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME — EXCLUDED BY THE WEIGHT LOSS, SAY SO.**

**TESTING: tTG-IgA WITH TOTAL SERUM IgA, TAKEN ON A GLUTEN-CONTAINING DIET, then DUODENAL BIOPSY showing villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia and intraepithelial lymphocytosis. Alongside: FBC, IRON STUDIES, B12, FOLATE, VITAMIN D, CALCIUM, TFTs, FAECAL CALPROTECTIN, STOOL MCS AND PCR, faecal elastase if pancreatic insufficiency is considered.**

**AFTER CONFIRMATION: A STRICT LIFELONG GLUTEN-FREE DIET WITH A DIETITIAN · REPLACE DEFICIENCIES · BONE DENSITOMETRY · SCREEN FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVES · COELIAC AUSTRALIA for practical support · repeat serology to confirm adherence.**

**ADDRESS THE ISOLATION, NOT JUST THE BOWEL: continence products and planning in the short term · a note for work if needed · CHECK MOOD — six months of being housebound by fear is a real burden · and REASSURE ABOUT PROCESS: 'once we know what this is, most people with coeliac disease get their life back on the diet.'** **SA: gastroscopy via TQEH with PATS; dietitian by telehealth in MM5.**
plan: **Hand hygiene, identity, open question, and RESPOND TO HER CONCERN before asking anything — with permission for personal questions.**
**TIMING: six months — sudden or gradual, constant or intermittent, getting worse, DOES IT WAKE YOU AT NIGHT?**
**C C C V O: how many times · consistency · blood or mucus · volume · odour — AND THE COELIAC TRIAD: GREASY OR OILY · FLOAT, STICK TO THE PAN, HARD TO FLUSH · PARTICULARLY OFFENSIVE?**
**EFFECT ON LIFE: 'HOW IS THIS AFFECTING YOUR DAY-TO-DAY LIFE?'** Then **ACKNOWLEDGE THE HOUSEBOUND ANSWER EXPLICITLY.**
**GENERAL GI: nausea, vomiting, bloating, wind, constipation before, ABDOMINAL PAIN, fever.**
**RED FLAGS, UNCONDITIONALLY: WEIGHT LOSS — HOW MUCH, OVER WHAT PERIOD, WERE YOU TRYING · appetite · lumps · TIREDNESS · BLOOD · family history of bowel cancer and at what age.**

**IRON: ever told you're low in iron, tired, breathless? LACTOSE: worse after dairy? MEDICATIONS — including anything from the chemist.**
**THYROID: hot weather, racing heart — and FAMILY THYROID DISEASE OR TYPE 1 DIABETES. PANCREAS: alcohol, pain through to the back.**
**SEXUAL HEALTH SCREEN. IBS: pain relieved by opening bowels, alternating habit, stress — asked last.**
**MOOD, briefly and kindly given the isolation: 'how has your mood been with all of this?'**
**A one-line summary back.**
**NAME COELIAC DISEASE with the reasons from her words, explain it plainly, and GIVE THE GLUTEN WARNING IN THE SAME BREATH.**
**DIFFERENTIAL TWO — BOWEL CANCER, AND WHY: the weight loss.** Then **the grouped rest, and IBS EXCLUDED BY THE WEIGHT LOSS.**
**If asked: tTG-IgA with total IgA on gluten, FBC and iron studies, then gastroscopy with duodenal biopsy — and REASSURE ABOUT PROCESS for the life she has lost.**
pefe: **Investigations: tTG-IgA WITH TOTAL SERUM IgA, ON A GLUTEN-CONTAINING DIET · FBC, IRON STUDIES, B12, FOLATE, VITAMIN D, CALCIUM, ALBUMIN · UEC, LFT, TSH · CRP AND FAECAL CALPROTECTIN · STOOL MCS AND PCR including Giardia · FAECAL ELASTASE if pancreatic insufficiency is considered.**

**IF ALREADY OFF GLUTEN: a supervised GLUTEN CHALLENGE — commonly quoted as FOUR SLICES OF BREAD DAILY FOR SIX WEEKS — or specialist advice; HLA-DQ2/DQ8 typing can help exclude it.** VERIFY.

**Management once confirmed: STRICT LIFELONG GLUTEN-FREE DIET WITH AN ACCREDITED DIETITIAN · REPLACE IRON, B12, FOLATE, VITAMIN D, CALCIUM, ZINC · BONE DENSITOMETRY · SCREEN FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVES · PNEUMOCOCCAL VACCINATION — functional hyposplenism is recognised · repeat serology to confirm adherence · COELIAC AUSTRALIA.**

**Avoid: GLUTEN-FREE DIET BEFORE SEROLOGY — it invalidates both tests · LABELLING IBS WITH 5 kg WEIGHT LOSS · LOPERAMIDE AS THE PLAN before a diagnosis · accepting 'my iron is low from my periods' without testing for malabsorption.**

**SA: gastroscopy through TQEH or Wallaroo with PATS for travel; dietitian often by TELEHEALTH in MM5; Country Health Connect; TIS National 131 450; Closing the Gap PBS co-payment for eligible patients.**

stem: A 40-year-old man on a cruise ship berthed in Sydney has been diagnosed with norovirus gastroenteritis. He is insisting on being discharged home.
tasks: Take a focused history (4 minutes)
Perform an assessment, directed to the examiner, of whether this patient can be released home
findings: A DIFFERENT TASK SET FROM THE DIARRHOEA HISTORY

FOUR MINUTES OF FOCUSED HISTORY, THEN AN ASSESSMENT DIRECTED TO THE EXAMINER OF WHETHER HE CAN BE RELEASED HOME. You are the SHIP'S MEDICAL OFFICER, berthed in Sydney after sailing from New Zealand. The diagnosis is already made — THE QUESTION IS DISPOSITION
HE OPENS ANGRY — AND THE ANGER HAS A REASON

'I'M FURIOUS. I'VE BEEN STUCK ON THIS SHIP IN THE HARBOUR FOR DAYS.' ACKNOWLEDGE, THEN ASK WHY: 'CAN I ASK WHAT'S MAKING YOU SO KEEN TO GET HOME? THERE MAY BE SOMETHING I CAN HELP WITH.' → 'MY CAT'S AT HOME ON HER OWN.' → 'WE CAN ALMOST CERTAINLY ARRANGE FOR SOMEONE TO LOOK IN ON HER TODAY'
THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT QUESTION
'WHEN DID IT START? IS IT STILL GOING? IF IT HAS STOPPED, WHEN?' THE EXCLUSION CRITERION IS TIME SINCE THE LAST SYMPTOM
HE MUST BE ASYMPTOMATIC — NOT JUST FREE OF DIARRHOEA
COUNT, CONSISTENCY, AND ANY BLOOD — blood would change the diagnosis entirely · FEVER OR CHILLS · ABDOMINAL PAIN · NAUSEA OR VOMITING · DIZZINESS
TOLERATING ORAL INTAKE IS A DISCHARGE CRITERION IN ITS OWN RIGHT
'ARE YOU EATING AND DRINKING NORMALLY, AND KEEPING IT DOWN?'
THE QUESTION WHERE THE 2025 FINDING HIDES
'WHAT TREATMENT DID YOU RECEIVE ON BOARD?' → INTRAVENOUS FLUIDS. That opens THE CANNULA SITE — which you must then ASK TO INSPECT BY NAME
TWO QUESTIONS THAT CHANGE THE ANSWER

IMMUNE STATUS — 'ANY CONDITIONS OR MEDICATIONS AFFECTING YOUR IMMUNE SYSTEM — DIABETES, CANCER, STEROIDS, CHEMOTHERAPY?' — norovirus is PROLONGED AND MORE SEVERE in the immunocompromised. OCCUPATION — 'ARE YOU A FOOD HANDLER, CHILDCARE OR HEALTHCARE WORKER?' — changes the exclusion period and creates a PUBLIC HEALTH DUTY
THE ASSESSMENT, SPOKEN TO THE EXAMINER

GENERAL APPEARANCE — does he look well, any DEHYDRATION · VITALS — temperature, pulse, BP INCLUDING POSTURAL, respiratory rate · A FULL ABDOMINAL EXAMINATION — 'I WOULD NOT RELEASE ANYONE WITH ABDOMINAL TENDERNESS' · AND THE CANNULA SITE
THE CARD THE EXAMINER HANDS YOU IN 2025 — on request
A PERIPHERAL CANNULA SITE INFECTION: ERYTHEMA, SWELLING AND PURULENT DISCHARGE AT THE INSERTION POINT. IT DOES NOT BY ITSELF PREVENT DISCHARGE IF HE IS WELL
THE RELEASE CRITERIA — say them as a list

NO DIARRHOEA AND NO VOMITING FOR 48 HOURS · AFEBRILE · TOLERATING ORAL INTAKE · NO CLINICAL DEHYDRATION · A NORMAL ABDOMINAL EXAMINATION. Some services use 48–72 hours — VERIFY against current SA Health and national guidance
findingsLabel: A disposition station — five release criteria, and the cannula you find by asking
must: FAIL — Never asking when the last symptom was. The criterion is time since last symptom.
FAIL — Not asking what treatment he had on board, so the cannula is never inspected.
FAIL — Keeping him on board for a cannula site infection when he is systemically well.
FAIL — Meeting his anger with rules instead of finding out why he wants to go home.
ASK — When did the diarrhoea and vomiting last happen?
ASK — Are you a food handler, or do you work in childcare or healthcare?

dx: **NOROVIRUS GASTROENTERITIS — RESOLVED — with a PERIPHERAL CANNULA SITE INFECTION from IV fluids given on board.** **The question is not the diagnosis but DISPOSITION: CAN HE BE RELEASED HOME?**
**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: APPLY DEFINED RELEASE CRITERIA OUT LOUD, FIND THE SECOND PROBLEM BY ASKING WHAT TREATMENT HE HAD, AND DO NOT LET A LOCAL INFECTION BECOME A REASON TO DETAIN A WELL MAN.**

**THE CRITERIA, SPOKEN TO THE EXAMINER: 'my criteria for release are: NO DIARRHOEA AND NO VOMITING FOR 48 HOURS, AFEBRILE, TOLERATING ORAL INTAKE, NO CLINICAL DEHYDRATION, and A NORMAL ABDOMINAL EXAMINATION.'** VERIFY the exclusion period — 48 hours is standard; some services use 48–72.

**THE ANSWER TO THE CHALLENGE — 'WOULD YOU STILL RELEASE HIM?': 'YES. He meets the exclusion criteria for norovirus — symptom-free for 48 hours, afebrile, eating and drinking, no dehydration and a normal abdomen. THE CANNULA SITE DOES NEED TREATMENT, BUT THAT IS ORAL ANTIBIOTICS I CAN PRESCRIBE, AND THERE IS NO REASON TO KEEP HIM ON BOARD TO GIVE IT.'**

**MANAGING THE CANNULA SITE: REMOVE THE CANNULA · START ORAL FLUCLOXACILLIN as for a skin and soft tissue infection · MARK THE EDGE OF THE REDNESS · GP REVIEW IN 48 HOURS, or ED for FEVER, SPREADING REDNESS OR FEELING UNWELL.** **IV ANTIBIOTICS ONLY FOR SYSTEMIC FEATURES — HIGH FEVER, HYPOTENSION, TACHYCARDIA OR DROWSINESS. HE HAS NONE.** VERIFY dose.

**THE OPENING THAT EARNS THE APPROACH MARKS: 'I can hear how frustrating this is, and I'D BE FRUSTRATED TOO — being held on board past your disembarkation date is really hard. CAN I ASK WHAT'S MAKING YOU SO KEEN TO GET HOME? There may be something I can help with. Whatever you tell me stays between us.'**

**SOLVE THE REAL PROBLEM: the cat. 'That's a real worry. WE CAN ALMOST CERTAINLY ARRANGE FOR SOMEONE TO LOOK IN ON HER TODAY. Let me ask you a few questions and then I'll tell you EXACTLY WHERE WE STAND.'** **A patient whose real concern is solved stops fighting the process.**

**WHY THE CRITERIA MATTER: NOROVIRUS IS HIGHLY INFECTIOUS WITH A VERY LOW INFECTIVE DOSE, SPREADS BY THE FAECAL-ORAL ROUTE, AEROSOLISED VOMIT AND CONTAMINATED SURFACES, AND CAUSES OUTBREAKS ON CRUISE SHIPS AND IN AGED CARE. VIRAL SHEDDING CAN CONTINUE AFTER SYMPTOMS STOP — hence the symptom-free window and hand hygiene advice.**

**IF ANY CRITERION FAILS — ongoing vomiting, fever, dehydration, abdominal tenderness, or blood in the stool — HE STAYS, and blood or tenderness REOPENS THE DIAGNOSIS. IMMUNOCOMPROMISE — prolonged shedding and more severe illness — lowers the threshold to keep him.**

**DISCHARGE ADVICE: HANDWASHING WITH SOAP AND WATER — ALCOHOL GEL IS LESS EFFECTIVE AGAINST NOROVIRUS · DO NOT PREPARE FOOD FOR OTHERS for at least 48 hours after symptoms stop · clean surfaces with a bleach-based product · and if he is a FOOD HANDLER, CHILDCARE OR HEALTHCARE WORKER, EXCLUSION FROM WORK FOR 48 HOURS AFTER SYMPTOMS RESOLVE, with public health notification of the outbreak per local rules.** VERIFY.

**Public health: outbreaks on cruise ships are reported through the ship's medical team to the relevant PORT HEALTH AND STATE PUBLIC HEALTH UNIT; occupational exclusion of 48 hours after symptoms for food handlers, childcare and healthcare workers.** VERIFY local notification requirements.

stem: Michael Reid, 32, presents with diarrhoea for two weeks. 'I'm gay, and my boyfriend has exactly the same thing.'
tasks: Take a focused, relevant history (6 minutes)
Explain your most likely diagnosis and your differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: THE PIVOT ARRIVES IN THE FIRST MINUTE

'I'VE HAD DIARRHOEA FOR ABOUT TWO WEEKS. I'M GAY, AND MY PARTNER HAS EXACTLY THE SAME THING.' DO NOT FILE IT AWAY FOR LATER. TREAT IT AS A SECOND PRESENTING COMPLAINT AND EXPLORE IT IMMEDIATELY. THE ROLE-PLAYER WAS INSTRUCTED TO SAY IT EARLY PRECISELY SO THAT YOU WOULD ACT ON IT
ONE OF THE HIGHEST FAILURE RATES IN THE ABDOMINAL BLOCK

NOT FAILED ON KNOWLEDGE. CANDIDATES RUN THE GENERIC DIARRHOEA STRUCTURE, REACH THE SEXUAL HISTORY AT FIVE AND A HALF MINUTES AS QUESTION TEN, ASK TWO SCREENING QUESTIONS, AND NEVER COLLECT THE RISK FACTORS THE WHOLE STATION WAS BUILT AROUND
THE PIVOT SENTENCE

'THANK YOU FOR TELLING ME THAT — IT'S DIRECTLY RELEVANT, SO I'D LIKE TO ASK SOME QUESTIONS ABOUT YOUR SEXUAL HEALTH NOW RATHER THAN LATER. EVERYTHING IS CONFIDENTIAL.' Then — 'BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — ARE YOU TAKING PrEP?'
PrEP — ADHERENCE, NOT JUST USE

'ARE YOU TAKING IT EVERY DAY, WITHOUT MISSING DOSES?' EFFICACY IS ADHERENCE-DEPENDENT; 'MOST DAYS' IS NOT PROTECTED. Then WHEN STARTED, WHO PRESCRIBES, LAST HIV AND STI SCREEN AND RESULT, and ANY TUMMY UPSET SINCE STARTING
THE THREE-BOX SEXUAL HISTORY — at ninety seconds

PARTNERS — STABLE RELATIONSHIP, MULTIPLE PARTNERS, GENDER · PRACTICES — CONDOMS, ORAL, ANAL, RECEPTIVE OR INSERTIVE · RISK — PREVIOUS STIs, SEX UNDER ALCOHOL OR DRUGS, SEX WORKERS, LAST SCREEN AND RESULT
WHAT HE GIVES

ON PrEP, TAKEN DAILY · MULTIPLE PARTNERS · CONDOMLESS ANAL SEX · PREVIOUS CHLAMYDIA, GONORRHOEA AND SYPHILIS · LAST SCREEN A MONTH AGO, RESULT NOT SEEN. SAY IT BACK: 'SO YOU'VE HAD SEVERAL INFECTIONS BEFORE, WHICH TELLS ME YOU'VE HAD EXPOSURES'
A PENDING RESULT IS NOT A NEGATIVE RESULT
'MY LAST CHECK WAS A MONTH AGO, I DON'T KNOW THE RESULT' → 'I'LL LOOK THOSE RESULTS UP TODAY'
THE SEROCONVERSION BLOCK

'ANY FEVERS, NIGHT SWEATS, SORE THROAT, SWOLLEN GLANDS IN YOUR NECK OR ARMPITS, A RASH, MOUTH ULCERS, OR ACHING MUSCLES ALONG WITH THE DIARRHOEA?' ANY OF THESE WITH DIARRHOEA IN THIS RISK GROUP IS A STRONG ARGUMENT FOR TESTING TODAY
THE ANORECTAL BLOCK — four questions

'ANY PAIN IN THE BACK PASSAGE? ANY DISCHARGE? ANY FEELING OF NEEDING TO GO WHEN THERE'S NOTHING THERE? ANY BLEEDING?' TENESMUS WITH DISCHARGE IS PROCTITIS — CHLAMYDIA INCLUDING LGV, GONORRHOEA, HERPES — TREATABLE TODAY AND MISSED IF NEVER ASKED
THE PARTNER IS A SECOND PATIENT

'TELL ME ABOUT YOUR PARTNER'S SYMPTOMS. HAS HE BEEN TESTED? IS HE ON PrEP?' Concurrent illness supports a TRANSMISSIBLE CAUSE — shared source, sexually transmissible enteric infection, OR BOTH SEROCONVERTING. And VACCINATION — hepatitis A and B, mpox, doxy-PEP

dx: **ACUTE HIV INFECTION — SEROCONVERSION ILLNESS — TO BE EXCLUDED, with PrEP SIDE EFFECT, INFECTIVE PROCTITIS AND SEXUALLY TRANSMISSIBLE ENTERIC INFECTION as differentials.** **Acute retroviral syndrome follows HIV acquisition BY TWO TO FOUR WEEKS: FEVER, SORE THROAT, LYMPHADENOPATHY, RASH, MYALGIA, MOUTH ULCERS — and importantly here, DIARRHOEA.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: TREATING THE DISCLOSURE AS A SECOND PRESENTING COMPLAINT. The sexual history is no longer a two-question screen at the end — IT BECOMES A FULL THREE-BOX HISTORY AT ABOUT NINETY SECONDS, BEFORE IBD, BEFORE COELIAC, BEFORE MEDICATIONS. THE CONTEXT RE-RANKS THE LIST: HIV MOVES FROM TENTH ON THE GENERIC LIST TO FIRST.**

**THE SECOND DISCRIMINATOR — HOW YOU NAME IT: 'I want to be upfront with you. THE MOST SERIOUS THING I NEED TO RULE OUT IS HIV. I'M NOT TELLING YOU THAT YOU HAVE IT — I'M TELLING YOU IT NEEDS TO BE EXCLUDED, AND HERE IS WHY I'M THINKING ABOUT IT.' CANDIDATES WHO ANNOUNCE A DIAGNOSIS, AND CANDIDATES WHO AVOID THE WORD ALTOGETHER, BOTH LOSE MARKS.**

**THE REASONS, FROM WHAT HE TOLD YOU: MULTIPLE PARTNERS · CONDOMLESS ANAL SEX · PREVIOUS CHLAMYDIA, GONORRHOEA AND SYPHILIS · A PARTNER WITH IDENTICAL SYMPTOMS · and DIARRHOEA IS A RECOGNISED FEATURE OF THE SEROCONVERSION ILLNESS.**

**'BUT I'M ON PrEP, SO I CAN'T GET HIV' — 'PrEP IS VERY EFFECTIVE, BUT IT ISN'T ABSOLUTE, AND IT DEPENDS ON TAKING IT CONSISTENTLY. THAT IS EXACTLY WHY I WANT TO TEST.'** **PrEP is TENOFOVIR DISOPROXIL WITH EMTRICITABINE, one tablet daily; COMMONEST SIDE EFFECT GASTROINTESTINAL, usually early and self-limiting; the IMPORTANT SERIOUS ONE IS RENAL.**

**CORRECTION — the source describes MONTHLY STI checks on PrEP. AUSTRALIAN PRACTICE IS THREE-MONTHLY REVIEW: HIV SEROLOGY, STI SCREENING INCLUDING ANORECTAL AND PHARYNGEAL SWABS, AND RENAL FUNCTION, with baseline renal function before starting.** If challenged: **'standard monitoring is three-monthly HIV and STI screening, with renal function at baseline and periodically; I would confirm against the ASHM PrEP guidelines.'** VERIFY.

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP: INFECTIVE — PROCTITIS from chlamydia INCLUDING LYMPHOGRANULOMA VENEREUM, gonorrhoea or herpes; SEXUALLY TRANSMISSIBLE ENTERIC INFECTIONS — SHIGELLA (SOME MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT), GIARDIA, CAMPYLOBACTER, AMOEBIASIS — spread by oral-anal contact with documented Australian outbreaks among MSM; HEPATITIS A · DRUG — PrEP GI upset · GI — IBD, coeliac, lactose, IBS · ENDOCRINE — hyperthyroidism · colorectal cancer, unlikely at 32 but never omitted.**

**TESTING WITH CONSENT: PRE-TEST DISCUSSION — WHAT THE TEST IS, THE WINDOW PERIOD, HOW RESULTS ARE GIVEN, CONFIDENTIALITY. FOURTH-GENERATION HIV ANTIGEN/ANTIBODY ASSAY — detects p24 from about 2 weeks; REPEAT AT 6 AND 12 WEEKS IF NEGATIVE INSIDE THE WINDOW; HIV RNA if very early. A NEGATIVE TEST INSIDE THE WINDOW DOES NOT CLOSE THE QUESTION.**

**THE SEXUAL HISTORY IS ADDED TO THE SPINE, NOT SUBSTITUTED FOR IT — still run timing, CCCVO, general GI, red flags, travel, hepatitis, IBD, coeliac, medications. ASK MATTER-OF-FACTLY: no averted eyes, no 'I'm sorry, I have to ask', NO MORALISING about partners or practices. Say confidentiality ONCE and move on.**

**SA: HIV, SYPHILIS, GONORRHOEA, CHLAMYDIA, SHIGELLA, GIARDIA AND HEPATITIS A ARE NOTIFIABLE. If positive, EARLY ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY — ADELAIDE SEXUAL HEALTH CENTRE (CLINIC 275) or infectious diseases; SHINE SA and telehealth make review workable from the Yorke Peninsula. PARTNER NOTIFICATION WITH SUPPORT — LET THEM KNOW and SA Health contact tracers. NEVER discuss his results with his partner without explicit permission.**

**PrEP BLOCK: EVERY DAY WITHOUT MISSING DOSES · WHEN STARTED, WHO PRESCRIBES · LAST HIV AND STI SCREEN, AND DID YOU GET THE RESULTS · ANY NAUSEA OR TUMMY UPSET SINCE STARTING?**
**THE THREE BOXES: STABLE RELATIONSHIP · MULTIPLE PARTNERS · MALE, FEMALE OR BOTH · CONDOMS · ORAL, ANAL OR BOTH, RECEPTIVE OR INSERTIVE · PREVIOUS STIs · SEX UNDER ALCOHOL OR DRUGS.**
**SAY THE RISK BACK: 'so you've had several infections before, which tells me you've had exposures' — and 'I'LL LOOK UP THOSE RESULTS TODAY.'**

**ANORECTAL: pain in the back passage · discharge · TENESMUS · bleeding.**
**THE PARTNER: his symptoms · tested · on PrEP? VACCINATION: hepatitis A and B · mpox · doxycycline after sex?**

**A one-line summary back, and 'is there anything you were particularly worried about?'**
**NAME IT AS THE CONDITION TO EXCLUDE: 'the most serious thing I need to rule out is HIV — I'm not telling you that you have it.' Then THE REASONS FROM HIS RISK FACTORS.**

**'BUT I'M ON PrEP' — very effective, not absolute, adherence-dependent.** Then **the grouped differentials — proctitis including LGV, STEIs like shigella, hepatitis A, the PrEP itself, then the generic list.**

**THE OFFER, WITH CONSENT: a fourth-generation HIV test today with its window period, three-site STI screen, syphilis serology, stool panel, hepatitis serology, renal function — and 'YOUR PARTNER NEEDS TO BE SEEN AND TESTED TOO — CAN WE ARRANGE THAT?'**

dx: **PSEUDOMEMBRANOUS COLITIS — CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE TOXIN-MEDIATED COLITIS — said as a condition you are CONCERNED HE MAY HAVE, which the stool test will confirm.** **Named for the YELLOW-WHITE PLAQUES — PSEUDOMEMBRANES — seen at sigmoidoscopy. It is the most severe form of antibiotic-associated diarrhoea.**

**THE DISTINCTION THE STATION RESTS ON: ANTIBIOTIC-ASSOCIATED DIARRHOEA is ANY loose stool caused by an antibiotic — COMMON, SELF-LIMITING, NO SPECIFIC ORGANISM. PSEUDOMEMBRANOUS COLITIS is THE SPECIFIC, POTENTIALLY LIFE-THREATENING SUBSET caused by C. difficile overgrowth and toxin. ALMOST EVERYONE WHO TAKES AMOXICILLIN GETS THE FIRST; ALMOST NOBODY GETS THE SECOND.**

**THE SINGLE AUTOMATIC-FAIL OMISSION: NOT SAYING 'WE WILL STOP THE ANTIBIOTIC' OUT LOUD. This belongs to the small family of stations BUILT AROUND STOPPING A DRUG — like the COCP in migraine with aura, or the serotonergic agent in serotonin syndrome. IF YOU DO NOT SAY IT, THE MARKER HAS NOTHING TO TICK.**

**THE SENTENCE: 'I'M CONCERNED YOU MAY HAVE A CONDITION CALLED PSEUDOMEMBRANOUS COLITIS… and THE FIRST THING WE'RE GOING TO DO IS STOP THE ANTIBIOTIC.'** Then **the mechanism: 'antibiotics kill some of the GOOD BACTERIA in the bowel. That lets ONE PARTICULAR BUG OVERGROW, and it produces A TOXIN — a poison — that INFLAMES THE LINING OF THE BOWEL.'**

**DIFFERENTIALS, EACH WITH A REASON FROM THE STEM — THIS CASE USUALLY FINISHES EARLY, SO USE THE TIME: 'I don't think this is GASTROENTERITIS — you haven't travelled, eaten out, and nobody around you is unwell. Not IBD — no blood or mucus and it hasn't been going on long. Not COELIAC — your stools aren't greasy or hard to flush. Nothing to suggest BOWEL CANCER — no weight loss, no bleeding, no family history.' SECOND DIAGNOSIS: PLAIN ANTIBIOTIC-ASSOCIATED DIARRHOEA — what you're left with if the toxin test is negative.**

**CORRECTION — FIRST-LINE IS ORAL VANCOMYCIN, NOT METRONIDAZOLE. The source gives metronidazole for mild-moderate disease. Contemporary guidance: ORAL VANCOMYCIN 125 mg FOUR TIMES DAILY FOR 10 DAYS for an initial episode of any severity; METRONIDAZOLE 400 mg THREE TIMES DAILY FOR 10 DAYS as an alternative in non-severe disease; FIDAXOMICIN particularly for recurrence.** If challenged: **'oral vancomycin 125 milligrams four times daily for ten days first line, confirmed against Therapeutic Guidelines; metronidazole remains an accepted alternative in non-severe disease.'** VERIFY.

**CORRECTION — IV VANCOMYCIN DOES NOT TREAT C. DIFFICILE. In FULMINANT disease: ORAL OR PER-RECTAL VANCOMYCIN PLUS IV METRONIDAZOLE — the vancomycin must reach the lumen, and IV vancomycin does not. A CLASSIC EXAMINER PROBE.** **The organism is now CLOSTRIDIOIDES, reclassified from Clostridium.**

**ONSET WINDOW: DURING THE COURSE OR UP TO 8 WEEKS AFTER, most often within about 2 weeks — 'I finished those tablets a fortnight ago' DOES NOT EXCLUDE IT. OTHER RISK FACTORS: AGE OVER 65, HOSPITAL OR AGED-CARE EXPOSURE, PPIs, IMMUNOSUPPRESSION, IBD, PREVIOUS C. DIFFICILE. CLASSIC ANTIBIOTIC: CLINDAMYCIN — plus amoxicillin, ampicillin, cephalosporins and quinolones.**

**MANAGEMENT ORDER: STOP THE ANTIBIOTIC — SAY IT FIRST · ORAL REHYDRATION — HYDRALYTE OR GASTROLYTE · IF TOXIN POSITIVE, ORAL VANCOMYCIN · WITHHOLD ANTIMOTILITY AGENTS · REVIEW THE PPI · SOAP AND WATER, NOT GEL; BLEACH-BASED BATHROOM CLEANING · REVIEW IN 2–3 DAYS WITH RESULTS.** **Recurrence in about ONE IN FIVE — VANCOMYCIN TAPER, FIDAXOMICIN, OR FAECAL MICROBIOTA TRANSPLANTATION.**

**SAFETY-NET, NAMED ALOUD: 'come back, or go straight to the emergency department, if you develop A FEVER, SEVERE TUMMY PAIN OR BLOATING, BLOOD IN THE STOOL, if you become DIZZY OR LIGHTHEADED, or you CANNOT KEEP FLUIDS DOWN. Those are the signs this is becoming THE MORE SERIOUS VERSION.'** **'Is it serious?' — 'It CAN be in some people, which is why I want to test and see you again in a couple of days — but you're well in yourself right now, and I expect you'll be fine.'**
