dx: **COLORECTAL CARCINOMA WITH HEPATIC METASTASES. A rectal mass palpable on digital examination, with hepatomegaly, in a 67-year-old with a change in bowel habit.** **COLORECTAL VENOUS BLOOD DRAINS THROUGH THE PORTAL VEIN, SO THE LIVER IS THE COMMONEST AND USUALLY THE FIRST SITE OF DISTANT SPREAD — WHICH IS WHY TWO FINDINGS ARE ONE DIAGNOSIS.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE — TWO BEHAVIOURS, BOTH OMISSIONS: ONE, THE RED FLAGS ASKED DESPITE A TWO-WEEK HISTORY — 'THERE ARE SOME QUESTIONS I ASK EVERYBODY WITH A CHANGE IN THEIR BOWELS.' TWO, ASKING FOR THE RECTAL EXAMINATION — the mass is released ONLY ON REQUEST.**

**THE REASONING THE STATION IS REALLY TESTING: EXAMINATION FINDINGS OUTRANK A NEGATIVE HISTORY. Suppose every red flag came back negative — THE DIAGNOSIS DOES NOT CHANGE. You can feel a mass in her rectum and you can feel her liver. A HISTORY THAT FAILS TO SUPPORT A FINDING DOES NOT CANCEL THE FINDING. And CANCER DOES NOT DECLARE ITS DURATION — the fortnight is when the symptom became annoying enough to bring her in.**

**THE DELIVERY — WARNING SHOT, THEN PAUSE: 'Mrs Harding, I need to talk to you about what I've found, and I'D RATHER BE STRAIGHT WITH YOU THAN VAGUE. Is that all right? IS THERE ANYONE YOU'D LIKE WITH YOU?' … 'When I examined you, I found TWO THINGS. There is A LUMP IN YOUR BACK PASSAGE, and YOUR LIVER FEELS ENLARGED.' PAUSE. LET HER REACT. DO NOT FILL THE SILENCE.**

**THEN THE CONCERN, HONESTLY: 'I'M CONCERNED THAT THE LUMP MAY BE A CANCER IN THE BOWEL, AND THAT THE ENLARGED LIVER MAY MEAN IT HAS SPREAD THERE. I CAN'T BE CERTAIN TODAY — I need tests to confirm it — BUT I DON'T WANT TO TELL YOU IT'S NOTHING WHEN I'M WORRIED THAT IT ISN'T.'**

**THE CONCRETE NEXT STEP: 'I'm going to arrange A CAMERA TEST OF THE BOWEL, URGENTLY, where they can look directly and take a small sample, and A CT SCAN of your chest, tummy and pelvis. I'LL REFER YOU TODAY, AND I'LL RING YOU MYSELF ONCE I HAVE THE DATES. I know that's a great deal to take in. WHAT QUESTIONS DO YOU HAVE?'**

**WHAT NOT TO SAY: NOT 'IT'S PROBABLY NOTHING'. NOT 'YOU HAVE METASTATIC BOWEL CANCER' — YOU HAVE NO TISSUE DIAGNOSIS. NOT A PROGNOSIS, A STAGE OR A TREATMENT PLAN. AND NOT A DIFFERENTIAL LIST THAT BURIES THE WORD CANCER IN THE MIDDLE — NAME YOUR CONCERN FIRST, CLEARLY, THEN THE ALTERNATIVES.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP: GI — colorectal cancer WITHOUT metastasis, with OVERFLOW PAST AN OBSTRUCTING LESION — 'were you constipated before this?'; IBD; ISCHAEMIC COLITIS · INFECTIVE — infective colitis, C. difficile · DRUGS — HER OWN LOPERAMIDE, which may be causing PARADOXICAL OVERFLOW · ENDOCRINE — hyperthyroidism · OTHER — a second intra-abdominal malignancy; BENIGN HEPATOMEGALY — fatty liver, alcohol, right heart failure.**
**THE OVARIAN TRAP: do not reach for the other famous pelvic-mass station. AN OVARIAN MASS IS FELT IN THE ILIAC FOSSA, NOT IN THE RECTUM — THE SITE OF THE MASS IS THE DISCRIMINATOR.**

**PLAN: URGENT COLONOSCOPY WITH BIOPSY · CT CHEST, ABDOMEN AND PELVIS FOR STAGING · MRI LIVER AND MRI RECTUM · FBC FOR IRON DEFICIENCY, IRON STUDIES, UEC, LFTs — ALP AND GGT RISE FIRST WITH LIVER METASTASES · CEA AS A BASELINE, NOT A DIAGNOSTIC TEST · COAGULATION, group and hold · STOP THE LOPERAMIDE · COLORECTAL MDT.** **SA: URGENT CATEGORY 1 REFERRAL — suspected colorectal malignancy with a palpable rectal mass, expected within 30 days; PATS; Country Health Connect; CANCER COUNCIL SA 13 11 20; a cancer care coordinator early.** VERIFY category timing.

**Do now: FBC — IRON DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA · IRON STUDIES, UEC · LFTs — ALP AND GGT RISE FIRST WITH LIVER METASTASES · COAGULATION, GROUP AND HOLD · CEA — A BASELINE FOR MONITORING, NOT A DIAGNOSTIC TEST · STOOL MCS AND PCR — the cancer does not excuse you from excluding a coexisting infection · STOP THE LOPERAMIDE.**

findings: READ THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE

EVERYONE KNOWS THE RECALL IS HAEMORRHOIDS. THAT KNOWLEDGE IS THE COMMONEST REASON CANDIDATES FAIL. IT IS NOT A HAEMORRHOIDS STATION — IT IS A RECTAL BLEEDING STATION. Candidates who ask about heavy lifting, chronic cough and liver disease — THE RISK FACTORS FOR THE ANSWER — NEVER EXCLUDE THE DIFFERENTIALS OF THE COMPLAINT, AND ARE FAILED DESPITE THE RIGHT DIAGNOSIS
THREE VERSIONS OFF ONE STEM

A: BRIGHT RED ON THE STOOLS, ON AND OFF, NO PAIN, no red flags; findings on PROCTOSCOPY only — soft bulky masses → HAEMORRHOIDS. B (2025): stool and paper, BALI with vomiting and diarrhoea and ANTIBIOTICS, FATHER WITH BOWEL CANCER AT 52, a lump he can push back → HAEMORRHOIDS, then cancer, travellers' infection, C. difficile. C (2025): BLOOD OVER THE STOOLS, PAIN ON PASSING MOTIONS, CONSTIPATION, and the patient REFUSES A RECTAL EXAMINATION → ANAL FISSURE
PAIN IS THE SINGLE DISCRIMINATOR

HAEMORRHOIDS BLEED PAINLESSLY. A FISSURE HURTS — a tearing pain during defecation followed by an ache lasting hours. When he says 'it hurts when I go', SAY IT: 'PAIN MAKES HAEMORRHOIDS MUCH LESS LIKELY'
THE FINDING LIVES ON PROCTOSCOPY, NOT DIGITAL EXAMINATION

INTERNAL HAEMORRHOIDS ARE SOFT, COMPRESSIBLE AND ABOVE THE DENTATE LINE — FREQUENTLY IMPALPABLE ON DIGITAL EXAMINATION. In 2025, candidates reporting 'normal examination' and candidates reporting soft bulky masses sat THE SAME STATION ON THE SAME DAY; THE DIFFERENCE WAS WHETHER THEY ASKED. 'I WOULD LIKE TO PERFORM A PROCTOSCOPY — internal haemorrhoids often can't be felt on digital examination'
LOCALISE THE SOURCE FROM THE BLOOD

BRIGHT RED, ON THE OUTSIDE OF THE STOOL OR ON THE PAPER → DISTAL: anal canal or low rectum. DARK, MIXED ALL THROUGH → MORE PROXIMAL: escalates cancer, diverticular disease and colitis. And AMOUNT — a few drops, streaks, or dripping into the bowl
THE LUMP — grade it

'CAN YOU PUSH IT BACK IN?' I — BLEED ONLY · II — PROLAPSE AND REDUCE SPONTANEOUSLY · III — NEED MANUAL REDUCTION · IV — IRREDUCIBLE. An irreducible lump should also make you think of SOMETHING THAT IS NOT A HAEMORRHOID
'MY FATHER HAD BOWEL CANCER' → 'HOW OLD WAS HE?'
UNDER 60 IN A FIRST-DEGREE RELATIVE CHANGES THE WHOLE FOLLOW-UP TASK. FATHER AT 52 → 52 MINUS 10 = 42; 42 IS EARLIER THAN 50 → FIVE-YEARLY COLONOSCOPY FROM 42
VERSION C — WHEN THE PATIENT REFUSES THE RECTAL EXAMINATION
DO NOT FORCE IT. SAY WHAT YOU WOULD HAVE LOOKED FOR, AND DIAGNOSE FROM THE HISTORY: PAIN PLUS CONSTIPATION PLUS NO LUMP IS A FISSURE. Candidates still said haemorrhoids, BECAUSE THAT IS THE RECALL
THE CANCER BLOCK — FIRST AND AT EVERY AGE

WEIGHT LOSS · APPETITE · LUMPS · TIREDNESS · CHANGE IN BOWEL HABIT · FAMILY HISTORY WITH THE AGE · THE SCREENING KIT. The source is explicit: A CANDIDATE WHO DOES NOT RULE OUT CANCER IN A RECTAL BLEEDING CASE DOES NOT PASS, whatever the age — including one who reached the right diagnosis of haemorrhoids
BLOOD THINNERS AND THE VOLUME QUESTION

'ARE YOU ON ANY BLOOD THINNERS — WARFARIN, APIXABAN, RIVAROXABAN, CLOPIDOGREL, ASPIRIN?' ANTICOAGULATION DOES NOT CAUSE A LESION — IT UNMASKS ONE; you still colonoscope. And 'ANY DIZZINESS OR LIGHT-HEADEDNESS?' — the volume question

dx: **VERSION-DEPENDENT: PAINLESS BRIGHT BLEEDING WITH A REDUCIBLE LUMP IS INTERNAL HAEMORRHOIDS; PAINFUL BLEEDING WITH CONSTIPATION IS AN ANAL FISSURE — WITH COLORECTAL CANCER NEVER OFF THE LIST.** **ONE-LINE STRATEGY: EXCLUDE THE DIFFERENTIALS OF THE COMPLAINT, NOT THE RISK FACTORS OF THE ANSWER.**
**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE — THREE BEHAVIOURS, EACH AN OMISSION: EXCLUDING CANCER AT EVERY AGE · REQUESTING PROCTOSCOPY BY NAME · DIAGNOSING WHAT YOU FOUND, NOT WHAT YOU MEMORISED.**

**THE DENTATE LINE EXPLAINS THE CLUSTER: ABOVE IT, VISCERAL INNERVATION — INTERNAL HAEMORRHOIDS ARE PAINLESS; BELOW IT, SOMATIC — A FISSURE OR THROMBOSED EXTERNAL PILE IS AGONISING. It is also why internal piles are so often missed on digital examination.**

**MULTIPLE PLANTED FINDINGS ARE DELIBERATE: the 2025 version gives A REDUCIBLE LUMP, A BALI TRIP, A COURSE OF ANTIBIOTICS AND A FATHER WITH BOWEL CANCER AT 52. A candidate on the recall asks five haemorrhoid questions and collects none of the others. NAME HAEMORRHOIDS FIRST BECAUSE THE FINDINGS SUPPORT IT, COLORECTAL CANCER SECOND BECAUSE OF THE FAMILY HISTORY, then TRAVELLERS' INFECTIONS AND PSEUDOMEMBRANOUS COLITIS. CONFUSION HERE MEANS YOUR HISTORY WAS GOOD.**

**THE ONE INVESTIGATION TO NAME: COLONOSCOPY. 'RECTAL BLEEDING IS NOT EXPLAINED BY HAEMORRHOIDS UNTIL THE COLON HAS BEEN SEEN. A VISIBLE HAEMORRHOID TELLS YOU A HAEMORRHOID IS PRESENT; IT DOES NOT TELL YOU NOTHING ELSE IS BLEEDING ABOVE IT.'** If asked about a 22-year-old: **'YOUNG AGE ALONE IS NOT A RELIABLE REASON TO OMIT COLONOSCOPY, and certainly not with a first-degree relative under 60.'** VERIFY — some guidance allows sigmoidoscopy alone in a young, typical, low-risk bleed.

**THE FOLLOW-UP TASK — SCREENING CATEGORIES: CATEGORY 1 — no family history, or one first-degree relative at 60 or over: iFOBT EVERY 2 YEARS FROM 45 TO 74. CATEGORY 2 — ONE FIRST-DEGREE UNDER 60, or one first-degree plus one or more second-degree at any age, or two first-degree at any age: COLONOSCOPY EVERY 5 YEARS FROM 10 YEARS BEFORE THE EARLIEST FAMILY DIAGNOSIS OR AGE 50, WHICHEVER IS EARLIER. CATEGORY 3 — FAMILIAL CANCER CLINIC.** VERIFY.

**HAEMORRHOID MANAGEMENT: FIBRE AND FLUIDS, AVOID STRAINING AND PROLONGED SITTING, topical preparations, sitz baths · GRADE I–II → RUBBER BAND LIGATION · GRADE III–IV OR FAILED CONSERVATIVE → HAEMORRHOIDECTOMY · THROMBOSED EXTERNAL PILE → EXCISE WITHIN ABOUT 72 HOURS, otherwise conservative.**

**FISSURE MANAGEMENT: SOFTEN THE STOOL — fibre, fluids, osmotic laxative · SITZ BATHS · TOPICAL GLYCERYL TRINITRATE OR DILTIAZEM to relax the internal sphincter · then BOTULINUM TOXIN OR LATERAL INTERNAL SPHINCTEROTOMY if chronic. About 90% are POSTERIOR MIDLINE — an off-midline fissure should raise CROHN'S, HIV, SYPHILIS, TB OR CANCER.** VERIFY.
**REASSURANCE THAT VALIDATES WITHOUT PROMISING: 'blood is frightening to see, and you were right to come in. It's something we always look into properly.' NEVER 'I'M SURE IT'S JUST PILES'.**

**NOT AN iFOBT — IT IS A SCREENING TEST FOR ASYMPTOMATIC PEOPLE AND HAS NO ROLE ONCE BLEEDING IS VISIBLE.** **SA: proctoscopy is realistic in a rural practice and worth naming for exactly that reason; colonoscopy via Yorke and Northern or Adelaide, URGENT with a family history or red flag, PATS; brisk bleeding with haemodynamic compromise → MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33.**

findings: VERSION D — HE IS LYING ON HIS SIDE IN OBVIOUS PAIN

ACKNOWLEDGE IT BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: 'I CAN SEE YOU'RE IN A LOT OF PAIN. I'LL BE AS QUICK AS I CAN, AND I'LL GET YOU SOMETHING FOR THE PAIN.' Six minutes of questions to a man visibly suffering, with no acknowledgement and no analgesia, is a listed fail
SITE DECIDES IT — ASK WITH AN EITHER/OR

'IS IT IMMEDIATELY BESIDE YOUR BACK PASSAGE, OR IS IT HIGHER UP, IN THE MIDDLE, BETWEEN THE CHEEKS OF YOUR BOTTOM?' PATIENTS ARE IMPRECISE ABOUT THIS AREA — 'MY BUM HURTS' COVERS THE ANAL VERGE, ISCHIORECTAL FOSSA, NATAL CLEFT AND BUTTOCK. GIVE THE OPTIONS; DO NOT ASK AN OPEN QUESTION AND HOPE
THE MAP

MIDLINE NATAL CLEFT, ABOVE THE ANUS, HAIR-BEARING SKIN, PITS → PILONIDAL. IMMEDIATELY BESIDE THE ANUS, HOT AND TENDER → PERIANAL ABSCESS. A SMALL OPENING DISCHARGING FOR WEEKS → FISTULA. AT THE ANAL VERGE, TENSE AND PURPLE → THROMBOSED PILE. POSTERIOR MIDLINE TEAR → FISSURE. IRREGULAR ULCERATED BLEEDING LESION → ANAL CANCER
WHAT HE GIVES

THREE DAYS · SEVERE, CONSTANT, THROBBING, 8/10 · A TENDER LUMP IMMEDIATELY LATERAL TO THE ANAL VERGE · WORSE ON SITTING · FEVERS AND CHILLS · FIRST EPISODE · no discharge, no bleeding, NOT SPECIFICALLY WORSE ON DEFECATION, no constipation, nothing he can reduce
FEVER IS NOT A FORMALITY HERE

IT IS WHAT SEPARATES AN INFLAMED LUMP FROM AN ABSCESS. And 'WORSE ON DEFECATION' points at fissure, thrombosed pile or proctitis; 'WORSE ON SITTING' points at pilonidal or abscess. A PILONIDAL ABSCESS HAS NO RELATIONSHIP TO DEFECATION
THE PHOTOGRAPH IS RELEASED WHEN YOU REQUEST INSPECTION
'EXAMINER, I'D LIKE TO INSPECT THE PERIANAL AREA, WITH CONSENT AND A CHAPERONE.' The card: AN ERYTHEMATOUS, INDURATED, FLUCTUANT SWELLING ADJACENT TO THE ANAL VERGE
DESCRIBE BEFORE YOU DIAGNOSE

'I CAN SEE A TENDER-LOOKING, ERYTHEMATOUS, FLUCTUANT SWELLING IMMEDIATELY LATERAL TO THE ANAL VERGE, WITH SURROUNDING INDURATION AND NO VISIBLE PUNCTUM. THAT APPEARANCE, WITH HIS FEVER AND THE SITE HE DESCRIBED, IS A PERIANAL ABSCESS.' Describing first also PROTECTS YOU WHEN THE PHOTOGRAPH IS NOT WHAT YOU EXPECTED
DECLINE THE DIGITAL EXAMINATION — WITH A REASON

'GIVEN THAT APPEARANCE AND THE DEGREE OF PAIN I WOULD NOT PROCEED WITH A DIGITAL EXAMINATION — IT WOULD BE EXTREMELY PAINFUL AND IT WILL NOT CHANGE MY MANAGEMENT. THIS NEEDS DRAINAGE.' Examination under anaesthesia is the alternative
HOST FACTORS — two questions that change urgency

'ARE YOU DIABETIC? ARE YOU ON ANY MEDICINES THAT AFFECT YOUR IMMUNE SYSTEM — STEROIDS, CHEMOTHERAPY? DO YOU SMOKE?' Diabetes and immunosuppression raise the risk of RECURRENCE AND NECROTISING INFECTION — FOURNIER'S GANGRENE
THE EARLIER VERSIONS

A: ANAL PAIN, NO EXAMINATION — the history alone must separate abscess, fissure and pilonidal. B and C: DISCHARGE ON THE UNDERWEAR — ODOUR AND EXPRESSIBILITY DECIDE IT: 'IS IT OFFENSIVE-SMELLING? DOES IT COME OUT WHEN YOU PRESS? IS THERE A SMALL HOLE?' → FISTULA

dx: **PERIANAL ABSCESS — ARISING FROM AN INFECTED ANAL GLAND AT THE DENTATE LINE, the infection tracking outwards to just under the skin.** **Thrombosed external haemorrhoid and anal cancer are the two the AMC holds photographs for but has not yet used.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE SITE QUESTION, ASKED AS AN EITHER/OR. In the versions with no examination and no photograph THAT IS THE STATION. In Version D, the marks are in ACKNOWLEDGING THE PAIN AND OFFERING ANALGESIA, REQUESTING INSPECTION SO THE PHOTOGRAPH IS RELEASED, AND DECLINING THE DIGITAL EXAMINATION WITH A REASON.**

**ANTIBIOTICS ALONE ARE NOT TREATMENT — A POCKET OF PUS MUST BE DRAINED. INCISION AND DRAINAGE, usually under anaesthesia. Add antibiotics ONLY for SURROUNDING CELLULITIS, DIABETES, IMMUNOSUPPRESSION OR VALVULAR HEART DISEASE.** VERIFY. **'I'll give you some flucloxacillin and see you in a week' IS A STARRED FAIL.**

**THE EXPLANATION, SIMPLE AND HONEST: 'most likely you have a PERIANAL ABSCESS — an infection right next to the back passage that has formed A POCKET OF PUS. It starts in one of the tiny glands inside the back passage and TRACKS OUTWARDS to just under the skin. The important thing is that ANTIBIOTICS ON THEIR OWN WON'T FIX A POCKET OF PUS — IT NEEDS TO BE OPENED AND DRAINED, and that usually means A SMALL OPERATION, TODAY.'**

**WARN ABOUT THE FISTULA: ABOUT ONE THIRD OF PERIANAL ABSCESSES GO ON TO FORM A FISTULA — a small tunnel between the bowel and the skin — so ARRANGE FOLLOW-UP FOR THAT REASON. A RECURRENT ABSCESS OR A COMPLEX FISTULA SHOULD ALWAYS RAISE CROHN DISEASE.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP, WITH REASONS: INFECTION — PILONIDAL ABSCESS, lower because NOT IN THE MIDLINE OF THE NATAL CLEFT; infective proctitis · ANORECTAL — THROMBOSED EXTERNAL PILE, less likely because NOT PURPLE AND NOT AT THE VERGE ITSELF; ANAL FISSURE, less likely because the pain is CONSTANT, NOT SPECIFICALLY ON DEFECATION · GI — CROHN PERIANAL DISEASE, especially if it recurs · MALIGNANCY — ANAL CANCER, unlikely with this acute course, ALWAYS ON THE LIST · SKIN — infected sebaceous cyst, HIDRADENITIS.**

**THE OTHER EXPLANATIONS, IF THE PHOTOGRAPH SAYS OTHERWISE: PILONIDAL — 'in the crease between your cheeks, A HAIR CAN GROW INWARDS AND MAKE A SMALL PIT; when it becomes infected and fills with pus we call it an abscess. It needs draining, and later a proper operation to remove the pit.' FISTULA — 'a small TUNNEL between the inside of your bowel and the skin — what leaks out is BOWEL CONTENT, which is why it's offensive and keeps coming back.'**

**THROMBOSED PILE, IF THAT IS THE CARD: 'one of the small blood vessels at the edge of the back passage has CLOTTED OFF. IF WE'RE WITHIN ABOUT THREE DAYS, we can numb the area and TAKE THE CLOT OUT, which relieves the pain very quickly. Beyond that, it settles over a week or two with painkillers, warm baths and soft stools.'**

**ANAL CANCER — THE PHOTOGRAPH NOT YET SHOWN: an IRREGULAR, ULCERATED, EVERTED lesion bleeding on the surface that resembles nothing else. Usually SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA, STRONGLY HPV-ASSOCIATED, more common in people living with HIV and in MSM. URGENT REFERRAL AND BIOPSY; treated with CHEMORADIOTHERAPY rather than primary surgery in most cases. DO NOT FORCE IT INTO THE ABSCESS OR HAEMORRHOID BOXES.**

**RED FLAGS FOR DEEP OR NECROTISING INFECTION: FEVER WITH RIGORS · SPREADING REDNESS · PAIN OUT OF PROPORTION · CREPITUS OR SKIN DISCOLOURATION — FOURNIER'S GANGRENE, especially in DIABETES OR IMMUNOSUPPRESSION. URGENT SURGICAL ASSESSMENT.** **SA: a same-day discussion with the on-call surgical registrar; a small pointing abscess may be drained locally by a credentialled practitioner, anything deep, extensive, or in a diabetic goes to theatre; suspected Fournier's → MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 or RFDS.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP, each with why it is less likely — pilonidal, thrombosed pile, fissure, Crohn's, ANAL CANCER, skin conditions.**

findings: THE A/B STEM IS IDENTICAL — WHAT SEPARATES THEM IS WHAT YOU PROBE OUT

VERSION A HANDS YOU CONSTIPATION AND NOTHING ELSE → ACUTE DIVERTICULITIS. VERSION B HANDS YOU CONSTIPATION, THEN 5 kg OF UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS OVER TWO MONTHS AND BLOOD IN THE STOOL IF YOU ASK, and a SCREENING KIT RECEIVED BUT NOT RETURNED → COLORECTAL CANCER
NO PHYSICAL EXAMINATION TASK
EVERYTHING YOU CONCLUDE MUST COME OUT OF THE HISTORY. The vitals are normal — BP 128/78, HR 78, RR 16, T 36.8 — so there is no systemic shortcut
THE SINGLE MOST COMMON REASON CANDIDATES LOSE REASONING MARKS

WHEN A POSITIVE FINDING IS HANDED TO YOU AND YOU MOVE STRAIGHT TO THE NEXT QUESTION, THAT IS SCORED AS POOR CLINICAL REASONING. CONSTIPATION IS NOT AN ENDPOINT — IT IS A DOOR: 'HOW LONG? ARE THE STOOLS HARD? IS IT PAINFUL OR DIFFICULT TO PASS THEM?'
QUANTIFY EVERY RED FLAG
'YES, I'VE LOST SOME WEIGHT' → 'HOW MANY KILOS? OVER WHAT PERIOD? WAS THAT INTENTIONAL — DIETING OR EXERCISE?' 5 kg IN TWO MONTHS UNINTENTIONAL IS SIGNIFICANT; 3 kg IN A MONTH WHILE DIETING IS NOT
RED FLAGS START AT 3:30 WHATEVER ELSE IS UNFINISHED

WEIGHT LOSS · APPETITE · LUMPS · FRESH OR BLACK BLOOD · CHANGE IN BOWEL HABIT · FAMILY HISTORY WITH THE AGE · SCREENING KIT · PAIN WAKING HIM AT NIGHT. If you are still exploring the pain at 3:00, ABANDON DETAIL AND MOVE
TWO CHRONIC-PAIN ADD-ONS TO SICORA

'HAS THE PAIN EVER WOKEN YOU AT NIGHT?' — night pain anywhere is a warning sign. 'HOW IS THIS PAIN AFFECTING YOUR DAY-TO-DAY LIFE?' And two named aggravators: FOOD — biliary and peptic; POSITION — pancreatitis
THE HERNIA QUESTION IS NEVER SKIPPED

'HAVE YOU NOTICED ANY LUMP OR SWELLING IN YOUR GROIN?' — asked in EVERY abdominal station, both sexes, every site. AMC LOVES THIS ONE. Then scrotal pain or swelling, and three 'other' questions: RASH, INJURY, RACING HEART
SAY THE GROUP NAMES OUT LOUD BEFORE YOU ASK

'Now some general bowel questions.' · 'These next ones are the important warning-sign questions.' · 'A few about the waterworks.' · 'A couple about your groin and private parts.' THE CHEAPEST WAY TO DEMONSTRATE CLINICAL REASONING — STRUCTURE THAT IS NOT AUDIBLE DOES NOT EXIST

DIFFERENTIALS ARE MARKED FOR SPREAD, NOT LENGTH

dx: **VERSION A — ACUTE DIVERTICULITIS: inflammation of a pouch herniating through the colonic wall, ALMOST ALWAYS SIGMOID — long-standing constipation, hard stools, LLQ pain, NO RED FLAGS. VERSION B — COLORECTAL CANCER: age 50, one month of pain, UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS, FRESH RECTAL BLEEDING.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: PROBE EVERY POSITIVE, CONVERT EVERY DENIAL INTO A SECOND QUESTION, AND LET THE FINDINGS — NOT THE LABEL YOU WALKED IN WITH — CHOOSE THE DIAGNOSIS. Candidates fail not because they don't know diverticulitis, but because they HEAR 'LEFT LOWER QUADRANT + CONSTIPATION', STOP LISTENING, AND NEVER ASK THE RED-FLAG BLOCK.**

**VERSION A — THE REASSURANCE MUST BE EARNED: 'before I tell you what I think this is, I want to be clear about WHAT I HAVE RULED OUT. You are NOT LOSING WEIGHT, you have NO BLOOD in your bowel motions, your bowel habit HAS NOT CHANGED and there is NO BOWEL CANCER IN YOUR FAMILY. That is genuinely reassuring, and IT IS WHY I AM COMFORTABLE CALLING THIS DIVERTICULITIS rather than something more serious.'**

**VERSION B — NAMING CANCER: 'Gary, during our conversation I was thinking about a number of conditions, and I AM CONCERNED ABOUT THE POSSIBILITY OF A BOWEL CANCER. I want to explain why I am thinking that, and what we do next.' Then the reasons: AGE, DURATION, UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS, RECTAL BLEEDING.**

**NEVER SAY 'A NASTY GROWTH' — a course-provider habit that has ended up in the AMC's OWN LIST OF THINGS NOT TO DO. Role-players understand the word cancer. SAY IT ONCE, THEN GIVE REASONS AND A PLAN.**

**DIVERTICULOSIS VERSUS DIVERTICULITIS — worth a mark in front of the patient: POUCHES ALONE ARE -OSIS; POUCHES WITH PAIN AND TENDERNESS ARE -ITIS. Telling a patient in pain he has 'diverticulosis' is a listed error.**

**DELIVERING THE DIFFERENTIALS, BY GROUP WITH A REASON: 'I was also thinking about URINARY causes — infection or a stone in the tubes — but you have NO BURNING, NO INCREASED FREQUENCY AND NO BLOOD IN YOUR URINE.' That single sentence SCORES MORE THAN TEN UNEXPLAINED WORDS. GI — diverticulitis or cancer, obstruction, IBD, ischaemic colitis · KUB — UTI, ureteric colic · HERNIA AND GENITAL — inguinal hernia, epididymo-orchitis · OTHER — shingles, trauma, mesenteric ischaemia.**

**ACUTE UNCOMPLICATED DIVERTICULITIS: CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST CONFIRMS — the one investigation if forced to give one · PARACETAMOL · CLEAR FLUIDS AND A SOFT LOW-RESIDUE DIET — FIBRE REINTRODUCED AFTER, NOT DURING · ANTIBIOTICS SELECTIVELY, NOT AUTOMATICALLY — well, immunocompetent, uncomplicated disease can be managed WITHOUT them with review in 48–72 hours; give them for immunocompromise, comorbidity, SYSTEMIC FEATURES, or failure to improve — AMOXICILLIN + CLAVULANATE 875+125 mg 12-HOURLY FOR 5 DAYS.** VERIFY.
**COLONOSCOPY 6–8 WEEKS AFTER RESOLUTION where malignancy has not been excluded, and after any complicated episode. VERSION B: FBC AND IRON STUDIES, URGENT COLONOSCOPY, STAGING CT.**

**CORRECTION — SCREENING AGE: the source says 'from 50'. The NBCSP mails a free iFOBT every two years to people 50–74, AND SINCE 1 JULY 2024 PEOPLE AGED 45–49 CAN REQUEST A KIT. If challenged: 'screening is two-yearly from 50 to 74, with opt-in access from 45 — BUT SCREENING IS FOR ASYMPTOMATIC PEOPLE; he is symptomatic, so an unreturned kit does not change my plan for colonoscopy.'** VERIFY.

**SUMMARISE WHATEVER IS UNFINISHED.**

**THE DIAGNOSIS WITH REASONS — Version A: THE EARNED REASSURANCE, LISTING WHAT YOU RULED OUT, then DIVERTICULITIS, explained as an inflamed pouch. Version B: 'I AM CONCERNED ABOUT THE POSSIBILITY OF A BOWEL CANCER' — once, then reasons.**
**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP — GI, KUB, HERNIA AND GENITAL, OTHER — each with the reason it is less likely.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: REFUSING DIAGNOSTIC MOMENTUM, OUT LOUD. PROBE EVERY POSITIVE, CONVERT EVERY DENIAL INTO A SECOND QUESTION, AND LET THE FINDINGS CHOOSE THE DIAGNOSIS.**

**THE SCRIPT: 'Jimmy, I know the pain is on the left and I DID THINK ABOUT DIVERTICULITIS. That scar tissue is THE COMMONEST CAUSE OF A BLOCKAGE.'** **Without sounding accusatory about the surgery.**

'I HAVEN'T PASSED ANY URINE FOR TWO DAYS.' TREAT THIS AS AN INDEPENDENT EMERGENCY. Ask about LEG SWELLING, DROWSINESS, and — in a 60-year-old man — POOR STREAM, HESITANCY, SUPRAPUBIC DISCOMFORT: OBSTRUCTIVE UROPATHY IS REVERSIBLE IN MINUTES WITH A CATHETER

**DEFINITIONS WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD: ABSOLUTE CONSTIPATION IS NO STOOL AND NO FLATUS — THAT IS THE OBSTRUCTION DEFINITION. ANURIA IS ESSENTIALLY NO URINE OUTPUT AND IS A DIFFERENT, AND ARGUABLY MORE URGENT, PROBLEM FROM THE CONSTIPATION.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: CONVERTING A REQUEST FOR A PRESCRIPTION INTO AN ARRANGED EMERGENCY TRANSFER — AND ARRANGING IT YOURSELF. ON A TELEHEALTH CALL WITH AN ANURIC, VOMITING 60-YEAR-OLD, ADVICE IS NOT A PLAN.**

The second, AND HONESTLY THE ONE THAT WORRIES ME MORE, is that you haven't passed urine for two days. stem: Mrs Margaret Doyle, 72, not present, was diagnosed with alcohol-related cirrhosis two years ago and has not consumed alcohol since. Her husband, Brian, has come because he has observed memory and behaviour change; she refused to attend. He has authority to discuss her care.
tasks: Take a focused history from the husband (6 minutes)
Explain the likely diagnosis and the differentials, with your reasons
findings: THE PATIENT IS NOT IN THE ROOM

A THIRD-PARTY HISTORY FROM HER HUSBAND, who has authority. DO NOT ASK FOR CONSENT — BUT SAY ONE SENTENCE THAT SHOWS YOU NOTICED: 'I UNDERSTAND YOU HAVE YOUR WIFE'S AUTHORITY TO DISCUSS HER CARE, THANK YOU.' And DO NOT ASK THE HUSBAND FOR HER HAEMODYNAMIC STABILITY — IT LOOKS LIKE A SCRIPT RUNNING WITHOUT THOUGHT
THE LINE IN THE STEM THAT CANDIDATES BELIEVE

'SHE HAS NOT CONSUMED ALCOHOL SINCE.' CANDIDATES THEREFORE DO NOT ASK. THE HUSBAND, WHEN ASKED, SAYS HE THINKS SHE IS DRINKING AGAIN — HE HAS FOUND BEER CANS HIDDEN IN THE CUPBOARD. THAT SINGLE FINDING IS THE PRECIPITANT, THE EXPLANATION AND THE MANAGEMENT PLAN. IT COSTS TWO SECONDS AND IT IS THE ENTIRE CASE
HOW TO RE-ASK WITHOUT CONTRADICTING THE STEM

'I KNOW FROM THE NOTES THAT SHE STOPPED DRINKING WHEN SHE WAS DIAGNOSED. CAN I JUST CONFIRM WITH YOU — AS FAR AS YOU ARE AWARE, IS SHE DRINKING ANY ALCOHOL AT ALL AT THE MOMENT?' → 'WELL — I THINK SHE MIGHT BE. I FOUND A FEW CANS OF BEER IN THE CUPBOARD'
EXPLORE WHAT HE ACTUALLY MEANS — offer three options

'IS IT THAT SHE DOES NOT REMEMBER THINGS, OR THAT SHE DOES NOT RECOGNISE YOU, OR THAT SHE IS BEHAVING ODDLY?' OFFERING CONCRETE OPTIONS IS NOT LEADING — IT SEPARATES FORGETFULNESS, DISORIENTATION AND DISINHIBITION, WHICH POINT IN DIFFERENT DIRECTIONS
THE EARLIEST RUNG — SLEEP REVERSAL

'HOW IS HER SLEEP — IS SHE SLEEPING IN THE DAY AND AWAKE AT NIGHT?' ENCEPHALOPATHY RUNS SLEEP REVERSAL → MEMORY → CONFUSION → SLURRED SPEECH AND ATAXIA → COMA. EXPECTING AN UNCONSCIOUS PATIENT IS WHY CANDIDATES MISS THIS DIAGNOSIS
WHAT HE GIVES

MEMORY IMPAIRMENT · DAYTIME SLEEPINESS, AWAKE AT NIGHT · INTERMITTENT CONFUSION OVER RECENT WEEKS · ABDOMINAL DISTENSION · BEER CANS IN THE CUPBOARD. No fever, no abdominal pain, no haematemesis or melaena, no fall in urine output, no focal neurology
THE FOUR CIRRHOSIS QUESTIONS

WHEN DIAGNOSED · WHAT TREATMENT · IS SHE TAKING IT AS PRESCRIBED · REGULAR FOLLOW-UP. SHE HAS MEMORY PROBLEMS — ASKING WHETHER SHE IS RELIABLY TAKING HER MEDICATION IS A CLINICALLY POINTED QUESTION HERE, AND THE EXAMINER WILL HEAR THE DIFFERENCE
THE SIX TRIGGERS OF DECOMPENSATION — all six, every time

ALCOHOL · INFECTION · MEDICATIONS — SEDATIVES, OPIOIDS, NEW DRUGS · CONSTIPATION · BLEEDING — HAEMATEMESIS, MELAENA · DEHYDRATION — including diuretics. ALCOHOL IS THE ONE EVERYBODY ASKS; THE PASS IS MADE UP OF THE OTHER FIVE AS WELL
COMPLICATIONS — ask them all, don't stop at encephalopathy

JAUNDICE, ITCH, BRUISING · ENCEPHALOPATHY · SBP — abdominal pain, fever · HCC — WEIGHT LOSS, APPETITE · HEPATORENAL — 'ANY DECREASE IN THE AMOUNT OF URINE SHE PASSES?' · HEPATOPULMONARY — breathlessness · VARICEAL BLEEDING
THE GERIATRIC SCREEN BELONGS HERE

FALLS · SUPPORT AT HOME · DIET · DAILY ACTIVITIES · MOOD. FALLS MATTER MORE THAN USUAL — COAGULOPATHY TURNS A SIMPLE FALL INTO AN INTRACRANIAL BLEED, AND A SUBDURAL HAEMATOMA IS ON YOUR DIFFERENTIAL FOR HER CONFUSION

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: RE-ASK THE QUESTION THE STEM HAS ALREADY ANSWERED. THE GENERAL RULE THIS CASE TEACHES: IF A FACT IN THE STEM IS CENTRAL TO YOUR DIAGNOSIS, RECONFIRM IT — STEMS ARE SOMETIMES WRITTEN PRECISELY SO THAT THE ROLE-PLAYER CAN CONTRADICT THEM. Do not re-ask everything — ONLY THE FACTS THAT WOULD CHANGE YOUR ANSWER.**
**FIVE BOXES THAT STRUCTURE ANY CIRRHOSIS STATION — NAME EACH OUT LOUD: 1 COMPLAINT · 2 CIRRHOSIS HISTORY — the four questions · 3 COMPLICATIONS · 4 THE SIX TRIGGERS · 5 GERIATRIC SCREEN.**

**TO THE HUSBAND, PLAINLY: 'the most likely explanation is a condition called HEPATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY. When the liver is badly scarred, IT CAN'T CLEAR TOXINS FROM THE BLOOD PROPERLY, and those toxins affect the brain — which is WHY SHE'S SLEEPING IN THE DAY, AWAKE AT NIGHT, FORGETFUL AND CONFUSED. It usually has A TRIGGER, and from what you've told me, THE MOST LIKELY TRIGGER IS THAT SHE HAS STARTED DRINKING AGAIN. THE GOOD NEWS IS THAT IT IS OFTEN REVERSIBLE WHEN THE TRIGGER IS TREATED.'**

**THE REASONS: THE REVERSED SLEEP PATTERN · THE MEMORY CHANGE · THE INTERMITTENT CONFUSION · THE ABDOMINAL DISTENSION suggesting ascites · AND THE BEER CANS — the precipitant. Say the NEGATIVES too: no fever, no bleeding, no fall in urine, no focal neurology.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS IN TWO GROUPS — NOT A FLAT LIST OF TWELVE: OTHER COMPLICATIONS OF CIRRHOSIS — SBP, HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA, HEPATORENAL AND HEPATOPULMONARY SYNDROME · THE CAUSES OF DELIRIUM — SEPSIS, MEDICATION OR WITHDRAWAL, INTRACRANIAL PATHOLOGY INCLUDING TUMOUR AND SUBDURAL HAEMATOMA, DEMENTIA (Alzheimer, Lewy body), and METABOLIC — hypoglycaemia, electrolytes, hypothyroidism, hypoxia, urinary retention, constipation.**

**WHY SUBDURAL MATTERS HERE: A COAGULOPATHIC PATIENT WHO FALLS MAY HAVE A SUBDURAL HAEMATOMA — hence the falls question in the geriatric screen and CT BRAIN IF THERE ARE FOCAL SIGNS, A FALL, OR THE CONFUSION DOES NOT IMPROVE.**

**MANAGEMENT: LACTULOSE TITRATED TO TWO OR THREE SOFT STOOLS A DAY · RIFAXIMIN ADDED FOR RECURRENT EPISODES · TREAT THE PRECIPITANT · exclude HYPOGLYCAEMIA — a failing liver cannot maintain glucose · septic screen and DIAGNOSTIC PARACENTESIS if ascites is confirmed · AVOID SEDATIVES AND OPIOIDS.** VERIFY doses.

**THE ALCOHOL CONVERSATION WITH BOTH OF THEM, WITHOUT JUDGEMENT: ABSTINENCE IS THE SINGLE INTERVENTION THAT CHANGES THE TRAJECTORY · THIAMINE · nutritional support · brief intervention and referral to DASSA · and SHE IS REFUSING TO ATTEND — ask what would help her come in, and whether her husband is safe and coping. WHERE CAPACITY IS IN DOUBT, DECISIONS ARE MADE UNDER AN ADVANCE CARE DIRECTIVE BY A SUBSTITUTE DECISION-MAKER.**

**A NORMAL LFT DOES NOT REASSURE IN ADVANCED CIRRHOSIS — little functioning liver is left. And if she has just stopped drinking again, watch for WITHDRAWAL AND WERNICKE ENCEPHALOPATHY — THIAMINE BEFORE GLUCOSE.** **SA: DASSA and ADIS; Country Health Connect for community nursing and palliative support; hepatology at the RAH; MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33; TIS National 131 450.**

**NAME IT — HEPATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY — in plain words: the liver can't clear toxins, they affect the brain, it usually has a trigger, and the trigger is the drinking. OFTEN REVERSIBLE.**
**THE REASONS, then THE DIFFERENTIALS IN TWO GROUPS — other cirrhosis complications, then causes of delirium, including SUBDURAL AFTER A FALL.**
**The next steps briefly — bloods including glucose, a septic screen, lactulose, treat the trigger — AND AN ALCOHOL CONVERSATION WITH BOTH OF THEM. Ask what would help her agree to come in.**

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with bruising and swelling of his legs. 'I started drinking again about six months ago — about five glasses of wine a day. And my tummy is getting bigger.' Results: albumin low · platelets low · INR raised · haemoglobin low · WCC raised with neutrophilia.
tasks: Take a focused history (4 minutes)
Interpret the examination findings card
Explain the results and your diagnosis
findings: THE RESULTS ARE ON THE STEM
ALBUMIN LOW · PLATELETS LOW · INR RAISED · HAEMOGLOBIN LOW · WCC RAISED WITH NEUTROPHILIA · LFTs deranged. EXPLAIN EACH ONE IN PLAIN ENGLISH BEFORE THE DIAGNOSIS — IT IS A TASK IN ITS OWN RIGHT
THE EXAMINATION CARD YOU ARE HANDED

FEVER · JAUNDICE · ASCITES — 'ascites present' or POSITIVE SHIFTING DULLNESS · HEPATOMEGALY, NON-TENDER · PAROTID ENLARGEMENT. USE EVERY ONE IN YOUR REASONING OUT LOUD — FINDINGS YOU ARE GIVEN BUT NEVER MENTION ARE MARKS YOU NEVER COLLECT
WHAT HE GIVES — THE TRIGGER

'I STARTED DRINKING AGAIN ABOUT SIX MONTHS AGO — ABOUT FIVE GLASSES OF WINE A DAY. AND MY TUMMY IS GETTING BIGGER.' QUANTIFY IT IN STANDARD DRINKS — a glass of wine is roughly 1.5 standard drinks, so five glasses is 7–8 a day, over 50 a week against an NHMRC limit of 10
THE STEP THAT GETS YOU TO SBP
'LOOKING AT THE TYPE OF WHITE CELL, THE NEUTROPHILS ARE RAISED, AND THAT POINTS TO A BACTERIAL INFECTION.' Candidates explain the white count and stop
THE BRUISING AND THE SWELLING ARE THE LIVER, NOT THE LEGS
LOW ALBUMIN → LEG SWELLING AND ASCITES. HIGH INR AND LOW PLATELETS → THE BRUISING. Say the link out loud — it is what turns a list of results into an explanation
ASK ABOUT FEVER AND ABDOMINAL PAIN — BUT SBP MAY HAVE NEITHER
'ANY FEVER OR SHIVERS? ANY PAIN IN YOUR TUMMY? ANY DIARRHOEA?' SBP CAN PRESENT WITH ONLY ENCEPHALOPATHY, AKI OR A GENERAL DECLINE — ANY CIRRHOTIC WHO DETERIORATES IS PARACENTESED
STILL RUN THE COMPLICATIONS AND TRIGGERS

ENCEPHALOPATHY — sleep reversal, confusion · VARICEAL BLEEDING — haematemesis, melaena, WHICH ALSO EXPLAINS THE LOW HAEMOGLOBIN · HEPATORENAL — urine output · HCC — weight loss · the other five triggers: infection, medications, constipation, bleeding, dehydration
PAROTID ENLARGEMENT IS A CLUE ABOUT ALCOHOL, NOT ABOUT CIRRHOSIS
PAROTID ENLARGEMENT AND DUPUYTREN'S CONTRACTURE INDICATE CHRONIC ALCOHOL USE RATHER THAN CIRRHOSIS ITSELF — SAY SO IF ASKED
DO NOT LET NORMAL-LOOKING ENZYMES REASSURE
IN ADVANCED CIRRHOSIS ENZYMES MAY BE NORMAL OR ONLY MILDLY RAISED BECAUSE THERE IS LITTLE FUNCTIONING LIVER TISSUE LEFT. The low albumin and high INR are the real markers of liver failure
NO JARGON TO THE PATIENT
'SYNTHETIC FUNCTION' AND 'PORTAL HYPERTENSION' SAID TO THE PATIENT LOSE MARKS. PROTEINS, CLOTTING FACTORS, FLUID IN THE ABDOMEN

dx: **SPONTANEOUS BACTERIAL PERITONITIS ON A BACKGROUND OF DECOMPENSATED ALCOHOL-RELATED CIRRHOSIS, PRECIPITATED BY A RETURN TO ALCOHOL.** **SBP is BACTERIAL INFECTION OF ASCITIC FLUID WITH NO SURGICAL SOURCE. CONFIRMED BY DIAGNOSTIC PARACENTESIS — ASCITIC NEUTROPHILS AT OR ABOVE 250 CELLS PER CUBIC MILLIMETRE.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: NAME THE SPECIFIC COMPLICATION, NOT THE GENERAL STATE — and JUSTIFY IT FROM FOUR SEPARATE PIECES OF EVIDENCE: THE FEVER, THE NEUTROPHILIA, THE ASCITES ON EXAMINATION, AND THE RETURN TO ALCOHOL AS THE TRIGGER. 'HE HAS DECOMPENSATED CIRRHOSIS' DESCRIBES THE PATIENT WITHOUT DIAGNOSING HIM.**

**EXPLAINING THE RESULTS, ONE LINE EACH: ALBUMIN — 'the MAIN PROTEIN YOUR LIVER MAKES, and yours is low — your liver is no longer producing proteins properly' · INR — 'your liver makes the factors that CLOT YOUR BLOOD; it has stopped producing them, so YOUR BLOOD TAKES LONGER TO CLOT' · PLATELETS — 'tiny particles that help clotting, and they're low' · HAEMOGLOBIN — 'carries oxygen, and it's low' · WHITE CELLS — 'part of your immune system, raised, which SUGGESTS AN INFECTION' · NEUTROPHILS — 'that type is raised, which POINTS TO A BACTERIAL INFECTION.'**
**LINK THEM: 'the low protein is WHY YOUR LEGS ARE SWOLLEN AND FLUID IS COLLECTING IN YOUR TUMMY. The clotting problem and low platelets are WHY YOU'RE BRUISING.'**

**THE DIAGNOSIS IN ONE BREATH: 'putting all of that together, I am suspecting a condition called SPONTANEOUS BACTERIAL PERITONITIS. That means AN INFECTION IN THE FLUID THAT HAS COLLECTED IN YOUR ABDOMEN because your liver is not working properly. My reasons are: YOU HAVE A FEVER; your WHITE CELLS AND PARTICULARLY YOUR NEUTROPHILS ARE RAISED; on examination you have FLUID IN YOUR ABDOMEN; and you have a clear reason for your liver to have deteriorated — YOU HAVE STARTED DRINKING AGAIN.'**

**IF THE EXAMINER PUSHES: 'this is DECOMPENSATED CIRRHOSIS PRECIPITATED BY SBP AND BY A RETURN TO ALCOHOL' — NAMING BOTH THE COMPLICATION AND THE TRIGGER. 'Decompensated cirrhosis' IS NOT WRONG, BUT IT IS NOT ENOUGH.**

**WHY THE PLATELETS ARE LOW: HYPERSPLENISM FROM PORTAL HYPERTENSION. WHY THE HAEMOGLOBIN IS LOW: BLOOD LOSS — ASK ABOUT VARICES — POOR NUTRITION, OR CHRONIC DISEASE. WHY THE ENZYMES MAY BE UNIMPRESSIVE: LITTLE FUNCTIONING LIVER LEFT.**

**MANAGEMENT: DIAGNOSTIC PARACENTESIS FOR CELL COUNT, CULTURE AND ALBUMIN · IV THIRD-GENERATION CEPHALOSPORIN · IV ALBUMIN TO REDUCE THE RISK OF HEPATORENAL SYNDROME · SECONDARY ANTIBIOTIC PROPHYLAXIS AFTERWARDS · treat the precipitant — ALCOHOL: complete abstinence, THIAMINE, nutrition, brief intervention, DASSA · watch for WITHDRAWAL.** VERIFY agent, dose and prophylaxis locally.

**THE DIFFERENTIALS: OTHER CIRRHOSIS COMPLICATIONS — hepatorenal syndrome, variceal bleed as the cause of the anaemia, hepatic encephalopathy, HCC · OTHER SOURCES OF SEPSIS — urinary, chest, skin, SECONDARY PERITONITIS from a perforation — a SURGICAL source changes everything · ALCOHOLIC HEPATITIS — fever, jaundice, tender hepatomegaly and a neutrophilia can mimic it · CARDIAC OR RENAL causes of oedema.**

**ALCOHOL IS THE SINGLE INTERVENTION THAT CHANGES THE TRAJECTORY. Raise it WITHOUT JUDGEMENT, AFTER the diagnosis, and offer support. AVOID NSAIDs — they precipitate hepatorenal syndrome — and sedatives.** **SA: MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 if he deteriorates; hepatology at the RAH; DASSA; Country Health Connect; TIS National 131 450.**
plan: **WIPE, open question, and respond to the drinking without judgement: 'thank you for being honest with me about that — it helps me work out what's going on.'**
**EXPLORE: the bruising — where, how easily · the leg swelling — both legs, how long · the tummy — how fast has it grown?**
**THE FOUR CIRRHOSIS QUESTIONS: when diagnosed · treatment · taking it · follow-up.** Then **QUANTIFY THE ALCOHOL — how many glasses, how big, how long — convert to standard drinks.**
**COMPLICATIONS — SBP: FEVER OR SHIVERS · ABDOMINAL PAIN · DIARRHOEA. ENCEPHALOPATHY: sleep, confusion, forgetfulness. BLEEDING: VOMITED BLOOD · BLACK STOOLS.**
**HEPATORENAL — passing less urine · HCC — weight loss, appetite · HEPATOPULMONARY — breathlessness · jaundice, itch.**
**THE OTHER TRIGGERS: infection elsewhere · NEW MEDICINES, PAINKILLERS, ANTI-INFLAMMATORIES · constipation · dehydration.**
**SADMA · social — who is at home · a one-line summary.**
**INTERPRET THE CARD — EVERY FINDING, ALOUD: fever · jaundice · ascites / shifting dullness · non-tender hepatomegaly · PAROTID ENLARGEMENT — a sign of chronic alcohol use.**
**EXPLAIN THE RESULTS, ONE LINE EACH, IN PLAIN ENGLISH — albumin, INR, platelets, haemoglobin, white cells, AND THE NEUTROPHILS.**
**LINK THEM TO HIS SYMPTOMS: low protein → swelling and fluid; clotting factors and platelets → bruising.**
**NAME SBP IN ONE BREATH, WITH THE FOUR REASONS — fever, neutrophilia, ascites, return to alcohol.**
**THE DIFFERENTIALS BRIEFLY — hepatorenal, variceal bleed, encephalopathy, other sepsis, SECONDARY PERITONITIS, alcoholic hepatitis.**
**THE PLAN: admission, A SMALL SAMPLE OF THE TUMMY FLUID to confirm, IV antibiotics and albumin — and the alcohol, offered as support, not a lecture.**
pefe: **Do now: vital signs including temperature · blood glucose · FBE, UEC, LFT, ALBUMIN, INR, CRP, BLOOD CULTURES · DIAGNOSTIC PARACENTESIS — cell count, culture in blood culture bottles at the bedside, albumin for the SAAG — THE TEST THAT MAKES OR EXCLUDES SBP.**
**Threshold: ASCITIC NEUTROPHILS ≥250 CELLS/mm³ = SBP. A POLYMICROBIAL CULTURE, very high protein or low glucose raises SECONDARY PERITONITIS — a surgical source — and needs imaging.**

**Treatment: IV THIRD-GENERATION CEPHALOSPORIN · IV ALBUMIN — commonly on day 1 and day 3 — to reduce HEPATORENAL SYNDROME · SECONDARY PROPHYLAXIS after the episode · treat the precipitant.** VERIFY agent, dose and albumin regimen against Therapeutic Guidelines.

**Then: septic screen — urine, chest X-ray · LIVER ULTRASOUND WITH DOPPLER — portal vein, focal lesions · gastroscopy for varices · HCC SURVEILLANCE six-monthly · ascites — salt restriction, spironolactone ± frusemide once infection is treated · THIAMINE, nutrition, alcohol support.**

**Do not miss: HEPATORENAL SYNDROME — watch creatinine and urine output · VARICEAL BLEEDING as the cause of the low haemoglobin · HEPATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY triggered by the infection · ALCOHOL WITHDRAWAL during admission · SECONDARY PERITONITIS.**

**Avoid: STOPPING AT 'DECOMPENSATED CIRRHOSIS' · NSAIDs · SEDATIVES · LARGE-VOLUME PARACENTESIS WITHOUT ALBUMIN COVER · aggressive diuresis during infection and AKI risk · a lecture about alcohol before the diagnosis.**
**SA: admit; MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 for a deteriorating patient; hepatology and transplant assessment at the RAH; DASSA and ADIS for alcohol; Country Health Connect; PATS; TIS National 131 450.**

stem: Mary Bennett, 40, presents with abdominal pain.
tasks: Take a focused history (6 minutes)
Explain your most likely diagnosis to the patient
Explain your differential diagnoses to the patient
findings: BOTH VERSIONS CAN BE DIAGNOSED FROM THE OPENING STATEMENT

RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT PAIN, JUST BACK FROM SOUTH-EAST ASIA. THE STATION IS NOT TESTING WHETHER YOU KNOW HEPATITIS A. IT IS TESTING WHETHER A TRAVELLER IN FRONT OF YOU TRIGGERS A FULL, STRUCTURED TRAVEL HISTORY
THE TRAVEL HISTORY IS A SCORED BOX ON ITS OWN

A CANDIDATE WHO REACHES THE CORRECT DIAGNOSIS BUT NEVER ASKS ABOUT BLOOD EXPOSURE, TATTOOS, INSECT BITES OR PRE-TRAVEL VACCINATION IS FAILED ON HISTORY TAKING. The same rule applies to ANY station with a traveller — fever, rash, joint pain, cough, diarrhoea, paediatric
SIGNPOST IT, THEN RUN A TO G WITHOUT PAUSING

'I WOULD NOW LIKE TO ASK ABOUT YOUR TRIP IN DETAIL' — EARNS THE BOX BEFORE YOU ASK A SINGLE QUESTION. A — WHERE, HOW LONG, ACTIVITIES · B — BUSHWALKING, INSECT OR TICK BITES · C — CONTACT WITH ANYONE UNWELL OR ANIMALS · D — DRUGS · E — EXPOSURE: TATTOOS, PIERCINGS, TRANSFUSIONS, MEDICAL OR DENTAL PROCEDURES · F — FOOD AND WATER · G — SAW A GP BEFORE LEAVING, VACCINES, MALARIA TABLETS
WHEN SHE VOLUNTEERS STREET FOOD AT F — DO NOT STOP
'THAT IS VERY HELPFUL AND I WILL COME BACK TO IT.' THEN FINISH G. PREMATURE CLOSURE HERE IS THE COMMONEST SINGLE REASON CANDIDATES LOSE THE TRAVEL BOX DESPITE NAMING HEPATITIS A
FEVER IS THE QUESTION YOU NEVER SKIP

FEVER CONVERTS PAIN PLUS JAUNDICE INTO CHARCOT'S TRIAD AND THE DIAGNOSIS BECOMES ASCENDING CHOLANGITIS — A SURGICAL EMERGENCY. Here the answer is NO — BUT YOU ONLY EARN THE MARK BY ASKING. ASK IT IN THE GI BLOCK BY 3:30 SO TIME CANNOT SQUEEZE IT OUT
RADIATION MATTERS HERE — ask it deliberately
SHOULDER-TIP → DIAPHRAGMATIC IRRITATION FROM GALLBLADDER OR LIVER. THROUGH TO THE BACK → PANCREAS. Both change your differential ordering
THE HEPATITIS SYMPTOM CLUSTER — one run

YELLOWING OF THE SKIN OR THE WHITES OF THE EYES · ITCHING · DARK URINE · PALE STOOLS. Ask about THE WHITES OF THE EYES, NOT JUST 'YELLOW SKIN' — sclera shows at lower bilirubin, and patients with darker skin often notice the sclera or palms first
THE RED FLAG SCREEN — even when it's obviously infective
WEIGHT LOSS · APPETITE · LUMPS · TIREDNESS · FAMILY HISTORY OF BOWEL, LIVER, PANCREAS OR STOMACH CANCER. SKIPPING IT BECAUSE 'IT'S OBVIOUSLY INFECTIVE' IS A LISTED FAIL
ABP FIT NO SEX — and don't re-ask what the travel block covered

SAY IT INSTEAD: 'I HAVE ALREADY COVERED BLOOD EXPOSURE, PIERCINGS, FOOD AND TRAVEL IN YOUR TRIP HISTORY, SO I JUST NEED ALCOHOL, ANTIBIOTICS, YOUR OCCUPATION AND A SEXUAL HISTORY.' SHOWS THE STRUCTURE IS DELIBERATE AND SAVES FORTY SECONDS
THE VERSION B VARIANT — no travel, AST and ALT 800

THE ROLE-PLAYER VOLUNTEERS, USUALLY LATE, THAT HE HAS BEEN CARING FOR A NEIGHBOUR'S UNWELL TODDLER WITH DIARRHOEA. CLOSE THE LOOP EXPLICITLY — 'HEPATITIS A SPREADS BY THE FAECAL–ORAL ROUTE, AND A YOUNG CHILD WITH DIARRHOEA IS A CLASSIC SOURCE.' SAY 'THIS IS A HEPATOCELLULAR PATTERN' BEFORE NAMING A DIAGNOSIS — A MARK ON ITS OWN

dx: **ACUTE VIRAL HEPATITIS, MOST LIKELY HEPATITIS A — HEPATOCELLULAR PATTERN — acquired from contaminated food or water overseas.** **Inflammation of the liver parenchyma producing JAUNDICE, RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT PAIN AND MALAISE, usually SELF-LIMITING. FAECAL–ORAL, INCUBATION ROUGHLY 2–6 WEEKS, NO CHRONIC CARRIAGE.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: A COMPLETE TRAVEL HISTORY — AND, HAVING FOUND STREET FOOD AT LETTER F, KEEPING GOING TO LETTER G INSTEAD OF CLOSING EARLY. History taking is the PREDOMINANT ASSESSMENT AREA; most of the marks sit before you ever say a diagnosis.**

**THE EXPLANATION, IN PLAIN ENGLISH: 'the most likely cause is A VIRUS CALLED HEPATITIS A, which has caused INFLAMMATION IN YOUR LIVER. It's usually picked up from CONTAMINATED FOOD OR WATER, and the street food on your trip fits that. The good news is that it USUALLY GETS BETTER ON ITS OWN over a few weeks and DOESN'T BECOME LONG-TERM.'** **'HEPATOCELLULAR PATTERN' IS FOR THE EXAMINER; 'INFLAMMATION IN YOUR LIVER' IS FOR THE PATIENT.**

**THE REASONS: TRAVEL TO SOUTH-EAST ASIA · STREET FOOD · JAUNDICE, DARK URINE, PALE STOOLS · RUQ PAIN · and the NEGATIVES — NO FEVER, NO RIGORS, NO WEIGHT LOSS, NO BLOOD OR SEXUAL EXPOSURE, NO ALCOHOL EXCESS, NO RECENT ANTIBIOTICS.**

**GROUPED DIFFERENTIALS — NAME THE BUCKET, THEN TWO OR THREE ITEMS, THEN WHY LESS LIKELY: HEPATOBILIARY — hepatitis B and C (no blood or sexual exposure), alcoholic hepatitis, gallstone disease, choledocholithiasis, pancreatitis · INFECTION — CHOLANGITIS (AFEBRILE), EBV, CMV, MALARIA, DENGUE, TYPHOID · DRUGS — Augmentin, flucloxacillin, paracetamol · CANCER — pancreatic, cholangio-, hepatocellular, KEPT ON THE LIST WITHOUT RED FLAGS · OTHER — autoimmune hepatitis, haemolysis, cardiac congestion.**

**LFT PATTERNS: HEPATOCELLULAR — AST/ALT ABOVE 8–10× the upper limit (800 against 40 is ~20×) · MILD RISE 2–5× suggests ALCOHOL OR FATTY LIVER, NOT VIRAL · AST:ALT ABOVE 2 FAVOURS ALCOHOL · CHOLESTATIC — ALP DOMINANT. INR ABOVE 1.5 WITH ENCEPHALOPATHY DEFINES ACUTE LIVER FAILURE — A TRANSFER, NOT A REVIEW.**

**MANAGEMENT — SUPPORTIVE: no specific antiviral · rest, oral fluids, small frequent meals · AVOID ALCOHOL ENTIRELY UNTIL ENZYMES NORMALISE · paracetamol at a CONSERVATIVE total dose · AVOID NSAIDs · most adults recover in 4–8 WEEKS; a small number relapse. Review in 48–72 hours with repeat LFT and INR.** VERIFY paracetamol ceiling.

**PUBLIC HEALTH, ONE SENTENCE AT THE END COVERS IT: HEPATITIS A IS NOTIFIABLE — SA Health Communicable Disease Control Branch · EXCLUDE FOOD HANDLERS, CHILDCARE AND HEALTHCARE WORKERS for a defined period after jaundice onset · HOUSEHOLD AND CLOSE CONTACTS OFFERED POST-EXPOSURE HEPATITIS A VACCINE; immunoglobulin for infants, the immunosuppressed and chronic liver disease · NEXT TIME, PRE-TRAVEL REVIEW 4–6 WEEKS BEFORE DEPARTURE.** VERIFY interval and notification line.
**DO NOT PROMISE IT IS 'JUST A TRAVEL BUG' BEFORE SEROLOGY — reassure about THE LIKELY COURSE, but commit only after anti-HAV IgM. DO NOT GIVE ANTIBIOTICS FOR A VIRAL HEPATITIS.**

**SAFETY-NET: 'come back immediately if you become DROWSY OR CONFUSED, VOMIT PERSISTENTLY, BRUISE OR BLEED EASILY, your jaundice DEEPENS RAPIDLY, or you develop A FEVER WITH SHAKING CHILLS.'** **Do not miss: acute liver failure, cholangitis behind a travel story, PARACETAMOL CO-INGESTION — ask the dose taken for the pain — and HEPATITIS E IN PREGNANCY, high mortality in the third trimester.** **SA: MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33; hepatology at RAH or Flinders.**
plan: **TO THE EXAMINER: 'may I have the patient's vital signs?'** Then **WIPE, 'how can I help you today?', and respond: 'I'm sorry you've been in pain — I'll ask some questions, then explain what I think.'**

**SOCRATES: where exactly · how bad · sharp or dull · onset, constant or coming and going · getting worse · DOES IT MOVE — TO YOUR SHOULDER TIP OR THROUGH TO YOUR BACK · better or worse with eating or position?**
**HARD RULE — TRAVEL BY 1:45. SIGNPOST: 'I would now like to ask about your trip in detail, because it changes what I need to look for.'**

**A TO G WITHOUT PAUSING: where and how long · activities, BUSHWALKING, INSECT OR TICK BITES · contact with anyone unwell or animals · DRUGS · TATTOOS, PIERCINGS, TRANSFUSIONS, MEDICAL OR DENTAL PROCEDURES · FOOD AND WATER — street food, shellfish, untreated water · DID YOU SEE A GP BEFORE YOU LEFT?**

stem: James Whitlock, 68, had colon cancer treated two years ago. His abdominal CT shows liver metastases; he was informed of the result yesterday.
tasks: Identify what he understood yesterday
Take a further history (5 minutes for tasks 1 and 2 together)
Explain your management plan
findings: THIS IS A CONTINUATION, NOT A FIRST TELLING

THE NEWS WAS BROKEN YESTERDAY. OPEN WITH: 'I HAVE GONE THROUGH YOUR FILE, AND I KNOW YESTERDAY WAS A HARD DAY. CAN YOU TELL ME A LITTLE MORE ABOUT WHAT YOU WERE TOLD?' Then explain what metastasis means, and only then turn breaking-bad-news mode on FOR THE PARTS HE HAS NOT ABSORBED
FIVE MINUTES FOR TASKS ONE AND TWO TOGETHER
WHAT HE UNDERSTOOD, THEN A FURTHER HISTORY. THE HARD TASK IS NUMBER THREE — THE MANAGEMENT PLAN. CANDIDATES FAIL BY JUMPING STRAIGHT TO PALLIATIVE CARE
CHECK UNDERSTANDING — ASK, THEN LISTEN

'WHAT DID YOU UNDERSTAND FROM YESTERDAY? WHAT DO YOU KNOW ABOUT WHAT METASTASIS MEANS? IS THERE ANYTHING FROM YESTERDAY THAT DIDN'T MAKE SENSE, OR THAT YOU'VE BEEN WORRYING ABOUT SINCE?' Correct what he has wrong gently, fill in what he missed
EXPLAIN METASTASIS IN PLAIN WORDS

'THE SCAN SHOWS THAT THE BOWEL CANCER YOU HAD TREATED TWO YEARS AGO HAS SPREAD TO YOUR LIVER. WE CALL THAT METASTASIS. IT MEANS SOME CANCER CELLS TRAVELLED THROUGH THE BLOOD FROM THE BOWEL TO THE LIVER — THE LIVER IS THE COMMONEST PLACE BOWEL CANCER SPREADS TO'
THE FURTHER HISTORY — symptoms of spread

PAIN — where, how bad · APPETITE AND WEIGHT · TIREDNESS · JAUNDICE, ITCH, DARK URINE, PALE STOOLS · ABDOMINAL SWELLING · BREATHLESSNESS OR COUGH — lung spread · BONE PAIN — AND NEW BACK PAIN · BOWEL HABIT, BLEEDING — local recurrence
NEW BACK PAIN IN A CANCER PATIENT = ASK THE CORD QUESTIONS

'ANY WEAKNESS OR NUMBNESS IN YOUR LEGS? ANY CHANGE IN YOUR BLADDER OR BOWELS?' SPINAL METASTASIS AND CORD COMPRESSION. Accepting back pain as bone metastasis with no neurological questions is a listed fail
SURVEILLANCE — the question that matters medico-legally and emotionally
'HAVE YOU BEEN HAVING YOUR REGULAR CHECK-UPS SINCE THE SURGERY — SCANS, BLOOD TESTS, COLONOSCOPY?' Missed surveillance is a do-not-miss item. Ask neutrally, not accusingly
SUPPORT, HOME AND WHAT MATTERS TO HIM

'WHO IS AT HOME WITH YOU? WHO DO YOU HAVE FOR SUPPORT? HOW ARE YOU COPING — HOW'S YOUR MOOD, YOUR SLEEP?' And ideas, concerns and expectations — 'WHAT IS WORRYING YOU MOST?' One card variant: HE LIVES ALONE WITH NO FAMILY SUPPORT
EMPATHY AND SILENCE ARE PART OF THE PERFORMANCE
Water, tissues, a few seconds of silence. IF THE ROLE-PLAYER DOES NOT REACT, CARRY ON WITH THE FULL SEQUENCE ANYWAY — THE EXAMINER IS MARKING WHAT YOU DID, NOT WHAT THEY DID
THE SA TERM — say it right

IN SOUTH AUSTRALIA THE INSTRUMENT IS AN ADVANCE CARE DIRECTIVE under the Advance Care Directives Act 2013, and the person appointed is a SUBSTITUTE DECISION-MAKER — NOT A 'MEDICAL DECISION MAKER', WHICH IS THE VICTORIAN TERM

FAIL — Skipping 'confirm the source' before committing to palliation.
FAIL — Back pain accepted as bone metastasis with no cord compression questions.

ASK — Any weakness or numbness in your legs, or change in bladder or bowels?

dx: **KNOWN COLORECTAL CANCER WITH LIVER METASTASES — STAGE FOUR DISEASE.** **COLORECTAL VENOUS BLOOD DRAINS THROUGH THE PORTAL SYSTEM, SO THE LIVER IS THE FIRST AND COMMONEST SITE OF SPREAD — then lung, lymph nodes and peritoneum; bone less often.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE ORDER OF MANAGEMENT — CONFIRM THE SOURCE BEFORE COMMITTING TO PALLIATION. Candidates fail by jumping straight to palliative care, or by making the whole answer 'morphine and hospice'.**

**THE FOUR ORDERED STEPS, VERBATIM. STEP 1 — THE TEAM: 'you will be looked after by a team — MYSELF AS YOUR GP, AN ONCOLOGIST, A SURGEON, A CANCER CARE NURSE, A PSYCHOLOGIST AND A SOCIAL WORKER.' — OPENS WITH SUPPORT RATHER THAN PROGNOSIS.**

**STEP 2 — CONFIRM THE SOURCE: 'first we need to BE SURE THIS LUMP HAS COME FROM YOUR BOWEL CANCER. We may take A SMALL SAMPLE WITH A NEEDLE, and we may do A SPECIAL MRI OF THE LIVER.' — THE STEP CANDIDATES SKIP. A SECOND PRIMARY OR A DIFFERENT CANCER ENTIRELY WOULD CHANGE EVERYTHING.**

**STEP 3 — PALLIATIVE INTENT, WITH CHEMOTHERAPY REFRAMED: 'the aim of treatment now is TO CONTROL SYMPTOMS AND KEEP YOU COMFORTABLE, and we call that palliative care. That includes PAIN RELIEF, ANTI-SICKNESS MEDICATION, and SOMETIMES CHEMOTHERAPY, RADIOTHERAPY OR SURGERY USED TO CONTROL SYMPTOMS RATHER THAN TO CURE.'**

**STEP 4 — PLAN AHEAD: 'I would recommend we make AN ADVANCE CARE DIRECTIVE, and that you choose A SUBSTITUTE DECISION-MAKER, WHILE YOU ARE WELL ENOUGH TO TELL US WHAT YOU WANT.' ADVANCE CARE PLANNING IS A SCORED ITEM IN END-OF-LIFE STATIONS.**

**NUANCE WORTH KNOWING IF PROBED: SOME PATIENTS WITH LIMITED COLORECTAL LIVER METASTASES ARE CANDIDATES FOR RESECTION OR ABLATION WITH CURATIVE INTENT, sometimes after chemotherapy to shrink them. That is exactly WHY THE MDT AND STAGING COME BEFORE THE PALLIATIVE LABEL — 'the team will look at whether these can be treated with surgery; if not, the aim becomes control and comfort.'**

**THE CONTINUATION OPENING: ask what he understood · CORRECT MISUNDERSTANDINGS GENTLY · explain metastasis in plain words · turn on breaking-bad-news mode only for what he hasn't absorbed — WARNING SHOT, OFFER OF SUPPORT, NAME IT PLAINLY ('CANCER THAT HAS SPREAD, WHICH WE CALL METASTASIS'), EMPATHY AND SILENCE, CHECK HOW HE IS FEELING.** **DO NOT HIDE BEHIND 'SPOTS WE NEED TO LOOK INTO'.**

**THE FURTHER HISTORY SERVES THE PLAN: symptoms of spread, surveillance, support, mood — and CORD COMPRESSION if there is back pain. Each answer changes what you arrange — a man living alone with no support needs social work and community palliative care early.**

**SA: specialist oncology at the ROYAL ADELAIDE OR FLINDERS with PATS; community palliative care through COUNTRY HEALTH CONNECT; ADVANCE CARE DIRECTIVE AND SUBSTITUTE DECISION-MAKER — the SA terms; Cancer Council SA 13 11 20; ACCHS and Closing the Gap; TIS National 131 450.**

**The management order: THE TEAM → CONFIRM THE SOURCE → PALLIATIVE INTENT (if not curable), with chemotherapy reframed as symptom control → ADVANCE CARE DIRECTIVE AND SUBSTITUTE DECISION-MAKER.**

**Do not miss: SPINAL METASTASIS AND CORD COMPRESSION — leg weakness, numbness, bladder or bowel change · BILIARY OBSTRUCTION causing jaundice, which may need drainage first · HYPERCALCAEMIA · MISSED SURVEILLANCE after resection · DEPRESSION AND SOCIAL ISOLATION.**

**Avoid: JUMPING TO PALLIATIVE CARE BEFORE THE SOURCE IS CONFIRMED · 'SPOTS WE NEED TO LOOK INTO' — hiding behind soft words · PROMISING A PROGNOSIS OR TIMEFRAME · re-breaking the news without asking what he understood · the Victorian term 'medical decision maker'.**

stem: Jenny Marsh, 45, presents with dark urine. She had a sore throat two weeks ago.
tasks: Take a focused history (about 4 minutes)
Ask the examiner for the physical examination findings
Explain your diagnosis to the patient
Explain your differential diagnoses
findings: THE TRAP BUILT INTO THE STEM

'SORE THROAT TWO WEEKS AGO' IS HANDED TO YOU SO THAT YOU WILL DIAGNOSE POST-STREPTOCOCCAL GLOMERULONEPHRITIS AND NEVER ASK ABOUT STOOLS. THE SORE THROAT IS IN THE STEM ONLY TO EXPLAIN WHY SHE WAS GIVEN AN ANTIBIOTIC. THE ANTIBIOTIC IS THE DIAGNOSIS
THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES THE STATION

'ALONG WITH THE DARK URINE, HAVE YOUR STOOLS BECOME PALE OR CLAY COLOURED?' — ASKED BY 1:20. DARK URINE PLUS PALE STOOLS = CONJUGATED BILIRUBIN SPILLING INTO URINE AND NOT REACHING THE GUT → LIVER. DARK URINE WITH NORMAL STOOLS = BLOOD OR MYOGLOBIN → KIDNEY
THE ANTIBIOTIC QUESTION IS THE WHOLE CASE

'YOU MENTIONED A SORE THROAT — DID YOU SEE A DOCTOR, AND WERE YOU GIVEN ANY MEDICATION OR ANTIBIOTICS?' → AMOXICILLIN–CLAVULANATE (Augmentin). CANDIDATES WHO ASK ONLY 'WHEN WAS THE SORE THROAT?' COLLECT THE INTERVAL AND MISS THE CAUSE
CHARACTERISE THE URINE FIRST

COLOUR — 'LIKE COCA-COLA, BROWN, OR JUST DARK YELLOW?' — ASKING HER TO NAME IT IS SCORED · THROUGH THE WHOLE STREAM OR ONLY PART · ANY BLOOD OR CLOTS · SMELL. Then timing — first time, every void, getting worse
COMMIT TO THE BRANCH OUT LOUD, THEN CROSS-CHECK

'THANK YOU, THAT IS IMPORTANT. DARK URINE TOGETHER WITH PALE STOOLS TELLS ME THIS IS VERY LIKELY COMING FROM YOUR LIVER OR THE DRAINAGE TUBES RATHER THAN YOUR KIDNEYS. LET ME JUST CHECK — ANY BURNING PASSING URINE, ANY FEVER, ANY SWELLING IN YOUR LEGS OR INJURY TO YOUR TUMMY?' THREE KIDNEY QUESTIONS, THEN FOCUS ON THE LIVER
WHAT SHE GIVES
PALE STOOLS · JAUNDICE · ITCH · sore throat resolved, PRESCRIBED AMOXICILLIN–CLAVULANATE (some recalls: amoxicillin alone) · NO FEVER · NO previous fatty-meal pain · NO surgery
THE EXAMINATION — request specifically

JAUNDICE PRESENT · TEMPERATURE NORMAL · BP normal · RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT TENDERNESS · HEPATOMEGALY PRESENT · SHIFTING DULLNESS ABSENT · DIPSTICK: BLOOD NEGATIVE, PROTEIN NEGATIVE, BILIRUBIN POSITIVE. 'ABDOMINAL EXAMINATION PLEASE' RETURNS GENERIC ANSWERS
NAME THE THREE DIPSTICK PADS, THEN INTERPRET
BLOOD · PROTEIN · BILIRUBIN. Bilirubin positive with blood negative = cholestasis, not glomerular. UROBILINOGEN ALONE IS NORMAL — don't let it distract you
FEVER TURNS THIS INTO CHOLANGITIS
FEVER SITS AT THE END OF EVERY LIVER BLOCK. Here it is negative — SAY SO, because it is what lets you call it drug-induced rather than an infected obstructed duct
THE LIVER BRANCH — four blocks in order
RED FLAGS — weight loss, appetite, lumps, tiredness, family cancer · HEPATITIS SYMPTOMS — yellowing, itch · RISK FACTORS — ABP FIT NO SEX · GALLBLADDER AND SURGERY — then FEVER

dx: **ANTIBIOTIC-INDUCED CHOLESTATIC HEPATITIS, MOST COMMONLY FROM AMOXICILLIN–CLAVULANATE — dark urine with PALE STOOLS, JAUNDICE, ITCH, TENDER HEPATOMEGALY AND BILIRUBIN ON DIPSTICK.** **Augmentin cholestasis characteristically appears DAYS TO WEEKS AFTER THE COURSE — sometimes after it has finished — and is more common in OLDER PATIENTS AND WITH REPEATED OR PROLONGED COURSES.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: ASK ABOUT PALE STOOLS EARLY, THEN COMMIT OUT LOUD. Both dark-urine versions look identical for ninety seconds; the pass is ONE QUESTION ASKED EARLY and an AUDIBLE COMMITMENT, then a SHORT DELIBERATE SWEEP of the organ you set aside.**
**THE STEM IS BAIT; THE STOOL QUESTION OVERRIDES IT. Anchoring on post-streptococcal GN because of the sore throat is the designed failure.**

**THE EXPLANATION: 'I think the most likely cause is A REACTION TO THE ANTIBIOTIC you had for your sore throat — Augmentin. In some people it causes THE BILE TO BACK UP IN THE LIVER instead of draining. That's WHY YOUR SKIN IS YELLOW AND ITCHY, YOUR URINE IS DARK AND YOUR STOOLS ARE PALE. It usually SETTLES ONCE THE MEDICINE IS OUT OF YOUR SYSTEM, though it can take some weeks.'**

**THE REASONS: DARK URINE WITH PALE STOOLS — cholestasis · JAUNDICE AND ITCH · AUGMENTIN FOR THE SORE THROAT · TENDER HEPATOMEGALY · DIPSTICK BILIRUBIN POSITIVE, BLOOD NEGATIVE · and the NEGATIVES — NO FEVER, NO PREVIOUS BILIARY PAIN, NO SURGERY.**

**TWO DIFFERENTIAL LISTS — A LARGE ONE FOR THE ORGAN YOU CHOSE, A SMALL ONE FOR THE OTHER. LIVER: viral hepatitis, alcoholic hepatitis, GALLSTONE OBSTRUCTION, CHOLANGITIS (AFEBRILE), pancreatic or biliary cancer (no red flags), other drugs — FLUCLOXACILLIN, DICLOXACILLIN · KIDNEY, BRIEFLY: glomerulonephritis and UTI — less likely with pale stools, bilirubin on dipstick and no blood.**

**MANAGEMENT: STOP ANY FURTHER DOSES — the course has usually finished · LFT WITH CONJUGATED BILIRUBIN, INR, FBE, UEC, CRP, lipase, viral hepatitis serology · UPPER ABDOMINAL ULTRASOUND TO EXCLUDE DUCT DILATATION AND STONES · REPEAT LFT TO CONFIRM THE TREND IS DOWNWARD · MRCP only if the ducts are dilated · symptomatic relief for itch.**
**RECORD THE ADVERSE DRUG REACTION — in the practice software AND MY HEALTH RECORD — so it ALERTS AT FUTURE PRESCRIBING. Do not re-prescribe the culprit. Consider reporting to the TGA.**

**DO NOT MISS: CHOLANGITIS — the fever question · ACUTE LIVER FAILURE — confusion, bruising, rising INR · MALIGNANT OBSTRUCTION in an older patient with weight loss. DO NOT REASSURE THAT PALE STOOLS ARE UNIMPORTANT.**

**SAFETY-NET: 'come back straight away if you develop A FEVER OR SHIVERS, become CONFUSED OR DROWSY, BRUISE EASILY, or the yellowing gets rapidly worse.'** **SA: Country Health Connect for follow-up; MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 for deterioration; TIS National 131 450.**

tasks: Take a focused history (about 4 minutes)
Ask the examiner for the physical examination findings
Explain your diagnosis to the patient
Explain your differential diagnoses
findings: DARK URINE HAS EXACTLY TWO HOMES IN THE AMC: LIVER AND KIDNEY
PALE STOOLS SIT IN THE MIDDLE BECAUSE THEY DEPEND ON BILIRUBIN REACHING THE GUT. ASK 'ALONG WITH THE DARK URINE, HAVE YOUR STOOLS BECOME PALE OR CLAY COLOURED?' BY 1:20
WHAT SHE SAYS FIRST
'I HAVE NOTICED A COLOUR CHANGE IN MY URINE FOR THE PAST FEW DAYS AND IT IS FREAKING ME OUT.' RESPOND TO THE FEAR BEFORE THE QUESTIONS
CHARACTERISE — and ask her to name the colour

'LIKE COCA-COLA, BROWN, OR JUST DARK YELLOW?' → COLA-COLOURED · THROUGHOUT THE STREAM · EVERY TIME · A FEW DAYS · NO CLOTS · NO ODOUR CHANGE. Coca-cola urine is glomerular haematuria until proven otherwise
NORMAL STOOLS → COMMIT TO THE KIDNEY OUT LOUD

'THANK YOU. BECAUSE YOUR STOOLS ARE A NORMAL COLOUR, I THINK THIS IS MORE LIKELY COMING FROM YOUR KIDNEYS OR BLADDER THAN FROM YOUR LIVER. I WILL JUST CHECK TWO THINGS — ANY YELLOWING OF YOUR SKIN OR EYES, ANY ITCHING?' Both negative closes the liver
THE INTERVAL DECIDES WHICH GLOMERULONEPHRITIS

'WHEN EXACTLY WAS THE SORE THROAT, AND WHEN DID THE URINE CHANGE?' → A SORE THROAT A FEW DAYS AGO, NO ANTIBIOTICS. IgA NEPHROPATHY IS SYNPHARYNGITIC — HAEMATURIA 1–3 DAYS AFTER THE INFECTION. POST-STREPTOCOCCAL GN NEEDS 1–3 WEEKS AFTER THROAT, 3–6 WEEKS AFTER SKIN
THE KIDNEY BRANCH — seven groups

CANCER — weight loss, appetite, family history · INFECTION — fever, dysuria, frequency, loin pain · CALCULUS — colicky flank pain, previous stones · GLOMERULONEPHRITIS — sore throat, timing, LEG OR EYE SWELLING · RHABDOMYOLYSIS — HEAVY EXERCISE, MUSCLE PAIN, STATINS · TRAUMA · PROSTATE only if male
THE EXAMINATION — findings only if named

JAUNDICE ABSENT · TEMPERATURE NORMAL · BLOOD PRESSURE ELEVATED — e.g. 152/94 · no tenderness · BALLOT THE KIDNEYS — no mass · RENAL ANGLE TENDERNESS absent · no hepatosplenomegaly · DIPSTICK BLOOD POSITIVE, PROTEIN NEGATIVE OR TRACE, BILIRUBIN NEGATIVE
NAME THE SPECIAL TESTS
BALLOTTING THE KIDNEYS — retroperitoneal, needs a named technique · RENAL ANGLE TENDERNESS — screens pyelonephritis · and ASK FOR THE BLOOD PRESSURE — hypertension supports a nephritic picture
NEPHRITIC VERSUS NEPHROTIC — say which, and why

NEPHRITIC: HAEMATURIA, HYPERTENSION, MILD PROTEINURIA, mild oedema, reduced urine output. NEPHROTIC: HEAVY PROTEINURIA, MARKED OEDEMA, LOW ALBUMIN, hyperlipidaemia. THIS IS NEPHRITIC — THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A PASS AND A STRONG PASS
NO DYSURIA, NO FREQUENCY, NO FEVER = NOT A UTI
CALLING THIS A URINARY INFECTION AND PRESCRIBING ANTIBIOTICS FOR GLOMERULAR HAEMATURIA IS A LISTED FAIL

dx: **IgA NEPHROPATHY — VISIBLE HAEMATURIA APPEARING WITHIN ONE TO THREE DAYS OF AN UPPER RESPIRATORY INFECTION, with DIPSTICK BLOOD, NO SIGNIFICANT PROTEINURIA AND A RAISED BLOOD PRESSURE.** **The commonest primary glomerulonephritis worldwide; IgA immune complexes deposit in the mesangium, and a mucosal infection triggers the flare.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: ASK ABOUT PALE STOOLS EARLY, THEN COMMIT OUT LOUD — and do a SHORT, DELIBERATE SWEEP of the organ you set aside. Candidates fail by asking every kidney and every liver question at random and running out of time with no structure the examiner can score.**

**THE INTERVAL IS THE REASONING: 'the haematuria BEGAN WITHIN DAYS of the throat infection, rather than after the TWO- TO THREE-WEEK DELAY of post-streptococcal disease' — IgA is SYNPHARYNGITIC; post-strep needs time for immune complexes to form.**

**THE EXPLANATION, IN PLAIN ENGLISH: 'I think the most likely cause is a condition called IgA NEPHROPATHY. The filters in your kidneys have become INFLAMED, and that lets BLOOD LEAK INTO YOUR URINE — which is what's turning it dark. It often FLARES WITH A THROAT OR CHEST INFECTION, which is why it came on just after your sore throat. Your blood pressure is also up, which fits with the kidneys being involved.'**

**THE REASONS: COLA-COLOURED URINE THROUGH THE WHOLE STREAM · ONSET 1–3 DAYS AFTER A SORE THROAT · DIPSTICK BLOOD WITHOUT SIGNIFICANT PROTEIN · HYPERTENSION · and the NEGATIVES — NO PALE STOOLS, NO JAUNDICE, NO DYSURIA, NO FEVER, NO FLANK PAIN, NO TRAUMA, NO HEAVY EXERTION, NO WEIGHT LOSS.**

**TWO DIFFERENTIAL LISTS — LARGE FOR THE KIDNEY, SMALL FOR THE LIVER. KIDNEY: POST-STREPTOCOCCAL GN (interval too short), UTI OR PYELONEPHRITIS (no dysuria or fever), CALCULUS (no colic), RENAL OR BLADDER MALIGNANCY (young, no red flags — but VISIBLE HAEMATURIA OVER 40 IS REFERRED REGARDLESS), RHABDOMYOLYSIS (no exertion), TRAUMA · LIVER, BRIEFLY: hepatitis and biliary obstruction — less likely with normal stools and no jaundice.**

**THE PLAN: URINE MICROSCOPY FOR DYSMORPHIC RED CELLS AND RED CELL CASTS — they confirm a glomerular source · UEC AND eGFR · ALBUMIN–CREATININE OR PROTEIN–CREATININE RATIO · FBE, CRP · ASOT OR ANTI-DNase B AND COMPLEMENT C3/C4 — C3 is LOW in post-strep, usually NORMAL in IgA · CK if exertion · RENAL ULTRASOUND · BLOOD PRESSURE REPEATED AND MONITORED · NEPHROLOGY REFERRAL. RENAL BIOPSY IS THE ONLY WAY TO BE CERTAIN — a specialist decision.**

**ONGOING: BLOOD PRESSURE CONTROL — often an ACE INHIBITOR OR ARB, which also reduces proteinuria — and regular monitoring of renal function and protein. Many have a benign course; SOME PROGRESS, which is why follow-up matters.**
**ESCALATE FOR RAPIDLY PROGRESSIVE GLOMERULONEPHRITIS — RISING CREATININE, OLIGURIA, WORSENING OEDEMA: a SAME-DAY RENAL DISCUSSION.**

**AVOID: CALLING IT A UTI AND TREATING WITH ANTIBIOTICS · ATTRIBUTING DARK URINE TO DEHYDRATION WITHOUT A DIPSTICK · a generic abdominal examination request · one differential list only.** **SA: nephrology at RAH or Flinders; Country Health Connect; PATS; MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 for rapid deterioration; TIS National 131 450.**

**A LARGE KIDNEY LIST, A SMALL LIVER LIST, each with a reason — including why post-strep is less likely.**

stem: James Petrou, 40, attends to discuss his liver function test results. AST ~95 (ref <40) · ALT ~40–50 (ref <45) · GGT elevated · ALP and bilirubin near normal. No presenting complaint.
tasks: Take a history (about 4 minutes)
Ask the examiner for the physical examination findings
Explain your diagnosis to the patient
Explain your differential diagnoses
findings: A RESULT AND NO COMPLAINT

'I AM JUST HERE FOR MY RESULTS.' MAKE THE ABNORMAL LFT THE COMPLAINT AND RUN THE STANDARD LIVER BLOCKS AGAINST IT. Candidates who sit down and start reciting enzyme values LOOK MECHANICAL, AND THE APPROACH-TO-PATIENT DOMAIN SUFFERS BEFORE THE CLINICAL CONTENT EVER STARTS
THE BRIDGE — two sentences

'THANK YOU FOR COMING IN TO DISCUSS THEM. I DO HAVE YOUR RESULTS HERE, AND I WILL GO THROUGH THEM WITH YOU. BEFORE I DO, MAY I ASK YOU A FEW QUESTIONS SO THAT THE RESULTS MAKE MORE SENSE WHEN WE GET TO THEM?' Results acknowledged, questions second, explanation third
READ THE MAGNITUDE AND THE RATIO

AST ~95 against <40 — ABOUT 2.4× · ALT 40–50 — at or just above the limit · GGT RAISED · ALP AND BILIRUBIN NEAR NORMAL. A MILD RISE (UNDER ~5×) IS WHAT ALCOHOL OR FAT DOES — viral hepatitis gives a far larger rise. AST:ALT ABOVE 2 FAVOURS ALCOHOL; BELOW 1 FAVOURS FATTY LIVER OR VIRAL
THE ALCOHOL QUESTION, DONE PROPERLY — by 2:10

'DO YOU DRINK ALCOHOL? HOW MUCH, AND HOW LONG AT THAT LEVEL? WHAT DO YOU DRINK, WHAT SIZE GLASS? ROUGHLY HOW MANY NIGHTS A WEEK?' → A BOTTLE OF WINE EVERY NIGHT FOR TWENTY YEARS. RESTAURANT OWNER. 'DO YOU DRINK?' — 'YES' — MOVING ON IS A LISTED FAIL
DO THE ARITHMETIC OUT LOUD — and get it right

A 750 mL BOTTLE AT 13% IS ABOUT 7.7 STANDARD DRINKS — NOT 12 TO 14. A NIGHTLY BOTTLE IS ROUGHLY 54 A WEEK. NHMRC: NO MORE THAN 10 A WEEK AND 4 IN ANY ONE DAY — so about FIVE TIMES THE GUIDELINE, FOR TWO DECADES. WRONG ARITHMETIC UNDERMINES AN OTHERWISE GOOD STATION
CAGE OR AUDIT-C — name one

CAGE: CUT DOWN, ANNOYED, GUILTY, EYE-OPENER — TWO OR MORE POSITIVES SUGGEST PROBLEM DRINKING. AUDIT-C is the three-question Australian GP screen. NAMING ONE AND SAYING YOU WOULD USE IT IS A STRONG ANSWER even without time to run it
THE REST OF ABP FIT NO SEX — then fever

ANTIBIOTICS · TRANSFUSIONS, TATTOOS, PIERCINGS, INJECTED DRUGS, TRAVEL, FOOD · OCCUPATION, NEEDLE-STICK · SEXUAL HISTORY · REGULAR MEDICATIONS INCLUDING HERBAL OR GYM SUPPLEMENTS · FATTY-MEAL PAIN · OPERATIONS · AND FEVER — FEVER CLOSES EVERY LIVER BLOCK, NO EXCEPTIONS
THE EXAMINATION — a normal examination is a finding

NO JAUNDICE · NO HEPATOMEGALY · NO SHIFTING DULLNESS · URINE DIPSTICK NORMAL · NOTHING ABNORMAL. SAY SO: 'THE EXAMINATION IS NORMAL, WHICH IS WHAT I WOULD EXPECT AT THIS STAGE — NO STIGMATA OF CHRONIC LIVER DISEASE AND NO DECOMPENSATION. REASSURING, BUT IT DOES NOT EXCLUDE ONGOING DAMAGE'
THE SEVEN-STEP REQUEST

GENERAL APPEARANCE — JAUNDICE, CACHEXIA, SCRATCH MARKS, OEDEMA · VITALS, PARTICULARLY TEMPERATURE · INSPECTION · PALPATION — HEPATOMEGALY, SPLENOMEGALY · PERCUSSION — SHIFTING DULLNESS · AUSCULTATION · URINE DIPSTICK FOR BILIRUBIN. Skip the rectal unless bowel symptoms
VERSION B — the fatty liver mirror

35-year-old, RUQ pain, AST AND ALT UNDER TWICE THE LIMIT, TRIGLYCERIDES AND CHOLESTEROL HIGH, NO ALCOHOL AT ALL. Everything else negative. 'HOW IS YOUR DIET?' INVITES 'HEALTHY AND BALANCED' — ASK FOR A TYPICAL DAY'S FOOD, SUGARY DRINKS, TAKEAWAY, AND EXERCISE. FATTY LIVER IS A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION — SAY SO

dx: **ALCOHOLIC HEPATITIS (ALCOHOLIC STEATOHEPATITIS) — a MILD TRANSAMINASE RISE WITH A RAISED GGT AND AN AST:ALT RATIO ABOVE 2, in a man drinking roughly FIVE TIMES THE WEEKLY GUIDELINE FOR TWO DECADES.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: QUOTE YOUR OWN NUMBERS BACK AS REASONS. Both diagnoses are guessable from the stem. A PASS SAYS THREE THINGS: THE MAGNITUDE OF THE RISE AS A MULTIPLE OF THE UPPER LIMIT, THE AST:ALT RATIO, AND THAT THE OTHER CAUSES HAVE BEEN ACTIVELY EXCLUDED. A FAIL NAMES THE DISEASE AND STOPS.**

**THE THREE REASONS, OUT LOUD: 'FIRST, you are drinking about A BOTTLE OF WINE A NIGHT, which is roughly SEVEN TO EIGHT STANDARD DRINKS, so AROUND FIFTY IN A WEEK — about FIVE TIMES THE RECOMMENDED MAXIMUM — and you have done so FOR TWENTY YEARS. SECOND, I have RULED OUT THE OTHER CAUSES: no viral risk factors, no medications, no gallbladder symptoms, no travel, no family history. THIRD, the PATTERN OF THE BLOOD TEST FITS: the enzymes are only MILDLY raised, which is what alcohol does, and THE RATIO BETWEEN THE TWO IS ABOVE TWO, which is characteristic. A viral hepatitis would have given a far larger rise.'**

**THE RESULT IN NINETY SECONDS, TO THE PATIENT: 'your liver enzymes are up, but only mildly. There is a second thing I look at — THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TWO OF THOSE ENZYMES. In your case ONE IS MORE THAN TWICE THE OTHER, and that pattern is VERY CHARACTERISTIC OF ALCOHOL. Drinking a large amount over a long time INFLAMES THE LIVER — alcoholic hepatitis. If it continues, it can lead to SCARRING — CIRRHOSIS — where the liver stops working properly. The important thing is that AT THIS STAGE IT IS LARGELY REVERSIBLE IF THE ALCOHOL STOPS.'**
**'IS MY LIVER DAMAGED?' — HONEST, NOT CATASTROPHIC: INFLAMMATION NOW, CIRRHOSIS LATER IF IT CONTINUES, REVERSIBLE IF IT STOPS.**

**DIFFERENTIALS BY BUCKET: GI HEPATOBILIARY — FATTY LIVER DISEASE, gallstone disease, CIRRHOSIS · INFECTION — hepatitis A, B, C, EBV, CMV · DRUGS — antibiotics, paracetamol, STATINS, methotrexate, HERBAL AND BODYBUILDING SUPPLEMENTS · CANCER — HCC, cholangiocarcinoma, pancreatic, metastases · OTHER — autoimmune hepatitis, PBC, HAEMOCHROMATOSIS, WILSON (under 40), alpha-1 antitrypsin, coeliac, thyroid · MSK — A RAISED AST CAN COME FROM MUSCLE; CHECK CK IF THE STORY FITS.**

**MANAGEMENT — BRIEF INTERVENTION, NOT MORALISING: FEEDBACK, RESPONSIBILITY, ADVICE, MENU OF OPTIONS, EMPATHY, SELF-EFFICACY. Agree a specific goal. ABSTINENCE IS THE TARGET, BUT A HEAVY LONG-TERM DRINKER SHOULD NOT STOP ABRUPTLY WITHOUT SUPPORT — WITHDRAWAL CAN BE DANGEROUS. THIAMINE. Vaccinate against hepatitis A and B if non-immune. Follow-up LFTs showing improvement ARE THEMSELVES MOTIVATING.** VERIFY thiamine dose.

**INVESTIGATIONS: REPEAT AND EXTEND THE LFT with GGT, ALBUMIN, INR AND FBC — A LOW PLATELET COUNT IS AN EARLY CLUE TO FIBROSIS · HBsAg and HCV antibody · IRON STUDIES for haemochromatosis · autoimmune screen · coeliac serology · TSH · caeruloplasmin if under 40 · metabolic work-up · UPPER ABDOMINAL ULTRASOUND — steatosis is a bright, echogenic liver with LOSS OF THE NORMAL HEPATORENAL CONTRAST · STAGE FIBROSIS WITH FIB-4, THEN FIBROSCAN.**

**VERSION B — NAMING A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION: 'fatty liver disease is what we call A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION, so I want to be clear about how I got there — I have ruled out cancers, viral infections, gallstones, a duct infection (no fever), medications, and you don't drink. What is left is the mild enzyme rise WITH THE RAISED CHOLESTEROL AND TRIGLYCERIDES.' Accept NAFLD, NASH or the newer MASLD/MASH. WEIGHT LOSS IS THE SINGLE MOST EFFECTIVE INTERVENTION.**

**CORRECTION FOR VERSION B — FATTY LIVER DOES NOT CAUSE ABDOMINAL PAIN. If challenged: 'fatty liver disease is usually asymptomatic and is not a recognised cause of abdominal pain, so I WOULD CONTINUE TO LOOK FOR A SEPARATE EXPLANATION — biliary disease, peptic ulcer or reflux — while treating the steatosis on its own merits.'** **SA: DASSA and ADIS; hepatology at RAH or Flinders; GP Management Plan and Team Care Arrangement for dietitian and exercise physiologist.**
plan: **WIPE, 'how can I help you today?' → 'I'm just here for my results.' THE BRIDGE: results acknowledged, questions second, explanation third, 'is that all right?'**
**SYMPTOMS OF LIVER DISEASE: yellowing of skin or eyes · itching · dark urine · pale stools.**
**RED FLAGS: weight loss · appetite · lumps · tiredness · family history of bowel, liver, pancreas or stomach cancer.**
**THE ALCOHOL QUESTION — QUANTIFIED BY 2:10: do you drink · how much, how long at that level · what, what size glass · how many nights a week?** Then **CAGE: cut down, annoyed, guilty, eye-opener.**
**CONVERT IT, OUT LOUD: 'a bottle is about 7.7 standard drinks — roughly 54 a week, about five times the guideline.'**

**THE REST OF ABP FIT NO SEX: antibiotics · transfusions, tattoos, piercings, injected drugs, travel, food · occupation, needle-stick · sexual history · MEDICATIONS INCLUDING HERBAL OR GYM SUPPLEMENTS.**
**GALLBLADDER — pain after fatty meals · SURGERY · AND FEVER OR SHAKING CHILLS.**
**Version B only: LIFESTYLE — 'describe a typical day's food' · sugary drinks, takeaway · 'do you exercise regularly?'**
**HISTORY STOPS. THE SEVEN-STEP REQUEST: general appearance · vitals, temperature · inspection · palpation — hepatomegaly, splenomegaly · shifting dullness · auscultation · dipstick bilirubin.**
**THE NORMAL EXAMINATION, SAID AS A FINDING — no stigmata, no decompensation; reassuring but not excluding.**
**EXPLAIN THE RESULTS — NINETY SECONDS MAX: mildly raised enzymes, the ratio above two, characteristic of alcohol; inflammation now, scarring later, reversible if it stops.**

stem: Lily Barrett, 27, presents with right lower abdominal pain for four days, much worse in the last 24 hours, vomiting, feels hot.

findings: A MULTIPLE-FINDINGS STATION — BY DESIGN

YOU WILL COLLECT POSITIVES POINTING AT APPENDICITIS, PID AND ECTOPIC PREGNANCY. THAT IS DELIBERATE — the AMC began designing cases this way because candidates who found one positive and stopped argued a correct diagnosis should equal a pass. YOU GET MULTIPLE FINDINGS BECAUSE YOU RULED OUT PROPERLY. THE SKILL ASSESSED IS RANKING THEM, NOT COLLECTING THEM
'MY LAST PERIOD WAS FIVE WEEKS AGO' — ESTABLISH THE CYCLE

'ARE YOUR PERIODS REGULAR OR IRREGULAR? HOW OFTEN DO YOU GET THEM?' A WOMAN WHOSE CYCLE IS 4–6 WEEKS IS NOT OBVIOUSLY OVERDUE — EXACTLY WHY THE CASE IS DESIGNED THIS WAY. 'Five weeks' recorded as a missed period without the cycle length is a listed error
'I'VE HAD CHLAMYDIA BEFORE' — DO NOT LOCK ONTO PID
NOTE IT AS A RISK FACTOR FOR BOTH PID AND ECTOPIC, THEN KEEP RULING OUT. Candidates fail by hearing 'previous chlamydia', deciding it is PID, and NEVER REACHING THE PREGNANCY TEST
PROBE RATHER THAN RECORD

'I FEEL FEVERISH' → 'HAVE YOU ACTUALLY MEASURED YOUR TEMPERATURE? ANY CHILLS OR SHAKES?' · 'I'VE VOMITED THREE TIMES' → 'WHAT COLOUR WAS IT? — I WANT TO KNOW IT IS NOT GREEN.' And THE SHIFT: 'DID THE PAIN START WHERE IT IS NOW, OR SOMEWHERE ELSE AND MOVE?'
THE O&G BLOCK STARTS BY 3:15 — HARD RULE

SYMPTOMS — VAGINAL BLEEDING, DISCHARGE · PERIOD HISTORY — LMP, REGULAR OR IRREGULAR, HOW OFTEN, COULD YOU BE PREGNANT · SEXUAL HISTORY — SEXUALLY ACTIVE, CONTRACEPTION, SAFE SEX, PREVIOUS STI. IT CONTAINS THE DIAGNOSIS AND IS THE BLOCK CANDIDATES RUN OUT OF TIME FOR — SHORTEN THE GI QUESTIONS, NOT THIS
THE EXAMINER'S ANSWERS

T 37.5 · RLQ TENDERNESS WITH GUARDING, RIGIDITY AND REBOUND · no mass · ROVSING NEGATIVE, OBTURATOR NEGATIVE · SPECULUM: cervix and vaginal wall normal · BIMANUAL: CERVICAL MOTION TENDERNESS POSITIVE, UTERUS NORMAL SIZE AND EMPTY, RIGHT ADNEXAL TENDERNESS · URINE PREGNANCY TEST POSITIVE, dipstick normal
37.5 IS DELIBERATE

THE AMC COULD HAVE GIVEN YOU 39. IT GAVE A NUMBER ON THE THRESHOLD SO THAT FEVER NEITHER CONFIRMS NOR EXCLUDES ANYTHING. Use 37.4 as a working threshold. LOW-GRADE FEVER AND FLU-LIKE SYMPTOMS DO APPEAR IN ECTOPIC PREGNANCY — it does not displace the diagnosis
THE SINGLE AUTOMATIC FAIL
NOT REQUESTING A URINE PREGNANCY TEST IN A WOMAN OF REPRODUCTIVE AGE WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN. IT DOES NOT MATTER HOW GOOD THE REST OF THE STATION WAS. ASK FOR IT BY NAME IN THE OFFICE-TESTS STEP
CONSENT AND CHAPERONE — SAID OUT LOUD

'WITH THE PATIENT'S CONSENT AND A CHAPERONE, I WOULD LIKE TO PERFORM A PELVIC EXAMINATION' — THEN INSPECTION, SPECULUM, BIMANUAL. 'Examiner, cervical motion tenderness?' out of nowhere is a starred fail
NAME THE SPECIAL TESTS

ROVSING'S SIGN, THEN OBTURATOR (psoas is awkward on a role-player). BOTH NEGATIVE, TOGETHER WITH NO SHIFT OF PAIN, IS HOW YOU EXCLUDE APPENDICITIS OUT LOUD. 'I'd press on the left and see if it hurts on the right' — DESCRIBING INSTEAD OF NAMING LOSES THE MARK
