dx: **ECTOPIC PREGNANCY — a pregnancy implanted OUTSIDE THE UTERINE CAVITY, most often IN THE FALLOPIAN TUBE.** **Late period on an irregular cycle · vomiting · feeling feverish · previous STI · CERVICAL MOTION TENDERNESS · RIGHT ADNEXAL TENDERNESS · POSITIVE URINE PREGNANCY TEST WITH A NORMAL-SIZE, EMPTY UTERUS. A RUPTURED ECTOPIC KILLS YOUNG WOMEN.**
**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: ASK FOR THE URINE PREGNANCY TEST, DO THE PELVIC EXAMINATION PROPERLY WITH CONSENT AND A CHAPERONE, AND THEN RANK THE FINDINGS INSTEAD OF COLLAPSING ONTO THE FIRST ONE.**

**RANKING MULTIPLE POSITIVES — THE SENTENCE THAT SCORES: 'several things were possible here. I was thinking about APPENDICITIS, PELVIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE AND ECTOPIC PREGNANCY. Of those three I am putting ECTOPIC PREGNANCY AT THE TOP, because YOUR PERIOD IS LATE ON A CYCLE THAT IS USUALLY FOUR TO SIX WEEKS, THE PREGNANCY TEST IS POSITIVE, YOUR WOMB IS A NORMAL SIZE AND EMPTY, and THE OPENING OF THE WOMB WAS PAINFUL WHEN I EXAMINED YOU.'**

**NAMING IT — IN ONE BREATH, TWO THINGS: 'Lily, two things. First, the test today shows YOU ARE PREGNANT. Second — and this is the part I need you to hear — I AM CONCERNED THE PREGNANCY IS GROWING IN THE WRONG PLACE, in the tube rather than in the womb. We call that AN ECTOPIC PREGNANCY. It is serious, because THE TUBE CAN BLEED, and that is WHY I AM SENDING YOU TO HOSPITAL TODAY RATHER THAN TOMORROW.'**

**WHY APPENDICITIS AND PID RANK LOWER — SAY IT: appendicitis — NO SHIFT OF PAIN, ROVSING AND OBTURATOR NEGATIVE; PID — NO DISCHARGE, UNILATERAL rather than bilateral tenderness, AND THE PREGNANCY TEST IS POSITIVE. A PAST STI IS A RISK FACTOR FOR ECTOPIC AS WELL — tubal damage.**

**DO NOW: URINE PREGNANCY TEST. IF POSITIVE AND UNWELL — TWO LARGE-BORE CANNULAE, FBC, UEC, GROUP AND HOLD WITH CROSS-MATCH, SERUM βhCG, IV FLUIDS, ANALGESIA, NIL BY MOUTH, URGENT GYNAECOLOGY. DO NOT WAIT FOR IMAGING IN A HAEMODYNAMICALLY UNSTABLE WOMAN.**

**DO NEXT: TRANSVAGINAL ULTRASOUND WITH QUANTITATIVE βhCG. An intrauterine sac should be visible above a DISCRIMINATORY βhCG OF ROUGHLY 1500 IU/L; AN EMPTY UTERUS ABOVE THAT IS HIGHLY SUSPICIOUS. The TUBAL RING — a small ring-like adnexal structure separate from the uterus. FREE FLUID IN THE POUCH OF DOUGLAS in a shocked woman with a positive test is HAEMOPERITONEUM. CHECK RHESUS STATUS.** VERIFY local threshold.

**MANAGEMENT: UNSTABLE → RESUSCITATE AND THEATRE — laparoscopy, usually SALPINGECTOMY. STABLE, SMALL, LOW βhCG, NO FETAL HEART → SINGLE-DOSE IM METHOTREXATE WITH βhCG FOLLOW-UP, or laparoscopic salpingotomy or salpingectomy. ANTI-D IF RHESUS NEGATIVE. Contraception and future-pregnancy counselling; EARLY SCAN NEXT PREGNANCY.** VERIFY against RANZCOG.

**DO NOT MISS: A RUPTURED ECTOPIC IN A WOMAN WHO LOOKS WELL — SHOULDER-TIP PAIN, SYNCOPE, TACHYCARDIA BEFORE HYPOTENSION · OVARIAN TORSION · APPENDICITIS IN PREGNANCY · PID PROGRESSING TO TUBO-OVARIAN ABSCESS.**

**SA: a haemodynamically unstable woman with a positive test in a Yorke Peninsula hospital is A RETRIEVAL CALL, NOT A REFERRAL LETTER — MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33, RFDS to the WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S or the receiving gynaecology unit. Stable outpatients use PATS. Sexual health follow-up through the ACCHS or SA Health services; TIS National 131 450.**

**SICORA — AND THE SHIFT: where, how bad, what's it like, onset, 'DID THE PAIN START WHERE IT IS NOW, OR SOMEWHERE ELSE AND MOVE?', radiation — SHOULDER TIP?, anything better or worse.**

**THE RANKING SENTENCE — appendicitis, PID and ectopic — ECTOPIC AT THE TOP, WITH THE FOUR REASONS.**
**NAMING IT TO LILY — pregnant, AND in the wrong place — hospital today.**

**WHY THE OTHERS RANK LOWER, then OVARIAN TORSION, UTI and URETERIC COLIC.** Then **serum βhCG, group and hold, URGENT TRANSVAGINAL ULTRASOUND, gynaecology today — and 'if you feel faint, get shoulder pain, or bleed heavily, call an ambulance.'**

stem: Jane Alcorta, 24, presents with right-sided lower abdominal pain since this morning. LMP exactly 14 days ago; two previous similar episodes. Ultrasound report: small ruptured right ovarian follicle with a little free fluid; gallstones with a normal gallbladder wall and no duct dilatation; appendix not visualised.
tasks: Take a focused history (5 minutes)
Explain the ultrasound report to the patient
Explain your diagnosis and differentials
findings: THE STEM SAYS 'RIGHT-SIDED' — NOT UPPER OR LOWER
THAT IS WHY YOU ASK LIVER AND GALLBLADDER QUESTIONS EVEN THOUGH THE PAIN IS LOW. And the hidden agenda sits there: HER MOTHER HAD GALLSTONES AND SURGERY, AND SHE IS SCARED SHE NEEDS AN OPERATION
THE ULTRASOUND REPORT — three findings, one explanation
A SMALL RUPTURED RIGHT OVARIAN FOLLICLE WITH A LITTLE FREE FLUID · GALLSTONES WITH A NORMAL GALLBLADDER WALL AND NO DUCT DILATATION · APPENDIX NOT VISUALISED, NO HISTORY OF APPENDICECTOMY
LMP EXACTLY 14 DAYS AGO → ASK ABOUT PREVIOUS IDENTICAL EPISODES
'HAVE YOU HAD PAIN LIKE THIS BEFORE, AROUND THE SAME TIME IN YOUR CYCLE?' → TWO PREVIOUS SIMILAR EPISODES THAT SETTLED ON THEIR OWN. MID-CYCLE, RECURRENT, SELF-LIMITING — OVULATION
WHAT SHE GIVES

MILD PAIN, 4–5/10 · SINCE THIS MORNING · BETTER WITH REST AND PARACETAMOL · NO SHIFT · NO LOSS OF APPETITE · NO NAUSEA OR VOMITING · NO FEVER · NO VAGINAL BLEEDING OR DISCHARGE · VERY WORRIED ABOUT HER MOTHER'S GALLBLADDER
THE PREGNANCY TEST IS STILL MANDATORY
EVEN WITH AN ULTRASOUND IN HAND, EVEN WHEN THE STORY IS BENIGN: 'IF I COULD DO ONE THING IT WOULD BE A URINE PREGNANCY TEST.' DECLARING MITTELSCHMERZ BEFORE THE PREGNANCY TEST IS A LISTED ERROR
THE APPENDIX NOT BEING SEEN IS EXPECTED, NOT SUSPICIOUS

UP TO 50–85% OF NORMAL APPENDICES ARE NOT VISUALISED ON ULTRASOUND. So the exclusion rests on the CLINICAL PICTURE — say it as a list: NO SHIFT, NO LOSS OF APPETITE, NO NAUSEA OR VOMITING, NO FEVER, MILD, RECURRENT AND CYCLICAL
THE GALLSTONES EXPLAIN NOTHING HERE

GALLSTONES WITHOUT INFLAMMATION — NO WALL THICKENING, NO DUCT DILATATION — IN A PATIENT WHOSE PAIN IS IN THE RIGHT LOWER QUADRANT. LETTING AN INCIDENTAL GALLSTONE CHANGE A CORRECT DIAGNOSIS IS A STARRED FAIL
ASK THE BILIARY QUESTIONS ANYWAY — so you can exclude aloud

PAIN UNDER THE RIGHT RIBS OR TO THE RIGHT SHOULDER · AFTER FATTY MEALS · YELLOWING · DARK URINE, PALE STOOLS · FEVER. All negative — and that is what lets you tell her she does not need her gallbladder out
THE FREE FLUID — two meanings
IN HER, IT IS PHYSIOLOGICAL FOLLICULAR FLUID AND A LITTLE BLOOD FROM THE RUPTURED FOLLICLE. IN A SHOCKED WOMAN WITH A POSITIVE PREGNANCY TEST, THE SAME APPEARANCE IS HAEMOPERITONEUM
STILL RUN THE O&G BLOCK
Bleeding, discharge, LMP, regularity, could you be pregnant, sexually active, contraception, safe sex, previous STI — the block that contains every dangerous alternative

FAIL — Calling the non-visualised appendix suspicious.
FAIL — No pregnancy test because there's already an ultrasound.

dx: **MITTELSCHMERZ — MID-CYCLE OVULATION PAIN — from RUPTURE OF THE OVARIAN FOLLICLE AT OVULATION, with a small bleed and follicular fluid entering the peritoneum. NOT A DISEASE — A NORMAL PROCESS.** **With INCIDENTAL, UNINFLAMED GALLSTONES and a NORMAL NON-VISUALISED APPENDIX.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: REFUSING TO BE MOVED BY AN INCIDENTAL FINDING. Candidates fail Version C by LETTING AN INCIDENTAL GALLSTONE CHANGE A CORRECT DIAGNOSIS. STONES PLUS A NON-FITTING STORY EQUALS AN INCIDENTAL FINDING.**

**THE SCAN IN THREE, VERBATIM: 'Jane, the scan shows THREE THINGS. ONE: A FOLLICLE IN YOUR RIGHT OVARY HAS BURST AND RELEASED FLUID — THAT EXPLAINS YOUR PAIN. TWO: there are SOME STONES IN YOUR GALLBLADDER, but they are NOT BLOCKING ANYTHING, the wall is NOT THICKENED and there is NO INFLAMMATION, so THEY ARE NOT CAUSING THIS PAIN AND YOU DO NOT NEED YOUR GALLBLADDER OUT. THREE: WE COULD NOT SEE YOUR APPENDIX — that is A VERY COMMON AND NORMAL FINDING ON ULTRASOUND, and it DOES NOT MEAN YOU HAVE APPENDICITIS.'**

**EXPLAIN OVULATION ON THE CYCLE: 'every month, around the MIDDLE OF YOUR CYCLE — about DAY 14 — one of your ovaries RELEASES AN EGG. The egg sits in a little fluid-filled bubble called a follicle, and when it BURSTS, a little fluid and sometimes a little blood can irritate the lining of your tummy. That's the pain, and it's why you've had it before at the same time of the month.'**

**WHY APPENDICITIS IS CONFIDENTLY EXCLUDED — THE LIST THE EXAMINER IS WAITING FOR: NO SHIFT OF THE PAIN · NO LOSS OF APPETITE · NO NAUSEA OR VOMITING · NO FEVER · THE PAIN IS MILD, RECURRENT AND CYCLICAL. The non-visualised appendix is EXPECTED — a large majority of normal appendices aren't seen.**

**IT IS STILL A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION — THE PREGNANCY TEST IS MANDATORY: ectopic pregnancy and ovarian torsion must be off the table, and 'DECLARING MITTELSCHMERZ BEFORE THE PREGNANCY TEST' is on the avoid list.**

**ADDRESS THE AGENDA DIRECTLY: 'I know you were worried because of your mum's gallbladder. The stones we saw are QUIET — they're not causing trouble, and MOST PEOPLE WITH QUIET GALLSTONES NEVER NEED SURGERY. What would make me think again is SUDDEN SEVERE PAIN UNDER YOUR RIGHT RIBS AFTER FOOD, A FEVER, OR YELLOWING OF YOUR SKIN OR EYES.'**

**MANAGEMENT — REASSURANCE WITH REASONS: rest when it happens · SIMPLE ANALGESIA — paracetamol or ibuprofen · a HEAT PACK on the lower abdomen · for recurrent troublesome pain, THE COMBINED ORAL CONTRACEPTIVE PILL is thought to help by suppressing ovulation · RED FLAGS — pain getting worse, UNUSUAL VAGINAL BLEEDING, fever → emergency department.** VERIFY — no strong Australian guideline; SAY SO IF PUSHED.

**THE DIFFERENTIALS BY GROUP: O&G — ECTOPIC PREGNANCY (pregnancy test), OVARIAN TORSION OR CYST (mild, settling, no mass), PID (no discharge, no fever) · GI — APPENDICITIS (excluded clinically), biliary colic (quiet stones, pain site wrong), gastroenteritis · KUB — UTI, URETERIC COLIC · hernia.**

**THE SAME FREE FLUID MEANS SOMETHING ELSE IN A DIFFERENT PATIENT — physiological here, HAEMOPERITONEUM in a shocked woman with a positive test. That is why the pregnancy test and the clinical picture decide it, not the scan alone.**

**'HAVE YOU HAD PAIN LIKE THIS BEFORE, AROUND THE SAME TIME IN YOUR CYCLE?' → two previous episodes that settled.**
**GI GENERAL: nausea, vomiting, APPETITE, bloating, bowel habit, FEVER.** Then **red flags, briefly.**
**BECAUSE THE STEM SAYS RIGHT-SIDED — THE BILIARY QUESTIONS: pain under the right ribs or to the shoulder · after fatty meals · yellowing · dark urine, pale stools.**
**KUB THREE and the groin.**
**O&G BLOCK: bleeding · discharge · LMP — EXACTLY 14 DAYS · regular · could you be pregnant · sexually active · contraception · previous STI.**
**SADMA, past and family history — the mother's gallbladder — and a summary.**
**'IF I COULD DO ONE THING IT WOULD BE A URINE PREGNANCY TEST.'**
**EXPLAIN THE ULTRASOUND IN THREE — follicle explains it; stones are quiet, no surgery; appendix not seen is normal.**
**THE DIAGNOSIS — MITTELSCHMERZ — explained on the cycle, with the reasons: day 14, recurrent, mild, settling.**
**WHY APPENDICITIS IS EXCLUDED, AS A LIST, then the grouped differentials — ectopic, torsion, PID, biliary, UTI.**

THE RULE FOR A TWO-COMPLAINT STEM

PICK THE COMPLAINT WHOSE DIFFERENTIAL LIST IS LONGER AND OVERLAPS THE OTHER — BLOATING BEATS CONSTIPATION: cancer, obstruction, coeliac, IBD and IBS cause both, and bloating adds the ovarian and dietary groups. dx: **OVARIAN CANCER — the 'SILENT KILLER', so called because it produces ONLY VAGUE GASTROINTESTINAL AND URINARY SYMPTOMS UNTIL IT IS ADVANCED. MOST AUSTRALIAN CASES ARE DIAGNOSED AT STAGE III OR IV.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THINKING OVARIAN BEFORE THE ULTRASOUND ARRIVES — AND EXAMINING THE ABDOMEN. The diagnosis is handed to you on a card; WHAT IS MARKED IS EVERYTHING BEFORE THE CARD: early satiety and distension, family history of BREAST as well as ovarian cancer, menstrual and postmenopausal bleeding history, and asking to examine abdomen and pelvis.**

**THE EXAMINER'S OWN STANDARD: you will pass on a good structure for the presenting complaint EVEN IF YOU DON'T NAME OVARIAN CANCER FROM HISTORY ALONE — the ultrasound is deliberately unambiguous. BUT THE CANDIDATE WHO NEVER ASKS A SINGLE OVARIAN QUESTION AND NEVER EXAMINES THE ABDOMEN HAS NOTHING TO CONNECT THE RESULT TO.**

**NAMING THE CONCERN DURING THE HISTORY: 'some of what you've described — the BLOATING, FEELING FULL QUICKLY, and NEEDING TO PASS URINE MORE OFTEN — can occasionally come from THE OVARIES, so those are things I always check for. I'd like to EXAMINE YOUR TUMMY now, and then arrange AN ULTRASOUND OF YOUR PELVIS AND A BLOOD TEST.'**

**THE SECOND DISCRIMINATING MOMENT — BREAKING THE NEWS. WARNING SHOT, THEN PAUSE: 'I have the results of your scan here, and I'M AFRAID IT ISN'T WHAT WE WERE HOPING FOR. IS THERE SOMEONE WITH YOU TODAY, OR SOMEONE YOU'D LIKE ME TO CALL?' (pause — let her respond.) DELIVER PLAINLY: 'the scan has shown A GROWTH ON YOUR RIGHT OVARY. There are features that CONCERN ME — IT ISN'T A SIMPLE, HARMLESS CYST. Together with your symptoms, I'M WORRIED THIS COULD BE A CANCER OF THE OVARY.' (pause) 'I know that's a very frightening thing to hear.'**

**REASON, THEN PLAN: 'the reason I'm saying that is THE COMBINATION — your symptoms have gone on for months, and THE SCAN SHOWS A MASS WITH CONCERNING FEATURES. I'll REFER YOU URGENTLY TO A SPECIALIST GYNAECOLOGICAL CANCER TEAM. They'll arrange a CT and a blood test, and THE DEFINITE ANSWER COMES FROM SURGERY, where they take the tissue and examine it. I'LL MAKE THAT REFERRAL TODAY.'**

**DO NOT EXPLAIN THE ULTRASOUND IN TECHNICAL TERMS — 'SEPTATIONS', 'SOLID COMPONENTS' AND 'PAPILLARY PROJECTIONS' BELONG IN YOUR ANSWER TO THE EXAMINER. TO HER, SAY 'CONCERNING FEATURES' AND STOP.** **Ultrasound red flags: THICK WALL OVER 3 mm, THICK SEPTATIONS, SOLID COMPONENTS, PAPILLARY PROJECTIONS, BILATERAL, LARGE, ASCITES, DOPPLER FLOW.**
**NEVER BIOPSY A SUSPICIOUS OVARIAN CYST PERCUTANEOUSLY — RISK OF SPILLAGE AND UPSTAGING. Tissue is obtained at SURGICAL STAGING by a gynaecological oncologist.**

**CA-125 IS RAISED IN ONLY ABOUT HALF OF EARLY-STAGE DISEASE and is also raised by endometriosis, fibroids, PID, menstruation, ascites, liver disease and heart failure — NOT A SCREENING TEST. RISK OF MALIGNANCY INDEX = U × M × CA-125, M = 1 PREMENOPAUSAL, 3 POSTMENOPAUSAL; referral commonly quoted at RMI ABOVE 200.** VERIFY against Cancer Council Australia and local gynae-oncology.

**REASON, THEN PLAN: urgent gynae-oncology referral today, CT and CA-125, definite answer from surgery.**

findings: TWO CLOCKS FOR THE SAME DISEASE

RESPOND BEFORE YOU QUESTION — SEPARATELY MARKED

'I'M SORRY YOU'VE BEEN DEALING WITH THAT FOR A WEEK, MARY — THAT MUST BE WEARING. I'D LIKE TO ASK YOU SOME QUESTIONS TO WORK OUT WHAT'S CAUSING IT, AND THEN I'LL EXPLAIN WHAT I THINK IS GOING ON. IS THAT ALL RIGHT?'
THE PLANTED POSITIVE — A SCREENING 'YES' IS A STOP SIGN

dx: **PELVIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE — infection ASCENDING FROM THE VAGINA AND CERVIX INTO THE UPPER GENITAL TRACT, producing ENDOMETRITIS, SALPINGITIS, TUBO-OVARIAN ABSCESS AND PELVIC PERITONITIS.** **Usually sexually acquired — CHLAMYDIA AND GONORRHOEA, with MYCOPLASMA GENITALIUM and vaginal anaerobes; IN A SUBSTANTIAL PROPORTION NO ORGANISM IS EVER IDENTIFIED.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE — VERSION A: DEVELOP THE POSITIVE FINDING, DON'T JUST RECORD IT. Characterise the discharge, ask the risk factors that go with it, then QUOTE IT BACK AS THE REASON FOR YOUR DIAGNOSIS.** **VERSION B: TREAT TODAY. 'I'll swab her and start treatment when the results come back' FAILS THE MANAGEMENT TASK, however correct the antibiotics — THE COST OF WAITING IS A SCARRED TUBE.**

**THE REASONING REPLAY, TO MARY: 'most likely you have PELVIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE — an infection has travelled up from the neck of the womb into the womb and the tubes. FOUR REASONS: the pain has been in your lower tummy for a week and IT NEVER MOVED — different from appendicitis. You've had A YELLOW DISCHARGE WITH AN UNPLEASANT SMELL. SEX HAS BEEN PAINFUL DEEP INSIDE, and you've had SOME BLEEDING AFTERWARDS. And when I examined you, MOVING THE NECK OF THE WOMB WAS PAINFUL AND THE WOMB AND THE RIGHT SIDE WERE TENDER.'**

**WHY EACH SIGN EXISTS — say it plainly and the explanation writes itself: MUCOPURULENT CERVICAL DISCHARGE AND CONTACT BLEEDING — CERVICITIS · UTERINE TENDERNESS — ENDOMETRITIS · ADNEXAL TENDERNESS — SALPINGITIS · A MASS — ABSCESS. ANY ONE OF THE THREE TENDERNESS SIGNS, IN A WOMAN AT RISK, IS ENOUGH TO START TREATMENT.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS IN GROUPS, ECTOPIC FIRST, ONE REASON EACH: ECTOPIC PREGNANCY — EXCLUDED BY THE βhCG · APPENDICITIS — NO MIGRATION, NO ANOREXIA, TENDERNESS PELVIC RATHER THAN AT McBURNEY'S · OVARIAN TORSION — GRADUAL ONSET, NO MASS · RUPTURED CYST · ENDOMETRIOSIS — cyclical, months to years · UTI — NO DYSURIA, CLEAR DIPSTICK · BACTERIAL VAGINOSIS OR CANDIDA — discharge WITHOUT pelvic tenderness · CERVICAL CANCER — never screened, post-coital bleeding, so still worth a screening test.**

**TREATMENT — THE SHAPE: NON-SEVERE, OUTPATIENT — CEFTRIAXONE 500 mg IM ONCE, PLUS DOXYCYCLINE 100 mg BD FOR 14 DAYS, PLUS METRONIDAZOLE 400 mg BD FOR 14 DAYS. SEVERE OR UNABLE TO TOLERATE ORAL — ADMIT FOR IV THERAPY, GYNAECOLOGY; an abscess may need drainage. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: COVER GONORRHOEA, CHLAMYDIA AND ANAEROBES.** VERIFY against current Therapeutic Guidelines or Australian STI Management Guidelines. **An IUD can usually stay while treatment starts.**

**PARTNER NOTIFICATION IS NOT OPTIONAL, AND IT IS EXAMINABLE — SAY BOTH SENTENCES ALOUD: TRACE AND TREAT ALL PARTNERS FROM THE PRECEDING SIX MONTHS, whether or not they have symptoms or results · ABSTAIN FROM SEX UNTIL SEVEN DAYS AFTER TREATMENT IS COMPLETED AND ALL PARTNERS HAVE BEEN TREATED.** VERIFY look-back periods. **Retest at THREE MONTHS — reinfection is common.**

**ADMIT IF: TEMPERATURE ABOVE 38 OR SEPTIC · VOMITING, UNABLE TO TOLERATE ORAL · A TENDER ADNEXAL MASS — TUBO-OVARIAN ABSCESS · PERITONITIS · PREGNANCY · NO IMPROVEMENT AT 48–72 HOURS · SURGICAL CAUSE NOT EXCLUDED.** **Ultrasound is NOT the first move — PID IS A CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS; a normal scan doesn't exclude it.**

**COMPLICATIONS, ONCE, AS THE REASON FOR FINISHING THE COURSE — NOT AS A THREAT: 'untreated or recurrent infection can SCAR THE TUBES, which can make it HARDER TO GET PREGNANT, RAISE THE CHANCE OF A PREGNANCY IN THE TUBE, and cause LONG-TERM PELVIC PAIN. That's why we treat it early and in full.'** **Mention FITZ-HUGH–CURTIS perihepatitis if asked about RUQ pain.**

**SA: CHLAMYDIA AND GONORRHOEA ARE NOTIFIABLE — say you know the laboratory notifies · ADELAIDE SEXUAL HEALTH CENTRE (CLINIC 275) · the anonymous LET THEM KNOW service — ANONYMITY OFTEN CONVERTS A REFUSAL INTO A YES · the rural sentence: 'in a small town confidentiality is a real concern for a nineteen-year-old, so I'd discuss where she'd prefer follow-up.'** **Sexual coercion or an under-age partner — ASK, AND ACT.**

findings: THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES THE STATION

'CAN I CHECK WHAT YOU MEAN BY THAT? DO YOU MEAN YOU FEEL BLOATED AND FULL OF WIND, OR HAS YOUR TUMMY ACTUALLY GOT BIGGER — WAISTBAND TIGHTER, CLOTHES NOT DOING UP?' BLOATING IS A SENSATION; DISTENSION IS A MEASURABLE INCREASE IN GIRTH — AND DISTENSION IS THE ONE THAT TURNS OUT TO BE A MASS OR ASCITES. DEFINE IT BY 1:20
SIX CAUSES OF A BIGGER ABDOMEN
FAT · FLUID · FLATUS · FAECES · FOETUS · FATAL GROWTH. The opening question decides which of TWO DIFFERENTIAL SPINES you run first — and you have six minutes for both
SAY BOTH LIST NAMES OUT LOUD, EARLY

'JENNY, THERE ARE TWO SORTS OF THINGS THAT MAKE A TUMMY GET BIGGER — PROBLEMS IN THE BOWEL, AND THINGS THAT CAUSE WEIGHT OR FLUID TO BUILD UP. I'M GOING TO ASK ABOUT BOTH.' That single sentence tells the examiner you know the structure of the station
THE CARD

A MASS FELT IN THE RIGHT ILIAC FOSSA · OBSERVATIONS NORMAL. EVERYONE WORKS OUT IT'S OVARIAN CANCER ONCE THE CARD APPEARS — THE DIAGNOSIS IS NOT WHAT IS BEING MARKED. What's marked is defining the complaint, running TWO complete lists, SAYING 'OVARIAN CANCER' ALOUD, and giving reasons
WHAT SHE GIVES WHEN ASKED

PROGRESSIVE BLOATING AND DISTENSION OVER 3–4 MONTHS · TIGHTER WAISTBAND · NEW CONSTIPATION · FULL AFTER HALF A PLATE · PASSING URINE MORE OFTEN · MOTHER HAD BREAST CANCER AT 50. No bleeding, no melaena, no postmenopausal bleeding, still passing wind
THE OVARIAN CLUSTER — by 4:30

'DO YOU FEEL FULL AFTER ONLY A SMALL AMOUNT OF FOOD? ANY PAIN LOW IN THE TUMMY OR PELVIS? PASSING URINE MORE OFTEN, OR A SUDDEN URGE? HOW LONG, AND HOW OFTEN IN A MONTH?' PERSISTENT, NEW, AND MORE THAN TWELVE TIMES A MONTH IS THE INVESTIGATE THRESHOLD. EARLY SATIETY IS A CLUSTER SYMPTOM, NOT FUSSY EATING
'IT'S PROBABLY JUST MY AGE, ISN'T IT?'

'IT MIGHT BE — BUT A TUMMY THAT IS CHANGING AT 55 IS WORTH CHECKING PROPERLY RATHER THAN ASSUMING.' MATCHING HER EXPECTATION ENDS THE STATION; SAYING 'CANCER' IN THE FIRST THIRTY SECONDS FRIGHTENS HER BEFORE YOU HAVE EVIDENCE
'MUM HAD BREAST CANCER AT 50'
'THAT'S RELEVANT, THANK YOU — BREAST AND OVARIAN CANCER CAN RUN IN FAMILIES TOGETHER.' Ask about BOWEL, OVARIAN, BREAST AND UTERINE cancer, AND THE AGES

'ANY LUMP IN YOUR GROIN? ANY ABDOMINAL OPERATIONS? ARE YOU STILL PASSING WIND NORMALLY?' IF SHE HAS STOPPED PASSING WIND, VOMITED, AND IT CAME ON OVER DAYS — 'I'D STOP HERE, EXAMINE HER, PUT IN A DRIP, KEEP HER NIL BY MOUTH AND ARRANGE AN URGENT SURGICAL REVIEW'

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: YOU ARE NOT MARKED FOR SAYING 'OVARIAN CANCER'. YOU ARE MARKED FOR ARRIVING THERE THROUGH TWO COMPLETE DIFFERENTIAL LISTS AND THEN HANDING BOTH LISTS BACK TO THE PATIENT.** **Almost every candidate recognises the mass. The ones who fail spent six minutes on a bowel history, never asked about periods, early satiety or urinary frequency, never swept thyroid, heart, kidney, liver or drug causes, and announced a diagnosis with no reasoning.**

Is it alright if I go through it with you now?' NAME THE CONCERN: 'there was A LUMP IN THE LOWER RIGHT PART OF YOUR ABDOMEN. Putting that together with everything you've told me, I'M CONCERNED ABOUT THE POSSIBILITY OF A CANCER OF THE OVARY. **THREE REASONS: 'FIRST, the bloating and the tummy getting bigger — ovarian cancer causes both, partly from wind and partly FROM FLUID COLLECTING. SECOND, the pattern — FEELING FULL AFTER A SMALL AMOUNT, THE CONSTIPATION, AND PASSING URINE MORE OFTEN. On their own each of those is nothing; TOGETHER, AND LASTING THIS LONG, THEY MATTER. THINGS THAT MAKE A TUMMY BIGGER FOR OTHER REASONS — fluid from the HEART, KIDNEYS OR LIVER, underactive THYROID, hormone conditions, MEDICATIONS, simple weight gain. Plus UTERINE FIBROIDS.**

**THE SECOND DISCRIMINATOR — THE WORD YOU MUST NOT USE: DO NOT SAY IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME AS THE ANSWER. It is a diagnosis of exclusion AND THERE IS A PALPABLE MASS ON THE CARD. Naming it here is the clearest signal you STOPPED THINKING WHEN YOU FOUND A COMFORTABLE ANSWER.**

tasks: Take a focused history (6 minutes)

findings: NO PHYSICAL EXAMINATION — EVERYTHING HANGS ON THE HISTORY

Six minutes of history, then explanation. NINE DIFFERENTIAL GROUPS WITHOUT AN EXAMINATION TO FALL BACK ON. You will not get through all of them in detail — you ARE expected to NAME EVERY GROUP AND ASK AT LEAST ONE DISCRIMINATING QUESTION IN EACH
QUANTIFY THE LOSS IN THE FIRST NINETY SECONDS

'HOW MANY KILOS HAVE YOU LOST, AND OVER WHAT PERIOD? WHAT DID YOU WEIGH BEFORE?' → ABOUT 6 kg OVER 4–5 MONTHS, UNINTENTIONAL. MORE THAN ABOUT 5% OF BODY WEIGHT OVER 6–12 MONTHS IS THE THRESHOLD FOR INVESTIGATION RATHER THAN OBSERVATION. YOU NEED THE PERCENTAGE, NOT AN ADJECTIVE
THE ORDER IS NOT NEGOTIABLE

MALIGNANCY AND INFECTION FIRST — between about 1:24 and 3:24, BEFORE ANYTHING THAT FEELS MORE COMFORTABLE. PSYCHIATRIC AND LIFESTYLE ARE NEVER SACRIFICED — THE DIAGNOSIS LIVES THERE. IF SHORT OF TIME, DROP THE RHEUMATOLOGICAL GROUP
'I'M AN ATHLETE — I TRAIN FOR THE OLYMPICS'
'THAT'S HELPFUL, THANK YOU — I'LL COME BACK TO THAT. FIRST I WANT TO RULE OUT A FEW THINGS.' THE WEAK CANDIDATE FEELS RELIEF, ABANDONS THE REMAINING GROUPS, AND DELIVERS A REASSURING EXPLANATION
'I TRAIN ABOUT EIGHT HOURS A DAY'

REPEAT IT BACK WITH A COMPARISON: THE ADULT GUIDELINE IS 150 TO 300 MINUTES A WEEK. Then HOW MANY DAYS A WEEK. And 'I HAVE A DIETITIAN, IT'S A PROPER PROGRAMME' → 'THAT'S GOOD. CAN YOU TALK ME THROUGH WHAT A NORMAL DAY OF EATING ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE?' An authority figure does not buy the plan a free pass
ASK INTAKE AND OUTPUT SEPARATELY

'WHAT WOULD YOU EAT ON A NORMAL DAY? HAS THAT CHANGED? WHO DECIDES WHAT YOU EAT?' AND 'WHAT DOES YOUR TRAINING LOOK LIKE — WHAT, HOW MANY HOURS, HOW MANY DAYS? HAS IT CHANGED?' OR YOU WILL ONLY GET ONE SIDE OF THE EQUATION
THE CONSEQUENCES — what turns a lifestyle finding into a diagnosis

'HAVE YOUR PERIODS CHANGED, BECOME LIGHTER, OR STOPPED? ANY CHANCE YOU COULD BE PREGNANT? ANY STRESS FRACTURES? DO YOU FEEL THE COLD? MORE INFECTIONS? PERFORMANCE DROPPING?' → PERIODS STOPPED A FEW MONTHS AGO, TIRED, FEELS THE COLD
THE EATING-DISORDER QUESTIONS — IN WORDS, NOT BY IMPLICATION

NORMALISE: 'THESE ARE QUESTIONS I ASK EVERYONE WHO COMES IN ABOUT THEIR WEIGHT.' THEN: HOW DO YOU FEEL ABOUT YOUR BODY · INTENSE FEAR OF GAINING WEIGHT · MAKING YOURSELF VOMIT, LAXATIVES, FLUID TABLETS, APPETITE SUPPRESSANTS · DO YOU EVER EXERCISE SPECIFICALLY TO MAKE UP FOR SOMETHING YOU'VE EATEN? — THE ONE CANDIDATES LEAVE OUT. THERE IS NO EXAMINATION, SO THE PURGING QUESTION MUST BE ASKED OUT LOUD
'WHY ARE YOU ASKING ABOUT HIV?'

'I ASK EVERYONE WITH UNEXPLAINED WEIGHT LOSS — INFECTIONS ARE ONE OF THE THINGS I HAVE TO RULE OUT.' Normalise BEFORE you ask: fever, sweats, travel, sexual history, injecting, TB contact, cough over three weeks
THE ONE RESPIRATORY QUESTION — ten seconds
'HAVE YOU EVER COUGHED UP BLOOD? ANY COUGH? ANY SHOULDER OR INNER-ARM PAIN?' COVERS THE LEGACY PANCOAST VERSION ENTIRELY

dx: **UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS DUE TO LOW ENERGY AVAILABILITY — EXCESSIVE TRAINING WITH INADEQUATE INTAKE — on the disordered-eating spectrum, with SECONDARY AMENORRHOEA AND CONSEQUENT BONE HEALTH RISK.** **To the patient: 'you are taking in less than your body is using.' To the examiner: RELATIVE ENERGY DEFICIENCY, ON THE DISORDERED-EATING SPECTRUM.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: FINDING THE EXPLANATION IS NOT THE SAME AS FINISHING THE STATION. Two things go wrong for the weak candidate — THE RED-FLAG GROUPS WERE NEVER COMPLETED, and THE FINDING WAS PRESENTED AS GOOD NEWS WHEN IT IS IN FACT THE PROBLEM. THE PASS SAYS CLEARLY: THIS IS WHAT IS CAUSING IT, AND THIS IS WHY IT STILL NEEDS TREATING.**

**THE CAUSE, IN CONTEXT: 'Anna, I think I know why you're losing weight, and I want to explain it properly rather than just reassure you. You're training AROUND EIGHT HOURS A DAY, most days. The general recommendation for adults is TWO AND A HALF TO FIVE HOURS A WEEK. At the same time your portions have come down. So YOU'RE TAKING IN LESS ENERGY THAN YOUR BODY IS USING, and the weight loss is the body making up the difference from its own reserves.'**

**WHY IT MATTERS EVEN THOUGH IT EXPLAINS THINGS: 'when that gap goes on for months, the body SHUTS DOWN THE THINGS IT CONSIDERS OPTIONAL. That's why YOUR PERIODS HAVE STOPPED — and that isn't a side issue, because THE HORMONE THAT DRIVES YOUR CYCLE IS ALSO WHAT KEEPS YOUR BONES STRONG. Left alone this leads to STRESS FRACTURES, MORE INFECTIONS, and — the thing that usually gets athletes' attention — PERFORMANCE THAT GOES BACKWARDS no matter how hard you train.'**

**THE SECOND DISCRIMINATOR — THE WORD 'INTENTIONAL': she's not trying to lose weight, and that's true. IT RULES OUT ONE CRITERION OF ANOREXIA NERVOSA; IT DOES NOT RULE OUT THE SPECTRUM, AND IT DOES NOT MAKE THE RESTRICTION HARMLESS. THE SECOND SENTENCE OF YOUR OPENING — it buys the pivot

'THAT SOUNDS FRUSTRATING, AND YOU DID THE RIGHT THING COMING IN. I CAN ALSO SEE YOU'VE HAD SOME BLOOD TESTS DONE, AND THERE ARE A COUPLE OF THINGS IN THERE I WANT TO TALK TO YOU ABOUT BEFORE YOU LEAVE.' 'I'VE PUT ON SIX OR SEVEN KILOS OVER ABOUT SIX MONTHS' → what he weighed before; a RATE, not an adjective. 'NOTHING HAS CHANGED, THAT'S THE STRANGE PART' → 'LET'S GO THROUGH IT ANYWAY' — PATIENTS DO NOT PERCEIVE SLOW LIFESTYLE DRIFT AS CHANGE
SAY THE GROUP NAME BEFORE THE QUESTIONS

FLUID RETENTION — THREE ORGANS, THREE QUESTIONS

HEART — breathless on exertion, LYING FLAT, waking at night; ankle swelling · KIDNEY — 'ANY PROBLEMS WITH YOUR WATERWORKS — FROTHY URINE, PASSING LESS?' — the nephrotic question candidates skip · LIVER — yellowing, tummy swelling

FEAR OF WEIGHT GAIN · VOMITING, LAXATIVES, FLUID TABLETS · 'EPISODES WHERE YOU EAT A LARGE AMOUNT IN A SHORT TIME AND FEEL OUT OF CONTROL?' — BINGE-EATING DISORDER IS THE COMMONEST EATING DISORDER IN AUSTRALIA AND FREQUENTLY MISSED IN MEN · MOOD · SNORING, WITNESSED APNOEAS

DOES NOT DRINK AT ALL · TAKEAWAY 4–5 NIGHTS A WEEK · TWO LITRES OF SOFT DRINK A DAY · DESK JOB · NO EXERCISE · SLEEPS POORLY AND SNORES. No cold intolerance, no orthopnoea, no oedema, no frothy urine, no striae, no weight-gaining medications, no jaundice

dx: **TWO ANSWERS, AND YOU MUST GIVE BOTH. THE WEIGHT GAIN IS LIFESTYLE — excess energy intake with very low activity. THE ABNORMAL BLOODS ARE METABOLIC DYSFUNCTION-ASSOCIATED STEATOTIC LIVER DISEASE (MASLD) — fatty liver — WHICH IS A CONSEQUENCE OF THE WEIGHT, NOT THE CAUSE OF IT.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: DELIVER TWO SEPARATE MESSAGES, AND DO NOT MERGE THEM. FATTY LIVER DOES NOT CAUSE WEIGHT GAIN. 'You are putting on weight because you have a fatty liver' INVERTS CAUSE AND EFFECT in front of an examiner and the whole explanation task collapses.**

**THE EXPLANATION, IN ORDER: 'James, I've got TWO THINGS TO TELL YOU and they're CONNECTED BUT NOT THE SAME THING. FIRST, THE WEIGHT. From what you've told me — takeaway most nights, a couple of litres of soft drink a day, a desk job and no regular exercise — the most likely reason is that YOU'RE TAKING IN MORE ENERGY THAN YOU'RE USING. I WENT LOOKING FOR MEDICAL CAUSES AND COULDN'T FIND ONE: your thyroid test is normal, no signs of heart, kidney or hormone problems, and no medication that does this.'**

**'SECOND, YOUR BLOOD TESTS. Three are mildly off — two liver enzymes, your blood fats, and your sugar is at the top of normal. TOGETHER, that pattern points to FATTY LIVER. When there's more fat around than the body can store in the usual places, SOME ENDS UP IN THE LIVER, and that irritates it. THE IMPORTANT PART: AT THIS STAGE IT IS REVERSIBLE — losing around FIVE TO TEN PER CENT of your body weight can clear the fat and settle the enzymes.'**

**'SO MY LIVER'S DAMAGED?' — 'IT IS NOT DAMAGED. THERE IS FAT IN IT, AND THAT IS REVERSIBLE AT THIS STAGE.' Reassure about REVERSIBILITY, NOT ABOUT THE ABSENCE OF DISEASE — 'it's only mild, don't worry' is false reassurance.**

**CORRECTION — HbA1c 5.7% IS NOT PRE-DIABETES IN AUSTRALIA. That is the American cut-off. AUSTRALIA: 6.0–6.4% HIGH RISK; 6.5% OR ABOVE DIABETES. Say: 'I'm using the Australian thresholds — 5.7% is at the upper end of normal, BUT IN A MAN WITH THIS WAIST AND LIPID PROFILE IT IS STILL WORTH ACTING ON; I'd screen with AUSDRISK and repeat it.' 'AM I DIABETIC?' — 'NOT ON THIS RESULT.'**

**GROUPED DIFFERENTIALS: ENDOCRINE — hypothyroidism (TSH normal — SAY SO), Cushing (no striae or proximal weakness; EXOGENOUS STEROID FAR COMMONER) · FLUID RETENTION — heart failure, CKD or nephrotic, cirrhosis — all unlikely · HEPATIC — alcohol-related liver disease (excluded by history), viral hepatitis (still serologically excluded) · DRUGS — steroids, antipsychotics, VALPROATE, MIRTAZAPINE, PREGABALIN, GABAPENTIN, lithium, insulin, sulfonylureas · PSYCHIATRIC — BINGE-EATING DISORDER, depression · OSA — worsens it, not the cause.**

**READING THE LIVER NUMBERS: PATTERN FIRST (hepatocellular), THEN MAGNITUDE (under 5× — the fatty liver range), THEN RATIO — AST:ALT BELOW 1 SUGGESTS FATTY LIVER; ABOVE 2 SUGGESTS ALCOHOL. NAME EITHER NAFLD/NASH OR THE NEWER MASLD/MASH TO THE EXAMINER; SAY 'FATTY LIVER' TO THE PATIENT.**

**STAGE IT — FIBROSIS MATTERS MORE THAN NAMING: CALCULATE FIB-4 from age, AST, ALT and platelets — BELOW 1.3 LOW RISK · 1.3–2.67 INDETERMINATE, DO ELASTOGRAPHY · ABOVE 2.67 REFER TO HEPATOLOGY, NOT A DIETITIAN ALONE.** **Weight-loss targets: ~5% IMPROVES THE FAT; 7–10% THE INFLAMMATION; 10%+ CAN IMPROVE FIBROSIS.**

**VERSION B — WHERE HE DOES DRINK: 6–8 standard drinks most nights for 20 years, minimised as 'a few beers'; AST:ALT ABOVE 2; spider naevi, palmar erythema, hepatomegaly, gynaecomastia → ALCOHOL-RELATED LIVER DISEASE. 'I'm not saying that to have a go at you — I'm saying it because IT'S THE ONE THING THAT WOULD MAKE THE BIGGEST DIFFERENCE. Can we talk about what cutting back might look like for you?'**

dx: **URETERIC COLIC — AN OBSTRUCTING RENAL CALCULUS, here at the VESICOURETERIC JUNCTION.** **Acute severe colicky pain from obstruction of the ureter by a stone. THE PAIN COMES FROM THE URETER CONTRACTING AGAINST THE BLOCKAGE AND FROM PRESSURE RISING IN THE COLLECTING SYSTEM BEHIND IT — NOT FROM THE STONE SCRAPING.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: INFECTION FIRST. SIZE SECOND. NEVER THE OTHER WAY ROUND. Every candidate recognises loin-to-groin colic. What separates them is whether they DECIDE OUT LOUD WHETHER THE OBSTRUCTED KIDNEY IS INFECTED — and whether they let a tender loin and blood in the urine talk them out of the diagnosis.**

**VERSION A — HOLD THE DIAGNOSIS, VERBATIM: 'I've been given tenderness in the right renal angle and blood on the dipstick. I want to be explicit that NEITHER OF THOSE CHANGES MY DIAGNOSIS. Renal angle tenderness is EXPECTED in ureteric colic, and the blood comes from the stone abrading the ureter. What would make me think pyelonephritis is A FEVER, or NITRITES AND LEUCOCYTES — he has neither. So this remains ureteric colic, and my next step is to prove that with a CT and a urine culture.'** **IF YOU RAISE PYELONEPHRITIS, RESOLVE IT IN THE SAME BREATH.**

**VERSION B — TWO PATHWAYS, IN THE RIGHT ORDER: 'what we do next depends on how big the stone is — BUT BEFORE ANY OF THAT, THERE ARE TWO THINGS I HAVE TO CHECK. First, THAT THERE IS NO INFECTION SITTING BEHIND THE BLOCKAGE — a urine culture. A STONE AND AN INFECTION TOGETHER IS THE ONE COMBINATION THAT NEEDS HOSPITAL THE SAME DAY. Second, a UEC for kidney function. Then — IF THE STONE IS SMALL, around 5 mm or less, most pass by themselves and we manage you at home. IF IT IS LARGER, around 7 mm or more, it is unlikely to pass on its own and I'd refer you to a urologist.'**

**THE THREE INVESTIGATIONS YOU MUST NAME: NON-CONTRAST CT KUB — THE GOLD STANDARD, confirming the stone, its position, size and obstruction · URINE MICROSCOPY, CULTURE AND SENSITIVITIES — because a stone plus infection is a different disease · UEC AND eGFR — renal impairment changes the plan from conservative to urgent.** **Ultrasound in pregnancy or where radiation must be avoided.**

**CONSERVATIVE PATHWAY (≤5 mm, well, afebrile, normal kidney function): IBUPROFEN 400 mg TDS WITH FOOD or INDOMETACIN 100 mg PR · OXYCODONE 5 mg if inadequate · ONDANSETRON or metoclopramide · TAMSULOSIN 400 microgram DAILY as medical expulsive therapy · STRAIN THE URINE AND CATCH THE STONE for analysis · REVIEW AT 48 HOURS · REFER IF NOT PASSED BY 4 WEEKS. DRINK TO THIRST — FORCED FLUIDS DO NOT EXPEL STONES AND WORSEN THE PAIN.** VERIFY.

**CORRECTION — TAMSULOSIN CAUSES POSTURAL HYPOTENSION, not 'hypertension' — plus abnormal or retrograde ejaculation, and INTRAOPERATIVE FLOPPY IRIS SYNDROME: 'I'd warn him to get up slowly and ASK WHETHER HE HAS CATARACT SURGERY BOOKED.' And name the operations correctly: URETEROSCOPY WITH LASER LITHOTRIPSY for a ureteric stone; PCNL is for stones inside the kidney.**

**ADDED — ANTIBIOTICS ALONE WILL NOT SAVE AN INFECTED OBSTRUCTED KIDNEY. PUS BEHIND AN OBSTRUCTION IS A CLOSED SPACE. IT MUST BE DRAINED — RETROGRADE URETERIC STENT OR PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROSTOMY — alongside IV fluids, blood cultures and IV antibiotics.** **Other same-day triggers: SOLITARY OR TRANSPLANTED KIDNEY, BILATERAL STONES, ANURIA, RISING CREATININE, UNCONTROLLED PAIN, PREGNANCY.**

**CORRECTION — THE SOURCE'S DIFFERENTIAL HAS ONE DANGEROUS GAP: A LEAKING ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSM presenting as first-episode 'renal colic' over 50 is the classic fatal misdiagnosis. At 40 it is very unlikely — BUT NAME IT ONCE: 'in anyone over fifty with a first episode I would exclude it before I settled on a stone.'** **Six groups: KUB · hepatobiliary (right-sided) · GI — appendicitis · groin and scrotum — hernia, TORSION · vascular — AAA · other — DKA, zoster, musculoskeletal.**

**PREVENTION: fluids 2.5–3 L a day aiming for over 2 L of urine · LOW SALT · NORMAL DIETARY CALCIUM — CORRECTION: DO NOT RESTRICT CALCIUM, IT INCREASES OXALATE ABSORPTION AND STONE RISK · reduce oxalate and animal protein · STONE ANALYSIS on every retrieved stone · family history raises his risk.** **SA: no after-hours CT at most Yorke Peninsula sites — discuss and transfer; MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 for a septic obstructed kidney; urology at RAH or TQEH; NO DRIVING ON OXYCODONE.**

dx: **BENIGN PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA CAUSING LOWER URINARY TRACT SYMPTOMS AND VISIBLE HAEMATURIA — non-malignant hyperplasia of the prostatic TRANSITION ZONE causing bladder outlet obstruction. BLEEDING COMES FROM DILATED FRAGILE SUBMUCOSAL VESSELS OVER THE ENLARGED GLAND — BPH IS A GENUINE CAUSE OF HAEMATURIA, NOT A BYSTANDER.** **MUST NOT MISS: UROTHELIAL (BLADDER) CARCINOMA · RENAL CELL CARCINOMA · PROSTATE CARCINOMA. FINDING BPH DOES NOT DISCHARGE THE DUTY TO EXCLUDE THEM.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: GIVING A CONFIDENT DIAGNOSIS WITHOUT CLOSING THE CASE. Hold two things at once — a confident provisional diagnosis AND an explicit, unhedged statement that VISIBLE HAEMATURIA IN A 55-YEAR-OLD MAN STILL REQUIRES CYSTOSCOPY AND UPPER TRACT IMAGING. Candidates fail in two opposite directions: some REASSURE — 'it's just your prostate'; others PANIC THE PATIENT — 'you might have cancer'. NEITHER PASSES.**

**THE SCRIPT: 'James, the most likely explanation for all of this is AN ENLARGED PROSTATE. That fits your symptoms and it fits what I felt on examination. But I want to be straight with you — WHENEVER A MAN YOUR AGE PASSES VISIBLE BLOOD IN THE URINE, WE HAVE A RULE THAT WE LOOK INSIDE THE BLADDER WITH A SMALL CAMERA AND TAKE A SPECIAL SCAN OF THE KIDNEYS, EVEN WHEN WE THINK WE ALREADY KNOW THE CAUSE. An enlarged prostate and something more serious CAN SIT SIDE BY SIDE, and the camera is the only way to be sure. I AM NOT EXPECTING TO FIND CANCER. I AM MAKING SURE WE DON'T MISS IT.'**

**'DOCTOR, IS IT CANCER?' — 'IT'S ONE OF THE THINGS I HAVE TO RULE OUT, and that's exactly why I want the camera test. IT IS NOT THE MOST LIKELY CAUSE.'** **NEVER PROMISE 'I'M SURE IT'S NOTHING SERIOUS' — you have not excluded cancer.**

**IF THE EXAMINER CHALLENGES THE REFERRAL: 'NEITHER ANTICOAGULATION NOR BENIGN ENLARGEMENT IS ACCEPTED AS AN EXPLANATION FOR VISIBLE HAEMATURIA. Men on antiplatelets or anticoagulants have at least the same rate of underlying malignancy — THE BLEEDING TENDENCY UNMASKS DISEASE RATHER THAN CAUSING IT.' The age threshold varies between guidelines — BUT A 55-YEAR-OLD MEETS EVERY ONE.** **NEVER STOP THE ASPIRIN UNILATERALLY.**
**DRE PATTERNS: BPH — SMOOTH, FIRM-RUBBERY, SULCUS FELT · CARCINOMA — NODULAR, STONY HARD, SULCUS LOST · PROSTATITIS — BOGGY AND EXQUISITELY TENDER.**

**DIFFERENTIALS BY SYSTEM, ORDERED BY WHAT IT COSTS TO MISS: OBSTRUCTIVE — BPH · MALIGNANT — BLADDER (smoker, clots, aniline dye or rubber exposure), RENAL CELL, PROSTATE · INFECTION — cystitis, pyelonephritis, prostatitis, urethritis · STRUCTURAL — UROLITHIASIS (his past stones), glomerulonephritis, polycystic kidneys · DRUGS AND HAEMATOLOGICAL — ASPIRIN, CONTRIBUTORY ONLY · TRAUMA, EXERCISE · RARE — pseudohaematuria (beetroot, rifampicin), schistosomiasis, renal TB — THE ONES YOU SACRIFICE IF THE BELL GOES.**
**CORRECTION — PROSTATITIS IN A 55-YEAR-OLD is usually caused by UROPATHOGENIC E. COLI AND COLIFORMS, not an STI; the STI link holds under about 35. Screen briefly, don't build the case around it.**

**SAFETY-NET, ALL FOUR: 'if you CANNOT PASS URINE AT ALL and your lower tummy becomes PAINFUL AND SWOLLEN — or you start passing LARGE CLOTS — go straight to the emergency department. FEVER, SHAKES OR BACK PAIN — seen the same day. FAINT OR LIGHTHEADED — call an ambulance. I WILL CHASE YOUR RESULTS AND MAKE SURE THE UROLOGY APPOINTMENT HAPPENS — if you haven't heard within two weeks, ring me.'** **SA: urology at RAH, TQEH, Flinders or Lyell McEwin; PATS — A COUNTRY PATIENT WHO CANNOT AFFORD THE TRIP DOES NOT ATTEND, AND NON-ATTENDANCE IS HOW THESE CANCERS ARE MISSED.**

findings: THE STEM IS VAGUE ON PURPOSE

'A YOUNG MAN WHO PRESENTS COMPLAINING OF URINARY PROBLEMS.' USE THE TWO MINUTES TO LAY OUT THE WHOLE URINARY DIFFERENTIAL — dysuria, frequency, urgency, haematuria, retention. DO NOT WALK IN HAVING DECIDED IT IS A URINARY TRACT INFECTION
THE MOST COMMON UROLOGY STATION — AND A POOR PASS RATE

NOT BECAUSE THE DIAGNOSIS IS HARD. THREE ERRORS: 1 CANDIDATES DIAGNOSE A UTI — IT IS NOT ONE. 2 CANDIDATES ANSWER 'AN STI' — THAT IS NOT A DIAGNOSIS. 3 A THIN OR CLUMSY SEXUAL HISTORY — FLAGGED AS THE KEY POINT, MARKED NO, AND THE REST OF YOUR PERFORMANCE DOES NOT SAVE YOU
THE SECOND OPEN QUESTION — do not move on without it

'YEAH, I'VE JUST BEEN HAVING SOME PROBLEMS PASSING URINE.' → 'THANK YOU. CAN YOU TELL ME A BIT MORE ABOUT WHAT YOU MEAN BY PROBLEMS — WHAT EXACTLY ARE YOU NOTICING?' → 'IT STINGS. IT'S PAINFUL WHEN I PASS URINE.' DO NOT START A CHECKLIST UNTIL HE HAS NAMED A SYMPTOM
THE QUESTION THE CASE TURNS ON

'HAVE YOU HAD ANY DISCHARGE FROM YOUR PENIS?' THE TRIAD IS DYSURIA + FREQUENCY + DISCHARGE. THE FIRST TWO OVERLAP COMPLETELY WITH A UTI; THE DISCHARGE SEPARATES THEM — AND IT IS THE ONE SYMPTOM A PATIENT WILL NOT VOLUNTEER
★ THE TRAP — 'I HAD A DISCHARGE LAST WEEK BUT IT SETTLED'
IT COUNTS. 'HE HAS HAD DISCHARGE WITH THESE SYMPTOMS' — THAT IS URETHRITIS, NOT A UTI. And ABSENCE of discharge doesn't exclude it either — CHLAMYDIAL URETHRITIS IS FREQUENTLY MINIMALLY SYMPTOMATIC
THE PREAMBLE — LEARN IT VERBATIM

'JAMES, BEFORE I GO ON, I NEED TO ASK YOU SOME PERSONAL QUESTIONS ABOUT YOUR SEX LIFE. THEY WILL BE FAIRLY DETAILED, BUT EVERYTHING WE DISCUSS IS CONFIDENTIAL AND STAYS BETWEEN US, AND THESE ARE QUESTIONS I ASK ALL OF MY PATIENTS. IS THAT ALL RIGHT?' SENSITIVITY IS SCORED AS A SEPARATE KEY POINT
THE FIVE BLOCKS — 90 unhurried seconds

ACTIVITY — active now; ever · PARTNERS — regular, how many recently, MEN, WOMEN OR BOTH · PRACTICES — condoms always or sometimes; VAGINAL, ORAL OR ANAL · PAST INFECTION AND RISK — previous STI, sex under alcohol or drugs, paid for sex or partner from overseas, HIV TESTING OR PrEP
WHY THE SITES QUESTION IS NOT CURIOSITY

IT DETERMINES WHERE YOU SWAB. URETHRAL OR FIRST-VOID TESTING ALONE MISSES PHARYNGEAL AND ANORECTAL INFECTION. 'I ASK BECAUSE IT DETERMINES WHICH SITES I WOULD TEST' — converts an awkward question into a clinical one
TONE RULES

DO NOT APOLOGISE REPEATEDLY — ONE PREAMBLE, THEN ASK NORMALLY · 'I'VE GOT MALE PARTNERS' → DO NOT REACT, SAME TONE, SAME PACE · NO EDITORIALISING — 'YOU REALLY SHOULD BE USING CONDOMS' BELONGS AFTER THE DIAGNOSIS, FRAMED AS AN OFFER · DO NOT RUSH IT
WHAT HE GIVES

FIVE DAYS OF STINGING AND FREQUENCY · DISCHARGE FOR A DAY LAST WEEK THAT SETTLED · MULTIPLE PARTNERS · NO CONDOMS · MALE PARTNERS. No fever, no flank pain, no haematuria, no scrotal pain, no back-passage pain, no rash or ulcers

dx: **ACUTE URETHRITIS, MOST LIKELY SECONDARY TO A SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTION — CHLAMYDIA, GONORRHOEA OR MYCOPLASMA GENITALIUM.** **Definition for the patient: 'inflammation of the urethra — THE TUBE THAT CARRIES URINE OUT OF YOUR BLADDER.' Say the tube, not the Latin.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE — TWO THINGS, AND NEITHER IS THE DIAGNOSIS: THE SEXUAL HISTORY IS A DESIGNATED KEY POINT — not a section, a critical item; FIVE BLOCKS, IN ORDER, ASKED CALMLY. AND SENSITIVITY IS SCORED SEPARATELY FROM COMPLETENESS — permission, normalising, confidentiality, level tone.**

**SAY 'URETHRITIS', NOT 'AN STI'. 'STI' NAMES AN AETIOLOGY, NOT A DIAGNOSIS, and you have no test result to say which organism. THE SCORED PHRASING: 'ACUTE URETHRITIS, MOST LIKELY SECONDARY TO A SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTION'.**

**TO THE PATIENT, PLAIN WORDS, THREE REASONS: 'James, I think you most likely have URETHRITIS — inflammation or infection of the tube that carries urine out of your bladder. That's why it stings and why you're going more often. The most likely cause is A SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTION, because of THREE THINGS: YOUR SYMPTOMS; THE DISCHARGE YOU NOTICED LAST WEEK, WHICH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART; and the sexual history you've given me — more than one partner and not using condoms. IT IS COMMON, AND IT IS VERY TREATABLE.'**

**'WHY NOT SIMPLY CALL IT A UTI?' — 'Because he reports URETHRAL DISCHARGE, which is not a feature of cystitis, and because UNCOMPLICATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION IS UNCOMMON IN A HEALTHY YOUNG MAN. When it appears to be one, THINK URETHRITIS FIRST, and a structural or urological abnormality second.'**

**THE DIPSTICK TRAP: LEUCOCYTES POSITIVE WITH NITRITES NEGATIVE IN A YOUNG MAN IS STERILE PYURIA — IT POINTS TOWARDS URETHRITIS, NOT AWAY FROM IT. Nitrites need nitrate-reducing coliforms, which urethritis organisms are not.**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS IN FOUR GROUPS, A REASON EACH: GENITAL TRACT — PROSTATITIS (deep pain around the back passage — none), EPIDIDYMO-ORCHITIS (scrotal swelling, testicular pain — none) · URINARY TRACT — CYSTITIS AND PYELONEPHRITIS (no fever, no back pain, and they don't cause discharge), URETERIC COLIC (no loin pain, no blood) · SKIN — BALANITIS, CONTACT DERMATITIS, HERPETIC ULCERS (no rash or sores) · RED FLAGS — BLADDER OR KIDNEY CANCER (very unlikely at 24 with no blood or weight loss, but on the list).**

**'I WOULD NOT NAME AN ORGANISM WITHOUT TESTING. The common causes are chlamydia, gonorrhoea and Mycoplasma genitalium, and I WOULD TREAT EMPIRICALLY FOR THE FIRST TWO WHILE NUCLEIC ACID TESTING IS PENDING.'** **Tests: FIRST-VOID URINE NAAT for chlamydia, gonorrhoea and M. genitalium · SWABS FROM EVERY EXPOSED SITE — urethral, PHARYNGEAL, ANORECTAL · GRAM STAIN AND CULTURE OF DISCHARGE — gives susceptibility · HIV, SYPHILIS, HEPATITIS B AND C SEROLOGY.**

**MANAGEMENT IF ASKED: EMPIRICAL TREATMENT FOR CHLAMYDIA AND GONORRHOEA SAME VISIT per current Australian STI guidelines · CONTACT TRACING — SA Health and LET THEM KNOW for anonymous notification · ABSTINENCE UNTIL HE AND PARTNERS HAVE COMPLETED TREATMENT · TEST OF CURE where indicated — pharyngeal gonorrhoea, M. genitalium · NOTIFIABLE — chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis · OFFER VACCINATION (hepatitis A and B, HPV, mpox) AND DISCUSS PrEP.** VERIFY regimens and intervals.

**SA: SHINE SA for confidential care and contact-tracing support; Adelaide Sexual Health Centre for complex cases; sexual health telehealth for rural access · IN A SMALL TOWN, CONFIDENTIALITY MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL — offer an alternative service by name if he's worried about being recognised · if under the age of consent, SAFEGUARDING AND MANDATORY NOTIFICATION TAKE PRIORITY.**

findings: A COMMUNICATION STATION WEARING A PROCEDURE'S CLOTHES

EVERY CANDIDATE CAN LIST THE STEPS. THE PASS IS DECIDED BY WHETHER THE CONSENT WAS GENUINELY INFORMED AND WHETHER YOU BUILT IN THE SAFETY GATES. YOU ARE NOT REQUIRED TO PERFORM THE PROCEDURE. CANDIDATES FAIL ON OMISSION, NOT ON TIME
THE CASE

55-year-old, DAY 0 AFTER RIGHT HEMICOLECTOMY, MORPHINE PCA · NOT VOIDED SINCE THEATRE · SUPRAPUBIC DISCOMFORT · PALPABLE BLADDER · SCAN 780 mL · HR 96 · T 36.8 · pain 6/10. Drivers: OPIOID, ANAESTHESIA, PAIN, IMMOBILITY, SUPINE — on probable prostatic enlargement at 55. Distinguish from OLIGURIC AKI, where the bladder is empty
THE OPENING — ends with the agenda question

'I'VE BEEN ASKED TO PASS A SMALL TUBE CALLED A CATHETER TO DRAIN THE BLADDER. BEFORE WE DO ANYTHING AT ALL, I'D LIKE TO EXPLAIN EXACTLY WHAT THAT INVOLVES, GO THROUGH THE RISKS AND ANSWER ANY QUESTIONS. WOULD THAT BE ALRIGHT? AND IS THERE ANYTHING IN PARTICULAR YOU'RE WORRIED ABOUT BEFORE WE START?' THE BRIEF ALMOST ALWAYS CONTAINS A CONCERN — ask, or it arrives at minute seven
WIPE + R — THE CONTRAINDICATION SCREEN BEFORE ANY EQUIPMENT

BLOOD AT THE MEATUS · PERINEAL OR SCROTAL BRUISING · HIGH-RIDING PROSTATE · PELVIC TRAUMA → DO NOT PASS A URETHRAL CATHETER — urology, suprapubic, retrograde urethrogram. Also: SADDLE NUMBNESS, LEG WEAKNESS → CAUDA EQUINA OR EPIDURAL HAEMATOMA · FEVER, RIGORS, LOIN PAIN → infected system · known stricture, recent urethral surgery, LATEX ALLERGY
CHAPERONE, PRIVACY, MINIMAL EXPOSURE — every time, in order

CURTAINS, DOOR, A CHAPERONE OFFERED BY NAME, A SHEET, EXPLICIT PERMISSION. 'I'd rather my wife wasn't here' → agree at once. Goes quiet → 'A LOT OF MEN FIND THIS AWKWARD — THAT'S COMPLETELY NORMAL. YOU'LL ONLY BE UNCOVERED FOR THE MINUTE OR TWO IT TAKES'
RISKS NAMED, NOT GLOSSED

'THE COMMON THINGS ARE STINGING, A LITTLE BLOOD FOR A DAY, AND FEELING YOU NEED TO GO WHEN THE BLADDER IS EMPTY. THE ONE I MOST WANT YOU TO KNOW ABOUT IS INFECTION — IT RISES FOR EVERY DAY THE TUBE STAYS IN. LESS OFTEN IT CAN GRAZE THE WATER PIPE. RARELY PEOPLE REACT TO THE MATERIAL. AND OCCASIONALLY IT WON'T PASS — IF SO I STOP AND ASK UROLOGY RATHER THAN PUSH'
THE ALTERNATIVE, OFFERED HONESTLY

'WAIT A LITTLE LONGER WITH BETTER PAIN RELIEF AND PRIVACY TO TRY AGAIN, OR IF THE TUBE CAN'T BE PASSED, ONE THROUGH THE SKIN ABOVE THE PUBIC BONE. DOING NOTHING ISN'T SAFE AT THIS VOLUME — THE BLADDER MUSCLE CAN BE STRETCHED AND DAMAGED.' 'Can't I try once more?' → privacy, standing, a running tap, analgesia, A TIME-LIMITED TRIAL IF STABLE
★ THE SAFETY GATE, SAID OUT LOUD

'I WILL ONLY INFLATE THE LITTLE BALLOON ONCE I ACTUALLY SEE URINE DRAINING. IF NO URINE COMES, I DO NOT INFLATE ANYTHING — I STOP AND GET HELP.' AND INSERT TO THE HUB FIRST — THE BALLOON SITS ~2 cm PROXIMAL TO THE TIP, SO URINE CAN FLOW WHILE THE BALLOON IS STILL IN THE PROSTATIC URETHRA
THE EQUIPMENT — count the ports at the funnel end

TWO-WAY FOLEY, 14 Fr, MALE LENGTH 40–45 cm · catheterisation pack · STERILE GLOVES (two pairs) · PPE · 0.9% SODIUM CHLORIDE for meatal cleaning · LIGNOCAINE 2% GEL, single-use urethral syringe · 10 mL STERILE WATER and syringe — NEVER SALINE · CLOSED DRAINAGE BAG · STATLOCK OR LEG STRAP · underpad, waste bag
THE NUMBERS

14 Fr DEFAULT (12–16); Fr ÷ 3 = mm · BALLOON — THE VOLUME PRINTED ON THE CATHETER, usually 10 mL · GEL DWELL 3–5 MINUTES · 90° THEN TOWARD THE TOES · RESIDUAL >1000 mL → HOURLY OUTPUT AND U&E · POST-OBSTRUCTIVE DIURESIS >200 mL/h for 2 hours or >3 L/24 h

dx: **ACUTE POST-OPERATIVE URINARY RETENTION — the commonest post-operative urological event — drained by an ASEPTIC TWO-WAY 14 Fr INDWELLING URETHRAL CATHETER.** **Painful inability to void with a palpable or scanned bladder, driven by OPIOID, ANAESTHESIA, PAIN, IMMOBILITY AND POSITION, likely on prostatic enlargement.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE WORD 'INFORMED'. Three moments carry the marks — RISKS NAMED, NOT GLOSSED · THE ALTERNATIVE, OFFERED HONESTLY · THE SAFETY GATE, SAID OUT LOUD. Then close the consent: 'ANY QUESTIONS? ARE YOU HAPPY FOR ME TO GO AHEAD? I'LL DOCUMENT OUR DISCUSSION.'**

**TELL THE PROCEDURE AS A STORY IN THREE ACTS — GET READY, GO IN, FINISH UP — in plain English. ASEPTIC NON-TOUCH TECHNIQUE, MEATAL CLEANING AND BALLOON INFLATION TRANSLATED FOR A FRIGHTENED POST-OPERATIVE MAN. 'I'll establish an aseptic field and perform meatal cleansing' IS A LISTED FAIL IN THE LAY VERSION.**

**GET READY: clean trolley · check expiry and package integrity · CURTAINS, DOOR, CHAPERONE · supine, waterproof pad · HAND HYGIENE, apron, non-sterile gloves · OPEN THE PACK WITH ANTT — the inner wrapper is the sterile field · drop extras onto the field without touching · HAND HYGIENE AGAIN, STERILE GLOVES, draw up the labelled volume of STERILE WATER.**

**GO IN: fenestrated drape · hold the penis through a sterile swab — THAT HAND IS NOW COMMITTED · RETRACT THE FORESKIN · CLEAN THE MEATUS OUTWARDS, ONE SWAB PER STROKE · INSTIL LIGNOCAINE 2% GEL, PINCH, WAIT 3–5 MINUTES · PENIS AT 90° WITH UPWARD TRACTION, INSERT STEADILY · AT THE EXTERNAL SPHINCTER, LOWER TOWARD THE TOES · NEVER FORCE · ADVANCE TO THE HUB · CONFIRM URINE, THEN INFLATE with the labelled volume · withdraw gently to seat at the bladder neck.**

**FINISH UP: CONNECT THE CLOSED BAG — AND IN THE SAME BREATH, REPLACE THE FORESKIN (paraphimosis otherwise) · SECURE with StatLock or leg strap, leaving slack · BAG BELOW BLADDER LEVEL, OFF THE FLOOR · MEASURE AND RECORD THE RESIDUAL · clean, dry, cover, restore dignity · dispose, hand hygiene, DOCUMENT.**

**TASK 3 — DEFEND TWO-WAY AND 14 Fr: 'a TWO-WAY FOLEY, because he needs drainage and there is NO HAEMATURIA OR CLOT TO IRRIGATE' (THREE-WAY = IRRIGATION, 20–22 Fr) · '14 FRENCH — the smallest that drains reliably; LARGER CAUSES MORE URETHRAL TRAUMA AND DOES NOT DRAIN CLEAR URINE ANY FASTER' · 'STERILE WATER, the volume printed on the catheter — NEVER SALINE, IT CRYSTALLISES AND THE BALLOON MAY NOT DEFLATE' · SILICONE IF LATEX ALLERGY · 'I'd confirm expiry and integrity of every sterile package.'**

**CORRECTION — HAND HYGIENE DURATION: 'wash your hands for two minutes' is A SURGICAL SCRUB. Bedside catheterisation with ANTT uses ALCOHOL RUB 20–30 SECONDS, or soap and water 40–60 s if soiled, AT EACH OF THE 5 MOMENTS. And GEL: instilled, pinched, 3–5 minutes anaesthetises the whole urethra; smearing it on the tip only lubricates.** VERIFY local volume.

**AFTERCARE: residual >1000 mL → HOURLY OUTPUT FOR 4 HOURS, U&E · POST-OBSTRUCTIVE DIURESIS >200 mL/h × 2 h or >3 L/24 h — replace losses · CLOSED SYSTEM, NEVER DISCONNECT, empty before two-thirds full · daily meatal soap and water — NO ANTISEPTIC, NO WASHOUTS, NO ROUTINE ANTIBIOTIC PROPHYLAXIS · REVIEW THE NEED EVERY DAY; remove once mobile and the opioid is reducing · TAMSULOSIN BEFORE THE TRIAL OF VOID in likely prostatic obstruction · DRAIN COMPLETELY — CLAMPING IS NO LONGER RECOMMENDED.** VERIFY.

A BLOOD PRESSURE OF 80/50 WITH A FEVER OF 39.5 IS THE WHOLE STEM
THE TIMING IS THE DEFINITION

'SHOULD I JUST GIVE HIM SOME ORAL ANTIBIOTICS AND WE'LL REVIEW IN THE MORNING?'

'MUDDLED IS IMPORTANT. PLEASE DO A FORMAL CONSCIOUS-STATE ASSESSMENT AND A BLOOD SUGAR, AND TELL ME IF IT CHANGES.' ALTERED MENTAL STATE IS A SEPSIS RED FLAG — DON'T ACCEPT AN EXPLAINING-AWAY

'I'VE ALREADY STARTED THE CEFTRIAXONE YOU CHARTED'

TELEPHONE RULES

ONE INSTRUCTION AT A TIME, AND ASK HER TO READ IT BACK · A TIMEFRAME FOR EVERYTHING — 'NOW', 'WITHIN THE HOUR' · SAY YOU ARE COMING: 'I AM WALKING DOWN NOW' · CLOSE THE LOOP: 'CALL ME BACK IMMEDIATELY IF…' · JARGON IS ALLOWED WITH A NURSE — VAGUENESS IS NOT; 'SOME FLUIDS AND SOME ANTIBIOTICS' SCORES NOTHING

dx: **A CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION THAT HAS PROGRESSED TO SEPSIS — CAUSE, THEN CONSEQUENCE, IN ONE BREATH. IF YOU REMEMBER ONE LINE FROM THIS STATION, REMEMBER THAT ONE.**

**THE THREE NEAR-MISSES: 'UROSEPSIS' — true, but NAMES THE SEPSIS AND HIDES THE CATHETER · 'A URINARY TRACT INFECTION' — names the cause and IGNORES THAT THE MAN IS SHOCKED · 'SEPTIC SHOCK' SAID AS A CERTAINTY — it needs persisting hypotension despite adequate fluid, requiring vasopressors to keep MAP ≥65, plus lactate >2. SAY 'SEPSIS, POSSIBLY SEPTIC SHOCK' AND YOU ARE RIGHT EITHER WAY.** VERIFY definitions.

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: TWO GATES, IN ORDER — OPEN THE SEPSIS DOOR BEFORE THE ANTIBIOTIC DOOR, AND THE CULTURE DOOR BEFORE THE ANTIBIOTIC DOOR. The candidate who begins 'I would start gentamicin and amoxicillin' HAS SKIPPED A SHOCKED MAN'S RESUSCITATION AND CONTAMINATED HIS CULTURES. The candidate who begins 'he is septic; two cannulae, fluids, oxygen; then cultures; then antibiotics within the hour' PASSES THE SAME STATION WITH THE SAME DRUGS.**

**TASK 1, BOTH HALVES, WITH FOUR REASONS: 'Jane, Mr Nolan has a CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION — seeded when he was catheterised two days ago — and it has PROGRESSED TO SEPSIS. With a blood pressure of 80/50 HE MAY ALREADY BE IN SEPTIC SHOCK, and I'll know once I see whether he responds to fluid. Because: HE WAS INSTRUMENTED 48 HOURS AGO; A TEMPERATURE OF 39.5; HE IS HYPOTENSIVE AND TACHYCARDIC; and HE IS HYPOXIC AND FATIGUED — a systemic picture, not a bladder one.'**

**THE SCRIPT, VERSION A: 'Jane, BEFORE WE GET TO ANTIBIOTICS, I AM TREATING THIS AS SEPSIS. TWO LARGE CANNULAE please, and START A 500 mL BOLUS OF CRYSTALLOID NOW. OXYGEN, aim for 92–96. Then, BEFORE ANY ANTIBIOTIC GOES IN, TWO SETS OF BLOOD CULTURES, A URINE SAMPLE for microscopy and culture, and A VENOUS GAS WITH A LACTATE. As soon as those are taken, INTRAVENOUS ANTIBIOTICS — WITHIN THE HOUR. I AM WALKING DOWN NOW AND I WILL CALL THE REGISTRAR ON THE WAY. Please read that back to me.'**

**EMPIRICAL ANTIBIOTICS — IV, THERAPEUTIC DOSE, WITHIN THE HOUR, AFTER CULTURES BUT NEVER DELAYED PAST ~45 MINUTES FOR A SPECIMEN: urinary source, no penicillin allergy — GENTAMICIN IV 4–7 mg/kg single loading dose on ideal body weight, adjusted for renal function, PLUS AMOXICILLIN OR AMPICILLIN IV 2 g 6-HOURLY · non-severe allergy — CEFTRIAXONE 2 g IV daily ± gentamicin · immediate or severe allergy — avoid beta-lactams, gentamicin plus ID advice. YOU ARE NOT EXPECTED TO RECALL DOSES — YOU ARE EXPECTED TO SAY INTRAVENOUS, EMPIRICAL, THERAPEUTIC, AFTER CULTURES, WITHIN AN HOUR, NARROWED AT ~48 HOURS.** VERIFY against Therapeutic Guidelines.

**FLUIDS — BALANCED CRYSTALLOID (Hartmann's or Plasma-Lyte), 500 mL BOLUSES, REASSESSED AFTER EACH, towards 20 mL/kg in the first hour if he keeps responding. The lecture said normal saline; balanced crystalloid is now generally preferred — EITHER IS DEFENSIBLE IF YOU SAY WHY.** VERIFY.

**DIFFERENTIALS — THE SECOND SOURCE IS WHAT KILLS HIM TOMORROW: OBSTRUCTED INFECTED SYSTEM — anuria, flank pain, no response → IMAGING AND DRAINAGE; ANTIBIOTICS ALONE WILL NOT SAVE IT · ACUTE BACTERIAL PROSTATITIS OR ABSCESS — gentle DRE, NEVER MASSAGE · A NON-URINARY SOURCE — cough, aspiration, CANNULA SITE, PRESSURE AREA, diarrhoea after antibiotics. 'WHILE YOU ARE WITH HIM, PLEASE CHECK HIS CHEST, HIS CANNULA SITE AND HIS HEELS.'**

**DURATION: 7 DAYS with prompt response; 10–14 IF DELAYED or bacteraemic · IV TO ORAL once afebrile, stable, tolerating oral · NARROW WHEN SENSITIVITIES RETURN · monitor gentamicin levels and renal function if it continues beyond a single dose.** VERIFY. **Avoid: NSAIDs and contrast in AKI · PROPHYLAXIS AT CATHETER INSERTION, REMOVAL OR CHANGE · TREATING ASYMPTOMATIC BACTERIURIA · reciting vasopressor protocols — that's the ICU conversation.**

**TASK 4 — ONLY 'ONCE HE IS STABLE', AND OFFER IT IF IT ISN'T ASKED: 'the long-term issue is HIS PROSTATE — TREATING IT PROPERLY IS WHAT STOPS THE NEXT CATHETER, AND THE NEXT INFECTION.' TAMSULOSIN 400 microgram daily · FINASTERIDE 5 mg (up to 6 months; halves the PSA) · combination · UROLOGY for TURP. PREVENTION: AVOID UNNECESSARY CATHETERS, INSERT ASEPTICALLY, CLOSED DRAINAGE, REMOVE EARLY.** **SA: SA Health adult sepsis pathway; MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 EARLY from a country site; ICU at RAH, TQEH or Flinders; DOCUMENT THE TIME CULTURES WERE TAKEN AND ANTIBIOTICS GIVEN — the audited number.**

**THE KEY CONCEPT — SAY IT OUT LOUD: ERECTION IS A VASCULAR EVENT. Arterial inflow and venous trapping produce it; anything that damages endothelium impairs it. THE PENILE ARTERIES ARE MUCH NARROWER THAN THE CORONARIES AND BECOME SYMPTOMATIC EARLIER — ED CAN BE THE FIRST SYMPTOM OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, and every man presenting with it earns a cardiovascular risk assessment.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE INTERVENTION BEING TESTED IS OPTIMISING THE DIABETES, THE BLOOD PRESSURE AND THE DRUG REGIMEN — WITH THE ED-SPECIFIC TREATMENT THIRD, AND THE NITRATE CHECK BEFORE ANY PRESCRIPTION. IF YOU DON'T DO THIS COMPONENT, IT IS VERY HARD TO PASS YOU.**

**THE CAUSES, EXPLAINED WITHOUT BLAME: 'erections depend on healthy blood vessels. The FIRST AND BIGGEST CAUSE is YOUR DIABETES — your sugar's been running at 8, where we aim for around 7, and over time that damages the small blood vessels and later the nerves. THE NUMBNESS IN YOUR FEET IS EVIDENCE IT HAS ALREADY STARTED ELSEWHERE. The SECOND is ONE OF YOUR TABLETS — ATENOLOL is known to cause this. The THIRD is YOUR HEART ATTACK — the arteries supplying an erection are much smaller, so they often show trouble first. WHAT I WANT YOU TO HEAR IS THAT THIS IS A PHYSICAL, TREATABLE PROBLEM — NOT A FAILING ON YOUR PART.'**

**THREE BOXES — AND SAY BOX TWO MATTERS MOST. BOX 1, TESTS: MORNING TOTAL TESTOSTERONE (8–10 am) WITH LH AND FSH, repeated; prolactin if low · repeat HbA1c, fasting lipids, eGFR and urine ACR, LFT, TSH, FBE · confirm the BP. BOX 2, THE CHRONIC DISEASE: CONFIRM ADHERENCE FIRST · MAXIMISE METFORMIN, ADD AN SGLT2 INHIBITOR — preferred with established CVD · CONFIRM THE BP, ADD AN ACE INHIBITOR · antiplatelet, high-intensity statin, CARDIAC REHAB · weight, exercise, smoking, alcohol — all independently improve erectile function. BOX 3, THE ERECTIONS.**

**THE ATENOLOL — THE TRAP INSIDE THE TRAP: IT CAN CAUSE ED, AND BETA-BLOCKERS AREN'T FIRST-LINE FOR UNCOMPLICATED HYPERTENSION IN AUSTRALIA. IT DOES NOT FOLLOW THAT YOU STOP IT — he is four years post-infarct and THE BETA-BLOCKER IS THERE FOR THE HEART. 'I'M NOT GOING TO STOP YOUR ATENOLOL ON MY OWN, BECAUSE IT'S PROTECTING YOUR HEART — BUT I'LL WRITE TO YOUR CARDIOLOGIST.' Some substitute a vasodilating beta-blocker — NEBIVOLOL or CARVEDILOL. A SHARED DECISION, PUT IN A LETTER.** VERIFY.

**BOX 3 — PDE5 INHIBITORS, AFTER THE NITRATE QUESTION: SILDENAFIL on demand ~30–60 min before, once in 24 h, off-patent and inexpensive · TADALAFIL — the only one licensed as a LOW DAILY DOSE · generally NOT PBS-SUBSIDISED for ED — DISCUSS COST · STIMULATION IS STILL REQUIRED · side effects vasodilatory · AN ERECTION OVER FOUR HOURS IS A UROLOGICAL EMERGENCY · rarely sudden visual or hearing loss. Then VACUUM DEVICE (band off within 30 min), INTRACAVERNOSAL ALPROSTADIL, UROLOGY — LATE, NOT EARLY.** VERIFY.

**THE ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION — ANY NITRATE, IN ANY FORM, INCLUDING A GTN SPRAY OR PATCH: profound, potentially fatal hypotension. 'IF YOU DEVELOP CHEST PAIN, DO NOT USE YOUR SPRAY WITHIN ABOUT 24 HOURS OF SILDENAFIL OR 48 HOURS OF TADALAFIL — CALL AN AMBULANCE AND TELL THE PARAMEDICS YOU'VE TAKEN THE TABLET.' Also caution: alpha-blockers, unstable angina, recent MI, severe AS, heart failure. IF HE CAN'T SAFELY CLIMB TWO FLIGHTS OF STAIRS, HIS FITNESS FOR SEXUAL ACTIVITY NEEDS REVIEW FIRST.** VERIFY intervals.

**COUNSELLING ISN'T A LAST RESORT: 'I'd also like to offer you and your wife a session with a counsellor — THAT IS NOT A SIGN I THINK THIS IS IN YOUR HEAD; IT'S BECAUSE THIS AFFECTS BOTH OF YOU.' Offer it alongside first-line drugs. 'IS IT PSYCHOLOGICAL?' — 'Psychogenic ED is a diagnosis of exclusion and HIS PICTURE IS ORGANIC — gradual, present in all settings, major vascular risk. BUT MIXED AETIOLOGY IS THE COMMONEST PATTERN.'**

**CORRECTION — PRIAPISM: aspiration, irrigation and INTRACAVERNOSAL DILUTE PHENYLEPHRINE with BP and pulse monitoring, in consultation with urology — ADRENALINE IS NOT THE STANDARD AGENT.** **Red flags: undiagnosed angina (THE ED IS THE SENTINEL), hypogonadism, prolactinoma, CAUDA EQUINA, depression with suicidal ideation.** **SA: Healthy Male handouts; Diabetes SA and NDSS; GP Management Plan; cardiac rehab via Yorke and Northern LHN; Relationships Australia SA or SHINE SA; MensLine 1300 78 99 78; Closing the Gap for cost.**

findings: THE DIAGNOSIS IS EASY — THE STATION IS WHAT YOU DO NEXT, AND HOW YOU SAY IT

Everything is in the stem: TWO DAYS OF DYSURIA AND FREQUENCY · NO FEVER, NO DISCHARGE, NO ABDOMINAL PAIN, NO VOMITING · ALLERGIC TO PENICILLIN · abdomen normal, DRE normal, afebrile · DIPSTICK: BLOOD TRACE, LEUCOCYTES +, NITRITES POSITIVE
THE TWO CRITICAL ERRORS ON THE MARK SHEET
FAILING TO ARRANGE A URINE MCS BEFORE STARTING ANTIBIOTICS · FAILING TO ADVISE FURTHER INVESTIGATION. EITHER ONE ON ITS OWN FAILS THE STATION, HOWEVER GOOD THE REST WAS
DON'T LAUNCH INTO THE DIAGNOSIS — ask, then the agenda

'BEFORE I GO THROUGH THE RESULTS, COULD YOU TELL ME IN YOUR OWN WORDS WHAT'S BEEN HAPPENING?' … 'IS THERE ANYTHING IN PARTICULAR YOU'RE WORRIED ABOUT?' EVERY COUNSELLING STATION HAS A HIDDEN AGENDA — ask early and it's handed to you with six minutes left
THE HIDDEN AGENDA

'IS THIS SOMETHING I'VE CAUGHT? DO I NEED TO TELL MY WIFE?' → 'THAT'S A FAIR QUESTION AND I'M GLAD YOU ASKED. THE INFECTION I THINK YOU HAVE ISN'T USUALLY SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED — BUT THERE IS ONE CONDITION THAT CAN LOOK SIMILAR, SO LET ME ASK YOU A FEW PERSONAL QUESTIONS AND WE CAN BE SURE'
WHY A MAN IS DIFFERENT — the concept the case is built on

IN A WOMAN YOU TREAT CYSTITIS AND MOVE ON. IN A MAN YOU TREAT IT AND THINK ABOUT WHY — THE LONG MALE URETHRA NORMALLY PROTECTS HIM, SO INFECTION IMPLIES STONES, PROSTATE DISEASE, A STRICTURE, A TUMOUR, INCOMPLETE EMPTYING OR DIABETES
THE DIPSTICK — what it does and doesn't prove
NITRITES are produced by bacteria and are the MORE SPECIFIC pad; LEUCOCYTE ESTERASE is the MORE SENSITIVE one. NEITHER REPLACES THE CULTURE IN A MAN
'CAN'T YOU JUST GIVE ME THE ANTIBIOTICS?'
'YOU'LL GET THEM TODAY — BUT I NEED THE URINE SAMPLE BEFORE THE FIRST TABLET, BECAUSE ONCE THE ANTIBIOTIC IS IN, THE TEST CAN'T TELL US WHICH BUG IT IS.' SAMPLE FIRST, TABLET SECOND, SAME VISIT
THE MIDSTREAM TECHNIQUE — THIS IS SCORED

WASH YOUR HANDS · CLEAN THE TIP, FORESKIN BACK · START PASSING URINE INTO THE TOILET AND LET THE FIRST PART GO · MID-STREAM, HOLD THE JAR IN THE FLOW UNTIL ABOUT HALF FULL · FINISH IN THE TOILET, CLOSE AND LABEL, TO PATHOLOGY TODAY. 'DOES THAT MAKE SENSE?'
THE PENICILLIN ALLERGY IS A DISTRACTOR
'WHAT HAPPENED WHEN YOU TOOK PENICILLIN? NITROFURANTOIN ISN'T A PENICILLIN, SO THAT ALLERGY ISN'T A PROBLEM HERE.' Reaching for amoxicillin is the error it's planted to catch
VERSION B — the reluctant patient

The role-player is briefed to be SURPRISED AND RELUCTANT when further investigation or urology is raised — BUT TO ACCEPT IT IF YOU HANDLE IT WELL. 'A SCAN AND A SPECIALIST? DO YOU THINK IT'S CANCER?' IS THE SCORED MOMENT

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: YOU MUST RAISE FURTHER INVESTIGATION — AND RAISE IT IN STAGES, WITH THE REASON FIRST. THE STATION IS A SQUEEZE: not advising investigation is a critical error; advising it badly — CYSTOSCOPY, CT AND 'CANCER' IN YOUR OPENING SENTENCE — TRIGGERS THE RELUCTANCE THE ROLE-PLAYER IS BRIEFED TO PRODUCE. THE PASS RUNS BETWEEN THE TWO: REASON, THEN STAGE ONE, THEN 'ONLY IF'.**

**TASK 1 — THREE REASONS, IN ORDER: 'the condition you have is called CYSTITIS — bacteria have got into the bladder and inflamed the wall, which gives you the stinging and the need to go. THREE REASONS: YOUR SYMPTOMS; THE URINE TEST — LEUCOCYTES, white cells from your immune system, and NITRITES, A CHEMICAL THE BACTERIA THEMSELVES PRODUCE; and THE EXAMINATION, which was normal and rules out some other causes.'**

**THEN THE DIFFERENTIALS, OUT LOUD — scored under diagnosis even though nobody asked: PYELONEPHRITIS — no fever, vomiting or back pain · URETHRITIS — the giveaway is discharge, and he has none (still take a sexual history) · PROSTATITIS — fever, difficulty passing urine, a tender gland; his DRE was normal. EVERY NEGATIVE IN THE STEM EXISTS TO CLOSE A DOOR — SAY WHICH DOOR EACH ONE CLOSES.**

**TASK 3 — TREATMENT TODAY, WITHOUT WAITING 48 HOURS: NITROFURANTOIN 100 mg ORALLY 6-HOURLY FOR 7 DAYS — 'AND THE SEVEN DAYS IS THE PART TO REMEMBER, BECAUSE MEN ARE TREATED LONGER THAN WOMEN.' WITH FOOD · HARMLESS BROWN URINE — warn him or he'll stop · paracetamol · NO URAL — ALKALINISERS REDUCE NITROFURANTOIN'S ACTIVITY. Alternatives: TRIMETHOPRIM 300 mg DAILY or CEFALEXIN 500 mg BD, 7 days.** VERIFY. **CORRECTION: NITROFURANTOIN IS NOW FIRST LINE; TRIMETHOPRIM HAS MOVED DOWN ON RESISTANCE GROUNDS.**

**NITROFURANTOIN DOES NOT TREAT PYELONEPHRITIS OR PROSTATITIS — IT CONCENTRATES IN URINE, NOT TISSUE. Avoid below eGFR ~45, at term in pregnancy, and in G6PD deficiency. NOT A PENICILLIN.** VERIFY. **SAFETY-NET: NO IMPROVEMENT IN 48 HOURS — resistant bug; FEVER, SHAKES, VOMITING OR BACK/SIDE PAIN — the kidney; same-day review or ED.**

**TASK 4 — THE REASON BEFORE THE TESTS, VERBATIM: 'there's one more thing, and I want to say WHY before I say WHAT. URINE INFECTIONS AREN'T COMMON IN MEN — the male plumbing usually protects you. So when one does happen, IT'S WORTH A LOOK, particularly if it happens again. I'M NOT EXPECTING TO FIND ANYTHING SINISTER. I'd do it in stages: TODAY, kidney function and a blood sugar with the urine. IN A FEW WEEKS, AN ULTRASOUND — NO NEEDLES, NO RADIATION. And ONLY IF THAT SHOWS SOMETHING would we go further. MOST MEN NEVER DO.'**

**IF HE PUSHES BACK: 'I can hear that, and you're right that most of the time this is straightforward. If there is something simple behind it — A SMALL STONE, OR THE BLADDER NOT EMPTYING FULLY — FINDING IT SAVES YOU HAVING THIS AGAIN AND AGAIN. If you'd rather start with just the urine and blood test today, that's reasonable too — BUT I'D WANT TO SEE YOU AFTER THE TREATMENT EITHER WAY. What would you prefer?'** **Four stages exist in your head; ONLY STAGE ONE LEAVES YOUR MOUTH UNPROMPTED.**

**CORRECTION — THE GUIDELINE TENSION: current Australian guidance RESERVES FORMAL UROLOGICAL EVALUATION FOR RECURRENT INFECTION OR INADEQUATE RESPONSE; the handbook marks 'no investigation' as a critical error. DO BOTH: 'strictly, guidelines reserve formal evaluation for recurrence — but a UTI in a man is uncommon enough that I'd do A BASELINE: renal function, glucose, and an ultrasound with a post-void residual — and RESERVE CYSTOSCOPY AND REFERRAL FOR RECURRENCE, PERSISTENT HAEMATURIA OR AN ABNORMAL SCAN.'**

**CORRECTIONS ON FOLLOW-UP: NO POST-TREATMENT CULTURE TO PROVE CURE — the only exceptions are PREGNANCY and A MAN WITH PROSTATITIS · NO PSA DURING ACUTE INFECTION — FALSELY RAISED; defer it · REPEAT URINALYSIS AFTER TREATMENT to confirm the blood has cleared — PERSISTENT HAEMATURIA IS A UROLOGY REFERRAL, NOT A REPEAT SCRIPT · ASYMPTOMATIC BACTERIURIA IN A MAN IS NOT TREATED.** **SA: MSU to SA Pathology same day; KUB ultrasound on the Copper Coast; urology at TQEH; PATS.**

VERSION B — FREQUENCY FROM EXCESSIVE FLUID INTAKE: A NORMAL BLADDER HANDLING AN ABNORMAL VOLUME. NOT A DISEASE; A BEHAVIOUR.** **SAY 'CYSTITIS', NOT 'UTI' — the level changes treatment length.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: THE EXPLANATION CARRIES THE MARKS, AND IT MUST BE BUILT FROM THIS PATIENT'S OWN FINDINGS. Candidates fail not on the history but on THE LAST TWO MINUTES — generic reassurance, jargon, or a diagnosis with no differential. RESERVE TWO FULL MINUTES: FINDINGS → NAMED DIAGNOSIS → WHY IT FITS HER → WHAT ELSE AND WHY NOT → WHAT HAPPENS NEXT.**

**THE DIPSTICK, PAD BY PAD, IN PATIENT LANGUAGE: 'we found WHITE BLOOD CELLS — the cells your immune system sends to fight infection. Most importantly, we found NITRITES — A CHEMICAL THAT CERTAIN BACTERIA PRODUCE, a very strong sign there really are bacteria in your bladder — THAT'S THE RESULT THAT CONFIRMS IT. We also found A SMALL AMOUNT OF BLOOD AND PROTEIN. I know those sound alarming, but THEY'RE WHAT WE EXPECT WHEN THE BLADDER LINING IS INFLAMED. To be thorough, I'LL RECHECK YOUR URINE ONCE YOU'VE FINISHED THE TREATMENT to make sure the blood has cleared.'**

**THE DIAGNOSIS, NAMED, AND LINKED TO THE STEM: 'I believe you have CYSTITIS — an infection in the bladder itself, rather than the kidneys — because of the burning and frequency, and NO FEVER OR BACK PAIN tells me it hasn't travelled up. THE PROLAPSE YOU WERE TOLD ABOUT IS RELEVANT: WHEN THE BLADDER DROPS IT DOESN'T EMPTY COMPLETELY, AND URINE THAT SITS THERE IS MORE LIKELY TO BECOME INFECTED. That's probably why this has happened.'**

**VERSION B — ANSWER THE FEAR WITH NAMED NEGATIVES, NOT WITH COMFORT: 'based on everything you've told me, PROSTATE CANCER IS VERY UNLIKELY TO BE THE CAUSE, and I want to tell you why rather than ask you to take my word for it. When the prostate causes trouble we expect DIFFICULTY STARTING, A WEAK STREAM, STOP-START, DRIBBLING, NOT EMPTYING, GETTING UP AT NIGHT — YOU HAVE NONE OF THOSE. No blood, no weight loss, no pain. WHAT YOU DO HAVE IS SIX LARGE GLASSES OF WATER A DAY — anyone drinking that much would be going often. That on its own explains it.'**

**THEN, WITHOUT DISMISSING HIM: 'if you'd like, we can talk separately about PROSTATE CANCER SCREENING and what a PSA test can and can't tell you, so you can decide. And if anything changes — blood, a weaker stream, getting up at night, weight loss — come straight back.' 'SHOULDN'T YOU JUST ORDER A PSA?' — 'PSA IS A SHARED DECISION, NOT A REFLEX — BENEFITS AND HARMS, INCLUDING FALSE POSITIVES, OVER-DIAGNOSIS AND BIOPSY.'**

A MAN — SAME AGENTS FOR 7 DAYS WITH AN MSU FIRST. SEND AN MSU HERE — SHE HAS AN ANATOMICAL PREDISPOSITION. Analgesia, fluids.** VERIFY every dose against current Therapeutic Guidelines.

LIFESTYLE ADVICE AND REPEAT IN 12 MONTHS; NO GLUCOSE-LOWERING TREATMENT.' Version B — A FLUID AND VOIDING DIARY, reduce intake, review.**

**SAFETY-NET, OUT LOUD: 'if you develop A FEVER OR SHIVERING, PAIN IN YOUR BACK OR SIDE, VOMITING, or you're NOT IMPROVING IN 48 HOURS, I need to see you the same day or you should go to the emergency department. THE PERMISSION LINE — say it early, verbatim

'I CAN SEE THIS ISN'T EASY TO BRING UP, AND I'M GLAD YOU DID. EVERYTHING WE DISCUSS IS CONFIDENTIAL. AND TO WORK OUT WHAT THIS IS, I'LL NEED TO ASK SOME PERSONAL QUESTIONS ABOUT YOUR SEX LIFE — HOW MANY PARTNERS, WHAT KIND OF SEX. I ASK EVERYONE WITH THIS PROBLEM. IS THAT ALRIGHT?' What separates candidates is whether they took a COMPLETE SEXUAL HISTORY — partners, gender, practices, condoms, previous STI, alcohol and drugs, travel — AFTER EXPLICITLY SEEKING PERMISSION AND GIVING A CONFIDENTIALITY ASSURANCE. dx: **SYSTEMIC SNAKE ENVENOMING WITH VENOM-INDUCED CONSUMPTION COAGULOPATHY (VICC) — most consistent with an EASTERN BROWN SNAKE in South Australia.** **VICC in one line: THE VENOM ACTIVATES PROTHROMBIN, THE CLOTTING FACTORS — ESPECIALLY FIBRINOGEN AND FACTORS V AND VIII — ARE CONSUMED WITHIN MINUTES TO AN HOUR, AND THE BLOOD STOPS CLOTTING. INR RISES OR BECOMES UNRECORDABLE, aPTT RISES, FIBRINOGEN FALLS, D-DIMER SOARS.**

**THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE: ACTIVELY HUNTING FOR BLEEDING — AND THEN CONNECTING IT TO THE NUMBERS ON THE CARD IN LANGUAGE THE PATIENT UNDERSTANDS. The candidate who passes asks the cannula-site question, NOTICES THE BLOODY GAUZE ON THE ELBOW WHEN THE BITE IS ON THE LEG, and says out loud 'that tells me the venom is already affecting your clotting.' The candidate who fails takes a competent generic history, reads the results back as numbers, and NEVER LINKS SYMPTOM TO TEST TO TREATMENT.**
**THE ONE SENTENCE TO LEAVE WITH: 'SNAKE BITE IS FOUR ORGAN SYSTEMS, ONE BANDAGE THAT STAYS ON, ONE SWAB, ONE DECISION ABOUT ANTIVENOM — AND TWELVE HOURS OF WATCHING.'**

**THE RESULTS, LINKED — INR: 'the INR measures HOW LONG YOUR BLOOD TAKES TO CLOT. Yours is higher than normal, which means it's taking longer than it should — AND THAT'S EXACTLY WHY YOU BLED FROM THE DRIP SITE. That finding TELLS US YOU NEED THE ANTIVENOM.' aPTT: 'a second clotting test — also prolonged, which confirms it.' WHITE CELLS: 'raised — your body's stress response to the bite.' CK: 'a muscle enzyme — NORMAL, so the venom ISN'T DAMAGING YOUR MUSCLES.' KIDNEYS: 'NORMAL, which is reassuring.'**

**THE COMMUNICATION CHALLENGE: A YOUNG, WELL-LOOKING, FRIGHTENED MAN MUST BE TOLD HIS BLOOD IS NOT CLOTTING — WITHOUT TERRIFYING OR MINIMISING. 'I feel completely fine' → 'I'm glad — SOME EFFECTS SHOW UP IN THE BLOOD BEFORE YOU FEEL THEM, so we still test and watch.' 'Am I going to die?' → pause, sit: 'THIS IS SERIOUS AND WE TREAT IT SERIOUSLY — BUT WITH THE ANTIDOTE AND MONITORING, PEOPLE RECOVER WELL. We've caught it early.'**

**ANTIVENOM — THE FOUR THINGS TO SAY: INDICATION — CLINICAL OR LABORATORY EVIDENCE OF ENVENOMING; 'WOULD YOU GIVE IT IF HE FELT COMPLETELY WELL?' — 'YES, LABORATORY EVIDENCE IS ENOUGH' · CHOICE — MONOVALENT if species known (description, geography, kit), POLYVALENT if not · GIVING IT — DILUTED IN NORMAL SALINE, IV OVER 15–30 MINUTES, in a resuscitation area with adrenaline drawn up; ONE VIAL IS USUALLY SUFFICIENT — MORE DOES NOT RESTORE CLOTTING FACTORS FASTER; NO ROUTINE PREMEDICATION · COMPLICATIONS — ANAPHYLAXIS (stop, ADRENALINE 0.5 mg IM 1:1000, fluids, restart slowly) and SERUM SICKNESS AT 4–14 DAYS — warn everyone.** VERIFY.

**THE BANDAGE COMES OFF ONLY ONCE BLOODS AND THE SWAB ARE TAKEN, IN A RESUSCITATION AREA, WITH ANTIVENOM AVAILABLE — then REPEAT BLOODS ~1 HOUR LATER, because venom can enter the circulation as a bolus. REPEAT COAGS, FBE, UEC AND CK AT 6 AND 12 HOURS; neuro obs hourly; MINIMUM 12 HOURS OBSERVATION — a night-time bite observed until daylight bloods.**

**THE VENOM DETECTION KIT — BITE-SITE SWAB BEFORE ANY CLEANING; urine second. IT SELECTS THE ANTIVENOM — IT DOES NOT DIAGNOSE ENVENOMING, AND A NEGATIVE RESULT EXCLUDES NOTHING.** **FFP BEFORE ANTIVENOM FEEDS THE CONSUMPTION — only after antivenom, for persistent coagulopathy with bleeding, on toxicologist advice.**

**DIFFERENTIALS — THE REAL QUESTION IS ENVENOMED OR NOT: VICC — THE ANSWER · NEUROTOXIC ENVENOMING — tiger, taipan, death adder; antivenom early, established paralysis reverses slowly · MYOTOXICITY/RHABDOMYOLYSIS — tiger, mulga, black · AKI/THROMBOTIC MICROANGIOPATHY — late · DRY BITE — CANNOT BE DECLARED EARLY · ANTICOAGULANT-RELATED BLEEDING — doesn't exclude envenoming; FIBRINOGEN AND D-DIMER DISCRIMINATE · other bite · VASOVAGAL — early collapse after a bite is envenoming until proven otherwise.**

**THE SAFETY POINTS THAT SCORE: TETANUS ONCE THE COAGULOPATHY HAS RESOLVED — NO IM INJECTIONS WHILE COAGULOPATHIC · ASK ABOUT ANTICOAGULANTS · WARN ABOUT SERUM SICKNESS BEFORE HE ASKS · DISPOSITION — admit 12–24 h; discharge only asymptomatic with normal coags, CK and renal function; written return advice; GP at 48 h.** **SA: POISONS INFORMATION CENTRE 13 11 26 for the clinical toxicologist on every case · many MM5 sites stock limited antivenom — CHECK STOCK EARLY, MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33 · 20-minute whole-blood clotting test as a bedside surrogate where no lab.**
