stem: General practice or paediatric outpatients, regional South Australia. AMELIA, 8, brought in by her mother, who has been told by THE SCHOOL NURSE that she is SHORT FOR HER AGE. Given to you: HEIGHT 117 cm, WEIGHT 23 kg, and GROWTH CHARTS IN THE ROOM.
The examiner will hand you: MOTHER 150 cm — FATHER 160 cm — height on the 3RD CENTILE — weight on the 25TH TO 50TH — TANNER STAGE 1 — examination otherwise normal and proportionate.
tasks: Take a focused history from the mother
Plot the height and weight on the growth chart and interpret them
Ask the examiner for the relevant physical examination findings
Explain your diagnosis and differentials to the mother
findings: ★ THE NUMBERS IN THE STEM

HEIGHT 117 cm — THE 3RD CENTILE. WEIGHT 23 kg — the 25TH–50TH. Say it while you plot: 'her WEIGHT IS BETTER PRESERVED THAN HER HEIGHT — which points AWAY from undernutrition and chronic illness, because those take the weight first'
★ THE PARENTAL HEIGHTS — only if asked

'I'M 150. MY PARTNER IS 160.' Given readily IF ASKED, never volunteered. MID-PARENTAL HEIGHT FOR A GIRL = (150 + 160 − 13) ÷ 2 = 148.5 cm, RANGE ABOUT 140–157. AVERAGING TO 155 without the 13 cm sex correction is a named error
★ PREVIOUS MEASUREMENTS — only if you ask the examiner
'She was ON THE 3RD CENTILE AT AGE 5 AS WELL.' SHE IS TRACKING, NOT CROSSING. The shape of the line beats the position of the point
★ THE EXAMINATION — handed over only for what you name

Well and PROPORTIONATE, NO DYSMORPHIC FEATURES. No pallor or rash. THYROID NORMAL. TANNER STAGE 1. Chest, heart and BP normal. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Joints, spine and nodes normal. FUNDI NORMAL. The growth charts and parents' heights are HANDED OVER IF YOU ASK AND WITHHELD IF YOU DO NOT
The complaint, clarified

'She looks smaller than all her classmates.' Shorter, or smaller all over? — 'SHORTER. She eats like a horse. She's just short.' Always, or recently? — 'ALWAYS — since reception, the smallest in the class photo'
★ HER HIDDEN AGENDA — the impact

'They call her SHORTY. She says it doesn't bother her, but SHE'S GONE OFF NETBALL.' Only if asked how it's affecting her — or raised LATE if you never ask. It upsets her MORE THAN THE HEIGHT ITSELF. Amelia, asked directly: 'I DON'T LIKE IT IN NETBALL. I NEVER GET THE BALL'
The benign block
Neither parent a LATE DEVELOPER — 'we were both just short.' No weight worries. NO PUBERTY SIGNS — 'she's only eight' — ask anyway; both precocious and delayed puberty change the reading
The pathological screen — all negative, and ALL must be asked

Diet: 'she eats everything — three meals and snacks' (don't accept the headline). Normal bowels; no greasy stools, blood, ulcers, tummy or joint pain; NO family coeliac, Crohn's or colitis. No chest trouble; HEEL-PRICK NORMAL; NO medicines, puffers or steroids. No cold intolerance, constipation or dry skin. No weight loss, lumps, sweats, bruising. NO HEADACHES, MORNING VOMITING OR VISUAL CHANGE. Urine normal
Birth, development, home
3.1 kg, born on her due date, uncomplicated pregnancy, no smoking or alcohol. BRIGHT — TOP READING GROUP. Home fine. 'I want to know if something's wrong — and WHETHER SHE'LL CATCH UP'
★ HER PUSHES

'WILL SHE CATCH UP?' — asked again if the answer is vague. Reassured too quickly: 'BUT HOW DO YOU KNOW NOTHING'S WRONG?' / 'how can you know that without testing anything?' When Turner is mentioned: 'TURNER SYNDROME? SHOULD I BE WORRIED?' She RELAXES once benign versus pathological and the bone age are named
★ VERSION B — the stools

Height AND weight both FALLING ACROSS CENTILES; 'her POOS ARE PALE AND THEY FLOAT'; always a sore tummy; tired; mild abdominal distension. PATHOLOGICAL — COELIAC DISEASE FIRST. DOWNWARD CENTILE CROSSING IS NEVER A NORMAL VARIANT. Keep gluten in until serology
Other practice cards

HEIGHT FALLING while WEIGHT RISES, cold, constipated, dry skin → HYPOTHYROIDISM — the ENDOCRINE SIGNATURE · 13-year-old girl, NO BREAST DEVELOPMENT, widely spaced nipples, a murmur → TURNER: karyotype, echo, renal ultrasound · height crossing down over two years, weight preserved, HEADACHES ON WAKING, vomiting before breakfast → INTRACRANIAL TUMOUR with GH deficiency: fundi, fields, URGENT MRI · 14-year-old boy, no puberty, FATHER SHAVED AT 18 → CONSTITUTIONAL DELAY, bone age behind · the mother asks for GROWTH HORMONE → specialist-only, strict criteria, not for a healthy child growing to a short family target

dx: **BENIGN FAMILIAL SHORT STATURE — a healthy child who is short because her parents are short, growing steadily along a low centile toward a short but appropriate adult height. CONSTITUTIONAL GROWTH DELAY runs a close second and CANNOT BE EXCLUDED TODAY.** **The source is explicit: rare — about once in several years of recalls — but a LOW PASS RATE, because candidates have no structure for it.**

**★ THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE — REASSURE ONLY AFTER YOU HAVE PUBLICLY EXCLUDED PATHOLOGY, AND NEVER PROMISE CATCH-UP. The examiner cannot see you thinking. A candidate who simply says 'this is familial short stature, she takes after her parents' has said something TRUE and earned ALMOST NOTHING. The mark is in the REASONING MADE AUDIBLE: benign versus pathological, the named conditions excluded and how, the correctly sex-corrected mid-parental height, and the honest statement that familial and constitutional CAN'T BE SEPARATED TODAY WITHOUT A BONE AGE.**

**DEFINITIONS: short stature = height BELOW THE 3RD CENTILE (more than 2 SD below the mean), or WELL BELOW THE MID-PARENTAL TARGET, or CROSSING CENTILES DOWNWARD. GROWTH VELOCITY ~5–7 cm/year from age 4 to puberty.** VERIFY **THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL IDEA: THE SHAPE OF THE LINE BEATS THE POSITION OF THE POINT. A child on the 3rd tracking along it is usually normal; a child falling from the 50th to the 3rd is PATHOLOGICAL UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE — even while still 'within the normal range'.**

**THE TWO QUESTIONS THAT SORT THE WHOLE CASE: 'shorter, or SMALLER ALL OVER?' (height alone vs height-plus-weight are two different differentials) and 'ALWAYS the smallest, or only RECENTLY?' (always = a normal variant; recently falling behind friends who used to be the same size = centile crossing = pathology).**

**MID-PARENTAL HEIGHT — SAY THE FORMULA AS YOU USE IT: GIRLS = (mother + father − 13) ÷ 2 · BOYS = (mother + father + 13) ÷ 2 · target range ± 8.5 cm. This case: (150 + 160 − 13) ÷ 2 = 148.5 cm, range 140–157.** **'Was either of you a LATE DEVELOPER — did her father shave later than everyone else, or keep growing into his late teens?' is the classic pointer to CONSTITUTIONAL DELAY.**

**★ THE PATHOLOGICAL SCREEN — worth TWICE the marks of anything else, because it's what candidates skip once they've decided the case is benign. RUN THE BUCKETS OUT LOUD: undernutrition (a real diet history, food security) · GUT (coeliac — pale, greasy, floating stools; IBD — blood, ulcers, joints; FAMILY 'GUT PROBLEMS' in plain words) · LUNGS (chest infections, CF, heel-prick) · DRUGS (STEROID puffers and tablets — name drug, dose, courses) · THYROID (cold, constipation, dry skin, slowing) · MALIGNANCY (weight, lumps, sweats, bruising) · BRAIN TUMOUR (MORNING HEADACHE, VOMITING ON WAKING, VISION — the question that covers growth hormone) · JOINTS and rash · KIDNEYS (drinking, urine, UTIs) · GENETIC (development, learning).** **Stopping after the gut is the named trap.**

**THE HORMONE SIGNATURE, worth saying if the pattern appears: HEIGHT FALLING WHILE WEIGHT IS FINE OR RISING points to a HORMONE cause — hypothyroidism, GH deficiency, excess steroid — the OPPOSITE of malnutrition or bowel disease, which take the weight first.**

**THE EXPLANATION, IN ORDER — NAME IT, THE ARITHMETIC, THE ALTERNATIVE, THE TEST, THE EXCLUSIONS: 'the most likely explanation is BENIGN familial short stature — benign meaning there's NO DISEASE behind it. A child usually ends up near the average of her parents' heights, corrected for being a girl — for you two about 148 or 149 cm, give or take eight. Amelia is on the 3rd centile, heading toward exactly that, on the same line since she was five. There's a second possibility, CONSTITUTIONAL GROWTH DELAY — growth and puberty both come late and she catches up. The only thing that separates them is an X-ray of her HAND AND WRIST — her BONE AGE. If it matches her real age, it's the familial pattern; if it's behind, there's catch-up to come.'** **Then the exclusions, NAMED.**

**★ 'WILL SHE CATCH UP?' — 'I can't promise that today, and I'd rather be straight with you than reassuring. If it's the constitutional pattern, yes — later than her friends. If it's the familial pattern, she'll keep growing normally and end up a short adult, which is NOT A DISEASE and doesn't shorten her life. The bone age tells us which.'** **TURNER: 'I don't think she has it — none of the usual features. But it's the ONE CONDITION WHERE BEING SHORT CAN BE THE ONLY SIGN, and it's treatable, so we test EVERY girl with unexplained short stature.'** **BONE AGE caveat: a delayed bone age is NOT specific to constitutional delay — hypothyroidism, GH deficiency, chronic disease and undernutrition all delay it; interpret it with velocity and the bloods, never alone.**

**INVESTIGATIONS AND PLAN: BONE AGE (left hand and wrist) · FBE and film, ESR/CRP, U&E, creatinine, LFT, calcium, phosphate, ALP · COELIAC SEROLOGY (tTG-IgA + total IgA) on gluten · TFT · IGF-1 (± IGFBP-3) as the GH screen · KARYOTYPE IN EVERY GIRL · urinalysis · MRI pituitary only if the GH axis is abnormal or neurological features · RE-MEASURE IN SIX MONTHS AND CALCULATE VELOCITY — 'a single point is a photograph; two points are a story' · write to the school about the teasing · safety-net: morning headache or vomiting, vision change, tummy symptoms, weight loss, or she seems to stop growing.** VERIFY **Never 'failure to thrive' — that describes weight. GROWTH HORMONE is specialist-only (proven GH deficiency, Turner, chronic renal failure, Prader-Willi, SGA without catch-up) under strict criteria — not for a healthy child growing to a short family target.** VERIFY SA: WCH paediatric endocrinology with **PATS** · **CaFHS 1300 733 606** · school nurse · **TIS 131 450** · ACCHS · **CARL 13 14 78** if neglect or food insecurity · growth charts aren't population-neutral — which is why MPH and trajectory matter more than the centile.
plan: **WIPE — and speak to the child**: **'hello, I'm Dr ___. You must be Amelia's mum — and hello Amelia. Is it all right if I ask some questions, then measure and examine her, and then we'll talk about what I think? Tell me what you've noticed.'** *'She looks smaller than all her classmates.'*

**★ DEFINE 'SMALLER'**: **'when you say smaller — do you mean SHORTER than them, or smaller ALL OVER, lighter and thinner as well?'** *'Shorter. She eats like a horse.'* **Height alone and height-plus-weight are two different differentials.**

**★ THE TIMELINE — the question that sorts the case**: **'has she ALWAYS been the smallest, or have you only noticed it RECENTLY?'** *'Always — since reception.'* **Always points to a normal variant; recently falling behind means centile crossing.**

**★ THE IMPACT — scored, and where her real agenda sits**: **'and how is it affecting her — at home and at school? Is anyone teasing her?'** *'They call her Shorty. She's gone off netball.'* → **to Amelia: 'do you mind being the shortest, or is it mostly Mum who worries?'** *'I never get the ball in netball.'*

**THE BENIGN DIFFERENTIAL**: **'can I ask how tall you are, and how tall her father is? Was either of you a LATE DEVELOPER — growing later than your friends?'** *'150 and 160. No — both just short.'* Then **'any concerns about her weight? Any signs of PUBERTY — breast development, hair under her arms or pubic hair?'** *'She's only eight.'* **Ask it anyway.**

**★ SIGNPOST THE PATHOLOGICAL SCREEN — worth twice everything else**: **'I need to go through the things that can slow a child's growth.'** Then **diet — 'describe a typical day: fruit and vegetables, meat or an alternative, dairy?'** *'She eats everything.'* **Don't accept the headline.**

**GUT**: **'any pale, greasy or bulky stools — ones that FLOAT or are HARD TO FLUSH? Diarrhoea, blood, mouth ulcers, tummy pain, joint pain? Any family history of COELIAC, CROHN'S or COLITIS — or ANY GUT PROBLEM AT ALL?'** *Normal; nothing.* **Families often say 'gut problems' for coeliac.**

**LUNGS AND DRUGS**: **'any recurrent chest infections, long-term cough or wheeze? Was her newborn HEEL-PRICK normal? Is she on any medicines — particularly STEROID PUFFERS OR TABLETS?'** *No; normal; none.*

**THYROID, CANCER, BRAIN**: **'does she feel the COLD more than others? Constipation, dry skin, more tired or slowed down? Has she lost WEIGHT, any LUMPS, night sweats, bruising? Any HEADACHES — especially in the MORNING — any VOMITING ON WAKING, any change in her VISION?'** *'None of that — she's a well kid.'* **Stopping after the gut is the trap.**

**BIRTH, DEVELOPMENT, HOME, AND HER EXPECTATION**: **'was she small at birth — weight, on time? Any problems in the pregnancy? Any concerns about her development? How are things at home? And what were you hoping we could do today?'** *3.1 kg, term; bright; 'whether something's wrong, and whether she'll catch up.'*

**★ PLOT, OUT LOUD, THEN ASK FOR THE TRAJECTORY**: **'height 117 on the 3rd centile; weight 23 on the 25th to 50th — weight better preserved than height, which points away from poor nutrition and chronic illness. Examiner, are there any PREVIOUS MEASUREMENTS?'** *'3rd centile at five as well.'* → **'so she's TRACKING, not crossing.'**

**THE SEX-CORRECTED SUM, SAID AS YOU DO IT**: **'her mid-parental height for a girl is (150 + 160 − 13) ÷ 2 = 148.5 cm, range roughly 140 to 157 — her trajectory is appropriate for that target.'** **Averaging to 155 is the named error.**

**★ THE EXAMINATION REQUEST — you get only what you name**: **'height, weight, head circumference and BMI plotted, and the parents' heights; general appearance including DYSMORPHIC FEATURES, pallor, rash, clubbing, ulcers; BODY PROPORTION — arm span versus height, upper-to-lower segment ratio; THYROID; TANNER STAGING with a chaperone; chest, heart and BLOOD PRESSURE; abdomen for organomegaly; joints, spine, nodes; FUNDI AND VISUAL FIELDS.'** *All normal; Tanner 1.*

**★ NAME IT, THE ARITHMETIC, THE ALTERNATIVE, THE TEST**: **benign familial short stature — 'benign meaning no disease behind it' · heading toward about 148 or 149 cm, same line since five · the second possibility, constitutional growth delay · 'the only thing that separates them is an X-ray of her hand and wrist — her bone age.'**

**★ 'WILL SHE CATCH UP?' — honest, never a promise**: **'I can't promise that today, and I'd rather be straight with you. If it's the constitutional pattern, yes — later than her friends. If it's the familial pattern, she'll grow normally to a short adult height, which isn't a disease. The bone age tells us which.'** **'She'll shoot up' is the named fail.**

**THE EXCLUSIONS, NAMED — then Turner, with its reason**: **bowel conditions like coeliac and IBD, lung conditions like CF, thyroid and growth hormone problems, poor nutrition, and rarer blood cancers, kidney and genetic conditions — 'nothing points to any of them, but I'll confirm with bloods — and a chromosome test for Turner syndrome, because being short can be the only sign, so we test every girl.'**

**FOLLOW-UP IS TREATMENT, AND THE SCHOOL**: **'I'll re-measure her in six months, because her growth rate tells us more than any single measurement. Come back sooner for morning headaches or vomiting, vision changes, tummy symptoms, weight loss, or if she seems to stop growing. And I'll write to the school about the netball and the teasing — that part matters too.'**
pefe: **Measure and plot HEIGHT, WEIGHT and BMI on the correct SEX-SPECIFIC chart — and FIND PREVIOUS MEASUREMENTS (school, child health record, GP notes).** The trajectory is the investigation.
**Calculate the MID-PARENTAL HEIGHT and target range (girls − 13, boys + 13, ÷ 2, ± 8.5 cm). Calculate GROWTH VELOCITY if two points ≥ 6 months apart.**

**Examination request: DYSMORPHIC FEATURES (Turner — webbed neck, low hairline, widely spaced nipples, cubitus valgus) · pallor, rash, clubbing, ulcers · PROPORTION (arm span vs height, upper-to-lower segment ratio — skeletal dysplasia) · THYROID · TANNER STAGE with a chaperone · chest, heart, murmur (coarctation), BLOOD PRESSURE · abdomen · joints, spine, nodes · FUNDI AND VISUAL FIELDS.**

**BONE AGE — X-ray of the LEFT HAND AND WRIST. The single most quotable fact: it separates familial (bone age = chronological) from constitutional (bone age behind).** It is non-specific alone — interpret with velocity and bloods.
**First-line bloods: FBE and film, ESR/CRP, U&E and creatinine, LFT, calcium, phosphate, ALP · COELIAC SEROLOGY (tTG-IgA + total IgA) on gluten · TFT · IGF-1 (± IGFBP-3).** VERIFY
**KARYOTYPE IN EVERY GIRL with unexplained short stature — no dysmorphism does NOT exclude Turner syndrome.**
**Urinalysis (urine pH and bicarbonate if renal tubular acidosis suspected). MRI pituitary only if the GH axis is abnormal or there are neurological features.** VERIFY
**RE-MEASURE IN SIX MONTHS and calculate velocity — follow-up is treatment here.**

**RED FLAGS: crossing centiles downward · height more than 2 SD below the MPH target · disproportion · dysmorphism · headache or morning vomiting · visual change · no breast development by 13 · weight falling before height · chronic diarrhoea or blood in stool.**

**AVOID: reassuring before the screen · promising catch-up · averaging without the 13 cm correction · 'failure to thrive' (a weight term) · requesting growth hormone (specialist, strict criteria) · 'she's just small' with no follow-up measurement.**

stem: General practice, regional South Australia. A 5-YEAR-OLD BOY brought in by his mother, WHO SAYS HE IS ALWAYS TIRED. The kindergarten teacher raised it. History 6 minutes, then explain the diagnosis and differentials to the parent. NO physical examination and NO investigations are provided.

VERSION A (older recall): tired all day BUT WORST IN THE MORNINGS, SNORING, waking at night, RECURRENT SORE THROATS, kindy performance affected — obstructive sleep apnoea. VERSION B (2022 onward): NO snoring, NO gasping, NO recurrent infections — but HE IS DRINKING MORE WATER AND PASSING MORE URINE.
tasks: Take a history from the mother (6 minutes)
Explain the diagnosis and your differential diagnoses to the parent
findings: ★ THE POINT OF THE PAIR

The STEM DOES NOT CHANGE — 'a 5-year-old who is ALWAYS TIRED'; only the ANSWERS change. Version A (older recall) is OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNOEA; Version B (2022 onwards) is TYPE 1 DIABETES. A memorised sleep-apnoea script FAILS VERSION B IN THE FIRST MINUTE. No examination and no investigations are provided
★ THE FIRST QUESTION — splits the differential in half

'Do you mean he's SLEEPY all the time, or LOW IN ENERGY?' Version A: 'SLEEPY — his teacher says he NODS OFF, worst first thing in the morning.' Version B: 'LOW IN ENERGY — he used to run around all day and now he JUST SITS on the couch'
Timing — Version B
About SIX WEEKS, EVERY DAY, GETTING WORSE. Nothing helps. He's STOPPED JOINING IN at kindy
★ THIRST — ask it properly, and PAUSE
Ask only 'any thirst?' as a throwaway and she says 'MAYBE A BIT' — making you ask properly. Asked properly: 'yes, actually — he takes a WATER BOTTLE EVERYWHERE and ASKS FOR DRINKS IN THE NIGHT'
★ THE URINE — asked SEPARATELY, or it doesn't come

Parents often answer only the first question. Only on urine or bedwetting specifically: 'he's started WETTING THE BED AGAIN. He'd been DRY FOR OVER A YEAR — I thought it was because of the new kindy.' NEVER DISMISS SECONDARY ENURESIS IN A TIRED CHILD
The malignancy screen
'His TROUSERS ARE LOOSER, now you mention it. He's EATING LESS.' Weight loss fits diabetes — but NO lumps, sweats, bruising, bone pain or fevers
★ THE SLEEP NEGATIVES — arrive early, and the station is built to catch you freezing

'NO SNORING AT ALL. He sleeps quietly — apart from GETTING UP TO DRINK and WETTING THE BED.' Answered FLATLY to see whether you RECOVER or keep pushing. The recovery line: 'THAT MAKES A SLEEP PROBLEM LESS LIKELY — let me ask about some other causes'
The rest — all negative

No fever, travel, rash or recent illness. NOT PALE; meat a few times a week, ONE glass of milk; no yellow skin or dark urine. Mood flat because he's tired; home and kindy fine, NO bullying. Bowels normal, no greasy stools. No cough; tired running but NEVER BLUE. Alert but flat. Normal birth, immunised, no medicines or allergies. HER MOTHER HAS AN UNDERACTIVE THYROID
★ HER REACTION AND HIDDEN AGENDA
Calm at first, SHOCKED at the word: 'DIABETES? HE'S FIVE.' Then: 'IS IT BECAUSE OF WHAT HE EATS? IS IT MY FAULT?' — a good candidate says NO and does not blame her
★ VERSION A — the answers swapped

Two months, every day, WORST IN THE MORNINGS; his teacher raised it. 'He SNORES EVERY NIGHT — you can hear him through the wall. Sometimes he seems to STOP, THEN GASPS.' SORE THROATS FOUR OR FIVE A YEAR. GRUMPY AND HARD TO MANAGE lately. NO thirst or urine change
KETOACIDOSIS VARIANT

Vomiting two days, breathing DEEP AND SIGHING, DROWSY, dehydrated → DKA: IV access, glucose, ketones and bloods, cautious fluids, insulin per paediatric protocol AFTER fluids, hourly neuro obs for CEREBRAL OEDEMA, MedSTAR — 'please don't drive him yourselves'
Other practice cards

BRUISES on shins and back, NIGHT LEG PAINS, intermittent fevers, pale → LEUKAEMIA, same-day FBE and film · tired since a bad sore throat TWO MONTHS AGO, tender nodes, big spleen → EBV / post-viral, no contact sport · flat since GRANDMOTHER DIED and a new kindy, another child hitting her → ADJUSTMENT and bullying — but screen the whole mnemonic first · pale, short, FLOATING STOOLS, aunt with coeliac → coeliac, keep gluten in · 'TIRED AND NOT PAYING ATTENTION AT SCHOOL' → a DIFFERENT station: the behaviour pathway (ADHD, autism, absence seizures, hearing)

dx: **VERSION B: TYPE 1 DIABETES MELLITUS. VERSION A: OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNOEA (adenotonsillar hypertrophy). BOTH ARE REACHED BY THE SAME HISTORY.**

**★ THE PASS/FAIL LINE — THIS STATION EXISTS TO PUNISH RECALL MEMORISATION. The stem is 'always tired' and it has produced at least two entirely different diagnoses with NO CHANGE IN WORDING. The mark is the COMPLETENESS OF THE DIFFERENTIAL SCREEN and the LENGTH AND SPECIFICITY OF THE LIST you give back. A long list is NOT PADDING — the examiner explicitly wants thyroid, malignancy, infection, anaemia, mental health, coeliac, cardiac and sleep apnoea ALL NAMED.**

**THE STRUCTURE FOLLOWS THE STEM, NOT THE RECALL. A candidate who memorised the sleep-apnoea case is STRANDED by the first three negatives in Version B; a candidate with the mnemonic simply KEEPS GOING and arrives at the thirst and the urine.** **The recovery line when your first suspicion dies: 'THANK YOU — THAT MAKES A SLEEP PROBLEM LESS LIKELY. LET ME ASK ABOUT SOME OTHER CAUSES.' Then continue without pause — never freeze, and never keep asking sleep questions hoping for a different answer.**

**★ DEFINE THE SYMPTOM FIRST — ONE SENTENCE THAT SPLITS THE DIFFERENTIAL IN HALF: 'is he SLEEPY all the time, or LOW IN ENERGY?' SLEEPINESS points to a SLEEP DISORDER; LOW ENERGY points to TRUE FATIGUE.** **Skip it and you can spend six minutes chasing fatigue in a child who actually has a sleep disorder, or vice versa.**

**HEMI-A-D-C-O-P, ADAPTED FOR CHILDREN — H (heart failure / hepatitis, rare) and P (period / pregnancy, n/a) effectively struck out; TWO OR THREE QUESTIONS PER LETTER FILLS SIX MINUTES EXACTLY: E — ENDOCRINE (thirst, urine and bedwetting, cold, constipation, family history) · M — MALIGNANCY (weight, appetite, lumps, night sweats, bruising, bone pain, fevers) · I — INFECTION (fever, travel, rash, recent flu or sore throat — EBV) · A — ANAEMIA (pale, red meat, cow's milk, yellow skin or dark urine) · D — DEPRESSION (mood, sleep, home, kindy, bullying) · C — COELIAC + CARDIOPULMONARY (greasy stools, cough, puffed or BLUE on exercise) · O — OSA (snoring, gasping or pauses, morning sleepiness, recurrent infections, behaviour).** **E comes FIRST for a reason. The examiner doesn't mark the filing — only whether each question was ASKED.**

**THE TIME BUDGET: 45 s define · 45 s timing and pattern · 3 min 15 s the mnemonic · 45 s well-child · 30 s BINDSMA leftovers and family history. Finishing the history at four minutes is under-using the time.**

**VERSION B — NAME IT AND EXPLAIN THE MECHANISM: 'the most likely explanation is DIABETES — the sugar level in his blood is TOO HIGH. My reasons: he's DRINKING much more, PASSING much more urine and WETTING THE BED AGAIN after being dry, LOSING A LITTLE WEIGHT, and TIRED. When the blood sugar is high, the body DUMPS THE EXTRA SUGAR IN THE URINE and that DRAGS WATER WITH IT — so he passes more urine and gets thirsty.'** **To 'is it what he eats?': 'it's the type where the body stops making insulin — it ISN'T caused by anything you did or by what he eats.'**

**★ THE FULL DIFFERENTIAL SENTENCE — eight or more, named: 'I thought about an UNDERACTIVE THYROID; blood cancers like LEUKAEMIA; INFECTIONS, especially viral ones like GLANDULAR FEVER that leave children tired for weeks; ANAEMIA; LOW MOOD or something happening at kindy; COELIAC disease; HEART problems he might have been born with; and SLEEP APNOEA. Nothing you've told me fits those the way this does.'**

**★ VERSION B — DO NOW: FINGER-PRICK GLUCOSE AND KETONES IN THE CONSULTATION; assess hydration, breathing pattern, conscious state, weight. If raised: SAME-DAY discussion with the WCH paediatric team — THE CHILD GOES TO HOSPITAL TODAY, NOT TOMORROW. 'It is serious, but it's very treatable, and children with diabetes live completely normal lives.' THE KETOACIDOSIS SAFETY-NET: DROWSY, VOMITING, or breathing DEEP AND SIGHING = an emergency — IV access, cautious fluids, insulin per the paediatric DKA protocol AFTER fluids, hourly neuro obs for cerebral oedema, MedSTAR retrieval; DON'T LET THE FAMILY DRIVE TO ADELAIDE UNSUPERVISED.** VERIFY **DKA can present as 'GASTRO THAT ISN'T GETTING BETTER' in a thirsty, tired child.**

**VERSION A — OSA: 'when he sleeps, the throat muscles become FLOPPY, and with large TONSILS AND ADENOIDS the airway BLOCKS OFF for short periods. That causes the snoring and gasping, INTERRUPTS HIS SLEEP over and over without properly waking him, and that's why he's tired all day and struggling at kindy.' Paediatric and ENT referral, SLEEP STUDY; ADENOTONSILLECTOMY is the usual treatment in children VERIFY; meanwhile treat nasal obstruction and allergic rhinitis. Untreated OSA causes behavioural and learning problems and rarely pulmonary hypertension. Adenotonsillar hypertrophy peaks 2–8 years.** VERIFY **AVOID: a memorised single-diagnosis script · reassurance in a child losing weight or drinking constantly · 'a blood test next week' when diabetes or leukaemia is on the list · blaming screen time or kindy without excluding the list.** SA: **WCH diabetes service** — new type 1 in a regional child discussed the SAME DAY; **MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33**; **NDSS** registration; **Diabetes SA**; WCH ENT and sleep services with **PATS**; ACCHS; **TIS 131 450**.
plan: **INTRO, OPEN, ACKNOWLEDGE**: **'hello, I'm Dr ___, one of the GPs. How can I help you today?'** *'It's Noah. He's just always tired, doctor. He's not himself.'* → **'that must be worrying, and you did the right thing bringing him in — we'll work out what's behind it together.'**

**★ DEFINE THE SYMPTOM — the split**: **'when you say tired, do you mean he's SLEEPY all the time, or that he's LOW IN ENERGY — not playing and running about like other children?'** *'Low in energy. He used to be everywhere; now he just sits on the couch.'*

**TIMING AND PATTERN**: **'how long has this been going on? Every day, or on and off? Worse at a particular time of day? Getting worse? Anything that makes it better or worse? Is it affecting him at kindy or at home?'** *Six weeks, every day, worse; stopped joining in.*
**Signpost the mnemonic**: **'I'd like to ask about a number of possible causes.'** **And E comes first for a reason.**

**★ E — THIRST, THEN PAUSE**: **'has he been more thirsty than usual — drinking more than he used to?'** *(let it land)* *'Yes, actually — a water bottle everywhere, and drinks in the night.'* **A throwaway 'any thirst?' gets 'maybe a bit'.**

**★ E — THE URINE, ASKED SEPARATELY**: **'and have you noticed him passing more urine, or WETTING THE BED?'** *'He's started wetting the bed again — dry for over a year. I thought it was the new kindy.'* → **'thank you, that's important.'** Then **'does he feel the cold? Any constipation? Any family history of diabetes or thyroid problems?'** *Grandmother — underactive thyroid.*

**M — MALIGNANCY, all five, thirty seconds**: **'has he lost weight — are you happy with his growth? Any change in appetite? Any lumps or bumps, night sweats, easy bruising, bone or leg pains, or fevers?'** *Trousers looser; eating less; nothing else.*

**I and A**: **'any fever, travel, rashes, or a recent flu-like illness or sore throat?'** *No.* **'Does he look pale? Describe his diet — red meat, how much cow's milk? Any yellow skin or eyes, or dark urine?'** *Not pale; meat a few times a week; one glass; no.*

**D and C**: **'how would you describe his mood and his sleep? How are things at home and kindy — any stressors or bullying?'** *Flat because tired; fine.* **'Any greasy stools — stick, float, hard to flush? Diarrhoea, blood? Cough? Does he get puffed or turn BLUE when he runs?'** *Normal; tired running but never blue.*

**★ O — AND THE RECOVERY LINE**: **'does he snore? Any gasping or pauses in his breathing? Sleepy in the mornings? Recurrent throat or ear infections? New behaviour problems?'** *'No snoring at all — he sleeps quietly, apart from getting up to drink and wetting the bed.'* → **'thank you — that makes a sleep problem much less likely.'** **Keep moving.**

**WELL-CHILD AND BINDSMA LEFTOVERS**: **'is he alert or drowsy? Eating and drinking as usual? Passing urine normally? Any concerns about development? Birth, immunisations, medicines, allergies? Family history of thyroid, diabetes or coeliac?'** *Alert but flat; eating less, drinking loads; all normal.*

**★ NAME IT, WITH REASONS AND THE MECHANISM — calm, unhurried**: **'from what you've told me, the most likely explanation is diabetes — the sugar in his blood being too high. The reasons: drinking much more, passing much more urine and wetting the bed again after being dry, losing a little weight, and being tired. When the blood sugar is high, the body dumps the extra sugar in the urine and that drags water with it — so he passes more urine and gets thirsty.'**

**'Diabetes? He's five.' — then 'not your fault'**: **'I know that's a shock. It does happen at this age — it's the type where the body stops making insulin, and it isn't caused by anything you did or by what he eats.'**

**★ THE FULL DIFFERENTIAL LIST — eight or more, by name**: **an underactive thyroid, blood cancers like leukaemia, infections such as glandular fever, anaemia, low mood or problems at kindy, coeliac disease, heart problems, and sleep apnoea — 'and nothing you've told me fits those the way this does.'** **Three is not enough after six minutes.**

**★ THE PLAN — BEDSIDE TEST NOW, HOSPITAL TODAY, DKA SAFETY-NET**: **'I'd like to do a finger-prick sugar test right now, and check for ketones. If the sugar is high, he needs to be seen at the Women's and Children's today — they'll start treatment and teach you both how to manage it. If he becomes drowsy, starts vomiting, or his breathing looks deep and sighing, that's an emergency and we arrange retrieval straight away. It's serious, but it's very treatable, and children with diabetes live full, normal lives.'**

findings: ★ THE LATERAL NECK X-RAY — Version A

A LARGE ADENOID SHADOW and ENLARGED TONSILS, NARROWING THE NASOPHARYNGEAL AIRWAY. Point at the shadow, name it, link it to obstruction — the colour lecture ('white is bone, grey is soft tissue…') EATS A MINUTE
★ THE OVERNIGHT OXIMETRY — Version A
MULTIPLE DROPS BELOW 90%. The mark is for 'BELOW 90 PER CENT, MORE THAN TWO OR THREE TIMES, AND THAT IS SIGNIFICANT' — describing the squiggles without the threshold and its meaning scores nothing
The PE card — some sittings
LARGE TONSILS on throat examination; MOUTH-BREATHING AT REST. Version B's card: large tonsils, GROWTH CHART NORMAL, DEVELOPMENTAL MILESTONES ACHIEVED
The snoring
About SIX MONTHS, EVERY NIGHT now, LOUDER. WORSE WITH A COLD — consistent with a narrowed airway. 'We can hear it from our bedroom'
★ APNOEA — ask it BOTH WAYS

Gasping: 'yes — he GOES QUIET AND THEN DOES A BIG GASP.' Pauses, asked SEPARATELY: 'I HAVE, actually. I've STOOD THERE AND COUNTED.' SOME PARENTS DESCRIBE PAUSES, NOT GASPS — asking only one is the named trap. Missing it is the SINGLE-ITEM AUTO-FAIL

MOUTH ALWAYS OPEN — the second named must-ask. THRASHES ABOUT, ends up upside down in the bed; sweaty

HARD TO WAKE, GRUMPY; FALLS ASLEEP IN THE CAR every afternoon. Kindy says he doesn't follow instructions — and he's been HITTING OTHER KIDS, NEW IN THE LAST TWO MONTHS. OSA presents as a BEHAVIOUR PROBLEM in children far more than as sleepiness
★ BEDWETTING — a marked item, ten seconds
'He was DRY AT NIGHT and now he's WET AGAIN most nights. We thought it was THE NEW BABY.' SECONDARY ENURESIS is a recognised association and resolves with treatment

dx: **OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNOEA SECONDARY TO ADENOTONSILLAR HYPERTROPHY — repeated partial or complete upper-airway obstruction during sleep, with snoring, arousals, disrupted sleep and intermittent hypoxaemia. The pharyngeal muscles relax in sleep and the already-narrowed airway collapses. Adenoid and tonsils are relatively LARGEST BETWEEN ABOUT 2 AND 8 YEARS.**

**★ THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE — COMPLETENESS BEATS SPEED, AND DIFFERENTIALS COME FROM THE STEM. VERSION A: everyone gets the diagnosis. Candidates fail because they ask snoring and gasping, ANNOUNCE SLEEP APNOEA, AND STOP. The examiner marks the SURVEY: apnoea both ways, mouth breathing, morning tiredness / concentration / school, behaviour, enuresis, runny nose and recurrent infections, hearing, growth and development, then BINDS.** **The script: 'I know this sounds like a lot of questions for snoring — snoring in a child is about HOW HE BREATHES WHEN HE SLEEPS, and that can affect his whole day, so I want to check each part.'**

**VERSION B: the father's aside about a fight TEMPTS AN AUTISM SCRIPT. The differential list must be generated from TIREDNESS + INATTENTION: OSA and ADHD first, then ASD, absence seizures, diabetes, thyroid, anaemia, hearing/vision, mood and home.** **The script: 'you've mentioned the fight at school — I'll come back to that. First I want to understand the tiredness, BECAUSE A TIRED CHILD CAN'T PAY ATTENTION.'**

**THE ONE-LINE STRATEGY, HEADINGS SAID OUT LOUD: snoring → APNOEA → daytime → behaviour → WET BED → infections and hearing → growth → BINDS.** **The communication challenge: a father who thinks snoring is a NOISE PROBLEM — you must convert it into a BREATHING-DURING-SLEEP PROBLEM WITH CONSEQUENCES, without frightening him. Acknowledge, don't reassure: 'lots of children snore' at the door is a named trap.**

**ADULT VERSUS CHILD — the exam contrast: CHILD OSA presents with BEHAVIOUR (hyperactivity, aggression, inattention) more than sleepiness; clues are MOUTH BREATHING, ENURESIS, RECURRENT URTI / OTITIS, POOR GROWTH; treatment is ADENOTONSILLECTOMY, not weight and CPAP first.** CORRECTION — **the lecture says children with OSA are 'mostly underweight'. Safer: the commonest cause is adenotonsillar hypertrophy and it isn't an obesity disease in preschoolers, but OBESITY is a growing risk factor in school-aged children and severe OSA can impair growth. 'Paediatric OSA is BIMODAL.'** **Severity (obstructive AHI): >1 abnormal; 1–5 mild, 5–10 moderate, >10 severe.** VERIFY

**THE X-RAY — FOUR SENTENCES, NO COLOUR LECTURE: 'this is an X-ray of the SIDE OF HIS NECK. I can see NARROWING of his airway — the tube air travels down behind his nose and throat. The narrowing is because of LARGE TONSILS and a LARGE ADENOID — a GLAND AT THE BACK OF THE NOSE AND THROAT. A narrow airway has a much higher chance of BLOCKING WHILE HE SLEEPS, and that's what causes the snoring and gasping.'** **Not routine in practice — ENT nasendoscopy is more useful — but it's the exam's investigation.**

**★ THE OXIMETRY — BASELINE, THEN THE ABNORMAL, THEN THE THRESHOLD: 'while he was asleep we measured the OXYGEN IN HIS BLOOD through the night. Normally it stays high with only tiny dips. On his trace there are MULTIPLE DROPS, and they go BELOW 90 PER CENT. More than TWO OR THREE drops like that in a night is SIGNIFICANT — a feature of a breathing problem during sleep.'** **Overnight oximetry is an accessible screen (clustered desaturations below 90% — McGill score); POLYSOMNOGRAPHY is the gold standard and MANDATORY for high-risk groups, discordant oximetry, or uncertainty before surgery.** VERIFY

**THE DIAGNOSIS — NAME, MECHANISM, REASONS, THEN BOTH TESTS: 'Liam has OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNOEA. The large tonsils and adenoid narrow the airway; when he sleeps the throat muscles become FLOPPY, the narrowed airway BLOCKS, and he snores, pauses, then gasps to open it. Everything you've told me fits — the gasping and pauses, mouth breathing, tired mornings, the behaviour, the bedwetting — and BOTH TESTS confirm it.'** **Plain language throughout — 'stops breathing for a few seconds', 'a gland at the back of the throat' — never 'apnoea' or 'adenotonsillar hypertrophy' to the father.**

**★ MANAGEMENT — REFERRAL TO BOTH A PAEDIATRICIAN AND ENT is the lecture's stated NON-NEGOTIABLE, because of the impact on growth, behaviour and the heart. ADENOTONSILLECTOMY is first-line — 'removing the two blockages', and childhood is the right time. CPAP — 'a small mask worn during sleep that gives a constant flow of air to keep the airway open' — if surgery isn't suitable or OSA is residual. Treat allergic rhinitis (intranasal steroid, saline). HEARING TEST and developmental / speech review. Measure BP — OSA is a recognised cause of hypertension in children. Reassess after treatment. SAFETY-NET: 'IF YOU EVER SEE HIM GO BLUE OR GREY DURING A PAUSE, CALL 000.'** **Don't promise surgery or a date — the surgeon decides.** **Answer his fear honestly: 'it's not dangerous tonight, but it does need fixing.'**

**VERSION B — the extra blocks the 6-minute history must contain: ADHD triad in two settings (finishes homework? waits his turn? acts without thinking?) · ASD triad (eye contact, friends, repetitive words, routines) · ABSENCE SEIZURES ('episodes of unusual long staring where he's not with you?') · DIABETES (thirst, urine, weight) · thyroid · vision and hearing · head injury · mood · plus anaemia. Skipping absence seizures and diabetes because you already 'have' OSA is the named trap — FINGER-PRICK BGL before you leave the room.** **HIGH-RISK GROUPS where adenotonsillectomy alone often fails and polysomnography is required: OBESITY, DOWN SYNDROME, CRANIOFACIAL ABNORMALITY, NEUROMUSCULAR DISEASE.** **AVOID: 'just snoring' / 'he'll grow out of it' · SEDATIVE ANTIHISTAMINES (worsen obstruction) · antibiotics for tonsils that are big, not infected.** SA: WCH paediatric sleep service VERIFY; Yorke and Northern LHN paediatric outreach; **PATS**; **Country Health Connect** for speech and audiology; ACCHS with a low threshold for audiology; **TIS 131 450**; **000 / MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33** for cyanotic apnoea or stridor.
plan: **WIPE, sit at his level, confidentiality in a line**: **'good morning, I'm Dr ___, one of the GPs here. And this is Liam? Everything we talk about stays confidential. How can I help today?'** *'It's his snoring — so loud we can hear it from our bedroom.'*

**★ ACKNOWLEDGE, DON'T REASSURE — then signpost**: **'I can hear that it's worrying you, and it's a good thing you've come in. Let's work together — I'll find out what's causing it and we'll make the best plan for him. I'll ask about the snoring, then how he sleeps, then how he is during the day, then a few routine questions.'** **Never 'lots of children snore'.**

**EXPLORE THE SNORING**: **'when did you first notice it? Every night or on and off? Getting worse? Anything that makes it better or worse — colds, lying on his back?'** *Six months, every night, louder, worse with a cold.*

**★ APNOEA — TWICE, TWO WAYS, IN THE FIRST MINUTE**: **'have you noticed him GASPING or CHOKING during his sleep?'** *Goes quiet, then a big gasp.* → **'and have you seen him STOP BREATHING for a few seconds — pauses in his breathing?'** *'I've stood there and counted.'* **Some parents recognise pauses, not gasps.**
**SLEEP QUALITY — pair mouth breathing with the apnoea**: **'does he BREATHE THROUGH HIS MOUTH? Is he restless, sweaty, sleeping with his head tipped back?'** *Mouth always open; thrashes about.*

**★ DAYTIME, then behaviour — linked aloud**: **'that's really helpful — now his daytime. Is he tired in the mornings? Sleepy during the day? Any trouble concentrating at kindy? Any change in his BEHAVIOUR — more aggressive, hyperactive, harder to manage?'** *Hard to wake, grumpy, asleep in the car; hitting other kids — new.* **Behaviour, not sleepiness, is how children present.**

**★ BEDWETTING — ten seconds, a marked item**: **'two or three things that often go with snoring — any bedwetting, or has he started wetting again?'** *'Dry, and now wet again most nights — we thought it was the new baby.'*

**ASSOCIATIONS AND GROWTH**: **'does he get a lot of runny or blocked noses or colds? Any ear infections? Any worry about his hearing or speech? Any concerns about his growth or development?'** *Permanent runny nose; two ear infections; hearing and speech fine; small but following his line.*

Anyone in the family with snoring, sleep apnoea, asthma or hay fever?'** *Normal; done; none; he snored and had his tonsils out, wife has hay fever.*

dx: **PRIMARY MONOSYMPTOMATIC NOCTURNAL ENURESIS — intermittent involuntary wetting during sleep in a child ≥ 5 years, NEVER DRY FOR 6 MONTHS (primary), with NO OTHER LOWER URINARY TRACT SYMPTOMS (monosymptomatic). Mechanisms: DEEP SLEEP with poor arousal, NOCTURNAL POLYURIA (low overnight ADH), small functional bladder capacity — STRONGLY FAMILIAL. About 15% of 5-year-olds; ~15% resolve spontaneously each year. A station with a VERY HIGH FAILURE RATE.**

**WHY THE AGE IS ALWAYS SIX: night-time control arrives between 5 AND 7. Under 6 the answer is 'wait and reassure'; the station is set at 6 so that ACTIVE MANAGEMENT — THE ALARM — is expected. At 7+ with no response → investigate.** **If challenged 'why treat at six?': 'most children are dry by five to seven, so at six an alarm is appropriate — particularly because it's affecting him socially.'**

**★ DISCRIMINATOR 1 — EARN THE WORD 'MONOSYMPTOMATIC'. The examiner's key-point list STARTS WITH THE URINARY QUESTIONS — the single biggest reason candidates fail. Candidates ask 'any burning? any infections?' and move on; THAT IS A UTI SCREEN, NOT A LUTS SCREEN. THE TEN, BY NAME: DYSURIA · FREQUENCY · URGENCY · DAYTIME WETTING / DAMP PANTS · DRIBBLING · WEAK OR INTERRUPTED STREAM · STRAINING / HESITANCY · HAEMATURIA · RECURRENT UTIs · POLYURIA. Then STATE THE CONCLUSION: 'so there are no daytime or other urinary symptoms — this is night-time wetting only.'** **The sentence that introduces it: 'I'm going to run through a list about his wee, day and night, because IF ANY OF THEM ARE POSITIVE, THIS IS A DIFFERENT PROBLEM WITH A DIFFERENT TREATMENT.'**

**WHY IT MATTERS: ANY daytime symptom — wetting, urgency, frequency, dribbling, weak stream, straining — means a STRUCTURAL OR FUNCTIONAL BLADDER PROBLEM (overactive bladder, dysfunctional voiding, posterior urethral valves, reflux, ectopic ureter in girls with continuous dribble). NOT AN ALARM CASE — dipstick, MCSU, renal tract ultrasound, continence clinic or urology. 'Monosymptomatic' is a conclusion you EARN by asking, not an assumption.**

**THE HISTORY IN FIVE BOXES: 1 TIMING — how long, EVER DRY 6 MONTHS, nights per week, DAYTIME WETTING, better or worse · 2 EVERY LUTS · 3 PSYCHOSOCIAL AND SLEEP — home, HOW SHE REACTS / PUNISHMENT, school, teasing, SLEEPOVERS, how he feels, deep sleeper, where the toilet is · 4 DIFFERENTIALS, one or two questions each — FLUIDS AND CAFFEINE, CONSTIPATION AND SOILING, DIABETES (thirst, polyuria, weight), SLEEP APNOEA (snoring, gasping), NEURO (walking, legs, back, dimple) · 5 BINDS, growth, medications, FAMILY HISTORY ('until what age?').** **Psychosocial impact is the SECOND key point — ask it early.**

**THE EXPLANATION — NAME, DEFINE, THE REASON, NOT HIS FAULT: 'Oliver has PRIMARY NOCTURNAL ENURESIS — bedwetting. PRIMARY because he's never been dry, NOCTURNAL because it only happens at night. Most children learn to hold on at night between five and seven; some — often DEEP SLEEPERS, and often where A PARENT WAS THE SAME — get there later. His brain doesn't yet WAKE HIM WHEN HIS BLADDER IS FULL, and at night the kidneys make MORE URINE than the bladder can hold. IT'S NOT LAZINESS AND IT ISN'T HIS FAULT — AND IT ISN'T YOURS.'** **Then THE EXCLUSIONS: 'from the questions, the examination and the two tests, I've ruled out infection, diabetes, constipation, sleep apnoea and any problem with his nerves or bladder.'**

**★ DISCRIMINATOR 2 — THE ALARM IS THE TREATMENT; DESMOPRESSIN IS NOT. SAY: 'the most effective treatment, AND THE ONE THAT LASTS, is a BEDWETTING ALARM.' Explain it properly — a SENSOR under the sheet or clipped to his pyjamas; the first drops set it off and wake him; HE switches it off and FINISHES IN THE TOILET; over 6–8 WEEKS, sometimes 3–4 months, his brain learns to WAKE TO A FULL BLADDER and then to hold on; STOP AFTER 14 CONSECUTIVE DRY NIGHTS; restart if relapse. 'IT'S HIS ALARM.' Hire or buy. Success roughly two-thirds with lasting effect.** VERIFY

**AND UNPROMPTED: 'there is a medicine, DESMOPRESSIN, but it's NOT THE TREATMENT — it only works on the nights it's taken. It's for ONE OR TWO NIGHTS for a SLEEPOVER OR CAMP, or if the ALARM HASN'T WORKED AFTER A FEW MONTHS.' Melt 120 mcg sublingual or tablet 200 mcg at bedtime; NO FLUIDS from 1 h before to 8 h after; ORAL / SUBLINGUAL ONLY.** VERIFY **If challenged 'why not just give the tablet?': 'it only works on the nights it's taken and most children relapse when it stops; the alarm retrains the brain and the effect lasts. It's also safer — the nasal spray was withdrawn.'** CORRECTION — **the nasal spray was withdrawn for enuresis because of HYPONATRAEMIA / WATER INTOXICATION — the transcript says 'hypernatraemia'.** **TRICYCLICS (imipramine) are no longer used.**

**THE REST OF THE PLAN — BULLET IT, OR YOU RUN OUT OF TIME: FLUIDS — drink well through the day (6–7 drinks), NO cordial, Coke, fizzy or caffeinated drinks especially in the evening, no big drinks in the last hour before bed, wee before bed — NOT FLUID RESTRICTION · treat CONSTIPATION if present · NO PUNISHMENT from now — 'he can't help it' · a STAR CHART for things he CAN control (drinking well, using the alarm, helping change sheets) · waterproof mattress protector · REVIEW IN 4–6 WEEKS · red flags: daytime wetting, pain, fever or smelly wee, very thirsty, soiling · refer if the alarm fails after 3 months or he's still wetting at 7.** **AVOID: lifting or waking the child at set times (helps the sheets, not the bladder) · nappies at 6 as the only plan · 'he'll grow out of it' alone at 6 · investigations (USS, urodynamics) for a classic monosymptomatic picture.**

**SECONDARY ENURESIS (dry ≥ 6 months, then wet) is a TRIGGER SCREEN: UTI, DIABETES (BSL today), CONSTIPATION, STRESS at home or school, OSA — and ABUSE. Wetting PLUS soiling, leg weakness, back pain or a sacral dimple → SPINAL CORD (tethered cord) — urgent MRI.** SA: alarms through pharmacies, **CaFHS 1300 733 606** continence clinics or the **WCH Continence Service**; **National Continence Helpline 1800 33 00 66** for suppliers and the 'Bedwetting' family guide; WCH paediatric continence / urology for daytime LUTS, red-flag secondary enuresis, alarm failure, or persistence beyond 7–8; a positive BSL is same-day WCH Diabetes / **MedSTAR Kids 1300 13 12 33** if ketotic; a letter to the school for camp; **PATS**; ACCHS; **CARL 13 14 78** — mandatory notifier.

**SCHOOL, SLEEPOVERS, FEELINGS, SLEEP**: **'how's school — any teasing? Does it stop him going on sleepovers? Oliver, how do you feel about it?'** *Won't go; camp next term; 'I don't like it.'* → **'that makes sense, Oliver.'** Then **'is he a deep sleeper? **★ DIFFERENTIALS — fluids first, the one modifiable positive**: **'does he drink a lot during the day? What does he drink in the EVENING — cordial, Coke, fizzy or caffeinated drinks?'** *Cordial and Coke with dinner and before bed.*

**Bowels, diabetes, OSA, neuro — one or two questions each**: **'any constipation — hard or infrequent poos? Does he ever soil himself? Has he been unusually thirsty, passing large volumes, lost weight, tired? Does he snore, gasp or stop breathing at night? Any trouble walking, weakness or numbness in the legs, back problems, a dimple on his lower back?'** *No to all.*

**BINDS AND THE FAMILY HISTORY — 'until what age?'**: **'any problems in the pregnancy or birth, any kidney or spine problems found as a baby? Immunisations, medical problems, regular medicines? Growing and developing as expected? Did either parent or a sibling wet the bed — until what age?'** *Dad, until about eight.*

**SUMMARISE, THEN THE EXAMINATION REQUEST — including dipstick and glucose**: **'lifelong night-time wetting, never dry six months, no daytime or other urinary symptoms, fizzy drinks in the evening, deep sleeper, dad the same, and it's upsetting him.'** Then **general appearance; growth chart; abdomen for a palpable bladder or faecal mass; genitalia and the meatus; perianal inspection and ANAL WINK; spine for a dimple or tuft; lower-limb tone, power, reflexes, gait; tonsils; and a URINE DIPSTICK and FINGERPRICK BLOOD GLUCOSE.**

**★ NAME IT, DEFINE IT, NOT HIS FAULT — OR HERS**: **'Oliver has primary nocturnal enuresis — bedwetting. Primary because he's never been dry, nocturnal because it's only at night. Most children learn to hold on at night between five and seven; deep sleepers, and children where a parent was the same, get there later. His brain doesn't yet wake him when his bladder is full. It's not laziness and it isn't his fault — or yours.'** Then **the exclusions — infection, diabetes, constipation, sleep apnoea, nerves or bladder.**

**★ 'IS THERE A TABLET?' — THE ALARM FIRST, EXPLAINED**: **'his dad was eight — children get there at different ages. The most effective treatment, and the one that lasts, is a bedwetting alarm: a small sensor under the sheet or clipped to his pyjamas. The first drops set it off, it wakes him, he switches it off himself and finishes in the toilet. Over six to eight weeks, sometimes a few months, his brain learns to wake to a full bladder. It's his alarm.'**

findings: The examination — if the task is given
Growth NORMAL. Abdomen: a FIRM, NON-TENDER MASS in the LEFT LOWER abdomen — LOADED BOWEL. Perianal: a SMALL HEALED FISSURE, ANAL WINK PRESENT. Spine and neurology NORMAL. Thyroid normal
★ WHERE THE MASS IS — a recall correction

The recall says 'RIGHT LOWER QUADRANT.' Impacted stool is usually palpable in the LEFT ILIAC FOSSA and SUPRAPUBICALLY (sigmoid and rectum); a right-sided mass is caecal loading in severe cases. Say: 'a firm, mobile, non-tender mass in the lower abdomen consistent with LOADED BOWEL'
★ NO RECTAL EXAMINATION

Say 'PERIANAL INSPECTION' and 'I WOULD NOT PERFORM A RECTAL EXAMINATION.' The RCH pathway doesn't recommend routine PR in children: 'it rarely changes management and can REINFORCE THE FEAR that started the withholding'
★ HER OPENING — and it needs a massive acknowledgement

'Doctor, I'm AT THE END OF MY TETHER. He's soiling his pants EVERY DAY — I'm washing clothes every day and it's not getting better. HE'S TEN.' She ONLY RELAXES if you acknowledge properly — a one-line 'I understand' doesn't do it. 'I don't know if he's doing it ON PURPOSE'
Box 1 — timing
About SIX MONTHS, every day, sometimes twice. DAYTIME — 'he comes home from school like that.' Worse. 'He had a bit of it AT FIVE and it settled'
★ Box 2 — describe it, then the wetting

'RUNNY, LIKE DIARRHOEA — SMALL amounts, it STAINS his pants.' NO BLOOD. 'He says he CAN'T FEEL IT.' Does he wet? — 'NO, NEVER.' Hearing 'runny' and thinking DIARRHOEA is the trap: LIQUID + SMALL + CAN'T FEEL IT = OVERFLOW
★ Box 3 — the constipation, only when asked about bowel motions

'CONSTIPATION, ALWAYS. Every FOUR OR FIVE DAYS — HARD AS ROCKS, BLOCKS THE TOILET.' No ribbon, no blood or mucus. Strains for ages. She volunteers 'runny' readily — the constipation comes ONLY WHEN YOU ASK HIS BOWEL HABIT
Diet, water, exercise
'JUNK — chips, nuggets, white bread. Maybe a banana.' BARELY ANY WATER — cordial and ABOUT A LITRE OF MILK a day. On the iPad, no sport
★ THE TRIGGER — only when asked directly

Won't go at school, ever. CROSSES HIS LEGS AND WRIGGLES. 'When he was SEVEN he had one that MADE HIM SCREAM — BLOOD ON THE PAPER — and after that he just wouldn't go.' The origin of the cycle and the key to the explanation
Differentials — all negative

A tummy ache before he goes; not bloated, no vomiting. Not greasy; NO coeliac or type 1 diabetes in the family. Not cold, skin fine. WALKS FINE, NO BACK PAIN, no dimple. No medicines. NORMAL BIRTH, MECONIUM DAY ONE. Immunised. Growing well, 50th centile. Toilet-trained at 3 'with a battle'
★ THE IMPACT

Liam, quietly, when asked how he feels: 'I HATE IT. Kids at school call me STINKY.' Jane: 'I've YELLED AT HIM and TAKEN THE iPAD. I'm not proud of it.' Bullied about the smell. If never asked how she reacts, at about 4:30: 'I'VE BEEN PUNISHING HIM — IS THAT WRONG?'

Say 'laxatives' WITHOUT 'clear it out first' and she asks: 'BUT WHY IS IT RUNNY IF HE'S CONSTIPATED?' Say TWO WEEKS of Movicol and she asks: 'AND THEN IT'S FIXED?' Register: exasperated → GUILTY AND TEARFUL at the mechanism ('so he's not doing it on purpose? I feel terrible') → relieved with a plan

dx: **ENCOPRESIS — overflow incontinence from FUNCTIONAL CONSTIPATION WITH FAECAL IMPACTION. Involuntary passage of stool, usually into clothing, in a child over 4 — in >90% due to functional constipation: hard retained stool STRETCHES THE RECTUM, the urge is BLUNTED, and LIQUID STOOL LEAKS AROUND THE MASS. The child CANNOT FEEL IT COMING and CANNOT STOP IT — it is NOT NAUGHTINESS.** **A 2025 recall with a HIGH FAILURE RATE.**

**★ DISCRIMINATOR 1 — MANAGEMENT STEP ONE IS 'EMPTY THE BOWEL' — SAID, EXPLAINED, AND PUT FIRST. Candidates fail this station IN MANAGEMENT, NOT HISTORY. They say 'laxatives, diet, toileting' and NEVER STATE THE PURPOSE. The examiner is listening for: 'this is happening because there's a BLOCKAGE OF HARD STOOL at the end of the bowel — the FIRST THING I have to do is GET THAT OUT.' Only after that do maintenance laxatives, diet and behaviour score.**

**★ DISCRIMINATOR 2 — THE HISTORY HAS NO OPTIONAL QUESTIONS. Day/night, BLOOD (TWICE), WETTING, the PAINFUL MOTION, WITHHOLDING, diet/water/exercise, coeliac, thyroid, neurological, FIRST MECONIUM, growth, home/punishment/school — EACH IS A SEPARATE MARK. The candidate who 'rules out a few differentials' and moves on fails on the missed boxes.** **There is no tail of the list to drop — and management needs two minutes because the first step must be explained.**

**THE SOILING IN THREE BOXES: 1 TIMING — since when, how often, DAYTIME/NIGHT/BOTH, worse, first time · 2 DESCRIBE — HARD OR WATERY (overflow = liquid), BLOOD, LARGE OR SMALL (overflow = small), can he feel it, AND DOES HE WET · 3 BOWEL MOTIONS — usually diarrhoea or constipation, how often properly, HARD AND LUMPY OR RIBBON, BLOOD OR MUCUS, straining.** **Then diet → fruit and veg → WATER → exercise · refusal → leg-crossing → the painful motion · GI red flags · coeliac · thyroid · neuro · MECONIUM · growth · home, punishment, school, how he feels.**

**THE RED FLAGS THAT CHANGE THE CASE: WETTING WITH SOILING, back pain, leg weakness, gait change, sacral dimple or tuft → SPINAL CORD · RIBBON STOOLS, constipation FROM BIRTH, MECONIUM AFTER 48 h, distension → HIRSCHSPRUNG / anorectal malformation · BLOOD OR MUCUS, weight loss, night stools, mouth ulcers → IBD (blood alone is usually a fissure — but ASK) · poor growth, greasy stools → COELIAC; cold intolerance, dry skin → HYPOTHYROID · NEW soiling with FEAR, withdrawal, sexualised behaviour → ABUSE.** **Why coeliac in constipation: 'coeliac and IBD usually cause diarrhoea, but both CAN present with constipation, and coeliac causes poor growth.'**

**NAME IT CORRECTLY: say 'ENCOPRESIS' — not just 'constipation'. She came in about soiling and liquid stool; 'constipation' alone sounds like you MISSED THE POINT. Then '…WHICH IS CAUSED BY CONSTIPATION.' THE MECHANISM: 'hard stool has built up and GOT STUCK at the end of the bowel. BEHIND THAT BLOCKAGE, liquid stool builds up and LEAKS AROUND the hard lump — that's the runny stool in his pants. Because the bowel is STRETCHED, he GENUINELY CAN'T FEEL IT COMING, so he can't stop it. IT ISN'T NAUGHTINESS.'**

**THE REASONS — in her words: the soiling is RUNNY AND SMALL — the leak around a blockage · HARD MOTIONS every four or five days for years · it started after a PAINFUL, BLEEDING MOTION at seven, and he's HELD ON since — which makes the stool harder, THE CYCLE · a diet LOW IN FIBRE AND WATER · 'I COULD FEEL THE STOOL IN HIS TUMMY.' Then the exclusions: 'he doesn't wet, his legs and back are normal and he's growing well — so I'm not worried about a nerve or gland problem.'** **To 'I feel terrible': 'most parents feel that way until someone explains it.'**

**★ STEP 1 — EMPTY THE BOWEL (DISIMPACTION): oral MACROGOL 3350 with electrolytes (Movicol / OsmoLax) in ESCALATING DOSES over 3–7 DAYS until clear/watery stools; if oral fails or he won't take it, an ENEMA (e.g. Microlax) — 'medicine through the back passage that works in minutes.' WARN: 'the soiling may get WORSE for a few days — that's the old stool coming out, and it means it's working.'** VERIFY **STEP 2 — MAINTAIN: a smaller DAILY macrogol dose, titrated to ONE SOFT, EASY STOOL A DAY, FOR MONTHS; stimulant (senna/bisacodyl) only as a short-term adjunct. 'It ISN'T ABSORBED, ISN'T HABIT-FORMING and WON'T MAKE HIS BOWEL LAZY — STOPPING EARLY is the commonest reason this comes back.'** VERIFY

**STEP 3 — RETRAIN: sit on the toilet FIVE MINUTES after breakfast, after school and after dinner, with a FOOTSTOOL so the KNEES ARE ABOVE THE HIPS; a STAR CHART FOR SITTING, NOT FOR RESULTS · more fruit, veg, wholegrains (fibre ≈ age + 5 g), a WATER BOTTLE at school, COW'S MILK ≤ 500 mL (about two cups — he's on a litre), less junk, exercise daily · NO PUNISHMENT — 'he can't control it, and FEAR MAKES HIM HOLD ON' · a LETTER TO THE SCHOOL for toilet access, a change of clothes, and the teasing. STEP 4 — REVIEW at 2 weeks, then monthly; SLOW WEAN only after months of normal stools; relapse is common.** VERIFY **'Why laxatives for months?' — 'the rectum has been stretched and needs months to regain its size and sensation.'**

**AVOID: 'laxatives' without saying EMPTY FIRST · FIXING THE DIET ALONE ('diet won't shift a blockage that's already there') · stopping laxatives after two weeks because 'they'll make the bowel lazy' · ROUTINE DIGITAL RECTAL EXAMINATION or ABDOMINAL X-RAY (never order it to 'prove' constipation to a parent) · blaming the child or agreeing with punishment · REFERRING TO ED — this is managed in general practice.** **No investigations are routinely needed; if red flags: TSH, tTG-IgA + total IgA, FBC, calcium; spine MRI via paediatrics.** **Safety-net: blood, getting worse, WETTING STARTS, vomiting or distension, not better in two weeks.** SA: GP-managed · **CaFHS 1300 733 606** school-age continence clinics · **Continence helpline 1800 33 00 66** · RCH 'Constipation' and 'Soiling' Kids Health Info sheets · WCH paediatric gastroenterology for red flags or treatment failure · a Mental Health Treatment Plan for shame or school refusal · **CARL 13 14 78** if abuse.
plan: **WIPE, OPEN, AND GREET THE CHILD**: **'hello, I'm Dr ___, one of the doctors here. Jane? And this must be Liam — hi Liam. I'll just clean my hands. Jane, how can I help today?'** *'I'm at the end of my tether… washing clothes every day… he's ten.'*

**★ ACKNOWLEDGE — MASSIVELY — reframe as medical, and speak to Liam**: **'I can hear how exhausting that's been — every day, and not knowing why. Thank you for bringing him in. I'm going to ask quite a lot of questions to find the cause, and then we'll make a plan that actually fixes it — for him and for you. Liam, some of the questions might be a bit embarrassing; lots of kids have this, and it's fixable.'** **Never side with 'on purpose'.**

**BOX 1 — TIMING, including day or night**: **'how long has he been soiling? How often? Is it in the DAYTIME, at NIGHT, or both? Getting worse? Is this the first time?'** *Six months, daily, daytime, worse; a bit at five that settled.*

**★ BOX 2 — DESCRIBE IT, BLOOD, AND THE WETTING**: **'what does he soil with — hard lumps or watery stool? Any BLOOD? A lot, or small smears? Does he know it's happening? And does he also WET HIMSELF, day or night?'** *'Runny, like diarrhoea — small, stains his pants. No blood. He can't feel it. No wetting.'* → **'thank you — that's important.'**

**★ BOX 3 — BOWEL MOTIONS, blood asked again**: **'does he usually have diarrhoea or constipation? How often does he open his bowels properly? Hard and lumpy, or ever a RIBBON shape? Any BLOOD OR MUCUS in the stools? Does he strain?'** *'Constipated, always — every four or five days, hard as rocks, blocks the toilet.'* **The pivot from 'runny' to overflow.**

**DIET, WATER, EXERCISE — all three**: **'describe his diet. Fruit and vegetables? How much WATER — and milk, fizzy drinks? Any exercise?'** *Junk; barely any water; cordial and a litre of milk; iPad.*

**★ BEHAVIOUR AND THE TRIGGER**: **'does he refuse to go, or avoid the school toilets? Have you seen him CROSS HIS LEGS or wriggle to hold it in? Has he ever had a really PAINFUL OR FRIGHTENING bowel motion, or bleeding?'** *'At seven — he screamed, blood on the paper, and after that he wouldn't go.'* → **'that makes sense of a lot.'**

**THE DIFFERENTIALS — one or two questions each, all marked**: **'any tummy pain, nausea, vomiting, bloating? Stools pale and greasy? Coeliac or type 1 diabetes in the family? Does he feel the cold, dry skin, tired? Any trouble walking, BACK PAIN, numbness or weakness in the legs, a DIMPLE OR TUFT on his lower back? Any regular medicines — iron, pain relief?'** *No to all.*

**BINDS — THE MECONIUM QUESTION — and growth**: **'did he pass his FIRST BOWEL MOTION in the first day or two? Immunisations up to date? Growing and gaining weight?'** *Day one; yes; growing well.* **The Hirschsprung screen.**

**★ THE IMPACT — Liam first, then how she reacts**: **'Liam — how do you feel about all this?'** *'I hate it. They call me stinky.'* → **'that sounds really hard — and it's not your fault.'** **'Jane, how do you react when it happens? Have you punished him? Is he being teased? Anything or anyone worrying him?'** *Yelled, took the iPad; bullied.*

**SUMMARISE, THEN THE EXAMINATION — no rectal**: **'six months of daily daytime soiling with small amounts of runny stool, on years of hard motions every four or five days, started after a painful bleeding motion at seven, holding on since, little fibre or water, no wetting, growing well. I'd like his growth chart, his tummy, a look at his bottom WITHOUT any internal examination, his back and his legs, and his thyroid.'** *LIF mass; healed fissure; wink present; all else normal.*

**★ NAME IT — ENCOPRESIS — AND THE MECHANISM**: **'Liam has a condition called encopresis, and it's caused by constipation. Hard stool has got stuck at the end of his bowel. Behind that blockage, liquid stool builds up and leaks around it — that's the runny stool in his pants. Because the bowel is stretched, he genuinely can't feel it coming, so he can't stop it. It's not naughtiness.'** *'So he's not doing it on purpose. I feel terrible.'*

**THE REASONS, THEN THE EXCLUSIONS**: **runny and small = the leak · hard motions every four or five days · the painful motion at seven and holding on since — the cycle · low fibre and water · 'I could feel the stool in his tummy.' 'He doesn't wet, his back and legs are normal, and he's growing well — so I'm not worried about a nerve or gland problem.'**

**★ STEP 1 — EMPTY THE BOWEL, SAID FIRST**: **'because the cause is that blockage, the VERY FIRST STEP is to clear it out completely — a laxative powder called Movicol in bigger doses for a few days, and if that doesn't shift it, a small enema, medicine through the back passage that works in minutes. The soiling may get WORSE for a few days — that's the old stool coming out, and it means it's working.'**

**STEP 2 — MONTHS, NOT WEEKS; STEP 3 — RETRAIN**: **'once it's clear, a smaller daily dose for MONTHS, adjusted until one soft, easy poo a day — it isn't habit-forming and won't make his bowel lazy; we wean it slowly. Liam sits five minutes after breakfast, after school and after dinner, with a footstool so his knees are above his hips, and a star chart for sitting. More fruit and veg, a water bottle, milk down to two cups, running around daily. No punishment from now — fear makes him hold on. I'll write to the school.'**

**'How long before it stops?' — then review and safety-net**: **'the clear-out takes a few days; the soiling usually settles over the following weeks; the bowel takes months to shrink back. I'll see you in two weeks, then monthly. Come back sooner for blood, if it gets worse, if he starts wetting, or if he vomits or his tummy swells. Liam — this is going to get better.'**
pefe: **General appearance and hydration; vital signs; GROWTH CHART — well with normal growth argues against coeliac, hypothyroidism and IBD.**
**ABDOMEN: distension, visible masses; PALPATE for a mass — especially the LEFT ILIAC FOSSA and SUPRAPUBIC region (caecal loading may be right-sided); tenderness; bowel sounds.**
**PERIANAL INSPECTION ONLY — position of the anus, FISSURES (the trigger), skin tags, soiling, the ANAL WINK (sacral nerves intact). NO ROUTINE DIGITAL RECTAL EXAMINATION.**
**SPINE: sacral dimple, hair tuft, pigmentation, scoliosis. LOWER-LIMB NEUROLOGY: tone, power, reflexes, gait. THYROID: goitre and features of hypothyroidism.**
**BRISTOL STOOL CHART with the mother — types 1–2 = hard and lumpy; target types 3–4 daily; the soiling is types 5–7 leaking around the impaction.**

**NO investigations routinely required for typical functional constipation. ABDOMINAL X-RAY only if examination is unclear or the child is too large to palpate — never to 'prove' constipation to a parent.**
**STEP 1 — DISIMPACTION: macrogol 3350 with electrolytes, ESCALATING doses over 3–7 days until clear/watery stools; ENEMA if oral fails. Warn that soiling worsens for a few days.** VERIFY

**STEP 2 — MAINTENANCE: daily macrogol for MONTHS, titrated to one soft stool a day; stimulant only as a short-term adjunct. STEP 3 — RETRAIN: sit 5 min × 3/day after meals, footstool, star chart for sitting; fibre, water, cow's milk ≤ 500 mL, exercise; no punishment; school letter. STEP 4 — review 2 weeks, then monthly; slow wean.** VERIFY

**DO NOT MISS: spinal cord lesion (soiling WITH wetting) · Hirschsprung (meconium history) · coeliac and hypothyroidism presenting as constipation · ABUSE (new soiling with fear) · psychological harm — bullying, punishment, school refusal.**

dx: **BEHAVIOURAL FUSSY (PICKY) EATING — food refusal and selectivity in a WELL, NORMALLY-GROWING toddler — with DIET-RELATED APPETITE SUPPRESSION. Common from about 2 TO 9 YEARS; appetite falls after the first year as GROWTH VELOCITY SLOWS. A label reached ONLY AFTER GROWTH IS PROVEN NORMAL.**

**★ THE DISCRIMINATING ISSUE — YOU MUST PROVE GROWTH IS NORMAL BEFORE YOU USE THE WORD 'FUSSY', and show a COMPLETE DIET AND BEHAVIOUR ASSESSMENT before you counsel. THE LABEL IS THE LAST STEP, NOT THE FIRST. The examiner is listening for the WEIGHT QUESTION, the GROWTH-CHART QUESTION and the MILK / JUICE / SNACK QUESTIONS — then for advice that is PRIORITISED, SPECIFIC AND DOABLE.** **Most recall candidates who failed JUMPED FROM THE WORD 'FUSSY' STRAIGHT TO THE ADVICE.**

**THE FIVE GATES BEFORE THE LABEL — only a child who passes all five is a fussy eater: 1 GROWTH normal and tracking · 2 a full DIET history · 3 a full MEALTIME-BEHAVIOUR assessment · 4 the ORGANIC screen negative · 5 the PARENTS and home explored.** **The one-line strategy: describe the problem → diet in detail → mealtime behaviour → weight / growth / development → organic screen → parents and home → explain → to-do / to-avoid → red flags and review.**

**THE COMMUNICATION CHALLENGE: the mother wants VALIDATION ('he's fussy, isn't he?') and a FIX. You must neither dismiss her nor ACCEPT THE LABEL PREMATURELY — 'I understand; let me check a few things before we call it that' — then hand over a routine she can ACTUALLY RUN.** **Define the complaint first: 'does he REFUSE food altogether, or EAT LESS than you'd expect? All foods, or particular types? Since when?'**

**★ THE DIET — SIX QUESTIONS, and the marks are here: a TYPICAL DAY, breakfast to dinner and everything in between · VARIETY — fruit, vegetables, meat, eggs, bread, rice, pasta · COW'S MILK — HOW MANY CUPS OR BOTTLES · JUICE, cordial, soft drink, flavoured milk · SNACKS — what and how often · a BOTTLE, especially AT NIGHT.** **AUSTRALIAN BENCHMARKS: up to about 500 mL COW'S MILK a day (~1.5 dairy serves at 2–3 years) — more DISPLACES SOLIDS and causes IRON DEFICIENCY; JUICE has no place — water and milk only.** VERIFY

**MEALTIME BEHAVIOUR: how long a meal takes · how many meals and snacks · REGULAR times, FAMILY at the table · TANTRUMS, throwing, spitting, leaving the table · TV OR TABLET on · SEPARATE MEALS if he refuses · BRIBES or food rewards. THEN THE ORGANIC FOUR: STOOLS — loose, greasy, pale, smelly (COELIAC) · CHRONIC COUGH or recurrent infections (CYSTIC FIBROSIS) · BLUE or PUFFED on play or feeding (CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE) · PALE, LUMPS, BRUISING, fevers (LEUKAEMIA) · plus vomiting/reflux, constipation and snoring — enlarged tonsils and constipation both blunt appetite.**

**THE PARENTS — 'HE EATS WHAT HE'S GIVEN, so a little about you': your own diet and family mealtimes · YOUR MOOD · MONEY — IS THERE ALWAYS ENOUGH FOOD? · alcohol or drugs · who's at home. This is where NEGLECT, FOOD INSECURITY and PARENTAL MENTAL ILLNESS are found.**

**THE EXPLANATION — THREE REASONS AND ONE RULE: 'Sam is growing well, he's active and healthy, and nothing suggests a medical cause. This is picky eating — very common at his age, and NOTHING YOU'VE DONE WRONG. His APPETITE has dropped because GROWTH SLOWS AFTER THE FIRST YEAR; REFUSING FOOD GETS HIM ATTENTION; and a LITRE OF MILK plus juice and snacks FILL A SMALL STOMACH so there's no room for meals — about double what he needs, and it can make him LOW IN IRON. Children eat when they're hungry: YOUR JOB IS WHAT AND WHEN; HIS JOB IS HOW MUCH.'** **Never 'you're giving him too much junk'.**

**★ THE ADVICE — PRIORITISED, NOT A LIST: 'THREE THINGS TO START THIS WEEK. One: REGULAR MEALTIMES — THREE MEALS AND TWO SMALL SNACKS, nothing in between. Two: MILK DOWN TO ABOUT TWO CUPS A DAY, WATER INSTEAD OF JUICE, phase out the NIGHT BOTTLE. Three: at meals, SMALL PORTIONS, TWO OR THREE CHOICES, TV OFF, THIRTY MINUTES, then TAKE THE PLATE AWAY WITHOUT A FUSS.' Then the rest, WRITTEN DOWN: offer a new food AT LEAST TEN TIMES · eat with him · involve him in shopping and cooking · self-feeding, mess allowed · limit drinks 30 minutes before meals · NO bribes, NO punishment, NO SECOND DINNER, no force-feeding or long stand-offs, no grazing.** VERIFY

**SAFETY-NET AND FOLLOW-UP: 'the ONE THING THAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND IS HIS WEIGHT — if he stops gaining, or you see PALLOR, tiredness, LOOSE STOOLS or COUGH, come back sooner.' FBE AND FERRITIN given the milk intake and night bottle; REVIEW IN 4–6 WEEKS WITH THE BLUE BOOK; CaFHS for routines. No other investigations if growth is normal and the screen is negative.** **AVOID: appetite stimulants, supplements or 'toddler milk' as a fix · force-feeding, punishment, short-order meals · blaming the mother.** **VERSION B: 'I'd normally expect a fussy eater to keep growing well, but his chart shows he's crossed two centile lines. That changes my thinking — this is FALTERING GROWTH, and I need to look properly for a cause before we talk about behaviour' → FBE, ferritin, coeliac serology, UEC, LFT, urine; paediatric review.** SA: **CaFHS 1300 733 606** · WCH paediatric outpatients, dietetics and the Feeding Clinic · the **Blue Book** WHO charts · Parenting SA easy guides · **PATS** · Country Health Connect · ACCHS and **Closing the Gap PBS** · Foodbank SA / Centrelink social work if food insecurity · **CARL 13 14 78** for neglect · **TIS 131 450**.

I'm at my wit's end.'* → **'I can hear how frustrating that is. Let me ask what he eats and how mealtimes go, then some health questions, and we'll make a plan together.'**

**★ DON'T TAKE THE BAIT — DEFINE THE COMPLAINT**: **'when you say poor eating, does he REFUSE food, or EAT LESS than you'd expect? All foods, or some? Since when?'** *Refuses most; chips, sausages, biscuits, some cucumber; since about eighteen months.* **'Let me check a few things before we call it fussy.'**

**★ THE DIET — TYPICAL DAY FIRST**: **'walk me through a typical day's food.'** *Toast or cereal with milk; picks at lunch; chips and sausages for dinner.* **'Any fruit, vegetables, meat, eggs, bread, rice, pasta?'** *Basically none.*

**★ THE VOLUMES — where the cause lives**: **'does he drink cow's milk — HOW MANY CUPS OR BOTTLES a day? Any JUICE, cordial or soft drink?'** *'Four or five bottles — about a litre. Orange juice at breakfast and a popper at kindy.'* **'What does he SNACK on, and how often? Does he still have a BOTTLE AT NIGHT?'** *Biscuits, chips, muesli bars whenever he asks; bottle at bedtime and overnight.*

**Transition, then MEALTIME BEHAVIOUR**: **'that gives me a clear picture of what he eats — now how mealtimes actually go. How long do they take? Regular times? Does the family eat together? Is the TV on?'** *An hour of battle; no set times; alone in front of the TV.*

**Tantrums, separate meals, bribes**: **'any tantrums, throwing or spitting? Do you end up making a separate meal, or bribing him with food?'** *Throws food and screams; makes him chips; tried chocolate.*

**★ THE GROWTH GATE — THE MOST IMPORTANT QUESTION, before any label**: **'the most important question: has anyone been concerned about his WEIGHT GAIN? How is his growth on the chart in the Blue Book — weight, length and head size?'** *'The nurse said he's right on his line.'* **Version B: 'dropped two lines' → stop, ask to see the chart, switch to faltering growth.**
**DEVELOPMENT**: **'any concerns about his development — talking, running, playing with other children?'** *Talks in sentences, never stops running.*

**★ THE ORGANIC FOUR — out loud**: **'some questions about his general health, to make sure nothing else is putting him off his food. Any loose, greasy, pale or smelly stools? Any chronic cough or infections that keep coming back? Does he ever go BLUE or get puffed running, playing or eating? Any lumps, pale colour, bruising or fevers? Vomiting, constipation, snoring?'** *All negative; a bit constipated; snores a little.*

**THE PARENTS AND HOME**: **'he eats what he's given, so a little about you — what's your own diet like, and how's your mood? Any money worries — is there always enough food? Alcohol or drugs at home? Who lives with you?'** *Skips meals, exhausted; tight but there's food; stable.*
**★ THE HIDDEN AGENDA**: **'before I explain — what worries you most?'** *'That there's something wrong with him. And that I'm doing it wrong.'*

**EXPLAIN — ANSWER BOTH HALVES OF HER WORRY**: **'Sam is growing well, he's active and healthy, and nothing suggests a medical cause. This is picky eating — very common at his age, and nothing you've done wrong.'** Then **the three reasons — slowing growth, attention, and a litre of milk plus snacks filling a small stomach — and the rule: 'your job is what and when; his job is how much.'**

**★ THREE PRIORITISED ACTIONS, WITH NUMBERS**: **'three things to start this week. One: regular mealtimes — three meals and two small snacks, nothing in between. Two: milk down to about two cups a day, water instead of juice, and phase out the night bottle. Three: at meals, small portions, two or three choices, TV off, thirty minutes, then take the plate away without a fuss.'**

**THE REST, BRIEFLY — then her pushback**: **keep offering new foods — it can take ten tries · eat with him, let him help cook · no bribes, no punishments, no second dinner.** *'I've tried all that.'* → **'most parents have tried pieces of it — let's pick the two you can hold for four weeks, and I'll weigh him so you're not doing this alone.'**

**'Won't he be hungry?' — then the safety-net and review**: **'he will — and hunger is what brings him to the table. Because of the milk I'll check a blood count and iron today. The one thing that would change my mind is his WEIGHT — if he stops gaining, or you see pallor, tiredness, loose stools or cough, come back sooner. Otherwise I'll see you in four to six weeks with the Blue Book. CaFHS can help with routines. I'll write the plan down.'**
