ask: THE FRAMING SENTENCE: 'Confusion in hospital usually has more than one cause at the same time — so rather than picking one and stopping, we look for all of them and treat all of them.' AND THE ONE THAT EARNS THE DISCRIMINATOR: 'The most likely cause is alcohol withdrawal, and day three fits that exactly. But there are THREE I have to exclude actively today: A CLOT ON THE LUNG, because he is three days after a knee replacement with a pulse of 120; AN INFECTION, because his temperature is up; and A HEART PROBLEM. So I am treating the withdrawal AND investigating all of them at the same time.'

ON THE COMPLAINT: 'I hear you, and that's a fair question. Ideally someone drinking that much would have had a plan in place before he came in. I CAN'T TELL YOU WHAT WAS ASKED, BUT I WILL FIND OUT, and I'll come back to you about it.'

ON THE TREATMENT AND THE SON'S ROLE: 'We give him thiamine BEFORE any glucose, which matters more than it sounds.' · 'We score his withdrawal every few hours and give diazepam whenever the score goes above a certain level, RATHER THAN ON A FIXED TIMETABLE — that way he gets exactly as much as he needs.' · 'The aim is CALM AND ROUSABLE, NOT UNCONSCIOUS.' · 'HAVING YOU AT THE BEDSIDE IS ONE OF THE GENUINELY EFFECTIVE THINGS — familiar faces help more than people expect.'
pefe: THE FINDINGS ARE ALREADY IN THE STEM AND EACH ONE IS THERE FOR A REASON: PULSE 120 is the pulmonary embolism prompt · TEMPERATURE 37.8 is the infection prompt · NO ORGANOMEGALY AND NO ASCITES does NOT exclude cirrhosis, because a cirrhotic liver is often small and shrunken · CANNULA SITES CLEAN, BUT THE WOUND HAS NOT BEEN DESCRIBED, so examine it.

WHAT IS NOT IN THE STEM AND SHOULD BE IN YOUR ANSWER: oxygen saturation and respiratory rate before deciding on a CTPA · the thromboprophylaxis chart · a formal pain assessment · a bladder scan and bowel chart · asterixis · and the full medication chart, because post-operative opioids, anticholinergics and sedatives all cause this.

THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: pulmonary embolism never mentioned · treatment given with no investigation plan · glucose before thiamine · suggested giving the patient alcohol · discussed the patient without checking consent · promised the son his father would definitely be fine.

The bloods in two sentences, then get out of them — 'His liver tests show the enzymes are raised — a sign the liver has been under strain, most likely from long-term heavy drinking.' 'His blood count shows anaemia, a low haemoglobin, WITH THE RED CELLS THEMSELVES LARGER THAN THEY SHOULD BE — also typical of long-term alcohol use, because alcohol affects how the bone marrow makes blood cells.' THE PAIRING WORTH NAMING TO THE EXAMINER: A RAISED GGT WITH A RAISED MCV IS THE CLASSIC BIOCHEMICAL SIGNATURE OF SUSTAINED HEAVY USE. Then bridge: 'what those two results tell me is that the alcohol has already been affecting his body in more than one way'

Open the differential the right way — before you name anything — 'Before I tell you what I think is most likely, I want to say something about confusion in hospital generally. IT USUALLY HAS MORE THAN ONE CAUSE AT THE SAME TIME — so rather than picking one and stopping, WE LOOK FOR ALL OF THEM AND TREAT ALL OF THEM.' That single framing is what separates a pass from a fluent fail, and it buys you permission to list emergencies without frightening him

Pulmonary embolism is the one that fails people — DAY 3 AFTER A TOTAL KNEE REPLACEMENT IS THE SINGLE HIGHEST-RISK PERIOD FOR VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM, AND CONFUSION WITH A PULSE OF 120 IS A PRESENTATION. A candidate who gives a flawless account of alcohol withdrawal and NEVER SAYS THE WORDS 'PULMONARY EMBOLISM' is very unlikely to pass. Check oxygen saturation and respiratory rate, review the thromboprophylaxis chart, and CTPA if suspected — a NEGATIVE LEG DOPPLER DOES NOT EXCLUDE IT, because the question here is the lung

The rest of the list, each with an action — INFECTION — temperature 37.8, cannula sites clean BUT THE WOUND HAS NOT BEEN DESCRIBED: examine it, urine MCS, chest X-ray, blood cultures. MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION — post-operative and tachycardic, CAN BE SILENT with analgesia on board: ECG and troponin. WERNICKE ENCEPHALOPATHY — thiamine deficiency is near-certain and THE CLASSIC TRIAD IS OFTEN INCOMPLETE, so treat on suspicion with parenteral thiamine. UNCONTROLLED PAIN — a knee replacement is very painful and PAIN ALONE CAUSES DELIRIUM, routinely under-treated in someone who cannot communicate. HEPATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY — A CIRRHOTIC LIVER IS OFTEN SMALL AND SHRUNKEN, so a normal examination does not exclude it. DRUGS · ELECTROLYTES AND GLUCOSE · INTRACRANIAL, including SUBDURAL in a drinker with atrophy and falls · URINARY RETENTION AND CONSTIPATION · SENSORY DEPRIVATION · AND FAT EMBOLISM, uncommon but specific to long-bone and joint surgery within 72 hours

The four steps, and the order is the point — STEP ONE, INVESTIGATE — this is the step that gets skipped because step two is the part candidates know: bloods including troponin, coagulation, magnesium, phosphate and a venous gas with ketones · ECG · chest X-ray · cultures and urine · CTPA if suspected · CT brain for any focal sign, any fall, or no improvement · BLADDER SCAN AND BOWEL CHART · full medication review with the pharmacist and a FORMAL PAIN ASSESSMENT. STEP TWO, TREAT THE WITHDRAWAL: THIAMINE PARENTERALLY AND BEFORE ANY GLUCOSE, because GIVING GLUCOSE TO A THIAMINE-DEFICIENT PATIENT CAN PRECIPITATE WERNICKE · CIWA-Ar SCORING repeated regularly · SYMPTOM-TRIGGERED DIAZEPAM WHEN THE SCORE CROSSES A THRESHOLD, not on a fixed schedule, with caution and a shorter-acting agent in significant liver impairment · CORRECT MAGNESIUM, because low magnesium makes withdrawal harder to control and lowers the seizure threshold VERIFY. STEP THREE, TREAT EVERYTHING ELSE FOUND. STEP FOUR, SUPPORTIVE DELIRIUM CARE

Supportive care, and giving the son a job — QUIET, WELL-LIT SINGLE ROOM with fewer moves between beds · REPEATED REORIENTATION with a clock, a calendar and staff introducing themselves · GLASSES AND HEARING AIDS RESTORED · PROTECT THE SLEEP–WAKE CYCLE, avoiding overnight observations where safe · EARLY MOBILISATION with physiotherapy · REMOVE UNNECESSARY LINES AND CATHETERS · AND FAMILY AT THE BEDSIDE, WHICH IS AN INTERVENTION AND NOT JUST A RELATIVE. 'The third thing is where you come in, actually' — this is the moment the son stops feeling helpless, and it is a marked item

Single-cause thinking — the diagnosis presented as certain, with no framing that delirium is usually multifactorial
Three or four minutes spent explaining ALT, AST and MCV, so the management task is never reached
Fixed-schedule benzodiazepine with no withdrawal score, an antipsychotic as first-line, restraint offered casually, or no consent asked before discussing the patient with his son

setting: Telling him the truth about the timeframe — that six weeks is far too early — while making it absolutely clear that stopping was the right thing and is still working. Two responses fail and they pull in opposite directions: the false promise sets him up for a second disappointment in three months, and the blunt truth delivered alone is accurate and potentially catastrophic — a man six weeks sober who concludes there was no point is a man at real risk of relapse.
stem: General practice. A 57-year-old man has come complaining of tingling and numbness in both feet, worse at night. He has been drinking five standard drinks every night for the last five years.
He stopped drinking six weeks ago, but the symptoms are continuing, and he is upset — he was told that if he stopped, the symptoms would go away. 8 minutes.

Examination: decreased sensation in both legs, reduced reflexes bilaterally. Investigations: full blood count shows a microcytic anaemia · blood sugar normal · vitamin B12 normal · liver enzymes raised.
Three explaining tasks and no history task. That is a lot of explaining, so the results must be delivered briskly.
tasks: Explain the physical examination findings and the investigation results to the patient
Explain your diagnosis and your differentials
Explain your immediate and your long-term management
time: Ninety seconds on the bloods, not three minutes — there are three explaining tasks to fit into eight minutes · signpost the management split out loud, because the task asked for two categories and an undifferentiated list tells the examiner you did not hear it
findingsLabel: Examination findings — open only when you would ask the examiner
findings: The examination findings, in plain words

'The feeling in both your legs is reduced compared to what I'd expect — that matches the numbness you've been describing. And YOUR REFLEXES, THE KNEE AND ANKLE JERKS, are weaker than normal on both sides.' THEN WHAT IT MEANS: 'together those tell me the problem is IN THE NERVES THEMSELVES. It's BOTH SIDES EQUALLY, AND IT STARTS AT THE FEET, which is the typical pattern when something affecting the whole body damages nerves — THE NERVES GOING TO YOUR FEET ARE THE LONGEST AND THEY GIVE OUT FIRST.' Never 'your reflexes are diminished bilaterally'

back.dx: ALCOHOL-RELATED PERIPHERAL SENSORY NEUROPATHY, PLUS AN UNEXPLAINED MICROCYTIC ANAEMIA THAT MUST BE WORKED UP SEPARATELY. IMMEDIATE MANAGEMENT: THIAMINE — oral here, and in any unwell or admitted patient BEFORE GLUCOSE, since he is a chronic drinker with likely poor nutrition · IRON STUDIES, and act on the anaemia · TSH AND UEC, the two untested differentials · FOOT EXAMINATION AND FOOT CARE ADVICE, because HE HAS REDUCED SENSATION AND WILL NOT FEEL AN INJURY · FALLS AND DRIVING RISK ASSESSED, given reduced proprioception and reflexes. NEUROPATHIC PAIN, IF IT IS TROUBLING HIM: a LOW-DOSE TRICYCLIC is commonly first-line, or GABAPENTIN OR PREGABALIN as an alternative; BOTH NEED SLOW TITRATION and both have significant adverse effects in older patients and in liver disease; DO NOT REACH FOR OPIOIDS, and ordinary analgesics do not help much with nerve pain VERIFY. LONG-TERM: CONTINUED ABSTINENCE, the single most important intervention, and he has already done the hardest part · NUTRITION, with a dietitian, thiamine and B-group replacement, and the anaemia addressed · FOLATE AND HbA1c · RELAPSE PREVENTION through an alcohol and drug service, counselling, and consideration of pharmacotherapy · LIVER FOLLOW-UP with repeat liver function, assessment for cirrhosis, and surveillance if cirrhosis is present · REGULAR REVIEW OF THE NEUROPATHY WITH REALISTIC TIMEFRAMES · PHYSIOTHERAPY AND OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY if balance is affected. CORRECTION — THE GUIDELINES GAP, AND HOW TO ANSWER FOR IT: Therapeutic Guidelines DOES NOT DISCUSS ALCOHOL-RELATED SENSORY NEUROPATHY AS A SEPARATE CONDITION, and most references treat all sensory neuropathies alike. That absence confuses candidates, who assume they have missed something. THEY HAVE NOT. The safe OSCE position is TREAT THE CAUSE — abstinence and nutrition — REPLACE THIAMINE, AND MANAGE NEUROPATHIC PAIN USING THE STANDARD APPROACH. If challenged → 'Australian guidance doesn't address alcohol-related neuropathy as a separate entity — it's covered under NEUROPATHIC PAIN GENERALLY, where the first-line options are a low-dose tricyclic or gabapentin. I'd treat the underlying cause, replace thiamine, and use that framework for the pain, and I'd confirm the doses against current Therapeutic Guidelines.' THE MOMENT THAT DECIDES THE CONSULTATION'S CREDIBILITY: when you raise gastrointestinal blood loss HE GETS THERE BEFORE YOU DO — 'CANCER, YOU MEAN.' DO NOT RETREAT. Confirm it plainly, put it in proportion, and move on: 'That's one of the possibilities, yes, and I'd rather tell you that plainly than have you find out from a referral letter. IT'S NOT THE ONLY POSSIBILITY, AND IT'S NOT THE MOST LIKELY ONE. BUT IT'S THE ONE WE CHECK FOR FIRST.' Candidates who backpedal here lose the trust they have just spent five minutes building. HIS HIDDEN AGENDA: HE IS QUIETLY WONDERING WHETHER THERE WAS ANY POINT STOPPING, AND HE HAS BEEN THINKING ABOUT HAVING A BEER. He says 'I'll be honest, I've been wondering why I bothered' ONLY if you ask directly what he is thinking or explicitly acknowledge how hard six weeks has been — AND IF YOU NEVER DO, HE LEAVES WITHOUT SAYING IT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE STATION. He pushes for a straight answer on recovery at least twice: if you promise he will be fine he says 'THAT'S WHAT THE LAST ONE SAID' and goes cold; if you say it may be permanent and stop there he goes silent and then says 'SO I STOPPED FOR NOTHING.' THE SENTENCE TO CLOSE ON: 'YOU HAVE DONE THE HARD PART, AND YOU DID IT WITHOUT SEEING ANY REWARD FOR IT YET. I want you to know that THE REWARD IS REAL, IT'S JUST SLOWER THAN ANYONE TOLD YOU.' SOUTH AUSTRALIAN SERVICES TO NAME: DASSA ADIS 1300 13 1340, 8.30 am to 10 pm daily, counselling, information and referral FOR HIM AND FOR HIS FAMILY · COUNTRY HEALTH CONNECT for rural allied health and community nursing · PATS if he needs to travel to Adelaide for endoscopy or specialist review · QUITLINE 13 7848, since he smokes fifteen a day and it very commonly co-occurs · TIS National 131 450 · the ACCHS and Closing the Gap PBS arrangements for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients · AND DRIVING: if sensation and proprioception are significantly impaired, fitness to drive must be considered under AUSTROADS ASSESSING FITNESS TO DRIVE, with the SA NOTIFICATION DUTY UNDER THE MOTOR VEHICLES ACT 1959 VERIFY.
plan: OPEN BEFORE THE RESULTS: 'I've got your results here — but before I go through them, TELL ME HOW YOU'VE BEEN.' He is flat, irritated, arms folded.

NAME THE DISAPPOINTMENT FIRST: 'that's a really fair thing to be frustrated about, and I THINK YOU WERE GIVEN A TIMEFRAME THAT WASN'T RIGHT, AND THAT ISN'T YOUR FAULT. Can I take you through the results, and then we'll deal with that?'
EXAMINATION FINDINGS IN PLAIN WORDS, and what the glove-and-stocking pattern means — longest nerves fail first.
Liver enzymes, one sentence. Then the normals and what they exclude — diabetes and B12.
THE MICROCYTIC ANAEMIA NAMED AS UNEXPECTED: with heavy drinking you would expect the cells to be LARGER. Small cells mean low iron.
WHAT THAT OBLIGES YOU TO DO: iron studies today, and arrange endoscopy. HE WILL SAY 'CANCER, YOU MEAN' — confirm plainly, proportion it, move on.
THE DIAGNOSIS WITH THREE REASONS, and the two differentials not yet excluded: thyroid and kidneys.
SIGNPOST THE SPLIT: 'let me split it into now and longer term.'
IMMEDIATE: thiamine · iron studies · TSH and UEC · foot examination and foot care advice · neuropathic pain medication started this week, with care given the liver.
LONG-TERM: abstinence as the single biggest factor · dietitian and nutrition · liver follow-up · regular review to track the feet.
'BUT WILL THEY GET BETTER?' — THE TWO HALVES, IN ONE BREATH. Honest timeframe, no guarantee, and the validation that stops a relapse.
VALIDATE THE SIX WEEKS EXPLICITLY · DASSA 1300 13 1340 for him and his family · written information · teach-back: 'what will you tell your wife tonight?'

ask: THE OPENING THAT BUYS THE ROOM: 'Before I go through them, tell me how you've been.' … 'That's a really fair thing to be frustrated about, and I think you were given a timeframe that wasn't right, and that isn't your fault.'

THE ANAEMIA: 'There's one result I want to be straight with you about BECAUSE IT DOESN'T FIT. With heavy drinking I'd expect the red cells to be LARGER. Small cells usually mean you're low in iron — and in a man of your age, that usually means you're losing a small amount of blood somewhere.' THEN, WHEN HE SAYS 'CANCER, YOU MEAN': 'That's one of the possibilities, yes, and I'd rather tell you that plainly than have you find out from a referral letter.'

THE CLOSE: 'You have done the hard part, and you did it without seeing any reward for it yet. The reward is real, it's just slower than you were told.' AND THE OFFER: 'Is there any support around the drinking I can help with — there's a service called DASSA, 1300 13 1340, that's free, for you or your family.'
pefe: THE EXAMINATION IS GIVEN TO YOU AND THE TASK IS TO EXPLAIN IT: DECREASED SENSATION IN BOTH LEGS AND REDUCED REFLEXES BILATERALLY — a symmetrical, length-dependent SENSORY NEUROPATHY in a glove-and-stocking distribution. What you add is the FOOT EXAMINATION you do today, because reduced sensation means he will not notice a cut or a blister, and an assessment of BALANCE, FALLS AND DRIVING.

THE RESULTS, AND WHAT EACH ONE BUYS YOU: LIVER ENZYMES RAISED — the alcohol has affected him elsewhere, and it is one of your three reasons for the diagnosis · BSL NORMAL — excludes diabetes, the commonest cause overall, though consider HbA1c to exclude it properly · B12 NORMAL — excludes the other common cause, though folate has not been checked · MICROCYTIC ANAEMIA — the one that does not fit, and the one that obliges you to act.

THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: attributed the microcytic anaemia to alcohol and did nothing · promised the symptoms would fully resolve · told him the damage was permanent without validating the abstinence · omitted thiamine · never addressed his expectation at all.

Correction — the anaemia is the wrong shape, and this is the highest-yield point — The source presents microcytic anaemia as an expected consequence of chronic alcohol use. IT IS NOT. ALCOHOL CAUSES A MACROCYTOSIS — direct marrow toxicity, often with folate deficiency alongside, thrombocytopenia common, and A RAISED MCV WITH A RAISED GGT IS THE RECOGNISED PAIRING. SMALL RED CELLS MEAN IRON DEFICIENCY UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE, AND IN A 57-YEAR-OLD MAN IRON DEFICIENCY MEANS GASTROINTESTINAL BLOOD LOSS UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE: oesophageal varices or portal hypertensive gastropathy, since he has liver disease · alcoholic gastritis or peptic ulcer · COLORECTAL CARCINOMA, right age and right sex · coeliac disease or poor intake. THIS OBLIGES YOU TO ACT — iron studies, and consideration of upper and lower endoscopy VERIFY

The diagnosis named with three reasons, and what is still outstanding — 'ALCOHOL-RELATED PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY, and I'm saying that for three reasons. THE PATTERN IS EXACTLY RIGHT — both sides equally, starting at the feet, worse at night. THE AMOUNT AND DURATION FIT. AND YOUR LIVER TESTS SHOW THE ALCOHOL HAS AFFECTED YOU ELSEWHERE AS WELL.' EXCLUDED ALREADY: diabetes by the BSL, B12 by the level. NOT YET EXCLUDED AND YOU SHOULD SAY SO: TSH AND UEC — ORDER THEM — plus folate and HbA1c. ALSO ON THE LIST: drugs and toxins (chemotherapy, isoniazid, metronidazole, amiodarone, phenytoin, heavy metals) · vasculitis, which would be ASYMMETRICAL OR PATCHY · sarcoidosis, paraproteinaemia and malignancy if the picture does not settle

The pass — both HALVEs, in one breath — 'I want to be honest with you about two things, and THEY SIT TOGETHER. THE FIRST is that SIX WEEKS IS GENUINELY TOO EARLY. Nerves recover very slowly — MONTHS, NOT WEEKS — because THE NERVE HAS TO REGROW ALONG ITS WHOLE LENGTH, from your spine to your feet. So the fact that it hasn't improved yet DOESN'T MEAN IT WON'T.' 'THE SECOND is that I CAN'T PROMISE YOU FULL RECOVERY, AND I'M NOT GOING TO. Some of it may be permanent. But what I can tell you with complete confidence is that STOPPING DRINKING IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT THING DETERMINING HOW MUCH OF IT COMES BACK — AND YOU HAVE ALREADY DONE THAT. IF YOU HAD KEPT DRINKING, THIS WOULD BE GETTING WORSE. IT ISN'T.'

Read the card — both versions circulate — If the examiner's card in your sitting says MACROCYTIC rather than microcytic, the explanation becomes straightforward: marrow toxicity and folate deficiency, CHECK FOLATE. THE WHOLE OF THE ANAEMIA SECTION TURNS ON WHICH ONE YOU ARE GIVEN. Examiner challenge 'isn't the anaemia just the alcohol?' → 'Alcohol typically causes a MACROCYTIC anaemia, not a microcytic one. A microcytic picture points to iron deficiency, and in a 57-year-old man that means I HAVE TO LOOK FOR GASTROINTESTINAL BLOOD LOSS — he has liver disease, so varices and gastritis are on the list, BUT SO IS BOWEL CANCER'

Name the normal results — an easy mark most candidates skip — 'Two things came back normal, and that's useful. YOUR BLOOD SUGAR IS NORMAL, SO THIS ISN'T DIABETES. And YOUR VITAMIN B12 IS NORMAL, SO THIS ISN'T A B12 DEFICIENCY — BOTH OF THOSE ARE COMMON CAUSES OF EXACTLY THESE SYMPTOMS.' Saying what a normal result excludes is worth a mark and takes one sentence. Liver enzymes get one sentence too: the liver has been under strain from the alcohol over the years
fails: ★ Dismisses the microcytic anaemia as the alcohol — it is the wrong shape, and an unexplained iron deficiency in a man of 57 needs iron studies and endoscopy
★ Answers the recovery question with only one half — a false promise that sets up a second disappointment, or a bleak truth that leaves a six-week-sober man concluding he stopped for nothing
Three minutes on the blood count, so two of the three explaining tasks are rushed or lost
Thiamine omitted, or TSH and UEC never ordered — the two differentials that have not yet been excluded and that you should say out loud are outstanding
Management not split into immediate and long-term when the task asked for both, no foot care or falls advice despite reduced sensation, and no abstinence support offered by name and number
numbers: Five standard drinks nightly for five years · six weeks abstinent, which is far too early to judge — nerve recovery is months, not weeks, because the axon must regrow its whole length · alcohol causes a macrocytic picture, often with low platelets · microcytic means iron deficiency, which in a man of 57 means GI blood loss · excluded here: diabetes by BSL, B12 by level · not yet excluded: TSH, UEC, folate, HbA1c VERIFY

Neuropathic pain: low-dose tricyclic or gabapentin, slow titration, caution in liver disease and in older patients, never opioids VERIFY · services: DASSA ADIS 1300 13 1340, 8.30 am–10 pm daily, for him and his family · Quitline 13 7848 · country health connect · PATS for endoscopy travel · TIS National 131 450 · driving assessed under Austroads with the SA notification duty, motor vehicles act 1959

setting: Treat immune thrombocytopenia as a diagnosis of exclusion — in both versions. In version 1 that means asking the malignancy and meningococcal questions, requesting the full node and spleen examination, and saying out loud that you have excluded them. In version 2 it means changing your mind when the card changes — candidates who have already decided walk past two enlarged cervical nodes and diagnose ITP anyway, which is premature closure and is the behaviour the second version exists to expose.
stem: General practice. A 20-year-old woman has come complaining of a rash on her legs. A photograph in the stem shows a non-blanching purpuric rash over both shins. 8 minutes.

Version 1 — the old recall. History: a flu-like illness last week, nothing else positive. Examination: everything normal, no fever, no lymphadenopathy, no splenomegaly. Diagnosis: immune thrombocytopenia, reached by exclusion.

Version 2 — the newer recall. Identical stem, identical history, identical examination request — but the card reports two large firm nodes in the cervical chain. Diagnosis: leukaemia or lymphoma until proven otherwise.
No investigation task and no management task — which does not stop you naming the full blood count and film, because they are part of the exclusion.

The picture is a STILL. It does not tell you whether it was weeping last night, whether it is spreading, or the three questions you must ask regardless: IS IT WARM? IS IT PAINFUL? IS IT ITCHY? A candidate who skips the rash history because there is a photograph HAS NOT TAKEN A HISTORY. And get the observations first: 'BEFORE I START — COULD I HAVE HER OBSERVATIONS, PARTICULARLY HER TEMPERATURE?' FEVER PLUS PURPURA IS MENINGOCOCCAEMIA UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE
The three findings that decide it

LYMPH NODES — everywhere, not just the neck — for MARROW INFILTRATION BY LEUKAEMIA. SPLEEN. TEMPERATURE. ITP IS A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION, AND THESE THREE ARE WHAT YOU ARE EXCLUDING. WET PURPURA — petechiae on the palate or buccal mucosa — means MUCOSAL BLEEDING AND A HIGHER BLEEDING RISK, so it fits ITP and it also tells you the risk is not trivial
Correction — you cannot diagnose ITP without a blood count

The source goes straight from a normal examination to a diagnosis. Clinically, IMMUNE THROMBOCYTOPENIA IS DEFINED BY AN ISOLATED LOW PLATELET COUNT with an otherwise normal full blood count and film — HISTORY AND EXAMINATION ALONE CANNOT MAKE IT. THE SENTENCE: 'my working diagnosis is immune thrombocytopenia, BUT I WOULD WANT A FULL BLOOD COUNT AND A BLOOD FILM to confirm an isolated low platelet count before I settled on it — THE FILM IS ALSO WHAT WOULD SHOW ME A LEUKAEMIA.' Examiner challenge 'the task was diagnosis, not investigations' → 'Understood. I'm naming it because ITP is a diagnosis of exclusion AND THE BLOOD FILM IS PART OF THE EXCLUSION — I didn't want to state it more confidently than the information allows'

back.dx: VERSION 1: IMMUNE THROMBOCYTOPENIA · VERSION 2: LEUKAEMIA OR LYMPHOMA UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE. THE STATION IS ONE OF THE CLEAREST EXAMPLES OF THE AMC CHANGING A SINGLE EXAMINATION FINDING AND CHANGING THE WHOLE ANSWER — designed to catch people who have MEMORISED THE RECALL RATHER THAN LEARNED THE REASONING. THE FULL DIFFERENTIAL, WITH WHAT SUPPORTS EACH AND HOW TO EXCLUDE IT: IMMUNE THROMBOCYTOPENIA — young woman, recent viral illness, FLAT purpura on both shins, otherwise well; wet purpura in the mouth; no nodes, no spleen; confirmed by FBC showing ISOLATED thrombocytopenia with a normal film · LEUKAEMIA OR LYMPHOMA, NOT TO MISS — lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, pallor, weight loss, night sweats, recurrent infection, bone pain; FBC and FILM, LDH, marrow examination if indicated; URGENT · MENINGOCOCCAEMIA, NOT TO MISS — FEVER, unwell, headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, a RAPIDLY SPREADING rash, tachycardia, hypotension, altered consciousness; clinical diagnosis, blood cultures and IMMEDIATE ANTIBIOTICS, DO NOT WAIT; EMERGENCY · IgA VASCULITIS (HENOCH–SCHÖNLEIN PURPURA) — PALPABLE purpura on legs AND BUTTOCKS, joint pain, abdominal pain, recent URTI; urinalysis for blood and protein, renal function; clinical diagnosis · DRUG-INDUCED — a new medicine or antibiotic in the last few weeks; medication history, stop the drug, FBC · HAEMOLYTIC URAEMIC SYNDROME AND TTP — recent diarrhoea, especially bloody, confusion, reduced urine output, fever, pallor, jaundice, oliguria, neurological signs; FBC and film for FRAGMENTS, UEC, LDH, bilirubin; EMERGENCY · INHERITED BLEEDING DISORDER — lifelong easy bruising, bleeding after dental work, family history, joint or muscle bleeds; coagulation profile and von Willebrand studies · CHRONIC LIVER DISEASE — alcohol, jaundice, pale stools, dark urine, stigmata, splenomegaly; LFTs, coagulation, FBC · VIRAL EXANTHEM — systemically well, other viral features. NOMENCLATURE, WORTH KNOWING BUT NOT WORTH ARGUING ABOUT: ITP NOW STANDS FOR IMMUNE THROMBOCYTOPENIA rather than idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, and HENOCH–SCHÖNLEIN PURPURA IS NOW CALLED IgA VASCULITIS — say the current name, and if the examiner uses the old one, use theirs VERIFY. EXPLAINING VERSION 1 TO HER: NAME IT — 'a condition called immune thrombocytopenia, or ITP'. EXPLAIN IT IN TWO SENTENCES — 'your immune system gets triggered, usually by a viral infection like the one you had last week, and it gets a little confused and STARTS ATTACKING THE CLOTTING CELLS IN YOUR BLOOD, called platelets. With fewer of them, small amounts of blood leak under the skin, which is the rash you can see.' THEN GIVE THREE REASONS, WHICH IS SCORED — the TYPE of rash is bleeding under the skin rather than an inflammatory rash · the SITE fits, both legs · and the VIRAL ILLNESS last week is the usual trigger. THEN the blood count caveat. EXPLAINING VERSION 2: SIGNPOST BEFORE YOU FRIGHTEN HER — 'I've found something on examination that I need to be straight with you about, and IT CHANGES WHAT I'M THINKING.' THEN NAME THE CONCERN SENSITIVELY — 'I've found two enlarged glands in your neck. Together with this rash, I'm concerned about the possibility of A CANCER OF THE BLOOD OR THE LYMPH GLANDS — leukaemia or lymphoma. I want to be honest that I DON'T KNOW YET which, or even whether it is that at all.' GIVE THE TWO REASONS, then the rest of the list: 'ITP is still one of them — BUT I CAN'T CALL IT THAT UNTIL I'VE RULED THE SERIOUS THINGS OUT, and the first step is an urgent blood test today.' THEN RUN THE BREAKING-BAD-NEWS SEQUENCE — warning shot, silence, empathy — BECAUSE THIS HAS BECOME A BAD-NEWS STATION WITHOUT THE STEM TELLING YOU SO. HER HIDDEN AGENDA: SHE IS A NURSING STUDENT WHO LOOKED IT UP LAST NIGHT AND HAS READ ABOUT LEUKAEMIA. She is terrified and will not say so unless asked an open question about her concerns — and if nobody asks, she brings it out at about six minutes: 'IS IT LEUKAEMIA? I LOOKED IT UP.' If you tell her it is definitely ITP with no mention of a blood test, she asks 'BUT HOW DO YOU KNOW? WITHOUT A TEST?'

THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: no malignancy questions · no lymph node examination requested · no temperature · diagnosed ITP without excluding anything · and in version 2, diagnosed ITP despite two enlarged cervical nodes.

Describing it properly — and the distinction the source omits — PURPURA IS BLEEDING INTO THE SKIN and DOES NOT BLANCH, because the blood is OUTSIDE the vessels. One family, three sizes: PETECHIAE UNDER 2 mm · PURPURA 2 mm TO 1 cm, the umbrella term · ECCHYMOSES OVER 1 cm. ADDED AND WORTH A MARK: FLAT (MACULAR) PURPURA → THINK A PLATELET PROBLEM — immune thrombocytopenia, marrow failure, drugs. PALPABLE PURPURA, standing proud of the skin → THINK A VASCULITIS — IgA vasculitis and other small-vessel disease. Ask the examiner both: 'can I confirm the rash is non-blanching?' and 'is it flat, or is it palpable?'

The history blocks, and the order is the point — MALIGNANCY FIRST — weight loss, appetite, LUMPS AND BUMPS ANYWHERE, tiredness, NIGHT SWEATS, bone pain, recurrent infections. THEN SEPSIS AND MENINGITIS — fever or chills, drowsy, headache, stiff neck, photophobia. THEN IgA VASCULITIS — joint pains, abdominal pain, blood in the urine. THEN THE TRIGGER: 'any recent flu-like illness?' AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER IT, 'DID YOU TAKE ANY ANTIBIOTICS OR NEW MEDICINES FOR IT?', which catches drug-induced thrombocytopenia. THEN BLEEDING ELSEWHERE — nosebleeds, GUMS, heavy periods, blood in stool or urine, AND HEADACHE OR DIZZINESS, because intracranial haemorrhage is rare but is why ITP is taken seriously. THEN inherited bleeding disorder, then diarrhoea and liver questions

The examination request — ask in this order and nothing gets dropped — General appearance — cachexia, scratch marks, level of consciousness, pallor · vital signs, especially temperature · the rash — non-blanching, flat or palpable, tender · a full lymph node survey: cervical, supraclavicular, axillary, inguinal, asked for early and by name · mouth and throat, specifically petechiae on the buccal or palatal mucosa · neck stiffness · cardiovascular · respiratory · abdomen for hepatosplenomegaly · a full joint examination · urine dipstick for blood. Omitting the node survey is the single commonest reason this station is failed

back.dx: URTICARIA OR SCABIES — THE ANSWER IS IN THE SITE AND THE HOUSEHOLD. WHEN A STATION GIVES YOU ALMOST NOTHING, THE EXAMINER IS NOT TESTING RECALL; they are testing whether you can CHARACTERISE A COMPLAINT SYSTEMATICALLY AND WORK THROUGH DIFFERENTIALS IN AN ORDER when the answer is not handed to you. THE FULL HISTORY BLOCKS: CHARACTERISE, as above · THE TRIGGER — what were you doing immediately before it started, any new foods, medicines, soaps, detergents, plants, insect bites, and DOES EXERCISE OR STRESS BRING IT ON, which is the cholinergic urticaria question · INFECTION — fever, chills, runny nose, sore throat, cough, AND THE EBV TRAP, a sore throat treated with amoxicillin followed by a rash, a storyline the AMC uses repeatedly · GASTROINTESTINAL — nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, for enteroviral exanthem and food-related urticaria · MENINGOCOCCAEMIA · TRAVEL AND ACCOMMODATION, including animal contact · SEXUAL HEALTH, because HIV SEROCONVERSION AND SECONDARY SYPHILIS both present with rash and SCABIES IS ALSO SEXUALLY TRANSMISSIBLE · THE HOUSEHOLD · AUTOIMMUNE — diarrhoea and greasy or bloody stools, mouth ulcers, eye problems, joint pain, scaly patches on elbows or scalp, photosensitive rash, hair loss, for coeliac disease, inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis and lupus · BLEEDING AND MALIGNANCY — easy bruising, family bleeding history, weight loss, night sweats, lumps, because HAEMATOLOGICAL DISEASE CAN PRESENT WITH ALMOST ANY RASH and belongs at the end of every rash list · BACKGROUND — past history, ATOPY, medications, allergies, IMMUNISATIONS, family history. IMMUNISATION HISTORY IS WORTH ASKING EVEN IN AN ADULT: it is cheap, it is on several mark sheets, and almost nobody asks it once the patient is over eighteen. URTICARIA MANAGEMENT: identify and avoid the trigger where one is found · AVOID HEAT, hot showers and overheating, with cool compresses · NON-SEDATING ORAL ANTIHISTAMINE, REGULARLY RATHER THAN AS NEEDED, with doses above standard used in persistent urticaria under specialist guidance · AVOID ASPIRIN AND NSAIDs, WHICH CAN AGGRAVATE IT · REFER if it persists beyond SIX WEEKS (chronic urticaria) or if there is angio-oedema VERIFY. SCABIES MANAGEMENT: TOPICAL PERMETHRIN 5% CREAM, whole body FROM THE NECK DOWN, LEFT ON OVERNIGHT, REPEATED AFTER ONE WEEK · TREAT EVERY HOUSEHOLD MEMBER AND CLOSE CONTACT ON THE SAME DAY, SYMPTOMATIC OR NOT — treating the patient alone is an AUTOMATIC FAIL · WASH ALL BEDDING, TOWELS AND CLOTHING hot and dry hot, sealing what cannot be washed for several days · ORAL IVERMECTIN is an alternative in crusted scabies, treatment failure or outbreaks · AND WARN THAT THE ITCH CAN PERSIST TWO TO FOUR WEEKS AFTER SUCCESSFUL TREATMENT, otherwise they will think it failed VERIFY. CRUSTED SCABIES, ALSO CALLED NORWEGIAN SCABIES: thick, crusted, hyperkeratotic plaques carrying ENORMOUS NUMBERS OF MITES, occurring in immunosuppression, frailty and neurological impairment, EXTREMELY CONTAGIOUS, and a significant problem in REMOTE ABORIGINAL COMMUNITIES IN AUSTRALIA, where scabies is also a driver of streptococcal skin infection and therefore of POST-STREPTOCOCCAL GLOMERULONEPHRITIS AND ACUTE RHEUMATIC FEVER. Raising this appropriately is a strong cultural-safety and public-health mark — raise it if the patient's circumstances make it relevant, NOT GRATUITOUSLY. EXPLAINING SCABIES: 'It's a tiny mite — a small bug — that burrows into the top layer of the skin and causes intense itching and a rash. IT HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH BEING UNCLEAN. It spreads through close contact and through shared bedding and clothing, which is why it moves through households.' THREE REASONS: the SITE, between the fingers and on the wrists · the ITCH WORSE AT NIGHT AND AFTER A HOT SHOWER · and THE HOUSEMATE. THEN THE BIT THAT MATTERS MOST: 'we treat you, AND WE TREAT EVERYONE IN THE HOUSE AT THE SAME TIME — even the ones with no rash. If we don't, it just passes back and forth.' EXPLAINING URTICARIA: 'certain cells in your skin release a chemical called HISTAMINE, which makes small blood vessels leak, and you get these raised itchy patches. It is very common and NOT DANGEROUS IN ITSELF.' THREE REASONS: raised and intensely itchy · EACH INDIVIDUAL ONE COMES AND GOES rather than staying put · heat makes it worse. THEN THE SAFETY-NET: 'if you ever get swelling of your lips, tongue or throat, or you feel short of breath or your throat is tightening, THAT IS AN EMERGENCY — CALL AN AMBULANCE.' HER HIDDEN AGENDA IN BOTH VERSIONS: SHE IS EMBARRASSED AND HALF-BELIEVES THIS MEANS SHE IS DIRTY, and she says so only if asked an open question about her concerns. IF YOU NAME SCABIES WITHOUT IMMEDIATELY SAYING IT IS NOT ABOUT HYGIENE she looks mortified and says 'SO IT'S BECAUSE THE HOUSE IS FILTHY, BASICALLY.' THE HONEST CLOSE WHEN YOU ARE NOT CERTAIN: 'the pattern fits scabies best, and I'd treat on that basis — BUT I WANT TO SEE YOU AGAIN IN TWO WEEKS, because if it isn't settling we'll need to think again.'

THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: no characterisation of the rash · never asked about household contacts · no airway question in an itchy rash · treated the patient alone for scabies · left her believing the diagnosis reflects poor hygiene.

The single most discriminating question, which the source omits — 'If you pick one particular spot and watch it — how long does that individual spot last before it fades?' Under 24 hours and it moves around → urticarial weals. Fixed, persisting for days → not urticaria: think vasculitis, infestation, eczema, drug eruption. And a weal that lasts more than 24 hours, leaves bruising, or burns rather than itches suggests urticarial vasculitis and needs further assessment VERIFY

The airway question — missing it in an itchy rash is not recoverable — 'ANY SWELLING OF THE LIPS, TONGUE OR THROAT? ANY DIFFICULTY BREATHING OR SWALLOWING? ANY LIGHT-HEADEDNESS?' URTICARIA WITH AIRWAY INVOLVEMENT IS ANAPHYLAXIS. And the meningococcal screen belongs in EVERY rash station: fever or chills, drowsy, headache, photophobia, neck stiffness

The household question — nearly always positive, and almost nobody asks it — 'IS ANYONE ELSE AT HOME OR AT WORK ITCHY, OR HAS ANYONE ELSE GOT A RASH?' The single most useful question for scabies, and an AUTOMATIC FAIL if omitted. Pair it with TRAVEL AND ACCOMMODATION — 'any travel, and WHERE DID YOU STAY — hotel, motel, hostel, shared accommodation?' — because SHARED BEDDING IS THE CLASSIC ACQUISITION ROUTE. She will not volunteer either the housemate or the hostel

The two pathways, side by side — URTICARIA: itchy raised red weals, OFTEN WIDESPREAD rather than confined · INDIVIDUAL SPOTS COME AND GO WITHIN 24 HOURS AND MOVE AROUND · often follows a viral illness, a new food, a new medicine or an insect bite · heat, HOT SHOWERS, EXERCISE AND STRESS make it worse, cholinergic urticaria in particular · may be associated with ANGIO-OEDEMA of lips, eyelids or tongue · personal or family ATOPY is common. SCABIES: a mite infestation, SARCOPTES SCABIEI — NOT an allergy and NOT a blood infection · intense itch, WORSE AT NIGHT and after hot showers · LOVES THE FINGER WEB SPACES, wrist flexures, elbows, axillae, waistband, genitalia and areolae · BURROWS are pathognomonic but often absent or invisible · acquired by PROLONGED SKIN-TO-SKIN CONTACT or from bedding, linen and clothing · OTHER PEOPLE IN THE HOUSEHOLD ARE USUALLY ITCHY TOO

The itch lags — say it out loud — ON FIRST INFESTATION THE ITCH STARTS WEEKS AFTER EXPOSURE, because it is an ALLERGIC RESPONSE TO THE MITE; on re-infestation it starts within days VERIFY. That is why a patient can insist NOTHING HAS CHANGED RECENTLY and still have acquired it in a hostel six weeks ago — and saying it makes the six-week-old travel history make sense to her

stem: General practice, rural South Australia. A 25-year-old man attends for the results of a sexual health screen taken last week. 8 minutes, no examination.
Version A — chlamydia positive on first-pass urine NAAT; HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B and gonorrhoea negative. The agenda is 'Is my partner cheating?'
Version B, the harder one — chlamydia and gonorrhoea both positive; HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B and C negative. The drug, the look-back period and the follow-up all change.
Read the stem for which version you are in. Both are failed the same way: vague management.

findings: The sandwich — the ninety seconds that set the tone

'The GOOD NEWS FIRST: your HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B are all negative. TWO HAVE COME BACK POSITIVE — chlamydia and gonorrhoea. They're two of the commonest sexually transmitted infections, and I want to be clear: BOTH ARE BACTERIAL AND BOTH ARE CURABLE with antibiotics I can give you today. HOW ARE YOU FEELING ABOUT THAT?' THREE WAYS THIS MINUTE GOES WRONG: leading with the positive, after which he stops listening · jargon — 'your NAAT was positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae' means nothing to him · and NO PAUSE, because THE PAUSE IS WHERE THE AGENDA ARRIVES

back.dx: UNCOMPLICATED GENITAL CHLAMYDIA, WITH GONORRHOEA ADDED IN VERSION B. CHLAMYDIA IS USUALLY SILENT — which is why the look-back window is long and why we screen. GONORRHOEA IS USUALLY LOUD IN MEN, with urethral discharge and dysuria in around 85–90% of penile infections, while ANAL AND PHARYNGEAL INFECTION IS USUALLY SILENT VERIFY. TESTING: FIRST-PASS URINE FOR NAAT in a man — THE FIRST PART OF THE STREAM, NOT THE FIRST URINE OF THE DAY, and the opposite of a midstream specimen · in a woman, a clinician-collected endocervical swab if examined, otherwise a self-collected vaginal swab, with FIRST-PASS URINE THE LEAST SENSITIVE OPTION · plus GONOCOCCAL CULTURE FROM EVERY INFECTED SITE, TAKEN BEFORE ANTIBIOTICS BUT NEVER DELAYING TREATMENT. TWO PRACTICAL POINTS THAT EARN MARKS: the request must say 'GONOCOCCAL CULTURE', not just 'culture', because the organism needs specific media and conditions; and the specimen should reach the laboratory WITHIN ABOUT 24 HOURS VERIFY. WHY AZITHROMYCIN IS ADDED TO CEFTRIAXONE — AND IT IS NOT TO COVER CHLAMYDIA: dual antibiotic treatment exists to CREATE A PHARMACOLOGICAL BARRIER TO WIDER CEFTRIAXONE RESISTANCE. Reduced susceptibility is emerging in urban Australia, and THE PHARYNX — where drug penetration is poor and resistance genes are traded between organisms — IS THE LIKELIEST SITE OF TREATMENT FAILURE, which is also why pharyngeal infection gets AZITHROMYCIN 2 g VERIFY. CORRECTION — THE CO-INFECTION REGIMEN IS THE ONE GENUINELY CONTESTED POINT: the teaching version is CEFTRIAXONE 500 mg IM PLUS DOXYCYCLINE 100 mg BD FOR 7 DAYS, dropping azithromycin because azithromycin no longer performs well against chlamydia, and the Australian guideline uses exactly that combination for RECTAL co-infection. BUT THE STRICT FIRST-LINE REGIMEN FOR GENITAL GONORRHOEA REMAINS CEFTRIAXONE PLUS AZITHROMYCIN 1 g, and chlamydia first-line remains doxycycline. BOTH READINGS ARE CURRENT AND BOTH APPEAR IN PRACTICE — DO NOT ASSERT ONE AS THE ONLY ANSWER. SAFE OSCE WORDING: 'For the gonorrhoea, CEFTRIAXONE 500 mg as an injection into the muscle, mixed with 2 mL of local anaesthetic so it stings less. For the chlamydia, DOXYCYCLINE 100 mg twice a day for seven days — AND THE DOXYCYCLINE ALSO ACTS AS THE SECOND AGENT FOR THE GONORRHOEA, which is why I'm not adding azithromycin on top.' IF CHALLENGED: 'the strict first-line regimen for genital gonorrhoea is ceftriaxone with azithromycin 1 g as a DUAL PHARMACOLOGICAL BARRIER against resistance. Where chlamydia is also confirmed, the guideline's co-infection regimen pairs ceftriaxone with doxycycline instead — which treats the chlamydia properly and still provides two agents. I'd CONFIRM AGAINST THE CURRENT AUSTRALIAN STI MANAGEMENT GUIDELINES and take local sexual health advice if there were any doubt.' ON ALLERGY: a history of rash after penicillin is not necessarily a contraindication, but ANAPHYLAXIS TO PENICILLIN, OR DOCUMENTED CEPHALOSPORIN ALLERGY, MEANS SPECIALIST ADVICE — NOT A GUESS AT AN ALTERNATIVE, because alternatives are otherwise not recommended given resistance VERIFY. CORRECTION — TEST OF CURE IS NARROWER THAN THE TEACHING SUGGESTS: the lecture says test of cure for every case of gonorrhoea always. THE AUSTRALIAN GUIDELINE IS NARROWER — NAAT TWO WEEKS AFTER TREATMENT IS COMPLETED, FOR EACH SITE OF INFECTION (PHARYNGEAL, ANAL OR CERVICAL), AND ESPECIALLY WHERE NO CULTURE WAS TAKEN BEFORE TREATMENT, WHERE CULTURE SHOWED REDUCED SUSCEPTIBILITY, OR WHERE A NON-STANDARD REGIMEN WAS USED. URETHRAL INFECTION IN A MAN IS NOT ON THAT LIST — though here it is still easy to justify, and if no culture was collected before the injection it is squarely indicated VERIFY. NOTIFICATION IN SOUTH AUSTRALIA, UNDER THE PUBLIC HEALTH ACT 2011 AND ITS NOTIFIABLE CONDITIONS REGULATIONS: GONORRHOEA — THE PRACTITIONER NOTIFIES AS WELL AS THE LABORATORY. CHLAMYDIA — AN EXCEPTION APPLIES: the laboratory notifies, and the practitioner routinely notifies ONLY WHERE THE PERSON IS 16 YEARS OR YOUNGER, or for a point-of-care test not reported by a pathology service, or a related death. REPORTING REQUIREMENTS CHANGED RECENTLY — CONFIRM BEFORE QUOTING THE DETAIL VERIFY. PARTNER NOTIFICATION: they should be tested and treated, and PRESUMPTIVE TREATMENT IS CONSIDERED FOR CONTACT IN THE LAST TWO WEEKS · offer to see the partner yourself BUT DO NOT HAND OVER A SECOND PRESCRIPTION. THE FIVE PRACTICE CARDS: A 22-YEAR-OLD WOMAN, chlamydia positive, asymptomatic, asking about fertility — HIDDEN: SHE IS NINE WEEKS PREGNANT AND HAS NOT TOLD YOU, so ask about pregnancy before prescribing, because DOXYCYCLINE IS CONTRAINDICATED and azithromycin plus a test of cure applies instead VERIFY · A 31-YEAR-OLD MAN, gonorrhoea positive on a THROAT swab with urine negative — hidden: he has not told you he has male partners; tests the PHARYNGEAL REGIMEN, AZITHROMYCIN 2 g, test of cure at two weeks, and three-site testing · A MAN TREATED TWO WEEKS AGO WHOSE TEST OF CURE IS STILL POSITIVE — hidden: he had sex with the same untreated partner on day 3; tests distinguishing TREATMENT FAILURE FROM RE-INFECTION and seeking specialist advice rather than repeating the regimen blindly · A 19-YEAR-OLD, gonorrhoea positive, FEBRILE WITH PAINFUL WRISTS AND PUSTULES — DISSEMINATED GONOCOCCAL INFECTION, no longer a GP counselling case: same-day referral, blood cultures, parenteral therapy · A 16-YEAR-OLD with chlamydia WHOSE PARTNER IS 24 — the SAFEGUARDING PIVOT: age of consent, capacity, coercion and mandatory notification obligations, which take priority over everything else VERIFY.

BOX THREE AND FOUR: SEVEN DAYS NO SEX and until partners are treated · review at one week · TEST OF CURE AT TWO WEEKS · RE-INFECTION TESTING AT THREE MONTHS with HIV and syphilis rechecked for the window period.
THE AGENDA, ANSWERED HONESTLY — and repeated unchanged when he presses.
BOX FIVE, EDUCATION AND CLOSE: red flags named specifically · fact sheet · PrEP and vaccination flagged for the review · 'is there anything you'd like me to go over again?'

THE MANAGEMENT SET: 'Have you ever reacted to penicillin or any antibiotic?' · 'I'll take a swab for culture before I treat you.' · 'Anyone in the last six months needs testing and treatment.' · 'There's an anonymous service called Let Them Know.' · 'It's notified to SA Health — not to your employer or your partner.' · 'No sex for seven days, and until your partners are treated.' · 'Two weeks after treatment, a test of cure.' · 'Three months, a re-infection test, and we recheck HIV and syphilis.'

WHEN HE SAYS 'I FEEL FILTHY': 'I hear that a lot, and I want to say clearly — these are VERY COMMON INFECTIONS AND THEY SAY NOTHING ABOUT YOU AS A PERSON. They're treatable, and YOU DID EXACTLY THE RIGHT THING BY GETTING TESTED.' AND WHEN HE PRESSES ON THE HIV WINDOW: 'a test can't detect an infection picked up in the last few weeks. That's why we repeat it — NOT BECAUSE I'M WORRIED, BUT BECAUSE THAT'S HOW THE TEST WORKS.'
pefe: THERE IS NO EXAMINATION — THE FINDINGS ARE THE RESULT SHEET AND WHAT HE TELLS YOU WHEN ASKED: a discharge and stinging on passing urine for about a week, still present but less · TWO PARTNERS IN THE LAST SIX MONTHS, his girlfriend of four months and one person before her · vaginal and oral sex only, CONDOMS SOMETIMES, NOT ALWAYS, and not with his girlfriend · no male partners, no injecting drug use · NO PAST STI AND NEVER TESTED BEFORE · no allergies, no regular medications.

PERSISTING SYMPTOMS CHANGE THE TEST-OF-CURE DECISION, so if he mentions the discharge, ACKNOWLEDGE IT AND PROMISE TO COME BACK TO IT rather than moving straight to treatment. And if you sound judgemental or awkward about the number of partners, HE GOES QUIET AND ANSWERS IN SINGLE WORDS FROM THAT POINT ON.
THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: he is told his partner has been unfaithful · he is promised nobody will ever know · the drugs are named without doses · or the cheating question is never answered.

Box one — the drug, with the allergy question and the culture — 'HAVE YOU EVER HAD A REACTION TO PENICILLIN OR ANY ANTIBIOTIC?' asked in the same breath as naming the injection, because CEFTRIAXONE IS A CEPHALOSPORIN. Then: 'I'll TAKE ANOTHER SWAB BEFORE I GIVE IT, to grow the bacteria and check which antibiotics work.' CEFTRIAXONE 500 mg IM IN 2 mL OF 1% LIGNOCAINE for the gonorrhoea · DOXYCYCLINE 100 mg TWICE DAILY FOR 7 DAYS for the chlamydia, taken SITTING UP WITH WATER, not lying down straight after because of OESOPHAGEAL ULCERATION, and careful in the sun VERIFY

Box two — the two notifications, and the look-back arithmetic — PARTNERS: 'anyone you've had sex with IN THE LAST SIX MONTHS needs testing and probably treatment. FOR GONORRHOEA ON ITS OWN WE'D GO BACK TWO MONTHS, BUT CHLAMYDIA IS SIX — SO WE USE THE LONGER ONE.' Giving the number without the reasoning shows you know one window; giving both shows you know two. AND IT DOES NOT HAVE TO BE FACE TO FACE — LET THEM KNOW sends an anonymous SMS or email, and SHINE SA and Clinic 275 can help by phone from a rural site. THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT: notified to SA HEALTH for statistics and contact-tracing support — 'IT DOES NOT GO TO YOUR EMPLOYER, YOUR FAMILY OR YOUR PARTNER.' NEVER SAY 'NOBODY WILL EVER KNOW'

Box three and four — abstinence, and two separate follow-ups — No sex for seven days from today, and not until partners are treated, or you pass it back and forth. Then the three appointments: review at one week, to check the course is finished and contacts are sorted · test of cure at two weeks after treatment is completed, asking did the antibiotic work · re-infection testing at three months, asking has it come back, and rechecking HIV and syphilis because those tests have a window period. Collapsing the two follow-ups into one loses a separate box — they are different tests asking different questions

The agenda — 'Is my partner cheating?' — learn this verbatim — BOTH EASY ANSWERS FAIL. 'Probably, yes' damages a relationship on no evidence; 'no, definitely not' is a claim you cannot support. THE ANSWER: 'That's a fair question and I want to be honest with you. WE HAVE NO WAY OF TELLING WHEN THIS WAS PICKED UP, OR WHO HAD IT FIRST. Chlamydia very often causes NO SYMPTOMS AT ALL, so it can sit quietly for a long time before anyone knows it's there. SO I CAN'T TELL YOU WHERE IT CAME FROM, AND I'M NOT GOING TO GUESS. What I can do is treat you, and make sure your partner gets tested and treated too.' HE WILL PRESS TWICE — REPEAT THE SAME SENTENCE UNCHANGED RATHER THAN SOFTENING INTO A GUESS

The things the source leaves out, each worth a mark — OFFER PrEP — the guideline says consider HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis for ANYONE DIAGNOSED WITH GONORRHOEA, not only men who have sex with men. VACCINATION — check and offer HEPATITIS A AND B, AND HPV CATCH-UP. AND THE RED FLAGS, SAID SPECIFICALLY: come back sooner for FEVER, PAIN OR SWELLING IN A TESTICLE, worsening pain passing urine, or JOINT PAINS WITH A RASH, which is DISSEMINATED GONOCOCCAL INFECTION

stem: General practice, rural South Australia. A 40-year-old man has come for advice. He is starting a new relationship with a male partner and would like to know what he should do beforehand. 8 minutes.
Nothing is wrong with him. No diagnosis, no examination, no results to explain — a pure counselling station in a well man, and you either have the PrEP knowledge or you do not.

There is no history-taking task, and the examiner will interrupt you — 'Stick to your task' — if you begin asking questions. You may ask a small number that directly serve the counselling (Vaccination, prior screening), framed explicitly as part of the advice. Do not open a sexual history.

back.dx: A WELL 40-YEAR-OLD MAN STARTING A RELATIONSHIP WITH A MALE PARTNER — ONE OF THE SEXUAL HEALTH CASES THAT ENTERED THE AMC FROM 2023. THE TASK LINE IS DECEPTIVELY VAGUE AND THE MARKS SIT ALMOST ENTIRELY IN ONE PLACE: WHETHER YOU CAN EXPLAIN PrEP THE WAY A GP WHO ACTUALLY PRESCRIBES IT WOULD. SAFE SEX, SPECIFICALLY: CONDOMS are the single most useful thing, WITH PLENTY OF WATER-BASED LUBRICANT, because OIL-BASED PRODUCTS DEGRADE LATEX and condoms fail more often in anal sex without adequate lubrication · a regular partner rather than casual ones lowers risk · AVOID SEX UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF ALCOHOL OR DRUGS, BECAUSE THAT IS WHEN CONDOMS GET SKIPPED · care with group sex and casual partners. AND MPOX VACCINATION is recommended for some men who have sex with men in Australia and is worth naming alongside hepatitis A, hepatitis B and HPV VERIFY. WHO PrEP IS FOR: MEN WHO HAVE SEX WITH MEN is the strongest indication in Australia, particularly with condomless anal sex, receptive condomless anal sex, RECENT RECTAL CHLAMYDIA OR GONORRHOEA OR SYPHILIS, travel with anticipated condomless casual sex, or sex under the influence · AN HIV-POSITIVE PARTNER, particularly where the viral load is not known to be suppressed · people who inject drugs, sex workers, people in custodial settings, and trans and gender diverse people at risk · AND ANYONE WHO ASKS FOR IT, INCLUDING ANXIETY ABOUT ACQUIRING HIV THAT IS AFFECTING THEIR LIFE even where the measured risk is low, provided they understand the monitoring and side effects · FOR WOMEN WHO HAVE SEX WITH WOMEN the data do not support routine PrEP, but take a proper sexual history first because the label DOES NOT EXCLUDE MALE PARTNERS, and anxiety remains a valid reason VERIFY. MONITORING: START WITHIN SEVEN DAYS OF THE NEGATIVE HIV TEST · THEN EVERY THREE MONTHS, HIV AND THE FULL STI SCREEN · RENAL FUNCTION REPEATED EARLY AND THEN EVERY SIX MONTHS. SIDE EFFECTS IN THE ORDER TO SAY THEM: minor and usually settling — nausea, headache, sometimes loose bowels in the first weeks · THE ONE THAT MATTERS IS THE KIDNEYS, hence baseline testing and repeat renal function · long term, A SMALL EFFECT ON BONE DENSITY with prolonged use · AVOID NSAIDs AND TELL EVERY PRESCRIBER AND PHARMACIST YOU ARE ON IT VERIFY. THE PBS SENTENCE, A MARKED ITEM: 'PrEP is SUBSIDISED THROUGH THE PBS, so it costs you a normal prescription rather than the full price — and the full price is substantial. The condition is that WE HAVE A NEGATIVE HIV RESULT ON YOUR FILE AND THAT YOU AGREE TO THREE-MONTHLY SCREENING. I can only write three months of script at a time, SO THE TEST AND THE PRESCRIPTION TRAVEL TOGETHER' VERIFY. DOXYCYCLINE POST-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS is now used in some Australian sexual health services to reduce bacterial STIs in selected men who have sex with men — MENTION IT AS SOMETHING TO DISCUSS, NOT AS SOMETHING YOU ARE STARTING TODAY VERIFY. DO NOT PROMISE A SCRIPT TODAY: he is not starting until the HIV test and the renal function are back, and 'I'd like you to go away and think about it while we wait for these results' is both correct and patient-centred. AND NEVER TELL HIM PrEP MEANS HE CANNOT GET HIV — he accepts it warmly and marks it down. SOUTH AUSTRALIAN SERVICES, AND NAME AN ALTERNATIVE UNPROMPTED IN A SMALL TOWN BECAUSE BEING RECOGNISED AT THE LOCAL CLINIC IS A REAL BARRIER: SHINE SA · ADELAIDE SEXUAL HEALTH CENTRE (CLINIC 275), free, confidential, including telephone advice for rural GPs · SAMESH for peer-based HIV and sexual health support · QLife 1800 184 527 · Country Health Connect and telehealth · PATS · Let Them Know VERIFY. HIS HIDDEN CONCERN: HE IS FRIGHTENED OF HIV SPECIFICALLY AND SLIGHTLY ASHAMED OF BEING FRIGHTENED — he volunteers it if asked about concerns, and otherwise raises it at about six minutes: 'CAN I ASK YOU SOMETHING? SHOULD I BE WORRIED ABOUT HIV?' HE ALSO SAYS HIS PARTNER 'IS CLEAN' — DO NOT REPEAT THE WORD; redirect: 'that's a very common thing to be told, and people say it in good faith. But BECAUSE MOST OF THESE INFECTIONS CAUSE NO SYMPTOMS, THE ONLY WAY ANYONE KNOWS IS BY TESTING.' AND WHEN HE SUGGESTS BOTH TESTING THEN STOPPING CONDOMS: TESTING TELLS YOU ABOUT THE PAST, NOT THE FUTURE, AND HIV AND SYPHILIS HAVE WINDOW PERIODS — say it without lecturing, and use it as the natural bridge into PrEP. THE FIVE PRACTICE CARDS: A SORE THROAT, TRUNCAL RASH AND SWOLLEN GLANDS FOR A FORTNIGHT — HIV SEROCONVERSION ILLNESS, so do not start PrEP; fourth-generation testing PLUS HIV RNA and same-day sexual health advice · HE ASKS FOR PrEP BY NAME AND MENTIONS CONDOMLESS SEX FOUR DAYS AGO — outside the 72-hour PEP boundary, and a negative test today does not exclude very recent infection · eGFR COMES BACK AT 52 because he has been taking ibuprofen daily for a shoulder problem — do not start, stop the NSAID, repeat renal function, seek advice about alternatives VERIFY · A 25-YEAR-OLD WOMAN IN A MONOGAMOUS HETEROSEXUAL RELATIONSHIP TERRIFIED OF HIV — anxiety affecting daily life is a legitimate reason to prescribe, AND THE ANXIETY ALSO NEEDS ADDRESSING IN ITS OWN RIGHT · A 19-YEAR-OLD IN A TOWN OF 900 LIVING WITH HIS PARENTS — confidentiality, an alternative service named unprompted, results to a chosen number, and NEVER PROMISING THAT NOBODY WILL EVER SEE ANYTHING.
plan: Introduce and use his name, open question — then congratulate him and thank him for coming in beforehand.
NORMALISE, GIVE CONFIDENTIALITY, AND SIGNPOST FOUR HEADINGS: why this matters, safe sex, the tests today, and a medication that prevents HIV.
THE EDUCATION BLOCK: higher rate in this group including HIV · MOST OF THEM CAUSE NO SYMPTOMS · which is why we screen regularly. Redirect 'he's clean' without repeating the word.
SAFE SEX, SPECIFICALLY: condoms with WATER-BASED LUBRICANT · regular rather than casual partners · avoid sex under the influence.
THE INVESTIGATIONS BY SITE: THROAT, BACK PASSAGE (self-collected if he prefers), AND FIRST-PASS URINE — with the reason. Then HIV, syphilis, HEPATITIS B ANTIGEN AND ANTIBODY, HEPATITIS A ANTIBODY.
HEPATITIS C EXPLAINED AS CONDITIONAL — and then added, because he is starting PrEP. That is the natural bridge.
PrEP: WHAT IT IS, THE DRUG NAMES, AND HOW WELL IT WORKS — highly effective, not absolutely perfect, which is part of why we keep testing.
THE TWO REGIMENS: daily preferred and why · ON-DEMAND, 2 TABLETS AT LEAST 2 HOURS BEFORE, THEN 1 DAILY FOR 2 DAYS, with its three conditions and the honest limitation.
The three conditions before a script: negative HIV test · kidney function and no NSAIDs · the PBS three-monthly screening condition.
SIDE EFFECTS IN ORDER, then the monitoring schedule — start within 7 days, three-monthly HIV and STI screen, renal function six-monthly.

CLOSE: vaccinate if hepatitis A or B antibody is low · HPV REGARDLESS OF AGE · SHINE SA fact sheet and Clinic 275 as an alternative away from town · GO AWAY AND THINK ABOUT PrEP WHILE WE WAIT · anything to go over again?

ask: THE FIRST THIRTY SECONDS: 'Congratulations — that's lovely news. And thank you for coming in beforehand; that's exactly the right thing to do, and not many people do it.' THEN: 'I'll be talking about some personal things to do with sex, because that's how I give you the right advice. Is that all right? Everything we discuss stays between us.'

THE SCREEN: 'For chlamydia and gonorrhoea I TAKE THREE SAMPLES, NOT ONE — a swab from the throat, a swab from the back passage, you can do it yourself if you'd rather, and a urine sample, THE FIRST PART OF THE STREAM, NOT THE MIDDLE. All three, because throat and back-passage infections usually cause no symptoms and don't show up in urine.' AND ON THE BLOODS: 'hepatitis B — BOTH WHETHER YOU HAVE IT AND WHETHER YOU'RE IMMUNE TO IT.'

PrEP, VERBATIM: 'HIV is the one we can't cure.' · 'We offer everyone in your situation a medication called PrEP.' · 'Tenofovir disoproxil and emtricitabine.' · 'DAILY IS OUR PREFERRED OPTION.' · 'Two tablets at least two hours before sex.' · 'THE SCRIPT AND THE THREE-MONTHLY SCREEN TRAVEL TOGETHER.' AND ON HIS PARTNER: 'most of these cause no symptoms, so THE ONLY WAY TO KNOW IS TO TEST.'
pefe: THERE IS NO EXAMINATION AND NO HISTORY TASK — ASKING A SEXUAL HISTORY IS A MARKED ERROR AND THE EXAMINER WILL INTERRUPT. The few questions you may ask are the ones that DIRECTLY SERVE THE ADVICE, framed as such: has he had Gardasil, has he had hepatitis vaccination, has he ever been screened, and — before you talk about PrEP — does he take ibuprofen or any anti-inflammatory.

WHAT HE GIVES YOU IF ASKED: previously married to a woman and divorced six years ago, THIS IS HIS FIRST MALE PARTNER · NOT YET SEXUALLY ACTIVE WITH HIM, which is why he came now · NEVER HAD A SEXUAL HEALTH SCREEN IN HIS LIFE · childhood vaccinations but NO GARDASIL, because it was not offered at his school · IBUPROFEN NOW AND THEN FOR HIS SHOULDER · no regular medications, no allergies, no kidney problems known · and 'I'VE HEARD OF PrEP — I THOUGHT IT WAS FOR PEOPLE WHO SLEEP AROUND.'

THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: PrEP is not discussed in any meaningful detail · screening is urine-only · he is told PrEP means he cannot get HIV · or the doctor's discomfort is visible throughout.

Manner is separately and deliberately tested here — THE ROLE-PLAYER IS BRIEFED TO GO GUARDED AND ANSWER IN SINGLE WORDS if you hesitate, apologise repeatedly, avoid eye contact, or CHANGE YOUR TONE when sex between men comes up. NON-JUDGEMENTAL IS A BEHAVIOUR, NOT AN ATTITUDE: do not over-apologise, because repeated 'sorry to have to ask this' READS AS DISCOMFORT, NOT COURTESY · use the guidelines' language, MEN WHO HAVE SEX WITH MEN, and avoid labels he has not used about himself · AND CONGRATULATE HIM FIRST, because you would congratulate anyone else starting a relationship

The education block, and the two barriers the guidelines name — 'Men who have sex with men have a HIGHER RATE of these infections, including HIV. And the part that matters: MOST OF THEM CAUSE NO SYMPTOMS AT ALL, so people carry them without knowing and pass them on. That's why we screen regularly rather than waiting for something to go wrong.' THE TWO BARRIERS, BOTH MARKED ITEMS: INSUFFICIENT FREQUENCY OF TESTING — annual is the floor, THREE-MONTHLY is the recommendation for men with new or multiple partners · AND INCOMPLETE TESTING — clinicians who send a urine sample and stop, when ANAL AND PHARYNGEAL INFECTION IS USUALLY SILENT AND URINE WILL NOT FIND IT

The three-site screen — a urine-only answer fails this station — PHARYNGEAL SWAB — 'like a COVID swab' · ANORECTAL SWAB — collected for every man who has sex with men, symptoms or not, and SELF-COLLECTION IS ACCEPTABLE · FIRST-PASS URINE — THE FIRST PART OF THE STREAM, NOT THE MIDDLE, which is the opposite of a midstream specimen. ALL THREE FOR CHLAMYDIA AND GONORRHOEA, WITH THE REASON GIVEN. AND WHAT IS NOT IN A ROUTINE SCREEN: MYCOPLASMA GENITALIUM, HPV AND HERPES are not part of routine asymptomatic screening — test for herpes or warts only with symptoms or visible lesions. KNOWING WHAT NOT TO ORDER IS WORTH AS MUCH AS THE LIST

The antigen/antibody point — where most candidates lose a mark without noticing — Reciting 'hepatitis B and C' is not enough. ANTIGEN ASKS WHETHER YOU HAVE THE INFECTION; ANTIBODY ASKS WHETHER YOU ARE PROTECTED. So: HIV SEROLOGY, fourth-generation antigen/antibody assay · SYPHILIS SEROLOGY · HEPATITIS B SURFACE ANTIGEN AND SURFACE ANTIBODY · HEPATITIS A ANTIBODY for immunity only · AND HEPATITIS C, WHICH IS NOT ROUTINE — add it for people who inject drugs, people with an HIV-positive partner, AND ANYONE STARTING PrEP. THE VACCINATION OPPORTUNITY LIVES IN THE ANTIBODIES: 'IF EITHER IS LOW, WE CAN VACCINATE YOU' — hepatitis A, hepatitis B, and HPV REGARDLESS OF AGE, because the usual age-based catch-up rules do not apply in this group VERIFY

PrEP — what it is, and the five checks before a prescription — 'Of all of these, HIV IS THE ONE WE CAN'T CURE — we treat it very well, but we can't clear it. So we offer everyone in your situation PRE-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS. It's a tablet taken before any exposure that stops the virus taking hold — a combination of TENOFOVIR DISOPROXIL AND EMTRICITABINE, and taken properly it is HIGHLY EFFECTIVE THOUGH NOT ABSOLUTELY PERFECT, which is part of why we keep testing.' STEP ONE IS ALWAYS THE HIV TEST, because STARTING PrEP IN UNDIAGNOSED HIV AMOUNTS TO TWO-DRUG THERAPY AND BREEDS RESISTANCE — and take a brief SEROCONVERSION HISTORY (fever, sore throat, rash, swollen glands, aching muscles, diarrhoea), because he may be inside the window period with a negative test. AN EXPOSURE IN THE LAST 72 HOURS IS PEP, NOT PrEP VERIFY

The two regimens, and the three conditions — Daily is preferred — 'More effective and continuous, but it depends entirely on taking it regularly.' On-demand — 'Two tablets at least two hours before sex, then one a day for the next two days', less effective, with three conditions: he would have to prefer it, be having higher-risk sex less than twice a week, and be able to wait the two hours. Voice the honest limitation: 'If you can't reliably wait the two hours, the daily tablet is the safer choice for you' VERIFY. The three conditions before a script: a negative HIV test on file · kidney function checked, eGFR above 60 plus a urine albumin–creatinine ratio, and no nephrotoxic medication — the one that matters is NSAIDs, bought over the counter for a sore back · and the PBS condition of three-monthly screening, which is why the script runs three months at a time
fails: ★ PrEP mentioned but not explained — the marks are in the drug names, both regimens, the three conditions, the side effects and the monitoring
★ Urine-only screening, when the throat and rectum are usually silent and urine will not find them
Visible discomfort — hesitation, repeated apology, a change of tone — after which the role-player goes guarded and answers in single words
Taking a sexual history when there is no history task, and being interrupted with 'stick to your task'

Hepatitis recited as a pair with no antibodies, a vague screening interval instead of three-monthly said in all three places, nothing said about vaccinating a low antibody, or a script promised before the HIV result and renal function are back

setting: Two ways to fail, and they are opposites. Minimising — 'The risk is very low, you probably don't need to worry' — which is inappropriate reassurance, is wrong, and answers her question with the opposite of the truth. Or treating her as a heterosexual woman with a different partner — reciting the standard screen and standard condom advice, never naming a dental dam, never mentioning toys or gloves, never acknowledging that the infection pattern is different. The pass is the middle.
stem: General practice, rural South Australia. A 25-year-old woman has come for advice. She is starting a relationship with a female partner and is seeking advice. 8 minutes, no examination.
Nothing is wrong with her. The station turns on two answers: yes, she can acquire a sexually transmitted infection — and yes, there is a barrier method, and it has a name.

Her agenda, given early if you ask: 'Can I even get an STI?' and 'Do I need to use condoms?' On the first day this station ran, candidates froze on the second question because it seemed not to make sense. It makes perfect sense — she is using 'Condom' as the everyday word for a latex barrier.
Roughly four minutes of history, four of counselling. The counselling content is genuinely short — do not rush the history to get there.
tasks: Take a history from the patient
Counsel the patient regarding her concerns
time: 1:00 open, congratulate, take the agenda, normalise · 4:30 the five history boxes · 5:15 answer both her questions by name · 7:15 the screen, safe sex, vaccination · 8:00 support, reading, her decision · park both questions explicitly rather than answering them immediately, or you wreck the history

back.dx: A WELL 25-YEAR-OLD STARTING A RELATIONSHIP WITH A FEMALE PARTNER — THE COMPANION CASE TO THE MSM STATION, AND THE ONE CANDIDATES UNDER-PREPARE BECAUSE 'THERE IS NOTHING TO SAY'. THERE IS: the infections are different, the barrier method is different, and NEARLY ALL OF THESE WOMEN HAVE HAD MALE PARTNERS BEFORE. WHAT SHE IS ACTUALLY AT RISK OF — SAME OVERALL RATE, DIFFERENT DISTRIBUTION, AND THE EVIDENCE BASE IN THIS GROUP IS GENUINELY THIN VERIFY: BACTERIAL VAGINOSIS, notably more common including CONCORDANCE BETWEEN PARTNERS, NOT CLASSIFIED AS A SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTION but clearly related to sexual activity — TEST IF SYMPTOMATIC, DO NOT SCREEN FOR IT · TRICHOMONIASIS, more common, A GENUINE STI TRANSMISSIBLE BETWEEN WOMEN, tested where there are symptoms, and TREAT BOTH PARTNERS · GENITAL WARTS (HPV), transmitted SKIN-TO-SKIN so readily transmitted here, not a routine screening test, examine and test only with visible lesions · CANDIDIASIS, common and reported as associated, not screened for · HERPES SIMPLEX, skin-to-skin and oral–genital, tested only with symptoms or lesions · CHLAMYDIA AND GONORRHOEA, less common but NOT ZERO, and the history usually reveals why — FINGERS, SHARED TOYS AND PREVIOUS MALE PARTNERS are the routes · SYPHILIS AND HIV, uncommon in exclusively female-to-female sex but still in the routine blood screen, with HIV TRANSMISSION DESCRIBED WITH SHARED TOYS, BLOOD AND BROKEN SKIN. THE ROUTINE SCREEN: CHLAMYDIA AND GONORRHOEA NAAT — preferred sample is a CLINICIAN-COLLECTED ENDOCERVICAL SWAB if she is being examined, otherwise a SELF-COLLECTED VAGINAL SWAB WHICH IS EQUALLY GOOD, and FIRST-PASS URINE ONLY IF SHE DECLINES A SWAB, because it is the least sensitive of the three · HIV SEROLOGY · SYPHILIS SEROLOGY · HEPATITIS B SURFACE ANTIGEN · plus a THROAT OR ANORECTAL SWAB if the history includes oral or anal sex · and the CERVICAL SCREENING TEST if due, which can be done at the same speculum examination. WHAT IS NOT IN A ROUTINE SCREEN HERE: HEPATITIS A ANTIBODY, WHICH BELONGS TO THE MSM SCREEN AND NOT THIS ONE · HEPATITIS C, only for injecting drug use, an HIV-positive partner, or PrEP · HEPATITIS B ANTIBODY, since the ANTIGEN is the routine test and immunity is checked if vaccination status is in question · BV, CANDIDA AND TRICHOMONAS, tested when symptomatic rather than screened for · HERPES AND HPV, only with symptoms or visible lesions · AND PrEP, which the data do not support routinely in this group, though it can still be considered if anxiety about HIV is affecting her life VERIFY. THE REST OF THE SAFE-SEX ADVICE, SPECIFICALLY: TOYS — a NEW CONDOM FOR EACH TOY AND EACH CHANGE OF PARTNER, washed after use, ideally separate toys · HANDS — washed, NAILS SHORT, and latex gloves for fingering or fisting, because THE RISK IS BROKEN SKIN · LUBRICANT — enough of it, water-based, particularly for anal contact · AVOID SEX IF EITHER HAS A RASH, A SORE OR UNUSUAL DISCHARGE, which is when you stop and get checked · MENSTRUATION — use protection or avoid sex, BECAUSE BLOOD CARRIES MORE RISK · and avoid sex under the influence. VACCINATION: HPV catch-up if she missed the school programme VERIFY on current age eligibility · hepatitis B if not immune · HEPATITIS A IS NOT ROUTINELY INDICATED FOR THIS GROUP as it is for men who have sex with men. LANGUAGE THAT KEEPS HER TALKING: DO NOT LABEL HER ORIENTATION — she may not have settled on a word and she does not need one from you · the guidelines suggest asking whether a partner HAS A PENIS OR A VAGINA where relevant, though for the exam 'male or female partners?' is safer, and IF SHE SAYS HER PARTNER IS A TRANS WOMAN, FOLLOW HER LEAD AND ASK WHAT KIND OF SEX THEY HAVE VERIFY · NEVER SAY 'CLEAN' OR 'NORMAL SEX'. OFFER THE SCREEN TO BOTH BUT DO NOT WRITE TWO SLIPS: 'I can offer this to both of you — ask her to come and see me, or any GP, and we'll sort hers out separately.' YOU CANNOT INVESTIGATE A PERSON WHO IS NOT YOUR PATIENT — offering to see the partner is a mark, handing over a second pathology form is an error. THE FIVE PRACTICE CARDS: A THIN GREY DISCHARGE WITH AN ODOUR FOR THREE WEEKS, WORSE AFTER SEX — bacterial vaginosis, and the symptom screen has just turned this from screening into diagnosis VERIFY · HER PARTNER IS A TRANS WOMAN WHO HAS NOT HAD SURGERY, which she will not say unless you ask what kind of sex they have — tests asking about practices rather than labels, CONTRACEPTION, and a screen that now includes the full range · SHE ALSO STILL HAS A MALE PARTNER SHE HAS NOT MENTIONED, volunteered only to an open, non-assuming question · SHE IS 25, HAS NEVER HAD A CERVICAL SCREENING TEST, AND HER MOTHER HAD CERVICAL CANCER AT 40 — family history does not change the programme, while her fear is still taken seriously and SELF-COLLECTION OFFERED TO REDUCE THE BARRIER · SHE IS 16 AND HAS COME WITHOUT HER PARENTS — confidentiality, competence to consent, the age of the partner, coercion, and SAFEGUARDING OBLIGATIONS THAT OVERRIDE EVERYTHING ELSE VERIFY. THE VARIANT MOMENTS, SCRIPTED: IF SHE PUSHES FOR REASSURANCE — 'I'M NOT GOING TO TELL YOU THERE'S NO RISK, BECAUSE THAT WOULDN'T BE TRUE and you'd find out eventually. What I can tell you is that THE RISK IS MANAGEABLE AND MOSTLY PREVENTABLE, and that the things that help are simple.' IF SHE STILL HAS A MALE PARTNER — 'thank you, that's important and I'm glad you said so. IT DOESN'T CHANGE HOW I FEEL ABOUT ANYTHING; IT CHANGES THE MEDICINE' — the full screen definitely applies, and contraception comes back into the conversation.
plan: Introduce and use her name, open question, then congratulate her and thank her for coming in first.

ASK FOR CONCERNS AND WRITE THEM DOWN. She gives both questions here — PARK THEM EXPLICITLY: 'neither of those is stupid, and I'll answer both properly. Can I ask you a few things first, so my answer actually fits you?'
BOX ONE: the new relationship, whether they have had sex yet, and WHAT KIND OF SEX SHE EXPECTS.
BOX TWO: previously sexually active · MALE OR FEMALE PARTNERS · regular or several · more than one at a time.
BOX THREE: condoms, always or sometimes · ORAL, VAGINAL OR ANAL — each answer is a swab site.
BOX FOUR: past STI in her or a partner · ever been tested · sex under the influence · injecting · tattoos or sex overseas.
BOX FIVE: LAST MENSTRUAL PERIOD and regularity · cervical screening status · Gardasil · AND THE SYMPTOM SCREEN AS A SEPARATE JOB.
ANSWER ONE, UNHEDGED: yes you can — then the different pattern, named.
ANSWER TWO: the DENTAL DAM, described, with the cut-open-condom trick. Then toys, hands, nails, lubricant, symptoms and menstruation.
THE SCREEN, JUSTIFIED BY HER HISTORY — previous male partners and never screened — WITH SAMPLE OPTIONS, and the partner invited in rather than handed a form.
CERVICAL SCREENING: same as for any other woman, 25 to 74, five-yearly, AND WHY THIS GROUP FALLS BEHIND. Self-collection offered.
READING AND SUPPORT — Rainbow Health Australia, SHINE SA, QLife — then CLOSE ON HER DECISION: 'what would you like to do today?'
