ask: THE OPENING SET: 'Congratulations — that's lovely, I'm really pleased for you. And thank you for coming in first.' · 'NEITHER OF THOSE IS A STUPID QUESTION.' · 'Can I ask you a few things first, so my answer fits you?' · AND THE HINGE: 'WERE YOUR PREVIOUS PARTNERS MALE OR FEMALE?'

THE TWO ANSWERS: 'YES — you can get a sexually transmitted infection from sex with a woman.' · 'What's different is WHICH infections we see.' · 'More bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis.' · 'THERE IS A BARRIER — IT'S CALLED A DENTAL DAM.' · 'Cut a condom open and you've made one.'

THE PRACTICAL SET: 'A new condom on each toy, and between partners.' · 'Short nails, clean hands, plenty of lubricant.' · 'If either of you has a rash or discharge, STOP AND GET CHECKED.' · 'You can take the swab yourself if you'd prefer.' · 'YOUR CERVICAL SCREENING IS EXACTLY THE SAME AS FOR ANY OTHER WOMAN.'
pefe: NO EXAMINATION — THE FINDINGS ARE WHAT SHE GIVES YOU, AND TWO OF THEM ONLY IF ASKED DIRECTLY: THREE OR FOUR PREVIOUS PARTNERS, ALL MEN, one a two-year relationship and the others casual · CONDOMS SOMETIMES, NOT ALWAYS · oral and vaginal sex, no anal · never diagnosed with an infection AND NEVER TESTED FOR ONE · last period two weeks ago, regular · NEVER HAD A CERVICAL SCREENING TEST, because she believed it started at thirty · she did have the school vaccination · and NO SYMPTOMS AT ALL.

She does not volunteer the previous male partners and she does not volunteer that she has never had a cervical screening test. Both are the point of the case. And if you hesitate, over-apologise or change tone when she mentions sex with a woman, she becomes brief and flat and marks you down.
THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: she is told the risk is negligible · no barrier method is ever named · previous male partners are never asked about · or cervical screening is never mentioned.

The hinge of the case — previous male partners — UP TO 90% OF WOMEN IN THIS GROUP HAVE HAD MALE PARTNERS AT SOME POINT, and anything she acquired then is still there. 'WERE YOUR PREVIOUS PARTNERS MALE OR FEMALE?' asked plainly and early in box 2. Without it your counselling FLOATS FREE OF HER ACTUAL RISK — and the silent failure of this station is a competent, kind consultation in which NOBODY EVER ASKS WHETHER HER PREVIOUS PARTNERS WERE MEN. She has had unprotected sex with male partners and has NEVER BEEN SCREENED

The five history boxes — ONE, THE COMPLAINT AND THE FUTURE HALF — tell me about the relationship, HAVE YOU STARTED HAVING SEX YET, and what sort of sex do you expect: oral, hands, toys. TWO, PARTNERS — previously active, MALE OR FEMALE, regular or several, and MORE THAN ONE AT THE SAME TIME, because 'regular partner' does not exclude multiple partners. THREE, PRACTICES AND PROTECTION — condoms, always or sometimes, and ORAL, VAGINAL OR ANAL, because EACH ANSWER IS A SWAB SITE and saying that out loud tells the examiner why you asked. FOUR, PAST INFECTION AND RISK — prior STI in her or a partner, sex under the influence, injecting, tattoos, sex overseas. FIVE, PREVENTION AND SYMPTOMS NOW

Box five holds the two things people forget — THE SYMPTOM SCREEN IS A SEPARATE JOB FROM THE RISK ASSESSMENT, and the examiner has a box for each: any discharge, ITCH, SORENESS OR UNUSUAL SMELL, any rashes, lumps, warts or sores, any pain with sex or passing urine. IF SHE HAS SYMPTOMS THIS STOPS BEING A SCREENING CONVERSATION. AND THE LAST MENSTRUAL PERIOD, which quietly covers PREGNANCY without the awkwardness of asking a woman starting a same-sex relationship whether she might be pregnant — AND SHE MIGHT BE, BECAUSE OF A PREVIOUS MALE PARTNER. Plus cervical screening status and Gardasil

The first answer — say both HALVEs — 'YES — YOU CAN ABSOLUTELY GET A SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTION FROM SEX WITH A WOMAN. THE OVERALL RATE IS MUCH THE SAME AS FOR ANY OTHER WOMAN. WHAT'S DIFFERENT IS WHICH INFECTIONS WE SEE. We see more BACTERIAL VAGINOSIS and TRICHOMONIASIS. WARTS AND THRUSH are also common, because they pass SKIN-TO-SKIN. Chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV are less common — BUT THEY DO HAPPEN.' 'Yes you can' WITHOUT the pattern is incomplete; the pattern WITHOUT 'yes you can' sounds like reassurance

The second answer — name the dental dam and describe it — 'YES, THERE IS A BARRIER YOU CAN USE — IT'S JUST NOT SHAPED LIKE A CONDOM. It's called a DENTAL DAM: a thin sheet of latex you lay flat over the vulva or the back passage for oral sex, so there's no direct skin contact. THEY'RE HARDER TO FIND THAN CONDOMS, so here's the practical trick: TAKE A CONDOM, CUT OFF THE TIP, CUT UP ONE SIDE, AND OPEN IT OUT INTO A RECTANGLE. Same material, same job.' Say the technical term once and then her word — the examiner hears the correct term, SHE HEARS THE WORD SHE CAN SEARCH FOR IN A PHARMACY

Cervical screening does not change — the most commonly missed mark — Women who have sex with women are SIGNIFICANTLY LESS LIKELY TO BE UP TO DATE, partly because they are WRONGLY TOLD IT DOES NOT APPLY TO THEM. HPV IS SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED AND IT TRANSMITS SKIN-TO-SKIN. The programme applies to ANYONE WITH A CERVIX WHO HAS EVER BEEN SEXUALLY ACTIVE, REGARDLESS OF THE GENDER OF THEIR PARTNERS: AGES 25 TO 74, FIVE-YEARLY IF HPV IS NOT DETECTED, with an EXIT TEST BETWEEN 70 AND 74, and SELF-COLLECTION AVAILABLE VERIFY. Say it like this: 'in fact women in same-sex relationships are MORE LIKELY TO FALL BEHIND with it, because people wrongly assume it doesn't apply. IT DOES'
fails: ★ Minimising — 'the risk is very low, I wouldn't worry' — which is the commonest failure here and is the opposite of the truth
★ Never naming a barrier method, or answering 'condoms aren't really relevant for you' to the only question she actually asked
Never asking whether her previous partners were male or female, so the counselling floats free of her real risk
Cervical screening never raised in a 25-year-old who has never had one and believes it starts at thirty
No symptom screen separate from the risk assessment, treating her as a heterosexual woman with a different partner, or handing over a second pathology form for her partner
numbers: Cervical screening 25 to 74, five-yearly if HPV not detected, exit test at 70–74, self-collection available · up to 90% of women in this group have had male partners · routine screen is chlamydia and gonorrhoea NAAT plus HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B surface antigen · sample preference: clinician-collected endocervical, then self-collected vaginal, then first-pass urine · contact tracing if positive: chlamydia 6 months, gonorrhoea 2 months, trichomoniasis treat current partners VERIFY

SAY — 'There is a barrier, it's just not shaped like a condom. It's called a dental dam — a thin sheet of latex you lay flat over the area for oral sex. They're hard to buy, so: take a condom, cut the tip off, cut up one side, and open it into a rectangle.'

setting: Genuinely answer the question she asked — 'Why not just operate?' — rather than selling her the plan the team has already made. The salesman explains angioembolisation beautifully, lists its advantages, never seriously engages with surgery, and ends with 'So that's what we'll do' — she has been informed, not consulted. The technician delivers microcatheters and embolic agents and never mentions re-bleeding or ischaemia, which is impressive and useless. She has not refused anything and she is not difficult — she asked a reasonable question and is entitled to a real answer.
stem: A 60-year-old woman was admitted with bleeding from the back passage, found to be due to diverticular disease. She has been resuscitated and is now stable.
The surgical team have recommended angioembolisation. She is concerned, and is asking why she cannot simply have an operation to fix it. 8 minutes.

There is very little to get wrong medically and the patient is calm and stable — if you have a structure for explaining a procedure, this is among the most passable stations in the block. The marks are for patient-centred shared decision-making, not for knowing more about interventional radiology than she needs.
tasks: Take a short, relevant history
Explain the procedure that has been recommended
Address the patient's concerns
time: Half the station is explaining and discussing, and the history is genuinely short — it should take ninety seconds, not five minutes · task 3 is the one being marked hardest: she has a specific question and it deserves a specific answer, not a brochure

back.dx: LOWER GASTROINTESTINAL HAEMORRHAGE FROM DIVERTICULAR DISEASE, STABILISED, WITH ANGIOEMBOLISATION PLANNED. ANSWERING 'WHY NOT JUST OPERATE?' DIRECTLY: 'That's a completely reasonable question, and I want to give you a proper answer rather than just tell you what's been decided. SURGERY WOULD BE DEFINITIVE — we'd take out the section of bowel that's bleeding and that would be the end of it. The difficulty is that it's A MAJOR OPERATION, WE'D BE DOING IT URGENTLY RATHER THAN PLANNED, it means a general anaesthetic and POSSIBLY REMOVING PART OF YOUR BOWEL, and it carries a HIGHER RISK OF COMPLICATIONS AND A MUCH LONGER STAY. The reason the team has suggested the other approach first is that YOU'VE STABILISED. That gives us the chance to try something much less invasive, and if it works you avoid a major operation altogether.' AND THEN THE SENTENCE THAT USUALLY SETTLES IT: 'IF IT DOESN'T WORK, SURGERY IS STILL THERE — WE HAVEN'T LOST ANYTHING BY TRYING. THE CHOICE IS NOT INSTEAD OF SURGERY; IT IS BEFORE SURGERY.' THE FOUR OPTIONS WITH HONEST PROS AND CONS: ANGIOEMBOLISATION — much less invasive, NO ABDOMINAL INCISION, no general anaesthetic, lower overall complication risk, shorter stay, quicker recovery, NO STOMA; against that, RE-BLEEDING leading to surgery anyway, BOWEL ISCHAEMIA, contrast load on the kidneys, groin haematoma or false aneurysm, and radiation · SURGERY — definitive, the bleeding segment removed and THE WHOLE SPECIMEN GOES TO PATHOLOGY; against that, a major invasive operation DONE URGENTLY WHICH RAISES THE RISK FURTHER, general anaesthetic, may involve removing part of the bowel, higher risk of bleeding and infection, longer stay, POSSIBLE STOMA · COLONOSCOPY — DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC, examines the whole colon, no radiation or contrast, no incision; against that, it NEEDS BOWEL PREPARATION WHICH IS DIFFICULT IN ACUTE BLEEDING, the view may be obscured by blood, and there is a small perforation risk · CONSERVATIVE — no procedural risk at all and MOST BLEEDS STOP SPONTANEOUSLY; against that, it does not treat an ongoing bleed, there is a risk of sudden deterioration, and NO DIAGNOSIS OF THE BLEEDING POINT VERIFY. THE PRACTICALITIES SHE WILL ASK ABOUT: done AWAKE, UNDER LOCAL ANAESTHETIC AND SEDATION, NOT A GENERAL ANAESTHETIC · usually AN HOUR OR TWO · she will need to LIE FLAT FOR A FEW HOURS AFTERWARDS to protect the groin puncture · and it is done by an INTERVENTIONAL RADIOLOGIST, NOT THE SURGEON. WHAT ELSE CONSENT REQUIRES, BEYOND THE TWO HEADLINE RISKS: CONTRAST ALLERGY, asked specifically and asked again · RENAL FUNCTION, because of CONTRAST NEPHROPATHY, particularly if she has been hypotensive · METFORMIN, which may need withholding around contrast administration if she takes it · GROIN COMPLICATIONS — haematoma, false aneurysm, infection · RADIATION EXPOSURE · FAILURE TO IDENTIFY THE BLEEDING VESSEL, because IF IT HAS STOPPED BLEEDING AT THE MOMENT OF THE SCAN THERE MAY BE NOTHING TO EMBOLISE · and ANTICOAGULANTS, reversal or withholding. You will not cover all of these in eight minutes — NAMING CONTRAST ALLERGY, KIDNEY FUNCTION AND THE GROIN IS ENOUGH to show you know consent is more than two headline risks VERIFY. A NOTE ON SOURCES: THERE IS NO DEDICATED AUSTRALIAN GUIDELINE ON ANGIOEMBOLISATION FOR LOWER GI BLEEDING THAT MAPS NEATLY ONTO THIS STATION; the content draws on general surgical references, so CONFIRM ANY SPECIFIC FIGURE OR THRESHOLD BEFORE QUOTING IT. THE COMMUNICATION STRUCTURE, WHICH IS WHAT IS BEING MARKED, IS NOT IN DOUBT. HER HIDDEN AGENDA: HER SISTER HAD BOWEL SURGERY EIGHT YEARS AGO, ENDED UP WITH A COLOSTOMY BAG AND NEVER GOT OVER IT — SHE IS FRIGHTENED OF A BAG, NOT OF SURGERY. She says so only if asked WHAT SPECIFICALLY WORRIES HER ABOUT AN OPERATION, or what her preferences are. AND THE BRIEFED QUESTION AT ABOUT SIX MINUTES: 'SO WHICH SHOULD I DO?' — DO NOT ANSWER IT WITH A DECISION. Answer it with the MISSING INFORMATION and then hand it back: candidates who say 'I'd have the embolisation' HAVE TAKEN THE DECISION OFF HER, and she accepts it flatly and disengages, which is a scored failure of shared decision-making. THE CLOSE: offer the SURGEON to come and go through it before anything is decided · offer FAMILY INVOLVEMENT, since her husband is better at remembering things · WRITTEN INFORMATION · STOP THE IBUPROFEN AND REVIEW THE ASPIRIN, because both are contributing · and TEACH-BACK.
plan: 'How are you feeling now? Is the bleeding settling?' — then signpost, then ask the concerns question.
SHE RAISES THE SURGERY. Acknowledge it as reasonable and PARK IT EXPLICITLY: a few questions first, then what's wrong, then what's suggested and why, then back to her question.
THE BLEED: onset, volume, colour, and ASK ABOUT PAIN — painless is the diagnostic point. Then dizziness and faintness.
RED FLAGS AND BOWEL SCREENING HISTORY, then ANTICOAGULANTS, ANTIPLATELETS AND NSAIDs, then CONTRAST ALLERGY, then renal and cardiac history, then what the surgeon has already told her.
EXPLAIN DIVERTICULOSIS: the pouches, why they bleed, WHY IT WAS PAINLESS, and that it is NOT diverticulitis.
STEP ONE OF THE PROCEDURE: CT ANGIOGRAPHY TO FIND THE VESSEL — you cannot block what you have not found.
THE PROCEDURE IN PLAIN WORDS: groin, fine tube, finer tubes, coil or absorbable gel. Then AWAKE WITH SEDATION, an hour or two, lie flat afterwards.
PROS OF EMBOLISATION — then, in the same breath, THE TWO COMPLICATIONS: RE-BLEEDING and BOWEL ISCHAEMIA, each with why it is uncommon.
ANSWER HER QUESTION PROPERLY: surgery explained with its own real pros and cons, and the reasoning for trying the less invasive option first.
'SO WHICH SHOULD I DO?' — give the MISSING INFORMATION: most settle spontaneously, and COLONOSCOPY IS A GENUINE OPTION that also looks at the whole colon. Then hand the decision back.
THE KILLER LINE: trying the small one first does not close off the big one. Then the surgeon, the husband, written information, and the NSAID and aspirin review.
TEACH-BACK: 'could you tell me in your own words what you'd say to him about the plan?'

ask: THE OPENING: 'How are you feeling now?' · 'Do you have any concerns you'd like me to address?' · AND WHEN SHE ASKS WHY NOT SURGERY: 'That's a completely reasonable question and I'm going to answer it properly. Let me ask you a few things first so I understand your situation.'

THE PROCEDURE, IN HER WORDS: 'We can't block something we haven't found.' · 'A small cut in your groin, and a fine tube into the artery — the same route used for heart angiograms.' · 'We block the bleeding vessel off with a gel or a small metal coil.' · 'Awake, with local anaesthetic and some sedation, so you'd be drowsy and comfortable but not under a general anaesthetic.'

THE TWO SENTENCES THAT CARRY THE STATION: 'MY JOB HERE ISN'T TO TALK YOU INTO ANYTHING. It's to make sure you understand both options properly, and then WE DECIDE TOGETHER — and I'll ask the surgeon to come and talk it through with you as well.' AND: 'CHOOSING THE LESS INVASIVE OPTION FIRST DOESN'T CLOSE OFF SURGERY. If it doesn't work, the operation is still there. WE HAVEN'T LOST ANYTHING BY TRYING.'
pefe: SHE IS STABLE AND THE EXAMINATION IS NOT THE TASK — THE FINDINGS ARE HER ACCOUNT: bleeding began yesterday evening, BRIGHT RED, ENOUGH TO FILL THE BOWL TWICE · NO PAIN WHATSOEVER, which is what frightened her most and is the diagnostic point · DIZZY ON STANDING, which is when the ambulance was called · fluids and blood overnight, AND TODAY IT HAS SLOWED RIGHT DOWN · no weight loss, normal bowel habit, BOWEL SCREENING TEST NEGATIVE TWO YEARS AGO.

The medication answer is the one that changes management and she does not volunteer it: she takes aspirin, and has been taking ibuprofen most days for her knee. No allergies, never reacted to scan dye, no kidney or heart problems, blood pressure tablet only. Nobody has ever mentioned pouches or diverticular disease to her.

THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: never asked what concerned her · never named re-bleeding or bowel ischaemia · dismissed surgery without explaining it · made the decision for her · never asked about anticoagulants or contrast allergy.

Open with 'How are you feeling now?' — and then ask the concerns question — Normally a weak opener, but AFTER AN ACUTE EVENT IT IS EXACTLY RIGHT, because something has just happened to her and she has something to say about it. THEN: 'I'm going to explain the procedure the surgeon has recommended, BUT I'D LIKE TO ASK YOU A FEW QUESTIONS FIRST. AND BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — DO YOU HAVE ANY CONCERNS YOU'D LIKE ME TO ADDRESS?' THAT IS WHERE SHE RAISES THE SURGERY, AT ABOUT FORTY SECONDS. IF YOU DO NOT ASK, SHE DOES NOT RAISE IT UNTIL SIX MINUTES AND YOU WILL HAVE ANSWERED A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED

The ninety-second history, and the three questions that discriminate — THE BLEED — when, how much, FRESH RED OR DARK, mixed with stool or separate, ANY PAIN, dizziness or faintness. RED FLAGS — weight loss, change in bowel habit, previous bleeding, BOWEL SCREENING HISTORY, because COLORECTAL CANCER MUST NOT BE FORGOTTEN AT 60 SIMPLY BECAUSE A DIAGNOSIS HAS ALREADY BEEN MADE FOR YOU. AND THE THREE THAT EARN MARKS: ANTICOAGULANTS, ANTIPLATELETS AND NSAIDs, which cause it, worsen it and change the management · ANY ALLERGY TO CONTRAST OR IODINE, because SHE IS ABOUT TO BE GIVEN INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST, TWICE · AND RENAL AND CARDIAC HISTORY. Then: 'WHAT HAS THE SURGEON TOLD YOU SO FAR?'

Explain the problem before the procedure, or the procedure is meaningless — 'In the wall of the bowel there are naturally WEAKER POINTS WHERE BLOOD VESSELS PASS THROUGH. Over the years, SMALL POUCHES CAN PUSH OUT through those weak spots. It's very common as people get older, and most of the time it causes no trouble at all.' THEN: 'SMALL BLOOD VESSELS RUN RIGHT OVER THOSE POUCHES. Occasionally one WEARS THROUGH AND STARTS BLEEDING — and that's why there was no pain.' TWO SMALL THINGS THAT EARN MARKS: DISTINGUISH DIVERTICULOSIS FROM DIVERTICULITIS, which patients and families confuse constantly · AND NAME THE PAINLESSNESS AS EXPECTED: 'the fact that it didn't hurt is TYPICAL of this kind of bleeding, and it's A POINT IN FAVOUR OF THE DIAGNOSIS RATHER THAN AGAINST IT'

The procedure in six steps — and step one is the one people omit — 'BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, WE NEED TO FIND EXACTLY WHICH BLOOD VESSEL IS BLEEDING. We do that with a CT ANGIOGRAM — a scan with dye put into your bloodstream, which shows the blood vessels up clearly.' THE SURGEON CANNOT BLOCK A VESSEL THAT HAS NOT BEEN FOUND. THEN: 'a small cut in your GROIN and a fine tube into the artery — THE SAME ROUTE USED FOR HEART ANGIOGRAMS' (the groin because the mesenteric arteries are much closer to it) · 'we SWAP TO MUCH FINER TUBES, because the vessel that's bleeding is very small' · 'when we reach it we BLOCK IT OFF — either with A GEL THE BODY ABSORBS over time, or with A TINY METAL COIL.' NOT 'MESENTERIC', NOT 'EMBOLIC AGENT', NOT 'VASOPRESSOR'

The two complications she must be told — name the risk, then why it is uncommon — RE-BLEEDING: 'it can bleed again afterwards. If that happens, WE'RE BACK WHERE WE STARTED AND YOU'D THEN NEED THE OPERATION. So this isn't guaranteed to be the end of it.' BOWEL ISCHAEMIA: 'by blocking a blood vessel we're DELIBERATELY CUTTING OFF THE SUPPLY to a small part of the bowel. Occasionally that leaves that piece without enough blood. THE BOWEL HAS SEVERAL OVERLAPPING BLOOD SUPPLIES, and when the procedure is done carefully and only one small vessel is blocked, WE DON'T EXPECT IT — but it is a real risk and you should know about it.' NEVER THE RISK ALONE. Both unnamed is an AUTOMATIC FAIL — this is consent, not marketing

Correction — this is not a straight choice between two things — The source presents surgery and angioembolisation as the only two options. THAT IS A FALSE BINARY, AND IT MATTERS BECAUSE SHE IS BEING ASKED TO CHOOSE. CONSERVATIVE: MOST DIVERTICULAR BLEEDS STOP ON THEIR OWN, she is already stable, and supportive care with correction of anaemia and coagulopathy and stopping contributing drugs IS A LEGITIMATE POSITION. COLONOSCOPY WITH ENDOSCOPIC HAEMOSTASIS — clips, adrenaline injection or thermal coagulation applied directly, WITH THE DIAGNOSTIC ADVANTAGE OF LOOKING AT THE WHOLE COLON, WHICH ANGIOGRAPHY DOES NOT, AND AT 60 THAT MATTERS VERIFY. Examiner challenge 'the surgeon has decided on embolisation, why are you discussing anything else?' → 'I'd SUPPORT THE TEAM'S RECOMMENDATION AND I'M NOT UNDERMINING IT. But she's asked me directly why she can't have surgery, and I don't think I can answer that honestly by PRETENDING THERE ARE ONLY TWO OPTIONS'
fails: ★ The concerns question never asked, so her actual question stays buried until six minutes and you have answered one nobody asked
★ Re-bleeding or bowel ischaemia never named — this is consent, not marketing, and both must be stated with why they are uncommon
Surgery dismissed rather than explained, or a false binary presented when most bleeds settle and colonoscopy is a genuine option
The decision taken for her — 'so that's what we'll do', or answering 'which should I do?' with a recommendation instead of the missing information
CT angiography omitted as step one, jargon used instead of plain words, or no question about anticoagulants, NSAIDs and contrast allergy before a procedure that uses contrast twice
numbers: Diverticular bleeding is characteristically painless, often brisk and bright red · step 1 is CT angiography to localise the vessel · access is the femoral artery via the groin · occlusion with absorbable gel or coils, occasionally vasopressin · awake with local anaesthetic and sedation, usually an hour or two, lying flat for a few hours afterwards · done by an interventional radiologist VERIFY

Ask about: aspirin, anticoagulants and NSAIDs · contrast or iodine allergy, because she receives contrast twice · renal function and contrast nephropathy · metformin around contrast · and do not forget colorectal cancer red flags at 60 · there is no dedicated Australian guideline mapping onto this station, so confirm any figure or threshold before quoting it

FAIL — AUTO-FAIL: never naming re-bleeding or bowel ischaemia — this is consent, not marketing; name each risk, then say why it is uncommon

FAIL — AUTO-FAIL: dismissing surgery rather than explaining it — she asked about it, so give it real pros and cons; and most bleeds settle spontaneously, with colonoscopy a genuine third option, so do not present a false binary

setting: A refusal handled well is a pass; an argument won is not. The clinical content is easy — the role-player becomes more resistant the harder she is pushed. If you lecture, interrupt, or repeat a point more firmly, she gets cooler and shorter with each exchange and ends by declining. If you ask permission before informing, validate her, and answer the specific claim, she softens steadily and ends by agreeing.
stem: General practice, South Australia. The 12-month immunisations are due. Jack Nowak, 12 months, is brought by his mother Ella — well, thriving, afebrile, fully vaccinated to date.
The mother is refusing vaccination today. A friend has told her vaccines are harmful, and she has read that MMR causes autism. 8 minutes.

She is not anti-vaccine — she has completed the schedule so far and would be offended by the label. The three AUTOMATIC FAILS: explaining before eliciting · using payments or childcare as leverage · pushing after a clear refusal.
tasks: Take a history (about 2 minutes)
Counsel the mother about her concerns
Negotiate a plan
time: Two minutes of history, then the counselling, then the negotiation · the safety screen is ninety seconds and it is real, not ritual, because MMR is a live vaccine · protect time for the delayed rash warning and the review appointment, which are the two things that keep the family

back.dx: VACCINE HESITANCY AT THE 12-MONTH MMR IN A WELL, THRIVING, FULLY VACCINATED CHILD — AND THE STATION IS THE RELATIONSHIP, NOT THE EVIDENCE. TASK 3, THE NEGOTIATION: 'So where does that leave you? I'M NOT GOING TO PUSH YOU INTO ANYTHING — IT'S YOUR DECISION AND YOU KNOW JACK BETTER THAN I DO. What I'd suggest is this: I'll give you the WRITTEN INFORMATION, from the immunisation handbook and the children's hospital — NEITHER OF THEM IS SELLING ANYTHING. Have a read, talk to Jack's dad, and COME BACK AND SEE ME IN A FORTNIGHT EITHER WAY. If you'd rather do one vaccine today and think about the rest, or space them out, we can talk about that too. AND IF THE ANSWER STAYS NO, THAT'S ALRIGHT — IT WON'T CHANGE HOW WE LOOK AFTER HIM.' IF SHE DECLINES, STOP: document, provide information, arrange review, keep the relationship. DO NOT REACH FOR FAMILY PAYMENTS OR CHILDCARE RULES TO CLOSE THE DEAL — raised before she asks about consequences, she says 'IS THAT A THREAT?' and declines; raised factually only after she asks, it is fine. AND NEVER IMPLY SHE IS A BAD MOTHER. 'ARE YOU ABSOLUTELY SURE?' IS ONE PUSH TOO MANY, AND SO IS A PARTING STATISTIC. THE VARIANTS, SCRIPTED: VERSION B, THE FEBRILE CONVULSION FEAR AT THE 18-MONTH MMRV — 'that must have been horrifying to watch, and it makes complete sense that it's stayed with you. THE AUSTRALIAN SCHEDULE IS BUILT AROUND EXACTLY THAT RISK: giving the CHICKENPOX COMPONENT TOGETHER WITH THE MEASLES VACCINE AS A FIRST DOSE IN A YOUNG CHILD CARRIES A SMALL EXTRA CHANCE OF A FEVER FIT — so we deliberately give MMR ON ITS OWN AT TWELVE MONTHS, and the combined one ONLY AT EIGHTEEN MONTHS, when that risk has fallen. IT ISN'T AN ACCIDENT; IT'S DESIGNED THAT WAY.' VERSION C, THE REFUSAL HELD — 'that's your decision, and I respect it, and IT WON'T CHANGE ANYTHING ABOUT HOW WE LOOK AFTER JACK HERE. Three small things: the written information so it's there if you want it · a note in his record THAT WE'VE HAD A PROPER DISCUSSION, SO YOU DON'T GET THE SAME CONVERSATION FROM EVERY DOCTOR YOU SEE · and I'd like to see you both in a fortnight anyway for his check — NOT TO HAVE ANOTHER GO AT YOU, JUST SO THE DOOR STAYS OPEN. Is there anything I could have explained better today?' VERSION D, THE HOUSEHOLD IMMUNOSUPPRESSION MYTH — 'it's a really sensible question and the answer surprises most people: IT'S THE OTHER WAY ROUND. THE MEASLES VACCINE VIRUS ISN'T PASSED FROM A VACCINATED CHILD TO ANYONE ELSE, so Jack having it is NO RISK AT ALL to your mum. WHAT WOULD BE A RISK TO HER IS JACK CATCHING REAL MEASLES AND BRINGING IT HOME, because someone recovering from chemotherapy is exactly who it hurts most. SO VACCINATING JACK IS ONE OF THE WAYS WE PROTECT HER.' And while you are there, ask whether the grandmother has had her flu and COVID vaccines and knows about shingles. VERSION E, POST-EXPOSURE — 'if Jack were ever in contact with a confirmed case, RING US THE SAME DAY, THIS IS TIME-CRITICAL. For a child who can have it, AN MMR DOSE WITHIN 72 HOURS of exposure can prevent or reduce the illness. Beyond that window, or for a child who cannot have a live vaccine, there's an ANTIBODY INJECTION THAT WORKS UP TO ABOUT SIX DAYS. MEASLES IS ALSO IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIABLE, so everyone else exposed can be contacted — that's not bureaucracy, it's how outbreaks get stopped.' THE CONSULTATION MAP: greet both → thank her for coming → elicit the specific belief and its source → establish this is selective → screen → correct the household myth → ask permission → what measles does, with numbers → herd immunity framed around Jack → the 1998 paper and the evidence since → why the belief persists → honest side effects including the day 7–10 rash → the two-number comparison → negotiate without pressing → written information → review in a fortnight either way → observe 15 minutes → AIR → book MMRV at 18 months → summarise → teach-back.
plan: GREET BOTH MOTHER AND BABY, acknowledge the refusal, and THANK HER FOR COMING IN ANYWAY.
ELICIT BEFORE EXPLAINING: what have you heard, and what worries you most? Then WHERE DID YOU COME ACROSS IT, and is it this vaccine or all of them.
NAME IT BACK — he has had everything else, so this is one specific worry. ASK ABOUT FAMILY, which is where the sister's son surfaces.
THE SAFETY SCREEN: previous reactions · prematurity and conditions · IMMUNOCOMPROMISE AND STEROIDS · IMMUNOGLOBULIN OR BLOOD PRODUCTS · well today · WHO IS AT HOME.
CORRECT THE HOUSEHOLD MYTH AND REFRAME IT — vaccinating Jack is one of the ways you protect his grandmother.
ASK PERMISSION, THEN MEASLES WITH NUMBERS: 1 in 10 complications · ~1 in 1,000 encephalitis · the rare fatal late condition · and why it still reaches Australia.
THE 1998 PAPER: flawed, retracted, author struck off · the scale of the evidence since · AND WHY THE BELIEF PERSISTS, without contempt.
HONEST SIDE EFFECTS INCLUDING THE DAY 7–10 FEVER AND RASH, then anaphylaxis and the fifteen minutes, then THE TWO-NUMBER COMPARISON.
NEGOTIATE WITHOUT PRESSING: written information · talk to Jack's dad · COME BACK IN A FORTNIGHT EITHER WAY · and if the answer stays no, that is alright.
IF SHE AGREES: one injection, fifteen minutes together, the information sheet, AIR, and BOOK THE 18-MONTH MMRV with the reason it is given later.
SUMMARISE AND TEACH-BACK: 'what will you tell Jack's dad tonight?'

ask: THE OPENING SET: 'Thank you for coming in anyway and being straight with me — I'd much rather we talked.' · 'BEFORE I SAY ANYTHING AT ALL — can you tell me what you've heard, and what worries you most?' · 'Where did you come across it?' · 'Is it this vaccine specifically, or vaccines in general?' · 'YOU'VE BEEN GETTING HIM PROTECTED ALL ALONG — so this isn't you being against vaccines.'

THE EVIDENCE SET: 'Would it help if I went through what we know?' · 'About one in ten children who catch measles gets a complication.' · 'Around one in a thousand gets inflammation of the brain.' · 'That idea comes from one small paper from 1998 that was retracted, and its author was struck off.' · 'AUTISM OFTEN BECOMES NOTICEABLE AT ABOUT THE AGE CHILDREN GET THIS VACCINE — so joining the two up is a completely reasonable thing for a parent to think.'

THE CLOSING SET: 'I'd rather be straight with you about side effects than gloss over them.' · 'Some children get a mild fever and rash about seven to ten days later — THAT'S EXPECTED, IT ISN'T MEASLES, AND IT ISN'T CATCHING.' · 'I'm not going to push you — it's your decision and you know Jack better than I do.' · 'COME BACK AND SEE ME IN A FORTNIGHT EITHER WAY. IF THE ANSWER STAYS NO, THAT'S ALRIGHT.'
pefe: NO EXAMINATION — THE SCREEN IS THE ASSESSMENT, AND WITH A LIVE VACCINE IT IS REAL: previous vaccine reactions (grizzly and warm after the six-month needles, nothing more) · BORN AT TERM, no medical conditions · NO IMMUNE PROBLEMS AND NO STEROIDS · NO IMMUNOGLOBULIN OR BLOOD PRODUCTS · WELL TODAY, no fever · AND THE HOUSEHOLD, which is where the grandmother's chemotherapy comes out — GIVEN ONLY IF YOU ASK WHO IS AT HOME.

THE OTHER TWO THINGS SHE HOLDS BACK: THE AUTISM CONCERN, given only when asked what worries her · AND THE SISTER'S SON, given only if asked about family or asked a second time what is really behind it. IF YOU NEVER ASK, SHE NEVER VOLUNTEERS, AND SHE MARKS YOU DOWN. She will also ask 'HOW CAN THEY BE SURE?' at least once, to see whether you get irritated.

THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: explaining before ever asking what she was worried about · using childcare or payments as leverage before she asked · and continuing to push after she declines in version C.

Open by thanking her for coming, not for agreeing — 'I understand you'd rather not go ahead with the immunisations today. THANK YOU FOR COMING IN ANYWAY AND BEING STRAIGHT WITH ME ABOUT IT — a lot of people just cancel, and I'd much rather we talked. BEFORE I SAY ANYTHING AT ALL: can you tell me what you've heard, and what worries you most?' She opens braced — 'I THOUGHT YOU'D BE ANNOYED WITH ME' — and watches what you do with it. Opening 'so why don't you want to vaccinate?' sounds like an accusation. AND GREET THE BABY: candidates who talk over Jack for eight minutes lose easy marks

Name back the fact that this is selective, not blanket — 'Where did you come across it? … Is it THIS VACCINE SPECIFICALLY, or vaccines in general?' She has had everything else done on time. 'YOU'VE BEEN GETTING HIM PROTECTED ALL ALONG, SO THIS ISN'T YOU BEING AGAINST VACCINES — IT'S ONE SPECIFIC WORRY.' THAT SENTENCE IS WORTH MORE THAN ANY STATISTIC, and answering a generic anti-vaccine speech she never made is the commonest early error. HER REAL REASON COMES OUT ONLY IF YOU ASK ABOUT FAMILY OR WHAT SPECIFICALLY WORRIES HER: her sister's son was diagnosed with autism at two, shortly after his MMR

The ninety-second screen — and the one answer people get wrong — Previous vaccine reaction · born on time and any medical conditions · ANYTHING AFFECTING HIS IMMUNE SYSTEM, OR STEROID MEDICINES · BLOOD TRANSFUSION OR IMMUNOGLOBULIN · well today, any fever · AND IS ANYONE AT HOME PREGNANT OR IMMUNOSUPPRESSED. Her mother finished chemotherapy in March and has Jack twice a week — and A HOUSEHOLD MEMBER WHO IS IMMUNOSUPPRESSED IS NOT A REASON TO WITHHOLD MMR. IF YOU HESITATE HERE YOU HAVE INVENTED A CONTRAINDICATION

Ask permission, then say what measles actually does — 'WOULD IT HELP IF I WENT THROUGH WHAT WE KNOW?' — two seconds, and it is the difference between a conversation and a lecture, AND IT IS A SCORED BEHAVIOUR. 'Measles gets thought of as a rash and a fever, and for most children that's how it goes. BUT IT IS ONE OF THE MOST CONTAGIOUS INFECTIONS THERE IS, and ABOUT ONE IN TEN CHILDREN WHO CATCH IT GETS A COMPLICATION — usually a chest or ear infection. AROUND ONE IN A THOUSAND GETS INFLAMMATION OF THE BRAIN, which can cause permanent damage. And very rarely, years later, it causes A DEGENERATIVE BRAIN CONDITION THAT IS ALWAYS FATAL.' Then herd immunity framed around Jack

The retraction script — the station, learned verbatim — 'That idea comes from ONE SMALL PAPER PUBLISHED IN 1998. It was investigated, FOUND TO BE SERIOUSLY FLAWED, FORMALLY RETRACTED BY THE JOURNAL, and the doctor who wrote it WAS STRUCK OFF THE MEDICAL REGISTER. Since then it's been studied in HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF CHILDREN ACROSS SEVERAL COUNTRIES, vaccinated compared with unvaccinated. NO LINK HAS BEEN FOUND.' THEN THE PART THAT DOES THE WORK: 'the reason this idea has stuck around ISN'T THAT PARENTS ARE GULLIBLE. AUTISM OFTEN BECOMES NOTICEABLE AT AROUND THE SAME AGE CHILDREN GET THIS VACCINE. So if you watch your child change in the months after a needle, OF COURSE YOU JOIN THE TWO TOGETHER — that's a completely reasonable thing for a parent to think.' ATTACK THE CLAIM, PROTECT THE PERSON — mock the article, the friend or the Facebook group and she says 'SO YOU THINK I'M STUPID' and closes down for the rest of the station

Honest side effects, and the delayed rash that keeps the family — 'I'D RATHER BE STRAIGHT WITH YOU ABOUT SIDE EFFECTS THAN GLOSS OVER THEM.' Common: a sore red leg and being unsettled a day or two. THEN THE ONE THAT MATTERS: 'because this vaccine contains a WEAKENED LIVE VIRUS, some children get a MILD FEVER AND A RASH ABOUT SEVEN TO TEN DAYS AFTERWARDS. That's expected, IT ISN'T MEASLES, AND IT ISN'T CATCHING — but I'd rather you knew now than got a fright next week.' Then anaphylaxis and the fifteen-minute wait. THEN THE TWO-NUMBER COMPARISON: ABOUT ONE IN A THOUSAND WITH MEASLES ITSELF, AGAINST SOMETHING LIKE ONE IN A MILLION AFTER THE VACCINE. CLAIMING THERE ARE NO SIDE EFFECTS DESTROYS YOUR CREDIBILITY ON EVERYTHING ELSE

numbers: MMR at 12 months, MMRV at 18 months — both live attenuated, 0.5 mL, nip-funded · measles complications ~1 in 10 · measles encephalitis ~1 in 1,000 · vaccine encephalitis ~1 in a million with causation unestablished · anaphylaxis ~1 in a million · expected fever and rash at 7–10 days · herd immunity threshold ~95% · the wakefield paper 1998, retracted 2010

Contraindications: anaphylaxis to a previous dose or component · significant immunocompromise · pregnancy, and avoid pregnancy for 28 days after · high-dose systemic steroids, roughly ≥20 mg/day prednisolone or ≥2 mg/kg/day for ≥14 days, deferring 1 month after stopping VERIFY · not contraindications: egg allergy · household immunosuppression or pregnancy · minor illness without fever · post-exposure MMR within 72 hours or immunoglobulin within 6 days · observe 15 minutes · measles is immediately notifiable · air reporting mandatory · catch-up free at any age

This is a three-way consultation about a 13-year-old's body, and speaking over her for eight minutes is a scored communication failure regardless of how good the content is.
stem: General practice, South Australia. Amelia hart, 13, is brought in by her mother Fiona. Amelia is well and present in the room throughout.
Amelia has been offered the Gardasil vaccine at school. Her mother wants to discuss it before signing the consent form. 8 minutes.

The concern, asked outright in the first ninety seconds and in front of Amelia: 'Will this encourage her to become sexually active sooner?' She has been rehearsing it in the car, and she watches your face.
The mother is not anti-vaccine — Amelia is fully immunised and she had her own flu shot last year. She would be offended to be treated as an anti-vaxxer.
tasks: Counsel the mother about the HPV vaccine
Address her concerns
Agree a plan
time: Park the loaded question, screen, then answer it straight — and close with the screening line · put cervical screening in the closing summary every single time, even if you are running out of time, because it is the most frequently omitted scored item in the station

back.dx: HPV VACCINATION COUNSELLING IN A WELL 13-YEAR-OLD, WITH A LOADED PARENTAL QUESTION ASKED IN FRONT OF HER. PRACTICALITIES: FOR A HEALTHY YOUNG PERSON AGED NINE TO TWENTY-FIVE IT IS A SINGLE DOSE — one injection and the course is done — AND IT IS FREE, whether at school or at the practice. QUOTING THE OLD THREE-DOSE SCHEDULE DATES YOU BADLY, and the mother is briefed to say 'THE SCHOOL LETTER SAID ONE' and watch whether you correct yourself. SIDE EFFECTS: mostly a sore red arm for a day or two, sometimes a headache · the serious one is ANAPHYLAXIS, which is why you watch fifteen minutes · AND VASOVAGAL SYNCOPE, which is REALLY COMMON IN TEENAGERS WITH NEEDLES, HARMLESS IN ITSELF BUT PEOPLE GET HURT FALLING — so give it SEATED OR LYING DOWN. THEN THE OFFER THAT COSTS NOTHING AND EARNS A MARK: 'IF YOU'D RATHER HAVE IT HERE THAN IN THE SCHOOL HALL WITH EVERYONE WATCHING, THAT'S COMPLETELY FINE — a lot of people prefer that', which is exactly what Amelia wants and will ask for. CONSENT AND CHOICE: give both the written information — the immunisation handbook and Cancer Council material, NEITHER OF WHICH IS SELLING ANYTHING · YOU DON'T HAVE TO SIGN ANYTHING TODAY, and producing the consent form and a pen is the trap · and SIGNPOST CONFIDENTIAL ACCESS: 'AMELIA — if you'd ever like to talk to a doctor on your own, without Mum, THAT'S SOMETHING YOU'RE ALLOWED TO DO. I just want you to know that' — a strong communication mark, and one sentence. THE VARIANTS, SCRIPTED: VERSION B, 'WHY ARE BOYS GETTING IT?' — 'it used to be given only to girls, and THAT CHANGED IN 2013 for two good reasons. HPV CAUSES CANCERS IN MEN TOO — of the anus, the penis, and increasingly OF THE THROAT AND TONSILS, WHICH ARE RISING IN MEN. It also causes most genital warts. And VACCINATING BOTH SEXES REDUCES HOW MUCH THE VIRUS CIRCULATES AT ALL, which protects everyone. SO IT ISN'T A COURTESY TO GIRLS; IT'S A CANCER VACCINE FOR HIM.' VERSION C, THE MOTHER REFUSES AND A 15-YEAR-OLD WANTS IT — 'I can hear you want different things, and I'M NOT GOING TO TAKE SIDES IN THE ROOM. In South Australia, A YOUNG PERSON OF SIXTEEN OR OVER CAN CONSENT TO THEIR OWN TREATMENT. UNDER SIXTEEN, it is possible for a young person to consent themselves IF THE DOCTOR — WITH A SECOND DOCTOR'S WRITTEN OPINION — IS SATISFIED THEY FULLY UNDERSTAND WHAT IS INVOLVED AND THAT IT IS IN THEIR INTEREST. So it isn't automatic, and IT ISN'T SOMETHING I'D DECIDE ALONE IN AN EIGHT-MINUTE APPOINTMENT. What I'd much rather do is understand what's stopping you.' THE SA PROVISION COMES FROM THE CONSENT TO MEDICAL TREATMENT AND PALLIATIVE CARE ACT 1995 AND DIFFERS FROM THE COMMON-LAW MATURE-MINOR TEST USED IN MOST OTHER STATES — CONFIRM THE CURRENT WORDING, AND IN THE EXAM ADD THAT YOU WOULD SEEK SENIOR OR MEDICO-LEGAL ADVICE RATHER THAN PROCEEDING UNILATERALLY, WHICH IS SAFER AND SCORES BETTER THAN QUOTING A STATUTE YOU ARE NOT CERTAIN OF VERIFY. VERSION D, 'SHE'S ALREADY GOT A BOYFRIEND, IS IT TOO LATE?' — 'not at all, and I'm glad you asked rather than assuming. EVEN IF SOMEONE HAS ALREADY BEEN EXPOSED TO ONE TYPE, THE VACCINE STILL PROTECTS AGAINST THE OTHER EIGHT, and most people who've been exposed have met only one. IT WON'T CLEAR AN INFECTION THAT'S ALREADY THERE — that's the one thing it can't do — but it will protect against what she hasn't met yet. BEST BEFORE ANY EXPOSURE, STILL WORTHWHILE AFTER. There's no point at which we'd say don't bother.' VERSION E, THE IMMUNOCOMPROMISED ADOLESCENT AFTER TRANSPLANT — 'for live vaccines we'd need to be very careful. BUT THIS ONE CONTAINS NO LIVE VIRUS AND NO VIRAL GENETIC MATERIAL AT ALL — just protein particles that look like the outside of the virus. So it's safe for him, and HE'S SOMEONE WE PARTICULARLY WANT PROTECTED, because HPV-RELATED DISEASE IS MORE COMMON AND MORE AGGRESSIVE WHEN THE IMMUNE SYSTEM IS SUPPRESSED. The one difference is the schedule: THREE DOSES AT ZERO, TWO AND SIX MONTHS instead of a single dose. I'd also let his transplant team know.' THE CONSULTATION MAP: greet both → ask Amelia's permission → elicit the mother's concern → park the loaded question and promise to return → screen including yeast and fainting → ask permission to explain → what HPV is and the nine types → the cancers in both sexes → return to the question and answer it with evidence → reframe as immunity before exposure → preserve the parental role → single dose, free → side effects → syncope and seated administration → offer the practice instead of school → CERVICAL SCREENING FROM 25, FIVE-YEARLY → written information → no pressure to sign → signpost confidential access → summarise → teach-back.
plan: GREET BOTH BY NAME AND ASK AMELIA'S PERMISSION — it's her body, and you want to hear what she thinks.
ELICIT THE MOTHER'S CONCERN BEFORE EXPLAINING ANYTHING. She asks the loaded question here, in front of Amelia.
PARK IT CALMLY AND PROMISE TO RETURN — a couple of safety questions first, then straight back to it.
THE SCREEN: previous reactions · ALLERGIES INCLUDING YEAST SPECIFICALLY · conditions, immune status, medications · bleeding problems · FAINTING, ASKED OF AMELIA · well today.
ASK PERMISSION, THEN WHAT HPV IS: very common, usually cleared, a few types don't — and the cancers named, IN BOTH SEXES. Check in with Amelia.
BACK TO THE QUESTION, ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE: no difference between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups in any of the three measures.
THE REFRAME: immunity before exposure, the seatbelt line — AND PRESERVE HER ROLE in the conversations about relationships and consent.
PRACTICALITIES: SINGLE DOSE FOR 9–25, FREE · sore arm, headache · anaphylaxis and fifteen minutes · SYNCOPE AND SEATED ADMINISTRATION · and offer the practice instead of the school hall.
THE SCREENING LINE, SAID TO AMELIA: FIRST CERVICAL SCREENING TEST AT 25, THEN EVERY FIVE YEARS — 'if you remember one thing from today, make it that.'
Written information, no pressure to sign today, and signpost confidential access for Amelia.
SUMMARISE AND TEACH-BACK — and let Amelia give it back, not her mother.

ask: THE THREE-WAY OPENING: 'It's your body, so I'd like to hear what you think as well, not just what Mum thinks.' · 'THAT'S A REALLY IMPORTANT QUESTION AND I WANT TO ANSWER IT PROPERLY — can I ask a couple of safety questions first, then come straight back to it?' · 'Any allergies at all — AND SPECIFICALLY, ANY PROBLEM WITH YEAST?' · 'Have you ever fainted with a needle or a blood test?'

THE ANSWER: 'THE ANSWER IS NO — AND THAT'S BEEN STUDIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.' · 'There's no difference in when young people become sexually active, how many partners they have, or their rates of other infections.' · 'THE VACCINE ONLY WORKS IF HER IMMUNE SYSTEM MEETS IT BEFORE THE VIRUS DOES. IT'S LIKE A SEATBELT — YOU PUT IT ON BEFORE THE JOURNEY.' · 'This doesn't replace anything you'd want to say to her about relationships and consent. THOSE CONVERSATIONS ARE YOURS.'

THE CLOSING SET: 'For a healthy young person aged nine to twenty-five, it's a SINGLE DOSE, and it's FREE.' · 'Fainting is common in teenagers with needles — so we'd do it sitting or lying down and keep her fifteen minutes.' · 'HAVING THIS VACCINE DOES NOT MEAN YOU CAN SKIP CERVICAL SCREENING — FIRST TEST AT TWENTY-FIVE, THEN EVERY FIVE YEARS.' · 'If you'd ever like to see a doctor on your own, that's something you're allowed to do.'
pefe: NO EXAMINATION — THE SCREEN IS THE ASSESSMENT: no previous vaccine reaction · NO ALLERGIES, INCLUDING NO YEAST ALLERGY · healthy, no conditions, no medications, no immune problems · no bleeding disorder or blood thinners · WELL TODAY · AND THE ONE PIECE OF HIDDEN INFORMATION AMELIA HOLDS: SHE WENT LIGHT-HEADED AND CLAMMY DURING A BLOOD TEST LAST YEAR, which she gives only if asked about fainting or needles — and having given it, SHE WILL ALSO SAY SHE WOULD RATHER HAVE THE INJECTION AT THE SURGERY THAN IN THE SCHOOL HALL.

The mother's hidden assumption is the other half of the station: she believes vaccination means Amelia will never need cervical screening, and she never volunteers it. If you don't raise screening, she says at the end 'So that's the smear tests sorted then' — and fails you on that item.

THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: never mentioning that cervical screening is still required from 25 · never addressing Amelia directly at any point · moralising about adolescent sexual activity. AND A SERIOUS ERROR TO NOTE SEPARATELY: ASKING A 13-YEAR-OLD WHETHER SHE IS SEXUALLY ACTIVE IN FRONT OF HER MOTHER.

Greet both, and ask the thirteen-year-old's permission — 'You must be Amelia — nice to meet you. IS IT ALRIGHT WITH YOU IF WE TALK ABOUT THE VACCINE YOU'VE BEEN OFFERED AT SCHOOL? IT'S YOUR BODY, SO I'D LIKE TO HEAR WHAT YOU THINK AS WELL, NOT JUST WHAT MUM THINKS.' IF YOU SPEAK ONLY TO HER MOTHER, AMELIA SAYS NOTHING FOR THE WHOLE STATION AND LOOKS AT HER PHONE. If you address her by name and ask her opinion, she answers properly and asks a question of her own

Park the loaded question — do not flinch and do not dodge — 'THAT'S A REALLY IMPORTANT QUESTION AND I WANT TO ANSWER IT PROPERLY — CAN I ASK A COUPLE OF QUICK SAFETY QUESTIONS FIRST, THEN COME STRAIGHT BACK TO IT?' TWO FAILURES AT ONCE ARE AVAILABLE HERE: VISIBLE DISCOMFORT, which tells both of them the topic is shameful and makes the concern harder to answer, not easier · and MOVING PAST IT TO SAFER GROUND. If you look uncomfortable or say 'that's not really relevant', she becomes closed and takes the form home undecided

The ninety-second screen — and the two specific questions — Previous vaccine reaction · ANY ALLERGIES AT ALL, AND SPECIFICALLY ANY PROBLEM WITH YEAST, because that is the actual component and a generic 'any allergies?' never reaches it · medical conditions, immune status and medications · BLEEDING PROBLEMS OR BLOOD THINNERS · 'HAVE YOU EVER FAINTED WITH A NEEDLE OR A BLOOD TEST?' asked of Amelia directly, because SHE WENT LIGHT-HEADED AND CLAMMY AT A BLOOD TEST LAST YEAR AND WILL SAY SO ONLY IF ASKED · and well today. THE FAINTING HISTORY CHANGES WHERE AND HOW YOU GIVE IT

What HPV is, said plainly and without euphemism — 'A VERY COMMON VIRUS — most people are exposed at some point, usually without ever knowing, AND THE BODY NORMALLY CLEARS IT. But a few types don't clear, and over many years those can cause CANCER OF THE CERVIX, AND ALSO CANCERS OF THE VULVA, VAGINA, ANUS, PENIS AND THROAT. A couple of other types cause genital warts. THIS VACCINE COVERS NINE TYPES: the two responsible for most of the cancers, five more that cause the rest, and two that cause most warts.' SAY 'SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED' PLAINLY IF IT COMES UP — hedging around it signals the subject is embarrassing

The answer, head-on: no, and it has been studied rather than assumed — 'Researchers have followed young people who were vaccinated and young people who weren't, and looked at WHEN THEY BECAME SEXUALLY ACTIVE, HOW MANY PARTNERS THEY HAD, AND THEIR RATES OF OTHER SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS. THERE'S NO DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE GROUPS.' THEN THE REFRAME: 'the reason we give it now ISN'T AN ASSUMPTION ABOUT AMELIA. It's that THE VACCINE ONLY WORKS IF HER IMMUNE SYSTEM MEETS IT BEFORE THE VIRUS DOES. IT'S LIKE A SEATBELT — YOU PUT IT ON BEFORE THE JOURNEY, NOT AFTER THE CRASH.' AND PRESERVE HER ROLE: 'this doesn't replace anything you'd want to say to her about relationships, consent and looking after herself. THOSE CONVERSATIONS ARE YOURS AND THEY STILL MATTER'

The two things that are not your role, and the one that always is — DO NOT MORALISE IN EITHER DIRECTION — commenting on when Amelia should or should not be sexually active reads badly, and so does reassuring her mother that she 'won't be like that'. AND NEVER ASK A 13-YEAR-OLD WHETHER SHE IS SEXUALLY ACTIVE IN FRONT OF HER MOTHER; IT IS NOT NEEDED FOR THIS DECISION AND IT IS A SERIOUS ERROR. WHAT ALWAYS BELONGS: 'HAVING THIS VACCINE DOES NOT MEAN YOU CAN SKIP CERVICAL SCREENING LATER. You'll still need your FIRST CERVICAL SCREENING TEST AT 25, AND THEN EVERY FIVE YEARS. The vaccine covers nine types, and there are others it doesn't.' The mother privately believes vaccination replaces screening, AND IF YOU NEVER RAISE IT SHE LEAVES STILL BELIEVING IT

stem: General practice. James Whitfield, 70, well, no acute illness. BP 132/78, HR 74, afebrile. No examination required.
He has come in asking about the shingles vaccine after hearing about it from a friend and seeing a pharmacy poster. 8 minutes.
Ran as a pilot station, so expect spare time. Variant B is a 62-year-old on methotrexate; variant C is a patient who had a previous nip-funded Zostavax dose.
tasks: Take a relevant focused history (about 4 minutes)
Explain shingles and educate him about shingles vaccination in Australia, including the newer vaccine
Address his concerns and answer his questions
time: About four minutes of focused history, then the counselling · mention Zostavax in twenty seconds and spend the time on Shingrix — two minutes on the old vaccine is time taken from the one the task actually asks about

back.dx: SHINGLES VACCINATION COUNSELLING IN A WELL 70-YEAR-OLD — SCREEN THREE THINGS, THEN COUNSEL TWO VACCINES. ZOSTAVAX IN TWENTY SECONDS, BECAUSE THE CONTRAST IS THE TEACHING POINT: 'it was the first shingles vaccine and the one that used to be on the national immunisation program. ITS PROBLEM WAS THAT IT CONTAINED LIVE VIRUS — a weakened form — so WE COULDN'T GIVE IT TO PEOPLE WHOSE IMMUNE SYSTEM WAS WEAK: people on cancer treatment, transplant medicines, steroids or methotrexate. VERY RARELY, IN THOSE PEOPLE, THE VACCINE VIRUS ITSELF COULD CAUSE AN INFECTION.' CONTRAINDICATION AND DOSING: 'the ONLY reason we couldn't give it is A SEVERE ALLERGIC REACTION TO A PREVIOUS DOSE OR TO ONE OF ITS INGREDIENTS. If you were unwell with a fever on the day we'd simply postpone. IT'S A COURSE OF TWO DOSES — the first whenever suits you, the second TWO TO SIX MONTHS LATER, or ONE TO TWO MONTHS if immunocompromised. YOU NEED BOTH — ONE DOSE ALONE DOESN'T GIVE THE FULL PROTECTION — and once you've finished the course you don't need to repeat it.' IF HE ASKS 'SO THAT'S ME DONE TODAY?', THE ANSWER IS NO — BOOK DOSE TWO BEFORE HE LEAVES. THE SAFETY-NET HAS TWO PARTS: come back if unwell beyond two or three days, or if the arm becomes HOT, SPREADING AND INCREASINGLY PAINFUL · AND SEPARATELY, IF HE EVER GETS A PAINFUL ONE-SIDED RASH, SEE US WITHIN 72 HOURS, BECAUSE ANTIVIRAL TREATMENT WORKS BEST EARLY. THE VARIANTS, SCRIPTED: VERSION B, METHOTREXATE OR LONG-TERM PREDNISOLONE — 'YOU'VE ASKED EXACTLY THE RIGHT QUESTION, AND THE ANSWER HAS CHANGED. With the older vaccine you'd have been right — Zostavax contained live virus and would not have been safe for you. SHINGRIX HAS NO LIVE VIRUS AT ALL, so we can give it to you safely. AND IN FACT YOU'RE ONE OF THE PEOPLE WE MOST WANT TO PROTECT, because a weakened immune system makes shingles BOTH MORE LIKELY AND MORE SEVERE. Because of that, IT'S FREE FOR YOU ON THE NATIONAL PROGRAMME EVEN AT 62, and we BRING THE SECOND DOSE FORWARD TO ONE TO TWO MONTHS. I'd also let your rheumatologist know we've given it.' TWO FAILURES LIVE IN THIS VARIANT — REFUSING THE VACCINE, AND GIVING IT WITH THE IMMUNOCOMPETENT INTERVAL — SO SAY THE INTERVAL OUT LOUD, LINKED TO THE REASON. VERSION C, PREVIOUS NIP-FUNDED ZOSTAVAX — 'they're different products, and we want A GAP OF AT LEAST TWELVE MONTHS between them, which you've comfortably passed, SO THERE'S NO SAFETY ISSUE. The separate question is cost: THE FUNDED PROGRAMME GENERALLY WON'T COVER A SHINGLES VACCINE WITHIN FIVE YEARS OF A FREE ZOSTAVAX DOSE, so there may be a charge. I'D RATHER TELL YOU THAT NOW THAN HAVE YOU FIND OUT AT THE COUNTER. Would you like me to check the current criteria before we book you in?' VERSION D, 'I NEVER HAD CHICKENPOX' — 'that's worth knowing, because IT CHANGES WHICH VACCINE IS RIGHT. The shingles vaccine ONLY MAKES SENSE IF THE CHICKENPOX VIRUS IS ALREADY SLEEPING IN YOUR SYSTEM — YOU CAN'T REACTIVATE SOMETHING YOU NEVER CAUGHT. Most people your age have had it without remembering, so I wouldn't assume you missed it. If we checked with a blood test and it showed you've genuinely never been exposed, THE RIGHT VACCINE WOULD BE THE CHICKENPOX VACCINE, NOT THE SHINGLES ONE.' AND IF VERSION D IS COMBINED WITH IMMUNOSUPPRESSION: THE VARICELLA VACCINE IS LIVE, so in a SERONEGATIVE, IMMUNOCOMPROMISED patient you CANNOT SIMPLY SUBSTITUTE IT — that is contraindicated. 'I wouldn't give either without specialist advice, and in the meantime the priority is AVOIDING EXPOSURE and coming to us straight away if you're in contact with chickenpox or shingles.' VERSION E, RECENT SHINGLES — 'HAVING HAD SHINGLES ONCE DOESN'T PROTECT YOU FROM HAVING IT AGAIN, so vaccination is still recommended. The advice is to WAIT ABOUT TWELVE MONTHS FROM THE EPISODE, because your immune system has just had a natural boost and the vaccine works better after that gap. Let me put a reminder in now so it doesn't slip.' HIS HIDDEN AGENDA: HIS BOWLS FRIEND RON HAD SHINGLES LAST YEAR AND STILL HAS BURNING PAIN DOWN HIS RIBS. He is frightened of ending up like Ron but FINDS IT EMBARRASSING TO SAY HE IS FRIGHTENED, SO HE SAYS IT AS A JOKE — 'put the wind up me a bit'. If you don't ask about concerns by about six minutes, he volunteers it late and marks you down. HIS SECOND CONCERN IS GOLF ON SATURDAY, which deserves a practical answer: HAVE THE INJECTION EARLY IN THE WEEK RATHER THAN THE DAY BEFORE. HE MAY ALSO ASK WHETHER IT IS SAFE TO BE AROUND A GRANDCHILD ON CHEMOTHERAPY AFTERWARDS, AND WHETHER HE CAN HAVE IT WITH HIS FLU VACCINE.
plan: Introduce and confirm his name, acknowledge the effort, and ask permission to take a history first.
What he already knows, and what made him come in today — the agenda lives here.
The three named questions: chickenpox · previous shingles · previous shingles vaccine, and which one.
ALLERGIES, SPLIT: reaction to any vaccination, then everything else.
Immune status, asked as two questions: conditions, then medications — steroids, methotrexate, cancer treatment.
WELL TODAY? AND WHAT CONCERNS WOULD HE LIKE ADDRESSED — before you counsel anything.
Explain shingles in plain English, and name the nerve pain that lasts months as the thing you are preventing.
SIGNPOST TWO VACCINES. ZOSTAVAX IN TWENTY SECONDS — live virus, and why that mattered.
Shingrix: three pros, then the sore arm and the day or two of feeling off, then anaphylaxis and the fifteen minutes.
CONTRAINDICATION, THEN DOSING TIED TO HIS IMMUNE STATUS — two doses, and book the second in the room.
ANSWER 'WILL IT DEFINITELY STOP ME?' HONESTLY — substantially reduces the risk, and reduces the nerve pain if he does get it.
Written information · a real choice rather than an instruction · the 72-hour antiviral safety-net · air · summarise and teach-back.

ask: THE HISTORY SET: 'Is it okay if I ask you a few questions first, SO THAT WHAT I TELL YOU ACTUALLY APPLIES TO YOU?' · 'Have you ever had chickenpox, as a child or at any time?' · 'Have you had any shingles vaccine before — PERHAPS A FREE ONE A FEW YEARS AGO?' · 'Have you had an allergic reaction to any vaccination? … And any other allergies?' · 'Any medications — STEROIDS, METHOTREXATE, CANCER TREATMENT?'

THE EXPLANATION SET: 'Shingles is a reactivation of the chickenpox virus that has been ASLEEP IN A NERVE ROOT SINCE CHILDHOOD.' · 'The rash settles in a few weeks, BUT THE NERVE PAIN CAN LAST MONTHS — that's what we most want to prevent.' · 'Zostavax contained live virus, so we couldn't use it in people with weak immune systems.' · 'SHINGRIX HAS NO LIVE VIRUS AT ALL — it works better, protects for longer, and it's free on the national programme from 65.'

THE HONEST SET: 'It's known for a sore arm, and some people feel achy and off for a day or two — that settles.' · 'IT SUBSTANTIALLY REDUCES THE RISK RATHER THAN REMOVING IT COMPLETELY.' · 'Have a read, think about it, and come back whenever you're ready — AND I'LL BOOK BOTH DOSES SO THE SECOND ISN'T FORGOTTEN.' · AND THE PRACTICAL ONE: if the golf matters, HAVE THE INJECTION EARLY IN THE WEEK RATHER THAN THE DAY BEFORE.
pefe: No examination required, and the observations are given: BP 132/78, HR 74, afebrile. The history is the assessment — chickenpox at seven · never had shingles · no previous shingles vaccine · no reaction to any vaccination, with a penicillin rash only · no immunocompromising condition and no immunosuppressive medication, just perindopril · well today · ex-smoker, quit 25 years ago.

HE VOLUNTEERS NOTHING AND ANSWERS IN ONE OR TWO SENTENCES. IF YOU USE JARGON — DERMATOME, REACTIVATION, RECOMBINANT, IMMUNOCOMPETENT — HE LOOKS BLANK AND ASKS WHAT IT MEANS. If you instruct rather than offer, he pushes back once: 'DO I HAVE TO DECIDE TODAY?' And if you tell him he cannot have the vaccine for any reason, he looks confused and asks why.
THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: refusing or deferring the vaccine because of immunosuppression in version B · and counselling without taking any history.

Acknowledge the effort, then buy permission for the history — There is no symptom to acknowledge, so candidates skip acknowledgement altogether and start reciting vaccine facts. BOTH HALVES ARE SCORED: 'I REALLY APPRECIATE YOU COMING IN TO TALK ABOUT THE SHINGLES VACCINE — THAT'S A VERY SENSIBLE THING TO BE THINKING ABOUT. Before I go through it with you, IS IT OKAY IF I ASK YOU A FEW QUESTIONS FIRST, SO THAT WHAT I TELL YOU ACTUALLY APPLIES TO YOU?' Then ask what he already knows AND WHAT MADE HIM COME IN TODAY, because his answer contains the hidden agenda

The three questions that change the plan — asked separately and by name — 'HAVE YOU EVER HAD CHICKENPOX, as a child or at any time?' · 'HAVE YOU EVER HAD SHINGLES ITSELF?' · 'HAVE YOU HAD ANY SHINGLES VACCINE BEFORE — PERHAPS A FREE ONE A FEW YEARS BACK? DO YOU REMEMBER WHICH ONE IT WAS?' Asking only 'any vaccines?' as part of a generic history misses all three, AND EACH ONE HAS A DIFFERENT CONSEQUENCE: no prior chickenpox changes which vaccine is right · a recent episode means waiting about twelve months · a prior funded Zostavax changes the cost

Split the allergy question in two — deliberately — 'HAVE YOU EVER HAD AN ALLERGIC REACTION TO ANY VACCINATION?' and then, separately, 'AND ANY OTHER ALLERGIES AT ALL — medicines, foods, latex?' ANAPHYLAXIS TO A VACCINE OR VACCINE COMPONENT IS THE ONLY ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION, so it deserves its own question. A penicillin rash is not a barrier

Immune status is the pivot of the station — Ask the condition and the medication separately: 'Any medical conditions that might weaken your immune system — diabetes, any cancer, HIV, a transplant, or an autoimmune condition?' then 'And are you taking any medications — I'm particularly interested in steroids, methotrexate, or any cancer treatment?' Hearing 'Methotrexate' and reaching for the old rule is the failure. Shingrix is not live. Immunosuppression is an indication, changes funding to age 18, and shortens the second dose interval to one to two months

Explain shingles by naming the harm you are preventing — 'Shingles is a REACTIVATION OF THE CHICKENPOX VIRUS. When you had chickenpox as a boy the virus NEVER REALLY LEFT — IT WENT TO SLEEP IN A NERVE ROOT NEAR YOUR SPINE. Years later, usually as our immune system weakens a little with age, it can wake up and travel down THAT ONE NERVE, giving a painful blistering rash IN A BAND ON ONE SIDE OF THE BODY. The rash usually clears in a few weeks, BUT IN SOME PEOPLE THE NERVE PAIN CARRIES ON FOR MONTHS — that's what happened to your friend, AND THAT'S THE MAIN THING WE'RE TRYING TO PREVENT.' IF YOU NEVER NAME POST-HERPETIC NEURALGIA IN LAY TERMS, YOU HAVE NOT EXPLAINED THE BENEFIT

Shingrix — three pros, then the honest cons — ONE, NO LIVE VIRUS AT ALL, so it is safe in people with weakened immune systems. TWO, IT WORKS BETTER AND THE PROTECTION LASTS LONGER, especially over 70. THREE, IT IS FREE ON THE NIP AT 65 AND OVER, for ABORIGINAL AND TORRES STRAIT ISLANDER PEOPLE FROM 50, and for ADULTS WITH A CONDITION THAT WEAKENS THE IMMUNE SYSTEM FROM 18. THE TRADE-OFF: it is KNOWN FOR A SORE ARM, and many people feel tired, achy, headachy or a bit feverish FOR A DAY OR TWO — that is the immune system doing its job. Then anaphylaxis and the fifteen minutes. NEVER SAY 'IT'S FREE' BEFORE ESTABLISHING AGE, ABORIGINAL AND TORRES STRAIT ISLANDER STATUS AND IMMUNE STATUS — AND NEVER PROMISE COMPLETE PROTECTION: 'IT SUBSTANTIALLY REDUCES THE RISK', NOT 'IT PREVENTS IT'
fails: ★ Refuses or defers Shingrix because the patient is on methotrexate or steroids — it is not live, and immunosuppression is an indication that brings funding to 18 and shortens the interval
★ Counsels without taking any history, so the three named questions and the immune status are never established
Asks 'any vaccines?' as a generic question instead of chickenpox, previous shingles and previous shingles vaccine separately — or rolls both allergy questions into one
Spends two minutes on Zostavax, says 'it's free' before establishing eligibility, or promises complete protection instead of substantial risk reduction
Quotes one dose, gives the interval without linking it to immune status, never names the nerve pain in lay terms, or books him in rather than offering a genuine choice
numbers: Two doses · 0.5 mL IM deltoid · 2–6 months apart if immunocompetent · 1–2 months if immunocompromised · recommended from 50, and from 18 if at increased risk · nip-funded at 65+, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander 50+, and eligible immunocompromise 18+ · at least 12 months after Zostavax and after an episode of shingles · not nip-funded within 5 years of a funded Zostavax dose VERIFY

Protection sustained at least 7 years with no booster · observe 15 minutes · antivirals within 72 hours of rash onset · the only absolute contraindication is anaphylaxis to a previous dose or component · postpone if febrile on the day · air reporting mandatory · separate 'Recommended from 50' from 'Free from 65' when you say it

setting: Characterise the allergy, then dismantle it — confidently enough to be believed. Referring to an allergist 'To be safe' is the AUTOMATIC FAIL: it is not current practice, and tentativeness here is itself a clinical error, because it produces a refusal. The role-player is briefed that if you hesitate or defer, she says 'So you're not comfortable giving it either' and declines — and the rest of the station is a formality.
stem: General practice, South Australia, early April. Mia Sullivan, 4, is brought in by her mother Katie. Mia is well and afebrile. No examination required.
The mother has come to discuss the influenza vaccine and is unsure whether she wants it. 8 minutes.

Three things are withheld and released one at a time, only if asked: egg allergy with lip swelling and an adrenaline autoinjector · asthma · and a short course of oral prednisolone last month. None of them is a contraindication, and two of them are reasons to go ahead.
The three AUTOMATIC FAILS: withholding or referring because of egg allergy · lecturing before eliciting · pushing after a clear refusal.
tasks: Take a relevant history (about 3 to 4 minutes)
Explain and educate about influenza vaccination
Address her concerns
time: Three to four minutes of history, and the concern she names first is what the rest of the consultation should be built around · ask permission before informing — 'Can I take you through what we know?' Costs two seconds and changes the dynamic from lecture to conversation

back.dx: INFLUENZA VACCINATION COUNSELLING IN A WELL 4-YEAR-OLD WITH THREE FALSE BARRIERS. PRACTICALITIES: ONE DOSE EACH YEAR — THE ONLY EXCEPTION IS THE VERY FIRST YEAR A CHILD UNDER NINE HAS IT, WHEN THEY NEED TWO DOSES FOUR WEEKS APART TO PRIME THE IMMUNE SYSTEM. Mia had one last year, so ONE DOSE THIS YEAR IS ALL SHE NEEDS. RECOMMENDED FROM APRIL, before the season builds, because protection fades over a few months — THOUGH IT IS NEVER TOO LATE ONCE WINTER HAS STARTED. AND IT IS FREE: children from SIX MONTHS TO FIVE YEARS are covered on the NIP. SIDE EFFECTS: most commonly a SORE, RED, SWOLLEN ARM, and some children get a mild fever, tiredness, aches or headache for a day or so — paracetamol and a quiet day usually cover it. The serious one is ANAPHYLAXIS, which is why you observe, and why you do it in the practice rather than anywhere else. THE ONLY REASONS NOT TO GIVE IT: a SEVERE ALLERGIC REACTION TO A PREVIOUS FLU VACCINE, or being UNWELL WITH A FEVER TODAY. THE VARIANTS, SCRIPTED: VERSION C, THE PARENT WHO DECLINES — 'that's absolutely your decision to make, and I respect it. IT WON'T CHANGE ANYTHING ABOUT HOW WE LOOK AFTER MIA. Can I do three small things? The written information so you've got it if you want to look again · A NOTE THAT WE DISCUSSED IT, SO NOBODY HASSLES YOU ABOUT IT EVERY VISIT · and I'll bring it up ONCE MORE NEXT AUTUMN — not to pressure you, just so the option stays open.' DO NOT PUSH AGAIN: NOT 'ARE YOU SURE?', NOT 'JUST THINK ABOUT THE RISKS'. ONE GRACEFUL ACCEPTANCE, INFORMATION PROVIDED, DOOR LEFT OPEN, DOCUMENTED — THAT IS THE FULL MARK. VERSION D, THE FIRST-EVER RECIPIENT — 'because she's UNDER NINE and this is her FIRST EVER influenza vaccine, she needs TWO DOSES, AT LEAST FOUR WEEKS APART, to prime her immune system properly. ONE DOSE ON ITS OWN DOESN'T GIVE THE FULL PROTECTION in a child who's never met the vaccine before. After this year, it's one a year like everyone else. SHALL I BOOK THE SECOND ONE NOW, SO IT DOESN'T GET FORGOTTEN?' VERSION E, FEBRILE ON THE DAY at 38.6 °C — 'I'd rather we postpone today — NOT BECAUSE THE VACCINE IS UNSAFE, but because IF SHE DEVELOPS A FEVER TOMORROW WE WON'T KNOW WHETHER IT'S THE VACCINE OR WHATEVER SHE'S BREWING NOW, and that makes life harder for both of us. A SNUFFLY NOSE WITHOUT A FEVER WOULD BE FINE; THIS ISN'T. Let's get her better and rebook for a fortnight — I'll put it in now.' VERSION F, THE IMMUNOCOMPROMISED CHILD ON MAINTENANCE CHEMOTHERAPY — 'for live vaccines you'd be right, and we'd need to be careful. BUT THE INFLUENZA VACCINE CONTAINS NO LIVE VIRUS, so it can be given safely — and CHILDREN IN HIS SITUATION ARE AMONG THOSE WE MOST WANT PROTECTED, because influenza is more dangerous for them. HIS IMMUNE SYSTEM MAY NOT RESPOND AS STRONGLY as another child's, WHICH IS ONE REASON WE ALSO VACCINATE EVERYONE AROUND HIM — you, his siblings, his grandparents. I'd also confirm the timing with his oncology team relative to his chemotherapy cycle.' HER HIDDEN AGENDA: A FRIEND AT PLAYGROUP TOLD HER THAT HER SON 'GOT THE FLU FROM THE FLU SHOT' and was off nursery for a week. SHE HALF BELIEVES IT AND FEELS SLIGHTLY FOOLISH ABOUT THAT, so she only says it if you ask what she has heard or give her an opening. UNDERNEATH THAT, HER REAL FEAR IS THE ALLERGY — SHE HAS WATCHED HER DAUGHTER'S FACE SWELL ONCE AND WILL NOT RISK IT AGAIN. SHE IS NOT ANTI-VACCINE: MIA IS OTHERWISE FULLY IMMUNISED, AND SHE JUST WANTS SOMEONE TO ACTUALLY ANSWER THE EGG QUESTION. AND IF YOU MENTION CHILDCARE EXCLUSION OR FAMILY PAYMENTS AS A REASON, SHE BECOMES COLD: 'ARE YOU THREATENING ME?'
plan: Greet both mother and child, and thank her for coming in to talk it through rather than just deciding.
ELICIT FIRST: what have you heard, and what's worrying you most? The egg comes out here.
Previous influenza vaccines, then vaccine reactions separately, then other allergies.
CHARACTERISE THE EGG REACTION IN FULL: timing, features, breathing, treatment, autoinjector, exposure since.
CONDITIONS (asthma surfaces) · MEDICATIONS AND RECENT STEROIDS (the prednisolone surfaces) · WELL TODAY · AND WHO ELSE IS AT HOME.
Ask permission, then what influenza is — not a bad cold — and that there is no live virus, so it cannot give her the flu.
THE EGG, ANSWERED HEAD-ON AND WITHOUT HEDGING: not a contraindication, even after a severe reaction · given here · THIRTY MINUTES RATHER THAN FIFTEEN · autoinjector stays with her.
Asthma as an indication, and the steroids as irrelevant to an inactivated vaccine.
Dosing and the two-dose rule · timing from April · and that it is free under five.
Side effects, anaphylaxis, and the true contraindications.
OFFER THE GRANDMOTHER'S VACCINATION, give the written information, AND LEAVE THE DECISION WITH HER — including that declining will not change Mia's care.
Air, thirty-minute observation if given, summarise, and teach-back.

ask: THE ELICITING SET: 'Thank you for coming in to talk it through rather than just deciding one way or the other.' · 'BEFORE I SAY ANYTHING, I'D LIKE TO HEAR FROM YOU — what have you heard, and what's worrying you most?' · 'Can I take you through what we know about that?' · 'Has Mia ever had a reaction to any vaccination? … And any other allergies?' · 'TELL ME EXACTLY WHAT HAPPENED WITH THE EGG — how soon, what did you see, did she need treatment?'

THE ANSWERING SET: 'Influenza isn't the same thing as a bad cold.' · 'THERE IS NO LIVE VIRUS IN IT AT ALL, SO IT CANNOT GIVE HER INFLUENZA.' · 'EGG ALLERGY IS NOT A REASON TO AVOID THE FLU VACCINE — AND THAT INCLUDES CHILDREN WHO'VE HAD A SEVERE REACTION.' · 'We'd give it here, where we're equipped to manage a reaction, and keep her thirty minutes rather than fifteen.' · 'HER ASTHMA IS A REASON FOR HAVING IT, NOT AGAINST.' · 'Steroids matter for live vaccines — this one has none.'

THE CLOSING SET: 'One dose a year; two doses four weeks apart ONLY in the very first year a child under nine has it.' · 'YOU DON'T HAVE TO DECIDE TODAY, AND IF YOU DECIDE AGAINST IT THAT WON'T CHANGE HOW WE LOOK AFTER MIA.' · 'Who else is at home? Anyone pregnant, a baby under six months, or anyone over sixty-five?'
pefe: NO EXAMINATION REQUIRED AND SHE IS AFEBRILE — THE HISTORY IS THE ASSESSMENT, AND THE THREE CRITICAL ANSWERS ARE RELEASED ONE AT A TIME AND ONLY WHEN ASKED: THE EGG ALLERGY when you ask about allergies — at two she ate scrambled egg, and WITHIN TEN MINUTES her lips and face swelled with hives and some wheeze, treated in the emergency department, NOW CARRIES AN ADRENALINE AUTOINJECTOR AND AVOIDS EGG ENTIRELY · THE ASTHMA when you ask about medical conditions — salbutamol as needed plus a winter preventer · AND FIVE DAYS OF ORAL PREDNISOLONE LAST MONTH when you ask about medications.

IF YOU NEVER ASK ABOUT MEDICATIONS, SHE NEVER MENTIONS THE STEROIDS — AND MARKS YOU DOWN. Likewise the household: her mother, 71, lives with them and helps with childcare. Mia had ONE INFLUENZA VACCINE LAST YEAR WITH NO REACTION, all other childhood vaccines are up to date, and there are NO OTHER ALLERGIES.

THE ROLE-PLAYER'S AUTOMATIC FAILS: withholding, deferring or referring the vaccine because of the egg allergy · lecturing without ever asking what she was worried about · and continuing to push after she declines in version C.

Greet the child, and ask before you tell — 'And this must be Mia — hello Mia.' IGNORING THE CHILD COMPLETELY FOR EIGHT MINUTES IS ONE OF THE TWO OPENING TRAPS. Then: 'THANK YOU FOR COMING IN TO TALK IT THROUGH RATHER THAN JUST DECIDING ONE WAY OR THE OTHER. Before I say anything about the vaccine, I'D LIKE TO HEAR FROM YOU FIRST — WHAT HAVE YOU HEARD, AND WHAT'S WORRYING YOU MOST?' If you start explaining before asking, she interrupts once: 'SORRY — CAN I JUST ASK ABOUT THE EGGS?'

Split the allergy question, then characterise the reaction properly — Vaccine reactions first, because anaphylaxis to a previous influenza vaccine is the only true contraindication — then everything else. When the egg comes out, take it seriously before you reassure: 'Tell me exactly what happened. How long after eating the egg? What did you see — lips, a rash, any trouble breathing, was she floppy or pale? Did she need treatment, and does she carry an adrenaline autoinjector now? Has she had egg since?' Jumping straight to 'That's fine, it doesn't matter' loses her — a mother whose child's allergy is brushed aside will not believe the reassurance that follows, and the examiner is marking whether you characterised it

The egg answer — the station's centre of gravity, said plainly — 'You're right that the vaccine IS GROWN IN EGGS, so it does contain A TRACE AMOUNT OF EGG PROTEIN. But here's the important part: EGG ALLERGY IS NOT A REASON TO AVOID THE FLU VACCINE — AND THAT INCLUDES CHILDREN WHO HAVE HAD A SEVERE REACTION, LIKE MIA. That's been looked at carefully in VERY LARGE NUMBERS of children with egg allergy, and THE RATE OF REACTIONS IS NO DIFFERENT from children without egg allergy. What we'd do is straightforward: WE GIVE IT HERE IN THE PRACTICE, where we are set up and trained to manage a reaction — and given her history I'd KEEP HER HERE FOR THIRTY MINUTES rather than the usual fifteen. HER AUTOINJECTOR STAYS WITH HER'

The other two 'Barriers' are reasons to go ahead — ASTHMA: 'that's A REASON FOR HAVING IT, NOT AGAINST. INFLUENZA HITS CHILDREN WITH ASTHMA HARDER, so she's exactly who we want protected.' STEROIDS: 'steroids matter for VACCINES THAT CONTAIN LIVE VIRUS, because a weakened immune system can struggle with them. THIS ONE HAS NO LIVE VIRUS, SO A SHORT COURSE OF STEROIDS MAKES NO DIFFERENCE AT ALL.' That one-sentence live-versus-inactivated distinction is what makes it sound like understanding rather than a memorised list

The myth, corrected without contradicting her — 'THE VACCINE CONTAINS ONLY PART OF THE VIRUS — THERE IS NO LIVE VIRUS IN IT AT ALL, SO IT CANNOT GIVE HER INFLUENZA.' And when she says her friend's son caught the flu from it: 'I HEAR THAT A LOT, AND I UNDERSTAND WHY — some children feel achy and warm for a day afterwards, WHICH DOES FEEL FLU-LIKE. But that's the immune system responding, NOT AN INFECTION.' Also worth saying plainly: INFLUENZA ISN'T THE SAME THING AS A BAD COLD — sudden high fevers, severe aches, a nasty cough, and IN YOUNG CHILDREN AND PEOPLE WITH ASTHMA IT CAN LEAD TO SERIOUS CHEST INFECTIONS AND HOSPITAL ADMISSION

Ask who else is at home — the opportunistic mark — 'Who else is at home — IS ANYONE PREGNANT, IS THERE A BABY UNDER SIX MONTHS, OR ANYONE WITH A WEAK IMMUNE SYSTEM?' Her mother, 71, lives with them AND IS ALSO FREE ON THE NIP — offering her vaccination is a scored opportunistic-prevention item and costs one sentence. If you never ask about the household, you never find her
